«7 минут. Столько длилась моя операция в Афганистане. Я зашел в игру, думая, что это ебаный Counter-Strike. А оказалось — это симулятор боевых действий, где физика Source играет роль ебаного талиба.

Я высадился на Dust2. В руках — Glock. В глазах — надежда. Но тут я увидел, как ебаная бочка от моего выстрела улетела в небо и приземлилась на голову моему тиммейту. Он умер. Я понял, что это не шутер. Это ебаная война с гравитацией. Мои ноги скользят по текстурам, как будто я на льду. Мои пули летят не туда, куда я целюсь. А модели персонажей выглядят так, будто их слепили из ебаного пластилина и забыли разгладить.

Потом я зашел на сервер с ботами. И тут начался настоящий пиздец. Боты в Source — это не противники, это ебаные зомби с аимботом. Они видят тебя сквозь стены, стреляют в голову с первого патрона и не тупят. Я проиграл им 5 раундов подряд, и мне стало казаться, что я — ебаный рак в этом мире.

Но настоящий позор случился, когда на сервер зашли мужики со смены. Они не стреляли. Они просто бегали и орали в микрофон «АЛО, ТАМ ЕСТЬ КТО?», кидали гранаты в своих и покупали дефузер, когда играли за террористов. И знаешь что? Я понял, что это — ебаный идеальный баланс. Боты убивают тебя тактически, а мужики — морально.

Я не проиграл. Я выжил. Но я больше не тот, кем был. Я — ебаный ветеран Source. И я оставляю этот отзыв как предупреждение всем, кто думает, что это просто "старая Контра". Это не Контра. Это Противоудар. Операция в Афганистане."

-RUSHING PRIVATE RYAN-

We set out in the morning, warily checking windows, corners, anywhere the Germans could spring a trap or an ambush.

Johannson was in the lead, Garand at the ready and bayonet fixed improperly. Rook was shadowing him, double checking each spot that Johannson had checked before. I was in the middle with Peters, helping him carry the M2 Browning. And Stewart was in the rear, covering our backs with his Thompson at the ready.

It was quiet. Too quiet.

The bridge we had set out to capture was undefended, and we quickly set up a defensive position in case a German patrol stumbled upon us.

The sound started as a low rumble. We looked around, at each other, confused as to why the ground was shaking. It got louder, and we could soon hear the sound of people yelling. We readied our weapons, getting ready for the enemy to throw a grenade or fire a Panzerschreck.

But nothing could prepare us for what happened next.

A giant tide of German soldiers, all carrying trench shovels and primed Steilhandgranates in their hands, came around the corner, rushing at us screaming at the top of their lungs.

We opened fire, but there were too many and we were quickly overrun.

Stewart was the first to go, having gotten overzealous with his Thompson. He had managed to push the wave of Germans back, when they surrounded him and began pummeling him to death with their shovels.

One of them, holding a grenade, charged Rook and Johannson from behind. They never saw it coming.

By now, it was only me and Peters, him firing his MG wildly at the advancing tide while I threw frag grenade after frag grenade. And then Peters started to run out of ammo.

Quickly, I rushed up to his position with a new box of ammunition, but by that time they were almost upon him. Peters quickly pulled out his M1911 and managed to squeeze off a few shots, but it wasn't long before he too was buried under the mass of grey and black.

I was cornered, back against a locked door while I blasted soldier after soldier back with my Sniper rifle. But it was no use. They descended upon me, swinging shovels indiscriminately at my already bruised and battered body. They were relentless, beating me until at last, I succumbed to the darkness.

As my vision blurred, they stopped screaming long enough for one of them to say something to me.

Something that would shock me to the core.

He said:

[h1]Half-Life 2: Deathmatch[/h1]

[b]Gêneros:[/b] Ação
[b]Avaliação na Steam:[/b] Muito positiva
[b]Preço:[/b] Gratuito

[b]Visão geral[/b]
Half-Life 2: Deathmatch traz a icônica física do universo de HL2 para o modo multijogador rápido. A proposta é simples: combate frenético, seja em partidas individuais de morte súbita ou em equipes Combine contra a Resistência. O jogo reutiliza ambientes familiares, porém adaptados para confrontos dinâmicos. A primeira impressão é de um título que prioriza a diversão caótica e a criatividade dos jogadores.

[b]Jogabilidade[/b]
O núcleo da jogabilidade gira em torno da manipulação de objetos físicos, permitindo estratégias inesperadas, como usar um vaso sanitário como arma improvisada. Os controles são responsivos e mantêm a sensação de peso dos objetos, algo que diferencia o modo de outros shooters. Existem dois modos principais: morte súbita, onde todos enfrentam a todos, e o modo de equipe, que acrescenta objetivos táticos. O ritmo é acelerado, com partidas curtas que incentivam múltiplas rodadas em uma única sessão. A progressão é mínima; o foco está na habilidade e na criatividade em tempo real, o que favorece a rejogabilidade. Ainda assim, há um sistema de desbloqueio de skins e mapas que oferece um leve incentivo à continuidade.

[b]Apresentação e atmosfera[/b]
Visualmente, o jogo mantém o estilo de Half-Life 2, com texturas ainda aceitáveis apesar da idade. Os mapas são bem projetados para facilitar o uso da física, com objetos interativos espalhados por todo o cenário. A trilha sonora e os efeitos sonoros são familiares, contribuindo para a imersão no universo da Combine. A atmosfera combina humor e tensão, especialmente quando situações absurdas surgem a partir da física descontrolada.

[b]Pontos positivos[/b]
[list]
[*] Uso criativo da física do motor Source
[*] Modos de jogo variados que atendem a diferentes estilos
[*] Partidas curtas e altamente rejogáveis
[*] Gratuito e fácil de acessar
[*] Comunidade ainda ativa com mapas customizados
[*] Sensação nostálgica para fãs de Half-Life 2
[/list]

[b]Pontos negativos[/b]
[list]
[*] Gráficos datados que podem parecer ultrapassados
[*] Falta de modos de progressão profunda
[*] Alguma instabilidade em servidores menos populares
[/list]

[b]Para quem é indicado[/b]
[b]Recomendado para:[/b] jogadores que apreciam shooters rápidos, fãs da física de Half-Life e quem busca partidas curtas e caóticas.
[b]Pode não agradar:[/b] quem prioriza gráficos modernos, modos de campanha elaborados ou competitividade extrema com ranking.

[b]Conclusão[/b]
Half-Life 2: Deathmatch entrega diversão instantânea ao combinar a física inovadora de HL2 com um formato de combate frenético. Embora não ofereça profundidade narrativa ou gráficos de última geração, sua jogabilidade criativa e acesso gratuito o tornam uma escolha sólida para sessões rápidas. É um título que brilha especialmente em grupos de amigos que gostam de experimentar estratégias improváveis.

[b]Nota final: 8/10[/b]‍

Reagiere geschickt und unerwartet, lege die auf die Lauer oder suche geheime Räume und Verstecke von denen zu aus zuschlägst.
Immer wieder eine amüsante Runde in diesem niemals endenden Irrsinn.

[h1]🎯 Half-Life Deathmatch: Source — Un jeu qui a perdu de son intérêt avec le temps[/h1]

[h2]💀 Une découverte qui ne m'a pas convaincu[/h2]

J'avais Half-Life Deathmatch: Source dans ma bibliothèque Steam depuis un bon moment, mais je n'avais jamais vraiment pris le temps de le lancer. J'avais notamment découvert le jeu grâce à une vidéo de CyrilMP4, un YouTubeur français qui testait différents jeux. Ça m'avait donné une petite idée de ce qu'il proposait, mais je n'avais jamais été particulièrement attiré par le jeu.

Finalement, c'est la Steam Roulette qui m'a décidé à le lancer. Et bon… je dois dire que je ne suis pas vraiment convaincu par cette expérience.

Dès mon arrivée dans le menu, le constat est assez triste : une quarantaine de serveurs affichés, quasiment tous complètement vides, à l'exception d'un seul. Je finis par rejoindre celui-ci et, au départ, nous sommes deux. Quelques minutes plus tard, nous sommes finalement cinq.

Autant dire que la communauté semble aujourd'hui assez limitée.

[h2]👥 Des joueurs qui connaissent le jeu par cœur[/h2]

Une fois dans la partie, je me retrouve face à des joueurs qui semblent avoir passé une bonne partie de leur vie sur ce jeu.

Les mouvements sont parfois assez impressionnants, les déplacements semblent parfaitement maîtrisés et on a rapidement l'impression de jouer contre des personnes qui connaissent absolument toutes les mécaniques.

À certains moments, on pourrait presque croire qu'ils utilisent des cheats, mais honnêtement, j'en doute. Déjà, il faudrait vraiment avoir une drôle de motivation pour tricher sur un jeu pareil. Je pense surtout qu'il s'agit de joueurs qui ont énormément d'expérience et qui continuent de jouer depuis des années.

Le problème, c'est que lorsqu'on découvre le jeu, se retrouver face à ce genre de joueurs n'est pas particulièrement amusant.

[h2]🔫 Un gameplay qui tourne rapidement en rond[/h2]

Concernant le gameplay, je trouve malheureusement que l'on fait très vite le tour.

On rejoint une partie, on se balade sur la map, on essaie de tuer les autres joueurs et on recommence. C'est globalement tout ce que le jeu propose, du moins de ce que j'ai pu découvrir pendant ma session.

Je ne dis pas que ce principe est forcément mauvais, mais personnellement, je n'ai pas trouvé ça particulièrement amusant sur la durée. Le gameplay devient rapidement répétitif et je n'ai pas vraiment ressenti l'envie de continuer à jouer.

Il manque quelque chose qui pourrait réellement me donner envie de revenir. Après quelques parties, j'avais déjà l'impression d'avoir compris l'essentiel de ce que le jeu avait à proposer.

[h2]🗺️ Des maps plutôt sympathiques[/h2]

Malgré tout, je dois reconnaître que certaines maps sont plutôt réussies.

J'ai particulièrement apprécié celle où l'on se retrouve minuscule dans une immense chambre. J'aime beaucoup ce genre de concept, avec ce petit effet Toy Story où les objets du quotidien deviennent gigantesques par rapport à notre personnage.

C'est clairement le genre de map qui apporte un peu de fraîcheur à l'expérience et qui permet de sortir des environnements habituels.

Malheureusement, même si certaines cartes sont intéressantes, ça ne suffit pas à rendre le gameplay suffisamment captivant à mes yeux.

[h2]📉 Un jeu qui a perdu de sa valeur[/h2]

Je pense que c'est finalement ce qui résume le mieux mon expérience avec Half-Life Deathmatch: Source.

On sent qu'il s'agit d'un jeu qui a vécu, mais aujourd'hui, entre les serveurs quasiment tous vides, le faible nombre de joueurs et un gameplay qui devient rapidement répétitif, j'ai du mal à lui trouver un véritable intérêt.

Son aspect visuel assez pixellisé et daté n'arrange pas non plus les choses. Je sais évidemment que le jeu n'est pas récent, mais cela ne m'empêche pas de trouver l'expérience assez peu engageante aujourd'hui.

Je peux comprendre que certains joueurs apprécient encore ce titre, notamment ceux qui y jouent depuis des années et qui ont leurs habitudes. Mais pour quelqu'un qui le découvre en 2026, l'expérience est franchement moins convaincante.

[h2]❌ Verdict : une expérience assez décevante[/h2]

Au final, Half-Life Deathmatch: Source est une découverte qui ne m'a pas particulièrement marqué.

J'ai apprécié quelques maps, notamment celle de la chambre, mais pour le reste, je n'ai pas trouvé grand-chose qui puisse me donner envie de continuer. Le gameplay est répétitif, les serveurs sont majoritairement vides et les quelques joueurs encore présents semblent avoir une expérience largement supérieure à celle d'un nouveau venu.

Je ne dirais pas que le jeu est complètement mauvais dans son principe, mais il a clairement perdu une bonne partie de son intérêt avec le temps.

Je suis content d'avoir enfin pris le temps de le lancer grâce à la Steam Roulette, mais je pense que je vais m'arrêter là.

Une petite découverte, quelques maps sympathiques, mais rien qui me donnera envie d'y retourner.

📝 English review below / Reseña en inglés más abajo

🔶 Una píldora de nostalgia competitiva pura que revive el caos desenfrenado del multiplayer clásico en línea y la época dorada de los ciberfórmulas de los años 2000.

📝 RESEÑA EN ESPAÑOL
Cuántas horas habré pasado en un ciber cuando este juego salió antes de Counter Strike, pude volver a rememorar esas partidas jugando con un ruso que me pegó un baile bárbaro, un abrazo si leés esta reseña. Más allá del paso de las décadas y la migración al motor Source, la velocidad endiablada del combate, el icónico Cañón de Tau, los saltos con el arma de gravedad y la búsqueda constante de suministros en el mapa siguen ofreciendo ese multijugador directo, feroz y adictivo que no necesita de pases de batalla ni clases para garantizar diversión instantánea.

✅ Puntos positivos:
• Conexión nostálgica inmediata para quienes vivieron la era dorada de las redes LAN en los cibercafés.
• Jugabilidad frenética, ágil y basada 100% en la puntería, el dominio del mapa y los reflejos puros.
• Servidores que, aunque con comunidades pequeñas, aún permiten encontrar partidas memorables con jugadores de todo el mundo.
❌ Puntos negativos:
• Apartado visual y motor que se sienten sumamente anticuados para los estándares actuales.
• Base de jugadores activa muy reducida, lo que dificulta encontrar partidas pobladas a cualquier hora.
• Curva de dificultad empinada frente a los pocos veteranos que aún dominan los mapas al detalle.

🎯 Conclusión:
Half-Life Deathmatch: Source es un viaje en el tiempo hacia una forma de entender el FPS competitivo donde solo importaban la velocidad, el control del mapa y las risas. Aunque hoy sea un título de nicho con servidores contados, reencontrarse con su caos vertiginoso es un homenaje imbatible a los recuerdos de la era del ciber.
🔸 PUNTUACIÓN FINAL: 7/10

📝 REVIEW IN ENGLISH
🔶 A shot of pure competitive nostalgia that revives the unhinged chaos of classic online multiplayer and the golden era of 2000s LAN cafes.

How many hours must I have spent in an internet cafe when this game came out before Counter-Strike! I was able to reminisce about those matches while playing with a Russian player who completely danced around me—sending a hug your way if you read this review. Decades later and despite the port to the Source engine, the blistering combat speed, the iconic Tau Cannon, gravity gun tricks, and the constant scramble for map pickups still deliver that straightforward, fierce, and addictive multiplayer experience that needs no battle passes or character classes to be insanely fun.

✅ Pros:
• Immediate hit of nostalgia for anyone who experienced the golden age of LAN party internet cafes.
• Fast-paced, frantic gameplay built 100% on raw aim, map control, and reflexes.
• Serves as a time capsule with dedicated server communities where you can still land memorable matches with global players.
❌ Cons:
• Visuals and engine feel severely outdated compared to modern arena shooters.
• Very small active player base, making it tricky to find populated matches at any time of day.
• Steep difficulty curve when matching up against the few remaining die-hard veterans.

🎯 Conclusion:
Half-Life Deathmatch: Source is a time machine back to a time when competitive FPS games were purely about movement speed, map control, and straight-up fun. While it stands today as a niche title with a handful of active servers, jumping back into its dizzying multiplayer chaos remains an unbeatable tribute to LAN cafe memories.
🔸 FINAL SCORE: 7/10

[h2]今までにない新感覚のパズルゲーム！[/h2]
空間をつなぐ「ポータルガン」を使って謎の実験施設からの脱出を目指す、一人称視点のアクションパズルゲームです。2007年という時代を感じるゲームにも関わらず、短時間で濃密な体験ができる不朽の名作でした。

[h3]■ 良かった点[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]ポータルを使ったパズルがとにかく斬新で面白い。[/b] 「入り口と出口をつなぐ」「落下速度を勢いに変えて飛び出す」といった発想の転換が求められるギミックが秀逸で、解けた瞬間の達成感がたまらない。
[*][b]無機質な世界観とブラックユーモアが最高。[/b] 案内役のAI[spoiler]（GLaDOS）[/spoiler] の皮肉たっぷりなセリフや、施設の不穏な雰囲気にどんどん引き込まれる。[spoiler](あとエンディングが神がかってる)[/spoiler]
[*][b]サクッと遊べる濃密なボリューム。[/b] 数時間でクリアできる長さなので、ダレることなく最後まで一気に楽しめた。
[/list]

[h3]■ 気になった点（注意点）[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]3D酔いしやすい人は注意が必要。[/b] 自分は一切酔わなかったものの、ポータルをくぐって上下左右の感覚が一気に切り替わる場面など、かなり酔いやすい画面の動き方をする箇所が多い。普段からFPSや3Dゲームで酔いやすい人は少し気をつけたほうがいいかも。
[/list]

[h3]■ まとめ[/h3]
パズルゲームが好きな人はもちろん、普段あまり一人称視点のゲームを遊ばない人にもぜひ触れてほしい傑作です。クリア後に続編の『Portal 2』へ進むとさらに楽しめます！

Portal is a brilliant example of a game that doesn't need a massive open world, dozens of characters or complicated combat to be memorable.

The entire experience is built around one simple but incredibly clever mechanic: the portal gun. Being able to create two connected portals completely changes how you interact with the environment. What initially seems like a straightforward puzzle quickly turns into a series of creative challenges involving physics, timing and spatial thinking.

One of the strongest aspects of Portal is its level design. Every new test introduces something different, gradually teaching you how to think with portals. The puzzles are satisfying because the solution usually comes from understanding the environment rather than relying on luck.

And then there is GLaDOS. Her sarcastic comments, strange sense of humor and increasingly unsettling personality give the game a unique atmosphere. The storytelling is surprisingly effective despite the relatively small cast of characters.

The game is fairly short, but that works in its favor. There is very little unnecessary content, and almost every room has a purpose.

Portal may be an older title, but its core idea hasn't lost its charm. It's one of those games that every puzzle fan should experience at least once.

Portal Review
Score: 8/10

Portal is a total triumph of game design that completely changed how first-person puzzle games work. It blends incredible dark humor, a surprisingly eerie atmosphere, and genius mechanics into a tight, unforgettable experience that everyone needs to play at least once.

The best thing about Portal is just how clever the design is. The portal gun adds such a unique spin to spatial puzzle-solving, forcing you to use momentum and angle your shots in ways no other game has ever made you do. On top of the brilliant puzzle mechanics, the pitch-black comedic writing and overall vibe are incredible. GLaDOS is easily one of the best, most hilarious, and subtly terrifying villains in video game history, and she carries the story completely on her own.

[h1]Left 4 Dead – Four Survivors, One Nightmare, and a Witch Nobody Should Have Disturbed[/h1]
[b]10/10 – Short, Terrifying, and Absolutely Legendary.[/b]

There was a time when Valve knew exactly how to create unforgettable multiplayer experiences.
No battle passes. No ridiculous cosmetic economy. No unnecessary bullshit.

Just four survivors, a zombie apocalypse and the terrifying realisation that one of your friends was a complete idiot.

[b]Welcome to Left 4 Dead.[/b]

[h2]The Atmosphere Was Everything[/h2]
What made the original Left 4 Dead special wasn't simply shooting zombies.

[b] It was the atmosphere ! [/b]

Abandoned hospitals, dark streets, underground tunnels, empty buildings and the constant feeling that something terrible was waiting around the corner.

The subway sections of No Mercy were genuinely horrifying.
Limited visibility, distant screams and the sound of infected moving somewhere in the darkness.
You never felt completely safe.

And unlike its sequel, the original game maintained that oppressive horror atmosphere almost perfectly.

[b]Left 4 Dead wasn't just a zombie shooter. It was a playable horror movie.[/b]

[h2]Four Survivors Who Actually Mattered[/h2]
Bill, Francis, Louis and Zoey.
Four characters with distinct personalities, memorable dialogue and fantastic chemistry.

Bill was always my favourite part of the group's story.
An experienced veteran trying to keep everyone alive in a world that had completely fallen apart.
Knowing his eventual fate in The Sacrifice makes returning to the original game surprisingly emotional.
Valve managed to make these characters memorable without hours of cinematics or endless exposition.
Sometimes a few well-written conversations are enough.

[h2]The AI Director Was Brilliant[/h2]
The AI Director made every campaign feel unpredictable.
Hordes, special infected and moments of relative peace created a fantastic rhythm.
Even when you knew the maps, you couldn't always predict what would happen next.

And the level design was outstanding.
No Mercy, Death Toll, Dead Air and Blood Harvest remain some of my favourite zombie campaign experiences.

The only real disappointment?
[b]I wanted more of them.[/b]

The original game was relatively short, but almost every moment was memorable.

[h2]The Real Horror Was Playing With Friends[/h2]
Nothing compares to experiencing Left 4 Dead with a group of friends.

We played cooperative campaigns and Versus, where teams alternated between survivors and special infected.
It was absolute chaos.

My friend Honza had a particular talent for disturbing the Witch.
I occasionally adopted a slightly questionable survival strategy:
[b]SET EVERYTHING ON FIRE AND HOPE FOR THE BEST.[/b]

Somehow, we occasionally survived.
And when we didn't?
At least we died laughing.

[h2]Final Verdict – A Masterpiece of Cooperative Horror[/h2]
Left 4 Dead proved that a game didn't need hundreds of hours of progression or endless unlockable content to become legendary.

It needed excellent atmosphere, clever design, memorable characters and friends willing to make catastrophically stupid decisions.

Yes, it was short.

But I'd rather have a short, unforgettable masterpiece than a hundred hours of meaningless grinding.

[b]⭐ 10/10 – One of the greatest cooperative horror games ever made.[/b]

[b]And Honza, for the love of God, LEAVE THE F*CKING WITCH ALONE.[/b]

en resumen juegazo 10/10

Left 4 Dead 1 es un excelente juego de zombies para relajarte, disfrutar y no pensar en nada, solo jugar con amigos en línea.
Es el shooter cooperativo de Valve que salió en 2008, donde juegas con 4 sobrevivientes, Bill, Francis, Louis y Zoey, que tienen que cruzar la ciudad infestada de zombies para llegar a un punto seguro. No es un juego de historia complicada, es de acción pura, avanzar, disparar y sobrevivir.
Lo mejor es pasarte las diferentes campañas con amigos, No Mercy, Death Toll, Dead Air y Blood Harvest. Cada capítulo tiene su ambiente, sus hordas y sus momentos de tensión, y con amigos se vuelve una risa total porque siempre hay alguien que la caga, alguien que corre, y alguien que te tiene que revivir.
Y lo que lo hace icónico son los enemigos especiales. No son solo zombies normales. Te topas con la Witch, que si la molestas te hace pedazos, el Hunter que te salta encima y no te suelta, el Tank que es un monstruo gigante que te avienta escombros, además del Smoker que te jala con su lengua y el Boomer que te vomita y te atrae a toda la horda.
Es un juego perfecto para desconectarte, jugar unas partidas con amigos, reírte y pasar un buen rato sin complicarte.
Un clásico de zombies que nunca aburre. 10/10.

The worst Valve game I've played (not including Artifact because it died before I even tried it). All of the weapons have no impact and feel limp and horrible. Enemies don't respond to what you do in a realistic or fun way and kind of flail about when you smack them or have jerky animations that just look unfinished. The gameplay is jank as hell compared to Half-Life or Counter Strike, and apparently this is because the tick rate of L4D (i.e. how fast the game processes inputs and calculates events in the world) is way lower than other Valve titles. There's only a small handful of levels in this game, all of which are recreated faithfully in Left 4 Dead 2 anyways. And it's a slog to play alone because the game is designed in such a way that you absolutely must rely on your AI teammates because of enemies like Hunters and Smokers, and the AI is braindead a lot of the time.

While I wouldn't really suggest L4D2 for most of the same reasons I list here, at least that game has more things going on (better weapons, way more map variety, more enemy variety, more interactive maps...). This game is just... Like I don't even know how this was considered a full game. When Portal came out, Valve released that as a tie-in bundle with The Orange Box instead of trying to sell it for full price. This game tries to pretend to be a real game, and at launch was selling for full price on multiple platforms, and it just doesn't succeed at reaching that level at all. Just thinking that some people paid $60 (or close to that) twenty years ago to play this on Xbox Live is unreal.

Left 4 dead is the game that defined the baseline for a modern zombie shooter for a reason.
The core gameplay is excellent! The mechanics are simple to understand and it has a good co-op experience for those who want to play it with other people. 
This game has in total 6 campaigns with a total gameplay time of about 8 hours.
When it comes to the graphics after all these years they aged really well as well for the fact that this game runs flawless on modern hardware.
The game has 4 different difficulties and has 2 extra game modes for replayability.
If I were to point out the weakest points of this game... I would say that the game is a bit short, the story being really simple without any cutscenes aside from the one at the game launch and the fact that even though it supports mods it does not have integration with steam workshop unlike its successor. 
As for the strongest points especially comparing it to its successor is the more fitted darker atmosphere, the clean ui and the fact that on this game unlike its successor you can actually see your legs without mods.
I recommend this game, in some ways I find it better than its successor.

2009年11月Valve发行的《求生之路2》，在Steam上拥有82万条评测、"好评如潮"。这个数据本身就是答案——一款十六年前的老游戏，至今仍有五千人同时在线游玩。

优点

AI导演系统是它超越时代的核心。游戏内置的"导演"会根据玩家状态动态调整僵尸刷新、道具分布与特殊感染者出现时机。这意味着同一张地图，每一次游玩的节奏都不同，重玩价值极高。

合作设计堪称教科书。四人分工、互相扶起、共享医疗包，缺一人就难以推进。它不靠脚本演出，而是靠系统压力逼出真实的团队配合——那种"你快走我断后"的临场感，至今少有作品复刻。

内容生态庞大。官方五章战役之外，创意工坊提供了海量MOD：新地图、新角色、新武器、甚至完全颠覆玩法的模组。这也是它能"活"十六年的关键。

手感与氛围。枪械反馈扎实，特殊感染者（猎人、女巫、坦克）设计各具威胁，配合昏暗的南方沼泽与小镇夜景，恐怖感与爽快感平衡得当。

缺点

画面与技术老旧。起源引擎放在今天明显过时，建模、光影、贴图都难言合格，新玩家可能需要适应期。

单人体验割裂。AI队友虽聪明，但无法替代真人，游戏的乐趣有一半在联机。

新手门槛。缺乏引导，特殊感染者机制需要经验积累，初见容易被"猎人"扑倒至死。

结语

《求生之路2》不是最好的僵尸游戏，却可能是最好的"和朋友一起玩"的游戏。它证明了优秀的系统设计可以跨越时间。如果你有几个愿意一起熬夜的朋友，它值得你按下购买键。

Portal 2 is a perfect example of how a relatively simple idea can turn into an unforgettable gaming experience.

The main mechanic is easy to understand: you use a portal gun to create connections between different surfaces and solve puzzles by manipulating space, momentum and physics. However, the game constantly finds new ways to challenge your thinking without making the experience feel unnecessarily complicated.

What really makes Portal 2 stand out is its presentation. The writing is genuinely funny, the characters are memorable, and the conversations between GLaDOS, Wheatley and the player make even the quieter moments entertaining.

The puzzle design is another highlight. New mechanics are introduced gradually, and the game does an excellent job of teaching you through experimentation rather than constantly explaining everything.

There is also a separate cooperative campaign, which is a fantastic addition. Solving puzzles with another player introduces a completely different experience and requires actual communication and coordination.

Even years after release, Portal 2 remains incredibly enjoyable. Its combination of clever puzzles, humor, atmosphere and excellent level design makes it one of the most memorable puzzle games on Steam.

If you haven't played it yet, you're missing out on something special.

An unforgettable classic and a massive sequel to one of the best titles ever in gaming. 

Extremely well designed, the atmosphere and maps are all grand and it makes you realize on how big of a building you are in, you're able to see more than just the test chambers and, yeah, Portal 1 isn't able to make you fathom as much as Portal 2 does about how massive the whole facility really is.

Writing is top-notch, the lore is laid out throughout the entire game through posters, dialogues, prerecorded messages, puzzles, everywhere. Voice actors did an extraordinary job immersing you and making the game feel alive, I love how many voice lines there are.

About the puzzles... they're really awesome, they get harder the more you progress, yet, with enough observation, you never quite feel like you're lost, you're able to get through it all just by yourself. New mechanics are always interesting to see and one of my favourites were the gels, they add more variety to what puzzles you can make and it would've been a pity if the gel concept were scrapped forever. While still on gameplay, the co-op mode? Undoubtedly worth it with friends, it's so damn fun.

Need I say a word about the music? Nothing but praise comes out of my fingers as I am writing this, 'Want You Gone' and 'Still Alive' have cemented themselves as one of the most recognizable, loved, and fitting songs in the history of gaming.

Overall, this series, and especially Portal 2, is a must-play. 10/10.

Alien Swarm (2010) от Valve — это такой изометрический тактический шутер про отряд морпехов, которые отбиваются от инопланетного роя. По духу игра близка к Left 4 Dead: тоже отстреливаешь волны монстров и стараешься выжить. Но есть крутая фишка, которая всё меняет: если в Left 4 Dead ты просто возрождаешься, то в Alien Swarm смерть — окончательная. Для меня это прямо плюс: появляется хардкор и азарт, начинаешь играть аккуратнее и больше полагаться на команду.

В отряде четыре класса, и у каждого своя незаменимая роль: техник взламывает терминалы (а без этого многие миссии не пройти), медик лечит и снимает паразитов, офицер усиливает отряд, а пулемётчик держит плотный огонь. Из‑за этого кооператив тут не просто «весело вместе», а реально обязателен: если кто‑то выпадает, прохождение становится почти невозможным.

Ещё в игре много тактических мелочей: взлом терминалов как отдельная мини‑игра, сварка дверей, турели, датчики движения — всё это заставляет думать и прикрывать друг друга. Атмосфера в духе «Чужих»: научная станция, рои жуков, нехватка ресурсов и постоянное напряжение.

Кампания короткая — 2–3 часа, а с опытной командой можно уложиться и в 30–40 минут. Зато благодаря SDK от Valve сообщество сделало кучу пользовательских кампаний, так что контента хватает.

Для меня Alien Swarm — незаслуженно забытая игра. Очень рекомендую проходить в коопе: так ещё веселее. Моя оценка — 8/10.

Alien Swarm to stara, ale nadal bardzo przyjemna gra od Valve. Jest to darmowy, taktyczny shooter z widokiem z góry, w którym razem z maksymalnie trzema innymi graczami walczymy z hordami obcych. Każdy wybiera swoją klasę i wyposażenie, więc współpraca ma tutaj naprawdę znaczenie.

Największą zaletą jest właśnie gra ze znajomymi. Trzeba pilnować amunicji, pomagać rannym, wykonywać cele misji i uważać, żeby nie przeszkadzać sobie nawzajem. Na wyższych poziomach trudności robi się naprawdę intensywnie.

Gra ma jednak swoje ograniczenia. Jest już dość stara, kampania jest krótka, a po pewnym czasie schemat rozgrywki zaczyna się powtarzać. Solo również nie daje tyle frajdy co wspólna gra.

Dużym plusem jest natomiast to, że jest całkowicie darmowa, więc szczególnie ze znajomymi zdecydowanie warto ją sprawdzić.

Ocena: 7,5/10

Plusy: darmowa, świetny co-op, różne klasy, dużo akcji, prosty i przyjemny gameplay.
Minusy: krótka kampania, powtarzalność, słabsza zabawa solo, grafika mocno się zestarzała.

Najlepiej sprawdza się jako szybka gra ze znajomymi, do której można wrócić od czasu do czasu.

A Tearful Review from an 86-Year-Old Gamer: After Playing Alien Swarm, My Body, Mind, and Every Organ Are Different
Intro

Hello, young gamers. I am 86 years old. On the day my pension came in, my grandson added some money to my Steam account and said, “Grandpa, play this. It’ll prevent dementia.” Well, the dementia is definitely gone now—because I don’t have a brain left to get dementia. The aliens ate it.

1. Physical Changes
1. Hands

I used to shake. Parkinson’s-level shaking. I could pick up a peanut with chopsticks and my hand would blur like a hummingbird. After Alien Swarm, my hands don’t shake anymore. Now I can headshot six aliens in a row while calmly telling my team, “Bugs on the left, throw a fire grenade.”

But there’s a problem: now when I pick up a peanut with chopsticks, I instinctively hit R to reload. Yesterday at dinner I “reloaded” a bowl of rice onto the floor.

2. Eyes

Eighty-six years of life taught me to accept my limits. Alien Swarm taught me that people who accept their limits get eaten by bugs. Now I can spot a medkit versus an ammo box on a screen full of bugs. My eyesight went from “can’t read the TV guide” to sniper-level.

The cost: when I see a cockroach in real life, my first thought is, “How much HP does it have? Headshot or body shot?”

3. Heart

Doctors used to say I had an irregular heartbeat and told me not to get too excited. Now my heart has evolved into an Alien Queen model—four layers of armor and a metronome. Every time a bug swarm shows up, my heart rate goes from 70 to 180 and stops exactly at “one beat away from death.”

The doctor calls it “stress-induced tachycardia.” I call it “professional gamer physiology.”

4. Bladder

This one needs its own section.

At 86, my bladder used to run on a once-an-hour schedule. After Alien Swarm, my bladder learned to hold it until a teammate says, “We’re safe, take a break.” Yesterday I played a 47-minute match and held it until the whole team extracted. When I finally stood up, my legs were numb and I dropped to my knees.

My grandson said, “Grandpa, are you licking your teammates’ boots?”

I said, “Nonsense. I’m paying my respects to the aliens.”

5. Spine

I used to be hunched over, walking like a question mark. Now I have to sit up straight for Alien Swarm—because I need to scan the screen for bugs. After one week, my back doesn’t ache, my lower back doesn’t hurt, and I walk with a breeze.

My neighbor asked if I was taking some miracle supplement. I said, “No. I just get chased by aliens. Run enough and you straighten out.”

6. Ears

At 86, I used to need a hearing aid to hear my grandson call me for dinner. Now my ears have evolved into a sonar system—I can tell exactly which vent an alien is crawling out of, and I can even hear a teammate reload and shout “Cover me!” before they do.

Yesterday I heard the neighbor’s cat meow, and my first reaction was: “We’ve got a lurker in Sector B2. Watch out!”

2. Mental and Emotional Changes
1. My Understanding of Death

At 86, you worry a bit about death. After Alien Swarm, death became a button: “Press space to respawn. Keep going.”

Now when my grandson asks if I’m afraid of dying, I say, “Why? It’s just a cooldown.”

2. My Understanding of Friendship

I used to think friends were people you play chess with, drink tea with, and chat with. Now I think friends are people who run over with a chainsaw when an alien pins you down—and then accidentally saw you in half too.

My grandson asked, “Grandpa, why don’t you play chess with Old Zhang anymore?”

I said, “Zhang is useless. He can’t even use a healing gun. We’re not on the same level.”

3. My Attitude Toward Life

Eighty-six years of life experience told me: be steady, be careful. Alien Swarm taught me: “Steady is useless. Push forward and kill everything.”

Yesterday my grandson saw me sitting at the computer with coffee and asked what I was doing. I said, “Waiting for the next bug wave.”

He said, “Grandpa, you’ve changed.”

I said, “Yep. I used to wait to meet God. Now I wait to kill bugs.”

3. Official Complaints from My Organs
Brain: “Owner, I’m for thinking about life, not calculating alien spawn timers.”

Stomach: “Owner, I’m for digesting food, not cramping every time a bug wave comes.”

Lungs: “Owner, I’m for breathing, not holding my breath while sniping aliens.”

Knees: “Owner, I’m for walking, not sitting in a chair for an hour and then refusing to stand up.”

Tongue: “Owner, I’m for tasting food, not getting bitten bloody while gaming.”

Heart: “Everyone shut up. I’m the one complaining here. I’m beating like this and you don’t hear me?”

4. Final Verdict
After one week of Alien Swarm, my body has gone from an 86-year-old man to an 86-year-old man with an irregular heartbeat, a bladder that makes his legs numb, hands that don’t shake but will reload anything, ears that think every cat is an alien, a mouth that yells “bugs on the left” at the screen, and a grandson who says, “Grandpa, you’ve lost your mind”—but I still think I’m cool.

Score: 10/10

Reason: I’m 86 and I can still fight aliens. What’s your excuse?

P.S. Old Zhang, if you see this, don’t be mad. Tomorrow we’ll team up and I’ll teach you how to use the healing gun. Stop shooting aliens with it. It’s for healing, not shooting.

P.P.S. Grandson, when next month’s pension comes in, buy me the Alien Swarm: Reactive Drop DLC. Grandpa isn’t too old to spend money on games.

P.P.P.S. Aliens, listen up. I’m 86. My hands don’t shake. My eyes don’t blur. My bladder can hold it for 47 minutes. Are you sure you want to fight me?

—Love,
Grandpa Li, 86 years old, still waiting for the bug wave in Sector B2.

UM DOS MELHORES JOGOS COOPS QUE EU JÁ JOGUEI, E AINDA DE GRAÇA!

O JOGO É BASTANTE COMPLICADO E DIFÍCIL ATÉ MESMO NO MODO EASY, UM VERDADEIRO DESAFIO PARA QUEM CURTE. TEM VARIAÇÕES ACEITÁVEIS DE ARMAS E 8 PERSONAGENS COM UM TOTAL DE 4 CLASSES DE ATIRADORES. O JOGO APRESENTA APENAS UMA ÚNICA CAMPANHA DE 7 FASES, MAS JÁ DAR A SENSAÇÃO DE SUFICIENTE E DIVERTIDO (PRA QUEM GOSTA DE DESAFIO ._.). PORÉM, O JOGO TEM MAPAS EXTRAS FEITOS POR FÃS E MONSTROS A MAIS, MAS PRECISA BAIXAR.

PROBLEMA DO JOGO É POR CONTA DELE ESTÁ QUASE MORTO, E PARA JOGÁ-LO, É NECESSÁRIO TER 2 JOGADORES NO MÍNIMO. ENTÃO SE VOCÊ É UM SASUKE GAYMES, SOFRA POR NÃO QUERER SER UM VEGETA PLAY. A GAMEPLAY NECESSITA DE COMUNICAÇÃO, ENTÃO MESMO CAINDO EM SALA GRINGA, É NORMAL ELES CHUTAREM SUA PIKA OU BUSSA PRA FORA, APENAS ACEITE E MANDEM ELES TOMAREM CAFÉ COM LEITE.

O SISTEMA DE LEVEL DO JOGO É MEIO VELHO BROXA. LEVEL MÁX É 27 E É FÁCIL ALCANÇAR, O PROBLEMA É QUE TEM COMO SE PROMOVER GANHANDO UMA MEDALHA DE CARGO MAIOR E DEMOSTRANDO QUE VOCÊ É O BRABO DA PORTARIA. PORÉM, O JOGO RESETA O SEU LEVEL E TODAS AS SUAS ARMAS E ARTEMANHAS, COMO SE VOCÊ FOSSE UM MERO INICIANTE DE NOVO. VOCÊ NÃO GANHA POHA NENHUMA POR SE PROMOVER DE PATENTE, SÓ UMA MEDALHA PRA TIRAR UMA ONDA. AH, AS ARMAS E ARTEMANHAS SÃO LIBERADAS A CADA LEVEL QUE VOCÊ SOBE.

É ISSO. SE INSCREVAM E DEIXA O LIKE.

The first non-Valve game on steam, and a very bizarre game to be given that honor. A fighting game without fight game controls, a goofy idea that lead to a very interesting title. Dragging around your character to fight off bad guys is pretty funny, and while I do enjoy the gameplay, my time was cut short rather quickly. The biggest component of the game, the online mode, doesn't work anymore and even if it did, the game is dead. The only real gameplay option is story mode, which I completed in about an hour. Looking at the title screen, it seems there were plans to expand this game further with updates, but the developer Mark Healey seemed to have abandoned it following the founding of Media Molecule. When this game first released for $14.95, that price for a game in this state would be unacceptable; 21 years later though at a price of $0.99... why not? One dollar for a piece of gaming history isn't bad at all.

Not surprisingly, my current computer's way better than whatever I had back in the day, so I get to experience it in 1080p at a silky-smooth 60FPS. The gameplay is niche and the networking's dated (not sure if anyone even plays the multiplayer anymore), but I mainly grabbed it for nostalgia's sake. Doesn't feel right not to own it. This game is quirky, fun, and one of the games that's been in my library the longest. The controls are a bit difficult to master, but there are few things better than single-session multiplayer on this innovative fighting game with your friends and multiple USB mice. Also, bear in mind that this game was released in 2005 and pay no mind to the haters who bought it in 2011 or later and got mad because it can't measure up to today's stellar indie titles.

Anyone considering getting this game at this point, because the price has come down to 10 bucks... don't. On a functional level, it's not playable. The control scheme is not for most people, and you will cause yourself carpal tunnel syndrome from spinning the mouse in rapid circles while holding a button to charge up. That's if it starts up. And considering it's been abandoned by the creators, there's no bug support if it won't. Beyond the technical issues, the plot and styling of this game is in some of the most poor taste I've ever seen, from fake Chinese speach clearly thought up by white people to blatant homophobia I get the uncomfortable feeling isn't actually joking, it really has all the most reprehensible behavior you'd expect from fratboys. If this crap was done in the guise of joking, it'd be comparable to if a standup comedian delivered a KKK-grade black joke and then spent five minutes yelling "ISN'T THAT FUNNY!?" at an audience that clearly doesn't agree. If you want a game that's playable or has a well-designed, non-offensive story, this one probably isn't for you. If you have no taste, waste ten bucks and see if it even runs for you. For my money, I'd be better off burning 10 bucks for warmth or literally eating it. It was on sale for $2.50 (I believe 90% off at the time) when I got it and I still want my money back.

For the time, it was really good. I enjoy playing it now.
There's something so satisfying about fighting ninjas with comical weapons, kickflying across the dojo, and unlocking everything just by telling the master that you like sticky rice.

Review — Red Orchestra: Ostfront 41-45

Red Orchestra: Ostfront 41-45 é um FPS de Segunda Guerra que aposta numa experiência mais “tática” e crua do que arcade: sua mira, recarga, recuos e até o modo de lidar com armas fazem diferença real. O jogo não tenta te agradar; ele quer que você aprenda e sofra um pouco—e, quando acerta, a sensação é muito recompensadora.

O que funciona muito bem
- Imersão e realismo na jogabilidade: o jogo pune movimentos e “rush” sem planejamento. A arma tem peso, o combate em equipe importa e o tempo de resposta das ações (trocar arma, recarregar, tomar posição) muda o jeito de jogar.
- Combate em escala e clima: as batalhas na linha de frente passam aquela ideia de cerco, avanço e caos controlado. É aquele tipo de partida em que você sente que faz parte de uma unidade.
- Diversidade de papéis e progressão prática: em servidor bem administrado, especializações (e o simples ato de posicionar e observar) elevam sua chance de contribuir de verdade.

Pontos fracos
- Curva de aprendizado e frustração inicial: para quem vem de shooters rápidos, pode parecer “lento demais” ou “duro demais”. Ajustar mira, controle de recuo, cadência e leitura de campo leva tempo.
- Qualidade muito dependente do servidor/comunidade: a experiência pode variar bastante conforme regras, mods e organização do time.
- Acesso/atualização não tão amigável para novos jogadores: é um título que envelheceu como muitos jogos focados em MP—o que ainda pode ser incrível, mas nem sempre é confortável para começar hoje.

Para quem é
- Você vai gostar se curte FPS tático, combate realista, armas com “personalidade” e partidas que dependem mais de posicionamento do que de reflexo.
- Você provavelmente vai achar menos divertido se busca ação arcade, partidas rápidas e aprendizado imediato.

Conclusão
se você quer um FPS de guerra com identidade forte e quer jogar em equipe de forma planejada. Ele recompensa consistência e leitura do campo—e quando o servidor e a equipe estão bons, vira um dos exemplos mais marcantes do gênero.

Nota: 8,5/10.
Trash bots

Gunplay feels really good for its age, runs very well and is insanely cheap on sale. However the bots are stupid beyond repair. They'll walk up right next to you and dismiss you most of the time. It's very slightly bewildering in a sense, but that's because they're made as a filler for when there's not enough players. Fun experience for two or three hours divided in a couple of months, then I dropped this. I do install it again and come back to it rarely, because of a couple of maps. They're fairly well designed and entertaining.
As a small opinion, I can only dream of this very same game but with engaging bots, just like the rest of the series. To me it'd be perfect.

By the way, I feel like I should've disclosed this first.
The game comes with the Darkest Hour: Europe '44-'45 mod and that one has at least a server running all day with real players and a new dollop of content, a nice breath of fresh air. It doesn't have singleplayer, however. Not that it's missing it. I'd highly advise to play that, it's a lot of fun, and I'd even go as far to say that at sale it's nearly unreasonably cheap.

优化贼差 GTX750 1024MB显存 8GB内存玩一半内存泄漏报错  设计及其的垃圾 报错窗口E5800认成奔腾PRO 但是后面识别出了3.2GHz 人机智商堪忧  物理效果垃圾 处处不合理  人物掏枪 举枪贼慢 然后枪械后坐力大到离谱 MP40都快赶上大口径弹药的后座力了 其他的更不用多说 突然鼠标上下不好使 重置设置才好使  或者有时候突然掉到20多帧 卡冒烟了 纯纯的垃圾 都没有2001的重返德军总部兼容性强 甚至德军总部基本没有兼容性问题 T社2005拉的一坨翔  UE2.5魔改到妈都不认识 唯一的作用衬托红色管弦乐队2好玩 给2代铺路 🔫 武器 & 手感设计：离谱到违背基本物理常识
后坐力数值全靠瞎写
MP40 这种冲锋枪，后坐力大到连发上天，堪比现实里 7.62×54R 全威力弹的机枪；波波沙也一样，连射压枪压到你怀疑人生，完全没有二战冲锋枪的可控性。
持枪体力系统畸形
拿一把冲锋枪 / 步枪跑两步就开始大口喘气、视野晃动，现实里二战步兵带几十斤装备都没这么虚，游戏里空着手都累得像刚跑完马拉松。
瞄准动画严重反人类
举枪、瞄准、收枪全是冗余的拖沓动作，近战遭遇战里，你还在做 “慢慢举枪” 的动作，对面已经把你打死了，完全不符合战场逻辑。
枪械伤害判定混乱
有时候打 torso 两枪不死，有时候擦边一枪秒，弹道散布和伤害全看心情，没有任何稳定的手感。
🚜 载具 & 物理：魔幻到离谱的 “二战模拟器”
坦克物理完全反常识
重型坦克（IS-2、虎式）碾不动电线杆、铁丝网，甚至连小土坡都能把坦克托底卡死，履带直接空转打滑。
30 度不到的沙石坡，坦克停住后满油门都能往后溜车，牵引力参数写得跟玩具车一样。
地面摩擦力不区分材质，泥地、冰面、柏油路一个手感，打滑全看脸。
坦克操作手感阴间
转向、加速、制动全是反逻辑的，没有真实坦克的机械延迟感，也没有现代游戏的直观反馈，开起来像在滑旱冰。
载具碰撞判定混乱
步兵撞一下坦克直接穿模，坦克撞障碍物有时候直接穿过去，有时候又像撞了钢板直接停下，判定完全随缘。
🧍 角色 & 人机设计：弱智到让人发笑
AI 人机纯纯智障
敌方步兵只会原地转圈、无脑腰射，不会找掩体、不会绕侧、不会配合，甚至连最基本的索敌逻辑都没有，你蹲在他脸上他都看不见。
角色动作僵硬到诡异
移动、换弹、受伤动作全是木偶式的僵硬动画，没有任何重量感，像个提线木偶在战场上晃悠。
受伤反馈形同虚设
中枪了有时候没任何反馈，有时候直接视角乱抖，完全不知道自己中了几枪、哪里中枪，毫无战场沉浸感。
⚙️ 系统 & BUG：薛定谔的 “能玩就行”
输入设备随机抽风
鼠标上下视角突然锁死、左右灵敏度乱飘、键盘按键失灵，必须重置设置甚至重启游戏才能恢复，纯纯的输入栈溢出 BUG。
帧率薛定谔式暴跌
前一秒还稳 60 帧，后一秒直接掉到 20 帧，没有任何征兆，只有重启游戏才能解决，全是内存泄漏堆出来的锅。
地图加载逻辑脑瘫
远处的地形、模型加载缓慢，有时候甚至加载不出来，直接变成空气墙，走过去直接卡进地图里。
音效系统完全摆烂
枪声、脚步声、爆炸声忽大忽小，有时候完全没声音，有时候又震耳欲聋，3D 定位基本等于没有，全靠瞎猜敌人位置。

Шел 2008 год, в этой игре происходили как слаженные баталии опытных уже экипажей техники и пехоты, так и классический дурдом. Пробегая мимо пулеметчика, который занимал позицию и мог часами держать одно направление-всегда подавали ему патроны. Был большой спрос на игроков, которые могли на своей мышке отсекать одиночным с пулеметов, особенно немецких как МГ-42. По краям карты с флангов гоняли полные маршрутки(БТРы на полугусеничной оси), за стоящими танками устраивали охоту с заездами советские броневички с сапером и его сумкой счастья, а сзади всегда прикрывал пулеметчик в БАшке, так как экипажник мог услышать, выпрыгнуть и тепло принять. Пехота на картах штурма выстраивалась гуськом за средним танком, который прокладывал путь своим непрерывным пулеметным и орудийный огнем, прорывая линию обороны противника на отдельных участках, частенько ценою потери машины и гибели экипажа, однако задача была выполнена и штурмовики врывались в укрепления противника, захватывали точки. Снайпера работали с флангов. В городских боях в коридорах и комнтаха самым страшным был автоматчик с ППШ, если он с опытом и залетит с зажимом, там просто хорони всех. Единственный, кто мог остановить, это занявший под прикрытием пулеметчик прямо на углу. Погони с ПТРД за легкой и средней бронетехникой со стрельбой в уязвимые участки. Были и отчаянные, которые уничтожали тяжелые Тигры и Пантеры. Рикошеты от углов бронирования. Нужно было занимать выгодно позицию к противнику, чтобы увеличить шанс рикошета или непробития.Самый страшный танк на поле боя ИС-2. Это после появились КВ-2, ИСУ-152, КТ и так далее. Интересно было играть на САУ(самоходках), так как частенько действуешь не просто из засады, а самые асы могли бить из-за зарослей вообще не наблюдая визуально в прицел противника, наводясь по биноклю, высунувшись из люка или из-за бронещитка. Присутствовал круиз контроль на технике, можно было сесть в танк, начать движение с базы, пойти, поставить чайник, налить его, вернуться и как ра з уже подъезжать к линии БД. Red Orchestra: Ostfront 41-45, developed and published by Tripwire Interactive, is a unique and unflinchingly realistic World War II first-person shooter that challenges conventional FPS expectations in favor of gritty authenticity and tactical depth. Originally born from a mod for Unreal Tournament 2004, Ostfront 41-45 matured into a full standalone title that centers on the brutal Eastern Front conflict between Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union. Released in 2006, it marked a departure from the Hollywood-style presentation of World War II common at the time, instead opting for immersion grounded in realism, and an unforgiving level of difficulty that demanded teamwork, patience, and situational awareness. Even nearly two decades later, it remains a cult classic and a milestone in tactical multiplayer gaming.

What immediately sets Red Orchestra apart is its uncompromising commitment to realism. Weapons handle with noticeable weight and recoil, and there's no crosshair in the center of your screen—aiming is done through iron sights, and shooting from the hip is both imprecise and often suicidal. Ballistics are modeled with bullet drop, penetration, and real-world damage models. Getting hit in Red Orchestra doesn’t just wound—it incapacitates or kills in one or two shots. There are no regenerating health bars, no arcade-style killstreaks, and no handholding. This results in a steep learning curve that initially frustrates but ultimately rewards players who are willing to adapt and learn the nuances of positioning, timing, and teamwork.

The maps are sprawling, atmospheric, and meticulously crafted to reflect historical locations from battles like Stalingrad, Kursk, and Arad. Urban combat and open-field warfare are both represented, with many maps offering combined arms scenarios—infantry fighting alongside tanks, each with their own roles. Vehicles are not afterthoughts here; they require multiple crew members and demand coordination. Tank combat is fully realized, with interior views, manual reloading, and armor penetration modeled realistically. You can play as a tank commander, gunner, driver, or infantryman, and each role feels essential. The game pushes you to play your part rather than go off on individualistic kill sprees, which is rare in the genre.

Another standout feature is the reliance on communication and coordination. Teamwork is not just encouraged but necessary. Without a solid squad, attacking objectives or holding positions becomes nearly impossible. The command system allows for structured teamwork, with squad leaders and commanders issuing orders and calling in artillery strikes—features that laid the groundwork for later games like Squad and Hell Let Loose. The minimalist HUD and lack of conventional kill confirmations keep you in constant doubt, intensifying the sense of uncertainty and paranoia on the battlefield. Every shot fired could mean survival or instant death, and the stakes always feel high.

Despite its age, Ostfront 41-45 still holds a certain appeal thanks to its solid core mechanics and the unique atmosphere it cultivates. The audio design, while not modern by today’s standards, is raw and impactful. Weapon fire echoes across battlefields, mortars crash down with unsettling force, and the sound of a distant tank’s engine can send chills down your spine. Visually, the game is certainly dated, with blocky character models and lower-resolution textures. However, the art direction and map design compensate by creating believable environments where the historical context shines through. Tripwire’s focus wasn’t on visual flash—it was on crafting a battlefield that felt lived in and lethal.

Community support was crucial to Red Orchestra’s longevity. Mods, custom maps, and organized multiplayer events extended the game's lifespan far beyond what might have been expected. It was never a mainstream hit, but it carved out a dedicated niche of players who appreciated its authenticity. In many ways, the game acted as a blueprint for later hardcore shooters. Titles like Red Orchestra 2, Rising Storm, Post Scriptum, and even Arma owe some design heritage to what Ostfront 41-45 pioneered. It proved that there was a market for military shooters that emphasized historical accuracy and tactical realism over speed and spectacle.

That said, the game isn’t without its flaws. Its accessibility is a major barrier—new players are often thrown into the deep end with little in the way of onboarding or tutorials. The harsh pace and lack of instant gratification make it a tough sell for players more accustomed to fast-paced modern shooters. The AI in offline mode is rudimentary, and the lack of a strong single-player component means its value is almost entirely dependent on active multiplayer communities. While these existed robustly in its prime, finding populated servers today can be hit or miss, though dedicated fan-run servers still keep the game alive in a limited capacity.

Ultimately, Red Orchestra: Ostfront 41-45 is a game for players who crave authenticity and a deeper connection to the historical realities of war. It doesn’t romanticize conflict—it depicts it with a rawness that still stands out in a market crowded with stylized violence and cinematic set-pieces. It's a title that respects its subject matter, demands respect from its players, and delivers a sense of tension and immersion few shooters ever achieve. It may be rough around the edges, but its bold design philosophy and tactical depth ensure that it still deserves recognition as one of the most influential hardcore shooters of its era. For those willing to embrace its challenges, it offers a deeply satisfying and memorable experience that remains unmatched in its genre.

Killing Floor ist ein Paradebeispiel dafür, dass ein Spiel nicht besonders kompliziert sein muss, um verdammt viel Spaß zu machen. Das Prinzip ist schnell erklärt: Mit bis zu sechs Spielern gegen immer größere Wellen von mutierten Kreaturen antreten, irgendwie überleben und am Ende einem völlig überdimensionierten Endgegner gegenüberstehen. Klingt simpel? Ist es auch. Aber genau das funktioniert erstaunlich gut.

Was mir besonders gefällt, ist das Spielgefühl. Die Waffen haben ordentlich Wumms, Treffer fühlen sich befriedigend an und wenn man mit einer Schrotflinte eine ganze Horde auseinanderpflückt, stimmt einfach alles. Dazu kommt das herrlich brutale Trefferfeedback mit abgetrennten Gliedmaßen, Blut und fliegenden Körperteilen. Hier wird nicht zimperlich gearbeitet.

Das Klassensystem sorgt zusätzlich für Langzeitmotivation. Ob Sanitäter, Scharfschütze, Sprengstoffexperte oder Unterstützer: Jede Klasse hat ihre eigenen Stärken und entwickelt sich mit der Zeit weiter. Gerade auf höheren Schwierigkeitsgraden merkt man schnell, dass ein gut abgestimmtes Team deutlich mehr wert ist als sechs Leute, die einfach nur möglichst laut herumballern.

Auch die Atmosphäre verdient Lob. Die düsteren Karten, der passende Soundtrack und die grotesken Gegner schaffen eine ziemlich stimmige Mischung aus Horror und schwarzem Humor. Besonders das Zeitlupensystem ZEDtime ist ein nettes Detail, wenn man dabei zusehen kann, wie eine komplette Gegnergruppe in Zeitlupe zerlegt wird.

Natürlich ist Killing Floor mittlerweile deutlich in die Jahre gekommen. Die Grafik wirkt altbacken, die Animationen sind teilweise etwas steif und die Kartenvielfalt könnte größer sein. Außerdem wiederholt sich das Spielprinzip zwangsläufig irgendwann. Wer eine spannende Geschichte oder abwechslungsreiche Missionen erwartet, ist hier definitiv falsch.

Aber darum geht es auch überhaupt nicht. Killing Floor ist ein ehrlicher Koop-Shooter ohne unnötigen Schnickschnack. Rein ins Gefecht, gemeinsam überleben, Waffen kaufen und die nächste Welle irgendwie überstehen. Und wenn der letzte Mitspieler gerade noch rechtzeitig wiederbelebt wird, während einem bereits die halbe Hölle entgegenkommt, sind das genau die Momente, für die man solche Spiele spielt.

Ein zeitlos unterhaltsamer Klassiker, der besonders mit Freunden seine Stärken ausspielt. Manchmal braucht es eben keine große Geschichte. Man braucht nur genügend Munition und Freunde, die im richtigen Moment nicht weglaufen.

I've over 600 hours on KF2. I know the animations well enough to track the weak spots on zeds, I know the animation cancel times by heart, and the parry window for zed attacks is practically seared into my mind. Playing Killing Floor 1 has made me realize that KF2 has genuinely spoiled me. I went into KF1 thinking all those hours would translate into an easy transition, that my experience would carry me through the waves without much trouble. I couldn't have been more wrong.

I can't even get past wave 5 on Hard.

KF1 is a completely different game almost. Immediately I cant run and it makes me nervous , the combat feels more loud and impactful but this applies for both party's, every mistake has consequences that KF2 has conditioned me to overlook due to perks or new mechanics, this causes me cling to my fundamentals more. In KF2, I can read enemy animations, time my parries, cancel attacks, and reposition myself before a situation gets out of hand. KF1, however, strips away much of that complexity. Combat is more straightforward: you shoot, throw a grenade, or swing a melee weapon, all while desperately trying to maintain control of a situation that grows increasingly chaotic with every passing wave. As stronger Zeds begin to appear, the margin for error shrinks (literally you die very fast in this game), and what initially seems manageable can quickly spiral into a desperate fight for survival. The muscle memory I've developed over 600 hours of KF2 is still there, but much of it feels useless in a game that operates by an entirely different set of rules. It's like I've spent hundreds of hours mastering one language, only to discover that its predecessor speaks an entirely different dialect.

And then there are the Fleshpounds.

exactly what their name entails: hulking, relentless monsters that feel like they're designed to make you regret ever loading into the match. When one starts charging, it doesn't feel like I'm fighting an enemy so much as trying to survive a natural disaster, no running away from it or bracing for a parry. They close the distance with terrifying aggression, hit like a truck, and punish you for every second you spend fumbling through the numbers on your keyboard for a gun that might hurt the damn thing. In KF2, I know how to read them. I know their animations, their noise ques, and the windows I can exploit to deal with them fast an cleanly. But KF1's Fleshpounds make me feel like all that knowledge is worthless. They're relentless, oppressive, and genuinely terrifying when you're already struggling to keep the rest of the wave under control. When I hear that radio static/machine like roar, I start getting nervous, I cant stop checking my back, trying to reload weapons that I've already reloaded.

The Husks are somehow just as infuriating and I love it. Their projectiles seem to come out faster than I'm accustomed to in KF2, leaving me with far less time to react, and they feel slightly more tanky (could be due to them being kinda hard to gib compared to kf2's idk). Instead of being enemies I can comfortably prioritize and eliminate, they become persistent threats that chip away at my health while I'm busy dealing with everything else. You can't afford to ignore them, but trying to focus them down can leave you exposed to the rest of the horde. They force you into these awful situations where every decision feels like the wrong one and its not too rare that I'm stuck sitting at the death screen trying to piece together what I should've done, how I should have done it. they become overwhelming when they work together and do things no longer supported in the 2nd game alongside general mechanics, Zeds pathfind around my grenades?? I un-ADS when I take damage, Clot grabs are outright demented and have taken many of my runs straight from my hands. The stakes just feel higher as well, I'm always having to conserve enough armor and ammunition to survive what's coming next as my coins are almost ALWAYS tight. One bad position, one missed attack, one moment of tunnel vision, and the entire run can fall apart faster than you can properly perceive. 

KF2 taught me to master the flow of combat and that my reads are usually better than my reflex's. KF1 feels like it's constantly trying to break that rhythm, to punish every instinct I've developed over hundreds of hours. I came in expecting to dominate because I knew a piece of the franchise, only to find myself getting humbled before I can even make it through wave 5 on Hard.

KF2 made me feel like a master of the slaughter. KF1 has made me feel like I'm the one that's going to be slaughtered. 11/10 would kill this floor again .

Первый Sin это исключительно история тотального невезения - игре не повезло выйти буквально чуть раньше первой Half life и остаться в ее тени, при этом творение студии Ritual Entertainment как по мне было на голову выше игры от Valve. Вторая часть получившая название SiN Episodes: Emergence мало того что наступила на те же грабли, выпустив продукт на несколько недель раньше Half-Life 2: Episode One, так еще добавила два фактора - новаторский подход к изданию и жадность разработчиков, после чего дальнейшая судьба всей серии игр можно сказать была предрешена.
Геймплейно перед нами все так же шутер от первого лица, игра обзавелась обновленным движком Sourse от все тех же Valve, поэтому многие геймплейные моменты достаточно легко узнаются. Ганплей в игре однозначно стал приятнее по сравнению с первой частью, импакт отличный и самое главное что даже стартовый футуристичный пистолет тут вполне играбелен даже на поздней части игры, но вот количество пушек тут крайне скромное - если не считать гранат, то представлено всего три единицы арсенала (пистолет, дробовик и штурмовая винтовка). Уровни стали более линейными по сравнению с первой частью, моментов, где можно затупить не понимая что делать и куда идти стало значительно меньше. Разработчики на полную используют фишки движка связанные с физикой - думаю фанаты той же первой Half-Life или Star Wars Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast помнят медицинские станции висящие на стенах уровней от которых можно подлечиться, так вот тут есть похожая механика, только если запас целительной смеси заканчивается, то игроку надо вынуть пустую колбу из аппарата, и вставить новую, если конечно удалось найти ее на уровне, так же при наличии такой колбы но отсутствия мед станции можно просто прострелить колбу и полечиться таким образом, но во первых качество такого лечения будет ниже, а во вторых нельзя дозировать расход - колба опустошится до конца и не важно надо это игроку или нет. Так же эту колбу можно использовать как подобие мины против мутантов, прострелив хилку у них под ногами - газ из нее не лечит, а наносит урон подобным типам противников. В отдельные моменты необходимо взять в руки условный ящик и подставить чтобы залезть на ранее недоступный уступ - данные фишки используются редко, поэтому не успевают надоесть и выглядят интересно. Разнообразие противников тоже невелико - несколько видов вооруженных солдат, парочка видов мутантов, турели и летающие дроны, их искусственный интеллект не сказать что выдающийся, но перестреливаться весело. Так же у игры есть адаптивная сложность (нечто похожее было в первых двух частях Max Payne), и если на начальных уровнях особо не отлетать от противников, то ближе к финалу они адаптируются и игра становится по настоящему сложной.
Сюжет повествует нам и продолжающемся противостоянии главного героя Джона Блейда против главы фармацевтической корпорации SinTEK Industries Элексис Синклер. Помимо уже известных персонажей в игре появляется напарница главного героя Джессика Кэннон, но в основном ее присутствие заканчивается в катсценах, в геймплейных моментах появляется всего пару раз. В остальном же говорить что то про персонажей и сюжет не представляется возможным, так как тут всплывает основная проблема, которая к слову является фактором низкого количества разнообразия противников и оружия, о котором я писал выше - игра просто не закончена.
Дело в том, что разработчики из Ritual Entertainment решились в далеком 2006 году на новаторский тип издания игры, а именно эпизодами. Сейчас это уже не кажется таким удивительным, хоть и не получило большого распространения, а тогда подобная манера выпуска игр могла оттолкнуть огромное количество игроков. Ну и как уже думаю стало понятно большинству читающих обзор перед нами только первый эпизод из запланированных 9, отсюда и такая урезанность игры во всех аспектах.  И возможно игра бы смогла пережить эти два фактора, в лице неудачного времени выпуска и новаторской системы распространения, но добила ее банальная жадность создателей - за каждый эпизод хотели полноценную стоимость среднестатистической игры, ну и после этого данная серия была обречена.
По техническому состоянию при этом проект полностью играбелен, лично я встретил всего один баг когда английская озвучка наложилась на русскую локализацию проиграв две дорожки одновременно, было это в самом начале игры и длилось от силы пару секунд. Графика у игры как по мне немного уступает своему главному конкуренту от Valve,  но зато тащит визуальным стилем, опять таки, имхо, Sin всегда превосходила в этом Half Life. У игры приятный саундтрек, а тема из заглавного меню так вообще мгновенно поселилась в моем плейлисте. Из минусов могу отметить странное решение сделать главного героя молчаливым и это при том что в первой части он активно комментировал происходящее в духе того же Дюка Нюкема.
К огромному сожалению продолжения истории мы уже точно никогда не увидим, а жаль, по мне Sin это по настоящему отличная серия шутеров, загубленная сочетанием неудачных факторов и решений и я советую всем поиграть в первую часть и ее продолжение, главное отдавать себе отчет в том, что все таки SiN Episodes: Emergence незавершенная, пусть и хорошая игра.

SiN Episodes: Emergence — небольшой, но весьма интересный проект, который способен увлечь с первых минут. Сюжет постоянно держит в напряжении, а атмосфера старых шутеров напоминает о золотой эпохе жанра.

До сих пор не понимаю, почему игра так и не получила продолжения и в итоге провалилась. Однозначно рекомендую всем любителям классических шутеров — отличный вариант, чтобы провести один вечер.

Оценка: 8/10 (РУС)

Что же, в детстве был диск, прошёл разок и не запомнил, сейчас, спустя 20 лет, прям кайфанул. Движок похоже тот, который Valve использовала для создания Half-Life 2, контры и прочих игр, таже физика, те же приколы. Разрабы прям вдохновлялись Half-Life 2: звуки, анимации, атака, головоломки, секреты, физика - всё так. Как раз в начале года пере проходил Half-Life 2 и сейчас так бальзамом на душу...  Игра короткая, на 2.5 - 3 часа, но любителям движка Source она зайдёт. Был один затуп, где потерял время, это в подвале, где трубы и из одной из них сочиться зелёный газ, там ещё вода "по колено", так вот, нужно идти в конец подвала, где лежит труп мутанта, присесть на корточки, идти в стену, там в воде, под стеной есть проход. 
Из минусов тут - это субтитры, которые вместо букв выдают знаки вопроса и озвучка (полностью на русском языке), но "с направлением слуха", как было модно 25 лет назад, так и сейчас "мода" продолжается: если собеседник, что-то говорит, то нельзя в это время обследовать округу, так как стоит повернуть голову в сторону и слов почти не слышно.

I originally gave this a good review, but I've taken more reflection. The campaign itself is good, but it is only a few hours and the developers have not fixed the issue of the SDK not showing up. Also know that not all aspect ratios are supported. If you're looking for a Half-Life game, I would recommend some of the masterfully crafted HL mods like EZ2 and the Raising The Bar Redux series. There are tons for really good Source games, and most of them are free! Only get this if you reaallly want it and it's on sale. The mechanics are cool, but you don't get too much gameplay. The weapons are a lot stronger compared to Half-Life, so in one or two hits you blow the head off of one of the main grunt enemies. While in HL2 it takes a small barrage of any gun (except the shotgun, crossbow, or rpg) to take a soldier down. I was really looking for combat to match the weight of HL2, while it gets close, it takes it in a different direction.

SiN Episodes: Emergence was released in 2006 as the first episode of this new episodic game. And I have played and replayed this game before, but revisiting it after playing through the original was very odd. For one, this title feels extremely inspired by Half-Life 2, so it features a lot of the same concepts (and runs on Source engine). You get “no cutscenes”, meaning that you almost always experience them from character eyes and usually can move around as they play out, but you cannot progress until they’re done or skip them. You get advanced physics interactions provided by Source engine. The protagonist is almost entirely silent, which really sucks, honestly. And you get a partner, who is clearly inspired by Alyx Vance’s personality.

There is no major non-linearity in this game, unlike the original title, and due to it being just the first Episode, you can easily complete it in under 3 hours. You also get only 3 weapons, all of which now get alternate firing modes. The game did have some interesting ideas to its name, like the fact that it openly used a dynamic difficulty system. Which was notoriously broken on launch, so it would almost immediately skyrocket to highest difficulty and get stuck there. But that has been patched and is no longer the case. And it also has a really cool title song “What’s The World Come To”, though the rest of the soundtrack is less interesting than that of the original game.

Overall, SiN Episodes: Emergence has always felt as a somewhat mediocre start to what could’ve been the next entry in the SiN series. And further Episodes could’ve improved on what was done here and turned the overall project into a memorable one. But it was not to be, no more Episodes were created and as a standalone product, it’s not very good. Especially when compared to the original game.
Nice source game, worth playing.

While i wouln't call this game complete or essential by any stretch of imagenation, just dismissing it as "Half Life 2 with boobs" would do it a injustice (cinematic mod has you covered on that front).
The music is really good, the diverse enemy types like the Jetpack troopers are interesting and while it dont exactly look like CSGO, for being one of the first 3rd party source games it looks pretty impressive.

Unexpectedly after also having tactical mechanics like Aim Down Sights & Shiftwalking, this game also has some of the easiest & best Bhopping i've ever seen in a source game where just chaining jumps (nevermind airstrafing) pulls you away at march 3, way faster than any source game designed to be fast like Fortress Forever or Smashball.

While its always disappointing to see a unfinished game with untapped potential be cancelled (especially when so short), this game didn't really make me sad about missing out on a sequel/DLC as the foundation didn't show that much promise compared to HL2 or even to modern indie titles. Its not bad, but its also not great so what we got was probably as good as it was gonna get.
Same goes with the story and characters. While i didnt find the supporting characters annoying, i also didnt care about them as much as Alyx Vance or Meryl Silverbough due to the lack of time spent with them.

The "insane levels of interaction" is a overexaggeration even by 2004 standards both in terms of tactical utility or immersive simulation. You cant even pour a cup of coffie from the countless coffie makers you encounter, though you can turn on water taps and pull out hankerchiefs so i guess A for effort.
Its about the same level of interactability as Dystopia with ingame touch screens.

Its not a hidden timeless gem but its also not offensively bad. Like i said, its not a must have, but if you are a source collector like i am, go ahead and buy it although in that case do it on a sale as it gets riddiculously cheap on discounts and that price is more representative of its runtime than the normal base price..

Вспоминая начало и середину 2000-х, я сразу вспоминаю проекты, сделанные на Source Engine, которые в то время впечатляли своей механикой и любая игра на этом движке вызывала большой интерес у меня. [b][url=store.steampowered.com/app/1300/SiN_Episodes_Emergence/]SiN Episodes: Emergence[/url][/b] как раз была одной из таких игр. Сделанная на Source 2004, на том движке, на котором были сделаны [url=store.steampowered.com/app/220/HalfLife_2/]Half-Life 2[/url] и [url=store.steampowered.com/app/300/Day_of_Defeat_Source/]Day of Defeat: Source[/url].

Спустя четыре года после событий первой части [url=store.steampowered.com/app/1313/SiN_Gold/]SiN[/url], Джон Блейд вновь противостоит Элексис Синклер. Сюжет разворачивается вокруг экспериментов, могущественных корпораций, мутантов и постоянных перестрелок, игра выглядела как классический фантастический боевик своего времени. Промышленные районы, переулки и интенсивные перестрелки с толпами врагов, что в некоторые моменты выглядело даже чересчур, все это создавало ту самую [u]атмосферу шутеров середины 2000-х[/u]. [b]Система динамической сложности впечатляла[/b], но на максимальной сложности ближе к концу начинался ад. Даже сейчас игра запросто бросит вам вызов, если в начале у вас все было хорошо, то потом играть станет заметно сложнее. Постоянно попадали врагам в голову? Тогда у противников появятся шлемы и более прочная броня, а сами они будут появляться десятками прямо за вашей спиной. При этом графика по тем временам выглядела очень хорошо, физика и взаимодействие с предметами впечатляла.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3774517575
В игре было довольно много знакомых моделей, текстур и элементов из других игр на Source, большинство объектов и части окружения выглядели настолько [u]узнаваемо[/u], что иногда казалось, будто перед вами другая игра от [url=store.steampowered.com/publisher/valve]Valve[/url].
