Shadowgrounds, developed and published by Frozenbyte, is a top-down sci-fi shooter that blends fast-paced combat with a tense, atmospheric setting. Set on the moon Ganymede, the game places players in the role of Wesley Tyler, a maintenance engineer who becomes the unlikely hero tasked with surviving a violent alien outbreak that has overrun a research colony. From the very first moments, the game establishes a sense of isolation and danger, using a combination of claustrophobic environments, dynamic lighting, and relentless alien encounters to immerse players in its world.

The gameplay in Shadowgrounds revolves around intense, tactical combat viewed from a top-down perspective. Players must carefully navigate corridors, rooms, and open spaces while managing ammunition, health, and resources. The arsenal includes standard firearms as well as more specialized weapons, each with distinct characteristics and upgrade paths, giving combat a layer of strategic depth. The game’s flashlight mechanic adds a constant element of tension, as dark areas hide lurking threats and players must balance illumination with vulnerability. Enemy encounters are varied and often overwhelming in numbers, encouraging players to plan their movement, prioritize targets, and make split-second decisions under pressure.

Visually, Shadowgrounds excels in creating a dark and foreboding atmosphere. The industrial, futuristic environments of the colony are richly detailed, from abandoned labs and machinery to dimly lit hallways and cavernous storage areas. The lighting system is particularly effective, casting deep shadows and forcing players to navigate partly blind, heightening the horror and suspense. Alien designs are grotesque and diverse, reinforcing the game’s sense of danger and unpredictability. The art style combines realism with stylized exaggeration, producing an eerie yet visually compelling experience that complements the gameplay.

While the narrative in Shadowgrounds is not its primary focus, it effectively supports the gameplay and enhances immersion. The story unfolds through environmental storytelling, in-game communications, and occasional scripted events, gradually revealing the scale of the alien outbreak and Tyler’s role in combating it. Character development is minimal, keeping the focus on action and survival, but the story’s pacing aligns well with the intensity of the gameplay, providing enough context to maintain engagement without interrupting the flow of combat.

Critically, Shadowgrounds has been praised for its ability to capture the tension and excitement of classic top-down shooters while introducing its own atmospheric flair. Reviewers have highlighted its challenging combat, compelling use of lighting and darkness, and overall immersion. Some criticism has been directed at the potential for repetitive encounters, as the game leans heavily on combat sequences, but many players appreciate the straightforward and satisfying gameplay loop. Its blend of horror, strategy, and action makes it appealing to fans of both shooters and sci-fi adventure games.

In summary, Shadowgrounds is a memorable top-down shooter that effectively combines intense action, strategic gameplay, and a dark, immersive environment. Its mix of weapon variety, tactical combat, and atmospheric design provides a challenging and engaging experience for players. While the narrative is secondary to gameplay, it offers enough context to enrich the world and motivate the player’s progression. For those seeking a shooter that balances tension, action, and suspense, Shadowgrounds remains a compelling and enjoyable title that has aged well within its genre.

Quel plaisir, parfois, de se plonger dans un jeu sans grandes prétentions ! Shadowgrounds est un top-down shooter simple mais redoutablement efficace. L'histoire, très basique, ne restera pas dans les mémoires, mais elle sert correctement un gameplay solide et plaisant.

L'arsenal est honnête : plusieurs armes sont disponibles, chacune proposant deux modes de tir. Graphiquement, le jeu reste agréable à l'œil en 2025 — surtout grâce à une excellente gestion des effets de lumière, qui donnent beaucoup de charme à l'ensemble.

Côté bande-son, en revanche, c'est plus inégal : les musiques sont peu nombreuses et rapidement répétitives. Le doublage est franchement mauvais... mais on sent que c’est partiellement assumé.

Quelques petits défauts viennent toutefois entacher l'expérience : des problèmes de collision assez fréquents et un système de sauvegarde daté (sauvegarde uniquement en fin de niveau, avec des missions qui peuvent durer une trentaine de minutes si on prend son temps).

Malgré tout, Shadowgrounds offre une aventure d'une demi-douzaine d'heures plutôt agréable. Si vous aimez les jeux old-school sans prise de tête, je vous le recommande chaudement !

Shadowgrounds — це ізометричний шутер від фінської студії Frozenbyte, випущений у 2005 році. Гра поєднує в собі елементи survival horror і динамічного екшену, занурюючи гравця в темну, напружену атмосферу колонії, атакованої інопланетянами. Чи витримала ця гра випробування часом? Давайте розберемось.

Сюжет та атмосфера: класика наукової фантастики
Події гри відбуваються на супутнику Юпітера Ґаніметі. Головний герой — технік на ім'я Вес Тейлор, який через збій у роботі генераторів опиняється в центрі хаосу, коли на колонію нападають агресивні прибульці. Історія подається через діалоги та записки, створюючи напругу в дусі Aliens і Doom 3.

Хоча сюжет не відзначається особливою оригінальністю, він виконує свою функцію — занурює гравця в світ, де панують темрява, страх і постійна загроза. Атмосфера підсилюється чудовим освітленням та грою тіней, що робить дослідження локацій ще більш напруженим.

Геймплей: динаміка, вибухи і знищення
Геймплей Shadowgrounds — це класика twin-stick шутерів: гравець керує персонажем зверху та знищує хвилі ворогів різноманітною зброєю. Головна родзинка — система освітлення: ліхтарик допомагає роздивитися ворогів, але водночас робить гравця більш помітним.

Арсенал включає класичні види зброї — від пістолета до гранатомета, а також систему покращень, що додає грі глибини. Гравцеві доведеться обирати, у що вкладати рідкісні апгрейд-поінти, що створює додатковий рівень тактичного планування.

Бойова система добре відполірована, а битви виглядають видовищно завдяки якісному саунд-дизайну та ефектам. Вороги не завжди вражають інтелектом, але їх кількість і агресивність компенсують цей недолік.

Графіка та звук
Попри вік, гра має приємну візуальну стилістику. Освітлення та тіньові ефекти виглядають чудово навіть сьогодні. Локації хоч і не надто різноманітні, але добре передають атмосферу похмурої колонії.

Музика та звуковий супровід заслуговують окремої похвали: напружені мелодії та глухі вибухи підсилюють відчуття небезпеки. Озвучення персонажів трохи дерев’яне, але це не критично для гри такого жанру.

Висновок
Shadowgrounds — це чудовий вибір для любителів old-school екшену. Гра пропонує швидкий, динамічний геймплей, похмуру атмосферу та цікаву систему освітлення. Вона може здатися дещо лінійною і повторюваною, але для свого часу (та навіть сьогодні) це один із найкращих ізометричних шутерів.

✔ Напружена атмосфера
✔ Цікава система освітлення
✘ Відсутність інтелекту в ворогів
✘ Дещо повторюваний геймплей

[h1][b]Shadowgrounds – Nostalgia with a Side of Chaos[/b][/h1]

[b]Game Title:[/b] Shadowgrounds  
[b]Developer/Publisher:[/b] Frozenbyte  
[b]Release Date:[/b] May 8, 2006  
[b]Platforms:[/b] PC  
[b]Genre:[/b] Top-Down Shooter  

[hr][/hr]

[h2][b]Introduction – A Frostpaw’s Perspective[/b][/h2]  
Greetings, my fellow fluff enthusiasts! I am [b]Kiba Snowpaw[/b], Alpha Ice Wolf of the frozen world HowlStrom. With 38 winters of gaming and over 5,000 titles under my fur, I’m here to share my impressions of [b]Shadowgrounds[/b]. This review is based on fuzzy memories of my limited playtime, but I’ll dig deep into the icy archives of my brain to provide an honest and thorough critique.

What struck me about Shadowgrounds was its resemblance to classics like [b]Alien Breed[/b], blending top-down action with survival mechanics. While I didn’t play it as much as I should have, the little time I spent felt like a throwback to simpler yet satisfying gaming days. Let’s dissect this title from snout to tail and see if it deserves a revisit.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2][b]Basic Plot Summary – The Howls in the Dark[/b][/h2]  
Set on Ganymede, one of Jupiter’s moons, Shadowgrounds pits players against hordes of alien creatures. You play as Wesley Tyler, a mechanic turned unlikely hero after a series of catastrophic events. The story involves power outages, alien infestations, and survival against overwhelming odds.  

The narrative isn’t groundbreaking, but it’s serviceable. It exists to frame the action and give you a reason to shoot aliens, which is exactly what you came for. It has that B-movie charm, complete with cheesy dialogue and plot beats you can see coming from a mile away—perfect for those who appreciate campy sci-fi.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2][b]Originality – A Familiar Pawprint[/b][/h2]  
Shadowgrounds doesn’t stray far from its inspirations, echoing games like [b]Alien Breed[/b] and [b]Crusader: No Remorse[/b]. The gameplay focuses on top-down shooting, environmental destruction, and weapon upgrades. While it doesn’t revolutionize the genre, it does polish the formula with fun mechanics and atmospheric design.  

What sets it apart is its use of lighting as a gameplay element. Shadows and darkness play a significant role, forcing you to rely on a flashlight to navigate and reveal hidden threats. It’s a clever touch that adds tension to an otherwise straightforward shooter.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2][b]The Studio – Frozenbyte’s Early Days[/b][/h2]  
Before bringing us the beloved [b]Trine[/b] series, Frozenbyte made their mark with Shadowgrounds. This was their first major title, showcasing their talent for creating atmospheric worlds. Despite its limited budget and occasional rough edges, Shadowgrounds remains a testament to the studio’s potential.  

Frozenbyte’s later successes in environmental storytelling and co-op gameplay can be traced back to the foundations laid here. Shadowgrounds feels like a prototype for the studio’s future brilliance, making it a fascinating piece of gaming history.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2][b]Gameplay Mechanics – Simple, Yet Savage[/b][/h2]  

[b]1. Combat and Controls:[/b]  
The core gameplay revolves around blasting aliens with an array of weapons. The controls are intuitive, with WASD movement and mouse aiming, allowing for smooth, fast-paced action.  
[list]  
[*] [b]Weapon Variety:[/b] From flamethrowers to railguns, the arsenal is diverse and satisfying.  
[*] [b]Upgrades:[/b] Each weapon has upgrade paths that significantly enhance their utility, from increased damage to alternate firing modes.  
[*] [b]Enemy Behavior:[/b] Aliens react differently to weapons and light, adding a layer of strategy to encounters.  
[/list]  

[b]2. Environmental Interaction:[/b]  
One of the game’s strengths is its destructible environments. You can shatter glass, topple furniture, and blow up barrels to your advantage. Combined with dynamic lighting, this creates a sense of immersion that few games of its time achieved.  

[b]3. Difficulty and Progression:[/b]  
The game is challenging but fair, with limited respawns adding tension. However, the lack of mid-level saves can be frustrating, forcing you to restart entire missions if you quit midway.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2][b]Character Development – Aliens vs. Mechanic[/b][/h2]  
The characters in Shadowgrounds are serviceable at best. Wesley Tyler is a gruff, no-nonsense protagonist with a tragic backstory, but his development is minimal. Supporting characters exist mainly to give you objectives or die in dramatic fashion.  

This lack of depth isn’t a dealbreaker, as the game focuses more on action than storytelling. Still, a bit more personality could have elevated the experience.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2][b]Impact and Legacy – A Hidden Gem[/b][/h2]  
Shadowgrounds didn’t make a huge splash upon release, but it has since gained a cult following. Its atmospheric design, fun combat, and unique lighting mechanics make it a standout in the top-down shooter genre. While it may not hold up against modern titles, it’s a worthwhile experience for fans of retro-style games.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2][b]Praise and Critique – Fur and Frost[/b][/h2]  

[b]What I Loved:[/b]

Gumboy: Crazy Adventures is a physics-driven platform game developed and published by CINEMAX, s.r.o. that takes a highly imaginative approach to the genre. Instead of controlling a traditional hero armed with weapons or special attacks, players guide a living ball-shaped creature through a collection of colorful fantasy worlds filled with puzzles, environmental hazards, and momentum-based challenges. The game's greatest strength lies in its willingness to build an entire adventure around movement and transformation mechanics, resulting in a platforming experience that feels remarkably different from many of its contemporaries.

The premise is simple but effective. Players control Gumboy, a cheerful and expressive creature whose journey takes him through a variety of magical environments. Rather than relying on a complex narrative, the game focuses on exploration, collection, and progression through increasingly creative levels. The simplicity of the story allows the gameplay mechanics and artistic presentation to become the primary attractions, which works well given the game's emphasis on experimentation and discovery.

What immediately separates Gumboy: Crazy Adventures from traditional platformers is its movement system. Gumboy behaves according to physics rather than strict platforming rules. He rolls, bounces, accelerates, and reacts to terrain in ways that feel surprisingly natural. Slopes generate momentum, jumps depend on speed and positioning, and environmental factors influence movement throughout every stage. This design choice gives the game a unique identity, as success often depends on understanding how physics affects navigation rather than simply executing precise button presses.

The momentum-based gameplay creates a learning curve that feels rewarding. Early stages introduce players to the fundamentals of movement, gradually teaching them how to use hills, ramps, and obstacles to their advantage. As the game progresses, levels become increasingly elaborate and demand a greater understanding of how Gumboy interacts with the environment. The result is a platformer where mastering movement feels like an accomplishment in itself.

A major source of variety comes from the transformation system. Throughout the adventure, Gumboy acquires different forms that dramatically alter his abilities and physical behavior. Some transformations allow him to float through the air, others enable underwater exploration, while certain forms grant unique interactions with specific environmental elements. These transformations function as both puzzle-solving tools and movement enhancements, constantly introducing fresh gameplay possibilities. The ability to switch between different forms keeps the experience from becoming repetitive and encourages players to approach challenges creatively.

Level design takes full advantage of these mechanics. Each stage introduces new combinations of obstacles, environmental effects, and traversal puzzles that require players to think carefully about how to use their abilities. Rather than simply moving from left to right, players often need to explore, collect objects, manipulate momentum, and solve environmental challenges. This emphasis on experimentation makes progression feel more engaging than many straightforward platformers.

Collectibles play an important role throughout the adventure. Many levels require players to gather items before a portal opens, encouraging thorough exploration of each environment. This objective structure works well because it motivates players to fully engage with the physics systems and search every corner of a stage. The collectible-driven progression also adds replay value, as players can return to improve their performance and uncover missed secrets.

The visual presentation remains one of the game's most memorable qualities. Gumboy: Crazy Adventures embraces a dreamlike aesthetic filled with glowing lights, vibrant colors, and whimsical scenery. Forests, caves, magical landscapes, and fantastical realms are rendered with an artistic style that gives the world a fairy-tale atmosphere. Rather than pursuing realism, the game focuses on creating visually distinctive environments that feel alive with imagination. Even years after its release, the artistic direction remains charming and helps the game stand apart from many other platformers.

Environmental variety contributes significantly to the sense of adventure. Each world introduces new visual themes and gameplay mechanics, ensuring that players are constantly encountering fresh ideas. The game's imaginative locations help maintain interest over its lengthy campaign and create a feeling of traveling through a series of magical storybook settings.

The soundtrack complements the visual design effectively. Atmospheric music and ambient sounds help reinforce the game's whimsical tone while providing a relaxing backdrop for exploration. The audio rarely dominates the experience, instead supporting the environments and enhancing immersion. Together, the visuals and soundtrack create a world that feels inviting and full of wonder.

One of the most impressive aspects of the game is the amount of content available. With dozens of levels spread across multiple themed environments, players receive a substantial adventure packed with challenges and secrets. The steady introduction of new mechanics helps maintain momentum and prevents the game from relying too heavily on any single idea. There is always a new obstacle, transformation, or environmental concept waiting around the corner.

However, the same physics system that makes Gumboy unique can occasionally become frustrating. Precision platforming is not always easy when movement depends heavily on momentum and environmental interaction. Certain sections require repeated attempts, and players may occasionally feel that the character's movement lacks the consistency needed for difficult challenges. These moments can interrupt the otherwise enjoyable flow of exploration and puzzle-solving.

Difficulty can also fluctuate unexpectedly. While many stages are accessible and enjoyable, later sections sometimes demand a level of control that may challenge players who never fully adapt to the physics-based mechanics. The game occasionally prioritizes experimentation over precision, which may not appeal to fans of more traditional platformers.

Despite these shortcomings, Gumboy: Crazy Adventures succeeds because of its creativity and individuality. Few platform games build their entire identity around rolling physics, environmental interaction, and transformation mechanics while maintaining such a strong visual personality. The game consistently demonstrates a willingness to experiment with ideas that many developers would have avoided.

Gumboy: Crazy Adventures remains a charming and inventive platformer that delivers a refreshing alternative to conventional side-scrolling adventures. Its physics-based gameplay, imaginative transformations, beautiful fantasy environments, and extensive level design create an experience filled with personality and originality. While occasional control frustrations and uneven difficulty prevent it from reaching the highest tier of the genre, its creativity and unique mechanics make it a memorable adventure that still deserves attention from fans of unconventional platform games.

Говоря прямо, Gumboy - это посредственная попытка чешских разработчиков сделать играбельный платформер с более-менее реалистичной физикой (в 2006 году такое было модно). У нее ужасно неудобное по сегодняшним меркам управление, которое превращает ее в rage-игру с первых же минут после запуска. Из-за этого буквально каждый уровень оборачивается пыткой в духе Sexy Hiking, или, если желаете, Getting Over It - одно неверное движение может привести к тому, что шарик-главгерой или ускачет в другую часть уровня ("резиновая" форма), или с разгону разобьется о выступ ("водная" форма), или станет совершенно неуправляемым в полете ("воздушная" форма). Избежать этого можно лишь одним способом - стать супер-крутым игроком в Gumboy, который жмет на кнопки с выдержкой идеального тайминга и не совершает ни одной ошибки. В противном случае игроку уготованы острые приступы фрустрации и, как следствие, снос несчастной игры с жесткого диска, а может и вовсе рефанд.

Я совершенно не понимаю, кто в своем уме станет тратить на нее время в 2019 году - естественно, кроме ностальгирующих игроков вроде меня, которые в более-менее юном возрасте застали Gumboy: Crazy Adventures в версии от издательства "Акелла" (так точно, это еще одна "низкобюджетная никому не известная зарубежная игра, в которой переводить пришлось только надписи в меню, которую мы продадим за вполне реальные деньги", как это зачастую бывало у приснопамятной "Акеллы" в середине 2000-х). Когда-то, когда у меня было больше времени и меньше выбора в плане игр, Gumboy действительно подарила мне пару приятных вечеров, окончившихся rage quit'ом, после чего диск на долгие годы отправился собирать пыль куда-то на шкаф, а потом, судя по всему, растворился в воздухе. Сегодня, поддавшись ностальгии, я попробовал сыграть в нее еще раз, и меня хватило на шесть минут в техно-демке движка Gumboy: Crazy Features и еще на пять минут в "полновесной" Gumboy: Crazy Adventures (первая поставляется в комплекте со второй). Честно говоря, понятия не имею, когда я снова ее запущу и насколько меня хватит, но сегодня в такое могут играть только самые отъявленные любители фрустрирующего, неуправляемого, устаревшего, бессмысленного и, судя по всему, ненамеренного (со стороны разработчиков) 2d-хардкора. Как видно из этого обзора, я к ним не отношусь.

Gumboy - Crazy Adventures ist ein niedliches Rätselabenteuer mit Plattformer Elementen das über eine schöne Grafik verfügt bei der vor allem die Partikeleffekte und Lichteffekte herausstechen. Die Musik ist entspannend und passt atmosphärisch gut zum Aussehen der Level. Die Steuerung gestaltet sich je nach angenommener Form teilweise schwierig und teilweise sehr leicht.
Es ist überraschend so viele negative Reviews zu sehen besonders mit Begründungen es wäre langweilig oder das es blöd ist dass man um die Sprungfähigkeit freizuschalten erst ein Power-Up benötigt. Zu diesen Bemerkungen möchte ich angeben  das dieses Spiel zuallererst ein Puzzle ist und es um das lösen der Level durch Erkunden und Nachdenken geht und nicht um schnelle Action wie es für Plattformer meist üblich ist. Des weiteren gibt es kaum ein Level in dem die Sprungfähigkeit wirklich von nöten ist da es eher gilt durch Einsatz der verschiedenen Verwandlungen die Gebiete zu meistern.

Meiner Meinung nach hat das Spiel eine 7/10 verdient dank tollem Leveldesign, teils knackigen Rätseln und einer tollen Grafik. Die Steuerung ist teilweise jedoch wirklich nicht leicht und führt oft zu frustrierenden Momenten was aber bisher das einzige Manko war das ich gefunden habe.

Игра представляет из себя платформер в котором мы управляем смешным зеленым шариком, который может менять свою форму путем подбора различных предметов, он может превратится, в газообразный шарик, морскую звезду и многое другое, причем преображение меняет и управление персонажем и его восприятие физики игры. Вся игра состоит из нескольких миров, в каждом из которых надо совершить свои особенные действия чтобы пройти уровень, например - принести семена древнему дереву, а чтобы их достать придется не раз менять свою форму и крутиться, крутиться и еще раз крутиться. 

[h1]Плюсы:[/h1]
¥ Приятная графика (именно фон и прорисовка локаций, персонажей же рисовали похоже разные люди, т.к. они выглядят не ахти)
¥ Веселая озвучка персонажей (их фирменные мычания понятные любому)
¥ Игра полностью на русском языке.
¥ Сложные и интересные уровни.

[h1]Минусы:[/h1]
¥ Обучение на фоне остальных уровней выполнено довольно халтурно и если бы не прошел его через силу, наврятли увидел бы всю красоту игры.
¥ Некоторыми сущностями очень неудобно управлять.
¥ Нет достижений.

[h1]Итог:[/h1]
Довольно долго пытался себя заставить поиграть в нее и через силу сделал это и не пожалел. Игра затянула уже с первого уровня после обучения и я незаметно для себя ее всю прошел. Рекомендую.

Очень противоречивые впечатления от игры. Gumboy - это платформер, выпущенный в 2006 году. И ряд плюсов в совокупности с солидным возрастом игру в целом оправдывают. Расскажу, пожалуй, подробно.

Главный герой игры - это зеленый шарик (изначально) с eбанутой мимикой. Он способен вращаться по часовой и против часовой стрелки и может делать это с ускорением. Суть игры проста - на довольно крупных уровнях надо собрать определенное количество предметов (ну, по сути очков) и после этого свалить через портал. Иногда собирать ничего не надо. 

Периодически на уровне можно найти спецспособность-расходник (типа короткого прыжка) или модификатор, который превратит главного героя в какой-нибудь подводный куб, летающую звезду и т. д. В таком случае меняется физика передвижения. Вообще, вся особенность геймплея строится именно на ней. Приходится использовать отскоки или сцепление с поверхностью, управляя неуклюжим и инертным персонажем. И это скорее минус, чем плюс, потому что тугое управление довольно быстро начинает вызывать раздражение. В итоге геймплей получился как будто бы оригинальным, но при этом достаточно неудачным.

Графика и звуки вызывают тоже очень противоречивые чувства. Главный герой постоянно издаёт "как бы забавные" звуки. Детям наверное бы понравилось. Мне - индифферентно. При этом окружающее пространство звучит приятно и однозначно хорошо. Графический дизайн в свою очередь выглядит так, словно его делали два человека. Внешний вид главного героя, меню, текст и прочие вещи навевают ассоциации с дешевыми флэш-поделками на коленке, а вот некоторые уровни и вторичные эмбиентовые персонажи словно сбежали из красивой, роскошной и современной Ori and The Blind Forest.

А ещё в игре длиннющее обучение - куча больших уровней, после которых начинается настоящая игра и при этом прилично подскакивает уровень сложности.

Всё выше сказанное, не даёт мне возможности однозначно рекомендовать или не рекомендовать игру. Но за красивые уровни, приятные звуки и геймплей на троечку с крошечным плюсом, поставлю "да". Это был 2006-ой, мы делали игры как могли. :D

Being a collection including three games, it's only fair to review each individually:

RIP - There's not a lot here. The core gameplay is very simplistic, waves of enemies approaching, shoot them to defend yourself. Being stuck in a static turret is pretty limiting, and the only real depth comes from weapon selection. It doesn't take long to complete, but it's not particularly interesting either. There's some enjoyment to be had, but the lack of depth makes it grow repetitive fairly quickly.

RIP 2 - This is a pretty basic top-down, wave-based shooter. While it expands on the first game with free movement, an EXP system, and upgrades, there's still not a lot going on mechanically, and the core gameplay isn't particularly engaging. It can be fun for a little while, but the lack of depth makes it repetitive and it grows boring fairly quickly. Thankfully, it's short enough to beat in an hour or two, so it doesn't overstay its welcome. There are just so many other games that do the same thing better that there's not much reason to play this one.

RIP 3 - This game improves the visuals a bit, adds more weapon variety, and even attempts to build up more of a narrative than the first two games. However, it fails to really build upon or fix any of the issues from the previous entries. The enemy AI is awful, with enemies regularly getting stuck behind walls and unable to find their way to you. The core gameplay still offers very little depth and grows stale quickly, which is only made worse by this entry having more levels and a longer runtime than the first two.

Этот обзор будет дописываться по мере того, как я буду вспоминать игры серии. Проходил я их пару раз и напоминают они мне о Crimsonland, хотя тут есть деление перков для прокачки персонажей на пару уникальных для каждого из трёх героев данной игры - Death, Halloween и Rock-N-Roll.

[b] Что касается первой части RIP [/b] - это максимально простенький прото - Tower Defense, с переходом в аркадные шутеры. Мы по сути сидим в башне и палим по противникам, подбираем разные стволы и бонусы, ну и прокачиваем наших героев. Сами перки у персонажей мне показались немного нелогичными, Хэллуиныч имеет перки к заморозке, а Рок-н-ролл являясь прообразом Сатаны - имеет вампирский навык, как будто хотели вместить в игру всё и сразу. Ещё есть какие-то проблемы с балансом, ибо некоторые оружия вообще не эффективны, особенно на высокой сложности и всего скорее вы всю игру будете выбирать дробовик или пулемёт, если у вас будет возможность их взять. Рекомендую играть на низкой или средней сложности, ибо на высокой враги несправедливо жирные и впитывают урон как губки, а сами наносят термоядерный урон. Но в целом, для нулевых хорошая убивалка времени, которой бы не помешал ремейк под андройд кирпичи. [strike]И пожалуйста, уберите из обсуждений стима спам связанный с Н-шопами, там всё в них. Кто догадался через  community RIP продвигать запрещёнку, тот настоящий психопат...[/strike]
[b] UPD: Удалили, спасибо модерации Steam, работаете оперативно! [/b]

[b] Второй же RIP [/b] - даёт уже тот самый опыт, который от этой серии игр и ожидаешь. Всего скорее, если вы в нулевые застали эту игру, вы играли либо во вторую, либо в третью часть. Я всё-таки запомнил именно третью часть и до неё мы ещё дойдём. А что касается игры, то поправили пушки - теперь они более универсальные и полезные, так что желание подбирать пулемёт или дробовик при первом удобном случае не возникает, для стандартного пистолета-пулемёта вообще добавили возможность подбирать второй и стрелять с двух рук. НЕОЖИДАННО, но доработали управление и теперь есть возможность перезаряжаться (да, в первой части этого тупо нет). Уровней, бонусов и противников стало больше, в общем, стало всё на голову лучше и солиднее (при условии, что перки у персонажей такие же нелогичные, хотя, как я понял, эти фишки ко второй части за персонажами уже закрепились).Но, что меня вводит в ступор, почему при всём разнообразии бонусов, некоторые встречаются единожды за прохождение, как будто авторы сами не были уверены, что эти бонусы отлично вписываются в игровой процесс и вкинули их чисто для "теста". Ещё из минусов, неработающий Rush режим, говорят в  достимовских версиях всё работало хорошо. В этой версии пули проходят сквозь врагов и опыт за убийство (если вам повезёт их убить) не зачисляется, так что в Rush вы не поиграете... Однако, если желание получить лютый "Дат фил" аркадного шутера вас не отпускает, то качайте эту часть, хотя всё познаётся в сравнении и я бы рекомендовал перетерпеть первую часть, что бы ощутить всю прелесть второй части. 
[b] К слову, "читы" которые даются после прохождения игры - у меня не работают при вводе. Если вы, как и я захотите "повеселиться" при повторном прохождении, а у вас также работать не будет, то можете в файле weapon.ini выставить "power" у УЗИ на 500-800 пунктов, после чего, вас сможет остановить только перезарядка (вкачайте перк на количество патронов или поправьте их количество в том же файле и веселитесь). Note : The playtime does not count all 3 games, I put about 15 hours in all 3 games.

The RIP trilogy is a franchise that starts out as a top down tower defense game and evolves to a twin stick shooter in its sequels. This collection includes 200 levels in total which sounds like a lot, but some of them are short and a couple of them are variations of the previous levels. Nevertheless, I think that for 5€ it is a good deal. The third game in particular has a lot to offer.

[h3] RIP 1 [/h3] - Tower defense game where you operate a turret and kill incoming waves of enemies. The levels mostly consist of what seem to be ruins of different types, some are rocky surfaces and other snowy with a few obstacles and explosives. There are 3 different characters which in my opinion only make a minor difference - the turret looks slightly different and when upgrading each hero has their own special ability. The upgrades after leveling up don't do that big of a difference, except the ones that stun or push enemies. There are also weapon pick ups and power ups which are RNG, but some levels will only drop 1 weapon ( because the dev wants you to play with that ) which is kinda annoying. One thing I find kinda weird is that they added dogs in the waves, it could be something else like zombies. No story, the game says that you gotta kill " Pigman's forces " and that's it.

[h3] RIP 2 [/h3] - An improvement from the first game, players can now see their character who is no longer stuck in his turret but can move. In other words RIP 2 is where the game became a twin stick shooter. Still no story but I like the changes they made here. The upgrades have a bigger impact and I like that weapon pick ups carry over to the next mission ( assuming you didn't die ). You can also drop a weapon if you picked it up by accident. New enemies were added as well as boss fights to make things more interesting. The player still has the option to enter a vehicle but only in some missions, they also added tanks and helicopters which is cool. Level design hasn't improved much, it is still the same generic landscapes from the first game. 

By the way, the first two games use the same soundtrack but I don't mind. I like the midi tracks, they have a gothic tone to them.

[h3] RIP 3 [/h3] - A huge improvement from its predecessors and also the first game in the trilogy to have a story. To sum it up - cyborgs invade the earth and conquer it. They also tried to invade a magical world but instead they just created a breech in a portal which allowed monsters to also invade earth. Your mission is to stop the core of all this mess - an AI ( kinda funny because this game is old and nowadays many people hate AI ).

The level design is a major improvement with many new textures too. Some also have animated trees. I like that the levels aren't just some random landscape, our hero has a reason to travel through all the different areas in the game. From labs to deserts, dungeons and rail roads. After finishing a chapter there is a screen with text to explain what happened and the next goal. It's not a cutscene but still better than nothing. New enemies and bosses were added in the game as well as many new weapons and vehicles ( you even get to pilot a space shuttle, how cool is that? ). The skill tree has been re-worked to make it more comprehensible, I like how you can see all the nodes to make better upgrade choices. The game has also NG+ and gives the player 3 bonus weapon options, only 1 can be chosen though. 

The soundtrack is alright, but I would prefer some atmospheric tracks in the style of the previous games. Especially for the levels with ghosts.

A very simple top-down shooter with a noteworthy premise; you control a turret instead of a mobile character and your job is to bombard and gun down the enemies as they all come to you.

The gameplay is simple, yet interesting. There are different weapons, different abilities, and cooldowns that ensure you're not just mindlessly holding the fire button. There's also a leveling choice between "levels" which gives reason to plan for the playthrough.

The presentation is interesting in my opinion. The top-down environments, vehicles (including your turret) look like serious scenes from some PlayStation  1/early PS2 - era game, yet the characters you play as are hand-drawn.

There is a light plot, but I don't really get it. Some pig guy does something some supernatural entities dislike, and they go after him. How they do that in a turret is anyone's guess.

On which note, visually, the star of this game are the playable characters. You can choose three and each has his own abilities. My personal favorite is Halloween; single-handedly these guys - with their art, animation, brief tongue-in-cheek, campy descriptions, and even some unique voice lines - make RIP an interesting thing to see and come back to.

On the cheap I recommend it.

Worth noting is I've only played the first. I have not even beaten it yet, let alone touch 2 or 3 yet. If you have an interest in hole-in-the-wall homebrew computer games, this could be interesting now and again.

The RIP trilogy is definitely a relic of an outdated era of gaming and I'm torn on whether to recommend it. RIP is a series of twin-stick shooters that play like classic flash games. They are not deep, they are not must-play, but they can be fun.

RIP 1 is an interesting one, as its a turret based shooter with no movement. It's a perfectly okay experience for what it is, even if I'd only buy it as part of this trilogy.

RIP 2 adds movement, but is ultimately a mixed bag of balance that I'd recommend skipping. 

But RIP 3 is worth a discounted sale price on its own. It's a good combination of interesting weapons, functional level ups, varied maps, big bosses and vehicle stages to break up the sameness. 

The RIP trilogy is a perfectly fine purchase if you're in the mood for an old school flash-style shooter. But if you're looking for something meatier then you should look elsewhere.

I've written three reviews for this trilogy now, as I've played through the three games.  They get a lot of hate on here, but I don't know why.  Yes, they're a bit... 90s... But RIP1 and 3 are great.. Huge sprites, challenging levels... Think of it as a mobile defense game, or a twin-stick shooter, but with the sprite-drawing power of a proper computer....  The sprites are so large they make me think of the Neo-Geo...

RIP1 is a pretty easy game. It took me an hour or so to complete.  You're a turret somewhere on the screen and things run at you and try to destroy you.    Occasionally a skeleton runs by withe a blue orb you can click or shoot to give a buff or a weapon.  In RIP1 you switch to the new weapon and the old one is discarded, which can be a bit of a shame sometimes.  All in all, I really enjoyed it.   

RIP2 is a mess. Level balance is all over the place, there are glitches and you just have to hack the game to progress. If you don't , you CAN get through, but it's a massive exercise in frustration, even on "normal" difficulty.  I'd skip RIP2, even though it adds more weps and buffs, and allows you to move around instead of being a fixed turret.

RIP3 is a brilliant ending to the trilogy. You can move around, there's a story, there's some really REALLY nice weapons,  the enemies are really varied and the levels (mostly) balance well. It's got a huge amount of variability and some MAAAAHOOOSIVE sprites flying around all over the place.   A seriously solid little game, and good fun to play through.  Took me about 2 hours to finish.


All in all, I'm giving this series a thumbs-up, but that's entirely due to RIP1 and 3.   RIP2 needs some love to be good, but the developer seems to have abandoned the project, and questions remain unanswered in the community hub.

The sounds are repetitive, as is the music, the resolution is low and the gameplay a bit repetitive.  However, for a quick blast of fun, have a go and see how far you get.  Then take a breather, work out a new strategy and try again.

The games DO need some strategy, it's not simply point-and-shoot.  RIP3 especially gives you a few weps to choose from.  One is almost always useless, but the other two you have are usually good to get the job done.

Lots of fun, recommended, especially RIP3.

This is a throwback to the quality of 1990s-era shareware titles - and I'm not talking about Doom, Stargoose, or One Must Fall: 2097. The RIP trilogy is worse even than Jill of the Jungle, The Catacomb Abyss, or the Hugo games - all second-stringers from the golden age of shareware. This is the bottom of the barrel - an eighth-grader's first game project, with all the gore and violence but none of the understanding that comes from an adult's intuition of how to create a compelling player experience. Please, I beg of you - your time is worth far more than this. Avoid it.

RIP 2 is the hardest game that I have ever played (on the hardest difficulty setting). I don't see how it's actually possible to beat it legitimately, I certainly wasn't able to and I have yet to see someone who has. It isn't the whole game that's hard, it's only the tanks. Everything else is relatively easy save for a few levels that are moderately challenging, but many levels with the tanks seem impossible to beat. They have an extreme amount of health and do massive damage per each hit. In fact, a couple levels have turrets you are supposed to get in to fight the tanks. However, the turret takes a few seconds to reload after you enter it, and it is destroyed by the tanks in a couple hits. So what ends up happening is that the turret you just entered ends up getting destroyed before you even get a chance to fire it, or if you get really lucky then just a few seconds after. 

It's an average game (as is RIP 1, which is far easier) that has a ton of artificial difficulty added to it, which is why you should skip this and go play Crimsonland instead which is the same type of game but much better in all aspects. Also if anyone actually managed to beat RIP 2 on the hardest settings with the reaper character without changing the config settings or anything, I am very curious as to how you did that.

Серия аркадных шутеров с видом сверху, в Steam их можно купить только все 3 сразу. Игровое время, указанное на счетчике в этом обзоре, относится только к первой части, на прохождение остальных уходит около 2-3 часов. Теперь по порядку о каждой части.

[b]RIP 1[/b] - очень примитивная аркада, игрок управляет неподвижной турелью и отстреливает прущих со всех сторон врагов. Чистый геймплей, никакого намека на сюжет и прочие сложные вещи - можно выбрать из трех персонажей, но разница между ними минимальная, прокачка строго линейная и их навыки ничем не отличаются друг от друга. Играть можно, как что-то простое чтобы отвлечься от дел на часок сойдет, но игре не хватает глубины и в целом ее можно пропустить.

[b]RIP 2 - Strike Back[/b] - вторая часть сделала неожиданно большой качественный скачок, игровой процесс оригинала был улучшен по всем фронтам. Теперь по уровням можно перемещаться на своих двоих, у персонажей появились уникальные способности, также была добавлена различная техника вроде танков и вертолетов, которые можно захватить и управлять ими. Типов врагов также стало больше, появились промежуточные боссы, уровни стали более изобретательными и разнообразными. В целом играть стало намного веселее, разработчики выдержали отличный баланс между интересностью и сложностью.

[b]RIP 3 - The Last Hero[/b] - в третьей части разработчики попытались продолжить добавлять новые фичи, но, к сожалению, это один из тех случаев, когда слишком много нововведений идут скорее во вред, чем на пользу. Уровней стало больше, декорации стали разнообразнее, появились космические этапы, персонажей стало в два раза больше со своими древами навыков, даже сюжет и тот добавили. Однако в то же время новые типы врагов неинтересные и только раздражают - например появились бессмертные призраки, которые возникают из ниоткуда и двигаются по случайной траектории, столкновение с которыми означает гарантированную смерть. Или танки, стреляющие лазерами, которые при появлении на экране в первую же секунду стреляют по игроку, не давая увернуться от их атаки. Еще сильно не хватает индикации попаданий во врагов, часто бывает непонятно попадаешь ли ты по целям или выстрелы уходят "в молоко". С оружием тоже беда, теперь новые пушки насильно заставляют брать (в предыдущих частях с этим был рандом и можно было бегать с чем угодно), даже если их невозможно использовать и старые экземпляры лучше. Ну и главное - что-то случилось с балансом, игра стала до смешного легкой, бонусы теперь падают пачками и восстанавливаются чуть ли не мгновенно. Из-за этого часто волны врагов тупо заканчиваются, и на экране может ничего не происходить по секунд пять. На некоторых уровнях враги появляются из одних и тех же точек, и тогда игра скатывается в унылую схему "уничтожил волну врагов - подождал 5 секунд - уничтожил следующую, абсолютно идентичную волну врагов - повторил 10 раз, уровень пройден". В общем, что-то разработчики перемудрили, в RIP 3 играть можно, но она заметно хуже чем предыдущая часть.

Если и брать этот сборник, то ради RIP 2 - Strike Back, она довела игровой процесс серии до идеала и в нее просто весело играть. Я бы посоветовал брать его по скидке, но проблема в том, что начиная с 2017 года издатель куда-то испарился и скидок на него больше не давалось, вообще никаких. Если вам вдруг захочется заморачиваться, дешевые ключи активации для Steam можно найти на сторонних сайтах за 5-10 рублей - вот за такую цену RIP - Trilogy стоит того.

I found this game to be unreasonable. The enemy aim and awareness is incredible, and your guns and health are pretty underwhelming. The shotgun is decent, but you have to be so close that the enemies will nail you well before you can get in range. The machine gun is also not bad but feels really lame to use because you don't get enough ammo and have to play perfectly for it to be useful. I'm almost convinced this game was meant to be played with cheats.

This is my main gripe with the game - you have to play pretty much perfectly to be able to make smooth progress. There are so many times even in the first half of the game that I found myself in a tight spot and had to rely on quicksaves to make sure I was making the perfect moves so I could progress. It started to feel like a turn-based game. It isn't fun.

The story is kind of interesting, actually very acceptable for an FPS game, although the main character is not a convincing action hero, he is just a regular guy who is somehow capable of overcoming robots and special forces. 

I think at the price, it's worth going for, if only for the ridiculous intro cutscene and to get absolutely destroyed by the aimbots a few times. I think playing games like this helps contextualize what aspects of gameplay are actually vital for a game to be successful and fun.

Runs well but the story and voice acting are so bad it actually takes away from the game. Gunplay is pretty fun but your damage output feels like you're shooting spitballs, while "Arnie" is made of paper mache and will have you back tracking for meds regularly. Love "retro" FPS games but this one is just kind of unfun. I'd leave this one in 2007.

Alpha Prime is nothing more than a fairly average sci-fi shooter, but what makes it different from similar titles is its difficulty. I decided to play on hard as most FPS games nowadays are not that difficult and was pleasantly surprised when I found myself losing half of my HP to one enemy and almost running out of ammo at various points in the game. The shooting mechanics aren't that bad and it's actually fun to have to use cover and the leaning mechanics to survive; the enemies are very accurate which is redeeming as you're mostly fighting against trained marines and robots that SHOULD realistically be accurate. I didn't even use any of the bullet time as you still die just as quickly if you try to use it to rush or play recklessly. 

Overall I was happy that I finally picked this up after it being in my library for 17 years, and I honestly feel like Alpha Prime is worth full price in 2026.

review:
One of the "typical scifi FPS from 2000's borrowing gameplay features from other successful titles" games that flooded the market after 2000's and kept coming for a while.

If you are looking for something like that, I can recommend this game but only with the fan made patch. With it the game feels complete, without it, the enemies are aimbots and the game doesn't feel that finished, altough it can be still fun.

Game takes place on a mining asteroid where you have to find your (once was?) friend after being asked by your ex. There you have to shoot your way through the game, moving objects with drag & drop, sometimes hack cameras, terminals and other stuff, but almost always just shooting.

You can slow time so the inspiration for this one is clearly FEAR, altough this is NOT a horror game, but a scifi action game.

Also the game can be finished in about 3 hours. For me it took 2x as that because without he fan made patch it was more...challenging...and after patching it up I've started a new game - glad I did.

The dialogues are sometimes cheesy and the dialogue sound quality is strange but this only adds to the "popcorn B movie" feeling.

Yes, the game is far from perfect and you'll se LOTS OF negative reviews talking about perfectly valid points so before playing it, consider them.

And don't forget the fan made Dominus Patch because most of those reviews are based on the non-patched state of the game.

好冷门的游戏，国内当年居然引进过正版。
流程不长，半天能打完，但他的存档位置居然在游戏本体文件夹里，如果你没打完就卸载，存档就没了，我就是打了三小时（游戏进度50%）的档没了，然后又花一个多小时重新打回这个位置。
记得关闭泛光，不然会很光污染。
很多地方看得出来是在模仿《半条命》，开局给个小锤子就很撬棍，但过完教程关就完全没用过了，那它存在的意义是？
和半条命一样可以把物品举起来拿着，也能丢出去（还有力度控制），丢没有什么实际作用，拿倒是可以打开盒子拿补给。
敌人血厚、火力猛、抬枪快还打的准，而主角只能下蹲和抬头，也没有护甲，除了捡血包还可以在和半条命一样的回血站补充，战斗就好像是一群战地6的pro在围剿战地1薯条。
好在玩家可以随时快速存读档，必须靠背板来过关。
比半条命多了子弹时间和黑客的玩法，但都不是很实用，子弹时间不会像《极度恐慌》那样自动恢复，必须捡注射剂补充，而且敌人的子弹哪怕开了子弹时间也躲不开，只能说是辅助射击；
黑客能力也有点浪费了，大部分时间都只能黑进摄像头看一下前面房间的敌人数量和位置，仅有几处可以黑进炮台。
武器不少但有用的不多，大部分时间都在用突击步枪，偶尔拿狙偷袭；
霰弹枪和喷火器必须贴脸输出，你要是像半条命那样安排僵尸之类的近战敌人可能会有点用，结果游戏里全是拿枪的，霰弹枪好歹在小房间开子弹时间用用（伤害不够高），喷火器纯纯垃圾；
火箭筒前面没啥子弹，只能留着关键时候用，最后（也是唯一的）boss战倒是可以爽射火箭。

Alpha Prime, developed by Black Element and published by Bohemia Interactive, is a sci-fi first-person shooter that reflects a transitional moment in the genre—caught between classic corridor shooters and more experimental, system-driven designs. Released in the mid-2000s, it attempts to layer narrative intrigue and light mechanics like hacking and time manipulation onto a traditional FPS foundation. The result is a game that feels ambitious in concept but uneven in how those ideas come together.

The story centers on Arnold Weiss, sent to investigate a mining facility on a distant asteroid where workers have begun exhibiting violent and erratic behavior. The cause is linked to a mysterious substance known as hubbardium, which introduces a psychological and scientific angle to the narrative. The premise is strong, blending corporate exploitation with sci-fi horror undertones, but the delivery is subdued. Much of the story unfolds through radio conversations and scattered environmental details, which creates atmosphere but lacks the cohesion and emotional engagement needed to make the plot truly compelling. It often feels like a backdrop to the action rather than a driving force.

Gameplay follows a linear progression through a series of enclosed environments, with a steady emphasis on combat. At its core, Alpha Prime plays like a traditional shooter, offering a range of weapons and straightforward objectives. Where it tries to stand out is in its additional mechanics. Players can use a hacking tool to interact with the environment, disabling security systems, manipulating cameras, or turning defenses against enemies. There’s also a bullet-time feature that slows down combat, allowing for more precise reactions during intense encounters. These additions provide moments of variety, but they are not deeply integrated into the overall design, often feeling more like occasional tools than essential systems.

Combat itself is functional but frequently frustrating. Weapons have a solid feel, and there is a decent variety, but enemy behavior and balance can undermine the experience. Opponents are often highly accurate and aggressive, leading to encounters that rely more on cautious repetition than dynamic engagement. Instead of encouraging creative use of mechanics, the game often pushes players toward safe, predictable strategies. This can make firefights feel more tedious than thrilling, particularly in later stages where difficulty spikes become more pronounced.

Visually, Alpha Prime was competent for its time, with detailed industrial environments that reinforce the isolated, mechanical setting of the asteroid facility. The use of lighting and confined spaces helps create a tense atmosphere, though the lack of environmental diversity becomes noticeable as the game progresses. Most areas share a similar aesthetic, which can make the experience feel visually repetitive. By modern standards, character models and animations appear dated, but they still serve their purpose within the game’s overall presentation.

Audio design contributes to the atmosphere but is inconsistent in quality. The soundtrack supports the setting with subdued, industrial tones, but voice acting lacks the strength needed to elevate the narrative. Dialogue delivery can feel flat, reducing the impact of story moments that might otherwise have added depth. Combined with occasional technical issues, this inconsistency prevents the audio from fully supporting the game’s intended tone.

The structure is entirely linear, with no multiplayer or significant side content to extend its lifespan. While this keeps the experience focused, it also limits replayability. Once the campaign is complete, there is little incentive to return, as the game does not offer alternative paths or meaningful variation in how levels can be approached. Its relatively short runtime reinforces the sense that it is a contained experience rather than one designed for long-term engagement.

What makes Alpha Prime interesting is not what it fully achieves, but what it attempts. The inclusion of hacking mechanics and time manipulation suggests a desire to move beyond straightforward shooting, hinting at a more layered design that never quite materializes. These ideas add moments of interest, but they lack the depth and integration needed to define the experience as a whole.

In the end, Alpha Prime is a game with clear ambition that struggles to fully realize its potential. It offers a competent core shooter experience supported by a strong setting and a handful of interesting ideas, but it is held back by uneven balance, limited variety, and underdeveloped mechanics. For players interested in older sci-fi shooters or curious about experimental design from that era, it provides a worthwhile, if flawed, experience. For others, it may feel like a title that sits just short of becoming something more memorable.

This is a game annoyingly on the cusp of being so-bad-it's-good, but it's both not bad enough to warrant it and not good enough to be clear of that label.

The story is extremely simple and predictable but also vague and inscrutable. We learn about story events almost exclusively through dialogue between characters, the voice acting is terrible, exposition is dumped on us in "well, as you know, Bob" lines and after spending 8 hours playing through the game and finishing it, I still can't tell you why any of this happened. It's also a game annoyingly full of potential.

The terrible voice acting is most intensely personified in the very-Italian-for-no-clear-reason character of Paulo Bellini. His flat and unenthusiastic delivery COULD have been great - it would have been CL4PTR4P levels of trying-to-be-annoying-to-be-funny, but it would have been WAY better than what we got. Instead of wondering what happened on Alpha Prime you're wondering, why an Italian...?

On the plus side, the combat is pretty serviceable, bar some physics weirdness here and there that causes bugs and inconsistent gameplay. The enemy AI is varied enough that you can't just camp and you can't just go in blasting. However, the enemies seem to be able to begin shooting the millisecond they spot you, making combat encounters frustrating when playing at higher difficulties and forcing you to game the level geometry to find spots where your bullets can reach them but theirs can't reach you.

The default controls are awkward and don't allow for a toggleable crouch, meaning you need to deform your hand to crouch and lean out from a corner while activating bullet time. Oh, did I mention this game has bullet time? Again, it's serviceable, but I have to ask why it was included.

If you were to line up the various elements of this game you would be forgiven for thinking that it was designed as a mash up between Doom 3, F.E.A.R., and Halo: Combat Evolved. And maybe Half-Life due to the inclusion of the slower-than-paint-drying light rail / tram car.

I'll give it bonus points for making me LOL when a rebounding basketball I threw instakilled me at 100% health, and when a forklift bot seemingly out of the path of the tram also instakilled me as it travelled past, but all of the above points AND the absolutely ridiculously easy (aka badly designed) boss fight meant this game was largely a waste of my time.

[h1]Приємна стрільба з усіх пушок[/h1]
Почну з того, заради чого ознайомлюються зі шутером вперший раз. Хтось каже, що стрільба в грі погана, проте я з цим не згоден. Тому що вона тут працює так, як має працювати. Проблема лише в тому, що ви можете не відчувати влучання по ворогам, особливо по силачам та роботам. Гра не розрахована на режим термінатора, і тому до кожної зброї потрібен буде тактичний підхід. Але скажу так, патронів на кожну зброю завжди вистачатиме. А найбезкорисніша зброя в цій грі — вогнемет, бо можливості підійти до ворога в притул, майже ніколи не буде, а поки змінеш зброю, вже мертвим будеш.

[h1]Цікавий та інтригуючий сюжет[/h1]
Гра нас сходу знайомитиме з міською легендою колонії Alpha Prime, про Серце Гломара, який походить з джерела Хабардіум. До кінця гра не пояснює що таке Хабардіум, але стає відомо, що це той матеріал, який міські шахтарі бояться та бажають в одночас. Бо Серце Гломара може виконати бажання. В основному, гравцеві дадуть можливість скористатися Хабардіумом, бо це якийсь наркотик у вигляді щеп. Підібравши таку щепу, у вас буде запас на використання уповільнення часу, але він не відновлюється й не дуже корисний, від куль ухилятися не вийде. Та от коли ви потрапите на Альфа Прайм, ви зустрінете розчленовані тіла й по якійсь причині місцеві робітники проявляють до вас агресію. Стає не відомо, хто навколо розчленовує трупи. Ба більше, один з сюжетних персонажів на початку гри говорить про якихось мутантів, називаючи так людей які збожеволіли. Та що там відбувається, раджу вам самим ознайомитися. На жаль, увесь сюжет розповідається лише в діалогах і в сценах з діалогами — свого роду чеська візуальна новела.

[h1]Різноманітні вороги[/h1]
Ще один з ключевих недоліків грі, це відчуття недоробленості. Та хай так, а різноманітних ворогів буде вистачати. Роботи, солдати, божвевільні й само собою кінцевий бос. Як я казав раніше, кожна зброя корисна за тактичною ситуацією, а тому й до ворогів доведеться підходити більш тактично. Хтось більш живучий, хтось у близі дуже небезпечний, але реагувати в бою доведеться дуже швидко.

[h1]Тактичний підхід до боїв[/h1]
Так, ворогів у грі буде багато, і за рівень ви встигатимете настрілятися сповна, на кожному куточку будуть по кілька ворогів, і завдяки камерам, іноді, перед тим як ви навідаєте наступну кімнату, зможете подивитися місця розташування ворогів, щоб завдяки запасу Хабардіуму, можна було швидко з усіма розправитися. Але от на жаль, чим ближчі ви будете до кінця гри, тим більш лінійними будуть рівні з меншим підходом до тактики. Через що, вороги вже часті будуть зустрічатися вам прямо перед носом.

[h1]Все ще приємна графіка навіть для 2007 року й музика[/h1]
Пригадую, колись уперше пограв у AP з диску Шпиль, там була демка гри. І як тільки я почав гру, тут же в неї закохався, бо мало крутого графону гри, а й музика яка була, мм-мм... Смакота, досі переслуховую музику й тащусь від неї, навіть маю збережений альбом на комп’ютері, час від часу переслуховую. Звичайно, бої більше потребуватимуть від вас тактики, а музика грає така, що «Біжи й Стріляй!» І скажу так, скільки вже перегравав у цю гру, тільки краще розумів як перемагати ворогів. Перший раз буде важко. Та от музика, може бути однією з причин чому захочете повернутися до гри. А от графон, для мене був не принциповий, я не знав на той момент навіть який зараз рік у якому живу. Для мене гра завжди залишалася грою, не залежно від графіки. Та мій комп’ютер не витягував цієї гри. Зараз гра працює шикарно, але в ті часи, думаю гра потерпала від поганої оптимізації, бо з таким графоном уже були в моді Quake 4 та Prey.

[h1]Атмосферна[/h1]
Граючи в цю гру, вам не покажеться, що в грі якась атмосфера жахів, усюди можна знайти розчленовані трупи, кров на поверхнях, і в цілому атмосфера така, що десь за куточками може ховатися якийсь монстр. І так, дійсно гра дуже добре інтригує тим, з чим ми матимемо справу. І до самого кінця, навіть у сюжеті, гравця постійно готують з тим, що він може зустріти, якщо продовжить свій шлях. Та я не буду спойлерити. Скажу, що гра чудово грає на настрій сюжету та атмосфери.

[h1]Гра працює добре, але не варто згортати[/h1]
Я зробив помилку згорнувши гру. І після цього вже не міг нормально пограти, бо гра постійно згорнута навіть після перезапуску, але рішення просте, зайдіть у папку гри й увімкніть «testapp.exe», налаштуйте гру, а потім можете запускати гру як завжди. Але від гріха по далі, краще зайвий раз не згортайте гру.

[h1]Поганий баланс і геймдизайн[/h1]
Я звичайно люблю всім серцем AP, але є речі які навіть через роки мене дратують. Це те, що вороги не нормально влучно по вам стріляють. Гаразд ще роботи, у них міцна рука й можуть контролювати віддачу. Але коли по вам стріляють влучно, навіть звичайні люди, це вже абсурд. Якщо хоча б трішечки буде виглядувати зі щилини ваше тіло, ви отримаєте купу шкоди. Один раз я вже пройшов гру на Важкому, і більше не хочу. Гра навіть на Легкому дуже важка. Ще врахуйте як погано зроблений хідбокс гравця, коли він не може нормально переступити низькі пригради на вигляд 10 см, або сковзає з тупих кутів. Я вже мовчу про те, що уповільнення часу в грі фактично безкорисне, воно не дасть гравцеві переваги, вороги що з ним, що без швидко реагують і починають стріляти по гравцеві. Також, на деяких рівнях іноді не справедливо забагато ворогів. Тож я не просто кажу про тактичний підхід до рівнів. Завжди треба добре готуватися перед штурмом наступної кімнати, переконатися скільки здоров’я й не лікуватися зайвий раз, бо раптом доведеться знову поповнити здоров’я останньою аптечкою в попередній кімнаті. Повірте мені, при першому проходжені, це буде дуже важкий шутер навіть на легкій складності. Та попри поганий баланс, гру реально пройти й грається приємно.

不知为何这个鼠游戏给我后劲有点大，害我赛博养胃，来写一下测评。。准确来说是纯主观个人感想和一点玩后感（repo？），0个客观性，不赞同请划走[strike] 不过这个小众游戏现在还有人看中文测评吗 [/strike]

[h3] 劝退点 [/h3]
主打一个欲扬先抑所以先说劝退点:
1.首先是年代问题，毕竟04年游戏，建模比较古早（不过我还挺喜欢古早建模），主角不能捏脸而且一个比一个丑，战斗手感有点一坨，没有小地图，只有城区公交车/下水道地图（不过这个很沉浸式就是了），更别讲把任务目标标地图上让玩家对着找了，所以有的任务地图让路痴/没仔细看任务要求的人真的很崩溃，而且老游戏攻略比较难找。。。（但是我玩一大半突然发现b站上竟然有视频攻略，之前的苦白吃了）
2.其次是制作组做完本作就暴毙了，因此bug逆天，没有售后补丁（但是有非官方补丁，我似乎下了整合包所以玩着也还好，没什么bug），后期赶工明显，belike好莱坞下水道那个任务是人类可以承受的吗，一堆死路伴随着雷霆大怪还没有额外奖励；唐人街真是我心心念念的第四章（？）吗，别说支线了主线也没多少，鬼人剧情刚出现没多久就没了，这我哪知道能不能信他们啊[strike] 不过别的组织我难道就知道能不能信了吗 [/strike]；最终战堆怪逆天，制作组自己玩了没，感觉是后期做不完了于是小巧思:诶，我只要复制粘贴量变引起质变就能让玩家感觉到有挑战性，这很燃，剧情就可以少写一点了对吧
3.有恐怖元素，毕竟这个建模在这，感觉和我看过的诸多恐怖/猎奇游戏建模都差不多，而且这还是个vtm世界观……具体的话，呃这个算剧透吗我打个码吧，[spoiler] 主要是海洋之家和好莱坞主线很大一部分。。一个闹鬼一个闹丧尸，一点预警也没啊我当时毫不知情地在大晚上点进去，差点没给我吓死 [/spoiler]不过我感觉这个给我带来的恐怖感主要来源于扣血，所以实在不行的话就开一下控制台吧，顺便一提好莱坞下水道也可以开控制台穿墙，收集结局实在不想打最终战了也可以穿墙（又在邪修哦休息一下吧）

[h3] 优点（剧透稍多） [/h3]
酣畅淋漓地骂了一顿终于可以夸了，千言万语汇成一句:求求出个高清加长重制版吧，我什么都会做的✋😭✋vtmb1魂兮归来……vtmb1魂兮归来……

吸血鬼部分:比较反直觉的是能力条（血条）是红色的，生命（死命？）条是蓝色的，虽然游戏UI简陋但这俩条还蛮漂亮，而且挺哥特的……对人类转化为吸血鬼的呈现很微妙，[spoiler] 一开始由选项看出主角还挺兴奋的，后面到了好莱坞昔日好友径直走来，竟认出了早已转化的主角，而为了维护避世诫律主角只能装傻，完全和过去脱离开来……玩到这还挺感慨的，不管愿不愿意，作为凡人的过去已经被抛在身后了…… [/spoiler]

The game's greatest aspect is the aesthetic and voice acting, along with the memorable levels. Here is a taste of the areas you visit while doing missions:
- A spooky mansion where things collapse and fly at you as a poltergeist torments you
- A mad scientist's warped mansion where he tested on lunatics
- A night museum
- A ship at sea carrying an ancient sarcophagus
- A trainyard filled with hooligans
- A complex sewer system leading to the haven of the most monstrous vampire bloodline
- A "doctor"s house who enjoys amputating parts of his patients
- A building made of human flesh/bones
- An italian mafia's stronghold
- Chinese temple

The lore and general style of the game are just really great as well. The combat is fine just not all that interesting overall, but you can barrel through it quickly most of the game anyway. It feels sort of like Deus Ex 1 but with less immersive sim elements. Same sort of night city areas to wander around in and do quests, with interesting individual levels in between.

My only complaints about the game are:
- One or two missions are kind of bullcrap or just designed to annoy you, such as the one where you guard against zombies in the graveyard - it almost instantly respawns zombies as you kill them, making guarding both exits nearly impossible without using a ranged weapon of some kind. I was using a melee build, so this mission's haphazard design really showed.
- Metalhead Industries didn't play any metal music. Why you have to punish metal fans like this?? All the clubs got cool music, and you don't have one for metalheads??
- The jade statue puzzle in the second last mission is stupid. Why would i pay attention to the pedestals i got the statues from when i was being pelted by a million fire arrows from enemies and am encouraged to run like a madman to get them? I guess this is just part of the last two levels in the game which are very rushed.

review: oooooh to be a kindred in early 2000's vampire-run LA....

民汉精翻出了后前来鉴赏一番，我个人在 11.5 Unofficial Patch + 民汉的基础上使用了 n 网的 HD overhaul，全程下来没有明显的 bug，顺利通关。

ImSim + RPG 的完美结合。依托 VtM 的世界观，血族背景本身就展现了一个崭新的吸血鬼视角，颇有都市怪谈的气质：现代的吸血鬼社会是怎么运行的，和大众认知里的吸血鬼族群有什么区别，有哪些不同的派系或者族裔？这些问题都吸引着玩家进入游戏的世界里。游戏里 LA 夜晚也很适合铺展一些怪诞诡谲的阴谋，加之 Source 引擎的支持，让这部作品的沉浸式代入感和互动性都十分出色。
图一圣莫妮卡真的让我有一种梦回 DEHR 的感觉。我花了几乎整整一天在图一漫游，在紧凑精致的地图进行自由的探索，在各个任务的对话中塑造对 VtM 世界的理解，挖掘一些潜藏的故事和秘密。主线支线不论是从叙事性还是任务设计都发挥了饱满的作用，甚至还有一个惊艳的得奖副本；图一结尾一个小秘密的揭晓更是令我印象深刻，总结下来几乎完美的游戏体验。
只可惜这种势头没有一直维持到最后，中后期明显存在赶工的痕迹，支线缩水，很多室内场景变成了服务单一任务的阅后即焚的地图，失去了丰富的互动性。终章堆怪现象十分严重，这对于一个战斗系统设计并不太好的游戏来说，折磨度实在太高了。故事最终也收束到了一个几乎相同的走向，我想象中的政治博弈戏码对应的网状分支并没有上演。
但这不意味着这部作品失去了体验的价值。你可以体会到老一辈写作者构造 RPG 系统的野心，有的氏族几乎能带来完全不同的体验：诺斯费拉图不能正常上街，只依靠下水道系统穿梭开放地图；末卡维几乎重塑了所有文本，以疯疯癫癫却暗含神启的精神状态完成进行所有对话。这种程度的完整差分才让人能切实体会到真正的 role-play，这样下苦功夫的态度用现在的话形容就叫“老一辈坚持手搓”，后继者也鲜有企及。而正如之前说到的，IS + RPG 的化学反应让沉浸感和代入感也到达了一个巅峰，你选择的 role 本身也在潜移默化地影响你解决问题和站队的方式，如此互相影响的代入感也是本作暗藏的优点之一。

半步神作的作品，充满了神作的气质却并不完美，如今仍然值得 IS 和 RPG 爱好者仔细品味。

If you don't want to read this wall of text, I completely get that and here's the short version: VtM:B is a great game and fully deserves its' underrated cult classic status. The rest of this review is me talking about what I did and did not like about it. It is spoiler free except for a couple minor details. This review is also available on my website at nordo7.neocities.org. Check it out and sign my guest book while you're at it.

With that out of the way, let's talk about what this game does well.

Atmosphere. This is by far the game's strongest aspect and is done so exceptionally well that I'd say it alone makes this game worth experiencing, no matter how flawed it may be in other aspects. I think the three main components that make this project feel so unique are the graphics, music, and writing/voice acting. Here's a bit more detail about each of those.

This game looks like a game that came out in 2004: textures are very low resolution, character models are reused across different environments, the animations seen throughout the game are laughably bad, and some areas have entire sections copy-pasted from one room to another. However, I think these things did not at all detract from my experience with the game. The game looks great when it needs to, and even with the graphics' low fidelity, there was never a time when I felt like I was confused about what I'm looking at. Most environments are packed full of small details that make them feel lived in, such as gamer scratch reading 'AWP WHORE' at an internet cafe, or posters for real goth bands at the various clubs. Technical limitations like the reused character models and bad animations are mostly handled in fun and quirky ways, with my favorite example being Officer Chunk at LaCroix's tower being explained to be Chunk's twin brother if you killed him at the art gallery at the beginning of the game.

The music in this game is amazing. It does an excellent job of making you feel like you are in a very cheesy early 2000s vampire movie. The numerous clubs and bars you visit throughout the game are brought to life by these gothic rock/techno tracks and I think the fact that each location has its own one single song that plays on repeat just adds to the charm. Songs like Isolated by Chiasm, Bloodlines by Ministry, or Pound by Aerial 2012 (or 'Pound is Featured in video Game Vampires and Bloodlines' on streaming lol) are now engrained in my head as the themes of The Asylum, Confession, and Glaze. Outside of the licensed tracks, the original songs made by Rik Schaffer are also pretty much all exceptional. A lot of the tracks have this post-rock, silent hill type sound that fits well into the vibe of walking around the city at night. This feels so silly to type out but I have had many genuinely impactful experiences walking around IRL while listening to the Hollywood Main Theme from the game's OST, it is so good at letting my mind wander about whatever it is I'm thinking about while keeping a very pleasant ambiance.

Lastly, I just want to quickly mention the writing and voice acting. I don't want to dwell on it too much because I feel like I don't have much to say that hasn't already been said. It's very good and I honestly can't think of a single example where I felt taken out of the game because of what a character said. Yes, it's sometimes simple and cheesy, but I think that just makes the game world feel more real since not everyone is walking around dropping Disco Elysium level quotes every time they talk. Shoutout to Imalia's quest in the Nosferatu area. I might've almost had a mental breakdown getting through the sewers to that section of the game, but I am thankful I got to experience that newspaper headline. 

--- 
Now let's talk about the bad. Unfortunately, this game is quite janky from a technical perspective. You most likely need to install an unofficial patch to get it to even launch and even with that you will still probably encounter many game-breaking bugs or straight up crashes throughout your playthrough. Some examples of what I experienced include: NPCs freezing up mid-action, spawning into a level with all enemies aggroed on me before I've even taken a step, my character losing the ability to sheathe their weapon, causing all NPCs to run away in fear and locking me out of progressing a quest, and many other small inconveniences. These are all fixed by a reload to the last save but are annoying to deal with regardless, especially if you're not used to quick saving after doing every little thing.

Another complaint I had about this game is that it's not very hard. Outside of a few spikes in difficulty (those Nosferatu sewers'. I have nightmares about that place), you can cheese through almost the entire game with the first gun/spell/weapon you pick up. This is a shame because the game's magic system is actually very fun to use, with spells that let you turn enemies against each other, summon wolves to maul them, or just blow them up into a bloody mist. There is just no reason to unlock those abilities when you can get by with a pistol, knife, and a blood strike spell you get taught in the tutorial of the game. On the topic of weapons, the standard combat in this game is also boring. Melee combat boils down to spamming left click and occasionally holding 'tab' to block attacks (optional in most cases). The gunplay is equally simple and limp. There is a resistance system where certain enemies are more susceptible to certain types of damage but due to the difficulty problems mentioned above, I never really thought about it outside of a few encounters where an enemy is completely invulnerable to specific types of damage. Stealth is also a joke. I leveled my sneaking to level 4 about 2 hours into the game and was able to breeze through almost every section in the game after that with absolutely no issues. There were multiple points where I crouched past an enemy while literally rubbing up against them and they still didn't see me.

This is next point is kind of a nit-pick, but I really wish there was a minigame tied to hacking or lockpicking that got easier as you leveled those skills up. As it stands, you simply interact with the object and watch an animation play out, hoping that your skill level is high enough to unlock a door/hack a computer. I think it'd be way more engaging to have some sort of skill expression system here. It could be something as simple as Skyrim's lockpicking or system shock's hacking minigames. That way, even if your character doesn't explicitly meet the level requirement to unlock a door, there's still a chance they get it by a combination of luck and skill, creating more fun stories for the player. 

---
TL;DR although this game is rough around the edges, I think there is enough charm and passion here to still make it worth experiencing, even 20+ years after its release date.

[h1]Кривая легенда[/h1]
Начну с того, что фанаты не просто так до сих пор заботливо поддерживают жизнь в этой игре, постоянно патча её и добавляя новый контент. И уж поверьте, она этого заслуживает.
Это одна из тех игр, которая дарит действительно крутую и уникальную атмосферу. Вечно дождливая Санта-Моника, ночной пляж с кучкой бездельников, Асайлум набитый готами и панками, особняк с приведениями, стрип-клубы, Голливуд, Чайнатаун... Причём все эти колоритные места дополнены деталями и NPC, создающими ощущение живого мира: санитары в больнице барыжат кровью, копы на пирсе обсуждают разорванный труп, на радио крутят передачу "Ночи с Деб" куда даже звонят сюжетные персонажи, а по телеку и в газетах освящают твои "подвиги".
Дополняет всё это шикарный саундтрек - как оригинальные, так и лицензированные треки.
Сами вампиры показаны свежо (не смотря на дату релиза), это не готические воздуханы из кино, а абсолютно разные по характерам, убеждениям и стилю кланы. Тут есть свои карьеристы, панки, изгои, а клановые дисциплины меняют геймплей.
Персонажи тут потрясающие, у каждого свои мотивы, логика и харизма. Даже распоследние ублюдки вроде ЛаКруа развлекают своим нарциссизмом и синдромом жертвы.
Сюжет спойлерить не буду, скажу лишь, что это было хорошее приключение, а финал заставил посмотреть на всё происходящее под другим углом и посмеяться.

🧛‍♂️ Vampire: The Masquerade – Bloodlines (2004) Review 🎮

As a speedrunner, I have to admit that a lot of this game can be skipped once you know the objectives. 😅 I barely had to fight in many sections because, most of the time, I could simply run past enemies and focus on getting where I needed to go. The only time I really felt the need to fight was during the final sections.

The gameplay is actually pretty fun, but there are so many things you can skip or bypass once you understand how the game works. For a speedrunner, that makes the experience even more interesting. 🏃‍♂️💨

The story is good, although I wouldn't say it's amazing. That said, the final plot twist is pretty great and definitely left a strong impression. 👀 The roles and personalities of the characters are also really well done, and each character feels like they have a purpose within the story.

One thing I really appreciate is that the story doesn't drag on too much. It keeps moving forward without becoming overly complicated or unnecessarily long.

Overall, I'd give Vampire: The Masquerade – Bloodlines an 8/10. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

A really enjoyable RPG with a good story, memorable characters, and plenty of opportunities to break the game if you know what you're doing. For a speedrunner, that's definitely a big plus. 😎🧛‍♂️💨

This game is both horrifically overrated and has aged terribly. It's extremely buggy - expect technical issues even with the patch (e.g. infinitely respawning enemies if they die out of eyesight, seemingly hardcoded loading times that make you wait even on modern hardware).

NPCs will body block you, with the community solution to it being "use noclip", you'll get permanently stuck on broken physics objects, doors will continuously open-and-close into your face, quest items on the ground will disappear, etc. etc.

If this game was just hubs and quests inside of them, it could've been great RPG - unfortunately, it's not. 80%+ of this game consists of horrible combat dungeons, and the combat in this game is [i]awful[/i]. Extremely inaccurate guns that struggle to kill even humans, despite the game stating that only vampires are meant to be resistant to them, and janky third-person-only melee that will either knock back your opponent too far repeatedly or send you swinging straight passed them, making it especially tedious.

If you foolishly made a character that didn't heavily specialize in combat, you only have one option - restart the game. Unfortunately, this lesson comes after multiple hours comes into the game and the back-to-back combat dungeons begin. 

Script-wise, the game is a mixed bag. Excellent voice-acting makes an otherwise mediocre script come off well - until you start encountering the cringy "I'm in my first year of university and I think George Carlin is really funny!" characters (i.e. Beckett, who is a character that will get several monologues about how he's a 300 year old big fan of "Science!" and doesn't believe in the established vampire lore which is canonical to the entire series), at which point the the voice-acting can no longer outweigh how outdated the writing is.

If you decide to try this game regardless, make sure to get the unofficial patch, or it's likely that you won't even be able to play the game in the first place.
