[h1]Pionero en su clase[/h1]
Hoy en día no existe un mejor juego del Salvaje Oeste que Red Dead Redemption 2, y probablemente el segundo mejor sea el Red Dead Redemption original. Hay más juegos basados en el Salvaje Oeste que son bastante meritorios también y tocan géneros diferentes como la estrategia, el rol por turnos, los FPS o incluso juegos de póquer, entre otros, aunque no suelen ser muy numerosos tampoco los que salen con esta temática.

Sin embargo, los dos más famosos son los basados en el género de acción sandbox, por razones obvias porque son realmente buenos. Dicho esto, no es improbable o descabellado pensar que muy probablemente sin la existencia de Gun es posible que Red Dead Redemption nunca hubiera visto la luz tal y como lo hizo, o al menos, por decirlo de otro modo, Gun fue el primer juego de acción sandbox sobre el Salvaje Oeste que salió al mercado, de hecho ostenta el Récord Guinness en ese aspecto, y tanto es así que se acuñó la frase de “Gun caminó para que Red Dead Redemption pudiera correr”, aunque Rockstar nunca ha admitido que se basara en nada de lo que Gun introdujo, molan demasiado para ser humildes, es obvio que con posterioridad su juego de 2010 utilizó muchas características que Gun ya había implementado por primera vez en el mundo de los videojuegos antes que nadie con esa ambientación. Hay que tener en cuenta que Gun es un título de 2005, cinco años antes de que saliera el primer Red Dead Redemption de Rockstar.

Obviamente, los dos Red Dead Redemption son mucho mejores que Gun, pero es sorprendente lo revolucionario que fue en su momento por todo lo que incluía y lo mucho que podía sorprenderte con las diferentes situaciones que te presentaba.

[h1]Una auténtica historia de vaqueros[/h1]
En el juego tomaremos el papel de Colton White, un hombre que ha vivido toda su vida en las montañas cazando búfalos junto a su padre y sacando dinero con la venta de las pieles y la carne, además de ser bastante conocedor del mundo indio que puebla esa zona.

En una de sus partidas de caza, la cual funciona a modo de tutorial, acaban montándose en un barco a vapor y todo empezará a ponerse algo extraño, hasta tal punto de que el barco sufre un asalto y dará como resultado que Colton inicie su periplo buscando respuestas y venganza en una trama bastante interesante y bien elaborada. No es que sea la historia del siglo, pero se nota que quien creó el guion sabía lo que hacía, ya que de hecho fue Randall Jahnson, guionista de películas como The Doors o La Máscara del Zorro, quien creó la historia, y se nota bastante porque los planos de ciertas cinemáticas y ciertas conversaciones tienen una calidad superior a la media, sin ser tampoco ninguna locura.

Sea como sea, Gun tiene una historia bastante interesante y, lo más importante, es una historia que se siente como salida directamente del cine del Oeste de toda la vida. Simple en su forma, elaborada en sus matices y bastante entretenida en términos generales.

[h1]Pues sí, es un sandbox[/h1]
Yo ya había jugado a Gun cuando salió al mercado en su día, pero nunca lo jugué más allá de un par de horas por lo que me sorprendió bastante descubrir al jugarlo ahora en Steam que el juego es realmente un sandbox. Sí, es un sandbox de 2005, lo cual quiere decir que no tiene un mapa gigantesco tipo RDR 2 ni nada parecido, pero no es un mapa pequeño por otro lado.

Además, para que veas las muchas cosas en las que probablemente Red Dead Redemption pudo inspirarse de Gun, nuestro protagonista no solo tendrá una misión principal que cumplir, sino que podrás pasearte por diferentes poblaciones realizando misiones o actividades secundarias, como por ejemplo ayudar a los sheriffs a dar caza a bandidos cuyos carteles de “Se Busca” estarán pegados en las paredes, realizar envíos rápidos trabajando para el Pony Express viajando de una ubicación a otra dentro del límite de tiempo indicado cruzando terrenos bastante extensos, mejorar las habilidades del personaje y su armamento, jugar al póquer en los salones de los bares o hablar con diferentes personas para que nos den misiones si queremos ayudarles, como ayudar en una granja guiando ganado, protegiendo el lugar de asaltos o saliendo a cazar. Es decir, una auténtica revolución para la época, ya que por aquel entonces lo juegos del Salvaje Oeste salidos con anterioridad, como Red Dead Revolver, también de Rockstar, eran lineales y de acción con niveles cerrados, cosa que Gun no es.

Hoy en día puede parecer muy normal, gracias a Red Dead Redemption y llevado a la máxima excelencia posible en Red Dead Redemption 2, montarte en tu caballo y salir a explorar libremente por el mero placer de hacerlo, cruzar el desierto, defenderte del asalto de bandidos que te salen al paso o disfrutar de una puesta de sol montado en tu caballo mientras observabas el paso del día a la noche. Una auténtica revolución para la época, que hoy en día sigue siendo muy disfrutable, aunque con sus limitaciones si lo comparamos con los dos RDR de Rockstar salidos con posterioridad, especialmente con el segundo, obviamente. Aunque particularmente la historia de Gun me parece más trabajada, sinceramente, ya que mezcla a indios, vaqueros, chinos y los primeros conquistadores españoles en un batiburrillo bastante interesante y bien hilado. Pero bueno, eso ya es cuestión de gustos.

En el apartado de combate, también incluyó algo muy novedoso que Red Dead Redemption utilizó con posterioridad, el cual era utilizar una especie de “tiempo bala” en el que se ralentizaba el tiempo para poder apuntar y marcar a múltiples objetivos y ejecutar el ataque rápidamente con posterioridad, algo que calcó Rockstar luego para sus juegos.

[h1]Poniéndolo al día[/h1]
Dado el tiempo que hace que salió el título al mercado, 2005, el juego por defecto no acepta resoluciones UHD y además la versión de Steam no incluye el idioma español que sí salió al mercado de manera oficial. Sin embargo, si sigues el enlace arriba indicado podrás ponerlo con subtítulos en español, los oficiales, y además mediante un mod hacer que soporte resoluciones UHD, como 4K, sin estirar la imagen o deformarla, lo cual es un puntazo, ya que siempre existió un modo para cambiar la resolución, pero deformaba a los personajes al estirar horizontalmente la pantalla, con este mod no pasa y todo se ve de maravilla. Obviamente las texturas son las que son, pero te aseguro que una vez metido en faena te va a dar igual la calidad gráfica porque el juego es realmente entretenido y está lleno de acción con una historia interesante.

[h1]Conclusiones[/h1]
En definitiva, Gun es un juego que fue pionero en ofrecer una ambientación del Salvaje Oeste con una jugabilidad estilo sandbox, y lo hizo realmente bien. A día de hoy sigue siendo bastante entretenido y si ya has acabado los RDR y quieres volver atrás, a los orígenes del Salvaje Oeste con el primer sandbox que salió al mercado de este estilo, a buen seguro te acabará encantando siempre que no entres en comparaciones absurdas que no tienen ningún sentido. Los dos RDR que salieron con posterioridad a Gun son muchísimo mejores, pero una cosa no quita la otra. Así que, si te gustan las buenas historias del Salvaje Oeste, es muy recomendable para todo vaquero que se precie. :)

Contrary to what some commentators have said, the controller support works just fine. You just have to assign the controls yourself. I'm using an 8Bit wireless controller with the dongle and it works as expected. 

The controls on OG XBOX were:

- Y to Quickdraw
- X to use melee weapon
- A to jump
- B to crouch and roll (while using left stick)

- Left stick to move (no need to assign Walk)
- Right stick to pan
- DPad up to draw weapon
- DPad down to holster weapon
- DPad left to lean left
- DPad right to lean right

- Left trigger to throw molotovs and dynamine
- Right trigger to shoot

The 8Bit controller lacks some of the keys my old Xbox controller had, so I've mapped some keys of my own. Feel free to map these to whatever buttons your controller has.

- Left shoulder for drawing shotgun/bow
- Right shoulder to interact 
Right stick for drawing rifle (used to be Zoom for rifle)
- 8Bit keys for switching between two chosen weapons (rifle/revoler; shotgun/revolver, etc).
- 8Bit keys for drinking from the flask

GOTY
O red dead redemption que tinhamos no ps2, muito bom, até os dias de hoje nao perdeu a graça, bem nostalgico.

Protože se moje recenze začínají spíše stávat informací že jsem nezemřel než-li pravidelnou činností, rozhodl jsem se probrat z celoživotního kómatu a dovolit hrám opět průchod do svého šedivého života všedních dní. Čas, který mi trval k tomu, abych se opět ponořil do hlubin videoher a konečně se odloučil od nesnesitelného tlaku bytím, byl dokonce tak dlouhý, že jsem tuhle gamesu kupoval ještě v době kdy můj počítač dokázal v zimním období kompletně vytopit můj pokoj jen co jsem zapl malování. A proto jsem se rozhodl že je nevyšší čas oprášit klobouk a vzhůru do sedla.

GUN je počin, který minimálně tady u nás nemá úplně silné zastoupení a celosvětově podle mě nebudu také daleko od pravdy. Působí to jako takový ten typický zapomenutý titul, na který pak náhodně narazíte na Youtube jak ho tam nějaký máslo vynáší do oblak a říká tomu "hidden gem". Já bych tak optimistický zase nebyl, ale v průběhu mého sáhodlouhého vylívání pocitů a přihlouplých názorů dojdu i k tomu, proč by měli tito staříčci od Vás dostat šanci. Jak už jsem říkal, GUN jsem si kupoval kdy můj kompjůtr neoplýval zázračnou mocí rozjet Red Dead Redemtion 2 a protože Red Dead Redemption na PC (na steamu) bylo ještě v nedohlednu, při procházení obchodu jsem zakopl právě o tento zmiňovaný western a řekl jsem si, že na svátky vánoční se podívám do teplých krajin plných písku, klobouků, koní, hor a oranžové záře. (Když si to teď tak uvědomuji oranžová = Firewatch, písek, hory = Mad Max, nejsem nějakej ujetej?) Takže mezitím co Activision dělal Call of Duty a Call of Duty a... Call of Duty a Cal... oukej asi mě chápete, tak vydal příběh o pomstě a sebepoznání. Úplně přehnané dějové zvraty sice nečekejte, ale v tom nejlepším slova smyslu se jedná o typický westernovský námět, který podobně jako většina filmů ze 40. a 50. tých let prostě neurazí. A protože nechci příliš prozrazovat co se přesně stane, co kdyby si někdo po mé bezchybné a jediné správné recenzi chtěl tento titul koupit, přesuneme se na hratelnost.

Ještě předtím, než se pustíte vůbec do hraní, vřele vám doporučuji stáhnout si widescreen fix a 60fps fix. Hra pak působí plynuleji (logicky), bude se vám lépe hrát a třeba když opustíte hru, tak nebudete mít přeházené všechny ikonky aplikací na ploše. A to se vyplatí! Já jsem si tuto vymoženost přidal asi ve čtvrtce nebo blíže k polovině herní doby a rozhodně to za těch pár minut stálo. Vylepší vám to herní zážitek, hra je líbivější a celkově už se necítíte že v tomto roce hrajete hru tak senilní, že ani nepodporuje rozlišení vašich obrazovek.

Hlavním bodem gameplayové kolonky je určitě něco co stojí za zmínku, neboť by to některé pistolníky mohlo odradit. PISTOLE i když nemá žádné zásadní nebo až katastrofické chyby, je přebraná z konzolí tuším např. z Playstation 2 a to se hodně podepsalo na pohybu, tedy otáčení myší (rozhlížení) a na střelbě. Ta je ve stavu takového kočkopsa mezi zdá se slabým aim assistem (netuším jestli něco takového přimo ve hře jde vypnout nebo vůbec je) a zčervenáním zaměřovače. Jednoduše řečeno nepotřebujete mířit úplně přesně. Ten zaměřovač je natolik velký, že by jste trefily stodolu i po slepu a prostě když z červená při najetí na nepřítele, kulka si ho najde sama. Mě to celou dobu vůbec nevadilo, má to takový dojem setsakra přesného bastarda a dodává mi to aspoň částečnou dávku sebevědomí, že nejsem úplný vemeno. Zbytek jsou poměrně jednoduché, avšak účinné mechaniky, které i po těch letech skálopevně drží. Jediné co chybí je sprint. To ale vyrovnává skutečnost, že hlavní postava Cole má dlouhé kroky takže nepřijdete zkrátka. 

Což mě přivádí rovnou k postavám a tomu jak badass by mohl celý svět být v kapánek lepší grafice. Záporáci jsou charakterově výrazní a jejich činy jsou až šokujícně brutální. Spojenci/hrdinové rezistence nebo aliance jak chcete až zase takovou hloubku nemají, no no i když nad tím tak přemýšlím tak zaleží jak který, ale všechny spojuje jedna zásadní událost daleké minulosti. Musím říct, že kromě majestátní a překrásné hudby, které jsem si snad poprvé opravdu výrazně všimnul u hry byl v pozadí slyšet i můj hukot v kládě jelikož lehké děvy procházející se po prknech stavení v Dodge nebo Empire City, popřípadě v nevěstincích, mají svůj šarm i po letitých službách společnosti. A to ani nemluvím o tom, když na vás jedna z nich vytasí zpod sukně nebo jemného prádelkového podvazku kvéra.

Na konec bych se chtěl k něčemu co mě tíží přiznat. Myslím si, že stejně jako tento dopis nad nímž sedím už asi 2 hodiny, i samotnou gamesku jsem zapínal a následně projížděl docela na sílu. Oprášil jsem hraní stejně jako psaní spíše z nutnosti než proto, že jsem to opravdu chtěl. A mohl bych vám věrným čtenářům psát o tom jaký GUN je i docela grind. Že vás všechna ta vylepšení zbraní, dovedností, zásob a hodiny strávené kopáním zlata a dělaní pár stejných, ale nikdy vyloženě stejných vedlejších misí, nezachrání před nepřátelskými NPCčkami z laserovou muškou. Že některé lokace působí jako z pohádky a jiné zase jako z levného ochotnického divadla 18. století v chudinské čtvrti smrdící splaškami. Mohl bych vyprávět jak zmíněný ochuzený gunplay vyrovnává velikost arzenálu a různá využití všech zbraní. Jak otravné jsou nájezdy znovuzrozených banditů na těch stejných místech. Jak velká celá mapa je a kam všude se dá zajet. Ta živost určitého prostředí a odumřelost zase jiného. Je PISTOL perfektní hra? Ne. Užil jsem si její průchod? Ano. Je tohle líný způsob jak vypsat všechny pro a proti bez toho aniž bych musel psát další odstavce ve kterých bych se zamotal protože už to chci mít dopsané a moje pisálkovské dovednosti zásadně za dobu mé nepřítomnosti ochably? 100x ANO! 

Vždycky mám při hraní takto staré hry určité dilema v tom, proč bych ji měl doporučit/nedoporučit dnešnímu publiku a hlavně v dnešní moderní době. Přijdu si příliš tvrdý a zároveň se snažím někdy krotit, abych očekával u her starších více jak 20 let, aby nevypadali jako vytažené z análů (staré letopisy, hovada) a ještě čekat něco převratného v rámci celé herní doby. Neříkám, že nic takového v těch hrách není, nicméně to už nemá takový ten úder. Pak tady může vyvstat argument, proč tedy hraješ tak staré hry když ti tolik nevoní? ...Je to asi proto, že se v nich skrývá něco speciálního. Je to docela těžko popsatelné, ale jedná se o určitou směsici atmosféry a takového pocitu. Mají nezapomenutelné kouzlo a i když teď můj rozsah je dosti obecný, GUN je na určitých místech se svojí scenérií velmi vřelé místečko kde se ve světě nacházet. Už teď vím co jsem chtěl zmínit a nezmínil a co jsem nechtěl zmínit a zmínil a co jsem nezmínil a vzpomenu si že jsem chtěl zmínit. Na úplný závěr jsem chtěl dát nějaký hrozně trapný nebo ohraný vtip, ale rozhodl jsem se, že jsem již dospěl a tak se podle toho budu chovat a napíši jen, že takhle docela v pohodě.

GUN is still a really good western game, if you're playing it on a PS2 from 2005.

The game itself holds up surprisingly well. The setting is great, the atmosphere is classic western goodness, and it's easy to see why so many people remember it fondly.

The problem is the PC version.

On a modern computer, this thing fights you harder than the actual enemies do. Bugs, weird issues, compatibility problems, random nonsense... getting the game running properly can become its own side quest. And then comes the fun part: figuring out which patches actually fix things and which ones create three new graphical problems.

It's a shame because underneath all that, there's still a genuinely fun game behind it.

If you have a PS2 or an OG xbox, absolutely play it.

If you're buying the PC version, be prepared to spend some time playing "Western IT Support Simulator."

Not recommended on modern PC. The game deserves better.

[h1]Gun: старый, но не сломленный вестерн из 2005-го[/h1]

Gun мне понравилась.

Причем, честно говоря, игра состарилась лучше, чем я ожидал.  
Супер ярких эмоций, как после серии Call of Juarez, у меня не было, но тут, скорее всего, причина не в самой Gun, а в контексте: это уже четвертый вестерн подряд, который я прохожу за последнее время.

Тем не менее, Gun ощущается совсем другой игрой.

Это не душевно-кривой вестерн, как Call of Juarez.  
Это скорее компактный вестерн-блокбастер середины 2000-х.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🎬 Вестерн-блокбастер из 2005[/h2]

С первых же катсцен видно, что у игры был нормальный бюджет и четкое понимание, какой эффект она хочет произвести.

Постановка сцен, ракурсы, движение персонажей, операторская работа — все выглядит так, будто смотришь вестерн или боевик эпохи VHS.

Сюжет простой, но подан уверенно.  
Главный герой крут, приходит, стреляет и решает свои проблемы.

Здесь нет такой ярко выраженной морали, как в Call of Juarez.  
Gun больше про прямолинейный кино-вестерн: плохие люди, личная история, месть, перестрелки, скачки и ощущение приключения.

И в этом формате игра работает.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🌄 Маленький открытый мир, который кажется больше[/h2]

В Gun есть открытый мир, но по современным меркам он совсем небольшой.

И это скорее плюс.

Мир компактный, но за счет разных биомов, переходов и визуального разнообразия создается ощущение не просто маленькой карты, а целого региона: города, равнины, каньоны, горы, разные зоны и маршруты.

Да, если смотреть строго, масштаб скромный.  
Но игра умеет маскировать это и создавать ощущение вестерн-путешествия.

Побочные задания, конечно, лишены той же постановки, что и основная история.  
Но мне все равно не было влом их закрывать.

Я прошел игру на 100%: основной сюжет, сайды, аналог коллекционок и прокачку.  
На это ушло примерно 10 часов, причем проходил я не спеша.

По современным меркам игра короткая.  
Но она не перегружена и не успевает надоесть.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🎨 Графика устарела, арт-дирекшн — нет[/h2]

Gun выходила почти на всех актуальных платформах своего времени: PS2, GameCube, PC, Xbox 360, оригинальный Xbox, а потом еще и PSP.

Из-за этого ждать графику уровня Doom 3, Half-Life 2 или Far Cry не стоит.  
Даже на момент выхода было видно, что полигоны и текстуры не топовые.

Но визуально игра все равно держится.

Видно, что у проекта был арт-директор и единый стиль.  
Блюр, тени, трава, цветовая гамма и общая подача хорошо маскируют технические ограничения.

Да, ноунейм-NPC и прохожие выглядят заметно хуже основных персонажей.  
Но в целом картинка ощущается цельной.

И это хороший пример того, как стиль иногда стареет лучше, чем чистый «графон».

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🔫 Стрельба и лошади[/h2]

Стрельба на удивление приятная.

У оружия есть хороший импакт:
[list]
[*]звуки
[*]отдача
[*]реакции врагов
[*]анимации смерти
[*]оторванные части тел
[*]общий визуальный фидбек от попаданий
[/list]

Причем апгрейд оружия ощущается не только в цифрах урона.

Когда получаешь новый пистолет или ружье в том же слоте, меняется не только эффективность, но и звук, ударность, общее чувство выстрела.  
И это очень важно для игры, где ты большую часть времени именно стреляешь.

Езда на коне тоже приятно удивила.  
Управление отзывчивое, скачки не раздражают, а вестерн-вайб от этого только усиливается.

В целом для консольной, не ПК-ориентированной игры 2005 года Gun играется хорошо.  
Да и сейчас — вполне нормально.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🛠 Технические моменты[/h2]

Теперь немного про минусы и технические нюансы.

Во-первых, игра изначально в 4:3, но патч на широкое разрешение ставится легко и без боли.  
С этим проблем нет.

А вот FPS залочен на 30, и скорость игры привязана к кадрам.  
То есть нормально разлочить частоту не получится — играть придется в 30 FPS.

Обычно я долго привыкаю к 30 кадрам, даже на консолях, где это норма.  
Но здесь, на удивление, адаптироваться было не так тяжело.

Правда, для 30 FPS я бы советовал играть на геймпаде.

Игра поддерживает геймпад, но с нюансами. Лучше загуглить раскладку с PS2/Xbox 360 и забиндить управление похожим образом.  
Сразу предупреждаю: максимальная скорость камеры с геймпада очень низкая по современным меркам.

Я решил это через Steam Input: заменил правый стик, отвечающий за камеру, на mouse joystick и настроил чувствительность под себя.  
Игра спокойно поддерживает одновременный ввод с клавиатуры/мыши и геймпада, так что такой вариант работает нормально.

После этого 30 FPS ощущаются заметно менее раздражающе, чем при игре на чистой клавиатуре и мыши.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]🎯 Aim assist, который нельзя отключить[/h2]

Самый неприятный технический момент — вшитый aim assist.

Похоже, из-за консольной ориентации игры он встроен прямо в управление.  
И отключить его нельзя.

Причем работает он даже на клавиатуре и мыши.

Это иногда добавляет фрустрации, потому что игра будто слегка вмешивается в прицеливание.  
Не катастрофа, но неприятно.

С этим, насколько я понял, ничего особо не сделать.  
Придется мириться.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]💸 Цена и издатель[/h2]

Отдельный минус — цена.

Microsoft в целом и Activision в частности отказались от нормальных региональных цен в Steam.  
Ладно новые игры, но старые проекты тоже стоят конских денег.

Базовая цена Gun:
[list]
[*]10000 тенге
[*]1533,90 руб.
[*]примерно 21 доллар
[/list]

Для игры 2005 года это многовато.

Я смог поймать скидку 75%:
[list]
[*]2500 тенге
[*]около 400 руб.
[*]примерно 5 долларов
[/list]

И даже так это ощущается не супер дешево.

Поэтому совет простой:  
[b]брать только на большой скидке или поднимать зеленый флаг.[/b]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]⏱ Итог[/h2]

Gun — хороший короткий вестерн-блокбастер из 2005 года.

Он не такой душевно-кривой, как Call of Juarez, и не такой масштабный, как RDR.  
Но в своем формате работает до сих пор.

Это киношный боевик про крутых ковбоев примерно на 10 часов.  
Без лишнего жира, без перегруза и с приятной стрельбой.

Если хочется большого вестерна на десятки часов — это уже RDR и RDR2.  
Я до них когда-нибудь дойду, но пока их масштаб и длительность немного пугают.

На этом фоне Gun оказался отличным промежуточным вариантом: короткий, цельный и вполне живой вестерн до эпохи RDR.

С техническими оговорками, странным aim assist и неприятной ценой — но все равно хороший.

Świetna gra, do której naprawdę warto wrócić, nawet w 2026 roku! Rozgrywka sprawiła mi dużo przyjemności, a całość została bardzo dobrze osadzona w realiach historycznych. Gra oferuje trzy kampanie: amerykańską, brytyjską oraz radziecką, dzięki czemu możemy spojrzeć na wydarzenia II wojny światowej z różnych perspektyw.
Bardzo podobało mi się odwzorowanie historycznych wydarzeń, klimat oraz sama rozgrywka. Jak na produkcję z 2003 roku gra nadal potrafi dostarczyć sporo frajdy. W 2026 roku naprawdę przyjemnie jest usiąść, odpalić taki klasyk i przypomnieć sobie, jak wyglądały początki tej kultowej serii.
Oczywiście nie obyło się bez drobnych niedociągnięć. Zdarzały się niewielkie błędy graficzne, np. blokowanie postaci na kamieniach czy elementach otoczenia. Trafiłem również na kilka błędów związanych z językiem – przykładowo podczas kampanii radzieckiej jeden z moich towarzyszy potrafił mówić po angielsku.
Nie zmienia to jednak mojej ogólnej oceny. To naprawdę bardzo dobra gra, która mimo upływu lat nadal daje dużo satysfakcji. Zdecydowanie polecam każdemu, kto lubi klimaty II wojny światowej i chce odświeżyć sobie kawałek historii gamingu.

Call of Duty (2003) was quite an interesting first entry into the entire series and a great start to what was to come later. The game was actually harder than i thought it would be and shows how different the series and each game changed over time. It was a struggle having to play the game and not have checkpoints as you traditionally do and instead relied on saving the game manually. Not to mention having to use health packs to replenish your health back up to 100% instead of the later games, health regeneration system. 

Despite those changes though and trying to deal with getting used to them. I absolutely loved the game and adored every moment of it, that i got to play through and loved the mission variety. You had 3 different campaigns to play through, the americans, the british and of course the soviets. I think the soviet campaign was my all time favourite though and loved how it was very similar in story, to the movie called enemy at the gates and gave me so many flashbacks to that movie. 

I have never had the chance to play this game until now and glad i've finally been able to go through it. It was quite a fun game to go through and mow down the nazi army as usual in these world war games. I loved seeing some npcs in the game that would later go onto inspire full blown beloved character of the series. Mainly captain price himself, his character seems to be a recurring one between all the older games and newer one. I know it's not the same price character in every game of course but it's nice seeing his name and legacy being passed on throughout the series.

I'm going through all the old cod games and quite interested in seeing how every game changes slightly and watching the graphics, guns and characters become different and improve over time. Despite how frustrating the difficulty was and how challenging it was going back to not having checkpoints or health regeneration. It was quite cool going though it and made me realise how harder some games were back then, in this one you have to memorise the locations and spawns of enemies and remembering to save frequently too. Otherwise you would have to redo huge stretches of campaign all over again.

I would easily recommend this game and say it's a must try for anyone who wants to see how the cod series begin and what it's roots were. If you have only ever played the newer cods and used to there systems, the old games will definitely challenge you and give you a run for your money.

I just finished playing this game, I want to say what I think of it. This is my first ever steam review.
The gunplay was very satisfying, and the movement felt very responsive. The non-regen health is both good and bad in a way. It adds real consequences to how you play, but it could also get frustrating sometimes. Atleast it's not like you get barely any health packs. The level design has held up moderately well. The missions are well paced, fun to play and memorable. Although, it could get frustrating sometimes too. The vehicle segments I felt were generally a bit weaker. I didn't hate them, but Call of Duty works best as a boots on the ground game. There is no grenade danger indicator like in later games, but funnily enough, grenades are less annoying here than in other CoD games I've played. The lack of sprinting makes the game slower but I like that. Also, I enjoy the weapon system. Being able to have a sidearm as a 3rd weapon slot instead of just being able to have 2 weapons at once is nice and adds a bit of variety to your arsenal. The game doesn't really have a story. Theres a bit of it and a few characters exist but thats basically it. Something I felt the game does well is making you attached to characters even if they don't have a lot of personality. Cpt. Foley or Cpt. Price for example are memorable characters. I do wish Price's death was done better. The visuals hold up pretty well. The technical side of things may be dated, but the artistic direction shines. It has a specific atmosphere only games from this era can have.
As for the performance on my hardware, I don't know how much this counts for the newest PCs as my hardware is quite a bit older (low mid end 2013 pc), but it ran well. There were occasional frame drops here and there but it worked well overall.
My thoughts on the game are overall positive and I do think its a very underrated game, but there are flaws and it's not perfect. So I would give it an 8/10. You can really trace the franchises DNA back to here. I am planning to also do a review for United Offensive when I beat it. Also, I will only review the campaigns, I'm not really a multiplayer guy.
Edit: I want to add that I played the game on Regular for my playthrough so if you played on another difficulty you're opinion on the difficulty may be different.

Call of Duty 2003 es uno de esos juegos que ayudaron a establecer muchas de las bases de los shooters bélicos modernos. Está ambientado en la Segunda Guerra Mundial y te pone en diferentes campañas donde participás en combates junto a soldados aliados.

Lo mejor del juego es la forma en la que intenta representar las batallas. No se siente simplemente como ir disparando enemigos uno detrás de otro, sino que muchas veces avanzás acompañado por otros soldados, participando en ataques y defendiendo posiciones mientras el combate ocurre alrededor.

La campaña también tiene bastante variedad. Podés jugar como soldado estadounidense, británico o soviético, y cada campaña tiene sus propias misiones y situaciones. Esto hace que la aventura no se limite siempre al mismo tipo de combate.

Obviamente, es un juego de 2003 y eso se nota bastante. Los gráficos, las animaciones y algunos controles pueden sentirse bastante antiguos comparados con los Call of Duty actuales. Además, la campaña es relativamente corta y las posibilidades fuera de ella son bastante limitadas.

Aun así, la ambientación sigue funcionando muy bien. Los sonidos de las armas, las explosiones y la música ayudan a transmitir bastante bien la sensación de estar en medio de una batalla de la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

En resumen, Call of Duty 2003 es un clásico que marcó el comienzo de una de las franquicias más conocidas de los videojuegos. Puede sentirse viejo en varios aspectos, pero su campaña sigue siendo entretenida y muestra cómo empezó la saga.

Un juego histórico para la franquicia y una buena forma de ver los comienzos de Call of Duty.

Call of Duty 2 is a great game. At its highest highs it is truly an immersive experience, you really do feel like a soldier in this game. It is absolutely worth the 20 dollars it's going for right now.
----------------------------------------------
The graphics are good for 2005. Nowadays you can certainly tell of its age, but it gets the job done and for me personally the quirks of older visuals are charming.

The game consists of three perspectives from the three major Allies of the war: Soviet, Commonwealth, and American. Each of those has 3 "Missions" (level-packs) that take place at various points in the war. (The Commonwealth gets a fourth for a couple tank missions.) This structure is perfect for CoD 2 since you can play the game in bite-sized chunks without having to recollect prior Missions. 

I do think most people will want to play in small doses since one of the few downsides of the game is that it's pretty much nonstop intense action from end to end. Playing the entire game in one sitting would be exhausting. If you like quiet moments in your games, you're going to be disappointed here. Also, if you like stories, then CoD 2 may not be for you. There is no real story going on here. "You have a job to do: kill Germans, go do it." That's the story.

Another downside is that there are definitely moments where it is OBVIOUS the world rotates around the player, and it really kills the fun. It can feel like nothing more than a target range with a death timer in those moments. Luckily those moments are vastly outnumbered by well-done set pieces and scripting. The only consistent nag in this department is enemies having different rules for being killed depending on what they are doing. (For example, you cannot kill an MG42 gunner in one good shot, you will always watch him stumble and then get back on the gun despite taking a .30 cal bullet between the eyes. Grrr.)

Multiplayer is good. I can't say much about it in detail since I didn't grow up with it, and you'll be hard-pressed to find a regular match of CoD 2 at all these days. It's either a bot server or some crazy mod that completely changes the experience. I'd take MP as the cherry on top these days, If you can find a good server somehow, great! If not, no big deal, the singleplayer is worth the asking price.

Call of Duty is an interesting franchise when you look at it as a whole. Looking back now, it feels like it had humble beginnings. What's interesting is that during this period of CoD, it feels like you were not meant to feel heroic. If you play on anything higher than the 'medium' difficulty, you end up feeling really small. It isn't about trickshots, or even much skill (as opposed to the newer ones) you have to be somewhat methodical. Not to any grand means, but still somewhat. It's hard to believe that CoD started off as a genuine attempt to make something akin to a war movie and not some, sci-fi dystopian techno dystopia. And although the textures are old as hell, it still looks and feels more grounded than anything produced in the last 10 years from the franchise. Even now, as I play this game, some 20 years later- for the first time, mind you, I can tell more passion went into this and it makes the experience enjoyable to this day. I have no sense of nostalgia for this game, and I can recognize that it is good, and is genuinely better than the CoD of today.

The controls feel responsive, the gunplay is satisfying, and the overall gameplay is simply fun. 

It’s easy to get immersed in the action, and the improvements over the first game make the experience even better.

The story is once again well done and, in some parts, even better than the first game. It delivers an engaging World War II experience that keeps you wanting to play more.

Overall, Call of Duty 2 is a great sequel that builds on the strengths of its predecessor and delivers an even better experience.

Call of Duty: United Offensive was an incredible and substantial build upon Call of Duty (2003) It added more mission variety, vehicles scenes and lots of new weapons to try out, which is always a plus to have. It was fun seeing some familiar faces from the first game come back and going into battle with them against a nazi occupation. It was still a very challenging game mainly because of the lack of health regeneration and having to use medpacks instead. 

I got quite frustrated myself and definitely blew my lid more than a few times. I repeatedly died in certain areas and felt like the game was almost near on impossible to get through. The enemies are very aggressive for sure and have been dialed up to 10 on the aggression meter. They were not easy to fight as well, sometimes the soldiers would take 3 shots to kill them and possibly even more. The same can be said for the vehicles, tanks and planes as well. 

Despite my troubles with the game and getting used to this surprisingly difficult game, it was a blast to play through and i loved every minute of the game. Some of the characters had nice personalities and made you want to follow them through combat and riled you up with great speeches and charisma. 

This game was amazing to go through and without a doubt i'd say it easily still holds up today. It's a game that will give new cod players and veteran cod players a run for their money. I would definitely say compared to modern cod games, the old ones had more difficulty to it and put some of the newer games to shame easily. A few of the newer games do feel pretty easy and are more story based whereas, the older cods are a challenge and want to test you skills in combat and remembering enemy positions.

I think you should definitely give this game a try and experience an amazing piece of cod history. You wont be disappointed at all and will enjoy the game and the old school vibes easily. It's a game that brings back lots of nostalgia and so many childhood memories.

"8/10." I actually really enjoyed this one. United Offensive takes what worked in the original and adds quite a few new things to the formula. Sprinting is probably the most obvious addition, but the new weapons and mission concepts also help make it feel like more than just a simple expansion.

The difficulty spikes are definitely more common this time around, though. There were a few sections where I found myself repeating the same segment a couple of times before finally getting through it. Still, some of the missions are absolutely worth it. The mission where you have to defend the plane was one of my favorites — such a cool concept and a great change of pace.

The new levels are intense and packed with action, throwing you into some genuinely huge battles with enemies coming at you from every direction. The scale of some of these missions is pretty epic for a game from 2004. And of course, getting to play around with new toys like the flamethrower is always a plus.

A really solid expansion that manages to build on the original rather than just giving you more of the same.

Call of Duty: United Offensive is a substantial expansion to the original Call of Duty, taking its cinematic World War II combat and increasing the scale of almost everything around it. Developed by Gray Matter Studios and published by Activision, the expansion focuses on larger battles, additional weapons, vehicle sequences, new multiplayer modes, and three distinct Allied campaigns. Although its technology and mission design clearly belong to an earlier generation of PC shooters, its energetic presentation and relentless battlefield atmosphere still make it an enjoyable piece of classic first-person shooter history.

The single-player campaign contains 13 missions divided between American, British, and Soviet soldiers. This structure gives the adventure considerable variety, taking players through conflicts associated with the Battle of the Bulge, Sicily, and Kursk. Switching perspectives also changes the atmosphere regularly. One moment may involve fighting through frozen defensive positions, while another can involve pushing across open terrain under heavy enemy fire. The campaign rarely allows the action to become comfortable, constantly introducing artillery, armored vehicles, machine-gun positions, and large groups of soldiers.

One of the expansion's strongest qualities is its ability to make battles feel larger than the player. Instead of portraying every encounter as a solitary mission, United Offensive frequently surrounds the player with friendly troops who advance, defend positions, and exchange fire with enemy forces. Explosions, artillery strikes, vehicle movements, gunfire, and shouted commands create an appropriately chaotic environment. Modern games can obviously produce far more sophisticated battlefields, but the carefully scripted presentation remains surprisingly effective considering the game's age.

Gunplay follows the straightforward style of the original while expanding the available equipment. Rifles, submachine guns, explosives, and other period weapons are complemented by heavier options, including flamethrowers and deployable machine guns. Artillery mechanics add another dimension to certain engagements. Weapons are uncomplicated by modern standards, but their direct handling suits the fast pace of the campaign. Enemies can still punish careless movement, encouraging players to make use of cover and friendly soldiers rather than simply charging into every position.

Vehicle gameplay contributes considerably to the expansion's variety. Tanks, jeeps, motorcycles, and aircraft sequences break up extended stretches of infantry combat. These sections are intentionally accessible rather than simulation-heavy, allowing the campaign to deliver spectacle without forcing players to master complicated vehicle systems. Some vehicle sequences have aged better than others, but they help give United Offensive a broader sense of warfare than a campaign built exclusively around fighting on foot.

Multiplayer was another significant part of the package. The expansion added 11 multiplayer maps alongside modes including Capture the Flag, Domination, and Base Assault. Objective-focused modes provide more structure than simple elimination matches, with Base Assault being particularly appropriate for the expansion's emphasis on large-scale warfare. The main issue for modern players is population rather than design. As an older multiplayer title, finding active matches can be considerably less reliable than it was during the game's prime years, making the single-player campaign the more dependable attraction today.

Presentation is naturally where its age becomes most obvious. Character models are basic, environments use relatively simple geometry, animations are limited, and visual effects cannot compete with contemporary shooters. Even so, the art direction remains effective enough to communicate the harshness and disorder of its battlefields. Smoke, snow, fire, explosions, military vehicles, and groups of soldiers create atmosphere despite the primitive technology. Audio remains particularly important, with artillery, gunfire, explosions, engines, and battlefield chatter providing much of the intensity.

The mission design can also feel restrictive by modern standards. Encounters are heavily scripted, enemy behavior is sometimes predictable, and progression occasionally depends on reaching specific locations before the next event activates. Players accustomed to open environments or highly dynamic artificial intelligence may find this approach dated. United Offensive works best when accepted as a tightly directed military action experience rather than a sandbox battlefield.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially listed as Unsupported. Players primarily interested in experiencing it on Valve's handheld should keep this limitation in mind rather than assuming that the simple controls automatically guarantee full compatibility. Its design may appear ideal for portable play, but the official Deck classification does not currently provide that assurance.

Another important consideration is that United Offensive is an expansion and requires the original Call of Duty. Viewed in that context, however, it provides a generous continuation rather than a minimal collection of extra missions. The new campaigns, weapons, vehicles, multiplayer maps, and gameplay additions meaningfully broaden the original formula while preserving its distinctive emphasis on fighting alongside other soldiers.

Call of Duty: United Offensive remains a compelling experience for anyone interested in the early years of the franchise or classic World War II shooters. Its graphics, artificial intelligence, scripted progression, and technical conventions have aged considerably, but its sense of battlefield scale remains impressive. The constant mixture of infantry engagements, defensive battles, vehicle sequences, artillery, and cinematic set pieces gives the campaign an energetic rhythm that still works. It represents an era when expansion packs could significantly extend and enhance an existing game rather than simply adding a handful of isolated extras.

**Call of Duty: United Offensive – An Absolute Classic**

*Call of Duty: United Offensive* is one of those expansions that shows how a great game should be done. Even after all these years, it still manages to deliver an incredibly fun and intense World War II experience.

The campaign is easily one of the best parts of the game. The missions are varied, action-packed, and full of memorable moments. The battles feel intense and exciting, and the atmosphere is fantastic. You really get the feeling that you are part of a larger military operation rather than simply playing another shooter.

The addition of new weapons, vehicles, and larger-scale battles makes the experience even better. Driving tanks and taking part in huge firefights is extremely satisfying, and the gameplay remains fast-paced without losing the classic *Call of Duty* feeling.

The multiplayer is also a lot of fun. The large maps, vehicles, and chaotic battles add a completely different level of excitement and make *United Offensive* incredibly enjoyable to play with others.

Sure, the graphics and some mechanics have obviously aged, but honestly, that doesn't take away from the experience at all. If anything, the old-school gameplay and atmosphere are part of what makes this game so special.

**9.5/10 – Highly recommended!**

If you enjoy classic war games, great campaigns, intense battles, and old-school *Call of Duty*, *United Offensive* is absolutely worth playing. It's not just a great expansion — in many ways, it's even better than the original game.

В некоторой степени уникальный проект для франшизы Зова Долга - официальное дополнение к полноценной части серии.

Делала её Gray Matter Studios, которая в последующем была закрыта, а многие её выходцы впоследствии составили основной костяк студии Treyarch. И несколько иной подход к созданию военных сюжетов чувствуется. В игре стало больше запоминающихся персонажей, особенно в советской кампании. Чуть больше остросюжетных сценок, раскрывающих грязь войны. 

Но самое главное, сами миссии стали куда интереснее. Почти. Американская кампания для меня так и осталась самое унылой частью игры - эти масштабные бои в зимних лесах и безликих французских деревушках, где тебе может прилететь абсолютно с любой стороны бесили ещё в первой части, здесь ничего кардинально не изменилось. Её я банально перетерпел, чтобы дойти до более интересной части игры - британской кампании.

Приключения британца Дойла с самого начала начинается со свежего хода - обороны бомбардировщика на высоте в несколько километров, а продолжаются падением в ночную Голландию, вливанием в отряд местного партизанского Сопротивления и эпичным подрывом моста, а полируются ещё одной диверсионной миссией в Сицилии (кстати, к своему стыду признаюсь, что до недавней Mafia: The Old Country я даже понятия не имел, что это за Сицилия такая). Всё это сопровождается красивой постановкой, интригой и постоянной сменой геймплейных ситуаций.

Советская кампания также поставлена куда лучше - но ровно до середины, где начинаются городские уровни, вызывающие самые худшие воспоминания о первой части. А уж финальный бой в этот раз я даже не стал проходить - за свою жизнь я прошёл его уже три раза и больше превозмогать этот кошмар (хотя в голову лезет более нецензурное слово) с бесконечным респавном пехоты, танков и самолётов-бомбардировщиков на небольшой арене я не намерен, нервная система дороже. Но вот первые уровни где-то в захолустных деревушках под Курском с постоянно идущим дождём почему-то всегда вызывали странное чувство уюта.

По итогу это очень крепкое дополнение, которое местами во многом превосходит оригинал.

RollerCoaster Tycoon 3: Platinum ist der unangefochtene König der Nostalgie, der bewweist, dass gutes Gamedesign kein Verfallsdatum hat. Wenn du es damals geliebt hast und deine Kids es heute feiern, liegt das nicht an der Grafik, die heute eher wie ein buntes Fiebertraym wirkt, sondern an der puren, unverfälschten Spielfreude. Es ist eines dieser seltenen Spiele, die den Spagat zwischen komplexer Management-Simulation und totalem kreativen Chaos perfekt meistern.

Während moderne Tycoon-Spiele dich oft mit Tabellen und kleinteiligem Mikromanagement erschlagen, kommt RCT3 direkt zum Punkt: Bau die krasseste Achterbahn, die physikalisch gerade noch vertretbar ist, und setz dich per Coaster-Cam selbst rein. Dass deine Kinder darauf anspringen, ist kein Wunder – die intuitive Bedienung und die Freiheit, in Soaked! Wasserparks zu bauen oder in Wild! Löwen durch den Park spazieren zu lassen, bietet einen Spielplatz, den aktuelle Titel oft hinter DLC-Paywalls oder komplizierten Menüs verstecken.

Es ist die Platin-Edition, die das Paket erst komplett macht. Du hast hier ein fertiges, vollgestopftes Spiel ohne modernen Live-Service-Müll. Dass die Grafik nach heutigen Standards "altbacken" ist, stört niemanden, wenn der Park erst einmal leuchtet und die Besuchermassen durch die Tore strömen. Es ist ein digitales Erbstück: Du zeigst ihnen, wie man ein Imperium aufbaut, und sie zeigen dir wahrscheinlich, wie man die Sicherheitsvorkehrungen der Bahnen ignoriert, um maximales Chaos zu stiften.

RollerCoaster Tycoon 3: Platinum! is a comprehensive and immersive amusement park simulation that stands as one of the high points in the genre. Originally released in the mid-2000s and later brought to Steam with all its expansions included, this version offers players a full-featured experience that blends creativity, strategy, and management in equal measure. With both the Soaked! and Wild! expansion packs bundled in, the Platinum edition turns an already robust simulation game into an expansive sandbox for park-building enthusiasts.

At its core, RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 tasks players with designing and managing their own amusement parks, complete with custom roller coasters, themed attractions, food stalls, and staff. The shift from the isometric, sprite-based graphics of the earlier titles to a fully 3D engine marked a major leap forward for the series. This not only improved visual fidelity but also opened up new gameplay possibilities. One of the most beloved features is the ability to ride the roller coasters you create, putting players in a first-person seat to experience their own designs in motion. This adds a unique layer of engagement and reward, as it’s not just about profit margins and guest satisfaction—there’s a genuine sense of amusement and pride in crafting thrilling, well-engineered rides.

The game’s management systems strike a careful balance between depth and accessibility. Players need to monitor guest happiness, ride reliability, staff workload, and overall park finances. While not as punishingly detailed as some hardcore sims, there’s enough complexity here to satisfy fans of the genre. Dynamic weather, time-of-day changes, and seasonal variations also affect guest behavior and park operations. The economy can be micromanaged through pricing strategies, advertising campaigns, and careful investment in research and development. The challenge modes offer structured scenarios with specific goals, while the sandbox mode gives players limitless freedom to build the park of their dreams without financial constraints.

The included expansions in the Platinum edition greatly enhance the gameplay. Soaked! introduces water park elements—wave pools, flume rides, custom water slides, and even choreographed water shows. It transforms your standard amusement park into a full-fledged aquatic wonderland and brings new guest needs like swimwear and lifeguard staffing. Wild! adds a zoo management element, allowing players to build animal enclosures, manage breeding programs, and design safari-style attractions. These additions don’t just feel like extra content—they meaningfully expand the simulation with new mechanics, more guest types, and additional challenges to consider when running your park.

Graphically, while the game does show its age compared to modern titles, the art direction remains charming and functional. The 3D models are bright, colorful, and full of character. The user interface is clear, though not always as intuitive as it could be—some of the menus and tools feel clunky, especially when working with terrain editing or fine-tuning coaster tracks. That said, once the learning curve is overcome, the game’s building tools offer impressive flexibility. Whether you’re constructing a towering steel monstrosity or a gentle family-friendly ride, the coaster builder allows for creativity and precision. The inclusion of day-night cycles and customizable scenery adds another layer of immersion and thematic flair to your creations.

Performance on modern systems is generally stable, although occasional bugs or graphical glitches can occur, especially with large parks or complex ride setups. The Steam version has been updated to run on current operating systems without needing compatibility tweaks, but the game still lacks some modern conveniences like high-resolution UI scaling or mod support baked into the launcher. However, the modding community has kept the game alive over the years, offering custom scenery, improved textures, and even user-made rides for those willing to explore fan-made content outside of Steam.

The audio design adds to the nostalgic appeal. From the excited screams of guests on coasters to the cheerful background music and theme park ambience, the soundscape enhances the feeling of being in a living, breathing amusement park. Each ride type has its own effects, and there’s a clear attention to detail in how audio feedback reflects guest mood and ride operation.

RollerCoaster Tycoon 3: Platinum! remains a benchmark for amusement park simulation. Its combination of open-ended creativity, strategic depth, and visual charm makes it a standout title even many years after its original release. While it may not have the polish of more recent entries or the ultra-modern graphics of newer sim games, it more than makes up for that with content, personality, and freedom of expression. For newcomers and nostalgic veterans alike, this Platinum edition delivers countless hours of amusement park management and roller coaster mayhem. Whether you're in it for the economic challenge, the ride design, or just the joy of building a park packed with happy guests, it’s still one of the most satisfying simulation experiences available on Steam.

Ogólnie mamy tradycyjnego RTS-a w 3d z wczesnych lat dwutysiecznych. Trzy strony konfliktu ( USA, USA do kwadaratu i ci żli ), budowanie baz i walka całkiem sporym arsenałem jednostek piechoty i pojazdów. Co ciekawe gra pochodzi zaskakująco poważnie ( no, poważnie /jak na/ wartkiego RTS-a oczywiście, symulator żadną miarą to to nie jest ) do realizmu walki. Piechota może się chować w krzakach i budynkach, pojazdy mają ograniczone pole widzenia, czołgi niszczą wszystko co nie jest dobrze opancerzone a siły specialne słabo sobie radzą w otwartym polu, ale za to absolutnie wymiatają wrogów z zasadzek czy budynków. Skala jednostek też jest tu bliższa realizmowi bardziej niż wielu innych strategiach.

W kampanii mamy zaś fabułę prezentowaną w serii przerywników filmowcyh z aktorami w które włożono ewidentnie sporo wysiłku ( i budżetu ). Dzięki temu historię, mimo iż jest bardzo kliszowata i totalnie przewidywalna, śledzi się całkiem nieźle.

Grafika, mimo wieku ( i silenia się na realizm, to zawsze mocno się starzeje ) ogólnie daje radę. Chociaż doskwierać pewnie będzie dość nisko zawieszona kamera.

[h1]Act of War: Direct Action[/h1]

[i]«Говорят, что будущее уже здесь. Просто оно распределено неравномерно: где-то летающие машины, а где-то нефтяной кризис и террористы. Разработчики похоже, заглянули в это будущее и решили, что лучший способ его описать — это собрать все штампы из боевиков 90-х и заставить вас ими управлять. И знаете что? Это всё ещё чертовски увлекательно.»[/i] 💣🎬

[quote][i]Всем привет. Автор не несет ответственности за причиненный вред своими обзорами. Любое сходство с другими обзорами случайно. Данный обзор является лишь мнением автора и вы можете всегда оставаться при своем мнении! Спасибо за понимание и приятной игры![/i][/quote]

[h2]📜Описание[/h2]
[b]Act of War: Direct Action[/b] — это RTS из середины нулевых, которая смотрит на вас с обложки, как на новобранца, и орёт: «Война будущего — СЕЙЧАС!». Сюжет, вырванный прямиком из заголовков газет того времени, повествует о глобальном энергетическом кризисе (бензин по $7 за галлон, представляете?), который организовал таинственный Консорциум нефтяных магнатов с помощью международного терроризма. Вы, в роли майора Джейсона Рихтера, возглавляете элитное подразделение Task Force Talon и мотаетесь по всему миру — от Лондона до Москвы, — чтобы надрать задницу заговорщикам. Игра не стесняется своей «клюквенности» и вторичности по отношению к Command & Conquer, но делает это с таким размахом, что на это просто приятно смотреть.

[h2]🎨Графика и звук[/h2]
Графически [b]Act of War: Direct Action[/b] — это машина времени. Да, модели персонажей угловаты, а текстуры сегодня кажутся мыльными. Но! Здесь есть одна фишка, которая в 2005 году сносила крышу: камеру можно приблизить практически вплотную к земле, и юниты не превратятся в кашу из пикселей. Вы можете наблюдать за перестрелкой буквально из-за плеча пехотинца. Здания красиво разрушаются, городские карты детализированы, а эффекты взрывов всё ещё выглядят внушительно. Отдельного упоминания заслуживают FMV-вставки с живыми актёрами. Это кринж высшей пробы: деревянная игра, пафосные диалоги и бюджет, которого хватило только на аренду пары джипов и дымовых шашек. Но, чёрт возьми, это работает! Это создаёт неповторимую атмосферу фильма категории «Б», от которой невозможно оторваться. Саундтрек — бодрый, милитаристский, идеально подходящий для марш-бросков.

[h2]🎮Геймплей[/h2]
В основе геймплея лежит классическая формула C&C: строим базу, добываем ресурсы (здесь это нефть и деньги), нанимаем армию и идём крушить врага. Но [b]Act of War[/b] добавляет несколько интересных нюансов. Во-первых, здесь есть механика военнопленных. Вражеских солдат можно и нужно брать в плен, чтобы допрашивать их и получать ценные разведданные или ресурсы. Во-вторых, раненые бойцы не умирают мгновенно, а истекают кровью, и их можно эвакуировать с поля боя, чтобы сохранить опытный отряд. Это добавляет игре микроменеджмента, но и делает юниты более ценными. Вам доступны три фракции: мощная, но неповоротливая армия США; высокотехнологичный, но дорогой Task Force Talon; и Консорциум, берущий числом и дешёвыми наёмниками. Кампания плавно подводит вас к управлению каждой из них, чередуя тактические миссии спецназа с масштабными танковыми сражениями.

[h2]📖Сюжет и атмосфера[/h2]
Сюжет, написанный Дейлом Брауном (бывшим капитаном ВВС США и автором технотриллеров), — это квинтэссенция американского патриотического боевика. Злобные русские (куда же без них), нефтяные магнаты, плетущие заговоры, и отважные американские вояки, спасающие мир. Всё это подаётся с абсолютно серьёзной миной, что делает происходящее ещё смешнее. Но в этой простоте и кроется его очарование. Сюжет не пытается быть глубоким, он просто даёт вам контекст для того, чтобы вы могли сровнять с землёй пару кварталов Лондона или Москвы. И делает он это с такой неподдельной уверенностью в своей правоте, что вы невольно проникаетесь духом этой «клюквы» и начинаете получать удовольствие.

[h2]✅Плюсы:[/h2]
[list]
[*] ⭐ Классический, но увлекательный геймплей. Знакомая формула RTS, отполированная до блеска и дополненная интересными механиками (пленные, эвакуация раненых).
[*] ⭐ Уникальная для своего времени графика. Возможность приблизить камеру к земле и наблюдать за детализированными боями впечатляет даже сегодня.
[*] ⭐ Разнообразные фракции. Армия США, спецназ Talon и Консорциум играются по-разному, предлагая разные тактические подходы.
[*] ⭐ Увлекательная кампания. Миссии не дают заскучать, постоянно подкидывая новые задачи и локации.
[*] ⭐ Отличный саундтрек. Музыка создаёт нужное настроение и не надоедает.
[/list]

[h2]❌Минусы:[/h2]
[list]
[*] ⚠️ Устаревшая графика. Модели и текстуры выглядят архаично, но к этому быстро привыкаешь.
[*] ⚠️ Проблемы с совместимостью. На современных системах игра может работать с ошибками или не запускаться вовсе без дополнительных «танцев с бубном».
[*] ⚠️ Читерский ИИ. Враги видят всё и всегда знают, куда вы направляетесь, что может раздражать.
[*] ⚠️ Вторичность. Игра не скрывает, что является клоном C&C: Generals, и не привносит в жанр ничего кардинально нового.
[*] ⚠️ Отсутствие системы достижений для истинных коллекционеров прекрасного.
[*] ⚠️ Отсутствуют дополнительные материалы в Steam вроде обоев или карточек.
[/list]

[h2]😈Заключение:[/h2]
[b]“Act of War: Direct Action”[/b] — это великолепный образец RTS старой школы. Он не пытается казаться тем, чем не является, и честно предлагает вам несколько часов увлекательного геймплея, приправленного отличной атмосферой и непередаваемым шармом видеовставок с живыми актёрами. Если вы готовы смириться с устаревшей графикой и возможными техническими проблемами, то вас ждёт одна из лучших военных стратегий своего времени. Это как найти на антресолях старый боевик на VHS: качество картинки так себе, сюжет предсказуем, но оторваться невозможно. Настоятельно рекомендуется всем фанатам жанра и тем, кто хочет поностальгировать по золотой эпохе RTS.

[h2]💎Итоговая оценка:[/h2]
[h3]Общий балл: 8/10💣[/h3]

*Act of War: Direct Action*, developed by Eugen Systems and published by THQ Nordic, is a real-time strategy title that captures the essence of mid-2000s RTS design while carving out its own identity through grounded storytelling and mechanically engaging combat systems. Rather than leaning into fantasy or distant sci-fi, it builds its world around a near-future geopolitical crisis, giving the entire experience a tone that feels closer to a military thriller than a traditional strategy game.

The campaign is structured like a cinematic narrative, following an escalating global conflict tied to energy shortages and coordinated acts of terrorism. What sets it apart is its presentation style, incorporating live-action cutscenes alongside in-game sequences to deliver its story. While the performances and production quality vary, the ambition behind this approach gives the game a distinctive flavor, making it feel like an interactive series rather than just a sequence of missions. The pacing of the narrative keeps the player engaged, even if the story itself occasionally loses focus as it progresses.

From a gameplay perspective, *Act of War: Direct Action* adheres to classic RTS fundamentals—base building, resource management, and unit control—but introduces several mechanics that add depth and encourage active engagement. Resource gathering, for example, is not limited to static collection points. Players can capture enemy units and civilians, generating income through interrogation or containment, and can also seize structures such as banks to boost their economy. This system shifts the focus toward battlefield interaction, rewarding aggressive and tactical play rather than passive resource accumulation.

Combat is one of the game’s strongest elements, emphasizing unit specialization and positioning. Infantry play a particularly important role, especially in urban environments where buildings can be occupied and used as defensive positions. This adds a layer of tactical complexity, as controlling structures and navigating tight spaces becomes critical to success. Battles feel dynamic and responsive, with a clear sense that strategy and decision-making have a direct impact on outcomes.

The variety of factions further enhances the gameplay. Each group offers a distinct approach, with differences in technology, unit capabilities, and overall strategy. This diversity encourages experimentation and keeps encounters from feeling repetitive, whether in the campaign or in skirmish modes. Learning how to adapt to each faction’s strengths and weaknesses becomes an important part of mastering the game.

Visually, the game reflects its era but still manages to deliver a sense of scale and intensity. Explosions, destructible environments, and detailed urban settings contribute to a battlefield that feels alive and reactive. While the graphics may not match modern standards, the clarity of the visuals supports gameplay effectively, ensuring that players can easily track units and actions during complex engagements.

Despite its strengths, the game does have some limitations. The campaign, while engaging, is relatively short and occasionally uneven in its narrative execution. The live-action cutscenes, though ambitious, can feel inconsistent and may not appeal to all players. Additionally, the level of micromanagement required during intense battles can be demanding, particularly for those less familiar with traditional RTS gameplay.

Replayability is supported by skirmish and multiplayer modes, which allow players to explore different strategies and refine their skills. The core mechanics provide enough depth to sustain repeated play, especially for those who enjoy experimenting with different faction combinations and tactical approaches.

In the end, *Act of War: Direct Action* stands as a strong example of classic RTS design, enhanced by a few distinctive ideas that set it apart from its contemporaries. It may not redefine the genre, but it delivers a well-crafted and engaging experience that balances strategic depth with cinematic ambition. For fans of traditional real-time strategy games, it remains a compelling and rewarding title.

[u][b]Initial Thoughts:[/b][/u]
I beat Act of War: Direct Action. I did not hate it, but lord do I have a lot to say about it. It annoyed me more than it impressed me. For a 2000s RTS, the overall graphics are fine. They hold up well enough and the presentation is serviceable. That said, almost everything else feels uneven.

[u][b]Story and Presentation:[/b][/u]
The story is cheesy and forced. Its a plot that exists purely to move you from mission to mission rather than something grounded or believable. A lot of what happens just would not be possible in reality, and the game plays it completely straight. The FMVs and acting are rough. Really rough. If you enjoyed the Command and Conquer live action cutscenes, you might get some nostalgic fun out of it. Otherwise, it comes off like a low budget action movie that thinks it is way more serious than it is. It is not even B movie energy. It is C tier at best. 

One area where Act of War genuinely impressed me was unit detail. The models are surprisingly well done for 2005, and in some cases I think they look better than C&C Generals. The M1A2 Abrams tanks look great. The attack helicopters are awesome. The fighter aircraft in particular are nicely modeled and animated. There is clear attention to detail in how the military hardware is presented. When you zoom in, the units actually look like they are using real equipment instead of blocks. Credit where it is due, the game nailed that aspect.

[u][b]Gameplay and Unit Control:[/b][/u]
This is where the game lost me.

The unit mapping is some of the worst I have seen in an RTS. Your weakest units constantly try to lead the charge. Instead of staying protected behind armor or heavier forces, they push to the front and get deleted. You are constantly redirecting units, separating them, and micromanaging multiple groups just to keep things from falling apart.

Games like Age of Empires handle formation and unit behavior far better. Here, it feels like your army has no basic survival instincts.

Line of sight can also be frustrating. Units lose vision in situations that make no sense, and they lack common sense overall. If you do not constantly babysit your army, you will lose units in fights they should have won.

[u][b]Balance and Design:[/b][/u]
Another reviewer mentioned that every unit has a hard counter, and that is clearly the design philosophy here. You cannot spam one strong unit and roll through the game. You must diversify or you will be punished.

On paper, that is good design. In practice, infantry feel extremely fragile and are prone to funneling into bad engagements. They die fast and often. It forces variety, but sometimes in a way that feels restrictive rather than strategic.

[u][b]Missing Features:[/b][/u]
There are also several quality of life features missing that other RTS games already had at the time. You cannot rotate buildings. That always drives me crazy in base builders. Sometimes you just want your base to look clean or fit efficiently, and the game does not allow it.

You also cannot select multiple production buildings and queue units at the same time. Considering many RTS games before this allowed it, that omission feels strange. It makes the game feel rushed, especially when it was clearly competing in the post C&C Generals era.

[u][b]Final Thoughts:[/b][/u]
I do not hate AOW:DA. There is some solid RTS design under the hood, and the counter based unit balance does force you to think. But the awkward unit behavior, lack of quality of life features, clunky mapping, and cheesy presentation kept pulling me out of it. Instead of scratching my RTS itch, it made me want to boot up something else.

For me, it lands at a [u][b]6.0 out of 10[/b][/u]. Playable, occasionally fun, but frustrating enough that I would not revisit it.

Imagine C&C Generals but smaller army sizes, capturing enemies and extracting ransom as a supplement, and better air combat. The problem is with the scales of urban combat, some modern weapons fall short here. It's fun but it can be hectic sometimes, and worst part is there is no select all units on screen button.

Act of War stands out for its high-quality FMV cutscenes, which add a strong cinematic feel and help ground the experience in a believable, modern setting. The story itself is well written and, unfortunately, feels uncomfortably relevant even today, giving the narrative extra weight.

The use of aerial bombardments and off-map support was a refreshing addition for its time, bringing intensity and spectacle to battles in a way that felt innovative compared to other RTS games of that era.

That said, the late-game difficulty spike feels unfair, putting excessive pressure on the player without a clear learning curve, which disrupts the otherwise solid pacing.

Overall, Act of War remains a very enjoyable experience for its time, with strong atmosphere and ambitious ideas that still deserve appreciation despite its late-game flaws.

O jogo entrega uma experiência militar tática com um pé na realidade e trás uma proposta ambiciosa ao unir uma narrativa de thriller militar com mecânicas estratégicas bem interessantes. Apesar das cenas live-action parecerem ter saído de um filme B de baixo orçamento e a história não ser algo memorável, o game em sim tem uma jogabilidade que oferece um excelente controle de unidades táticas, onde cada tropa tem uma função clara e, quando bem utilizada, pode virar o rumo da batalha. Há um nível considerável de microgerenciamento que achei bem legal pois você pode, por exemplo, colocar soldados dentro de edifícios para ganhar vantagem tática, transformando aquele café da esquina num mini-bunker improvisado. Ver seus atiradores munidos de javelins eliminando tanques das janelas do segundo andar é gostoso demais.

O sistema de recursos também foge do tradicional “coletar e construir” já que você ganha dinheiro ao capturar inimigos, resgatar civis e controlar pontos estratégicos. Isso incentiva uma abordagem mais agressiva e dinâmica, típica de conflitos urbanos modernos.

Üç oynanabilir fraksiyon olması ve ABD'nin ön planda olması biraz propaganda özelliği taşıması niteliğini barındırıyor.  Serinin diğer oyunları da bu planda düzenlenmiş durumda. Yani genel olarak temelde ABD güçlerinin Kartel ve benzeri yasa dışı oluşumlarla savaşmasını konu ediniyor. 

Oyun oyananabilirliğini halen korusa da daha yeni versiyonlarını eğer tercih yapmak zorunda kalırsanız seçmenizi öneririm. Oynanışı eski tarz gzs modelinde yapıldığından çok büyük ayrıntılı bir oynanış beklemeyin ancak yine de stratejik doyum açısından yeterliliğini koruyan bir oyun. 

Modern askeri birimlerin olması, soğuk savaş sonrası ve ikinci milenyuma yakın bir tarihi konu edinmesinden dolayı çağdaş dönemi konu edinen strateji oyunlarının kısırlığını da düşündüğümüzde değerlendirilebilir oyunlardan. Oynanış esnasında genel olarak fraksiyonlar arasında ve oynanışta bir çeşit dengesizlik olduğunu söyleyebilirim. Gelirinizi ve onun korunması işlemine doğru ayarlama yapmazsanız baştan kaybetmenize neden oluyor. İlerleyiş ivmenizi kaybetmenize, derin ve sonu gelmez bir kısırdöngüye düşmenize neden oluyor. Bu durum act of war serisinin kronik sorunlarından birini oluşturuyor. 

Yine de modern-askeri-gerçek zamanlı strateji oyunlarının kısırlığındaki piyasada hala oynanabilirliğini koruyor.

Disable Data Execution Prevention (DEP):
Open the System dialog (right-click "This PC" -> Properties).
Click "Advanced system settings".
Go to the "Performance" settings and click "Settings".
Select the "Data Execution Prevention" tab.
Choose "Turn on DEP for all programs and services except those I select".
Click "Add" and navigate to the ACTOFWAR.exe file to exclude it from DEP

after that it worked perfectly.

A pretty fun RTS and while similar to C&C generals it does enough to be different and in some ways better (mainly in terms of campaign gameplay and storytelling).

The campaign is pretty fun and builds up pace nicely with more advanced units being introduced across time so as not to overwhelm with in which way to kill the enemy and every unit does have its place though some are better than others but without any glaring redundancies in the rosters. 

In terms of how it plays as an RTS, its pretty generic and while a bit thin on the building an economy side, the urban combat, terrain acquisition and combat mechanics are done well and are simple enough for anyone to get into and reward tactical play. 

I don't really want to say negative points as I don't think this game really commits any cardinal sins so things that could have been better:

- More context in the story, villain is very one note who gets too many lucky escapes with their infinite supply of back up plans
- Lack of campaign for the antagonist is a missed opportunity however the campaign we have is just long enough for a good experience and ends on a tough challenge without wearing out its welcome
- Economy is pretty flimsy with all factions effectively making bank off taking prisoners of war, the oil is good but since it runs out quickly, everyone goes for a POW economy instead
- Feels like there's a missing fourth faction such as a Middle Eastern faction or Russia to aid the mixed consortium forces.

So your mouse cursor can go off screen and into your other monitor and if you click off the game screen or if the cursor triggers a pop up, then the game will minimize then reset to window and it will also mess up all your desktop settings. 

This is absolutely incompetent as pretty much everyone runs more than 1 monitor these days. There's no options within the game to lock the mouse to the game screen or even to run the game's resolution in a window. Even entering "-window" in the Steam launch properties does nothing. So be prepared for accidental clicking outside the game window and having to restart your system constantly because this game will mess up your desktop settings constantly.

Threadspace: Hyperbol is one of those unique games that you think about from time to time and remember the good times you've had. Followed by the thought that perhaps it could be revived. The game's premise is that you are a member of one of three factions, controlling a ship and fighting for territory.


That may not sound like much, but the gameplay mechanics is where this game really shines. Even back when it was released it was a really fresh take on the tactical action genre and even to this day I have come across very few games that can match Threadspace for its skill ceiling and unique concept. All things considered it is very well thought out and plays smoothly in multiplayer.


The soundtrack is decent enough, and the visuals are somewhat outdated by this point, but it's not off-putting at all.


The only downside to this wonderful game is that the community is kinda non-existent. If you want to try it out, please get together with a few friends. I sincerely hope the game gets a reboot at some point.

After over 10 hours of playing ThreadSpace Hyperbol I feel ready to slowly post a review here.

First of all, TSHB is a polished game, much more so than any other game I've laid my eyes on yet (barring maybe SPAZ considering it has similarly active developers and good support).
I've encountered a few bugs, but given that I seem to be very alone with those bugs it might be something about my system. I've written in the forums and the dev has replied very fast, for a game with pretty much 8 years on it's back that's really something special.

What about the lack of human players? To be honest, there are a bunch of active players, so it's just about getting on at the same time as those. Just post or look on the forums, add the right persons and you're set to have some fun with human players. Not right any second you'd like to but it's really not that much of an issue. And then there is the hyper hour every saturday, during which the game is freely playable with the demo, and apparently at that time there are a lot more players.

The gameplay itself is really smooth and nice. Very often I have the feeling that certain things in games work wrong or weird, or that this and that is just not really my fault. In TSHB? If I die it's either because I'm facing too many enemies at once or because I make mistakes, it's as simple as that. There are no lethal glitches or the likes and the physics system is very straightforward, reliable and understandable.

The tutorials are also made with great care, they're short, fun, and teach you most though not quite everything you should know. Bonus points for having voices in the tutorials which aren't annoying one bit.

I can recommend getting this game, even if it is 8 years old. I got it vastly reduced myself, and to be honest I wouldn't pay the full price because it'd be more money than I can comfortably spend right now, but the game is worth it.

I remember when this game was launched. back when the big players were JackD, Derek.B, TinyTurtle. and many others, the epic moment where at one point we all decided to unleash the max ammo count from all our ships in hyperbols at the gate. it failed but one person ended up recording this and it was put in one of their videos. I have tried time and time again to get people to pick this game back up. Still it is a very small number of players, so spread the word! this game needs to be revived!
