[h1]Lineární westernový zážitek[/h1]
[i](doba čtení 2 minuty 11 sekund)[/i]

Ještě než bylo Red Dead Redemption, skvělé zpracování westernového zážitku nám poskytlo polské studio Techland, ačkoliv s odlišnou filozofií. Namísto otevřeného světa, jde o lineární příběhovou střílečku / adventuru. Takových vídáme dnes málo a kvalitou vůbec netratí.

Příběh vyčnívá už jen díky dvěma hlavním postavám, jejichž cesta se odehrává odlišně a zároveň v určitých místech spojuje. Dostáváme tak náhled z druhé strany doplňující následky nebo příčiny protistrany. Každá epizoda je navíc zábavná a plná různých akcí. Nějaké výjimky jsou, ale nebyla téměř situace, kdyby mě hra nezaměstnávala stále něčím novým. A to platí i o příběhu jenž pumpuje události nahoru a dolů. Během nich lze sbírat Wanted plakáty s obličeji vývojářů čistě pro odemčení té nejtěžší obtížnosti.

První postavou zmíním kněze Raye McCalal, bývalého vojáka a pistolníka. Call of Juarez ho znovu přivede na původní dráhu a honbu za pomstou. Při této cestě doslovně káže slovo Boží díky Bibli, ze které můžete citovat, zatímco trestáte všechny hříšníky. S Rayem budete často podstupovat přestřelky a akčnějších částí hry. Můžeme používat dva revolvery zároveň a spouštět schopnost, kdy dojde ke zpomalení času. Během této doby zaměřovací kříže postupně letí ke středu obrazovky a střílíme pokud nám zaměřovač zčervená po zacílení nepřítele. Využití podle mě minimální. Zvlášť u těžkých obtížností je lepší soupeře odstřelovat než vběhnout mezi ně. Ve zpomalovacím módu totiž soupeři pořád mohou střílet. Ray má k dispozici i pušku, dynamit (těch moc není), vykopávat dveře, případně nepřátele. Zažijete i několik klasických westernových duelů se zajímavou mechanikou tasení zbraně pohybem myší dopředu a dozadu. Následně opět přichází zpomalený čas. Pohyb z místa nelze, ale lze naklánět postavu do stran nebo použít skrčení. Může použít revolver i k rychlé střelbě. Především proti nepřátelům útočící blízko. Disponuje i jakýmsi pancířem odrážející občas kulky.

U Billhyo Svíčky jakožto druhé postavy jde spíše o pravý opak. S ním budeme zažívat tu adventurní část. Příběh o útěku a strachu i získání odvahy vůči nepřátelům. Takže plníme mimo bojové úkoly, často související s překonáváním překážek. Billy u sebe nosí bič. S jehož pomocí se můžeme zhoupávat, přitahovat či slaňovat. Ovšem krapet záludná věc. Nacházet správné místo trvá, jelikož postava musí stát i blízko srázu. S bičem jdou zabíjet hadi anebo pavouky. Zaměřování pro bič však není optimální a pravidelně zasahujete jiné místo než míříte. Součástí jsou stealth sekvence. Hra Vás do nich vyloženě nenutí. Nejste omezeni a situaci můžete řešit přestřelkou. Avšak hrajete za mladého a nezkušeného kluka. Nejsme ostřílení pistolníci. Může používat pouze jeden revolver bez schopnosti, pušku a speciálně i luk. Má podobnou schopnost jako Ray, akorát pouze jednu ránu s nehybným křížem, zato automaticky u každého šípu mimo nutnosti čekání na nabití.

Střelecký systém je celkem dobře zpracovaný. Lehce nastaven, aby nelítaly kulky přesně k místu zaměření. Soupeři mají občas šanci přežít o něco déle. Nejde o příšernou věc, spíše má nabudit trochu realismu. U revolverů i pušek máme několik verzí. Klasická puška, brokovnice, odstřelovací puška. U revolverů bohužel nerozpoznáte jejich rozdíl ve statistice, a tak jde o malou záhadu kromě rychlopalné verze nebo u dámské pistolky.

Po grafické stránce sice již žádný skvost. Hlavně u prostředí to poznáte. Nadmíru jsou zpracovány postavy, především jejich tváře. Detail snadno zapomenete skvělou hudbou, kterou bych přesně očekával u westernového příběhu. Jak u toulání se divočinou či přestřelky.  Taková lehčí verze Morriconeho, nezahlcující množstvím nástrojů. Omezujících bugů tolik nezažijete. Kamera někdy uzemnila svou pozici. Celkem asi dva bugy za celou hru.

[h3]Rozhodně lze doporučit pro veškeré fanoušky westernových příběhů (a nejen ty), kteří jistě budou překvapeni poutavým příběhem i zábavným gameplayem, který Vás neunudí k smrti. Navíc nejde o nic příliš zdlouhavého a neunaví hráče.[/h3]
Güzel bir oyunmuş. Yaşına göre oynanışı bir tık yaşlansa da hikayesi son ana kadar sürükleyiciliğini hiç bırakmadı.

[h1]Eski Başyapıt[/h1]

Oyunu bitirdim tek kelimeyle enfesti! Aksiyon bir saniye bile durmadı. Müziği beni hep tetikte bekletti, bir sonraki bölüme geçme heyecanı hep zirvedeydi. Sanki bir diziydi. İki karakter arasında gidip geldik, aynı zamanda kendimizi kovaladık, sonra birlik olduk ve doğrular ortaya çıktı. Hikayesine emek verilmiş, her bölümünde bunu gördük çokça hissettik. Ben "Tamam, bu kadardır." derken üstüne ekledikçe ekledi. İyi işler görmeyeli çok oldu. 2007 yapımı bir oyunun bu kadar kapsamlı, derin bir hikâyesi ve oynanışı olacağını hiç beklemiyordum. Birkaç saatlik, sıradan bir hikaye sanıyordum. Her şeyiyle beni çok şaşırttı. Günümüzde bu kadar uğraş verilmezken eskiye dönük bu oyunu oynamak, eskinin ne kadar kaliteli işler yaptığını hatırlattı. Eski oyunların yeri başkaydı, insanlara ve oyunculara gerçekten değer verildiği zamanlar.. Eskinin verdiği kalitenin yanında, oyunda bir sürü hatayla cebelleşmekte bezdirmedi değil 😄​ iki farklı karakterin oynanış mekanikleri, atmosferi gerçekten çok sürükleyiciydi.

"The Lord has made me his right hand. So Billy, beware boy, for I bring the wrath of God."
-Ray McCall

[h2]Hikaye & Karakterler[/h2]

Hikayede inanılmaz karakterler ustaca işlenmiş. Oyunda tamamen farklı iki ana karakter var, Ray ve Billy her birinin kendine özgü yetenekleri, kusurları ve oyun tarzları var. Bu farklılık onları olağanüstü akılda kalıcı şekilde iyi tasarlamışlar. Buna üst düzey seslendirme eklenince deneyim tamamen sürükleyici hissettiriyor.

Bizim Billy henüz genç bir adam. Geri kasabaya dönüyor. Biz dönünce Thomas'ı öldürüyorlar ama biz yapmıyoruz. Ray, onun öldüğünü görüyor. Biz de kaçarken denk gelince bizim yaptığımızı sanıyor. Aslında biz de birkaç dakika öncesinde denk gelip öğreniyoruz. [spoiler]Oyunun sonunda kimin Thomas'ı öldürdüğünü ögreniyorum meğerse Juan öldürmüş. Kendisi katiller çetesinin lideri aynı zamanda Billy'nin öz babası oluyor, nedeniyse Marisa yani karısı onu terk edip Thomas'a aşık olması[/spoiler]

Ray ise eskiden çok kötülük yapmış bir adam. Sonradan imana gelip insanlara vaaz veriyor, onları yola sokmaya çalışıyor. Ama bu olaylar kardeşinin ölümünden sonra onu eski haline döndürmeye başlıyor. Şerif gözü önünde öldürülünce serseri, eşkiya kim varsa indiriyor. Amacı Billy'nin yani bizim oynadığımız diğer karakterin peşine düşüp kardeşinin intikamını almak. Biz uzun süre kaçıp bir yandan da çakal itle savaşarak hayatta kalmaya çalışıyoruz. Ray ise Billy'yi yakalamak için elinden geleni yapıp peşinden geliyor ama ne gelmek! Sanki Terminatör gibi hep bir adım geride her yerde karşımıza çıkıyor. Bir yandan da biz hem kendimiz kaçıyor hem peşimize kendimiz düşüyoruz 😂 Oyun, hem kaç hem yakala hırsının hakkını fazlaca veriyor. Biz de "Ne olacak sonunda, kendimizi mi avlayacağız?" diye düşünüp duruyoruz (en azından ben düşündüm). Bir remake yapılsa sorunlu hatasız yeniden bir yapımı.. özledik böyle her şeyin tadında yapıldığı oyunları.

[h3]Ufacık Detaylar Harika İşler[/h3]

Oyunda at arabasını kovalamak çok keyifliydi. Onu kovalarken atla peşinden gitmek, bir yandan da başka atlıların silahlarla, tüfeklerle peşimizde oluşu tam aksiyon filmi havasındaydı, Vahşi Batı atmosferinde gerçekten macera peşinde, gerçek kovboylar gibiydik. Bu oyuna başlarken bu kadar uzun ve düşünülmüş olmasını beklemiyordum, özellikle bu kadar eski bir oyunda. Farklı silahların az da olsa gelişi, bunun gibi güzel eklemeler titizlikle düşünülmüş. Bazı nadir silahlar, mesela pompalı tüfeği bırakıp dürbünlü bir silah bulunca o dönemin keskin nişancı hissiyatını veriyordu. Adamlara genellikle tek atan tabanca da vardı. Silahları aşırı kullandığımızda kırılıp paslanabiliyor, bunu bile o yıllarda düşünüp yapmışlar.

Ray McCall daha sert bir abimiz gibiyken Billy Candle daha genç, toy, kızılderili imajında giden bir karakterdi. Oyun sadece tek karakterin hikayesini değil, iki farklı karakterin gözünden oynayıp anlamamızı sağlıyorlar. Ray ağır ortalığı toza dumana katarken Billy ok ve yay gibi sessiz, odak isteyen silahları kullanıyodu. Üstüne kırbacıyla daldan dala atlaması da parkur ve puzzle çözmesine yardımcı oluyordu.

Ray'in özelliklerinden biri ise düşmanı görünce belli zamanlarda konsantrasyon modunu açıp Max Payne Bulley zamanı ile birden fazla düşmana aynı anda ateş edebilmesi, Max Payne gibi zamanı yavaşlatıp silahlarını ateşleme özelliği koymaları kalabalık düşmanlarda çok işinize yarıyor. Yakında ise daha kolay hedef olup ölebiliyorsun.

Oyunda iki kısım beni sıktı. Bunlar sadece aksiyon olsun istemedikleri için farklılık olsun diye konmuş. Açıkçası pek sorun etmedim, sadece parkur ve tırmanma kısımları sıkıcıydı. 

Silahların nişan aldığım yere vurmadığı zamanlar "Hadi hadi, vur artık!" dediğim oldu. Çünkü tam nişan alsanız bile gidip kutuyu vuruyordu ya da mesafe yetişmiyordu. Bazen de düşman birden tekliyordu.

Oyun hep kayıt yapmaya yöneltiyor çünkü en ufak hatada ölürseniz sizi baya geriye atabiliyor
Ray'in dublajı beni benden aldı. Billy Ray'i gördüğünde o korku anı anlatılmaz yaşanır!

[h3]Hatalar[/h3]

Review:
As someone who has played cowboy games—not to an extreme extent, but just enough to really love the genre—I have to say that, in my opinion, this game is absolute perfection.

Story and Characters:
The story is incredible, and the characters are brilliantly crafted. The game features two completely different protagonists, Ray and Billy, each with their own unique abilities, flaws, and playstyles. This contrast makes them exceptionally well-designed and memorable. Add to that top-tier voice acting, and the experience feels completely immersive.

Visuals and Mechanics:
Visually speaking, considering it came out in 2006, the graphics are more than decent, featuring beautiful environments that capture the true vibe of the Wild West.

The gameplay system also has some awesome details—for instance, the mechanic where you can pick up enemy weapons off the ground, only for them to occasionally break or explode in your hands, adding a great layer of tension and realism to the action. On top of that, the shooting mechanics are amazing; when things get intense, you get that awesome slow-motion effect where you draw your pistols and take everyone down like a true outlaw.

World and Freedom:
Although Call of Juarez isn't a true open-world game, it somehow manages to give you that exact feeling. It might not be fully open, but it delivers a specific atmosphere and a sense of freedom, giving you plenty of space to enjoy the surroundings depending on the mission and situation.

The Flaws and Rough Edges
As good as the game is, it also has its flaws, which are key to the overall experience.

1. Billy’s Stealth and Pacing:
First, let's talk about Billy. Even though he’s well-designed as a character, his gameplay sections can be a catastrophe when it comes to progression. When you have to play quietly and stealthily, the process is way too long, and if you mess up just a little bit, you have to restart from the very beginning. While playing as Ray—who just blasts everything in sight—is always fun, playing as Billy often feels more like a tedious delay and waiting for something interesting to happen. However, a huge plus is that if you get caught during these stealth sections, you aren't completely forced to replay it: you have the choice to fight your way out and defend yourself instead of strictly adhering to stealth (depending on the situation, of course).

2. Jumping and Lasso Physics:
The second major issue is the jumping and lasso physics. The way the characters jump is honestly funny and stupid—they jump like they weigh 300 tons, barely clearing 5 centimeters off the ground! And don't even get me started on the lasso. Because of this poor jumping physics, you can easily slip, fall, and die multiple times in the exact same spot. Things that look simple on paper turn into frustrating platforming hurdles when trying to get from point A to point B.

3. Clunky Duels:
The third thing is the duels. They are a bit imprecise; while I understand the developers wanted them to be challenging, the mechanic feels so clunky that a slight refinement would have made it much better.

4. Enemy Variety and AI:
Finally, the enemies are a bit repetitive. You mostly fight gang members and Native Americans, with no real variety beyond those two archetypes. On top of that, the AI isn't particularly smart—enemies often just stand in one place and wait until you shoot them, lacking the tactical awareness to properly take cover or adapt, though they do occasionally peek or react when you get close. Still, the AI could definitely use some improvement.

Recommended. A mid-2000s western shooter that alternates a stealth-hunting drifter with a sermon-fuelled preacher's gunplay, trading polish for personality and two-protagonist storytelling, and the trade still holds.

Mouse-driven quick-draw duels register cleanly, concentration slow-mo elevates the mine, train and fort set pieces, and a wieldable Bible plus rust-and-explode weapon durability give the preacher's chapters real character. Dev wanted posters and a moral-irony script outclass the era's average. The stealth passages are genuinely the hardest part of the game, and that difficulty earns respect rather than resentment.

Whip and lasso traversal is finicky and momentum-less on climbs, stealth detection swings between unfair and blind, and health pickups dry up exactly when the train bridge needs them. Tolerate the jank and the duels justify the trip.

A primeira impressão que o jogo dá é um baita choque generacional.

Jogar Call of Juarez em 2026, em meio à discussão a respeito do jogo novo do Wolverine, foi um abrir de olhos. Temos o pináculo da filosofia ludonarrativa moderna, com sêmen de dev por todo o mapa e todos os vícios da indústria AAA, e aqui temos um jogo de 2008 com mecânicas esotéricas, exploração carregada pelo level design e uma história madura em todos os sentidos, desde os temas, os diálogos e a estrutura da história.

Foi difícil entender Call of Juarez, falando como um gamer moderno. Atirar não é tão satisfatório sem hitmarkers ou recuo nas armas, falta o refinamento com o qual estou acostumado. Uma das principais mecânicas do jogo é a de sacar sua arma durante os duelos, e isso envolve puxar o mouse tão rápido que precisei virar o mousepad na vertical para poder cobrir a distância necessária. É algo tão estranho, mas ao mesmo tempo tão diferente. Sinto falta de quando jogos eram assim, únicos. Quando jogos faziam de tudo para se sobressaírem em relação ao resto. Mas isso também quer dizer que CoJ é um jogo estranho, fora das convenções. Eu precisei me aclimar a ele. Aprender a gostar.

Depois desse ponto, que aconteceu por volta das duas horas, entendi onde estava a diversão do jogo. Segmentos de stealth e de tiroteio tirados de filme clássico de faroeste, e uma história previsível, mas que entrega tudo que se poderia esperar da fórmula.

A idade, apesar do charme que ela traz, acaba se mostrando de formas negativas também. Os gráficos do jogo não envelheceram tão bem, ele não roda tão fácil em sistemas modernos, esse tipo de coisa. Uma rara instânica na qual penso que um remaster poderia melhorar a experiência. Ao mesmo tempo, certas coisas se perderiam simplesmente porque não se fazem mais jogos como esse. O uso de certas palavras, a posição que mulheres e minorias ocupam na história. As sensibilidades atuais não comportam um jogo como esse, em mais de um sentido.

Gostei bastante. Vamos ver se a sequel melhora a experiência como um todo.

Polski deweloper Techland zyskał sławę dzięki serii Call of Juarez; pierwszy z czterech obecnie dostępnych odcinków ukazał się w 2006 roku. Ukończyłem go wtedy kilka razy – mam gdzieś na półce sklepową wersję. Zdecydowałem się kupić ją również przez Steam, żeby móc wyrazić swoją opinię na jej temat. 6 godzin spędzonych z grą pokazuje czas ukończenia jej historii.
Chłopcy: gra w Red Dead Redemption
Męskie: odtwarza Call of Juarez
W serialu Call of Juarez musi być najlepszy, Techland wykonał dobrą robotę, przedstawiając stary westernowy motyw,
broń działa dobrze i masz swobodę używania jednego rewolweru, dwóch z nich pod bokiem, używania różnych rodzajów broni dwuręcznej, takiej jak strzelby, piły, karabiny, LUB! możesz być twardzielkiem i czytać Biblię, strzelając do bandytów. A skoro mowa o byciu twardzielkiem, głównym bohaterem jest wielebny Ray, któremu podkłada głos Marc Alaimo, który nie tylko wykonał świetną robotę, ale jest to jeden z głównych powodów, dla których po prostu KOCHAM tę grę, nie wspominając już o tym, że sama historia uczy ważnych lekcji.
Granica Polski?

To właśnie podoba mi się w tej grze najbardziej. Polski zespół programistów dostosował amerykańską granicę do litery. Można tu znaleźć wszystko, co lubisz na Dzikim Zachodzie: bohaterowie dzierżący dwa pistolety, jeżdżący konno, używający lassa, złoczyńcy krzyczący „żółtobrzuch”, rdzenni Amerykanie mówiący w swoim rdzennym języku (chyba Navajo), pojedynki z bossem ostatniego poziomu, kaniony i doliny w oddali, bandyci próbujący napaść na pociąg, strzelanie z karabinów, spotykanie prostytutek w salonie i kowbojskie kapelusze lecące po nocy strzał w głowę w niezbyt dobrym momencie.

Dwa Asy

Aby było ciekawiej, wszystkie powyższe zdarzenia mają miejsce, gdy jeden z naszych bohaterów, Billy, jest ścigany przez innego o imieniu Ray. Ten pierwszy jest błędnie uważany za mordercę, drugi za ścigającego go rewolwerowca, który stał się księdzem. Co więcej, legenda o złocie Juareza jest również zawarta w tej opowieści o Dzikim Zachodzie, która składa się z 15 rozdziałów. Zawsze zostaje jeden odcinek dla Billy'ego, który jest ekspertem w posługiwaniu się lassem i łukiem, ale jeśli nie będziemy uważać, łatwo go zastrzelić. Zalecana jest rozgrywka w ukryciu, jeśli jest dostępna. Ray natomiast nosi zbroję, bardziej nadaje się do strzelanin i często będziemy brać udział w pojedynkach. Nie musisz trzymać pistoletu w obu rękach - możesz trzymać Biblię i jednym naciśnięciem przycisku „ogień” Ray może zacytować fragment Biblii, jednocześnie rozpętając piekło na wrogu.

„Para sześciu strzelców pokonuje parę asów”.

Myślę, że ta gra jest trudniejsza niż ta, do której ludzie są przyzwyczajeni obecnie. Automatyczne zapisywanie nie jest zbyt regularne, więc możesz używać szybkich zapisów tak często, jak to możliwe. Uważam, że podkład głosowy i muzyka są niesamowicie dobre – szkoda, że ​​od ostatniego odcinka (Gunslinger) minęło 5 lat. Bardzo chciałbym zobaczyć nową grę CoJ z możliwościami przeglądarki Chrome obecnej generacji lub z nowym silnikiem. Nie ma zbyt wielu gier FPS o tematyce zachodniej, ale jeśli lubisz gatunek, Call of Juarez musi znaleźć się w Twojej bibliotece. Gra zawieszała się dopiero, gdy byłem w menu ustawień - nawet po wielu latach mogłem ją łatwo uruchomić bez żadnych usterek.
Czy ta recenzja była możliwa?

A game which is at times clunky and misshapen, but also often gritty and admirable for its reach.

This was 2006, and we were still in the process of figuring out how to structure and design sweeping three dimensional narrative titles. Yes this is an FPS, but it is also at times an awkward 3D platformer, a sort-of-open world adventure, a stealth game, and a throwback to Sergio Leone's spaghetti westerns. 

The gunplay ranges from awful to quite good, depending on what you happen to be wielding. I understand the desire to create a sense of progression, but the early rusty poopoo-peepee guns you spend the first third of the game carrying around often leave you feeling at the mercy of luck rather than skill as bullet trajectory veers wildly from one shot to the next. Once you get rifles and bows in the mid-game it almost becomes too easy to mow down the millions of bandits that clog the west, although shots are always punchy and satisfying. 

Platforming is often dodgy, although the whip is the real culprit. Its momentum-based usage feels at odds with the otherwise stiff and deliberate nature of the vertical sections of the game. I suppose a solid 50% of my deaths in the first half of the game were due to missed whip-aided jumps rather than bullets, and it really doesn't feel good bouncing off the level geometry to your doom. The stealth segments are where we really suffer though, as the mechanics of hiding (crouch in a bush) are far too basic to facilitate anything other than tedious waiting games as racist ranchers and angry farmers amble slowly from one end of a field to another. They are mercifully brief if you can get them right, but good luck getting by without a half dozen retries.

Ultimately a half-shapen lump of clay that can be striking, but is often clumsy and narratively derivative. It is however an interesting look for those of you who are interested in exploring when game design in mainstream titles felt more like the wild west.

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
Xpand Rally Xtreme es un juego de [b]carreras todoterreno[/b] con aspiraciones de [b]simulador de automóviles[/b]: tierra, lodo, derrapes largos y esa sensación de que el auto pesa lo suficiente como para discutirle a la física… pero igual termina obedeciéndola cuando te pasas de listo en una curva.

La primera impresión es clara: esto va de [b]domar el terreno[/b], no de lucirte con neones. Si vienes buscando una experiencia de rally “a lo arcade”, aquí te van a exigir más manos que excusas. Y si vienes por el multijugador… bueno, trae una ouija, porque [b]no hay nadie[/b].

[h2]Lo Bueno vs. Lo No Tan Bueno (modo Rally: tracción total, paciencia parcial)[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
 [b]Enfoque todoterreno[/b] que se siente alineado con su propuesta de simulación   
 [b]Ideal para un jugador[/b]: puedes competir sin depender de que exista vida inteligente en los servidores   
 [b]Multijugador incluido[/b] (sí, existe… en teoría)   
 [b]361 recomendaciones[/b]: señal de que, al menos, a varios les sacó una sonrisa o un latigazo de nostalgia   

Lo No Tan Bueno:
 [b]0 jugadores actuales[/b]: el multijugador es una sala de espera eterna con eco   
 [b]0 logros disponibles[/b]: Steam no te va a aplaudir aunque manejes como dios del barro   
 [b]Depende mucho de tu tolerancia al “simulador”[/b]: si esperas gratificación instantánea, aquí te dan tierra en la cara   
 [b]Comunidad apagada[/b]: para un juego con modos online, esto se siente como invitar gente a una fiesta y que llegue tu gato

[h2]Conclusión (Aceptable)[/h2]
Xpand Rally Xtreme es como ese piloto veterano que todavía sabe manejar, pero ya no lo invitan a las competencias grandes. En [b]un jugador[/b] puede ser disfrutable si te gusta el enfoque de [b]simulación todoterreno[/b] y no necesitas que el juego te esté premiando cada 30 segundos por respirar.

El problema es el elefante en la habitación: [b]0 jugadores actuales[/b]. Tener multijugador así es como venderte un estadio con asientos premium… pero sin público, sin partido y con el vendedor de palomitas de vacaciones. Aun así, sus [b]361 recomendaciones[/b] sugieren que hay un núcleo que lo valora, aunque hoy esté más silencioso que chat de clan a las 3 a.m.

I remember trying this back in the days and thinking its hardcore and unforgiving... 
And now I've just blasted through the career mode without breaking a sweat XD
I guess I can pat myself on the back for making such progress as a gamer ;p 

Imo, it still looks good, and it's just very easy on the eyes with its colorful but not oversaturated color palette, sharp and detailed car models, long drawing distance, different times of day and weather effects affecting not only looks, but also the driving itself. 
 
 Cars are similar, but legally distinct from the real-life rally classics :) Each model is easily recognizable and you can tell where it draws inspiration from, even if you aren't a big time car guy. 
 You have to buy all your cars yourself, modify and tune up with your hard-earned money, repair if you destroy them and even change tires regularly. 
 It sounds more hardcore than it really is. Most of the time I managed to win races on first or 2nd try, as the margin for mistakes the game leaves for you is rather wide. 
If you stay focused and use brakes sometimes, you should stack up big pile of cash and collect (or win in races) at least 3 - 5 cars in the span of your career. 
 So even if theoretically you can lose all your money and destroy all your cars - and therefore lose completely in career mode, it's rather unlikely to happen, unless you intentionally go for auto-destruction. 

The game has few big maps with different environments, and all the tracks are marked out within their constrains. So, you will see the same corners, straights, hairpins or bridges on many different races. 
 It's all completely fictional, and only loosely mimics real-life rally stages, but is pretty creatively laid out, and will throw at you a solid flurry of different corners, hills and valleys, bridges, jumps etc... 
 There's a impressive amount of physically active assets around the tracks, so you can destroy some fences or barriers when you crash into them. 
 Also, many corners look like they were designed to be cut, often you can squeeze your car between the palmtrees and gain half a second on your opponents. It's risky, bc just a small touch of a tree trunk at high speed can shatter your chance of winning, but the game just let's you take that risk and doesn't restart your car immediately and doesn't impose a penalty on you for cutting. 
 Very cool, I like when racing games don't punish me for having fun :)

Xpand Rally Xtreme, developed and published by Techland, is a rally racing game that seeks to strike a balance between realistic driving physics and accessible gameplay. Set against the backdrop of various challenging rally courses around the world, the game aims to immerse players in the high-octane, adrenaline-fueled world of off-road racing. From the outset, it becomes clear that Xpand Rally Xtreme is designed for players who appreciate both the thrill of fast-paced racing and the nuance of vehicle tuning and terrain mastery.

One of the most compelling aspects of Xpand Rally Xtreme is its focus on the authenticity of driving mechanics. The game’s physics engine emphasizes the ruggedness of rally racing, making every jump, slide, and turn feel impactful and demanding. The tracks themselves are packed with features that mirror real-world rally challenges—steep inclines, sharp corners, moguls, and varying surfaces like gravel, dirt, and mud. This variety ensures that players must constantly adapt their driving style to maintain control and speed. The sense of momentum and weight transfer in the cars is palpable, giving the player a strong connection to the vehicle and the environment. Mastering these dynamics is rewarding but requires practice, contributing to a steep but satisfying learning curve.

Xpand Rally Xtreme further deepens its gameplay through a detailed car tuning system. Players can modify key components such as the turbocharger, suspension, brakes, and tires, tailoring their vehicles to specific tracks and racing conditions. This layer of customization adds strategic depth, as fine-tuning can mean the difference between winning and losing. The tuning interface, while not overly complex, offers enough granularity to appeal to enthusiasts who want to experiment with setups. Alongside vehicle adjustments, the game features an economic system where race winnings can be used to purchase new cars or repair damage, injecting an element of resource management into the racing experience.

The game offers a variety of racing modes, broadening its appeal. The Off-Road Series focuses on 4x4 extreme cars tackling rough terrain, emphasizing endurance and control, while the Touring Challenge mode shifts to high-powered GT and DTM supercars, offering a faster, more aggressive racing experience. These distinct modes provide a welcome change of pace and allow players to test their skills across different driving disciplines. Each race mode brings unique challenges and requires a slightly different approach, keeping the gameplay fresh and engaging over time.

Visually, Xpand Rally Xtreme presents a solid if somewhat dated package. The environments are well-designed with attention to detail in the tracks, including environmental features like rocks, trees, and weather effects that influence driving conditions. The dynamic weather system adds another layer of realism, with rain or fog impacting visibility and traction, forcing players to adapt their driving. While the graphics may not compare to modern racing titles, they remain functional and contribute effectively to the game’s immersive atmosphere. The sound design complements the visuals, with engine noises, tire screeches, and ambient sounds enhancing the sense of being in the middle of a high-stakes rally race.

However, the game is not without its drawbacks. The difficulty level is notably high, especially for players new to rally racing. The unforgiving physics and punishing track designs can lead to frequent crashes and vehicle damage, which may frustrate casual gamers. The economic system, while adding depth, can also slow progression for those who struggle to win races consistently. Additionally, some players might find the game’s presentation and user interface somewhat clunky or outdated, which can impact accessibility and overall enjoyment.

In summary, Xpand Rally Xtreme is a rally racing game that caters primarily to players seeking a realistic and challenging off-road driving experience. Its detailed physics, vehicle customization, and diverse racing modes combine to create a rich and rewarding package for fans of the genre. Although its difficulty and dated visuals may limit its appeal to a broader audience, those who appreciate the nuances of rally racing and are willing to invest the time to master its mechanics will find Xpand Rally Xtreme to be a compelling and immersive title that delivers a true taste of the sport’s demanding nature.

Також, що до пошкоджень, тут усе поділено. Мотор, колеса, корпус, батарея, коробка передач, шасі, усе що основне - окремо. Також є пошкодження водія. Вони теж впливають на керування. Траси - цікаві, на них не нудно. Самі перегони тримають баланс темпу, не повільно й не занадто швидко, а це великий плюс, як на мене. На 11 віндовс запускається та працює відмінно, жодних нарікань. Będąc na 82% w karierze, po przejechaniu jakieś tam trasy w Japonii wyskakuje mi okienko z informacją, że tam "Gratulejszyn, skończyłeś karierę, jesteś zaje*isty", nawet pomimo tego, że zostały jeszcze do zrobienia dwa etapy "Premium" i cała masa odcinków "Xtreme" (nawet jednego nie ukończyłem, bo chciałem sobie to zostawić na koniec kariery). Есть немало хороших и интересных стратегий про Вторую мировую, но на их фоне больше всех выделялась серия игр В тылу врага или же Men of War. Причём выделялась она своими механиками, а именно модульностью повреждения техники, возможностью прямого управления юнитом и инвентарём у юнитов.

Чёрные бушлаты, они же Men of War: Red Tide, не исключение из этого правила, и отличительные механики серии тут присутствуют. Сама же игра показывает нам черноморский театр боевых действий во время Великой Отечественной войны. Как понятно из названия, управлять мы будем в основном морской пехотой. Это означает, что нас ждут высадки на берега, в порты, прорывы обороны, а также диверсионные операции в тылу врага. В общем, всё, чтоб понять, насколько тяжела жизнь морского пехотинца и почему они считаются элитой.

Что по геймплею?
Миссии тут можно разделить условно на 2 типа. Первый тип это прорывы и захваты. Сюда можно отнести высадки на берега и в порты, прорывы линии обороны и захваты городов. Второй тип это работа ДРГ. Сюда же отнесём все диверсионные операции. Причём в обоих типах нам дают ограниченное количество юнитов, которых стоит беречь. 
Если с первым типом миссий всё понятно, то вот второй тип по началу превращается в подобие стелса, где маленький отряд должен выполнить большую миссию, а значит каждый боец на счету, как и боеприпасы, что требует время от времени следить за количеством оставшегося БК в инвентаре юнита. Благо лутать трупы и подбитую технику в данной серии игр можно. Также в данном случае модульность повреждений техники важная механика, которая позволяет захватить тот же танк, чтобы облегчить себе миссию.

Что ещё из интересного?
Самое главное тут это исторический справочник, который можно почитать и узнать о той или иной операции и как она проходила. Причём он открывается по мере прохождения. Также из интересного это вступительная заставка. Не, ну вы её видели и слышали? Тут даже говорить не о чем, это великолепно.

Что по минусам?
Любая игра имеет как сильные, так и слабые стороны. В данном случае слабой стороной выступают скрипты. Что же скрипты любят делать? Правильно, ломаться и говорить "привет, рестарт". Ну и, как обычно, при частых загрузках игра может просто вылететь, да и в особо редких случаях крашнуться на миссии. На маленькие недочёты и баги можно закрыть глаза и списать всё на то, что игра старенькая.

Что в итоге?
В итоге мы получаем достаточно сложную и относительно реалистичную стратегию, которая местами заставит помучиться, но также даст нам достаточное количество миссий, чтобы скоротать пару вечеров.

Men of War: Red Tide is one of the most underrated entries in the franchise. While it doesn't introduce revolutionary gameplay changes, it delivers one of the richest and most rewarding single-player campaigns in the entire series.

Rather than revisiting the usual World War II battles, the game follows the legendary Soviet Naval Infantry—the Black Coats—through more than twenty missions spanning the Black Sea campaigns and the final offensives of the war. The historical setting feels fresh, and the sheer variety of objectives keeps the campaign engaging from beginning to end.

The core Men of War formula is as brilliant as ever. Every soldier, vehicle, weapon, and shell matters, rewarding careful planning, smart resource management, and tactical improvisation. The series' signature Direct Control mechanic remains one of the best features ever introduced in a tactical RTS, allowing you to take manual control of any unit whenever precision matters most.

The game also expands the battlefield with new units, amphibious operations, armored trains, naval support, and additional equipment, making many missions feel distinct despite the Soviet-only perspective.

Its biggest drawback is the complete lack of multiplayer, and some missions can be brutally unforgiving. Still, if you're looking for an outstanding single-player tactical RTS, Red Tide is one of the finest games in the series and an easy recommendation for any Men of War fan.

Pro tip: Hold CTRL to enter Direct Control mode. Knowing when to switch between RTS commands and Direct Control is the key to victory—and yes, don't hesitate to abuse it.

A worthy addition to the Men of War series, Red Tide provides more RTS squad based action, continuing the Soviet struggle with 22 varied and challenging missions, spread across 6 unique campaigns.

From the Soviet perspective, Red Tide immerses the player within the operations of the naval infantry of the Black Sea Fleet, creating an engaging and captivating experience. The storyline is excellent, the selection of historically accurate weapons and vehicles is vast providing significant replay value (especially in direct control).

Like previous installments of Men of War, being an older title, the game is a little buggy at times. There also appears to be an issue with the music in the steam edition of this game. In addition, your virus guard might view Red Tide as a threat and initially prevent the running of it.

That being said, if you can get over the small issues, Red Tide is another Men of War game that is worth playing, and can be picked up for a relatively small price.

Внешне это та же самая История рыцаря с почти те же самыми шутками, рекрутами, школами магии и системой прокачки. Но на самом деле это ужасная косячная игра, которую сгубил отвратительный геймдизайн. Играть решительно невозможно, всё сделано в стиле "аля хардкор", лишь бы игроку было некомфортно. Вместо нон-стоп схваток мы теперь по пять минут реального времени восстанавливаем ману, ярость сливается в ноль за пару шагов, а шагать мы будет много, плавать между островами в поисках хоть кого-нибудь, кого сможем победить. Почти все встреченные враги после первого острова - имбы. Мы - слабое звено, прощайте! Превозмогая, сжимая зубы, мы потихоньку идём вперёд, чтобы столкнуться с главной сложностью - запасы юнитов и расходников не восстаналиваются!  Или практически "не". Денег никогда не хватает - ведь за квесты платят скудно, а людские потери из-за нерфа школы магии невероятно велики. Да, в конце у вас окажутся лишние миллионы, только вот и игра внезапно закончится. Боссы - Бурильщик, Залгадис, Ящер - просто чудовища, ломающие баланс. У каждого персонажа, даже не мага, мана под двести. У вас - ну, если сотня, то моё почтение. Мана сливается влёт. В бою вы только и думаете, что о драгоценной мане. Маги просто недоразумение. Если, конечно, они не воюют против вас. Сам геймдизан следующий - уже на первом уровне вам дают задание убить какое-то чудовище на каком-то острове. К слову, этот остров я нашёл к уровню двадцатому и ещё долго раскачивался, чтобы вообще живым добраться, не то, чтобы кого-то победить. Какой в этом смысл? Какой смысл давать новичку в принципе невозможные задания? Карты островов приходится отбивать у стражей - отрядов мобов, превосходящих вас на две головы. Чтобы их победить, приходится тупо раскачиваться - искать слабаков на всех картах. Ваш геймплей - это бесконечная беготня в поисках фарма. Вы не будете играть, красиво драться и читать прикольные диалоги - вы будете страдать, копить деньги и кристалы магии. Почему мы слабаки? Потому что с повышением уровня больше не растут статы защиты, маны и атаки. Всё это открывается только рунами. Любой встреченный персонаж раскачан лучше нас. Мы - отстой. Со второй попытки - лет десять между попытками - я прошёл этот кошмар. Игра становится терпимой с тридцатого уровня, комфортной - с сорокового. Но даже на 50 я всё равно страдал от босов. Страдал - подбирая тактики. Страдал - от потерь драгоценных юнитов, за которыми приходилось даже в ад спускаться! Каждая смерть юнита - это новая беготня на другой конец света.
Самое забавное, что игру починить проще простого: если ничего не менять - просто добавить патчем восстановление рекрутов и расходников в магазинах. Уменьшить скорость падения ярости. Разрешить применение дракона против боссов. Или пойти сложным и правильным путём и переписывать квесты, награды и прочее. Сейчас - это История рыцаря, сделанная в режиме хардкор-мод с нарочитым и бессмысленным усложнением. Повторять сей опыт нет никакого желания. А вот в Историю Рыцаря я ещё  не раз поиграю.

It's pretty fun, but I can't in good consciousness recommend this to anyone that is actually interested in completing games. The fundamental problem is that the game really is just the same thing over and over. You find a battle you can complete with acceptable losses, then you repeat. It drags on too long.

I had previously played "King's Bounty: The Legend" and I was hoping this one had better balance, and it does, but not enough to make the game worth playing. I think one of the fundamental problems is that obtaining higher troop counts requires more leadership, but troops have diminishing returns the more you get, so if you have 10 troops and get enough leadership to get 11 troops then you are only getting a 9% increase, if you have 100 troops and can finally get 101 you'd get less than 1% increase in power. Meanwhile leadership grows linearly so it's a long time before you can get enough troops for it to actually matter, so you never feel powerful. You always feel like you are just making it by.

While I don't like the progression, the game is balanced around it, so I can't say it's a flaw per se, but it just drags on too long. Apparently I've only played for 15 hours, but I don't want to go on. It's not even for lack of being able to find battles I can complete, it's because of boredom. I'm pretty sure I've had as much fun as I'm going to, and I've seen everything the game has to offer. Part of me wants to try to get to the end, but another part of me remembers that in "The Legend" after 40 hours I gave up and cheated to get to the end.

I actually started this game over a year ago, and just left it installed thinking I'd casually come back to it, but I always knew it wouldn't be good, and I was right.

EDIT: To follow up after completing the game, I should mention this is one of those games where boss battles are insanely difficult compare to the rest of the game. They require different strategies, and are inconsistent with the rest of the game. Ultimately I hate the game so much now that I've played it. It's really meant for people that want to punish themselves. Even easy difficulty is not for casual players, so yeah just pass this one unless you are super into strategy games (in which case I don't think this review applies to you).

King's Bounty: Armored Princess es un juego paradójico. Por un lado, refina la fórmula del original, con enemigos que pueden huir, una nueva mecánica de medallas, el dragoncito mascota, y la presencia de muchas tropas nuevas. Por otro lado, pese a continuar la historia del primero, se siente mucho menos fresco. Le falta chispa. Su sentido del humor no termina de aterrizar y el diseño de los mapas (ahora todos islas) se siente más encorsetado. Pese a todo, sigue siendo una barbaridad de juego. Quién sabe si no volveré a él dentro de unos años.

Desde que me recomendaron hace unos 10 años la saga de Kings Bounty me he convertido en un seguidor y jugador casi empedernido de todos los juegos de la saga.

Me encanta el sistema de juego, la estrategia para cada enfrentamiento y el argumento. Tanto que cada vez que termino uno casi vuelvo a comenzar de nuevo con el que terminé mas antiguo :).

Muy recomendable tanto para veteranos como nuevos jugadores.

Its kinda hard to even explain why i sunk 70 hours into this game because its not some 10/10 hidden gem of the past. Its not well balanced.. the story isnt very interesting.. it doesnt really do anything crazy impressive. But i think the game has a lot of charm. It has your usual fantasy tropes but i always found it kinda funny how you just walk up to a demon, expect him to be cartoonishly evil and they are just very chill usually.. same with vampires or nekromancers. Its kinda dumb and i think the translations arent always very well made but its fun. For the gameplay all i can say is that you just have to find some strategy you can abuse because the fights aren't balanced at all... that means you can abuse the system too tho. Overall i don't know if i would even recommend this to the average person but what i enjoyed was the art, the music and also finding out how to game the system. It does have some Mechanics that are fun to play around with. i'd give it a decent 7.5/10 or something.

Игра продавалась по скидке, поэтому решила воспользоваться шансом и потрогать ее. Графика напомнила Warcraft III и игра прям потянула за ниточки ностальгии. В игре несколько островов, которые вы исследуете посредством уничтожения всего что движется и квестов принеси - подай. Первые часы прям весело. Боевка напоминает героев 3. 
В начале игры у вас на выбор 3 класса: воин, паладин и маг. Так вот - играть не за мага = страдания. Ваше количество войск ограничивают очки лидерства, которые по крохам увеличиваются с повышением уровня, некоторых предметов и в виде флажков. Кроме вашей магии и войск у вас есть пет со способностями, но он не будет вам помогать с боссами. Получается такая ситуация: у вас войск с гулькин нос, ящерица помогает, но когда нужна реально помощь линяет и остается только магия. (Вообще как бы вы можете прокачивать хоть все ветки классов, но на начале приоритет на фулл прокачку имеет больше всего именно маг.)
Вишенка на торте это другое - большую часть времени вы потратите не на битву с боссами, не выполнение квестов, а на пополнение армии после пары сражений. Особенно если вы выбрал комфортную команду и ради юнитов надо ездить по разным островам + держать  в голове альтернативные места, так как некоторые юниты имеют ограниченное количество. Эти разъезды очень тянут время игры и выбивают из ритма прохождения.
А так игра атмосферная, много забавных квестов. Я бы ее перепрошла через пару лет снова.

1.1) Раньше интеллект за каждую единицу давал 10% урона атакующим заклинаниям, можно было таааак его разогнать, что чуть ли не любой стак можно было попросту сдуть огненным шаром или армой. Здесь сделали 5%, интеллект и так растет медленно, а теперь еще и урон перестал  заметно расти. 
1.2) Где моя мана? У меня её настолько мало, будто окончил магическую шарагу, а не институт магии. Маны хватало на 2 раунда, иногда 3. Потом самое лучшее. 0 маны. И она не регенится.
1.3) Умение на регенерацию маны, которое было первым в ветке мага в легенде о рыцаре, в принцессе находится в КОНЦЕ левой ветки магии ахахаха. Т.е. ты либо идёшь к регенерации нищих 2 маны за раунд в конце левой ветки, либо в атакующую магию в правой ветке. Но тогда ты пукаешь 2 огненных шара и превращаешься в недовойна, тупо командуя войсками в дефе.
1.4) После боя мана восстанавливается по 1 единице. Ты сидишь минуты 3 просто афк, чтобы пополнить ману, тк перк на ускоренную регенерацию ТОЖЕ в конце левой ветки!!!
1.5) Т.е у мага в начале прохождения нет ни войск с кефом прироста х1, нет маны на заклинания, нет регенерации маны в бою, нет регенерации между боями. Я ощущал себя максимально подавленно от всех этих изменений. Класс мага убили. 
1.6) Плюс ко всему теперь атака, защита, инта, ярость, мана не растут сами по себе за выбор при повышении уровня. Статы нужно искать в умениях. Теперь маг не только нищий, так еще и с 0 атаки и 0 защиты.
2) Игра для тех у кого есть уйма свободного времени. 20 минут на 1 файт на невозможной. И потом еще стоять афк ману регенить. В легенде я уничтожал противников за несколько ходов уже почти сразу после начала игры. Здесь из за отсутствия маны и малого количества войск это майнд геймс по пол часа на один файт без потерь. У меня столько времени на это нет.
3) Перк торговли убрали. Зачем? В легенде я честно прокачал торговлю на 3 и продавал лут по 100% стоимости. В принцессе торговцы лишь тебе по лбу стукнут и по губам поводят за артефакт. ~30 от стоимости это сильно. Меня это не устраивает.
4) Персонаж постоянно застревает казалось бы на ровном месте на глобальной карте, какие-то странные невидимые границы, это настолько часто происходило, что не упомянуть это я не мог. В легенде застреваний вообще не помню практически.
5) Я за 8 часов прочистил 4 острова настолько, насколько мог. Около 40% противников побеждено. Остальные - смертоносные и непобедимые. Карты новых островов украсть я не могу, ведь разрабы привязали намертво мобов охранников к спотам у карт. Больше драться не с кем, принцессовский маг без магического преимущества и без армии ничего не может противопоставить таким. На новые острова я попасть не могу. 
~~~ Как итог скажу, то что получилось в принцессе мне не понравилось вообще. Баланс невозможной убит. Маг убит. Ползунок духоты выкручен на максимум, как и количество мобов во вражеских отрядах. Как-то так.

Бои заставляют интенсивно думать и быть в напряжении на протяжении всего времени. Диалогов в этой игре очень много, не скажу что они супер крутые только из за того, что часто появляется ощущение, что ты этого персонажа как будто видел, но это абсолютно другой, но всё равно они остаются очень вайбовыми и отсылают тебя прямиком в 2000ые. it does not render on the rtx 2080 ti. it is an interesting game however. just wish the developers had fixed that rendering problem. i tested its multiplayer mode and it is stable. it is not exactly easy to play because the gameplay involves fighting very strong neutrals but, it works perfectly. i can unfortunately not recommend it in its current state. the game`s unit cap is built around capturing space stations. that gameplay mechanic does not work at all. capturing stations is completely broken and the invasion genes does absolutely nothing. the game is also very unbalanced, to the point where one faction is very strong and the others is useless(at least the military is weak compared to the defiance). gathering blood from destroyed enemy units is also flawed, as there is a timer on them.

WARNING: This game does not support Modern Intel Graphics Card from Intel HD 4000 and later(Mine was Intel UHD630). I had a dual Graphics laptop I used Nvidia 1050ti to play(not sure about AMD users).

HOW TO GET THE GAME WORKING

i) Disabling steam overlay is the most important thing to get the game running as it doesn't support it properly.

Go to steam Library, right click and click on "properties"
Uncheck both "Desktop Theatre" and "Steam overlay" and save.

ii) Missing files fix that causes crashes

After installing the game make sure you go to "C:\Program Files\Steam\steamapps\common\Genesis Rising"
Right click and create new folders that are missing. Add and rename the missing folders from the following numbers.
1. save 
2. replay 
3. temp
Then open "C:\Programs\Steam\steamapps\common\Genesis Rising\data".
Right click and create one more folder and rename it to "scripts" without quotes.

iii) For GRAPHIC NOT SUPPORTED ERROR. Note: you may have to do this every time you restart computer if you want to play the game. The game was set on default integrate graphics card for me. 

Right click Desktop and open "Nvidia Control Panel". Click on "Manage 3D setting" then click on "Add". Select "Genesis Rising.exe"

On "selected preferred graphic processor for this program" select "High-performanced Nvidia Processor". Leave everything as global settings defaults as I turned off V-sync before and it crashes during mission.

I am not sure for AMD. AMD users may have to do the same thing with their own control panel setup.

iiii) Do not forget to set your game on Low and double check minimum requirements compare to your graphic cards. Minimum requirements players must turn off V-sync in game but not the graphic card control panel manager(do not touch the control manager settings).

REVIEW

There is no point of playing the game on Hard mode, you do not unlock anything (this game is harder than Homeworld). Out of all the Space RTS, this game is the worst. The good thing is there are three endings. You do not have to replay the whole game. It is on the last mission where you chose who to side with. All you need to do is select last mission save point. There is no way to save unlike other Space RTS except loading to next mission. All the saves are autosaves(so be careful starting new game). The Story is meh.

I bought this game a long time back and only just recently manage to make it work.
This method might not work for everyone but for those that want to try anyway for a good old game.
Right click on your desktop
Open Nvidia Control Panel
Select Manage 3D settings
Select Program settings
Click Add then to Browse
Find GenesisRising.Exe it should be at the steam library -> steamapps -> common -> Genesis Rising -> bin
Click open and it should be in the 1. Select a program to customise
At 2. Select the preferred graphics processor choose the High-Performance Nvidia Processor. Don't use Global.
Click apply, wait for it to process.
Now you should be able to open up the game without any problems.
All you need to do now is adjust the graphic settings for the window resolution size so it all fits on the screen.
Enjoy.

Genesis Rising: The Universal Crusade is the only tactical space combat game I know of which uses the idea of organiform spaceships which is even a rare topic in Scifi literature. You upgrade your ships via genetic mutation. The necessary genes can be acquired through devouring conquered enemy ships or by trading with other races. It is fully voice acted and looks quite nice for a ten year old game. Movement is limited to a plane so no six degrees of freedom here.
There is only one catch - you have to get it working on a modern OS. After an hour of testing I succeeded in getting the game running on Win10_64 Pro in 4K. I set the compatibility for TestApp3230.exe and GenesisRising.exe to 'Disable display scaling on high DPI settings' and 'Run this program as an administrator' in the bin subfolder of the SteamLibrary. Good news is the game is already patched  to version 1.0.44 which seems to be the latest. After clicking away the dozen error messages at start up the game starts and runs without issues for me.
Also read this guide http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=842187710 
original post http://forums.steampowered.com/forums/showthread.php?t=2592425 to fix the save and missing ships issue.
I would say if you can get it to work Genesis Rising is a game worth your money especially if you are into obscure and unique space games.
The game itself gets a well deserved 7/10 but keep in mind the possibility that it will not work with your setup.

Genesis Rising на словах выглядит как игра мечты - необычный и действительно оригинальный сеттинг, нелинейный сюжет, тысячи комбинаций для модификации кораблей, даже кооператив завезли! К сожалению, отличная идея похоронена под провальной реализацией практически всех элементов игры.

Поначалу ничего не предвещает беды. Туториал знакомит игрока с ключевыми особенностями Genesis Rising и интригует нестандартным дизайном и геймплеем. Все корабли в игре органические и натурально отращивают оружия и нужные модификации по вашему приказу. Для отращивания оружия нужны гены, которые производятся в генетической лаборатории либо извлекаются с хладных трупов ваших врагов. Главный ресурс в игре - кровь, которую буквально нужно высасывать из жутковато выглядящих "хранилищ" либо из всех тех же останков врагов после битв. Атмосфера так и прет, получив приказ атаковать пилоты истребителей кричат "Высосем их досуха!", а некоторые корабли после попадания ракеты взрываются кровавым пятном, которое буквально застилает весь экран:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=841520907
Выглядит игра пристойно даже несмотря на свой возраст, в наличии космические пейзажи и сочные эффекты вроде той же кровищи на полэкрана. Сюжет поначалу выглядит как хорошая эпическая космоопера, а бои то и дело прерываются диалогами главного героя с другими персонажами, в которых прям как в каком-то Mass Effect можно выбирать каким будет ваш ответ - положительным или отрицательным. В общем, поначалу все выглядит просто замечательно и крайне отрицательные отзывы в стиме удивляют - так и кажется, что ты нашел недооцененный и всеми забытый шедевр из прошлого.

Но чем больше пытаешься играть, тем быстрее Genesis Rising возвращает в реальность. Первыми дают о себе знать технические проблемы - во второй миссии у меня не появились корабли и я некоторое время любовался пустым космосом, не понимая что происходит. Основательно порывшись в обсуждениях на форуме игры, я нашел как исправить эту проблему, так что [b]если у вас игра не сохраняется и не появляются корабли, то здесь описано, как решить эту проблему[/b] - http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=842187710 Заново пройдя первую миссию, я вновь попытался пройти вторую миссию, и когда игра вскоре неожиданно без каких-то видимых причин вывалилась на рабочий стол, выяснился еще один неприятный момент, который исправить уже было невозможно - в Genesis Rising напрочь отсутствует возможность сохраняться в любой момент, так что если вдруг игра вылетела посреди миссии, то извольте начать сначала. 

Ладно бы проблемы только технические. Но когда я в 3 раз попытался пройти ту проклятую вторую миссию, становилось все очевиднее, что все крутые на словах идеи тупо не работают как надо и играть во все это просто неинтересно. Идея с генами оказалась фикцией, потому что нет никакого смысла подбирать разные комбинации генов для каждого отдельного корабля, когда намного проще и эффективнее по максимуму закинуть генов на дальнобойные пушки, обвести все имеющиеся войска рамкой и отправить их на врага. Ни о какой тактике даже речи не идет, бои проходят в двумерном пространстве и постоянно сводятся к унылейшим перестрелкам стенка на стенку. Интерфейс настолько бесконечно далек от понятия "интуитивно-понятный", насколько это только возможно, перетягивать по одному гены в свободные слоты для каждого корабля просто невыносимо муторно. Корабли на команды реагируют заторможено и часто по неведомым причинам прекращают стрелять во врагов. Genesis Rising в целом очень плохо взаимодействует с игроком, в той же второй миссии в самом конце я неожиданно проиграл, когда игра дала задание захватить корабль, который я уже успел сожрать во время битвы ради починки своих кораблей. В итоге с четвертой попытки миссия все же была пройдена, но вот от моего первоначального энтузиазма не осталось и следа. Так что когда игра вылетела в третьей миссии, мое знакомство с Genesis Rising закончилось.

Очень интересная в качестве концепта, но фундаментально сломанная игра. Если с частью технических проблем еще как-то можно бороться, то с пустым геймплеем и дизайнерскими ошибками уже ничего не поделаешь. Genesis Rising интересна разве что для истории, в качестве примера для молодых и амбициозных разработчиков, что не стоит с первым же своим проектом пытаться сделать крупнобюджетную игру с нелинейностью и кооперативом.

Meh. I keep buying these space sims, expecting something that actually attempts to simulate a spaceship. This is really a naval combat game without the water. It's 2-dimensional (the graphics are 3D but the actually playing field is not; you can only move in 2 dimensions). Say what you want about Homeworld not NEEDING a 3rd dimension; at least it had one.

Having said that, this is a pretty unique naval RTS. When you kill another ship, you get to harvest it for both health and abilities for your own ships. I've only played the first couple missions but the mechanics seem solid and the ship customization is very intuitive. Once you've killed a few enemies, it's very easy to customize your identical ships into specialized individuals.

For example: on the second tutorial mission, I loaded all my beams onto one ship, all my short-range projectiles onto the second and all my long-range missiles onto a third. What started out as three ships with two pea-shooters each quickly became a useful unit with very distinct roles.

Haven't played far enough to say how the story or mission variation is but just based on the core gameplay elements, I recommend Genesis Rising.

[h3]TLDR[/h3]
Safecracker is a short, but sweet puzzle game wherein you try to find the will of a deceased safe enthusiast in his mansion, which is bursting with various puzzles. The game requires some tweaks to work okayish with modern hardware. The rest of its enjoyability depends on your tolerance for puzzles. For 4.99 it's perfectly fine.

[h3]The Good[/h3]
The game is very on point. It knows exactly what it wants to be and delivers: puzzles upon puzzles upon puzzles in a big mansion. There is something for everyone here--clues from pictures/letters you find, sudoku, wordle (with numbers), interlocked switches, chess, ciphers, maths, you name it. I appreciate the inclusion of an in-game map that shows which rooms still have unsolved puzzles and which are done. The music is unintrusive, what little voice-acting there is is fine, and the game features multiple endings, so save before you open the last safe!  Speaking of, there are multiple profiles (keys) and within those multiple safe slots, so multiple people can play this at the same time.

[h3]The Bad[/h3]
It is a very short game. I got tripped up by several of the puzzles to the point where I had to use a walkthrough (I am REALLY awful at combination puzzles and I know diddly-squat about chess), and it still only took me around 5-6 hours to finish. Also, if you are planning to stream it, know that it only works properly in windowed mode and some of the music in there will get your video demonetized. Finally, I am going to save everyone some googling: press S to see UI, left mouse to move/interact, and right mouse to access inventory, map and save menu.

[h3]The Ugly[/h3]
This is a 32 bit game that was very much not designed for modern hardware. To get it running even remotely well, I had to force it into Window mode by editing the bFullScreen= value in the config.ini file in the game's install folder. Once that was done, the game booted in a stable state, but half the UI (including the cursor) was invisible unless I kept S pressed, and sometimes the UI would flicker. Finally, the game crashed when selecting one of the endings (the second time I selected that same ending, it worked).

Noticeable issues with menus, they like to either not display text, not show your cursor, or jitter in and out. It is still playable, and quite fun to solve all the puzzles, although I was lazy and partially used a walkthrough for half of them.

Couldn't get it to work on two different machines.  One showed the opening logos, then got stuck on a black screen.  The other flashed the logos, then lagged heavily with mouse movement and sometimes didn't show the mouse pointer,, which made it impossible to click on buttons.  I understand the game is oldish, but I find this unacceptable.
This is a great game, but can we get some Windows 11 fixes for the mouse?

Safecracker: The Ultimate Puzzle Adventure is actually a pseudo sequel of a better regarded game, called just Safecracker. The plot is that you are hired by a family of a rich man who recently died to open all the safes inside his mansion.

The game features a total of 35 safes/locked puzzles. There's no tutorials nor guiding, you just explore the couple of unlocked initial rooms to fiddle with the few safes or mechanisms that are available. This is a linear game, with typical inventory from adventure games that will allow you to open locked doors and get access to more rooms and floors in the mansion.

Most puzzles are fair with the game lasting a couple of hours. There's just one specific puzzle near the start that takes a ton of time to solve, it's one of those jigsaws where you rotate 4 pieces of the puzzle clockwise at the same time. Even knowing the exact solution, is still a chore to solve.

The plot ends up being just an excuse for the setting and puzzles, you will get some development on the relatives that are looking for the final reward as well, but it's completely optional and to add a bit of flavor. There's also a map mechanic to easily check your progress.

It's a cool game while it lasts, some of the challenges are typical stock puzzles, while others are creative enough to be worth of a run.

Mind that this is one of those mid 2000s games that tend to have problems with certain newer hardware. I found no such issues, but your mileage may vary.

I bought this who knows how many years ago, I was probably still on Windows XP or Windows 7 at the time. Either way, I never ran into any issues running the game then or now, when I finally got around to actually playing through it to the end. Perhaps I was merely lucky.

What I can tell is that Safecracker is a rather barebones puzzle game where any and all dialogue is coming from the safe-cracking protagonist here to find the late Duncan Adams' missing will and testament. It is from an era where the games frequently leave you completely in the dark, and if there's a clue somewhere you have to keep your eyes peeled in order to find them. It could be a letter on a sofa arm, it could be something the player character says - and they [i]won't[/i] repeat it - during the middle of a puzzle.

The puzzles will frequently fall into two categories: relatively simple or otherwise straightforward, and absurdly obtuse where you'll either beat your head against the wall until you look it up or have a miraculous serendipity moment of revelation at something you overlooked. There's really no in between. Depending on how much that terrifies or excites you is probably a good indication of whether this is for you or not.

Personally speaking, I doubtless got it on sale and would suggest the same of a potential buyer; it's 20 years old and the original devs are unlikely to see much (if any) of this money now. I openly admit to looking a few answers up, either they were puzzles I didn't want to deal with outright (there was at least two) or I had absolutely no idea what the game was even asking me to look for. The snooker one falls into the latter, although the answer makes sense in hindsight.

So I'll give it a recommendation, but hesitant one. It is an [b]old[/b] game and it shows, but I still found it oddly charming and do not regret the roughly 3 hours it took to complete.

Safecracker: The Ultimate Puzzle Adventure is a cerebral and atmospheric title from Kheops Studio, published by HandyGames, that caters to players who thrive on logic, observation, and patience rather than action or storytelling. It presents a singular premise: you play as a professional safecracker hired by the heirs of a recently deceased billionaire to explore his vast mansion and unlock the thirty-five safes scattered throughout it. Each safe hides clues to the next, leading you deeper into the eccentric millionaire’s obsession with puzzles, mechanisms, and secrecy. Unlike most adventure games that weave puzzles into a narrative framework, Safecracker strips away unnecessary plot embellishments and focuses entirely on intellectual engagement. It is a test of pure reasoning—a puzzle anthology disguised as an exploration of a wealthy man’s labyrinthine estate.

The mansion itself is the real protagonist of the game, a meticulously designed puzzle box filled with ornate rooms, cryptic devices, and intricate contraptions. Navigation is handled through a node-based system that allows full 360-degree viewing, reminiscent of classic titles like Myst or The 7th Guest. Every room is a microcosm of challenge—libraries filled with secret locks, art galleries hiding mechanical riddles, laboratories lined with safes waiting to be decoded. Progress depends on your ability to notice patterns, deduce sequences, and interpret environmental details that often serve as clues to each safe’s solution. The puzzles are extraordinarily varied, ranging from simple number combinations and logic grids to elaborate multi-step mechanisms that require information gathered across several rooms. This diversity keeps the game intellectually stimulating throughout, rewarding players who take notes, think methodically, and enjoy the satisfaction of discovery earned through persistence.

Visually, Safecracker creates a refined yet isolated atmosphere. The environments are rendered with rich textures and detail for their time, evoking the sense of wandering through a luxurious but lonely museum of mechanical curiosities. Each room is distinct—some modern and sterile, others baroque and heavily ornamented—reflecting the eccentric personality of the mansion’s late owner. The absence of characters or dialogue heightens the sense of solitude, immersing the player in a quiet world where the only sounds are the clicks of tumblers, the soft hum of locks, and the occasional triumphant chime of a successfully opened safe. The audio design contributes greatly to the immersion: subtle background noises, gentle ambient music, and mechanical effects create a rhythm that mirrors the mental process of problem-solving—steady, deliberate, and precise.

What sets Safecracker apart from many puzzle-adventure games is its unwavering commitment to logic over narrative. There are no dramatic revelations or emotional arcs—only the gradual satisfaction of unraveling an elaborate chain of interconnected enigmas. This purity of design is both its strength and its weakness. For dedicated puzzle enthusiasts, it offers hours of engrossing problem-solving and a rewarding sense of accomplishment as each new safe opens. For others, especially players seeking character interaction or storytelling depth, the experience can feel sterile and impersonal. The game provides minimal guidance, and its difficulty curve occasionally spikes sharply, leading to potential frustration when clues are too obscure or connections too tenuous. There is no built-in hint system, so progress depends entirely on patience and careful observation. However, for those who relish intellectual rigor, this lack of handholding enhances the authenticity of the experience.

The pacing of Safecracker is deliberate and methodical. Each solved puzzle opens another room or reveals a new piece of information, maintaining a steady sense of progression without ever feeling rushed. The interconnected structure of the mansion allows for a natural rhythm of exploration—moments of discovery followed by stretches of deep concentration. The satisfaction of cracking a particularly complex mechanism or uncovering a hidden code is amplified by the knowledge that every solution is the result of one’s own reasoning rather than chance or scripted convenience. The game demands attention to detail and rewards curiosity, making every corner of the mansion worth investigating. Even when repetition sets in or certain puzzle types reappear, the overall variety of challenges ensures that no two safes feel exactly alike.

Ultimately, Safecracker: The Ultimate Puzzle Adventure succeeds as a celebration of pure problem-solving. It offers an elegant, cerebral experience for those who view puzzles not as diversions but as the essence of gameplay. While it may lack the emotional storytelling or dynamic interactivity of more modern titles, its clarity of purpose and careful craftsmanship give it lasting appeal. It’s a game best enjoyed slowly, with a notebook at your side and the patience to ponder every dial, symbol, and mechanism. For fans of logic puzzles, mechanical contraptions, and the quiet satisfaction of unlocking secrets through intellect alone, Safecracker remains one of the most authentic puzzle experiences ever designed—a rare work that challenges the mind as much as it rewards it.

Juego de puzles en primera persona, adaptación para consolas (de la época) y PC de la versión de 1997. Desarrollado por la compañía francesa Kheops Studio.

[h1]Testamento oculto[/h1]
Duncan W. Adams, magnate multimillonario gracias al negocio del petróleo, ha fallecido. La trifulca familiar por la herencia ha comenzado, pero hay un problema, Adams era un fanático de las cajas fuertes y ha escondido su testamento en una de ellas. Como experto en cajas fuertes, hemos sido contratado para encontrar las escrituras.

Dispondremos de 35 puzles repartidos por toda la mansión por la que nos moveremos “de punto a punto” (como en el clásico [i]Myst[/i]). Podremos mirar alrededor, 360, y nuestro puntero cambiará en función de si es un sitio al que podamos desplazarnos o un elemento con el que interactuar. No es un movimiento rápido pero permite mostrar lo que el juego quiere mostrar, sin temor a que nuestro ángulo no sea el correcto y perdamos algún detalle.

Los puzles a resolver pueden llegar a ser bastante complicados. En general son de observación y lógica; sólo hubo uno que tuve que mirar la solución e incluso entonces no terminaba de convencerme (el de la mesa de billar). Pero también los hay de esos en los que al mover una pieza, cuatro más se mueven, y al mover otra, dos de la anterior también se desplazan mientras que el puzle quiere que lo alineemos todo perfectamente. En la mayoría de ocasiones suelen resolverse más por suerte y fuerza fruta hasta que lo tienes casi alineado y afinas su resolución. Por suerte no son la mayoría.

Algo con lo que no estoy muy de acuerdo es la dirección. Cada puzle resuelto da algo útil para otro, pero no hay orden ni razón. La apertura de una caja en el estudio te puede dar una pista para la solución del museo, o una llave para una sala que visitarás en la segunda planta. Vas de un lado a otro sin ton ni son.

Los escenarios no cuentan con mucha resolución, pero es suficiente para apreciar los detalles necesarios. El audio no es muy relevante, en especial la música, que tiende a sonar en bucle, deteniéndose de vez en cuando para volver después. Un tanto extraña pero al menos no se entromete demasiado.

El juego viene con voces en inglés y textos en español.

Pese al número de desafíos, no debería llevar más de unas 4-5 horas completar el juego, en función de cuánto nos atasquemos con los mencionados puzles con muchas piezas móviles. Existe un único final pero con distintas variaciones dependiendo de cierta decisión. Una vez terminado no se desbloquea nada nuevo.

En cuanto al estado técnico. De primeras no funcionaba, pantalla en negro pero oía la música del menú, simplemente no podía hacer nada. Por suerte, con dgVoodoo2 funciona sin problema, he perdido la cuenta de las veces que este programa me ha permitido disfrutar de juegos antiguos no compatibles o conflictivos con sistemas operativos modernos.

[b]Safecracker: The Ultimate Puzzle Adventure[/b] cuenta con algunos problemillas de diseño y dirección, pero a la vez ofrece algunos puzles la mar de interesantes y desafiantes que es, al fin y al cabo, lo que uno busca en este tipo de títulos. Buena distracción para un fin de semana.

Back before “escape room” overload, in a year 2006, aspiring adventurers were looking forward to pure puzzle games like this one. The set-up is quite simple – you’re in mansion of a deceased rich guy with an obsession for safes and codes, his will is (of course) missing, and his relatives hire you to crack the safes to find it. That’s it, no other fuss.

What follows is quite challenging and varied string of puzzles that will make it irrelevant in what year this game is being played. From math to logic to cryptography to pure observation skills – all this and more can be found in the fancy estate that still got the looks to please the eye. This is a solitary journey through beautifully furnished rooms from safe to safe, as you (with your British TV anchor accent) think of nothing more complex than the current puzzle if front of you, periodically chuckling at the letters from relatives who, for some unexplained reason, might or might not want just a little bit of that sweet uncle’s money.  There’s no complex story, meaningful writing, active characters or impressive cut-scenes to speak of, just puzzles upon puzzles upon puzzles. They aren’t brain-breakingly hard, but they will make you tinker around and think for a bit – which is a welcome activity in the world of QTEs and “choose a dialogue option to progress” games, on occasion. 

The game does have a bit of music – quite good selection of tracks, (some of which strangely seem to be there to create tension in a game where you can pretty much lazily waddle from puzzle to puzzle at your own pace), that tends to cut off and take a few minutes break before restarting again (an old age showing, no doubt), but it does provide for a nice company in this intellectual solo pursuit.

If you like puzzle games- this is an oldie but goodie. Take a look at the guides and/or forums for instructions on how to run it first, and then dive in – this won’t disappoint. It’s actually quite charming in its simplicity. Makes you realize that all the frou-frou stuff we are anticipating from modern games right now isn’t as important in making a solid title. It’s cool to have it, yeah, but it’s by no means necessary, and what do you know – taking a break from it might even feel refreshing.

[h1]Painkiller: Overdose: More of the Same, With Less of the Fun[/h1]

[b]Gameplay & Gunplay: 7/10[/b]

[i]The shooting itself isn't the problem. If you've played Painkiller, you know what you're getting: fast, simple and familiar. But there's nothing new here, and you're just doing the same thing again.[/i]

[b]Level Design & Structure: 4.5/10[/b]

[i]This is where the game falls apart. The levels and their structure are extremely repetitive and boring, and no matter how hard I tried to push through, I couldn't get much further. It was the level design and nothing else that made me drop it, not the graphics and not the gameplay.[/i]

[b]Graphics & Sound: 7/10[/b]

[i]Nothing here bothered me. The visuals and sound do the job and fit the genre, but nothing stands out either.[/i]

[b]Innovation & Content: 5/10[/b]

[i]There's no innovation at all. It feels like it was released just to be released, with no special points to make it memorable.[/i]

[b]Value: 6.5/10[/b]

[i]It might be fine for someone who's sick in bed with nothing better to do. But if you're looking for an experience and real enjoyment, you won't get much out of it.[/i]

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]

[i]Painkiller: Overdose is weak, repetitive and lacks any new ideas. The gameplay is okay and the presentation is fine, but the level design is so tiresome that I dropped it quickly and couldn't make myself go back. I'd only recommend buying it if you're a huge Painkiller fan. Otherwise, it isn't worth your money or your time.[/i]

[h1]Final Score: 6/10[/h1]

[b]Verdict: Not Recommended[/b]

[i]A repetitive, uninspired expansion that only die-hard Painkiller fans should consider.[/i]
