City Life 2008 - Возведите город 21-го века с помощью City Life!City Life 2008 Edition — это строительный симулятор нового поколения. Трехмерный движок игры поднимает планку качества детализации и анимации данного жанра на невиданный ранее уровень и дает полную свободу творчества.

City Life 2008 is a deep and ambitious city-building simulation that reflects a very particular design philosophy from the late 2000s, one that prioritizes complexity, social dynamics, and long-term planning over instant gratification. Rather than simply asking players to zone land and watch a city grow, the game positions you as a true urban planner who must consider not just infrastructure and finances, but the cultural and social makeup of the population itself. From the very beginning, it is clear that City Life 2008 aims to simulate a living, often fragile urban ecosystem where every decision can ripple outward in unexpected ways.

The defining feature of the experience is its focus on social groups and how they coexist within the same city. Citizens are divided into multiple distinct subcultures, each with their own lifestyles, expectations, and tolerance levels for other groups. These differences are not cosmetic; they actively shape how neighborhoods function and whether they thrive or collapse. Placing incompatible groups too close together can lead to dissatisfaction, protests, and even full-blown riots, while careful planning and thoughtful separation or integration can result in stable, prosperous districts. This system forces players to think far beyond simple efficiency, encouraging a more realistic approach to urban design that mirrors real-world challenges such as segregation, gentrification, and social inequality.

City management systems are layered and demanding, offering a sense of scale that feels genuinely earned. Players must balance transportation networks, utilities, public services, employment opportunities, and tax structures while keeping an eye on the needs of each demographic. Roads and public transit must be laid out intelligently to avoid congestion, industrial zones must be positioned to minimize pollution impact, and service coverage must expand alongside population growth. The game rarely holds your hand, and mistakes can compound quickly, making recovery difficult if early planning decisions were flawed. This unforgiving nature can be daunting, but it also gives City Life 2008 a strong sense of consequence that rewards patience and foresight.

Visually, the game was ambitious for its time, presenting fully three-dimensional cities that can be freely rotated and explored at street level. Watching traffic flow through intersections, citizens move between buildings, and neighborhoods take shape provides a tangible sense of scale and immersion. The wide selection of buildings and landmarks allows cities to develop a distinct visual identity, whether you aim for dense urban cores, sprawling suburbs, or carefully curated mixed-use districts. While the graphics and interface now feel dated compared to modern city builders, they still serve their purpose effectively, emphasizing function and readability over visual flair.

The game offers both structured and open-ended ways to play, catering to different player motivations. Scenario-based objectives provide clear goals and constraints, challenging players to reach specific milestones under pressure, while sandbox modes remove most restrictions and allow experimentation with city layouts and social structures. This flexibility makes the game approachable for creative builders as well as those who enjoy problem-solving within defined limits. However, even in its more relaxed modes, City Life 2008 never truly becomes effortless; its systems are always active, quietly judging the sustainability of your choices.

Despite its depth, the game is not without friction. The interface can feel clunky, information is sometimes buried in menus, and the learning curve is steep, especially for players accustomed to more streamlined modern simulations. Performance issues and minor technical quirks also remind players of its age. Additionally, those familiar with earlier versions of City Life may find that the 2008 edition refines and expands existing ideas rather than reinventing them, making it feel more like a definitive compilation than a radical evolution.

Ultimately, City Life 2008 stands as a thoughtful and demanding city-building game that dares to center its design around social complexity rather than pure optimization. It may not offer the polish or accessibility of newer titles, but its willingness to model the human side of city planning gives it a distinctive identity. For players who enjoy slow, methodical simulations and appreciate games that challenge them to think about cities as living, socially layered systems, City Life 2008 remains a rewarding and intellectually engaging experience that still holds relevance years after its release.

Rating: 7/10

City Life 2008 is a city-building simulation game that offers a unique blend of urban planning, management, and strategy. Here's my review of the game:

I enjoyed the game's sandbox mode, which allowed me to build and manage my own city without any specific objectives or time limits. The game's graphics and sound effects were also impressive, with detailed 3D buildings and realistic soundscapes that immersed me in the game world.

One of the standout features of City Life 2008 is its focus on social and economic balance. The game requires you to balance the needs of different social classes, from low-income workers to wealthy entrepreneurs, and manage the city's economy to keep everyone happy. This added a layer of depth to the game that I found engaging and challenging.

However, I did encounter some issues with the game's interface and controls. The game's menus and UI can be clunky at times, making it difficult to navigate and manage different aspects of the city. Additionally, the game's AI can be unpredictable, leading to unexpected problems and challenges that can be frustrating to resolve.

Despite these issues, I would recommend City Life 2008 to fans of city-building simulations. The game offers a unique blend of strategy and management that is both challenging and rewarding. If you're looking for a game that will keep you engaged for hours, City Life 2008 is definitely worth checking out.

Overall, I would give City Life 2008 a solid 7 out of 10. While it has its flaws, the game's engaging gameplay and immersive atmosphere make it a great choice for fans of the genre.

Отличный олдскульный градостроительный симулятор! Да, в чем-то он будет менее детализирован, чем, к примеру тот же СимСити, но не в графике уж точно. Присутствует приближение и ротация камеры, а так же смена времени суток, но, увы, не сезонов. Здесь вам придется не просто выстроить удачный мегаполис с позитивным сальдо баланса, а и смотреть, чтобы жители не поубивали друг друга, им хватало досуга, больниц, охвата пожарных частей и полиции, шикарных отелей для туристов, и так далее. Фишка состоит в том, что в Сити Лайф существует классификация групп жителей, и условное их разделение - радикалы, синие воротнички, неимущие и элита. Красные не терпят синих, элита терпит оранжевых и голубых, но не неимущих, а оранжевые и голубые, опять же, не терпят друг друга. То есть, город будет состоять из районов, в которых будут проживать разные группы людей. Их может объединять лишь работа, требующая наличие тех и других вместе для большей эффективности, и все. Если дом красных появится в квартале синих, начнутся стычки, и это может перерасти в крупный скандал с пожаром на полгорода. Утихомирить неспокойную зону и помочь ужиться разным группам вместе в определенной точке трения интересов помогут социальные центры. Шкала спроса и предложения формируется на основе предлагаемых рабочих мест, но учтите, что при наличии хорошего образования и его доступности, одна социальная группа может запросто перетечь в другую - более богатую. Например: построили вы рабочие места для голубой группы. Некоторые из синих могут стать голубыми, чтобы наняться туда, а неимущие  - подтянуться на место не хватающих синих, которые стали голубыми. Вопрос только в том, чтоб хватало еще и неимущих. Элита же - очень требовательна, и так уж просто вам ее не вырастить, как и не превратить весь город в элиту - все равно кто-то должен работать на мусоросжигателях, кто-то на электростанциях, или на иных работах, где элита работать не может. В общем, то, что на первый взгляд, может показаться простым на самом деле куда труднее, чем кажется. Чем больше ваш мегаполис, тем заметнее и ощутимее станут изменения при каждом вашем действии.

Silverfall: Earth Awakening is a substantial standalone expansion that builds upon the foundations of the original Silverfall by broadening its systems, world, and thematic ambitions. Developed by Monte Cristo and published by Focus Entertainment, the game represents a distinctly mid-2000s approach to action RPG design, one that prioritizes scale, customization, and player agency over streamlined presentation. Even today, it stands as an interesting snapshot of an era when ARPGs were experimenting with large worlds, complex skill trees, and moral alignment systems rather than tightly scripted experiences.

The setting of Earth Awakening centers on the fantasy world of Nelwë, a land fractured by the growing conflict between the forces of nature and the rise of technology. This philosophical divide is more than narrative flavor; it underpins the game’s core identity and influences how the story unfolds. Rather than presenting a single linear plot, the game offers a looser narrative structure where exploration, side quests, and faction interactions gradually reveal the broader state of the world. The storytelling is understated and sometimes fragmented, but it provides a steady sense of purpose as players uncover corrupted regions, ancient secrets, and political tensions simmering beneath the surface.

Character creation is one of the game’s strongest elements and a major contributor to its replay value. Players can choose from several distinct races, each with unique traits that subtly shape playstyle and role-playing flavor. Progression is deep and unapologetically complex, featuring an extensive skill system with a wide range of active abilities, passive bonuses, and powerful ultimate skills unlocked at higher levels. This breadth allows for highly specialized builds, whether focused on melee combat, ranged attacks, spellcasting, or hybrid approaches. The freedom to experiment is central to the experience, and the game rewards players who invest time into understanding how skills and attributes synergize.

Combat follows the traditional hack-and-slash formula, with real-time encounters against large groups of enemies that emphasize ability usage and positioning. While moment-to-moment fighting can feel repetitive over long sessions, the sheer variety of skills and spells helps maintain engagement. Encounters often become more about managing cooldowns, resource consumption, and crowd control than reflex-driven precision. The inclusion of crafting systems further enriches this loop, allowing players to forge weapons, armor, and enhancements that meaningfully affect performance rather than serving as minor statistical upgrades.

Exploration in Silverfall: Earth Awakening is ambitious, if occasionally unwieldy. The world is expansive, filled with diverse environments ranging from lush forests to barren wastelands and ancient ruins. This sense of scale contributes to immersion but also exposes some of the game’s age, as navigation tools and quest guidance are limited by modern standards. Players are often expected to pay close attention to dialogue and environmental cues to determine where to go next. While this can lead to moments of confusion, it also reinforces a feeling of genuine discovery that many contemporary games smooth away with explicit markers and constant direction.

A defining feature of the game is its alignment system, which tracks the player’s affinity toward either nature or technology. This choice subtly alters quests, dialogue, and available equipment, adding a layer of role-playing depth that encourages multiple playthroughs. Although the system is not as reactive or far-reaching as modern morality mechanics, it does succeed in making decisions feel more than cosmetic. The thematic contrast between organic magic and mechanical progress gives the world a unique flavor that distinguishes it from more conventional fantasy settings.

Visually and technically, Earth Awakening clearly reflects its era. Character models, animations, and interface design feel dated, and the camera and controls can take time to adjust to for players accustomed to modern ARPG polish. Occasional technical quirks and clunky menus are part of the experience, but they rarely undermine the core gameplay once familiarity sets in. Instead, they serve as reminders of the game’s ambition relative to the tools and conventions of its time.

Ultimately, Silverfall: Earth Awakening is a game defined by scope and flexibility rather than refinement. It may lack the cinematic storytelling and mechanical smoothness of newer action RPGs, but it compensates with deep customization, an expansive world, and a willingness to let players shape their own path through complex systems. For fans of classic hack-and-slash RPGs who value freedom, experimentation, and old-school design philosophy, it remains a rewarding and distinctive experi

Se Silverfall si rivelò una delusione assoluta, con questo Earth Awakening le sorti non si sono affatto risollevate.

Per spiegare al meglio ogni cosa, ho bisogno di riprendere alcune cose già scritte nella mia precedente recensione sul gioco di base. Installando infatti Silverfall sul mio PC, subito notai come l’avatar fosse ben visibile, ma al contrario il menu di gioco con le varie opzioni era del tutto sgranato, indistinto, indefinito; di fatto non si capiva dove si stesse cliccando. E dire che i requisiti per far girare correttamente il gioco li avevo tutti… e invece non ha funzionato nulla. Capisco che i giochi vecchi abbiano talvolta problemi di compatibilità e che sicuramente, affidandosi a un esperto nel settore, sarebbe stato possibile sistemare in qualche modo la questione, ma quanto tempo e soldi extra avrei dovuto investire? Senza contare che, alla prima occasione in cui si disinstallerà il gioco e lo si reinstallerà, succederà la medesima cosa. Ecco perché ho bocciato Silverfall con un gran nodo al cuore.

Earth Awakening avrebbe dovuto teoricamente risolvere la situazione. Graficamente è visibile ogni cosa, gira bene sul PC e nessuno dei precedenti problemi elencati dal gioco di base pareva essere presente. Hanno persino introdotto una razza giocabile in più! Cosa poteva andare storto? Quando si crea un personaggio, è possibile scegliere se giocare a Silverfall (campagna di base) partendo dal livello 1 oppure, alternativamente, accedere direttamente a Earth Awakening (campagna dell’espansione) cominciando dal livello 45. Senza Silverfall installato non è però possibile iniziare dal livello 1. Quando tuttavia ho installato Silverfall e ho avviato Earth Awakening per poter finalmente giocare all'avventura di base tramite l’espansione, ecco che, pur avendo avviato Earth Awakening, ad accogliermi c’è stato Silverfall con tutti i medesimi problemi tecnici descritti sopra! In buona sostanza, con Earth Awakening potete solo giocare all’espansione. Un altro doloroso nodo al cuore. Ed è un vero peccato, perché dai video che ho visto in rete sia Silverfall sia Earth Awakening si presentavano davvero molto bene. Quando poi le lingue elencate da Steam non hanno neppure coinciso con quelle effettive usufruibili dal gioco, lì non ci ho visto più; c’erano almeno due idiomi disponibili che avrei potuto utilizzare senza troppi problemi, ma per me quella è stata la goccia che ha fatto traboccare il vaso.

Cala così un lugubre e funesto sipario su un gioco che mi aveva incuriosito fin dai tempi di Windows XP, su un prodotto che è sempre stato tra le mie mani ma che non ho mai davvero potuto godermi quanto e come avrei sperato. Spero che voi, se scegliete di sfidare ugualmente la sorte, possiate essere più fortunati di me.

BEFORE YOU BUY, PLEASE READ THIS!!!

First off, this game is 11 gigs on the hard drive. WHY?!?!? It's an old game, why would an old game need over 11 gigs? The original game is 8 gigs. This is already fouled up in so many ways.

When you buy this game, the game won't work right away, there's a Steam bug that prevents you from playing the game until you do a few things.

1.) You don't need to buy the original "Silverfall" game, however, it is required
2.) This is an expansion pack that goes with this game
3.) Why Steam hasn't fixed this bug is beyond me

THis game works just fine, however, here is what you need to do to get this game to work if/when you buy this game...

1.) Install the game as normal with Steam
2.) After you install this game, right-click on the game title in Steam
3.) Select "Properties" from the menu
4.) Select "Installed Files" from the menu
5.) Click on the "Verify Integrity of game files"
6.) When it does this, it will say that it's missing 150 files
7.) Let it do it's thing and install the rest of the missing files
8.) Once done, now the game is installed, however, you are not done yet
9.) Go to google, and search for "PhysX_2.4.4_SystemSoftware.exe"
10.) Make sure it's the PhysX_2.4.4_SystemSoftware, and nothing else
11.) Download that file and install, it's needed to play ths game
12.) Do not install the current or newer version of PhysX, it won't work

(For the record, when you install this game, this file is in the "Silverfall" folder in the Steam directory, go to your Steam folder...

Usually in "C:\Program Files\Steam\steamapps\common\Silverfall"

In there, there should be a file "PhysX_2.4.4_SystemSoftware.exe", install this file because it is needed.

Once installed, now it should work.

(If it doesn't work, there's one more thing you might do. In the "Silverfall" folder in Steam, look for the...

"silverfall.exe"

Right-click on the "silverfall.exe", click on "Properties", click on the "Compatibility" tab, and in the "Compatibility Mode" section, check the box and select "Windows XP Service Pack 2", then click "Apply". It should work now. If the game still doesn't work, I am not sure what other advice I can offer you, other than a refund.

Now, with that being said, time to review...

Silverfall is a 3D style RPG game, similar to "Baldur's Gate". When you begin the game, it will ask you to first, make a character, and then if you want to start at Lv 1 for the main game, or Leverl 45 for the expansion pack, which is this game. This game requires you to be level 45 as the original game you start out with the main story and build yourself up.

Graphics are actually not too bad compaired to today's games. The character design is very nice and 3D models are very smooth. The animations are very well done, and the characters, monsters, and environments have a very ncie look to them.

Movement can be done in 2 ways. You can use the "WASD" keys to move, or you can use the mouse to click on where you want to go. You can use the "Delete" and "Page Down" keys to rotate the camera around, and use the "End" and "Home" keys to angle the camera where you want it. Use the mouse wheel to zoom in and out as needed. Press the "C" key to see your character stats as well as increase your stats when you level up. Press the "I" key to see your characters items, weapons, and armor as well as used to equip your weapons and armor. Equiping your weapons and armor is as simple as click and drag to the proper locationon the character. Press the "M" key to see the map of the area you are in. When you start out, it's covered in a tan like fag, but as yuo travel, you will show more of the game as you progress through the game. To attack monsters, you just find one and click on the monster.

Along the way, you can interact with NPC characters in certain locastions. Warning, not all NPC characters will allow you to interact with. Only those with a "!" or some kind of icon on top of their heads will be allowed to talk to you. Most cases, those with a "!" are quest NPC's.

Money can be obtained from either killing monsters, selling items you find, or finishing quests. As you battle or find chests, items will be found all over the place. Everytime you kill a monster, they will drop items, weapons, or armor. You can also find NPC's who sell weapons and armor in various locations. 

Moving from one location to another is a bit odd. Sometimes you will reach an area where it takes you to another realm. (for example, you start out in the swamp, but as you travel, you find the edge of the map that takes you to a desert area) Once in a while, you will find a cave. When you get close, it will ask you if you want to enter the cave or not.

You can also learn spells and crafting in this game. They are updated and upgraded by talking to certain people in verious towns. How much you can upgrade is based on your characters level.

Overall, it's a very neat game. It's just sad that this game has so many issues to deal with before you can play the game. Oddly enough I did not have any crash issues playing this game. Every time I have played, it plays smoothly without crashing or dumping me back to Windows.

Some things to keep in mind when you get this game...

1.) It's an old game, it came out around 2007, a time when Windows XP was still used. So if the game does not work for you, please don't be too upset, it's an old game and ran under Windows XP, Windows Vista, and Windows 7.

2.) When changing the settings in your game, please set it no higher than 1366x768. It works great in 1920x1080 and the graphics are just fantastic for it's time, even at higher resolutions. However, the text will shrink in size the higher you set the resolution. This is a gaming bug that they did not consider at the time. So please keep this in mind when you set your settings. Keep the resolution a bit low so you can read the text.

3.) It's sad that Steam sells the original game and this expansion as 2 different games. During the time when the game was out, they made a "Gold" version, which was both games in 1. If you want to master this game you'll have to do a lot of in-game experimentation and theory crafting; however, no one will bother because the game isn't really good enough to make you do so. Silverfall является моей первой RPG. На тот момент я не был избалован гигантами жанра (aka Diablo 2) , не знал принципов отыгрыша роли, не слышал о D&D и тд. Но даже сейчас, спустя много лет, я возвращаюсь в этот мир, где странным образом уживается классическое фентэзи и стимпанк, где сюжет банален и прост, а ветви прокачки довольно выразительны и  разносторонни. И так, давайте немного по подробнее поговорим об этой игре.

Плюсы:
+ Разнообразные ветви прокачки и огромное количество сетовых вещей с привязкой к параметрам позволяют вам отыграть абсолютно любого героя, которого вы придумаете. Даже если это саппорт.
Паладины, некроманты, охотники, оборотни, маги, инженеры. Этот список довольно объёмен. 
+ Рисованная графика и селшейдинг позволили игре не состарится, и картинка все еще может радовать глаз. Особенно в "зеленых" локациях и уровнях из DLC.
+ Вместо системы морали ( тк герой все равно идет по сюжетным рельсам) представлена система мировозрения. С помощью доп квестов и диалогов с напарниками герой становится на сторону прогресса или природы. Это открывает возможность использовать уникальную броню и оружие, а так же вкладку инжинера / друида. Вы сможете стать киборгом с имплантами, или диким оборотнем, который разрывает в клочья все на своем пути.
+ Система крафта из DLC позволяет создавать эквип под ваши нужды, настраивать визуал и свойства предметов, выбирать любой цвет из палитры RGB

Минусы:
- Сюжет в игре представлен для галочки. Он нужен только для того, что бы герой посетил все локации в правильном порядке.
- Напарники очень тупые, они не рационально используют свои скилы, и по сути нужны для прокачки мировозрения героя. Действительно эффективными являются Денселейм (убийца) и Лина (маг). Полезность остальных спутников варируются от инвалид до "ну, он прикольный". Если играть от саппорта, то эти двое - ваш выбор.
- Стрельба очень сильно проигрывает в нанесении урона. Вы пройдете игру любым стрелком и без пати, но маги и милишники сделают это быстрее и драйвовее.

Итог: в свое время вышло множество клонов Diablo, но этот проект имеет свой самобытный стиль, приятно играется, и дает волю в билдостроении. Рекомендую всем любителям стимпанка, или старых Action RPG!

I'm mixed about this game.

- It looks nice visually with a partially cell-shaded style that blends well and doesn't give off an overly cartoony presentation for the darker story and setting.

- It has some innovative systems that set is apart from other ARPGs like the crafting system and Technology VS Nature branches

- Loads of loot and gear with various properties that all appear on your character 

- Endless character building options

But there are some issues.

- Some environments look nice, others are bland and feel low effort. 

- Party management can be tricky, and controls can feel clunky

- Some bugs and crashes, along with some confusing and buggy quest objectives

Overall, if you just want to try a new Hack and Slash ARPG that isn't a diablo clone and you like to really build a customized character, this one will scratch that itch. None of it's drawbacks ever make the game feel broken, and you can adjust the dificulty from the standard easy to brutal difficulty right from the start.

I don't recommend this game to people looking to try the ARPG genre for the first time, as there are smoother experiences with a richer world to explore. For veterans, I recommend this is as a nice alternative to the big hitters that we've all played for hundreds of hours. There's enough depth and variety of loot to make it a satisfying experience.

I have some hardcore nostalgia for this game on PSP, it was simple but very focused, all abilities were actual abilities with special effects (bleed, haste, poison, regen) and were effective with even just a few points so on PSP it really encouraged you to weave abilities on any build to maintain buffs and debuffs. Additionally the only prerequisite for leveling abilities is your character's current level so you can skip and pick specific abilities without having to take any that won't help your build. 
The combat was very fast and generally didn't drag out with nice spacing to let you pick your fights at your own pace so you didn't get bogged down fighting the same enemies for extended periods of time and while enemies generally didn't diversify within zones between zones there was a LOT of enemy diversity so while within zones things don't change up much between zones you have a fresh experience and zones didn't outstay their welcome (with a few exceptions, mainly Cloudworks thought that may have been because I played it a lot trying out different builds).
There were places to explore on every level with a simple map and checkpoint system to assist in this and chests and secrets hidden on most levels to reward you for going off the main path, everything from items to alignment points and quests.
The story was definitely weak but the gameplay made up for it the speed and focus of the game letting me ignore it outside of the very strong aesthetics every zone had, from the foreboding swamp and ruins around the refugee camp to the desolation of the cloudworks desert, the industrial slum of Lower Cloudworks, the floating estates of Upper Cloudworks and the teeming forests and rivers of Gaian to say the least, only continuing to impress as you continue.
While the graphics were nothing to write home about they were pretty standard for the PSP at the time of the game's release.

Sadly in a bout of teenage folly I sold my PSP and all my games for what was basically drug money so it's no longer something I can play.

When I saw this on steam I thought it'd buy it and relive some nostalgia only to be horrified to discover that this game is one of a few victims of platform diversity, The Force Unleashed being a notable victim of this). Basically every good thing I said about the PSP version has been ruined in some way in the PC release with the exception of the zones' visuals though they're sorely muted thanks to the poor pacing and pathing (both in the lack of direction and the actual pathing, your character will get stuck on many, many, many things).
There's a lot more enemy diversity and a lot of the bonus concept art on the PSP release I finally got to see in action as a lot of enemy types were cut from the PSP probably to save space but on PC it just feels like everything is overpacked and enemies are placed VERY lazily in clumps of 2-4 that you have to engage in clusters.
Abilities are mostly passive % bonuses to damage or defence and are very boring, the contols are wonky and just ugh. It's awful and it makes me sad. No doubt I have some rose tinted goggles for the PSP version but I find it very disheartening that the 'full' version of the game is so watered down and soured.

[h3]TLDR[/h3]
Full Spectrum Warrior is a first person tactical shooter that manages to be quite enjoyable and well-balanced, even for people who don't usually play games in this genre, right up until you get to the final mission.

[h3]The Good[/h3]
The general atmosphere and style of the game is very cohesive and immersive. If one of your squad mates gets downed, you can carry them back to a med evac point to get them patched up, which strikes a nice balance between "unforgivingly realistic" and "boringly easy". Flanking works very well. Controls are easy to learn. Tutorial is good.

[h3]The Bad[/h3]
The AI is a cheating BEEP sometimes. I have seen them rebound my grenades, shoot me through solid cover, and no-sell six grenade launcher blasts to the face that should have hit, according to the game's UI. For 11/12 missions, this was little more than an occasional annoyance, but then you get to the final mission... I spent almost two hours on this one before calling it quits and happily not thinking about it until I sat down to write this review. Most of the enemies in this mission can only be hit by the grenade launcher, which only seems to work as intended about 5% of the time. Rarely does a game make me feel like I wasted hours of my life, but this last mission unfortunately did.

[h3]The Ugly[/h3] 
Surprisingly, nothing. Despite its age, this game actually ran really well on my PC from 2021, so kudos to the devs for future proofing this one.
To fix the sound issues, download "Indirect Sound" wrapper library (see a guide in the Community tab).

Full Spectrum Warrior, developed by Pandemic Studios and published by THQ Nordic, stands as one of the most distinctive tactical experiences to come out of the early 2000s, merging military realism with strategy in a way few games dared to attempt. Originally conceived as a training aid for the U.S. Army before being adapted into a commercial release, it occupies a unique space between simulation and entertainment. Rather than casting the player as a superhuman soldier mowing down waves of enemies, it demands leadership, planning, and control. You don’t fire a single bullet yourself—instead, you command two fire teams through the tense, unpredictable streets of a fictional Middle Eastern city. The focus is not on reflexes but on tactics, suppression, and coordination. The result is a game that feels both grounded and cerebral, emphasizing discipline and teamwork over raw aggression.

The game’s premise is simple yet immersive: you play as a squad leader guiding Alpha and Bravo teams through hostile urban environments. The fictional setting—Zekistan—is a war-torn landscape reminiscent of real-world conflict zones, filled with bombed-out buildings, alleys, and ambush points. The campaign’s missions vary from street patrols and hostage rescues to full-scale assaults on entrenched enemy positions, each designed to teach and test different principles of squad tactics. Every action you take feels deliberate, from ordering your team to take cover behind a burned-out car to flanking an enemy position under suppressive fire. There’s no room for carelessness, and the penalty for poor coordination can be swift and brutal. Pandemic’s design philosophy was clear: success comes not from speed or brute force, but from patience, communication, and methodical precision.

One of Full Spectrum Warrior’s most notable features is its control system. You don’t directly control soldiers in the traditional sense; instead, you issue commands through contextual orders, moving your squads as cohesive units. Point to a location, and they’ll automatically take cover and face likely enemy threats. Order them to suppress a target, and they’ll lay down covering fire while another team maneuvers. It’s a fluid, intuitive interface that allows for complex tactical decisions without overwhelming the player with micromanagement. This system forces you to think like an officer rather than a foot soldier—planning angles of attack, maintaining overlapping fields of fire, and ensuring that one team always supports the other. The combat feels tense and deliberate, as every move exposes your squad to potential danger, and every victory feels earned through smart, measured play.

Visually, the game captures the gritty, oppressive atmosphere of urban warfare. The dusty streets, crumbling facades, and smoke-filled skies create a convincing backdrop for the tactical engagements. While the graphics may show their age today, at the time of release they were impressive in both environmental detail and animation fidelity. The soldiers move realistically, taking cover with believable motions, leaning around corners, and ducking instinctively when under fire. The sound design plays a major role in heightening immersion—radio chatter, distant explosions, and the crack of rifle fire give every mission an authentic sense of chaos. The voice acting, while at times stiff, effectively conveys the camaraderie and professionalism of trained soldiers under stress, lending credibility to the game’s tone.

The realism extends to how the game treats combat. There are no health packs, no regenerating armor, and no heroic firefights where one man can turn the tide. Your soldiers are vulnerable, and once one is down, it’s a serious problem. This vulnerability changes how you approach every encounter. Instead of rushing in, you’re constantly scanning for cover, planning suppressive routes, and positioning your squads to minimize exposure. The game rewards cautious, disciplined play and punishes recklessness, which gives it a rhythm distinct from most shooters. It’s not about action spectacle; it’s about tension and anticipation. Each street corner and doorway becomes a potential threat, and that slow, deliberate pacing adds weight to every decision.

Narratively, Full Spectrum Warrior keeps things understated. The story, told through brief cutscenes and mission briefings, focuses on the professionalism of the soldiers rather than dramatic heroics. There are political undertones and glimpses into the chaos of modern conflict, but the narrative never overwhelms the gameplay. It’s clear that the developers’ goal was to present a grounded depiction of military operations rather than a cinematic war story. The fictional setting of Zekistan provides enough distance from real-world events to avoid controversy, while still conveying the gritty reality of asymmetric warfare. The dialogue between squad members, sprinkled with dark humor and military jargon, humanizes the experience, reinforcing the idea that these are ordinary people navigating extraordinary circumstances.

Despite its many strengths, Full Spectrum Warrior isn’t without flaws. The rigid command structure that defines the game’s realism can also make it feel restrictive. There’s little room for improvisation outside of the tools the system gives you, and some players may find the pace too slow or the control scheme too detached. Occasional AI hiccups can also break immersion—soldiers may expose themselves unnecessarily or fail to respond quickly to threats. The difficulty curve can be unforgiving, particularly for players unfamiliar with real tactical principles, as the game expects you to think in terms of cover arcs and fire suppression rather than direct confrontation. However, for those who embrace its demands, these limitations reinforce the game’s commitment to authenticity and precision.

In terms of legacy, Full Spectrum Warrior remains one of the most innovative tactical games of its era. Its hybrid design—half training simulator, half strategy game—paved the way for future titles that emphasized realism and squad-based tactics, influencing games like Ghost Recon: Advanced Warfighter and even modern tactical shooters. What makes it stand out even now is its refusal to compromise its identity. It’s a game about leadership under pressure, about making decisions with incomplete information, and about the stark difference between success and disaster in a combat environment. While it may lack the spectacle of Hollywood-style shooters, it offers something more rare: an authentic sense of command responsibility and the satisfaction of executing a flawless maneuver under fire.

Full Spectrum Warrior endures as a remarkable experiment in tactical realism and design restraint. It’s not a game for everyone—it demands patience, thought, and precision—but for those who appreciate slow, methodical strategy wrapped in a believable military context, it delivers an experience that few other games can match. Its combination of intuitive squad control, tense combat, and grounded atmosphere makes it a standout in the history of tactical gaming. Even years after its release, it remains a powerful reminder that sometimes the most compelling victories in war games come not from pulling the trigger, but from making the right call when everything is on the line.

Rating: 7/10

[h1]Full Spectrum Warrior — тактика, рейнджеры США, опасность за каждым углом [/h1]

Тактика Full Spectrum Warrior от Pandemic Studios выходила в 2004 году на Xbox, PS2 и ПК. Игра разрабатывалась как тренажер для Армии США, чтобы укрепить групповое слаживание в войсках. Это преподносилось как самое реалистичное представление городских боёв на уровне Пехоты через уникальный геймплей тактического действия.

Сюжет повествует о волне террористических атак в Европе и Юго-Восточной Азии. После нескольких месяцев активных поисков разведка США наконец отслеживает источник нападений в государстве Зекистан, что в Центральной Азии. Начинается вторжение НАТО с целью уничтожить диктатора страны Мохаммеда Джаббура Аль-Афада и положить конец терактам.

Геймплейно игра представляет из себя тактику в реальном времени. У нас есть два сквада Альфа и Браво по 4 человека. В каждой из огневых групп есть:
• Командир с карабином М4, картой, GPS и длинноволновой рацией
• Заместитель командира и по совместительству пулеметчик с М249
• Гренадёр, вооруженный M4 с подствольным гранатометом M203
• Стрелок с карабином М4

Каждый отряд это полноценная боевая единица. У всех есть небольшой запас дымовых и осколочных гранат. Иногда могут выделить дополнительно одного-двух бойцов для определенной задачи, определив их в огневую группу Чарли. Но не часто.

Отдельно солдатами мы не управляем: под нашем руководством отряды в целом. В распоряжении есть команда занять позицию (укрытие) и обозначить сектор для огня. Например, перед нами поставлена задача пройти по улице до перекрестка. Ставим Браво в укрытие, обозначаем направление взгляда. И вторым отрядом двигаемся вперед уже под прикрытием союзников.

Оснащение отделений, кстати, отражает реальное вооружение и оснащение, применяемое в настоящее время Армией США. А еще в игре реализовано достоверное осуществление доктрины Пехоты Армии США. Благодаря чему, боевые действия выглядят натурально, осмысленно, а не похожими на обычный шутер, где мы летим вперёд сломя голову.

Мы также можем приказывать отдельным солдатам куда выстрелить из M203, куда кинуть ту или иную гранату. Ведь некоторые особо сложные места без прикрытия дымовой завесы пройти ой как непросто, а то и невозможно. Иногда, при помощи рации и дымовой гранаты мы вольны вызвать поддержку в виде вертолета, которая знатно так облегчает задачу по устранению врагов или бронетехники.

Потенциал опасности кроется на каждой аллее, за каждым окном. Наблюдайте за этими углами, парни, у нас тут работка. Ура!
Full Spectrum Warrior — тактика, рейнджеры США, опасность за каждым углом, изображение №5
Именно вокруг этих механик строится весь геймплей Full Spectrum Warrior. Миссий много. И зачистка, и оборона, и сопровождение, и спасение. Но механика управления остается неизменной.

Если солдата ранили в бою, то необходимо приказать спасти его: взвалить на плечо и оттащить к ближайшему пункту с медиком, который подлатает нашего брата по оружию, а заодно там же пополним боекомплект. Два в одном!

Jeu sortie en 2004 et conçu à la base par l'armée américaine pour aider les vétérans à surmonter les traumatismes liés à la guerre.

Histoire :
Le grand classique. L'OTAN est en guerre contre le terrorisme alors qu'une vague d'attentats cible l'occident. En réaction, l'OTAN décide d'envahir le Zekistan, un pays fictif dirigé par des terroristes et et surtout un dictateur. Comment ne pas penser à l'Afghanistan ou à l'Irak ici... L'histoire est donc inspiré de faits géopolitiques réels.
Concrétement, le jeu est aussi axé autour de 2 équipes de l'armée américaine. Chaque équipe est composée de 4 soldats ayant chacun leurs caractéristiques et compétences. L'objectif du jeu sera de diriger vos 2 équipes de façon à remplir vos objectifs de missions tout en gardant vos soldats en vie, ce qui est loin d'être évident si vous ne réfléchissez pas un minimum.

Gameplay :
Vous n'incarnez pas les soldats, vous les dirigez et leur donnez des ordres et ils font le boulot. Ce jeu est donc axé tactique et vise à sensibiliser les joueurs à l'enfer de la guerre ou la moindre erreur peut être fatal en terme de décisions.
Les ordres peuvent être de tenir la position, émettre un tir de suppression, contourner l'adversaire, etc...
Chaque membre de l'escouade a un rôle différent :
- Le chef d'escouade qui peut communiquer avec le QG par radio et repérer la position des ennemis.
- Le mitrailleur équipé d'une M249, grosse arme lourde qui peut faire de la suppression facilement. 
- Le grenadier utilisé pour tout faire péter...
- Le simple fusilier polyvalent.
Ce type d'escouade est (ou était au vu de la date du jeu) ressemblant avec la réalité au niveau de l'armée américaine. Tout comme les équipements utilisés.

Graphismes :
Le point noir du jeu. En 2024, tout a mal vieilli pour ma part. Les textures sont moches ce qui gâche un peu l'immersion à mon sens. Le comble pour un jeu qui se veut simulation...

Difficulté :
Là aussi, je vous conseil de bien maîtriser les tutoriels avant de vous lancer car ce n'est pas facile. Vous allez vous planter plus d'une fois c'est clair, surtout que la moindre erreur est souvent mortelle pour votre équipe.

Prix :
Moins de 5 euros en soldes sur steam.

Je recommande pour ceux qui ne sont pas refroidis par la difficulté et qui aiment les jeux tactiques.

FSW作为一个美军官方外包民间做的针对NCO指挥步兵小队3D训练软件改的军转民游戏，理论上是有点新意的小时候玩到也感觉很神秘，难度很高。然而今天军事理论和知识太多了以后真的这游戏从远不如续作FSW10锤，本来游戏理论上没什么难度（前提是你明白步兵基础战术，看其他评论感觉一般fps玩家觉得这游戏很难。。。），但实际游玩的高难度基本都来自于玩家和敌人有限的机制根本适应不了理论训练软件改成游戏以后的作战烈度（非常有幽灵行动荒野一命通最大的威胁是各种载具相关bug和大结局后脸上刷4名机枪兵的感觉）。

Pro优点：
即便今天也是独一家的，聚焦于美军步兵班组，指挥与控制流程最普通的基本功之一：火力压制与侧袭，的模拟游戏（实际也半模拟化了）
【补充：FSW还真不能完全算独一家，突然看到有up主更新提到了战火兄弟连系列，才想起来是有概念续作的，育碧2005-8 2005-10和2007-9月找Gearbox做的战火兄弟连，也使用了A B+剧情C 双步兵小队以压制与侧袭为核心玩法，Gearbox在05两部因为玩家作为NCO，以FPS状态进行战斗与指挥，所以为了逼迫玩家使用A队机枪压制B队汤姆森侧袭，把玩家削弱到贴脸也完全打不中人的超高散射模式，而07年地狱公路为了更适合大众是能当FPS玩的。】

Cons缺点：
编制，历史，装备，展示的战术，知道的越多越感觉问题多，而很多问题你也不知道是Pandemic开发缺乏军事知识的问题还是美军要求和谐的问题（介于Pandemic加入EA与生软合并后出的续作游戏性显著提高，我更倾向于P社负主要责任）。

首先需要说些历史背景，美军2004年步兵班标准编制一位Staff Sergeant-班长，2位Sergeant指挥的2x4人步兵小队：TL-队长 AR-机枪兵 G-榴弹兵 Rife-步枪兵（一般就是纯新兵），软件原型就是训练NCO小队指挥基本功，所以玩家理论上就是Staff Sgt但是不存在这个角色所以隔空指挥。剧情上是平行世界的并不是沙漠风暴行动的美军按联合国授权入侵不是伊拉克的泽什么斯坦（且游戏中的不是伊拉克被塑造成了真邪恶帝国，后期和结局满街万人坑），时间上也不是2003改到了2004。
介于这游戏最初为米军开发时刚好同期有个类似于未来战士的项目，理论上应该有点先进物件然而没有，只有两只小队的队长都非常出戏的背着营团级无线电进行通讯。
于是引出了玩家单位的装备问题，第一个问题作为三等人精锐机瞄M4和M249（虽然可以解释但03年三等人应该已经在用足量的红点了），第二个问题小队4个人装甲完全不一样，理论上沙漠风暴美军紧急购置的大量OTV可携板背心和4级板都是BDU林地迷彩，但是玩家小队4个人2个BDU林地1个棕色1个沙漠迷彩（沙漠迷彩人看起来还跟没穿甲一样），4个甲模型完全不一样你也搞不清是PASGAT？OTV？越战夹克？
友军布莱德利模型全部比真货小2圈，且不知P社故意要蹭终结者和第一滴血热度还是米军和谐要求，并不是M2A2布莱德利而是M6Linebacker把TOW拆了换4连装毒刺的防空型，于是游戏里布莱德利反载具过场里更神奇的就来了，布莱德利冲入战场冲着bmp连射4发谜之火箭弹。总之类似的谜之问题真的越看越难受。

游戏性部分，2个小队弹药应该是按实际米军步兵班弹药基数并且是正经按每发和弹匣计算的，给玩家的HUD提示却是按百分比的计算且队员弹匣内残弹不计算，只有队员换弹后才会从弹药池扣除弹药M249一次换弹就吃掉10%起步，而此时游戏脑瘫机制问题就来了，即便在补给点队员也不会检查弹药并补充武器半空弹匣（比如M4弹匣都是1/30的状态，是不会换弹的，虽然对交战影响不大，但如果你经常使用全队火力压制而操作又不熟练对剩余弹药计算续航的影响就很大了）

另一个超级出戏的点就是部分任务里情报和你的指挥官明知要对付载具，但是我们美军没LAW和AT4分给你们这种精锐，于是必须呼叫支援火力对敌人装甲进行剧情杀，小队必须辗转腾挪贴到载具脸上才能叫火炮或CAS。。。我真的无话可说。你可是军转民游戏啊，这绝对是P社故意的。

每只小队特殊技能，也让我无话可说的😓，每次任务每队限量6颗手雷 6颗烟雾 3发M203榴弹，在补给点只补充556不补充这些技能，榴弹但凡做成每次试射4发只有一发能中也比这谜之40mm火球术符合模拟啊。

最后就是导致游戏难度特别高的机制问题了，步兵基础战术就是一队压制另一队去侧袭，无论是游戏目标硬件的机能问题还是原作军版主要目的在于训练指挥和控制而不是战斗，游戏设定战斗仅限于MOUT（军事行动在城市环境），这游戏没有的一个内容就是MOUT里非常不重要的但是很适合表演也很火的CQB。因为设定是MOUT，所有的掩体（包括建筑街角）都是四方形同时也可有一定角度，敌我双方在掩体内顶盾状态无法伤到对方，只能进行基础火力压制或者全队齐射的完全压制，基础压制就是普通对枪此时玩家另一小队在敌人中远距离跑过双方枪线不会被攻击到，全队齐射是一个小队4人全部离开掩体冲压制区域全力燃烧备弹，这样另一队贴脸甚至没有掩体也不会被击毙（但友军枪线是有友伤的）。想击毙对方，就只能一队压制敌军，另一队绕到对方掩体侧面几乎90度和以上的无盾状态才可进行击杀，小队特殊技能手雷和M203特定位置可跨掩体击杀，烟雾弹可以遮蔽双方视野用于机动。

看似很合理？于是盘外招来了，敌人的bot是按FPS规则来的，只有玩家你才是被规则绑死的🤡。玩家的2只小队看似无论在何时都在警戒，对枪的时候4号位还在看屁股？其实并没有，除了玩家发出的攻击区域的指令外，玩家小队几乎不会主动攻击，被敌方侧袭绕后除非是中远距没打死队员，小队才会去反击，而敌方要是在掩体里顶了盾，除非你正在操作被攻击的小队不然基本上就灭队了，而此游戏最多只能被击倒一名队员可以救起搬回补给点复活，被击倒2名直接任务失败。玩家bot假警戒碰到CQB的情况，那就更搞笑了，邪恶帝国军在转角CQB碰到玩家的99%的情况下不仅可以无视掩体直接打死顶盾的人，速度也更快更准完全就是FPS游戏的bot，而玩家的小队还在回合制游戏等roll骰子，即便玩家使用攻击跃进枪线驾到目标了，能打赢的情况也是bot逼近中距离而不是贴脸CQB了。

于是玩家小队丢骰子等回合和FPS级bot打，再配合上玩家所有的指挥命令必须等小队长说完命令，读完条才会去执行，再慢一步。直接导致这游戏在中后期任务里给玩家加入更多只有掩体而没法‘战略侧袭’的大走廊，街区和各种转交遇到爱的CQB，难度飙升，越打头越大，越打感觉哪里都不如ARMA（即便用的无modARMA官方bot）。

FSW这玩意也就这样了，我看THQ以后也不会有任何重启这化石的可能性，而THQ Nordic作为THQ的亡魂诈尸后，不仅没卖这游戏的IP（估计也卖不出去），也没对这游戏进行任何现代系统的兼容性适配，虽然我只碰到了过场直升机没声音的bug并没碰到别的win10兼容问题，评论区很显然win10还有完全不兼容，声音大多有问题之类的毛病。更好玩但是角色模型被生软重做以后更烂的续作FSW十锤训练关所有文字还会闪烁或消失。

Tips小提示：真有别人也来考古的话，启动一次游戏后根目录会生成一个叫分辨率的cfg文件，里面只有分辨率这一个项目，改成自己的分辨率就半支持现代宽屏了，画面会被轻度拉伸。

I have mixed feelings about this game. It was good when it came out and it stands as a unique third-person strategy game.
In the game, you are the leader of 2 marine squads (some times 3) and you should move them around in a kind of strategy game where they should take cover, shoot, cover the other team, use items, etc. It is not a shooter and it should not be compared with CoD, MoH or BF.
It is somewhat still innovative as you were not used to pick soldier squads and play with them as an RTS while you are trying to not lose anyone. And as an important point, each time one of the soldiers is wounded, you should organize the squads to take the fallen soldier out of combat and move him to the medical post, which is very cool. Your items are limited on each mission and you should keep a track of how many grenades you have and the ammo, which add a realistic touch.
Graphics are pretty good for 2004 and the gameplay is kind of good taking in count the strategy part of the game.
Downsides... I found some bugs that I am pretty sure are coming from this being an old game, in one of them, the objective did not updated after I completed it and I needed to restart the level. Some minor bugs are that when you kill the enemies they remain standing on their place, which is only a kind of graphical bug but looks funny. Other bug, when I ask the grenadier guy to blow some stuff up he gets stuck behind the squad and does nothing, some times he is even kill because of that, lol.
The story is pretty mainstream, just go to a desert country in the Middle East and start shooting against a Muslim dictator while you clean the way for UN help for the civilians.
I recommend this game if it is on sale

For $2.49 you better grab this sh*t, and its sequel (you can get both for $4 USD). This game is still fun as hell to play in 2023, and was WAAAAYYYY ahead of its time. Some people don't consider it a shooter, but it is. you have to command certain soldiers to aim and even dictate where they shoot. This game is what set the ground work for games like Six Days in Fallujah. The features in this game, and the tactical nature of it are what would pave the way for tactical shooters to become what they have. It wanted to give full squad based commands without the ability to do that in 2004. 

If you have never played this game, welcome to old school gaming, because these are the games that made gaming great.

Full Spectrum Warrior: Ten Hammers, developed by Pandemic Studios and published by THQ Nordic, is a tactical shooter that expands on the unique gameplay of its predecessor, offering a strategic and immersive approach to modern combat. Released in 2006 for PC, PlayStation 2, and Xbox, the game places players in command of small fireteams navigating the war-torn fictional country of Zekistan. Unlike traditional first-person shooters, Ten Hammers emphasizes squad-level tactics over direct control, challenging players to think carefully about positioning, cover, and coordination in dynamic urban combat environments.

In Ten Hammers, players guide multiple squads through a series of missions that focus on suppressive fire, movement, and engagement with enemy forces. The game encourages strategic planning, as success depends on coordinating team movements, splitting squads effectively, and using available assets such as armored vehicles and mechanized support. This command-focused gameplay sets it apart from more reflex-based shooters, rewarding players who approach encounters thoughtfully and adapt to evolving battlefield conditions. The addition of new features, including interior positioning for squads and the ability to manage mechanized units, further enhances tactical options and provides a sense of realism to each engagement.

The visual presentation in Ten Hammers is a step up from the original Full Spectrum Warrior, with detailed character models, realistic urban environments, and smoother animations. The game successfully conveys the intensity of urban warfare, portraying narrow streets, fortified positions, and complex building layouts that require careful maneuvering. Complementing the visuals, the sound design is robust and atmospheric, with authentic weapon effects, ambient city sounds, and voice communications that help immerse players in the experience. The combination of visuals and audio reinforces the game’s tactical focus, allowing players to make informed decisions based on cues in the environment.

The story in Ten Hammers adds depth to the tactical gameplay, exploring the experiences of soldiers caught in asymmetric warfare. Players follow characters such as Sergeant Eric Daniels, navigating missions that highlight both the dangers of combat and the moral dilemmas faced in high-stakes operations. Themes of duty, sacrifice, and redemption are woven into the narrative, providing motivation and context for the player’s actions and enhancing engagement beyond the strategic mechanics.

Multiplayer adds another layer to the experience, offering both cooperative and competitive modes. Cooperative play allows friends to tackle missions together, emphasizing communication and teamwork, while competitive modes challenge players to outmaneuver and outthink opponents in objective-based scenarios. This variety not only extends replayability but also showcases the tactical depth of the game when human decision-making is involved, making multiplayer an appealing option for those looking for more dynamic challenges.

While Ten Hammers has many strengths, it is not without its drawbacks. Some players have noted that the AI can be inconsistent, with enemies occasionally behaving unpredictably or unrealistically. The control scheme, focused on issuing squad commands rather than direct character movement, may feel cumbersome to those accustomed to conventional shooters. Additionally, the absence of direct control over individual soldiers can reduce the sense of immediacy for players seeking a more hands-on combat experience.

Overall, Full Spectrum Warrior: Ten Hammers is a compelling and distinctive entry in the tactical shooter genre. Its focus on strategic squad management, realistic urban combat, and immersive storytelling provides a unique alternative to traditional first-person shooters. While it may not satisfy those looking for fast-paced action or direct character control, it rewards careful planning, coordination, and tactical thinking, offering a deep and engaging experience for fans of strategy-driven combat games.

La suite du premier volet !

Histoire :
Elle se déroule toujours dans un pays fictif, le Zékistan aprés les événements du premier jeu.
Alors que vous avez zigouillé le premier dictateur, voilà qu'un nouveau tyran surgit de nul part et essaye de repousser l'armée américaine qui a envahi le Zékistan.
A l'instar du premier jeu vous devrez donc diriger 2 unités de 4 soldats au fur et à mesure de missions dont le succés participera à la victoire de l'US army contre l'armée d'insurgés.

Gameplay:
Identique à celui du premier volet, il consiste à diriger quasiment en temps réel et avec une base tactique et stratégique vos 2 équipes.
Chacun de vos soldats est précieux car ils possédent tous des compétences uniques (sniper, mitrailleuse lourde, éclaireur, etc...). Votre objectif sera donc de finir les missions tout en gardant vos hommes en vie, chose qui ne sera pas aisée suivant le mode de difficulté que vous choisissez !
Au début, il est vrai que le gameplay est assez complexe à prendre en main, mais ne vous laissez pas avoir par cet obstacle, le jeu en vaut la peine par la suite.
Vous aurez aussi la possibilité d'utiliser des véhicules avec des armes lourdes comme des lances grenades par exemple.
Les possibilités tactiques sont donc multiples et ce sera à vous en tant que chef de faire les bons choix en permanence car la moindre erreur ne pardonne pas dans ce jeu, heureusement qu'il y la sauvegarde. Je vous conseil donc de sauvegarder trés réguliérement !

Graphismes : 
C'est le point noir du jeu bien évidemment.
En même temps, pour un jeu sorti en 2006 c'est normal... Les textures ont malgré tout mal vieillies, ce qui casse un peu l'immersion, heureusement on se laisse prendre par le gameplay unique en son genre.
Pour ma part, pas de bugs ni de lags.

Difficulté :
Il y a 3 niveaux de difficulté au choix. Le niveau sergent est le plus facile et vous êtes guidés tout le long du jeu. Vient ensuite le niveau moyen puis difficile. Le niveau difficile est hardcore car vous n'aurez plus aucune visibilité sur la position des ennemis par exemple... Donc le stress est total !

Durée de vie :
12 missions à accomplir en l'espace de 20 h

Prix :
Moins de 5 euros en soldes !

Zacznijmy od tego jak w ogóle natrafiłem na tę grę. Historia jest krótka: pewnego dnia, kiedy sprzątałem u siebie w pokoju, znalazłem pudełko z tym tytułem na biurku u góry. Okładka pudełka przykuła mą uwagę, więc, po sprzątnięciu biurka z kurzy, wyjąłem płytkę, włożyłem do komputera i zainstalowałem. Po uruchomieniu gra wymagała podania klucza produktu, który był podany z tyłu pudełka z płytą, który z jakiegoś powodu nie działał. 

Cóż, kombinowałem i kombinowałem, ale nie wyszło i musiałem grę kupić gdzieś indziej by w nią zagrać. Padło na platformę Steam, a z racji że gra była pewnego razu na przecenie, zakupiłem produkt wraz z częścią pierwszą. 

Ograłem jedynkę i mi się spodobała pomimo dużej ilości łacińskich zwrotów rzuconych na ekran monitora, gdyż gra była wymagająca i trudna. Po jej przejściu przyszło na cześć o podtytule Ten Hammers. 

Czy kolejna część tej małej i nieco zapomnianej serii mnie kupiła? Początkowo, tak, nawet jak się szybko okazało, że gra jest nieco popsuta. To był dopiero początek, zanim dowiedziałem się o większej ilości błędów, ale wracając: grało mi się przyjemnie, ze względu na klimat, muzykę (która jest świetna) oraz, co najważniejsze, mechaniki. Otóż grę można nazwać taką dopieszczoną jedynką, gdyż w porównaniu z poprzedniczką, lepiej rozwiązano dowodzenie oddziałami kontrolowanymi przez gracza czy poprawiono sztuczną inteligencję przeciwników, przez co stali się bardziej przebiegli i cwani (mimo, że miewają swoje gorsze momenty podczas rozgrywki). Poprawiono również grafikę, m.in modele postaci czy strukturę poziomów.

Ogółem, Ten Hammers daje graczowi nieco większą swobodę dobierania różnych taktyk niż jedynka, ale i tak kończymy zwykle w tym samym miejscu, w taki sam sposób.

Niestety, wcześniej wspomniane przeze mnie błędy dają się we znaki. Podam kilka przykładów: muzyka grana podczas walki, która mimo tego, że jest super i idealnie pasuje do klimatu gry, to, względem jedynki, nie przestaje się odtwarzać w chwilach gdzie żaden z oddziałów nie walczy z jakimś przeciwnikiem. Trochę to zaburza immersję. Kolejny przykład: moment, w którym choćby jeden z waszych żołnierzy pada, a gra staje w miejscu. Czytałem w sekcji dyskusje na Steam o pewnym rozwiązaniu tego problemu, który działa, lecz niezawsze, przez co musiałem nie dopuszczać do zastrzelenia choćby jednego z moich żołnierzy. Oj, męczyłem się okrutnie, ale ostatecznie uważam, że było warto.

Jednakże, mimo pewnych niedoskonałości, uważam, że status bycia zapomnianą gra nie przysługuje żadnej z serii FSW, a już na pewno nie Ten Hammers. Polecam serdecznie zagrać w obie te gry. Co prawda, są nieco przestarzałe, w końcu jedna już ma 20 lat na karku, ale jeśli ktoś szuka chociażby dobrej gry taktycznej, to niech już nie szuka, bo zamiast jednej ma do ogrania aż dwie dobre gry taktyczne, tylko niech przymknie oko na błędy, bo naprawdę warto.

Dobra, koniec. Idę spać, bo w nocy to pisałem. Dobranoc.

FSW as a franchise is very unique and this game makes quite a few changes to the original, to mixed success. 

The good:

you can split your fire-teams, effectively giving you 4 teams to command

selecting team members to use their ability feels natural and works well

you can lose 3 team members before game over, up from 2 in the last game

you have significantly more equipment ammo (smokes, grenades, 203s) and you actually resupply them at your CASEVAC points

The 'scout' movement profile allows much more careful exploration or corners and unknown areas

being able to command the movement of both squads from either TL is a great QOL improve, overall fluidity of orders feels better.

controlling armored assets is kinda fun, if a bit gimmicky and cheesy at time.

The Mixed:

Your team carries much less ammo for their primary weapons, I've had guys running out of ammo after a couple combat encounters, not even using suppression. This means frequent trips to CASEVAC to re-up. To add to the pain, Authentic difficulty again removed your ammo count from the UI, so you basically don't know your guys are running out until they practically dry.

Firefights are more dynamic, enemies move more. Unfortunately, the devs also decided to go the route of infinite re-spawning enemies until you advance to a certain point. 

The Bad:

Performance is weird, gets good FPS and runs smooth, but there can be a lot of graphical glitches, especially in lager areas, with things disappearing/popping in, gunshot tracers going in weird directions, smoke grenades shooting grey tracers. ect. none of them are really game breaking , but they can definitely be annoying. 

The AI for you squad members seems overall worse. They will just...do random stuff sometimes, I swear. I had a squad in cover behind a solid corner, went to maneuver my other team up, and 2 of the guys just decided to glitch out and walk out from cover and get shot. Sometimes, they will be great and auto shoot some enemy I hadn't even seen, others they won't shoot someone directly in front of them no matter how much you spam point fire

They removed the jump into replay feature of the first one, making Authentic playthoughs even more tedious, especially with the general wonky nature of the AI in this game.

A frustrating buggy messy sequel that I recommend anyway. (Helps the bundle for both is very cheap) 
While it still technically expands on the gameplay, the difficulty has been increased purely via unfair poorly balanced elements.

Your troops can't go prone if caught without cover, somehow take even longer to react to danger and they always go down in one shot as opposed to sometimes taking a hit and now worst of all, Permadeath is added and you only have a small finite amount of replacement soldiers per mission.

Add in some blatantly unfair level design, sometimes even outright including enemies blatantly spawning infront of you and Ten Hammers is something that can only be recommended if you seriously need more Full Spectrum Warrior.

However what it *adds* is good, every soldier has a special action (M203 and SAW are basically functions from the first game, rifleman can do risky headshots and Team Leader can either headshot or call in air support), being able to command Bradleys (Even if sadly only other vehicle aside from a BMP once and a Humvee as a glorified turret for the end of the tutorial) and being able to split the squads in half makes Ten Hammers *very* satisfying when it works.

It's a shame since when Ten Hammers *works* it's actually great which is why I (semi-reluctantly) kept it, positive, it's still a neat expansion on the first game (With the only other game in the same style being SOCOM Tactical Strike for the PSP) but one that has alot of frustration due to the increased difficulty and a bunch of small reworks that lead to things that would work in the first game not working here with no indication they're changed until your troops get shot.

Legend: TL - Team leader
              AR - Autorifleman
              GR - Grenadier
              RF - Rifleman

I played the first game originally on PS2 when it first came out. The first game remains one of my favourites, and I revisit it now and then. I never played this game until I'd bought it here and decided to give it a go after completing the first game again.

However, the sequel isn't quite a good experience. It's enjoyable enough, even with the mediocre narration but that can be overlooked. The option to split each fireteam into battle buddies is a great idea I always wanted in the first game. It gives more options for moving around and securing paths.

What I can't get past is the atrocious cover-based system that somehow leaves your squads exposed, and some controls problems. There are numerous cases where I have a fireteam behind cover and they still manage to get taken out.

On first glance the new controls are great. You have battle buddies, the team leader can use different abilities depending on the mission, the grenadier uses his M203, the Rifleman can perform more accurate shots, and the autorifleman can suppress. I won't lie that calling in air-support is pretty cool, and controlling different vehicles is too. My biggest gripes are with the abilities though. The team leader and rifleman can both perform accurate shots, but this leaves them exposed to enemy fire as there's a short time needed for them to aim or the shots will miss. The grenadier has the same issue. Yes, you can suppress the enemy, but this also means the team leader and rifleman's aimed shots are useless as the enemy's now ducked behind cover. Obviously the M203 can hit those behind cover as long as you can hit a surrounding surface. The biggest problem I have is your autorifleman is now the only one who can suppress the enemy.

Here's an example, you take a fireteam to a corner and encounter multiple targets behind hard cover. From the corner only the TL and the AR are able to engage. In order to deal with the enemy you'll need to either suppress them, or toss smoke (these are limited so we decide not to go for smoke). With the AR selected you hold down the ability key and set the area to suppress. Problem is the ability can be blocked by your own cover if the angle's too sharp, so it fails to set up suppression. The AR blurts out his line saying he can't do that, so we try again and adjust a little. This time we're unlucky, and he goes down because using abilities leave our guys exposed. We now have to resort to a smoke and have completely lost our ability to suppress the enemy. We then us the GR to fire the M203 at our targets, but the game can be fickle and decide smoke isn't good enough obscurement and now our GR goes down. In the first game our AR would go down, but we'd still be able to suppress since logically any soldier can lay down suppression. We'll rewind now and say we successfully lay down suppression. Great, now we have to split into battle buddies in order to aim our GR at the targets. We do so and successfully take out our targets. This is different from the first game as we'd be able to suppress our targets and use the GR while the suppression is going on without splitting up. It's extra steps that get annoying over time because you're constantly dealing with splitting up teams, guys getting hit because, again, aiming abilities takes time for accurate shots.

On the shorter side, selecting Charlie and Delta units is awful. You have to hold down the team select key which opens a map where you select the unit you want. There's other radial menus, so why isn't there one for unit selection? "Hot" move is a worse version of suppress and move from the first game. I've had "hot" move fail numerous times because the fireteam decides not to shoot. With the first game half the team suppresses while the other half moves and shoots to cover, and I always had better results with this. Being able to clear buildings and go up stairs is cool, I won't lie, that was a very pleasant surprise.

The map sucks. Why did we have a GPS system in the first game and a shitty road map here that's kind of difficult to read?

If you bought the bundle, give it a try just to see the new systems, but expect some frustration. However, if you only bought the first game and are looking at this one, I'd honestly say avoid this one. On the missions that are better laid out with technicals that don't cheat by shooting through multiple smokes, it's fun. Half of the time, though, it's a bit of a frustrating chore to get through the missions.
