One of the games of my childhood, so this review is entirely biased.

Graphics: The game uses the Quake III engine to its fullest, the same engine as Jedi Outcast. The animations are really good, and the explosions and lighting are superb, especially the lightsaber effects. The size and variety of each planet is a bonus for any SW fan. Still, it shows its age, which is understandable for a 2003 game.

Sound: Difficult to review, since with John Williams behind the music, every track is one we all know and love. The saber and blaster effects sound as good as ever, considering we’re talking about 2003. The dialogue is really good, and the voice actors sound great for their time.

Story: Compared to the modern SW movies, this is top notch. Even compared to the prequels (Episodes I and II were out by the time this game was made), I’d say it’s above average. Many aspects could have been improved, but it’s more than enough to be enjoyed. The mission system looks obsolete today, but it’s straightforward, and having two different endings (light side and dark side) was really good for its time. Creating your own character and choosing your lightsaber style and hilt is a nice touch too.

Gameplay: The strongest point of this game. The saber fights, the Force powers, and the multiplayer are some of the best in any SW game. It’s mostly balanced, and it even surpasses the Battlefront games in lightsaber battles. For a game over 20 years old, I can easily say it’s among the best in terms of gameplay. The multiplayer is still strong, and mods have kept the game alive with extra campaigns and a ton of added content.

Difficulty: Average. If you know what to level up, it’s average. If not, it can be a bugger in some places. I’d say it takes above-average brain usage, but not by much.

Verdict: One of the best Star Wars games ever. It’s a must-play for any SW fan, a classic and a true gem, both in its original campaign and its multiplayer. It holds a place in my heart until the day I die.

EDIT: I recommend the SW jedi academy rebalanced. Its a mod that allows to play widescreen, bugfixes, and makes it more stable to modern computers. Also adds more character and lightsaber variety with a vanilla experience.

When the game is good, it's REAL good, with some fun levels and very satisfying lightsaber combat/force abilities to play with. Unfortunately to be frank I just did not have fun for most of the latter half of the game. The missions become 95% sith lightsaber enemies where the combat turns into a janky random feeling mess that I could not figure out a way to feel good with enemies casually blocking everything while the moment I try to attack my character falls over dead due to the idle saber animation of the enemy clipping into my body. I'm sure it's a skill issue but throughout the entire campaign past the halfway point while giving it the constant benefit of the doubt, it just kept on feeling unfair and shitty regardless of trying new strategies or methods, especially whenever the game throws 2-3 lightsaber enemies at you at once.

The story is kind of dog water, with the (necessary?) conflict with the dark side hinging on your non relationship with a character who is, frankly, super annoying and does nothing to redeem himself, but the rest of the game is great. Rather than being a Half Life like where you go through big open ended levels, you instead select missions in whatever order you want, tackling a variety of objectives.

The game smartly gives you access to your lightsaber right away, as well as all the base force powers, and from there you can choose how to develop your Jedi between levels. Pro tip: regardless of your build, make sure you have Force Healing maxxed out, because the end game has little in the way of health pickups and the combat can get brutal. There's great variety in the levels, and by the end when you've selected a new lightsaber (I went for the dual bladed staff and it rocked) you feel like a God, able to push multiple enemies at once (and the game wisely gives you plenty of excuses to Force push dudes into the abyss, which is always fun) and use Force Speed to move at 4 times your usual rate. It's almost comical how powerful you become, and your rampant brutality makes the story's gestures at exploring light side vs dark side that much sillier.

It's got just the right amount of charming 2000s jank, and has aged pretty well. It has arguably the best lightsaber combat in a game, and even though the story isn't very good this is still more than worth playing. Apparently there's a thriving mod scene too, so I need to check out those Movie Duels.

I just wrapped up Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy, a game I played often in my childhood, and It still holds some solid magic even if it doesn't live up to Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Outcast. What stood out to me the most after playing through the game most recently was the RPG elements this game brought to the table. You get to pick your character's gender, race, clothes, lightsaber hilt, lightsaber color, mission order, what weapons to bring on each mission, what force powers to upgrade at the start of each mission, and even what choice to make near the end of the game that alters the final levels and bosses. I think what Raven Software did here was pretty awesome considering the Jedi Knight series was never a light RPG prior to this game. My only issue with the game is that once you are offered the ability select either a double-bladed lightsaber or duel-bladed lightsabers about two-thirds through the game you start cutting through lightsaber opponents like butter. The parry system that makes the one on one lightsaber duels so intense all throughout Jedi Outcast and the first two-thirds of this game goes out the window. That's why I typically keep my character restricted to a single blade so that the magic of lightsaber duels are never lost.

Jedi Outcast is awesome! Honestly one of the best Star Wars experiences you could have! Topped with one of the best free-flowing lightsaber and force combat every seen, and hasn’t been bested aside from its sequel.
However it does have several flaws that you’ll have to endure to fully enjoy the game.

The biggest hurdle is absolutely the first several levels. The weapons, while I feel they are quite natural in the context of a Star Wars game (In the sense that you’re unintentionally doing your best Stormtrooper impression)… are difficult to get used to. Your Blasters are not very powerful, are hard to aim because the bolts are projectiles instead of hitscan, and enemy imperials like to move around a lot. The guns actually are pretty good once you complete your arsenal… but you’re stuck with kinda poor and inaccurate laser weapons in the first couple of levels aside from the Bowcaster which has very limited ammo. That combined with very stingy health and shield pickups can make playing the harder difficulties quite frustrating.

That is until you get your Lightsaber and force powers, where the game transforms from an okay Star Wars Adventure FPS, to what is possibly the definitive Jedi simulator, only beaten out by Jedi Academy.

The lightsaber combat is amazing, it feels incredible and feels just how it should with it cutting anything down effortlessly. Also the more you progress the more powerful your force powers get, where it becomes fun to throw around, and toy with the enemies that gave you so much trouble earlier in that game. Funnily because of this progression system that the game gets a lot easier the further into it to are.

Of course the game still has its fair share of Star Wars locales, and everything in this game looks so good for the time, and really the only thing that I think has aged are the stiff character models. Otherwise this game has a great atmosphere.

The game still has its fair share of questionable design choices. Obscure paths and puzzles, Snipers without any sort of tracer, random explosions and trip mines being placed explicitly to catch you off guard, but the game is so fun once it gets going that I think it’s mostly excusable.

I HAVE to mention Kyle Katarn man… his dialogue, remarks, design, his vocal performance, just EVERYTHING about him in this game and his story is so COOL. Just another part of the experience that is this amazing game.

Yes, as a Jedi/Lightsaber sandbox game, Jedi Academy is a strictly better game mechanically, but there’s just something so magical about Jedi Outcast’s Single Player. Maybe it’s because of how it’s paced, it’s structure, it’s story or Kyle himself, but it all results in one of my absolute favorite Star Wars games, and just a dang fine game in general.

I remember getting this game for Christmas when I was 9 years old. Turns out I was gifted one of the top 5 Star Wars games ever created. Even after two decades few other games, let alone Star Wars games, have come close to being this good. It has this way of treating you like you're smart enough to figure out how to proceed in a level without holding your hand with waypoints, an AI telling you every which way to go, or a compass. It's combat is fantastic and always has this way of holding a little bit back so that you always come back wanting more. For instance, you don't retrieve your lightsaber until 7 levels into the game. You would think that this choice would be a horrible idea given that this game is, at its core, a jedi game but its not. It allows for the story to play out without being too fast paced and, like I said earlier, keeps you wanting to return because you didn't quiet get that scratch itched fully the first time. For more context, Jedi Outcast is a soft sequel to Dark Forces (1995) and Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II (1997). No need to play those unless you're curious to see what the road to perfection looks like (and if you enjoy Kyle Katarn's story). There is a sequel to this game that is just as much fun even if the story isn't as polished called Jedi Academy (2003) but if you want my honest opinion this is the single game to play if you're looking for a kick-ass Jedi Adventure. If you've never played Jedi Outcast before you should and if you already have you should play it again.

This is real Star Wars. They say Jedi Outcast and Jedi Academy have the best lightsaber combat ever. It’s very easy to believe.

These games have amazing jedi gameplay. You can swing your saber and unleash force powers while running and jumping. You can swing your saber in multiple directions, and utilize multiple styles and techniques. You can mind trick stormtroopers into shooting each other. You can throw enemies around with force grip, and fry them with force lightning. You can even pull a Disney, and throw your lightsaber away.

Jedi Outcast and Jedi Academy have a few important differences. I’d list them like this:

1. Story-
Basically, Kyle Katarn had once given up on the life of a jedi, but, when something bad happens, he seeks the power of the force once again so that he can “fix” the problem. Outcast focuses on its plot. Academy is very episodic, and is more like a jedi career sim with bad guys occasionally appearing between missions. Outcast’s story is easily more interesting and immersive than the bland nothingness in Academy. Also, Kyle is great as the main character. Jaden Korr (Academy’s MC), on the other hand, has no character. The story in Outcast won’t blow your mind, but it IS entertaining, which is all it’s supposed to be.

2. Lightsaber and The Force-
In Outcast, you have to play the first few levels without a lightsaber or force powers. That’s how the story goes, of course. After that, your force powers develop on their own without any input from you. I understand the story reasons for not having the lightsaber at first. If this game was ever remade though, there wouldn’t really be any reason to not let the player choose which of Kyle’s force powers to upgrade at each level, aside from jump and mind trick. In Academy, you have your lightsaber from the very beginning, and, after the tutorial, you can pick and choose the force powers you want. This has a huge impact on difficulty, as you can deflect enemy fire and heal on your very first mission. Of course, the freedom to customize your character, force powers and lightsabers gives Academy a lot more replay value. I admit, I replay Academy more often than Outcast for this reason.

3. Difficulty-
(I have completed the game on “jedi master” difficulty, which might affect my review...) Difficulty hits WAY harder in Outcast than it does in Academy, and not just because you’re not a jedi for the first few levels and can’t use heal for half the game. In Outcast, the difficulty is sometimes purposefully scaled up to keep ahead of you. For example, as soon as you get your lightsaber, the game introduces snipers who will disintegrate you from across the map, shooting you with lasers that can’t be blocked with your lightsaber. (This laser rifle isn’t as convenient for you, of course.) Sometimes you’ll die to this sniper fire a few times before you’re even able to figure out where it’s coming from. In this way, the difficulty is sometimes very artificial, and blatantly unfair. In this game, just expect that you’re going to die on certain levels. There are also levels where you have to defend a target from an army of enemies. They’re the kind of defense missions where the target you’re supposed to protect is always in the thick of it, and your only option is to destroy all enemies as quickly as possible with reckless self-abandon. On jedi master difficulty, you frankly just have to be lucky to pass these objectives in less than 50 attempts each. These defense objectives are easily the most frustrating part of the game. It can also sometimes be difficult to find the way forward. Sometimes you need to crawl through a small hole, or shoot a specific object that’s hidden somewhere, or jump down far enough that you can’t avoid taking damage. There’s one level where the way forward is hidden underwater in an inconspicuous pond. Academy has none of these difficulties. There are a few snipers out of reach, but none of them will disintegrate you with their first shot. Instead, Academy has a few enemies that can protect and heal themselves, and a few enemies with a new overpowered “rifle”. In the end though, the feats of Jaden Korr are absolutely nothing compared to Kyle Katarn taking down an army of stormtroopers and walkers by himself, without the force, while protecting unarmed prisoners who are too stupid to take cover. If you play Outcast on one of the easier difficulties, it’s not too bad though. (Just… don’t play Outcast on the jedi master level, unless you actually are one.)

In short, play Outcast when you want story (or difficulty), and play Academy when you want to rule the galaxy with your force grip. Overall, I feel like Outcast is more dear to my heart as a nostalgic Star Wars memory, but I feel like some people might choose Academy instead.

One more thing. You will probably take a look at the controls before you play, but just so you know… There is one level that you can NOT complete without the datapad if you want to stay sane. (It gives you the codes that you need to contact Rogue Squadron.) This game has the usual WASD keyboard and mouse controls, and you can remap them if you need to. (You can also remap force powers.) Just make sure you know how to access the datapad for that one level. (The datapad also tells you what force powers have been upgraded at each level.) This game doesn’t tell you about saber styles or the different moves you can use, but you can figure that out.

There are a lot of nice things you can say about JO:
I like the weapon variety, the way it expands lore past the OG trilogy (the sequel writers could learn a lot from it if they gave a shit), Kyle Katarn works well as a protagonist, the fact that you can lure enemies into traps and the level verticality, it allows a very creative playstyle in theory. 

[b] H O W E V E R [/b]

The fucking level design man, it has so many traps if you are playing it for the first time, just a ton of "you rounded the corner and there are 20 stormtroopers on the other side with hit scan accuracy", meanwhile the E-11 blaster which you'll be using for the first 7 levels just feels terrible as a main weapon. Once you get access to tripwires, detpacks and grenades it gets better, but not by much.

In later levels you get access to force powers and a lightsaber, so you are probably thinking "Okay, now I'll be able to handle the enemies with ease". No, the random disruptor rifle wielding aliens in 8th level will bend you over and fuck you. They always know where you are and they will nail you from across the map during a jump mid air. The grenade throwing aliens must have graduated the Star Wars version of Oxford with honours, because they will perfectly calculate the trajectory of grenades to hit you three floors down on the fly.

The damage calculation is inconsistent. Sometimes the Remnant officer will die to one crossbow hit. Other times he will tank 3 of them like it's nothing. I have seen a Rodian take a fully charged disruptor rifle shot to the head and just shrug it off. Grenades thrown by the enemy have an explosion radius the size of a football stadium, but when you throw them if you don't score a direct hit they do jack all.

I don't know if it ever gets better, because the game is actually so frustrating I quit at that point.

Many great memories attached to this game. 
I remember how groundbreaking this was when it released. I used to play multiplayer splitscreen for hours on the GameCube. 
As the years have gone on, this one has certainly shown its age. 
However, this is still one of the best Star Wars games ever released. 
I really like the mixture of gunplay and lightsaber fighting. 

Kyle Katarn is a cool character in this. He's moved from a young man into a more grizzled older man that is more wise-cracking and skeptical. A bit of a smuggler, but still on the side of good and the force. 
It gets a lot better once you obtain the lightsaber and get your force powers back, since the lightsaber combat is really what makes this special. It's a drastic improvement over Dark Forces II. 
Your force powers grow stronger as the game progresses too. 
So you gain more abilities and get a lot stronger in the force. 
And it's super satisfying to throw your lightsaber and cut off a Stormtrooper's arm. 

I think Desann is a visually cool villain (he's basically a talking dinosaur). 
He's absolutely massive and has an awesome voice. 
However, he's barely in the game, and his character development is wafer thin. 

The level designs are cool. 
Really interesting designs that were what made the Expanded Universe so special. 

There were a few weird bugs - nothing that crashed or broke the game. 
However, there was a scene where Kyle didn't have eyelids or lips... kinda scary... 
Some of the enemies had parts of their faces disappear when you looked at them through scopes. 
And for some reason there was no way to change the aspect ratio from widescreen to 4:3. It was stuck in what appeared to be an artificially stretched aspect ratio.
Too boomer of a boomer shooter for me.

[h1]"Изгой-джедай"[/h1]

[quote][b]Культовый проект, являющийся основоположником всей дальнейшей серии игр по ЗВ. Именно в этом произведении вам выпадает честь испытать на себе всю мощь силы джедаев и побывать спутником в их нелегкой, но полной приключений жизни.[/b][/quote]

[h3]Сюжет[/h3]

[b]Давным-давно, 
в далекой-далекой галактике...[/b]
Наш главный герой (известный по ранее вышедшим проектам серии и имеющий статус маскота игровой ретро-линейки) [b]Кайл Катарн[/b] и его спутница [b]Джен Орс[/b], расследуют подозрительную имперскую активность на планете [b]Кеджим[/b]. [b]Кайл[/b], являющийся ранее джедаем, отказался от своей силы в связи с тем, что были повадки перейти на темную сторону. В этом же эпизоде, протагонист представляет собой одного из наемников [b]Новой Республики[/b]. Но, во время выполнения поручения на [b]Кеджиме[/b], происходит неожиданное столкновение с темным джедаем [b]Десанном[/b] и его соратницей [b]Тавион[/b]. После тяжелой встречи, [b]Кайлу[/b] предстоит пересмотреть свое решение об отказе от "силы" и посетить [b]Долину джедаев[/b]...

[h3]Геймплей[/h3]

Проект представляет из себя смесь нескольких игровых жанров и богатую геймплейную вариативность.
Игра плавно и гармонично раскрывается, не разбрасываясь козырями раньше времени.
Изначально, в нашем арсенале, как и подобает стандартному наемнику - [b]электрическая дубинка[/b], [b]бластер[/b] и [b]бинокль[/b].
Постепенно, инвентарь пополняется найденными у врагов пушками: 
[list]
 [*][b]Бластерная винтовка[/b]
 [*][b]Арбалет вуки[/b] 
 [*][b]Ракетница[/b] 
 [*][b]Снайперская винтовка[/b]
 [*]и много прочего
[/list]
Помимо огнестрельного вооружения, вам предстоит использовать - [b]очки ночного видения[/b], [b]гранаты[/b], [b]мины[/b], [b]бомбы[/b], [b]турели[/b], [b]дроида-стрелка[/b].
В общем арсенал здесь богатый, и это мы еще не поднимали тему [b][u]светового меча[/u][/b]...

Как только в руки [b]Кайла Катарна[/b] попадает тот самый лазерный клинок, геймплей и ведение боя в корне меняется. Из безобидного солдатика с пистолетиками, вы превращаетесь в берсерка, после встречи с которым [b]Империи[/b] остается только молить о пощаде. 
Великолепно и зрелищно воссозданная боевка с фехтованием на мечах, с [b]3-мя[/b] стилями боя:
[olist]
 [*][b]Быстрый стиль[/b] (голубой) - молниеносные, но легкие атаки, которые не нанесут много урона, но позволят эффектно расправиться с массированными атаками рядовых противников.

 [*][b]Нейтральный стиль[/b] (желтый) - базовый стиль, подходящий под большую часть хронометража. Поможет вам как с "мелким" оппонентом, так и с более грозным.

 [*][b]Сильный стиль[/b] (красный) - лучшее решение для дуэли на световых мечах. Наносит колоссальный урон, но имеет в себе медленную скорость замаха, в связи с чем [b]Кайл[/b] становится "открытым" для ударов врага.
[/olist]
Конечно же [b]джедаи[/b] известны не только умением обращаться с клинком, но и своей могущественной силой.
Здесь вас ожидают все возможные способы взаимодействия с ней: [b]бросок светового меча[/b], [b]рикошет[/b] вражеских бластеров, [b]удушение[/b], [b]отбрасывание[/b], [b]притягивание[/b], [b]высокие прыжки[/b], [b]излечение[/b], [b]замедление времени[/b], [b]управление разумом[/b] и [b]извержение молнией[/b].

На каждой из локаций вам предстоит много бродить и изучать их, ведь здесь нет никаких опознавательных знаков для дальнейшего продвижения, хотя на первый взгляд дизайн уровней может показаться коридорным. Помимо этого, приходится искать много [b]секретных[/b] проходов, которые являются стандартными для продвижения по сюжету, но некоторые из них настолько запрятаны, что могут продлить хронометраж определенного уровня на приличное количество времени, пока вам удастся отыскать задуманный путь. 

Персонаж имеет шкалу [b]здоровья[/b] и [b]брони[/b], вследствие чего предстоит собирать [b]медпакеты[/b], [b]аптечки[/b] (бакта) и [b]стимуляторы[/b] брони. Также встречаются "[b]станции[/b]" на которых можно "подзарядить" здоровье и броню. 

Не забыли и про [b]секретные[/b] места на большинстве локаций, но отыскать каждый из них является крайне трудной задачей, да и награда за это не столь велика (патроны, аптечки, гранаты и т.п)

Помимо [b]стрельбы[/b] и [b]дуэлей на мечах[/b] предстоит заниматься "[b]платформингом[/b]" и решением различных [b]загадок[/b]. В основном, загадки строятся на глобальном изучении локации, чтобы понять что от вас требуют для продвижения, а также на взаимодействии с определенной способностью "[b]силы[/b]" в назначенных для этого местах.

В основном, свой путь [b]Кайлу[/b] предстоит пройти в одиночку, но иногда его сопровождают товарищи с бластерами или световыми мечами, и на удивление очень хорошо помогают в борьбе с [b]Империей[/b]. Но, если это важный для сюжета персонаж, то вы можете надеяться на его поддержку, также как и он на вашу, ведь если он погибнет, то будьте добры начинать сначала.

Также проект подразумевает сетевые баталии, но мне не удосужилось их испробовать.

Хронометраж - около [b]16[/b] часов (на тяжелом уровне сложности).

[h3]Атмосфера[/h3]

Сразу же хочется сказать за превосходную графику проекта, которая радует глаз и в настоящее время. Каждый из персонажей отлично воссоздан, также как и [b]выстрелы бластеров[/b] или же модель [b]светового меча[/b]. Пользоваться клинком и слышать звуки скрещивания мечей с оппонентом - одно удовольствие. 

Проект затрагивает обильную географию и демографию вселенной Звездных войн, поэтому вам посчастливиться побывать на таких локациях как:
[list]
 [*]База империи на [b]Кейджиме[/b] 
 [*]Горнодобывающий комплекс на [b]Артусе-Прайм[/b] (шахты и тюрьма [b]Империи[/b], где удерживают пленных)
 [*][b]Академия джедаев[/b] (дом [b]Люка Скайуокера[/b])
 [*]Улицы [b]Нар Шаддаа[/b] (луна заполненная наемниками и контрабандистами)
 [*][b]Беспин[/b], облачный город (дом [b]Лэндо Калриссиана[/b])
и прочие
[/list]
Каждая из локаций масштабна для изучения и может порадовать своей каноничностью тех, кто уже знаком с ними по прочим произведениям вселенной.

По ходу прохождения, своим присутствием вас смогут порадовать такие знаменитые персонажи, как: [b]Люк Скайуокер[/b], [b]Лэндо Калриссиан[/b], [b]Мон Мотма[/b], [b]R2-D2[/b] и [b]C-3PO[/b]. Было приятно и отрадно увидеться с ними и взаимодействовать по ходу приключения.

За фоновое музыкальное сопровождение будут отвечать каноничные знакомые фанатам треки из кинематографа.

[h3]По итогу[/h3]

Проект, который дал старт свежей и играбельной линейке игр по вселенной [b]ЗВ[/b]. 
Имеющий в себе вариативный и качественный геймплей, о котором игроки (в корне фанаты) могли только мечтать в свое время. Бережно передающий атмосферу известных локаций и дающий достаточно времени, чтобы насытиться ими. Сюжет малость поверхностный и созданный скорее для заминки всех событий, но и этого достаточно, чтобы с интересом погрузить вас в необъятную вселенную.

На этом этапе оканчивается наше знакомство с [b]Кайлом Катарном[/b] - харизматичным, дерзким и своеобразным наемником-джедаем, который выделяется среди большей доли персонажей своим характером. Далее нам удастся его лицезреть в последующем релизе - [b]Jedi Academy[/b], но лишь в роли второстепенного персонажа. [b]Ретро-эпоха[/b] закончилась вместе с уходом этого колоритного персонажа, как и началось свежее переосмысление линейки в ногу со временем, в связи с чем [b]Кайл[/b] передает эстафету и уходит на покой.

Это проект не о джедае. А просто о парне со световым мечом.
[b]Сила[/b] — это здорово, но хороший бластер на боку тоже никогда не помешает.

[h1]𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝔻𝕀𝔾™[/h1] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3815747880 K Zemi se blíží obří asteroid Attila hrozící globální katastrofou. Posádka raketoplánu Atlantis, vedená Bostonem Lowem, je vyslána přímo k tělesu. Cílem této nebezpečné misie je odpálit jaderné nálože a změnit kurz asteroidu. Záhy se však ukáže, že to není jen tak obyčejný vesmírní šutrák, ale...

Vývoj hry The Dig trval sedm let pod vedením LucasArts. Původní nápad pochází od Stevena Spielberga, který chtěl příběh natočit jako film nebo epizodu seriálu Amazing Stories. Kvůli obrovským finančním nákladům na triky projekt nakonec předal studiu LucasArts k herní adaptaci. Na hře se vystřídali čtyři různí hlavní designéři. Projekt začal Noah Falstein, ale po neshodách odešel. Další verze vedli Brian Moriarty a Dave Grossman, až hru do finální podoby roku 1995 dotáhl Sean Clark. Hra původně plánovala mnohem temnější a krvavější tón. V Moriartyho verzi měla jedna z postav zemřít brutálním rozsekáním a hra obsahovala drsné násilí. LucasArts však projekt kvůli strachu z ratingu přístupnosti radikálně zmírnilo. Během sedmi let se neustále přepisoval herní engine a grafika. Vývojáři začínali s klasickým 2D stylem SCUMM, experimentovali s renderovaným 3D pozadím a nakonec složitě kombinovali ručně kreslenou grafiku s tehdy moderními digitálními efekty. 

Koncept Stevena Spielberga provázela i obří porce chaosu. Hra prošla čtyřmi restarty pod jinými autory, měnila engine ze 2D na 3D a škrtala drsnou brutalitu. Z původního epického sci-fi přežilo jen jádro příběhu. Záchranná mise raketoplánu Atlantis se mění v epickou mezihvězdnou odyseu. Boston Low, novinářka Maggie Robbins a geolog Ludger Brink jsou uvězněni na opuštěné planetě v jiné galaxii. Místo záchrany Země před asteroidem Attila teď bojují o vlastní přežití v cizím ekosystému. Svět Cocytus je plný podivných technologických věží, energetických mostů a mystických tajemství. Nebezpečí nepředstavují monstra, ale neznámé fyzikální zákony a podstata samotného života a smrti, reprezentovaná záhadnou mimozemskou energií. Low prochází nehostinnou krajinou, kombinuje nalezené artefakty a komunikuje s duchovními zbytky dávné civilizace. Pouze pochopení této vyšší formy existence umožní lidem zprovoznit transportní loď a vrátit se domů.

The Dig je čistokrevná příběhová adventura, která využívá vyvolatelný inventář a hráči hru servíruje v plné obrazovce bez jakéhokoliv ořezání jak to bylo v předešlých hrách. Hratelnost je hodně podobná moderním new-retro point and click adventurám a její "filmovost" tohle jěště více upevňuje. Taky obsahuje solidní porci cut-scén a v neposledním řadě se herně jedná o typický příklad stylizace herniho ovládání adventur na konci minulého tisíciletí. The Dig se hraje dobře, ale chce dosti otevřenou mysl a né zcela typický způsob uvažování, obzvláště pak po příletu na planetu Cocytus. Mimozemská technologie je kort jiná a založená na geometrii a lomu světla. A pro Ty, co chtějí hrát zcela bez návodu pak nastává jasná nutnost počítat se zákysy a "zkoušením všeho na všechno". Puzzlík, puzzlice a puzzlíčata. Klasikové a pro žáner zapálení "pojnt-end-klikové" to znají... [hr][/hr] Slovo Kokytos (v latinské transkripci Cocytus) původně v řecké mytologii označovalo „řeku nářků“, která protékala podsvětím. Slavný italský básník Dante Alighieri pak ve své Božské komedii (konkrétně v části Peklo) tento koncept upravil. Udělal z Cocytu zamrzlé jezero v devátém, úplně posledním kruhu pekla, kde v krutém mrazu pykají ti nejhorší zrádci. Znáte anime seriál Overlord? Podobnost je až podezřele vysoká a to v mnoha směrech:[list][*][b]The Dig[/b] ([i]LucasArts, 1995[/i]): Když trojice astronautů uvízne na opuštěné, nehostinné a zdánlivě mrtvé mimozemské planetě, pojmenuje ji archeolog Ludger Brink právě Cocytus. Je to přímý odkaz na Dantovo ledové peklo, ze kterého je nesmírně těžké uniknout. [*][b]Overlord[/b] ([i]anime seriál od roku 2015[/i]): Strážce 5. podlaží Velké hrobky Nazaricku – ten obří, modrý ledový hmyzí válečník se čtyřma rukama – se jmenuje Cocytus ze stejného důvodu. Jeho domovské 5. podlaží je totiž kompletně zamrzlý ledovec a on sám vládne mrazivými útoky a ledovou aurou.[/list] Není to tedy náhoda ani vzájemné kopírování, ale skvělé využití historické a literární symboliky pro mrazivá či izolovaná místa. Když v Overlordovi navrhovali postavu strážce ledového podlaží, spojení jména Cocytus s designem, který vzdáleně připomíná ikonické hmyzí emzáky z legendární hry The Dig (která se odehrává na planetě Cocytus), dává až příliš dokonalý smysl, než aby to byla čistá náhoda. Buď jde o záměrný skrytý odkaz (Easter Egg), nebo o hluboko zakořeněnou podvědomou inspiraci.[hr][/hr] Vesmírné sci-fi s duší klasického pekla.

[b]P.S.[/b]: Jelikož se jedná o "talkie" SCUMM CD verzi, tak pro ukončení hry jsou tlačítka Q, nebo X. Nejjednodušší je ale hned po spuštěni hry ([b][i]a pak i kdykoliv během hraní[/i][/b]) zmáčknout F5 pro základní menu a nastavení hry.

Spielberg bankrolled a sci-fi adventure game in 1995 because apparently that's what genius filmmakers do when they get bored, and somehow LucasArts made something genuinely worth playing out of it. This is what happens when a studio has enough budget to make every pixel count and enough restraint to not waste it on bloat.

You're an astronaut sent to nuke an asteroid, find an alien megastructure instead, and immediately realize everything's about to go sideways in the most mysterious, atmospheric way possible. The game's a point-and-click adventure, which means: lots of clicking, minimal combat, and the kind of puzzles that'll make you feel stupid until the moment you crack them, then instantly brilliant. No hand-holding, no dialogue trees begging for your choice, just "figure this out yourself or die wondering."

The soundtrack is orchestral perfection — Michael Land built something that'd make a legitimate film score composer jealous. The atmosphere is thick, genuinely unsettling in that "why is this alien planet so dead?" way. The story lands because it's written with actual restraint, treating sci-fi like an art form instead of an excuse for laser guns.

It's dated in the way classic adventure games are dated — the point-and-click mechanic feels older than it is, the graphics are 1995 — but the fundamentals are timeless. Spielberg's fingerprints are all over this (he dreamed it up for TV, got bored, made it a game instead), and it shows in the weird maturity of a LucasArts game that refuses to crack jokes.

Get it. Embrace the clicking. Your brain will thank you.

The Dig dividiu bastante os fãs dos jogos Adventure da LucasArts, e agora que joguei entendo perfeitamente o motivo: ele é muito mais similar a um jogo da franquia Myst do que qualquer outro jogo que a empresa lançou previamente. O jogador passa grande parte do jogo sozinho desvendando a lógica de mecanismos alienígenas, e mesmo quando interage com outros personagens o humor e a leveza característicos da empresa não estão presentes aqui, os personagens são cientistas que nos melhores momentos se aturam, e nos piores se odeiam.

Isso tudo contribui para uma experiência bem mais fria e cerebral do que os jogos anteriores da empresa mas, especialmente sendo fã de Myst, eu consegui ver o valor dessa abordagem. Eu gostei bastante da ambientação do planeta alienígena, achei ele lindo e interessante de explorar, e a excelente trilha sonora ambiente dele ajuda a imergir o jogador nesse mundo. Os puzzles são mais pro lado difícil aqui também, com alguns até bem complicados (o puzzle da tartaruga é temido por muitos mas não é tão impossível quanto parece), mas no geral podem ser resolvidos sem problemas.

O que eu menos gostei foi a narrativa, acho que ela é decente mas que podia ter sido melhor trabalhada. O estilo cartoon das cutscenes animadas não me agradou tanto também, acho que não combinam com os outros elementos visuais do jogo e nem com seu tom. Mas para quem for fã dos jogos da empresa, de Myst ou de point-and-clicks dessa era como um todo, eu com certeza recomendo que dêem uma chance pro The Dig.

IMPORTANTE: Usem as teclas Alt + S pra tirar o filtro de smoothing horroroso que botaram por padrão nessa versão.

Genuinely one of my favorite of the old point and click adventures. The story is great, the characters are fun, the gameplay is pretty good compared to some of the moon-logic you got from point n clicks in those days. Most of the puzzles are pretty fun to solve, and straightforward enough to actually intuit on your own. The interface has been massively scaled down from some of the earlier SCUMM engine games, there's no 'push/pull/look/speak' actions you need to use on every fucking pixel, just click on things; it's so much better.

The graphics, while dated, still really hold up. The design on this world is still so eery, hauntingly beautiful. It really captures the vibe of a dead world filled with derelict unknowable alien artifacts.

The latter half of the game doesn't fully escape the more esoteric moon logic where instead of combining items in logical ways you end up clicking every combination just to see which ones the devs decided would work. Like, why can I jam a plate with a rod, but the 5 colored rods I have don't work, nor do the two scepters, or the tusk that I found? But it's not too egregious. Only time I had to look up solutions is when you're expected to either remote-view an area with an elevator that you already know is an elevator before the character will actually deign to step on it; and a puzzle where suddenly you need to talk to another character to trigger an action instead of interacting directly with the game world like you do the entire rest of the game. But those are small hiccups in an otherwise stellar game.

Story is fun and was less well trodden ground when this game originally came out. The ending is sort of interesting, though undercut by a lack of consequences.

The Dig is a LucasArts classic—like, actual classic. Spielberg came up with the concept, and legends like Sean Clark, Brian Moriarty, Orson Scott Card, and Michael Land helped make it real. With that much talent, the presentation is so good it practically kicks down your door and demands an 11/10.

And then… the puzzles show up.

Imagine taking a beautifully written sci‑fi movie script, stretching it into a game, and then sprinkling in puzzles designed by an alien who has never seen a human brain before. That’s The Dig. Halfway through, the puzzles stop being “challenging” and start being “a social experiment to test your patience.” Logic? Never heard of it. Trial and error? Oh, you’ll get plenty of that. Even the walkthroughs read like the authors gave up halfway through and just started guessing.

“Press the crystal thing into the glowing slot until it makes a noise.”
“Which noise?”
“¯\(ツ)/¯”

The game begins to play like you're watching a movie. Puzzles start to work with the flow of the story—but not in a way that makes sense for a game, or to the person actually playing it. But here’s the thing: the story is fantastic. The music is incredible. The acting is great. Everything about this game—except the actual game part—is absolutely amazing.

Final verdict:
Pro: Amazing sci‑fi story, gorgeous atmosphere
Con: Puzzles designed by a committee of confused space ghosts

It’s a great story, but honestly? A pretty bad game… And I just can't recommend it anymore. I'd suggest playing with a guide to finish the game once. Then replay it right after without the guide and enjoy the story. Because to me, the frustrating puzzles kill the flow of this game.

The major thing that I caution prospective players for is that THERE IS NOT AN AUTOSAVE OR INTUITIVE MENU WITH A SAVE FEATURE ON THIS VERSION OF THE GAME. It takes several hours to complete and if you close the game you will lose all of your progress. Some folks are able to save without issue using function keys, others are not. Buyer beware. Look into mod support/playing on an emulator from another source if you're not willing to binge it like I was... 

Otherwise, absolutely gorgeous artwork and animations (except the bug we don't talk about the bug) that ooze with nostalgia for the hand-drawn animation media of the time while also calling to something truly alien and bizarre. The music alone is so wonderful. The presentation of this game really is the strongest element. Savor it - drink it in, because it's what the game is really about.

The gameplay itself is a bit clunky, but nothing that experienced point-and-click gamers aren't used to. I would recommend just swallowing your pride and pulling up a guide for some of these puzzles. You literally interact with alien technology, I don't think there's any shame in not understanding what a puzzle even wants from you - there is some classic moon logic at times. The characters are kind of confusing and self-contradictory at times that makes them tough to love or to think of as 'real', but it's, again, the sort of lovable jank that adds more to the experience than it takes away IMO.

The Dig is one of the most ambitious and tonally distinct adventure games ever produced by LucasArts, standing apart from the studio’s more comedic legacy in favor of a serious, contemplative science-fiction experience. Originally inspired by a story concept from Steven Spielberg, the game embraces a cinematic scope and emotional weight that were unusual for the genre at the time. Rather than relying on humor or rapid-fire dialogue, The Dig draws players into a slow, methodical journey defined by mystery, isolation, and the awe of encountering something truly alien.

The narrative begins with a grounded, almost realistic premise: a massive asteroid is on a collision course with Earth, and a small NASA team is sent to divert it. You take control of Commander Boston Low, accompanied by journalist Maggie Robbins and scientist Ludger Brink, as they land on the asteroid to plant explosives. This opening establishes a strong sense of urgency and professionalism before dramatically shifting gears. When the asteroid is revealed to be hollow and artificial, the crew is transported to an unknown alien world, transforming what seemed like a disaster-mitigation mission into an existential exploration of a lost civilization. From that point on, the story becomes less about saving Earth and more about understanding a place abandoned long ago and the price its creators paid.

Gameplay follows traditional point-and-click adventure conventions but is structured to emphasize discovery and logical reasoning rather than overt puzzle signposting. The interface is streamlined, allowing players to focus on interacting with objects, manipulating alien technology, and piecing together how this unfamiliar world functions. Many puzzles are built around experimentation and observation, requiring players to study the environment carefully and learn the rules governing alien devices. This design choice reinforces the feeling of being stranded somewhere incomprehensible, though it can also make progress feel opaque. Some puzzles are deliberately demanding, and players are often expected to infer solutions from subtle environmental clues rather than explicit hints.

What truly defines The Dig is its atmosphere. The alien planet is vast, quiet, and melancholic, filled with strange machines, skeletal remains of long-dead beings, and architecture that suggests both immense intelligence and profound tragedy. The visual presentation, while limited by the technology of its time, uses detailed hand-painted backgrounds and moody lighting to convey scale and loneliness. Pre-rendered sequences and carefully framed scenes give the game a cinematic flair, helping it feel more like an interactive science-fiction film than a traditional adventure game.

Sound design and music play a crucial role in sustaining this mood. The orchestral score leans heavily into subdued, haunting melodies that underscore the sense of wonder and isolation. Silence is used just as effectively, allowing moments of quiet exploration to feel introspective and tense. Voice acting adds another layer of immersion, with Boston Low portrayed as stoic and pragmatic, Maggie as emotionally grounded and empathetic, and Brink as increasingly obsessive and volatile. Their evolving personalities and philosophical disagreements become an integral part of the story, giving emotional stakes to what might otherwise be a purely intellectual mystery.

The Dig’s pacing is slow and deliberate, asking players to be patient and attentive. This approach can be deeply rewarding for those willing to immerse themselves, but it can also feel unforgiving. Backtracking is common, and some sequences require careful trial and error. The game is not afraid to let players struggle, reflecting its commitment to portraying the alien world as genuinely unfamiliar rather than conveniently game-like. This design philosophy is one of the reasons the game remains divisive: for some, it enhances immersion; for others, it introduces frustration.

Taken as a whole, The Dig is a bold departure from LucasArts’ typical output and a landmark example of serious storytelling in adventure games. It prioritizes mood, thematic depth, and world-building over accessibility or humor, resulting in an experience that feels mature and introspective even by modern standards. While its puzzles and pacing may test the patience of some players, its commitment to atmosphere and narrative cohesion make it a memorable journey. For fans of classic adventure games, science fiction, or games that dare to slow down and ask bigger questions, The Dig remains a compelling and influential work that rewards curiosity and thoughtful engagement.

Growing up I played pretty much any Point & Click adventure game I could get my hands on, so I'm not sure how The Dig managed to slip under my radar.  I've been hearing about it for years now as something many P&C fans put in the top of their nostalgia lists so, I finally decided to give it a try.  I enjoyed playing it, but I'd rank it more mid list, personally.

The game does have a lot of good points.  It certainly hit a lot of nostalgic notes being very visually appealing as a a great representation of 90's pixel graphics.  Many of the backgrounds are gorgeous and detailed.  They bring a very alien other worldly aesthetic to life.  I thought the 90's cartoon animation cut scenes were charming and at times the game feels more like an interactive movie experience than a game.  They also give you plenty of spaces to explore which I really appreciate.  It plays like a true P&C adventure with an inventory you can interact with and dialogue based clues you have to pay attention to if you want to understand what needs to be done.  The games mechanics are about as simple as you can get with clicking on a hotspot pretty much being the only interaction you need.  The story was good, but maybe not as engaging and interesting as some of the other games at the time.   The voice overs and acting were excellent as well.  The game does have the cursor change color and display text description when mousing over a hot spot and there are quick skip options when double clicking exits or skip dialogue options when pressing ".", all of which make for a more enjoyable experience.

I wouldn't say the game really has many "bad" aspects, but it does have some mediocre points and places where there could have been a little improvement.  I'm aware that at this time, the game is 30 years old and so there can be different expectations for modern games.  I'm trying to keep a balanced view of good/bad for it's time and good/bad compared to modern standards.  Overall, I think the game holds up pretty well.   You might have to fiddle with some display and compatibility settings to play it full screen, but other than that it's still very playable, offers challenging puzzles, and feels like the story could be taking place now and not limited to the past or in an unrelateable future.

So what are the things I thought made it more mediocre?  Well, looking at it compared to other games of it's time (1995) we have games like Beneath A Steel Sky and King's Quest VII: The Princeless Bride which came out a year before in 1994.  Both had far more interesting and engaging stories.  Like by the end of this game l didn't have a strong feeling of closure or completion and I didn't really care much about the characters, which are feelings I got from both those other games.   I also felt that the animated cut scenes from say KQ7 were more polished and consistent than The Dig.  The characters look vastly different in quality and don't always even look like the same character in one  scene to another.  The same could be said for Space Quest 6 which released the same year as this game, far more polished animation.  All of those also had better controls.  The Dig, for example, still requires use of "F1" to access menu options for save/load, quit and settings as opposed to mouse-over, on-screen buttons, or what had already become more popular "Q" or "esc" buttons. It's not a huge issue, but feels particularly dated now and the menu option control is unintuitive.  Most modern PCs you also have to press "fn"+"F1" to now access those menus.  I also disliked that it was often difficult to tell if you could walk further to the left or right on a screen.  The game features a tram system and a later unlocked light bridge system.  The light bridges don't make travel that much quicker and it feels unnecessary to have put both in the game.  The only thing I would actually say was bad was the dialogue menu.  When you have a dialogue and exhaust the options it turns blue so you know you won't ask or hear any new things.  However, each time you open a dialogue your options are reset so you never know if there's something new to hear or just a repeat of what's already been said and that wastes time.

Finally, let's talk puzzles!  I know moon logic puzzles and dead ends where you can't complete something because you forgot to pick up something you can go back for anymore, are among the reasons why the genre is hated by many players and bad puzzles can turn off even steadfast lifelong fans like myself.  That said, the puzzles in this game were relatively easy and logical.  The hard part for most of these puzzles is that there aren't many clues as to how to solve them or more obvious instructions.  You get tiny tidbits if you pay attention in the conversations and things around you but it can leave you feeling like you don't know what to do which is frustrating.  That said there are two puzzles that felt especially frustrating and leave you to the old try everything on everything method of progression.  A puzzle to open a door by catching a critter took far longer than it should have for example.  It's pretty common to have one or two difficult to solve puzzles in a P&C game but the amount of having to guess or walk back and forth trying to figure out how to do things because there weren't better clues or instruction can feel a little annoying.

Despite it's flaws, The Dig is a worthwhile game that I think many people would enjoy playing.  I realize that for a positive review that recommends the game, there is a disproportionate amount of my review that addresses negative aspects, but that's why I say it's mid list, not top list.  It still makes the list of good Point & Click Adventure games.  If you've never played it and enjoy both P&Cs and SciFi it might be time to give it a try.  Without a guide, for a first time payer, it probably takes about 8-10 hours.  With a guide and/or previous playthrough, probably 4-6 depending on whether you skip cutscenes or dialogues.

O jogo da minha infância. Foi um dos primeiros jogos que joguei quando cheguei ao Brasil, e tenho ótimas lembranças de jogar na casa dos meus amigos. Mesmo depois de tantos anos, continua sendo um jogo incrível e, na minha opinião, superior em quase tudo à versão da DICE de 2017.

Pontos positivos:

✅ Trilha sonora épica: as músicas de Star Wars dão uma identidade única às batalhas e tornam a experiência ainda mais imersiva. As composições clássicas de John Williams são inesquecíveis e representam a identidade original da saga, da era de George Lucas, e não a versão da Disney.

✅ Gameplay e mecânicas: para a época, o jogo já oferecia muita variedade e mecânicas excelentes. Mesmo hoje, continua sendo extremamente divertido. Sinto falta de muitas dessas características na versão de 2017.

✅ Multiplayer: mesmo depois de tantos anos, ainda é possível encontrar partidas e aproveitar o modo multiplayer.

✅ Gráficos: os cenários, os soldados e os veículos têm um visual muito bonito e bem definido, que continua agradável até hoje.

✅ A verdadeira essência de Star Wars: não é a versão da DICE nem a da Disney. Para mim, este é o Battlefront II que preserva a essência clássica de Star Wars e entrega a experiência que tornou o jogo tão especial.

Pontos negativos:

❌ Multiplayer com muitos veteranos estrangeiros: atualmente, a maioria dos jogadores que encontro online parece ser estrangeira, fala inglês e tem muitos anos de experiência no jogo. Isso pode tornar as partidas difíceis para quem está começando, além de o ping elevado prejudicar a experiência. Infelizmente, é uma consequência de jogar um clássico tão antigo, mas, na época em que o jogo foi lançado, isso não era um problema.

❌ Gráficos datados: por ser um jogo de 2005, os gráficos naturalmente mostram a idade. Apesar de ainda achar o visual bonito, pode não agradar a todos, principalmente aos jogadores das novas gerações, que estão acostumados com jogos mais modernos.

Vale a pena comprar?

Sim, principalmente para quem já jogou esse clássico e quer reviver as lembranças, agora rodando o jogo no ultra e aproveitando os gráficos no máximo. Por R$ 32,99, acredito que vale a pena, mesmo sendo um jogo de 2005.

Sei que muita gente vai reclamar do preço por ser um jogo antigo e dizer que deveria ser mais barato ou até gratuito. Mas, na minha opinião, STAR WARS Battlefront II merece esse valor pela qualidade, pela gameplay e por tudo o que oferece. É um clássico que continua divertido até hoje e que vale cada centavo.

A propósito: já joguei as duas versões, a clássica de 2005 e a da DICE de 2017. Tenho o jogo de 2017 em duas contas diferentes, pois comprei o jogo para cada conta. Também continuo jogando a versão clássica de 2005 até hoje. São 21 anos jogando o mesmo jogo.

This is a nostalgic (if ultimately mediocre) game. But it is a TERRIBLE PORT.

The worst offender is by far the horrendous minigame input lag. Not everyone has this issue, but many people have posted about it, and no one has offered a single fix that actually works. Restarting the game does not help, or minimally at best. It affects both controller and mouse/keyboard. Not all minigames are affected, but several required for progression (or at least 100%) are. Trying to complete this game is an absolutely miserable task.

If you really want to buy this, then I'd recommend you complete the tutorial as fast as possible, then go try out a minigame like Vendor Tendor, buggy racing, or groundskeeper  cleanup. If you find the input lag makes it unplayable, then refund the game right away, because it only gets worse.

Then there's the constant crashing, and the fact that this game has no autosave. So every time it decides to crash randomly, you get to play "how much progress did I lose this time!" Hope you saved after spending an hour fighting with the horrible controls for a required minigame!

Then there's the other assorted issues, like mouse/keyboard controls being generally terrible even when you aren't dealing with input lag, loading screens being 30+ seconds on a 20-year-old game regardless of how good your computer is, or the game just refusing to play any more cutscenes halfway through and forcing you to go look them up on YouTube. But still making you wait 30 seconds whenever it tries and fails to load a cutscene.

[h1] Good Nostalgia, Mediocre Game [/h1]

Thrillville is a series of amusement park manager games where the sell is that "you play the games! you talk to park-goers! you can do it all!" and what that leads to is every aspect being shallow, easy, and or repetitive. Don't get me wrong, it's a fun little thing to play around with. I wish there were more games as accessible as this one. but it's not a theme park sim, it's not really a good minigame collection, it's doesn't have anything to hook or motivate you beyond "yeah i saw a trailer for this game on the lego star wars disc. might as well see what's up with it." It's good nostalgia if you ignore literally everything else about the title.

Park "management" is literally pressing buttons and letting things idle. as long as you don't actively go out of your way to make your park bad or piss off guests, you'll have constant money flowing in, no penalty, no major bonuses for doing certain things. Missions are just random fetch quests. go here. do this. say this. click this button. play this minigame. that's it.

Game has plenty of issues not attributed to the steam port being eh, including: 
- playing games without accessing them in missions will not give you anything for them. you are actively missing out on full game progression if you play games without searching for what to do in your missions tab first.
- walking is painfully slow. fast travel is only for your parks and not the "zones" in each park.
- plenty of minigames just have downright confusing or terrible controls (multiply this by 100 if you decide to play with keyboard and mouse)
-prizes mean nothing other than brownie points. this is concerning because one quest requires a "rare" item when nothing gives you distinction of what is rare. (luckily these are easy to obtain so this is a minor issue)

This game is all flash and marketing before anything substantive. And if you were hooked on that back then like i was, you'll be in for a solid 30 minutes of random messing around before you get bored (or 7 easy albiet boring hours if you wanna play the whole game.)

Otherwise, I don't recommend this title. but it's not bad if you get it on heavy sale. barely recommend.

This one will probably always be remembered as the game that effectively killed the franchise. It became the poster child for vaporware, spending well over a decade trapped in development hell while constantly being delayed, rebooted, and joked about across the gaming industry. Back in the '90s, though, I absolutely loved these games. I spent countless hours blasting aliens, finding ridiculous secrets, and laughing at Duke's over-the-top one-liners. Like a lot of fans, I eagerly waited for this game, convinced it would eventually live up to the hype.

Of course, I never imagined it would take that long to release. By the time it finally came out, I wasn't a kid anymore, and both gaming and I had changed quite a bit. Expectations had grown, shooters had evolved, and the humor that once felt edgy landed a little differently. It's easy to see why the game disappointed so many people after such an incredibly long wait.

That said, I've been working through my backlog lately and finally decided to give it a fair shot. Is it the best Duke Nukem game? Not even close. There are definitely rough edges, dated mechanics, and moments where you can almost see the scars from its troubled development. But despite all that, I still had fun. It felt like revisiting an old friend from my childhood. It is flawed, cheesy, and unapologetically over the top.

Duke himself remains the same wisecracking action hero who doesn't care what anyone thinks, constantly throwing out absurd one-liners while mowing down aliens in true old-school fashion. Sometimes it's nice to play a game that doesn't take itself seriously and just embraces being loud, ridiculous, and entertaining.

If you're expecting a masterpiece, you'll probably be disappointed. But if you're looking for a nostalgic, old-school FPS packed with explosions, alien blasting, cheesy humor, and a healthy dose of late-'90s attitude, it's still worth experiencing at least once.

Thrillville: Off the Rails is a vibrant and playful theme park management game that blends traditional simulation mechanics with arcade-style minigames and a light narrative framework. Developed by Frontier Developments and published by LucasArts, the game expands significantly on the ideas introduced in the original Thrillville, offering a more varied, energetic, and personality-driven experience. Rather than aiming for strict realism, it embraces spectacle, humor, and accessibility, making it a standout entry for players who enjoy creative freedom and constant variety over deep micromanagement.

At its core, the game places you in charge of building and managing a series of theme parks, each with its own theme, layout, and set of challenges. You’re responsible for placing rides, shops, decorations, and attractions in ways that maximize guest happiness and revenue, but the experience is far more hands-on than most management sims. You can walk freely through your park, talk to guests, respond to their requests, and even personally test rides, which gives the parks a lively, interactive feel. This approach keeps the focus on fun and engagement, ensuring that managing a park never feels like staring at spreadsheets or menus for too long.

One of the most defining features of Thrillville: Off the Rails is its roller coaster creation system, which encourages wild experimentation rather than realistic engineering. The game’s signature “WHOAH!” coasters allow tracks to leap gaps, launch cars through the air, and perform exaggerated stunts that would be impossible in real life. Designing these rides is intuitive and immediately satisfying, as you can instantly ride your creations and tweak them based on guest reactions. This emphasis on spectacle over realism fits perfectly with the game’s playful tone and makes coaster building accessible even to players with little experience in simulation games.

Minigames play an unusually large role in the overall structure and pacing. Scattered throughout the parks are dozens of optional and mission-critical minigames spanning a wide range of genres, including shooting galleries, racing challenges, puzzle games, and reflex-based tests. These minigames break up the management gameplay and give the experience a party-game energy, especially when played with friends in local multiplayer. Importantly, they’re not just distractions; completing them often directly benefits your park by boosting guest satisfaction, unlocking new content, or advancing the story, which helps integrate them naturally into the broader experience.

The game’s progression is guided by a lighthearted narrative that unfolds across multiple themed parks and regions. Rival park owner Vernon Garrison and his over-the-top Globo-Joy corporation provide a constant source of comic conflict, framing your objectives and giving the missions a sense of continuity. Missions range from straightforward construction goals to more creative challenges that require balancing guest moods, solving park-wide problems, or completing specific minigames. While the story is intentionally goofy and never takes itself seriously, it gives structure and motivation to what might otherwise feel like disconnected sandbox environments.

Visually, Thrillville: Off the Rails opts for a colorful, cartoon-inspired art style that prioritizes clarity and charm over technical realism. Guests are expressive, rides are vibrant, and each park theme has a distinct personality that makes it easy to tell them apart. Although the graphics are clearly from an earlier generation and may feel dated by modern standards, the art direction ensures that the game remains inviting and readable, even during busy moments when your park is packed with visitors.

In terms of depth, the management systems are intentionally streamlined. While you still need to think about ride placement, variety, pricing, and guest satisfaction, the game rarely punishes experimentation or mistakes too harshly. This makes it welcoming to casual players and younger audiences, though players seeking the complex economic simulations found in more hardcore theme park games may find it a bit light. That said, the sheer amount of content, missions, and unlockables provides plenty of long-term engagement, especially for completionists.

Ultimately, Thrillville: Off the Rails succeeds by knowing exactly what it wants to be. It is not a hyper-realistic park management simulator, but a joyful, chaotic celebration of theme park creativity, packed with minigames, outrageous roller coasters, and constant surprises. Its blend of management, direct interaction, and arcade-style fun gives it a unique identity that still holds up on Steam today. For players looking for a relaxed, imaginative, and endlessly entertaining take on the theme park genre, Thrillville: Off the Rails remains a charming and memorable ride.

O jogo foi feito em 2010 por uma engine interna que integrava ao adobe flash.
Provavelmente você vai zerar em 2 horas a campanha principal + 2 horas o modo coop.

O jogo foi um dos primeiros jogos da KLEI então eles estavam aprendendo muita coisa, então vai ser bem comum ver alguns erros de game design. 
Só que esses erros também eram comuns em muitos outros jogos + a engine tinha muitas limitações, principalmente ao que tange animação skeletal.

Em termos de combate + animação + combos funciona muito bem.
Ao que tange sensibilidade, cancelamento entre animações e precisões ficam a desejar, isso geralmente acontece em engines prematuras, lidar com essas coisas é muito chato e estressante e ficam para as fases finais de polimento.
Não é culpa deles, geralmente isso é chato pra um caralho fazer dentro de uma engine do 0, todavia impacta e muito na jogabilidade, principalmente para quem tá acostumado a jogar jogo moderno.

Por muitas vezes a decisão de game design de colocar muitos mobs + mira imprecisa + mobs no corner te atirando foi bastante insatisfatória, mas tudo bem pra idade do jogo. 

Foi bem legal jogar o jogo mesmo com esses poréms, se você estiver sem nada para fazer é um ótimo passatempo e quase como um abraço a uma época e estilo de jogo que não existe.
E de qualquer forma esse e o shank 2 foram base para lançarem seu novo jogo de 2026, então foi um aprendizado e tanto, e da para ver que eles colheram os feedbacks com carinho e endereçaram corretamente no novo jogo.

[h1][b]血浆与复仇的暴力美学[/b][/h1]

[h2][b]游戏总评：7.5/10[/b][/h2]
如果想找一部纯粹靠连招和血浆解压的横版清关游戏，《闪客》绝对是一部不会出错的经典老作品。刚上手这游戏的时候，那种浓郁的美式漫画风格和行云流水般的暴力美学直接就把我镇住了。你扮演一个背负血海深仇的硬汉，手里同时操着双枪、砍刀甚至电锯，在一群残暴的黑帮匪徒里杀进杀出。整个游玩过程就像是在看一部节奏极快的Cult动作片，那种拳拳到肉、刀刀见血的爽感非常原始且直接。

游戏的优点极其鲜明，打击感扎实到没话说。近战连击、枪械压制和投掷武器的无缝切换让战斗花样百出，你可以把敌人挑空然后用双枪在空中疯狂输出，操作上限很高，打起来赏心悦目。手绘的美术风格和复古的爵士摇滚配乐把整体的暗黑复仇氛围拉到了满格。

不过，缺点同样无法忽视。作为一款老游戏，它的判定机制有时候显得不够精细，尤其是在面对大批量敌人围攻时，闪避和防御的容错率低得让人头大。此外，关卡设计的重复度偏高，大部分时间都是在换汤不换药地清版推图，后期的视觉和玩法疲劳感来得比较快。

总而言之，《闪客》是一部个性十足的暴力动作小品。虽然系统和关卡在今天看来略显复古和单薄，但它带来的纯粹血腥爽感依然很顶。如果你喜欢硬派的街机风格战斗，抽空花个几小时爽一把绝对过瘾。

Shank — это невероятно бодрый, мясной и стильный 2D-эффектный слэшер, выполненный в духе брутальных комиксов и фильмов Квентина Тарантино или Роберта Родригеса (особенно напоминает «Мачете»).Сюжет (7/10): Классическая история мести. Главный герой по имени Шэнк идет по следам латиноамериканских мафиози, которые убили его возлюбленную и предали его самого. Сюжет прост, но подается через отличные кинематографичные вставки.Геймплей (9/10): Максимально динамичный. Вы можете на ходу комбинировать три вида оружия: парные ножи, тяжелое оружие (бензопила или мачете) и огнестрел (пистолеты, дробовики). Боевка ощущается сочно благодаря захватам, прыжкам на врагов и жестоким добиваниям.Визуал и звук (9/10): Рисованная анимация выглядит потрясающе даже спустя годы. Стиль напоминает анимацию Геннадия Тартаковского («Самурай Джек»). Музыкальное сопровождение в стиле спагетти-вестернов идеально дополняет атмосферу.Минусы: Игра довольно короткая (проходится за 3–4 часа), а управление на клавиатуре без геймпада может показаться неудобным.Итог: Превосходный «антистресс» на вечер. Первая часть ценится игроками даже выше сиквела за счет более мрачной и выдержанной атмосферы. Оценка: 8.5 из 10.

[h1]Rise for your Master[/h1]A rather peculiar game in which you control various ghosts to complete objectives across levels - from simply scaring all the people and freeing new ghosts along the way so they can be used in other levels, to more specific tasks. Technically, the game’s genre is strategy, but it feels more like a puzzle: to achieve your goals, you need to perform certain actions, sometimes in a specific order, and you don’t always succeed on the first try.

[h1]Un classico con non poche criticità ma che si fa amare[/h1]

✅❌ [b]Ghost Master[/b] è una vera e propria leggenda tra i rompicapo dei primi anni 2000. Il vero boom — almeno nel nostro Paese — avvenne sulle console di sesta generazione grazie al porting curato da Spiral House, intitolato [i]Ghost Master: Memorie da Gravenville[/i].

Il concetto alla base del gioco si spiega in meno di due minuti: nei panni di un "Master spiritico", il nostro compito è posizionare e gestire una squadra di fantasmi per spaventare gli abitanti della mappa e liberare altri spettri imprigionati. Ogni fantasma possiede caratteristiche uniche o condivise, può imparare nuovi trucchetti ed è, di norma, invisibile all'occhio umano. Una volta liberati, i nuovi spettri diventano subito utilizzabili nello stesso scenario o possono essere impiegati nei livelli precedenti per migliorare il proprio punteggio spavento. Ogni umano presenta fobie e resistenze specifiche che vanno studiate con cura, sia per scacciarlo sia per sfruttare le sue azioni a favore della liberazione degli altri fantasmi.

La versione qui proposta è quella originale PC del 2003: non c'è da stupirsi, quindi, se presenta qualche problema di avvio o fenomeni di stuttering sui sistemi moderni. Bisogna mettere in conto che, subito dopo l'acquisto, sarà necessario applicare patch amatoriali e regolare l'affinità dei core del processore dedicati al gioco. Paradossalmente, però, il vero limite del titolo non è tecnico, ma risiede nel gameplay stesso. Come anticipato, le azioni degli abitanti sono fondamentali per sbloccare determinati fantasmi: questo significa doversi spesso armare di pazienza e attendere che la routine di movimento (pattern) di uno specifico individuo giochi a nostro favore. In certi contesti non è persino possibile usare poteri di attrazione verso il punto desiderato, pena il game over. Il tutto si traduce in lunghe attese senza la possibilità di velocizzare il tempo, mentre l'Ectoplasma a nostra disposizione (la risorsa necessaria per schierare i fantasmi) continua a consumarsi. Un'altra nota dolente è il tutorial, decisamente poco esaustivo. Per chi si approccia al titolo per la prima volta è tutt'altro che semplice capire cosa fare o come farlo, complici le descrizioni dei poteri, spesso ambigue e poco intuitive. All'epoca si trattava di una scelta volutamente rigida da parte degli sviluppatori, pensata per costringere il giocatore a spremersi le meningi e ad affrontare lo stesso scenario più volte prima di padroneggiare le abilità degli spettri. Inoltre, non esiste una scheda descrittiva dello scenario o degli obiettivi di sblocco prima di fare ingresso nella mappa: nella fase di selezione della squadra ci si trova costretti quindi ad affidarsi al party consigliato dal gioco oppure ad andare per tentativi.

Al netto di queste criticità, Ghost Master si lascia giocare ancora oggi con grande piacere e offre un livello di sfida appagante, specialmente se ci si impone di non consultare guide o soluzioni online. Bisogna sempre contestualizzarlo al periodo in cui è uscito, un'epoca dominata dalla meccanica del trial and error, dove l'unica strada per vincere era incaponirsi e riprovare fino al successo.

В таком виде, как продаётся, игра неиграбельна. Поверх нужно установить Complete Edition, и запускать через её файл запуска.
Игра весьма интересная.
Игрок - крутой загробный маг, типа властелина часов из книги Кинга "Сияние". Только его нет в самой игре, ни в мире духов, ни в мире смертных, потому что это - ты, игрок за компьютером. А ещё, действие происходит во вселенной "Охотников за привидениями" - как бы обратная сторона реальности, что роднит игру со "Злым Гением", где отыгрыш - обратная сторона "Бондианы" и суперзлодейских книг и фильмов.
В распоряжении игрока-героя есть МНОГО (реально много) разнообразных призраков, как бывших людей, так и полтергейстов, овеществлённых страхов, мифических персонажей. Несмотря на кислый уровень графики, прорисованы все персонажи "с душой" - визуальный стиль интересный, каждый персонаж уникален.
Задачи - в основном, пугать и сводить с ума смертных, в духе игры на Сегу Генезис "Полтергейст", но есть и другие. Призраки и уровни имеют множество отсылок на мифологии, широкоизвестные книги, фильмы и более ранние видеоигры. В большой мере, можно утверждать, что сюжет собран по принципу "лоскутного одеяла".
Игра - смесь стратегии с непрямым управлением, даже скорее тактики с непрямым управлением, и головоломки. Вот те самые другие задачи, помимо "выгнать всех с уровня" - и есть головоломки.
Оперативной паузы нет, всё в реальном времени.
Оригинал очень плохо состарился, Complete Edition+HD patch его вытягивают на уровень запускаемости на современном железе и очень неплохой играбельности.
Есть явление "кладбище интересных механик": очень много всего задумано, но так сделано, что пользоваться всем имеющимся не особо удобно.
Непонятно, куда побежит смертный, множество механик влияния на веру, безумие и страх, и все работают по-разному - тоже роднит игру со "Злым Гением" в этом плане.
Нет магии трекинга пути смертных, либо магии закрытия дверей, у смертных на головах нет статусов, каждый грёбаный раз надо лазить в карточку смертного.
Призраков много, все прикольные, у всех разная магия, и такая штука, как одна и та же магия у разных призраков на разных уровнях цены. Например, у одного элементаля Землетрясение надо купить за 2000 золотой эктоплазмы (это ОЧЕНЬ дорого) и стоит 200 зелёной эктоплазмы (это midgame, надо ещё набрать столько!), а у другого оно сразу есть и стоит 70 (это со старта или почти со старта можно применять).
Даже имея prima strategy guide, весьма сложно совладать со всей этой магией. Но при этом, игре не хватает глубины "Злого гения-1" или любой части "Анно".
Игра подразумевает переигрывание каждого уровня раза по 4.
Из хорошего: игра держит внимание. Отыгрыш каждого уровня интересен. Загадки на освобождение прикованных сущностей (которые приходят в команду игрока) ОЧЕНЬ интересны. Вскрытие страхов смертных для отыгрыша тоже интересно. Противостояние с ведьмами, медиумами и охотниками за привидениями весьма весело, но тоже утомительно иногда из-за кладбища механик и непрописанных иммунитетов (например, Гипнос может до усрачки колдовать на врагов (враги=изгонятели) - им никакие счётчики не прибавляются, и спать они не хотят.)
Вот Complete Edition, ставится на гог либо стим версию, но на гог хотя бы работает. Запускать потом надо через exe из папки GhostData, а не основной.

Even from a retrospective point of view, [i]Ghost Master®[/i] was nothing more than a standard, bargain-basement video game, where creativity is heavily discouraged in favor of linear gameplay. All levels have a "recommended" button where specific ghosts are automatically added to the player's roster to fit the interactable objects in them. This does not sound too terrible until it is realized that certain levels have puzzles that require specific skills from certain ghosts, meaning that levels can become softlocked or completely uninteractable. 

Any outcome wherein players are punished, directly or indirectly, for their creativity or want of roster freedom is an immediate turn-off for most individuals, especially in a game where ghosts [b]can[/b] be unlocked and upgraded. It does not matter what combinations one may come up with, if a certain power is not available to any one of your ghosts, such as “quake” to knock a brick out of the wall hiding a corpse or “telekinetic storm” or disrupt certain electronic device, then one can expect to fail mission objectives completely and have no means of unlocking ghosts tied to an objective. Players naturally enjoy having options and utilizing them appropriately, but this game provides little to no windows of opportunity for experimenting with roster combinations with the possibility of winning in the end.

There are no options, at the very least, evaluating the level, its props, and its NPCs to understand what the player can expect when it comes to what can be exploited in terms of the phobias some NPCs have, along with interacting with objects. Even when players accept the recommended roster of ghosts, the game remains trial-and-error, all the while their score is tied to how quickly they can complete the level. All of this while the player has to bind and unbind ghosts to rooms like clockwork if they are to keep the pressure on NPCs that constantly scatter like ants and ghosts that have to [b]charge up[/b] their scares before they can execute them.

For $5, players are given pint-sized level variety, no breathing room for having ghost rosters that differ from what the developers wanted, and little reward even when they kowtow to recommendations by the game. It is no wonder that only two levels are present in the game’s screenshots on the store; you would have to lose your mind to think that this game is deserving of an hour of your time, let alone a five-dollar bill.

Спустя 23 года наконец-то допрошёл её. По сути это идейное продолжение игры с сеги Haunting Starring Polterguy от тех же ребят. У неё, кстати, классный трагичный бэкграунд про некачественные скейтборды и злого босса из ЕА, погугите. Крутой концепт, визуал, музыка, анимации. Выглядит и ощущается топ даже сегодня. Под пивас самое то. 

Но играется так себе. Половить фан от кинца круто, но тактической глубины никакой. Задачи делятся на два типа. Первый: напугай всех. Вы будете просто прикреплять призраков и перебирать их способности. Тут типа есть намёки на планирование: раскрыть страхи болванчика, приманить всех в одну комнату, но всё это рудиментарно. Будет скучно и рутинно, если пытаться играть, а не режиссёра отыгрывать. Второй - это квесты, которые скорее всего вы будете играть по гайдам, постоянно альтабясь. Они подразумевают, чтобы вы запустили уровень, поняли что к чему, вышли, выбрали новых призраков, купили им новые способности, и попробовали ещё раз. И то не всегда понятно, что от вас хотят. Тут, например, есть момент, когда нужно просто ждать, активировав нескольких призраков, и без прохождения я бы не понял, что всё делаю правильно. Но это только звучит так душно, на самом деле телепатических моментов здесь всего два, остальное решается перезапуском миссии с новыми призраками и перебором способностей. Современному игроку это может показаться скучным и унылым: либо перепроходи, либо с прохождением сиди, но что поделать. Но такие моменты можно простить, потому что игра уникальна и второй такой нет. 

Технических проблем не испытал. Запустилось с первой попытки и никакие патчи не понадобились. 

С русификатором есть нюансы. В руководствах стима есть только одно прохождение на русском, и оно заканчивается на втором акте. С английскими руководствами у вас будут проблемы с именами персонажей. Беды нет, потому что вне стима на старых сайтах можно найти несколько прохождений, написанных по русской версии.

Если вы старый дед, который в молодости думал, что диск на полке от акеллы: Ghost Master Смертельный Испуг - это какой-то аддон, то можете успокоиться. Здесь лежит она. По сути это один дополнительный уровень после титров. Видимо разрабы поняли, что сиквела не будет, поэтому решили историю так закончить. 

Было бы таких игр много, я бы не рекомендовал. Но такого опыта вы больше нигде не получите, так что ознакомиться всё же стоит. Главное играйте в неё как в кинцо, а не как в тактику. И морально готовьтесь к перепрохождению, если хотите получить полноценный опыт. Не хотите - читайте гайды.
