В Департаменте Загробного Мира, как обычно, было шумно. Бесконечные очереди недавно упокоенных перешептывались, ожидая приема в окошке социальной помощи, чтобы получить талон на Поезд Душ и наконец отправиться в Великое Запределье. Клерки скрипели ручками, заполняя бесконечные бланки опросов и тестов. Кто-то яростно спорил с дежурным, заверяя, что "[i]еще не умер[/i]" и вообще - “[i]произошла чудовищная ошибка![/i]”. Громоздкая дама в истлевшей синей форме регулировщика, окруженная зеленым свечением, громко шваркала чаем. Она методично указывала на табличку "ОБЕД" высокому, под два метра ростом парню в черном смокинге, который замер перед ней, словно оживший манекен.

Я быстро прошел сквозь зал ожидания, стараясь не встречаться взглядом с другими неупокоенными, крепче прижимая к боку папку с документами. Но делал я это не из страха. За годы работы в Департаменте я свыкся с обликом прибывающих и тем, насколько потерянными они чувствуют себя первые пятьдесят-семьдесят лет пребывания в Зале Ожидания. Именно эта "потерянность" и мешала перемещаться: каждый норовил ухватить тебя за рукав и начать исповедь, уверяя, что его нахождение здесь - нелепая случайность.

Случайность, как же. Когда-то и я думал так же, но посмотрите на меня теперь. Почти 423 года я работаю социальным работником, помогая душам уйти в Запределье, в то время как сам остаюсь здесь в вечном ожидании собственного билета.

Войдя в 125-ю аудиторию, я бросил папку на стол, выдохнул и повернулся к собравшимся. Их было всего несколько сущностей - язык не поворачивался назвать их "людьми", особенно учитывая, что сюда частенько попадают и существа иного порядка.

Присутствующие обратили лица в мою сторону и медленно потянулись к стульям. Некоторые, впрочем, так и остались висеть в воздухе ввиду отсутствия привычных ног.

- [i]Что ж, вижу, сегодня Вас еще меньше, чем на прошлой встрече,[/i] - я мысленно пересчитал головы. - [i]Я бы сказал, в разы меньше. И искренне надеюсь, что отсутствующие просто опаздывают. В противном случае мне придется дополнить их характеристики, что лишь усугубит их положение в Потустороннем мире и еще сильнее отодвинет от заветного билета.[/i]

По залу пролетел шепот: присутствующие принялись гадать, куда подевались остальные. Я подождал минуту, затем хлопнул ладонью по папке.

Паук примостился в углу, плетя паутину, чтобы комфортно разлечься, но все же отвлекся от дела, внимая моим словам.

Призрак попытался скрыться от моего взора, буквально просочившись сквозь стол. Однако через секунду из столешницы показалась призрачная рука, и я услышал тихое возражение, граничившее с дуновением ветра:

- [i]Но я не виноват, что мне достался дом престарелых... Они плохо видят, да и вечером не было персонала... [/i]- начал оправдываться Бу.

Я мягко прервал его: - [i]Согласен. Но тем не менее, перед Вами были люди со слабыми сердцами. Я вздохнул, всем видом демонстрируя разочарование. Хотел было продолжить разбор промахов, но взгляд зацепился за часы над входом. Времени на нравоучения не оставалось - нужно было проводить урок. A hauntingly entertaining experience that will have you both parts equally [b] enamored [/b] as you are every bit [b] infuriated [/b] !

Ghost Master is an incredibly unique one... 1 part "The Sims", 1 part "Tecmo's Deception", and a pinch of "Scooby Doo" for added comedy. And what you end up with is a fascinatingly unique strategy-puzzle-simulator-[b]thing[/b] , and its awesome! You skulk and stalk your victims, as you strategize and execute the best plan of attack through 15 spooky themed levels, mostly all based off famous movies & troupes from the past. All the while building your legion of the lemures larger and larger, as you help free them by solving [b]sometimes[/b] clever and [b]sometimes[/b] frustrating puzzles.  And this is where Ghost Master's largest caveat lies. For every bit as clever, unique, and admittedly fun GM gets with its level design and puzzles, they also try to get a little too cute with the whole ordeal. And border on near obtuse solutions that require a great deal of patience and luck to succeed, [b]ESPECIALLY[/b] the later half.

However, for every moment I wanted to smash my face through the monitor because an NPC didn't want to play along with a step in my grand scheme, I would be lying if I said I didn't enjoy a lot of my time along the way, frustration and all. It finds that sweet spot between "wanting to give up entirely...but...after this ONE last try!", and I'm all here for it.

If the idea of a haunted house themed, strategy-puzzle based, "The Sims", sounds appealing to you at all. And you aren't afraid to get stuck do to, quite honestly, annoying RNG in the late half of this game. Then I think Ghost Master is actually a hidden classic in the vast sea of Steams storefront, especially for 5 bucks! 

Just heed one thing, this game is in fact [b]old[/b] and it does tend to have issues running on newer hardware, like aspect ratio issues and some annoying npc bugs. Nothing unbeatable or unsolveable, but it may require you to fix a thing or two beforehand. So just keep that in mind.

Jsi připraven? Odvaž se a sestup do podsvětí, protože Ghost Master je hra, která tě vtáhne do strašidelné říše a už tě nepustí!

Co je Ghost Master?

Ghost Master je unikátní strategická hra, kde nehraješ za hrdinu, co honí duchy, ale naopak! Jsi nový „mistr“ duchů a tvým úkolem je ovládat partu spektrálních bytostí, aby strašily lidi a vyhnaly je z domů, které obývají. Každý duch má své speciální schopnosti a je jen na tobě, jak je zkombinuješ, aby jsi vytvořil tu nejděsivější show.

Hratelnost

Hra je rozdělena do misí, kde na tebe čeká nový dům nebo lokace k vystrašení. Ze začátku máš jen pár duchů, ale postupem času se odemykají nové a nové bytosti s širším arzenálem schopností. Můžeš tak rozpoutat peklo na zemi – od jednoduchého rozsvěcení světel až po seslání tornáda, které ti ve vteřině obrátí celý dům naruby!

Každý obyvatel má svou vlastní úroveň strachu a slabiny. Musíš proto pečlivě plánovat, jakého ducha na koho použiješ, abys dosáhl kýženého efektu. Ghost Master klade velký důraz na strategii a kreativitu. Musíš přemýšlet jako opravdový mistr zla a promyslet každý svůj tah. Budeš schopen nahnat obyvatelům strach dřív, než na tebe zavolají vymítače?

Grafika a zvuky

Ghost Master možná není nejnovější hra, ale má své kouzlo. Grafika je barevná, stylová a skvěle podtrhuje atmosféru. Zvuk je kapitola sama o sobě. Každé zjevení, každý skřípot dveří nebo zvuk řetězů tě donutí se usmát a užívat si každý moment hrůzy.

Resumé

Ghost Master je poctivá a originální hra, která nabízí osvěžující pohled na strašení a nadpřirozeno. Pokud máš rád strategické hry a neotřelé nápady, je to titul přesně pro tebe. Připrav se na spoustu zábavy a hromadu dábelsky dobré zábavy!

A co ty? Troufneš si vstoupit do stínů a stát se mistrem duchů?

Ghost Master, developed by Sick Puppies and published by Strategy First, is a unique blend of strategy, simulation, and supernatural horror that has carved out a distinct niche since its original release. The game invites players to assume the role of the titular Ghost Master—an unseen orchestrator controlling a squad of ghosts with the goal of terrifying and driving out the living from various haunted locations. While its concept might sound straightforward, Ghost Master combines tactical gameplay with dark humor and atmospheric storytelling, delivering an experience that feels fresh and inventive even years after its debut.

At its core, Ghost Master is a strategy game wrapped in a horror-themed package. Unlike traditional horror games where you play as the victim, here you wield supernatural powers and manage a team of spirits, each with unique abilities and personalities. You must carefully select which ghosts to deploy, balancing their strengths and weaknesses to maximize fear and efficiently clear out human occupants. The game encourages creativity in haunting strategies, mixing stealth, psychological manipulation, and direct supernatural assaults. The AI-controlled humans react dynamically to your tactics, making every haunting a puzzle that requires both planning and adaptability.

The environments in Ghost Master are richly detailed, atmospheric locations that range from old mansions and asylums to graveyards and crypts. Each setting is designed with haunting in mind, offering multiple hiding spots, interactable objects, and environmental elements to exploit for maximum effect. The eerie sound design and moody visuals effectively build tension without relying on jump scares, allowing dread to seep in gradually. What sets the game apart is its tone—while it is a horror game, it leans into campy, tongue-in-cheek humor that often undercuts the tension with clever ghostly quips and absurd scenarios, creating a uniquely engaging atmosphere.

One of the most compelling aspects of Ghost Master is the variety of ghosts you command. Each ghost comes with its own set of abilities, strengths, and quirks—from poltergeists who can hurl objects to spectral children whose innocent appearance hides a terrifying presence. Managing your roster involves strategic choices about which ghosts complement each other and how to deploy them effectively against different human targets with varied fears and personalities. As you progress, you unlock new spirits and powers, adding depth and complexity to your haunting tactics.

While the game’s mechanics are innovative, Ghost Master can be challenging due to its sometimes opaque interface and steep learning curve. Mastering the nuances of ghost abilities and human psychology requires patience and experimentation. Additionally, the game’s older graphics and somewhat clunky controls may feel dated to modern players. However, these limitations are largely overshadowed by the creativity and originality embedded in the core gameplay. For those willing to invest the time, the satisfaction of successfully orchestrating a haunting and watching terrified humans flee is genuinely rewarding.

Narratively, Ghost Master is woven together with darkly humorous cutscenes and mission briefings that provide context and flavor to your supernatural endeavors. Rather than a linear story, the game offers episodic missions where your role as the Ghost Master evolves. The writing cleverly blends horror tropes with comedic elements, making the experience entertaining without losing its spooky edge. This balance allows the game to appeal to both horror enthusiasts and strategy fans who appreciate a lighter tone.

In conclusion, Ghost Master stands out as an inventive and entertaining hybrid of strategy and horror. Its distinctive premise of controlling ghosts to scare humans, combined with tactical depth, atmospheric environments, and a playful sense of humor, make it a memorable title that still holds up for those seeking something different from traditional horror or strategy games. Though it shows its age in presentation and interface, the core gameplay loop remains engaging and original. For players interested in a game where you get to be the haunting force, rather than the hunted, Ghost Master offers a uniquely satisfying experience that’s worth revisiting or discovering anew.

Vegas: Make It Big is an ambitious casino management simulation that tries to replicate the complexity of building and running a Las Vegas resort, but it does so with a level of detail that can be both impressive and overwhelming. Developed by Deep Red, the game gives players control over every aspect of their casino empire, from laying out gaming floors and hotel rooms to managing staff, pricing, and customer satisfaction. Rather than simplifying systems for accessibility, it leans heavily into simulation depth, creating an experience that feels closer to a business management sandbox than a traditional tycoon game.

At its core, the gameplay revolves around designing a profitable resort while catering to a wide range of guests, each with their own behaviors, expectations, and spending habits. Players must carefully place slot machines, table games, bars, restaurants, and entertainment venues in ways that maximize foot traffic and revenue. There is a strong emphasis on understanding how different elements interact—noise levels, crowd flow, proximity of services, and even the type of clientele you attract all play a role in determining success. This layered approach gives the game a surprising amount of strategic depth, rewarding players who take the time to experiment and refine their layouts.

However, this same complexity quickly becomes one of the game’s biggest hurdles. The interface is dense and often unintuitive, making even basic tasks feel more complicated than they need to be. Important information is buried within menus, and the game does little to guide players through its more intricate systems. As a result, much of the learning process comes from trial and error, which can be frustrating, especially in the early stages. Instead of easing players into its mechanics, the game expects a level of patience and persistence that may not appeal to everyone.

Micromanagement is a constant presence throughout the experience. Nearly every aspect of the resort requires direct attention, from hiring and assigning staff to maintaining facilities and adjusting pricing strategies. While this level of control can be satisfying for players who enjoy fine-tuning every detail, it also creates a sense of relentless oversight. As the resort grows, the workload increases significantly, and without strong automation systems in place, players can find themselves spending more time managing small issues than making meaningful strategic decisions. This can make the game feel more like a continuous balancing act than a rewarding progression.

Despite these challenges, there is a compelling simulation underneath the surface. When systems are working in harmony, the game captures the chaotic energy of a busy casino remarkably well. Watching crowds move through your carefully designed floors, seeing profits rise as your strategies pay off, and gradually expanding your resort into a sprawling complex all contribute to a satisfying sense of accomplishment. The game’s attention to detail, particularly in how different systems influence one another, gives it a depth that many simpler management games lack.

Visually, Vegas: Make It Big reflects the era in which it was released. The fully 3D environment was a notable feature at the time, allowing players to zoom in and observe their resort from different perspectives. Today, however, the graphics feel dated, with low-detail models and textures that lack modern polish. Animations are basic, and while the overall presentation is functional, it does little to immerse players beyond conveying the layout of the resort. Technical issues can also arise, particularly on newer systems, which may affect performance or stability.

The audio design is serviceable but not particularly memorable. Background sounds help establish the atmosphere of a bustling casino, but they are repetitive and lack variety. Music tracks fit the theme but do little to enhance the experience in a meaningful way. Over time, the audio fades into the background, neither adding nor detracting significantly from the gameplay.

Replayability depends largely on the player’s tolerance for the game’s complexity. The freedom to design different types of resorts and experiment with various strategies offers some incentive to return, but the demanding nature of the systems can make each playthrough feel like a substantial commitment. For players who enjoy deep, intricate simulations, this can be a major draw, while others may find it difficult to revisit after an initial experience.

In the end, Vegas: Make It Big stands as a deeply detailed but uneven management simulation. It succeeds in offering a rich and interconnected set of systems that reward careful planning and experimentation, but it struggles with accessibility, interface design, and an overreliance on micromanagement. For a niche audience that appreciates complex tycoon games and is willing to invest the time to master its mechanics, it can be a rewarding experience. For most players, however, its rough edges and steep learning curve may prove to be significant barriers.

And let me tell you the visuals in this game hit the eye like a fireworks display! (incidentally you can get fireworks for your casinos.) The casinos, hotels, arenas and decorations that come with your chosen theme are hugely thematic and extravagant with lights, neon, animatronics and the shear level of imagination make it a feast for the eyes. I suspect this game is more imaginative and extravagant then the real Vegas!

The game is much more then ploping down buildings. The casinos have the option to go inside and customise the layout, which you can do with strategy and imagination. Recently I played with the America theme and found myself using the carpeting tool to make the whole room into a giant U.S. flag.
You can place gaming tables to your discretion, customise the betting range and house edge, you can save layouts to use later or load pre-made ones.

There is strategy in placement. Certain buildings and gambling games attract different kinds of patrons, you can target groups and create an ideal venue for them or make a place with something for everyone and broaden your appeal.
Some buildings, inside and out of your casinos, have a negative aura that will drive away guests. You need to either plan ahead and put them out of the way and or use decorations with positive auras to counter them.

Speaking of which, I used to find this game very difficult until I realized the way to solve the problem of negative auras was positive auras. After that it lost a lot of it's challenge. 
there is no difficulty setting, the closest thing is a few sliders in the sandbox mode for things like starting money, frequency of events and max population of guests. Once you've built a decent casino money starts FLOODING in weather patrons win or lose. Which makes everything else a breeze but is not unlike real life casinos. : )

So is it worth it? Put it this way... recently Sim Casino, a much more modern, complex and customizable game went on sale but I turned it down. Sim Casino's graphics make it look far better but Vega$: make it big makes it look boring!

Good:
- Performance. The game works really great on the laptop with 3k res. UI scaled perfectly, no issues at all
- Variation of the game modes
- Graphics
- Good memories from childhood

Bad:
- The game design. WHO decided to put replay logic at the end of the EVERY RACE? Do you know at least 1 person who will watch his own race over and over again at the end of the race?
- No "restart" button on the bonus lvl. If 1 of 3 attempts is bad, you want to immediately restart the level. The problem is: **you can't**. You need to make ~5 steps to restart it instead of 1. Poor design guys...
- Bots literally working outside of game design. Their logic is predictable tho it's really hard to play against them because of the following perfect trajectory all the time. The only option is to crash them against some environment. Ex.: when you try to crash the enemy, he will go back on the track without hesitation
- This game has nothing to do with your skill. If you're good player the game will not give you satisfaction of winning. There is no enjoy to play, pure luck is the key. The better league you play, the more "restart" button will be pressed. Ex.: You can win and get the "enjoy" of winning without nerves only if the bots crash themselves. This way your mistake will not count as critical and you can continue play without restarting it
- Tuning mechanic is broken (THE BIGGEST PART OF THE RACE GAME). No point spending money on upgrades if there are **ALWAYS** bots who drive faster than you (despite you've won all the races). Ex.: you've bought compressor, your hp bar raised up above your ego still bots faster than you
- Reward for destroying environment is poor. There is a lot of stuff to destroy, a lot to dodge but you are not awarded for it. Like 1-2$ (i'm not sure about it, maybe it cost nothing) for cone when upgrade costs 1k$+
- Bonus games. You need to complete the league to open new one but the problem is that your fully upgraded car of your league (if it is not the last one) still can't make you win the 1-2 place. Power is just not enough so what the point of opening new bonuses through the career mode if you can win only in the endgame? More correct approach is to open everything at the start
- Achievements. It's really frustrating to complete the game 100% and still not get the 100% achievement. The game statistics says 100% so you have logic to define it. Why not just reuse it for steam achievements?

Конечно же, налёт ностальгии неизгладим, но если постараться быть объективным, то:

1. [b]Достойная физика авто[/b]. Видно, что было потрачено не мало сил на её калибровку, чтобы приблизить к реальной реальности и даже, извинитесь, "симуляторности".

2. [b]Великолепная графика[/b]. Не только для тех лет, она и сейчас смотрится неплохо: сочная и яркая картинка, детализация авто, мелкие частицы, разлетающиеся от столкновений, и вишенкой на торте - полная поддержка 4К (напоминаю, игре 22 года)! На её фоне не менее легендарная NFS Underground - мыло мыльное, а она вышла всего на год раньше. 

3. [b]Разрушаемость авто и окружения[/b]. Одни эмоции от того, насколько это круто ощущалось что сейчас, что тогда! До появления Burnout Paradise, разумеется :) Честно говоря, именно в первой Flatout эта фича выглядит немного инородно и скорее воспринимается, как приятный "бонус" за наглость или, наоборот, непредусмотрительность на дороге, и не особо поощряется игрой.

4. [b]Уровень сложности "Профи" - в топку[/b]. Испортит весь опыт (привет, @RYTSAR), а из эмоций подарит только ощущение нечестности происходящего. Вместо интересных заездов с вполне себе достойным для тех лет ИИ вы получите биение в стенку головой и лютую дрочь: по сути неадекватные характеристики противников при том, что ваши остаются на базовом уровне.

5. [b]Челлендж и трассы[/b]. Даже в стандартной сложности Flatout бросает игроку вызовы. Цель противников - не развалить вам кабину, несмотря ни на что, а добраться до финиша первыми, из-за чего они редко ошибаются, вынуждая и вас действовать с холодной головой на каждом повороте. Даже держа лидерство, вам приходится ехать как можно более идеально, так как вы знаете, что любая ошибка приведёт к потере места в гонке - но не потому, что кто-то невидимой рукой тянет врагов за вами, а потому что они тоже "хотят победить" и только и ждут вашей ошибки. Цель трасс - дать игроку почувствовать машину, её сцепление с разными поверхностями, но не нестись, сломя голову, а аккуратно входить в заносы, притормаживать перед поворотами настолько, насколько позволяет поверхность, где-то во время заноса легонечко бортануть соперника, отправляя его за трассу, при этом самому не сильно потеряв в скорости, и т.д.

6. [b]Каскадёрские трюки[/b]. Вылеты через лобовуху - абсолютно уникальная механика серии. И разрабам было мало того, что это происходит в обычных заездах, так ещё и какой-то безумец из команды (спасибо ему) сделал целый отдельный режим, в котором нужно метать водителя в цели и получать за это очки. Сильно разбавляет градус обычных заездов и привносит щепотку веселья в игру.

7. [b]Музыка - дефолтно-роковая, альтернативная[/b]. Без каких-то откровений или мурашек по коже, в целом соответствует достаточно размеренному темпу игры.

8. [b]Экономика в игре - отсутствует[/b]. При покупке одна тачка навсегда пропадает, вместо неё с небольшой скидкой появляется другая. Лажа.

9. [b]Контента и разнообразия - немного[/b]. Что карт, что автомобилей. Тут разработчики пошли по принципиально другому пути завлечения игрока, об этом сразу дальше и закончим :)

Первый Flatout - наследник школы "хардкорности" игр прошлого, которые держали игрока у экрана не разнообразным контентом, а постоянной борьбой с условиями вокруг и ростом над собой, заставляя раз за разом становиться лучше до тех пор, пока цель не будет достигнута. И эта мысль касается как обычного прохождения карьеры, так и трюковых метаний болванчика в мишень.

FlatOut: Симулятор того, як знищити власну колимагу і запустити водія крізь лобове скло
Оцінка: 10 із 10 вщент розбитих бамперів і водіїв, що летять через усі Billboard-щити на трасі.

Якщо ви хоч раз грали в якісь стерильні гоночки, де за кожну подряпину на кузові розробники кажуть «ай-я-яй», то FlatOut — це вам не якийсь там симулятор. Це чистий, непідробний руйнівний екстаз із нульовими правилами дорожнього руху. Тут перемагає не той, хто їде швидше за всіх, а той, хто встигає влетіти у ворогів на повній швидкості і залишитися хоч із якимись колесами.

Головні закони та секрети виживання брутального водія:
Фізика руйнування (краще за будь-який тюнінг).
Твоя машина тут — це просто тимчасова збірка деталей. Будь-яке лобове зіткнення з деревом чи суперником перетворює твій спортивний болід на акуратний кубик металу. Двері відлітають, капот зриває з петель, колеса вигинаються під дикими кутами... але машина чомусь їде! І це прекрасно.

Аварії як стиль життя.
Тут не можна просто акуратно обійти суперника на повороті. Ти зобов'язаний вибити його у кювет, загнати в стовп або просто врізатися в стіну так, щоб двигун вилетів уперед метрів на десять.

Легендарне «Викидання водія» (Stunt Mode).
Вишенька на торті будь-якої частини FlatOut — це мініігри, де водій стає живим снарядом. Ви розганяєте тачку до сутінкової швидкості, тиснете на гальмо... і ваш віртуальний пілот із криком вилітає крізь лобове скло, лечачи через усе поле, щоб влучити у величезну мішень для дартсу, збити кеглі для боулінгу чи перелетіти через планку для стрибків у висоту. Зі спортивної етики тут тільки чорний гумор!

Траси-пастки.
Карти тут спроєктовані так, щоб ви постійно кудись врізалися. Шпали, трактори, брудні калюжі, неогороджені прірви та величезні купи покришок чекають на вас за кожним поворотом.

Піковий ігровий момент:
Останнє коло. Ви йдете першими, до фінішу кілька метрів. Серце калатає. Раптом з кута вилітає божевільний суперник і на повній швидкості б'є вас у бік. Ваша машина робить п'ять сальто в повітрі, врізається в рекламний щит, водій вилітає через дах... і перетинає фінішну лінію живою головою чи шматком тіла на солідному плюсі, приносячи вам перше місце. Комп'ютер у шоці, ви смієтеся на весь голос.

Вердикт:
FlatOut — це вічна класика аркадних перегонів, яка й досі дарує більше ефектних емоцій, ніж більшість сучасних ігор із бюджетами в мільярди. Вона брудна, гучна, неймовірно смішна і жорстока до вашої техніки.

Купувати (чи встановлювати)? Обов'язково! Особливо якщо хочете згадати золоту епоху ігрової безтурботності та влаштувати з друзями чемпіонат із польотів водіїв крізь лобове скло.

[h2]Купил FlatOut 1, чтобы узнать, из чего родилась легендарная вторая часть, и быстро забрать 100% ачивок (ушло 6.2 часа). Истоки я понял, но етить это душная тема.[/h2]

[i][b]Важное примечание:[/b] В игре на удивление присутствует выбор уровня сложности. Сложности всего две, и когда игра предложила выбор, я взял ту, что посложнее. На что именно это влияет — игра умалчивает. Но весь мой дальнейший опыт родился на основе этой самой сложности «посложнее». Как дела обстоят на уровне попроще — без понятия.[/i]

Главные фичи игры — физика, разрушаемость и покатушки — полностью ломаются о геймплей и баланс.

[b]Парадокс геймплея:[/b] Игра создана ради красивых аварий, но авария на первом же повороте — это гарантированный рестарт. Несмотря на то, что впереди еще 4 круга. Ошибаться нельзя вообще. Врезался или вылетел — первого места не будет. Ты либо едешь уныло и идеально, либо ретраишь гонку по 20 раз. Какой в этом смысл?

[b]Токсичные боты:[/b] Местные противники весят под 40 тонн и едут как по рельсам. Сдвинуть их нереально, зато они считают своим долгом развернуть твою 1.5-тонную машину в ближайший столб и уехать в закат. А на первом слоте с шансом 30% сидит местный Макс Ферстаппен, который уносится за горизонт без единой ошибки.

[b]Физика грязи:[/b] 90% трасс — не асфальт. Сцепления ноль. На кой хер тут 400 лошадиных сил на заднем приводе, если на скорости выше 60 миль в час тебя сносит в канаву? А обочина обладает свойствами льда под летними кроссовками — выехать обратно физически невозможно. Все «гонки» проходят на скорости 40–70 миль в час. Не успев оттормозиться до тех самых 40–50 миль,  гарантированно улетишь за пределы трассы. А трассы, к слову, на 95% состоят из поворотов.

[b]Срезки-рулетка:[/b] Понять, где тут адекватный срез, а где путь в соседнее село на дискотеку — нереально. Можно получить метку «вылет с трассы» и смотреть, как «удачно» срезав маршрут, ты перемещаешься с 1 места на 8-ое, формально всё еще возглавляя гонку. Плюс можно поймать кривой хитбокс трассы даже не "срезая", получить метку «вылет с трассы» и при нажатии кнопки R телепортироваться на чекпоинт на круг назад. Потрясающе.

[b]Дисбаланс трасс:[/b] Да, есть локации (например, все зимние), где приехать первым вообще не составит труда, а противники отстанут чуть ли не на круг. Есть трассы, где челлендж вполне адекватный. Но добрые 50% гонок — это именно та лютая дрочь, что описана выше.

[b]Возраст игры:[/b] Добавим и то, что игра уже, откровенно говоря, старая. Если чувства ностальгии вам не знакомы, то делать тут абсолютно нечего.

[b]Итог:[/b] Ожидал долбежки от трюков, а в итоге сам кор-геймплей отправил мою задницу на околоземную орбиту. Спасибо игре за то, что она подарила нам великий сиквел, и за хороший саундтрек. Но играть в это сегодня — сомнительное удовольствие.

Лучше сразу запускайте вторую часть и не делайте себе нервы.

Осторожно: этот отзыв может вызвать фантомные боли в позвоночнике и непреодолимое желание вылететь через лобовое стекло под бодрый альтернативный рок.
Когда я впервые запустил эту игру, у меня ещё не было водительских прав, но я уже точно знал, как правильно уничтожать подвеску и заставлять пассажира страдать. FlatOut в Steam — это игра из тех славных времен, когда словосочетание «симулятор автокатастроф» означало не унылое ковыряние в настройках, а весёлое безумие под гитарные запилы.
За что я оставил в этой игре свои нервные клетки и молодость:
• Водитель-катапульта: Главная фича игры — это, конечно, физика Ragdoll. Мужик в синем комбинезоне, вылетающий через лобовое стекло при любом удобном случае, стал мне роднее соседа. А мини-игры? Дартс, прыжки в высоту, боулинг — и всё это живым (или не очень) водителем! Олимпиада, которую мы заслужили.
• Разрушаемость всего и вся: В то время как в других гонках ты врезался в картонный деревянный забор и останавливался как вкопанный, здесь ты разносил этот забор в щепки, попутно прихватив с собой сарай, пару покрышек и капот соперника. К финишу твоё корыто доезжало без дверей, бамперов и, кажется, без здравого смысла.
• Тот самый саундтрек: Стоит только услышать первые аккорды из главного меню, как в организме начинает вырабатываться адреналин. Под эту музыку хотелось не просто побеждать, а крушить, ломать и идти на таран. Современным гоночным плейлистам до этого драйва как до Луны.
Да, искусственный интеллект соперников здесь не знает жалости — они будут вжимать тебя в стену, даже если вы боретесь за предпоследнее место. Графика по нынешним меркам уже простовата, но физика поведения машин до сих пор уделывает многие современные гонки.

FlatOut — это культовая аркадная гонка от финской студии Bugbear Entertainment, которая запомнилась не столько реалистичной симуляцией, сколько безудержным драйвом и разрушением. Если хочется не «красиво проехать круг», а устроить на трассе настоящий хаос — эта игра идеально подходит.

Что особенно цепляет
Физика разрушений. Машины реально «ломаются»: отваливаются колёса, кузов мнётся, каждое столкновение заметно влияет на управляемость. Это не просто визуальные эффекты — механика напрямую сказывается на гонке.
Мини‑игры с водителем. Самая узнаваемая фишка серии: водитель вылетает из машины, и нужно забросить его как можно дальше или попасть в конкретную цель (например, в мишень или гигантский стакан). Эти испытания добавляют игре фирменного абсурда и веселья.
Дерби и агрессивные гонки. Соперники не церемонятся: таранят, пытаются выбить с трассы, и это делает заезды напряжёнными. В режиме дерби вообще главная цель — не доехать, а выжить и разбить как можно больше машин.
Саундтрек в духе альтернативного рока. Музыка отлично подчёркивает бешеный темп и «трешевый» дух игры: треки задают настроение и делают каждую гонку ещё более энергичной.

Нюансы, которые стоит учитывать
Устаревшая графика. Для 2004 года картинка была хорошей, но сейчас выглядит простовато. Если для вас важна современная визуальная составляющая, это может немного отвлекать.
Специфическое управление. Машина ощущается тяжёлой, её нужно «чувствовать» и заранее планировать манёвры — новичкам может показаться неудобным.

Итог
FlatOut — отличный выбор для тех, кто ищет весёлые, динамичные гонки без лишней серьёзности. Игра берёт атмосферой, разрушаемостью и мини‑играми, которые до сих пор вспоминают как визитную карточку серии.

A sweet but short game that to this day has impressive physics and still feels fun to play but shows its age in a few places:
- The cars either feel completely floaty on gravel/ ice/ snow or glued to the ground on tarmac, there is no in between
- Vehicle selection is pretty large but you dont get to try most of them because you barely make enough money to upgrade a single car per cup and YOU CANT OWN MULTIPLE CARS AT ONCE
- Nitro as a feature feels almost discouraged to be gained/used because crashing into nearly any obstacle can result in a completely unpredictable situation ranging from your driver shooting out the windshield to your car flipping multiple times, usually its simply not worth the risk
- The bonus gamemodes are painfull, unreliable and not fun what so ever because you have little to no control over anything, this has been VASTLY improved up on in Flatout 2
- Lastly, but most importantly, whoever designed the Achievements for the re-release can BURN IN HELL. Its absolute pain and misery, some of the most rng dependant nonsense I have ever had to do in any game. Getting achievements for the bonus gamemodes probably took considerably longer than all three cups combined and brought so much anger and disappointment.
Despite all these downsides I would still highly recommend to pick this game up on sale and just give it a go since it is a lot ot fun and would probably run on a smart fridge at this point, but for the sake of your own sanity forget that achievements exist.

FlatOut – a journey into the past that I still cherish

When I first picked up FlatOut, it felt like stepping back into my youth. This game became a symbol of reckless road trips, noisy highways, and endless adventures with friends. Instead of smooth driving, you experienced pure chaos: gripping the wheel, shaking windows, and heart-pounding moments of near-crashes.

The most thrilling part? That split-second escape from a car that “broke free” and barreled toward you. Your pulse raced, hands sweated from the effort to stay in control. We’d forget traffic laws, laughing as we sped down highways, chasing the rush of pure freedom.

Even today, amid modern games with polished graphics and perfect controls, FlatOut holds a special place in my heart. It reminds me how simple, high-octane drives could bring such unforgettable joy.

Recommendation: If you want to relive those wild days — give yourself a chance to dive back into the world of FlatOut.

Another issue is the AI and the behavior of the other drivers, who can also be pretty frustrating at times! Especially at the start of the race.
Despite all that, the game is still fun but it's a challenge!

Flatout 1 deserves a remake with AAA graphics, where they would fix all these issues which are mainly related to the old engine.

• Gerenciamento profundo: economia, pesquisa, diplomacia e produção militar dão bastante camada estratégica pra quem gosta de planejar a longo prazo
• Boa porta de entrada pro gênero: é mais acessível que grand strategies mais complexos tipo Hearts of Iron, sem perder a essência

Pontos negativos:
• Visual e interface datados: o jogo já tem seus anos e isso aparece bastante na apresentação
• IA irregular: em partidas mais longas a inteligência artificial pode tomar decisões estranhas
• Combate simplificado: comparado a jogos mais recentes do gênero, a parte tática é bem mais rasa

No fim das contas, é uma boa porta de entrada pro gênero de grand strategy histórico, principalmente pra quem gosta de gerenciar nações sem tanta complexidade. Recomendo, com ressalvas pela idade do jogo.

New York styled Pizza:
Pizza dough:
14 g instant yeast
617g water - 95F
950g all-purpose flour
19g fine sea salt
25g granulated sugar
American Pizza Sauce and Toppings:
1 tablespoon (14g) butter
1 tablespoon (9g) extra virgin olive oil
6 cloves garlic, rough chopped
2 teaspoons (4g) red pepper flakes
28 oz (794g) can of crushed tomato
2 teaspoons (2g) dried oregano
1.5 tablespoons (21g) granulated sugar
salt and pepper to taste
Splash of olive oil
2 cups (227g) low moisture mozzarella, fresh grated
2 cups (200g) Monterey jack cheese, fresh grated
1/2 cup (26g) parmigiano reggiano, fresh grated
American Pizza Dough:
Preheat the oven and a baking steel or pizza stone at 500F for 45 minutes before utilizing it.
Whisk yeast and sugar into your water, and allow it to sit for 5 minutes. In a separate bowl, add flour and salt and mix by hand to combine. Pour your water mixture into your flour and mix by hand until you get a rough dough, then transfer to a work surface and knead until it starts to pull away from the work surface and is relatively smooth.
Place your dough in a greased bowl, then cover with plastic wrap and let rise for 1 - 2 hours at room temperature or until double in size.
Punch down your dough and dive into 300g pieces. Form those pieces into balls and place them in a floured proofing pizza box, cover with a lid, and proof at room temperature for 3 - 4 hours. (If you do not have a proofing pizza box, you can use a floured baking sheet, cover it with an inverted baking sheet and wrap it in plastic wrap.)
American Pizza Sauce and Toppings:
In a medium sauce pot, add butter and olive oil. Set that over medium-high heat; once the butter melts add garlic, cook until fragrant, add pepper flakes, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the garlic begins to brown on the edges.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, salt, and a splotch of olive oil, boil over medium-high, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 12 minutes, stirring occasionally or until thickened and viscous—season with salt to taste and let it cool down.
Assembly.- Place one of your pizza doughs onto a floured pizza peel, and flour your dough generously.
Punch your dough down in the center, working your way out to create a ¼” wide. Pick up your dough, place it over your closed fists, and rotate it around, gently stretching to 13” to 14”.
Place a couple of spoons of your sauce, starting in the center, spreading in little circles, and working your way to the edge until it gets evenly spread out.
In a medium-size mixing bowl, place mozzarella cheese, Monterey Jack, and Parmigiano; mix until combined. Sprinkle your cheese mixture to your desire and place in the oven onto your baking steel and bake for 5 - 7 minutes or until the edge gets golden brown and the cheese melts.
Enjoy.

Making History: The Calm & The Storm, developed by Muzzy Lane and published by Strategy First, is a grand strategy title that explores one of history’s most turbulent periods through large-scale political, military, and economic simulation. Focused on the years surrounding the Second World War, the game places players into positions of national leadership where success depends not only on battlefield victories but on careful management of diplomacy, industry, resources, and international influence. Rather than treating war as a series of isolated military conflicts, the game attempts to capture the broader systems that shape global events, creating a strategic experience built around planning and long-term thinking.

The scale immediately stands out as one of the game’s defining strengths. Players are not limited to controlling only the major powers commonly associated with World War II. While nations such as Germany, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Japan naturally occupy central roles within historical scenarios, the game allows players to guide many countries through one of history’s most unstable eras. This flexibility creates tremendous replay value because strategic priorities change dramatically depending on the nation selected.

Playing a global superpower creates challenges centered around managing enormous military responsibilities and maintaining international influence. Smaller nations often present entirely different obstacles involving survival, economic growth, or political maneuvering. This variety keeps campaigns feeling fresh because each nation introduces unique circumstances and opportunities.

The game adopts a turn-based structure that emphasizes thoughtful decision-making over speed or reflexes. Military operations remain important, but success depends heavily on balancing competing priorities. Expanding armed forces too aggressively can damage economic stability. Ignoring industrial development weakens long-term military strength. Diplomatic relationships influence trade opportunities and political leverage. Every system interacts with others in ways that encourage careful planning rather than impulsive action.

Economic management becomes one of the experience’s deepest mechanics. Nations require stable production systems to sustain military growth and civilian needs simultaneously. Resource shortages can disrupt plans quickly, forcing players to adapt strategies based on available materials and industrial output. Oil supplies, food production, manufacturing capacity, and trade relationships all contribute toward national strength. Building a successful nation requires understanding how interconnected these systems become over time.

Diplomacy introduces another major strategic layer. Alliances can shift, political relationships evolve, and negotiations influence future opportunities. Military expansion alone rarely guarantees victory. Strong diplomatic positioning often creates advantages that military power cannot achieve independently. Players can shape international relationships according to preferred strategies, creating alternate historical outcomes that move beyond real-world events.

Combat remains an important component throughout campaigns, but battlefield engagements operate within a larger strategic framework. Armies require logistical support, stable economies, and long-term preparation to remain effective. The game consistently reinforces the idea that military success depends on infrastructure and planning rather than battlefield decisions alone.

One of the strongest aspects of Making History: The Calm & The Storm is its willingness to embrace alternate history possibilities. Historical scenarios establish the foundation, but players are free to alter outcomes significantly through their decisions. Nations that struggled historically may thrive under different leadership approaches. Alliances can form unexpectedly. Political developments may unfold in entirely different directions depending on player priorities.

The freedom to reshape global history adds considerable replay value. Each campaign can evolve differently because player decisions influence international relationships and geopolitical stability. The experience becomes less about repeating historical events and more about exploring possibilities within historical conditions.

Scenario editing tools further expand long-term value by allowing players to modify conditions and create unique geopolitical situations. The ability to experiment beyond historical boundaries helps maintain longevity while encouraging creativity and strategic experimentation.

Visually, the presentation reflects the era in which the game originally released. Interface design prioritizes information delivery over modern visual spectacle. Maps, menus, and data systems remain central to gameplay, reinforcing the simulation-focused nature of the experience. While newer players may initially notice older presentation standards, strategy enthusiasts will likely appreciate the emphasis on functionality and clarity.

The learning curve remains one of the largest barriers to entry. New players unfamiliar with grand strategy design may initially feel overwhelmed by the number of systems demanding attention simultaneously. Military planning, diplomacy, economics, industrial management, and political decisions all require consideration. Patience becomes essential because much of the game's depth reveals itself gradually.

Pacing also reflects its strategic focus. Players seeking nonstop action or constant battlefield engagement may struggle with the slower structure. Making History values preparation and long-term planning above immediate excitement. Campaigns unfold through careful choices rather than rapid escalation.

What makes Making History: The Calm & The Storm memorable is how effectively it captures the complexity behind global conflict. The game consistently reminds players that wars are shaped not only by soldiers and battles but by economies, diplomacy, resources, and leadership decisions unfolding behind the front lines.

Players who enjoy historical simulation, alternate history scenarios, and strategy experiences built around large-scale decision making will find considerable depth here. Despite showing its age in some areas, the underlying systems remain engaging and rewarding for those willing to invest time mastering them.

A detailed and ambitious grand strategy experience that successfully combines historical authenticity, political complexity, and meaningful decision-making into a rewarding simulation of one of history’s most important eras.

[h1] Short review [/h1]

Halfway between geopolitical simulation, management game, and wargame, Making History: The Calm & The Storm presents a rich and intricate view of World War II. Initially designed as an educational program, Making History evolved into a full-fledged video game, offering a uniquely detailed, if somewhat niche, experience. While it shares similarities with Civilization and Hearts of Iron, it doesn’t quite reach the same level of entertainment or ease of play. However, Making History is far from lacking in interest; it provides a substantial range of strategic choices and an impressive scope that rewards thoughtful decision-making and long-term planning. That being said, this title is best suited for devoted fans of the genre.

[h1] Long review [/h1]

Making History: The Calm & the Storm is a grand strategy game that immerses players in the tensions and conflicts of World War II. With a global perspective, it allows players to take control of a major power or a smaller nation, each with unique historical, economic, and military challenges. While its approach to WWII is often more academic than spectacular, setting it apart from other military strategy games, The Calm & the Storm proves to be a captivating simulation that will appeal to those who enjoy strategic and diplomatic management.

Making History: The Calm & The Storm challenges players to manage a country’s economy, political relations, scientific research, and military maneuvers, all at once. It requires a careful balance; neglecting one aspect can weaken others. For example, maintaining a strong army is impossible without a steady supply of weapons and provisions, while developing resources without defending them leaves you vulnerable to neighboring powers. In wartime, invasion is always a possibility, though the game’s AI is generally not overly aggressive. International relations hold more significance than they might initially seem. Indeed, facing militarized nations like Germany or Japan requires diplomatic skill and perhaps the assistance of allied nations. Managing alliances carefully and respecting national sensibilities is crucial to securing support when needed. Additionally, keeping up with military advancements by investing in research is essential: outdated technology could quickly become a country’s downfall in this high-stakes setting.

The world map is rendered in 3D, allowing players to easily rotate the globe and zoom into any region, though the fog of war often obscures details. Units are effectively represented by markers, each accompanied by a flag and a number indicating their theoretical strength. There’s enough variety among these units to form armies that reflect real-world forces well. Moving units is simple—just click on the unit and then on the desired destination. If enemy forces are present at the destination, a battle ensues. Players can bring in air and naval support to help sway the outcome in their favor. At the end of each turn, a summary shows the casualties on both sides. Players then have the option to withdraw or press on, with the last surviving unit gaining control of the contested region.

While some major historical trends are unchangeable, much of the game's enjoyment comes from experimenting with alternative strategies. What if the U.S. had advanced through the Central Pacific instead of prioritizing the Philippines? Or if England had joined forces with Germany against the USSR? What if the Western Allies had launched a second European front as early as 1942? Exploring these "what if" scenarios—known as counterfactuals to historians—is incredibly engaging.

However, Making History: The Calm & the Storm is not without weaknesses. Its interface, while functional, remains relatively simple and may feel outdated by today’s standards, though it allows for smooth navigation between management screens. The graphics are somewhat lacking in detail and visual dynamism, and the absence of detailed maps or views detracts slightly from the WWII-era immersion. For players who prioritize strategy over visuals, this is not a major obstacle, but it’s worth noting that the overall aesthetic can feel basic.

Also, in a game this complex, good documentation is essential. The tutorial covers the basics of the interface reasonably well, but it doesn't go far enough in explaining how your choices affect your overall standing in the war. While it's helpful to learn how to move units and transfer territory, figuring out why liberating conquered nations might be advantageous or how research points translate into actual technological progress requires consulting the manual. Unfortunately, even then, some aspects remain unclear.

Another drawback lies in the artificial intelligence, which, while occasionally challenging, also reveals some limitations in responsiveness and realism. In diplomacy, certain AI reactions may seem inconsistent or counterintuitive, at times affecting the flow and strategic immersion. The military management, while adequate, lacks depth compared to other titles, and combat tactics are often limited to basic movements and positioning, without the richness of advanced military maneuvers.

Despite these flaws, Making History: The Calm & the Storm offers a rewarding experience for fans of global strategy and historical simulation. The game requires long-term thinking, as each decision impacts the progression of events. Economic, diplomatic, and military choices intersect in a complex web, often leading players to adapt their plans based on changing global situations. This focus on strategy and planning appeals to players who prefer in-depth, gradual management over direct action. If you're a big fan of the genre, feel free to buy it. Or, you can also look at their newest WWII games: Making History II : The War of the World and Making History: The Second World War

"Making History: The Calm & the Storm" is an ancient game from 2007.  It's a whopping 17 years old at the time of this review.  The game lacks support for any modern gaming display resolutions (or 16:9 widescreen monitors), hasn't been modernised or updated to run smoothly on modern gaming PCs.  Despite this lack of modernisation, it carries a pretty high price tag for such an ancient game.  This seems to have been put on Steam as a nostalgia gouge, or just a cash grab to try profit from abandonware.

This is a somewhat simplistic turn based strategy game where you control various world powers and battle for world domination, building your armies and choosing your fights carefully.  There's hundreds of games like it, so of course to recommend this over the competition, it must be exceptional, and it's not. 

The developers didn't design the game for modern gaming PCs, as such the display resolution caps out at 1200p (and there's no support for any 16:9 resolutions, not even 1080p!!!!).  The game simply won't look right on modern gaming displays due to this failure on the part of the developers.

The game is very badly optimised, with low framerates and janky gameplay even on a high end rig, probably just because it's using dated engine components/middleware that needs to be modernised, but the devs refuse, instead wanting money for an abandoned, unmaintained game.  Developers must take the time and polish their games and ensure they are optimised and will play well on any potential customers system.

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

"Making History: The Calm & the Storm" is relatively expensive for an abandonware nostalgia gouge, at $4 USD, and it's not worth it.  The game is just too old, hasn't been modernised.  And as the old saying goes, you can't go home again.  This is also competing with over 9,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.

普通過ぎるタイル形式のストラテジーゲーム。
第二次世界大戦を基準に各国と戦闘を繰り広げるが、史実通りに進めるかどうかはプレイヤー（とAI）が決められる。

・悪い点
　・内容
　　・UIが貧弱過ぎる（内政編）
　　　研究や売買など、何をするにしても一手間かかってしまう。
　　　研究なら「右のパネルでDOMESTICを開いて研究を開く」といった感じ。
　　　交易なら「右のパネルでECONOMYを開いて交易を開く」といった感じ。
　　　なぜ直接表示できるようなボタンが無いのか...。
　　　このゲームの性質上、そんなに頻繁に研究画面を開くことは無いだろうが、やはりストレスを感じてしまう。
　　・UIが貧弱過ぎる（ユニット操作編）
　　　ユニットを動かすときに移動先を間違えてしまい、再指定することは良くあるだろう。
　　　このゲームでは移動先決定後に別の場所に移動させようとすると、前の移動先を経由した移動になる。
　　　そのため、現在の行動を中止してから移動先を指定する...といった作業になるため面倒。
　　　わざわざあるタイルを経由して移動させることはほぼないのだが、この仕様は意味があるのだろうか。
　　・UIが貧弱過ぎる（画面操作編）
　　　支配した地域の施設の一斉操作ができない。
　　　例えば、石炭の生産量を最大にしたい場合、一覧からちまちま最大を指定していく必要がある。
　　　また、何かを大量生産したい場合（戦争に備えてユニットを...など）もちまちま指定していく必要がある。
　　・全体的に遅い
　　　研究や生産や施設の改善など、あらゆる項目に多くのターンを要する。
　　　そのため、ひたすらターン終了を連打することになる。
　　　1ターンが一週間の扱いであるため、核開発などがすぐ終わるのは現実的ではないかもしれないが、これはゲームである。
　　　何の変化もなくただボタンを押しているだけの状態は結構辛いものがある。
　　・研究が貧弱過ぎる
　　　研究の殆どがユニットの性能向上か、似たようなユニットの生産を可能にするもの。
　　　残りは攻撃防御の効率上昇、弾道ミサイル開発などである。
　　　もうちょっと何とかならなかったのだろうか。
　　　しかも一部の研究はXXが研究できるようになるという単なる踏み台の研究であり、存在意義が不明である。

The worst sin this bike racing game commits is its physics. They're way too simple. There's little nuance or real difficulty when it comes to handling bikes in this game. The tracks aren't that complicated either. The AI is very easy to beat. I switched from normal difficulty to hard and it was still easy. The manual gearbox is terrible, I couldn't tell when to shift gears using the RPM gauge and had to rely on guessing based on the speedometer. It wasn't fun, so I switched to automatic.

Career mode can be repetitive. You'll be doing races across different tracks, times of day, and weather conditions. Occasionally, there are challenges: completing a certain number of laps within a time limit, overtaking a specific racer within the first lap, and so on. The whole thing is divided into four parts: Class C, B, A, and Events. To unlock Class B, you have to complete Class C, and for Class A, you need to complete Class B. Throughout your career, you'll unlock different racers, whom you can choose when playing single races, championships, or multiplayer (split-screen).

Championship mode is simply 14 races against opponents.

The Capirex Challenge tasks you with completing different types of challenges, such as performing a certain number of wheelies within a time limit or overtaking someone within the first lap, similar to career mode. Some of these events are quite difficult.

The soundtrack consists of a small selection of songs from what seems to be a single band. I think all of the songs are absolute bangers and easily the best part of the game.

Visually, it looks fine. The graphics were already outdated in 2006, but there's nothing inherently wrong with how the game looks.

There are some cool mechanics sprinkled in. If you fall off your bike, you lose character health and bike health. After that, the game has you visit a doctor, who will tell you whether you're fine or not. Throughout the entire career, you can only fully restore your health three times. You regain a small amount of health after completing events. There are also pit stops, which can restore health and repair your bike. The game isn't very difficult, though, so I never really had to worry about any of this.

I can't recommend it, but I don't regret playing it.

Ducati World Championship, developed by Artematica Entertainment and published by Strategy First, is a motorcycle racing game that tries to capture the essence of riding for the legendary Italian brand. Built around the Ducati license, the game offers more than seventy officially modeled bikes divided into several classes, including Classic, Sport, Road, and Grand Prix. On paper, this breadth of content sounds impressive, promising a complete immersion into the world of Ducati motorcycles, but once you get past the surface, the execution tells a different story. While the game has the heart of a Ducati enthusiast’s dream, its technical and design shortcomings often undermine what could have been a solid racing experience.

From a gameplay perspective, Ducati World Championship offers a mix of arcade-style accessibility and simulated handling, but it fails to fully commit to either. The physics system is inconsistent, making the bikes feel light and floaty rather than grounded in realistic motion. Braking, acceleration, and cornering lack the sense of tension and precision that define great motorcycle racing games. There is little sense of weight transfer or risk when taking turns, and collisions or off-track excursions carry minimal penalty or visual feedback. While this makes the game easier for newcomers, it strips away the challenge and thrill that should accompany high-speed motorcycle racing. Even the differences between bikes are subtle, meaning progression through the various classes rarely feels transformative. What should have been a layered experience of mastering distinct machines ends up feeling repetitive and shallow after a short time.

Visually, the game struggles to impress even by the standards of its release period. Track environments are sparse, lacking in both texture detail and atmosphere. The circuits themselves, while numerous, often feel interchangeable, with few memorable landmarks or environmental touches to distinguish one location from another. The riders are animated stiffly, the crowds look static, and lighting is flat and lifeless. These issues are compounded by poor optimization and uninspired sound design. The roar of the engines—a defining feature of the Ducati experience—comes across muted and artificial, robbing each race of the sensory excitement that should make the player feel connected to their machine. The overall presentation feels dated, as though the game were built on an older engine never designed for the visual or auditory intensity expected of a modern racing title.

Despite these flaws, Ducati World Championship does contain a wealth of content. The inclusion of so many officially licensed Ducati models gives the game a sense of authenticity that might appeal to collectors or fans of the brand. There are over thirty tracks to race on, along with various modes such as single races, time trials, and a career mode that allows players to advance through multiple tiers of competition. The Capirex Challenge, a mode focused on stunts and precision riding, attempts to add variety to the standard racing format. Local split-screen multiplayer is also available, offering some replay value for casual sessions with friends, though the lack of online play limits its longevity. In many ways, these features highlight the ambition behind the project—the developers clearly wanted to build a comprehensive Ducati experience—but the game’s core mechanics and presentation simply do not keep pace with its feature list.

Where the game falters most is in its inability to capture the visceral thrill of motorcycle racing. A Ducati, in real life, is a symbol of speed, elegance, and mechanical precision, yet Ducati World Championship never conveys that essence. The handling lacks finesse, the speed feels hollow, and the connection between player and bike is superficial. It becomes evident that while the game carries the Ducati name, it does not carry its spirit. There is also a sense of missed potential—had the developers focused more on refining the physics, improving the track variety, and polishing the audio-visual presentation, the foundation for a respectable racing experience was already in place. Instead, the result feels more like a budget release wrapped in premium branding, one that relies on the Ducati license to mask its mechanical weaknesses.

Ultimately, Ducati World Championship serves as a cautionary tale about licensed racing games. While the Ducati brand provides it with identity, the gameplay and presentation do little to honor that legacy. For dedicated Ducati enthusiasts, it may still hold nostalgic or collector’s value, offering a virtual gallery of classic and modern bikes to unlock and race. But for players seeking an engaging or realistic motorcycle simulation, the game’s clumsy physics, dated graphics, and lack of immersion will likely lead to disappointment. It is an example of a project with strong potential that never quite found its rhythm. The ambition to deliver a complete Ducati experience is commendable, yet the execution fails to deliver the adrenaline and precision that define both the machines and the sport they represent.

Rating: 5/10

Ducati World Championship is an ancient game from 2006.  It's a whopping 18 years old at the time of this review.  The game lacks support for any modern gaming display resolutions (or widescreen monitors), hasn't been modernised or updated to run smoothly on modern gaming PCs.  Despite this lack of modernisation, it carries a pretty high price tag for such an ancient game.  This seems to have been put on Steam as a nostalgia gouge, or just a cash grab to try profit from abandonware.

The game is broken under Windows 10/11, but you can make it run and avoid the "AVIStreamGetFrameOpen failed!" error by running the game in Windows XP compatibility mode... a hoop, through which, gamers should not be expected to jump.  If a game developer wants to keep [i]selling[/i] their game on Steam, they must keep [i]maintaining[/i] their game on Steam.  The developers failure to do this is unacceptable. 

On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.

The game only displays in 4:3 pillarboxed aspect ratio, due to the age of the game, it predates the 16:9 widescreen gaming standard established back in 2006.  It's possible they're marketing this towards people using an old CRT they found in a dumpster, or this game is being specifically marketed towards people gaming on PC's from 1995... either way, this isn't really acceptable in the modern era of PC gaming.  It's obviously not going to look right on a modern 16:9 gaming display.

The game is incredibly dated, buggy, and unfun to play.  There may be some argument that a remaster is in order, but that seems unlikely, and either way, this is not a remaster.  It's abandonware. 

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only 13 players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 100,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.

So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?

Ducati World Championship is relatively expensive for an abandonware nostalgia gouge, at $4 USD, and it's not worth it.  The game is just too old, hasn't been modernised.  And as the old saying goes, you can't go home again.  Even when it was new, this was never a triple-A game.  This is the kind of game that went almost directly from the warehouse into the cheap bargain bins at the front of the shop.  Now, on Steam, without any modernisation?  This is impossible to recommend.

What we have here is a pretty cute clone of [b]Motor Racer[/b] with licensed [b]Ducati[/b] motorcycles and music by [b]Lacuna Coil[/b] (ten tracks total). The original [b]Motor Racer[/b] mechanics is still fine, [b]Lacuna Coil[/b] adds quite a lot to the atmosphere (not really a fan of this kind of music, but it feels totally great in things like [b]AMV[/b]s and video games), there are some game modes to choose from (single race, career, championship and even multiplayer)... In other words, like I've said, it's a pretty cute [b]Motor Racer[/b] clone. The problem is – [b]Motor Racer[/b] was released in [b]1997[/b], while this one? This one came out in [b]2006[/b].

That's right, folks, you've read it right. What we have here is a clone of [b]1997[/b] game... that came out in [b]2006[/b]. [i]La-da-da-da-dah~ It's the mo*****ckin' D-O-double-G~[/i] ♫ I mean, seriously. When you start [b]Ducati World Championship[/b] for the first time, you begin to feel like you've just being trolled. The game looks like [b]Motor Racer[/b], the game feels like [b]Motor Racer[/b]... and yet, it claims to be from [b]2006[/b].

I don't know who screwed up the timeline this time. [b]Barry Allen[/b], [b]Marty McFly[/b], or [b]Steven Moffat[/b]. But this? This is just wrong. I mean, sure, everybody loves good ol' [b]Motor Racer[/b]. But in [b]2006[/b] we've already got games like [b]MotoGP '06[/b], [b]MotorStorm[/b], [b]Crusty Demons[/b], [b]Jacked[/b] and the others. Having something like [b]Ducati World Championship[/b]? Let's just say it was an instant no. [b]Harley-Davidson[/b] did better in [b]2006[/b]. [b]Kawasaki[/b] did better in [b]2006[/b]. [i]Everybody[/i] did better in [b]2006[/b]. Ten years prior, [b]Ducati[/b]'s game sure had a chance to become a thing. When compared with the first [b]Moto Racer[/b]? [b]Ducati World Championship[/b] feels totally competitive. But in the middle of [b]2000[/b]s, while being compared with the real deal? It's close to impossible to take this title seriously.

Once in awhile comes an artist with a vision so distinct that it has the power to crystallise the voice of an entire generation. Artematica, creator of Ducati World Championship, is such an artist.

Ducati World Championship is a game that innovates the racing game genre. The gameplay is simple to comprehend yet truly shows and rewards mastery of the gameplay mechanics, with crisp and fluid controls to boot. The graphics, while seemingly outdated, provide a powerful and immersive asesthetic that makes the player feel as if they are actually in the game. The scenery is breathtaking in its simplistic beauty with vivid and evocative colours. The soundtrack is incredible with unique and ground-breaking orchestral pieces that truly inspire passion and wonder. The story is a gem not seen in videogames, period. The story maintains a realistic nature while exploring thought-provoking questions that have plagued society for ages, possibly since the dawn of man. The characters are relatable with interesting idiosyncrasies that truly make them seem real and relatable. Character development and depth is common theme throughout the story.

In short, Ducati World Championship is a magnificent, towering achievement for video-games, it's unique, creative, and memorable. If you haven't purchased this game, you are not only hurting yourself, but those around you.

Disclaimer: 
This game ends on a massive cliffhanger- so just be aware that the ending of this game doesn't resolve itself. This game is continued in "Dreamfall Chapters." 
So in order to complete the story, you must purchase both games. 

Dreamfall is a fantastic sequel to "The Longest Journey" (another totally underrated gem). 
There's a new protagonist, and a slightly different aesthetic- but all the heart is still there. 
TLJ had more of a Gen X ~ Y2K vibe, whereas Dreamfall is a softer Frutiger Aero vibe. 
But both these aesthetics blend together terrifically here. 
It's very cool to see the two worlds brought to life with enhanced graphics and gameplay. 
The game itself is very different from TLJ, but is also extremely close. It's different where it should be, but also similar in all the right ways- it's a perfect blend of new/old. 
There's a new location: the city of Casablanca, which is absolutely gorgeous, and just oozing with an early 2000s atmosphere. Between the art, colors, architecture, and technology it's like a blast of nostalgia. 
It's also really cool to explore Marcuria again, and to see what's changed over the course of time. And it's also remastered in a very beautiful way. 

The new main character introduced is Zoë, who's likable and down to Earth. 
It's a "coming of age" story just like April's in TLJ: Zoë is lost and not sure what she wants to do next in life, and an adventure falls right into her lap. 
It's great to see April Ryan again, and to see her story and how she's progressed as a character. She's really grown up, and has become her own person. 
There's another new character called Kian Alvane that's an antagonist and a part of the Azadi who you also play through in crucial parts. 

Should you play "The Longest Journey" before playing Dreamfall? 
In my opinion, yes (BUT, it's technically not required). 
I think Dreamfall does a good enough job placing you in the two worlds and showing how things actually work for the lore. 
However, it certainly helps you understand and appreciate the game, setting, atmosphere, and the characters more- especially April. And there's quite a lot of lore and character development that you'll miss if you don't play TLJ. 
There's so many throwback locations and characters from the first game that reappear in this one. 
However; TLJ is a very old and antiquated point & click game that's certainly not for everyone- so it's recommended, but not 100% necessary. I think most people would find it very boring. 

There's also some annoyances in the game:  
Just like in TLJ, there's some really bizarre obtuse puzzles, and there's some that are super obvious. 
And there's waaaay too many loading screens. 
There's a lot of backtracking, and the maps are generally not very big or sparsely populated. The fight sequences aren't anything to write home about. 
I think the controls for both the keyboard & controller for this port are awful and need to be redone. I initially used a keyboard, but ended up switching to a controller - this was better, but still imperfect. 
This game is rated M, but aside from a few F-Bombs, there's not really a reason for this rating. These could've easily been cut and just given the game a T rating instead, and I think this would have helped the game immensely. There's not really any blood, gore, nudity, or profanity. In fact, I'd forgotten that this was rated M until I heard a few F-Bombs. If it'd been rated T instead, I think it would have attracted a wider audience- including teenagers (which is what it feels like the target audience was for this game). 

This port of Dreamfall is great, but it really deserves a Remaster or Anniversary Edition. 
Even after playing this game, it still really lingers with me long afterwards... 
The dialogue is oftentimes a little corny, the graphics are dated, and the gameplay isn't amazing. But the overarching narrative, characters, and world that's created supersede all this. It sounds cheesy, but the game really exudes a feeling that cannot be replicated. 
It's an entirely unique experience, and there's not really any other game that truly captures the feeling of this one. 
A feeling of melancholy, nostalgia, and a lingering beauty that cannot be replicated.

[h1]Dreamfall: The Longest Journey[/h1] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3813041861 Hra navazuje na titul [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/sintarandir/recommended/6310]The Longest Journey[/url] (Funcom, 1999) a odehrává se o deset let později. Děj sleduje tři hlavní postavy ve dvou paralelních světech – technologickém Starku a magické Arcadii. Ústřední hrdinkou je nová postava, zhruba dvacetiletá  Zoë Castillo ze Starku, která při pátrání po zmizelém expříteli narazí na April Ryan, hlavní protagonistku prvního dílu. April v Arcadii bojuje proti zlověstné Říši Azadi, jejíž elitní voják Kian Alvane (třetí hratelná postava) ji (April) má zlikvidovat. V příběhu vystupují i známé tváře jako Brian Westhouse či Gordon Halloway, avšak znalost předchozího dílu není pro hraní nutná. Na to, že hra oslávila už 20 let vypadá pořád moc hezky i když se ovládání může mladším hráčům zdát poněkud kostrbaté... 

Ve hře Dreamfall postavy často zmiňují katastrofické „Zhroucení“, k němuž došlo ve Starku po událostech prvního dílu. Podle oficiálních doplňkových materiálů šlo o totální selhání vyspělých technologií, které zdevastovalo tamní infrastrukturu. Tato událost se časově shodovala s nástupem teokraticko-průmyslové Říše Azadi („svoboda“ v perštině) v druhé dimenzi, Arcadii. Azadi obsadili Severní země i město Marcuria a začali utlačovat nelidské obyvatele, což vedlo ke vzniku odboje, do kterého se zapojila i April. Příběh hry Dreamfall vypráví Zoë Castillo z Casablanky roku 2219 (nebo uváděno kolem roku 2209 v závislosti na zdroji), která z kómatu rekapituluje uplynulé události. Její výpověď odhaluje projekt Alchera – mezinárodní spiknutí japonské korporace WatiCorp. Tato společnost vyvinula konzoli pro lucidní snění, kterou tajně zneužívá k masovému vymývání mozků a vraždám. Klíčovou figurou výzkumu byla dívka Faith, na níž testovali halucinogenní drogu Morpheus. Faith po smrtelné otravě přenesla své vědomí do sítě DreamNet, odkud nyní proniká do digitálních systémů světa Stark a ochromuje jeho infrastrukturu bílým šumem, takzvanou „statikou“. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3813020911 V časech, kdy zuřila první velká PC-GPU válka a hráčů na tomhle poli bylo o něco více, než dnes - existovali sestavy od jisté americké společnosti... Společnost Alienware byla oficiálně založena 15. října 1996 pod názvem [b][i]Sakai of Miami Inc.[/i][/b] dvěma přáteli z dětství, Nelsonem Gonzalezem a Alexem Aguilem. Firma sestavovala stolní počítače, notebooky, pracovní stanice a herní konzole na bázi PC. V roce 1999 byl název společnosti změněn na Alienware Corporation. Podle zaměstnanců byl název „Alienware“ zvolen kvůli oblibě zakladatelů v populárním televizním seriálu *Akta X* (The X-Files); tento seriál rovněž inspiroval názvy produktových řad s tématikou sci-fi, jako byly [i]Area-51[/i], [i]Hangar 18[/i] a [i]Aurora[/i]. Dreamfall je hra, která vyšla v podstatě zároveň s akvizicí Alienware s dodnes mateřskou firmou Dell po velkém souboji s konkurenčním ASUSem. ASUS pak záhy založil sekci [b]ROG[/b] (Republic of Gamers) a později pak vojensky orientovanou řadu [b]TUF[/b] (The Ultimate Force)...
