TL;DR: What supposed to be a Deus Ex spin-offs, turned into something else. Very good game with technical issues on PC.

Technical TL;DR: It's buggy. Go to PCGamingWiki for more details.

Summary:
Previously played on PlayStation 2 back in the day. Project Snowblind developed by Crystal Dynamics, started off as a Deus Ex game, but turn into a new game, with Deus Ex DNA (Going from vents, skipping enemies in some chapter and Augmentation). Basically, the game is ALMOST an IMMERSIVE-SIM experience.

You play as soldier Nathan Frost, who after being injured in the line of duty, is treated with a cybernetic enhancement to fight a war against China, because of a RAM crisis. Which, really puts it into perspective.

Gameplay:
You'll be given a standard weapons from Assault Rifles, Sniper, Shotgun, Pistol, etc...and several gadgets you can use on your playthrough. From an EMP grenade that is useful against Droid enemies and Riot Grenade the display shield to protect you from hostile forces.

Further down the line, you're augmentation started to developed maturely from Wall-hacking, Armor Shield, Camouflage and many other essentials.

PROS:
When I say Immersive-Sim, this game is almost like this. I mean, there is one mission scenario, where you can just avoid enemies by using the Camo Aug and passing them through vents, Luring them to a live-turret or Mines and so many of those fun kills. It's a fun shooter with 18 mission tops to keep you occupied.

CONS:
A lot. Here's what's it is:
- The game lack widescreen supports. You can try the unofficial widescreen fix. But that has it's downs. So if you wanna stretch it out, go with dgVoodoo2 instead.
- The game lacks Native Controller support. "but RAZE, there is Steam Input!". THAT'S NOT THE F@#K!NG SAME, DIP$H!T! No! Why it's not? There is no button prompt icons. So it's not the same thing, you a$$h0le!
- The game crashes when you died. It happened when I got killed for stepping into a landmine. TWICE and accidentally stepping into a burning barrell, which probably my stupidity. I did the same sh!t back in my PS2 days. Setting the Compatibility options doesn't work (at least for me) and there is an error when I tried to launch the game, because Valve forgot to put Steam.dll into this game.'
- Graphically, it's buggy without dgVoodoo2. Like some environment can be too dark at times. Which is annoying.
- No achievements! Yea. sadly. no achievements for this game. So, you're gonna have to deal with it.

This version of the game is ported by Nixxes Software, before they became a very big deal they are today. It's their 4th time porting for Crystal Dynamics back then. Will either Nixxes of CD fixed this port? Very unlikely, given the game age is 21 years old. With Crystal having Tomb Raider up their a$$ and Nixxes being owned by PlayStation who recently dip-out of the PC market for a console they about to f@#k up, because of their physical media removal.

Will NIGHTDIVE do a remaster of this? Doubtful. But given how they are doing a Remastered version of the first Thief game, then we'll see. If not, then this game is forgotten.

VERDICT:
Would I recommend this game? At full price? Hard no. At sale, most definitely. It's buggy, but it's not so bad. I just wish for the game to be updated to modern standards. No remaster, just a simple fix. Will modders do an unofficial fix for this? Very unlikely. Given how the Widescreen author seemingly abandoned it. So, I don't think so.

[b]What your mission in HongKong？[/b] 

本作开发商是水晶动力，也就是后来接手古墓丽影系列的工作室，这是他们第一个也可能是最后一个fps，一开始还准备作为杀出重围系列的外传，你可以在游戏里看到很多类似的设定，但最后改为独立世界观。
背景设定过于离谱，虽说是未来世界，但扮演一名“国际维和部队”的超级士兵在hk对抗pla实在是太扯了。
打完序章后主角就被改造成了超级士兵，有着各种技能，比如说透视、子弹时间、隐身、护盾等。
没机瞄但可以直接缩放，没奔跑只能下蹲，没有背包限制，和半条命一样能同时带十几种枪械，每把枪（除了火箭筒）还都有副射击模式，挺有意思。
游戏提供了正面和潜入两种玩法，设计多条前进路线，但由于主角性能太强、敌人火力太弱，再加上还有一种在死后可以直接原地复活的道具，使得正面战斗的难度非常低，因此完全没有潜行的必要了。
作为杀出重围外传废案，黑客玩法肯定是有的，也是给了一把专门入侵的枪，射击控制面板或者机器人后黑入，可以关闭摄像头和红外线、控制机枪炮台等，因为有弹药限制，所以有时候子弹用完了只能硬闯。
除了步战，还能开车和机甲，但没有设计专门的关卡去强制你使用，经常出现我把敌人杀完了才发现旁边有的情况…
总结就是，玩法丰富，但是过低的难度导致很多玩法被浪费了，如果能穿插一两关强制的载具或潜行关卡，感觉体验会好不少。
If you are a fan of the original Deus Ex or the second one, go for it. Otherwise, skip it. It's a relic from 2005 and it shows.

[h1] Project: Snowblind? Nah, Project Comedy Times! [/h1]

It's a huge shame Ross didn't cover this game in his Game Dungeon series, because its quite entertaining how little this game has with Deus Ex franchise, even though this game was meant to be a spinoff title in the same universe. So I'll try reviewin the game in same way he would(but shorter), so hope he doesnt mind.

So the game's story starts off, generic, but what it does have is unintentional hilarity. The story pace also goes at breakneck speed, which I think actually enhances overall experience

In first mission, I already encountered a funny bug. See, the reason I called this game Comedy Times because of its unintentional comedy from bugs. I cleared an area, and now some generic ally grunt blocks the doorway forward, so I smack him a few times with melee attack. He dies, allies dont aggro on you, he makes funny pose on death, and disappears into floor. Now the game doesnt constantly have these moments, and you do have some unfun bugs, but so long as you used guides to fix bugs,then you'll be fine

Here's another hilarity with this game for me. Cutscenes. Now I get that its supposed to be a serious game, and it does have a few serious cutscenes, but the way some of them are choreographed, and the logic behind certains actions of characters ends up being funny. The final cutscene of first mission, ends up with [spoiler] enemy helicopter dropping a bomb/rocket on some injured guy [/spoiler], [spoiler] every soldier spreads out(obviously) [/spoiler], but our character, [spoiler] runs towards said guy [/spoiler], even though logically they'd both die, and the way he tries to help him is, not by blocking a guy from the blast, no, [spoiler] by trying to gently take his hand xD [/spoiler] Ya gotta see it to believe it, its just feels overly dramatic

Then 2nd map starts with you obviously surviving, get cool augmentations,Sadly from this point on, the story kinda takes a backseat, so I won't be mentioning it too much. This is one of major differences between Deus Ex and Snowblind Deus Ex was THE best story game, especially back in the day. From the main story, to lore, to even random npc's dialogue, it was just so, realistic, you actually felt like you were in a living, breathing world, full of conspiracies. Snowblind... doesn't do that, which is fine,but it definitely feels shallower as a game

Now is as good time as any to discuss, The Gameplay. Now the game has a funny way to go about introducing its weapons. You know how a moon knight has meme, where he goes "random bs go"? Well this game certainly does this, but with constantly giving you something new, usually its the guns I mean, its just a 2nd map, your character just woke up from near death experience, and you get your rifle back, you also get your pistoi, some rookie points you to an area with a push boxes gun, and you also immediately get your first aug the vision aug. The augs themselves are fine, its just the last and especially the first aug that are kinda lame. The vision aug just gives you heat vision, but its kinda pointless when the game doesnt have any really dark areas, plus the enemies themselves arent tough. You also shortly get introduced to ice pick gun, well its just a lockpick that looks like n shoots like a gun to hack terminals.

Btw, after mission debrief(you hear sad out of place classical music) before we go onto 3rd map, we IMMEDIATELY get 2nd aug activated, the slow mo aug. Im quite glad the game unlocks 2nd aug so early, since I ended up using it the most. Speaking of quick, yhis is officially your 2nd mission, and you already get a shotgun! Did I forgot to mention that all guns have alt fire button mode on right click? Pistol, carbine and shotgun have similar explosive alt modes. I didnt actually notice at first, is that, there's no alt ammo types, so all you have to do to use said alt fire modes, is just using extra ammo. Which might be an issue for shotgun n sniper rifle, but for pistol and carbine, you just SWIM in their ammo, so you always have spare ammo for a few explosives here n there, on top of regular flash and frag grenades. And you get ANOTHER gun shortly, a rocket launcher, so I ended up forgetting to even test out alt fire modes until later, because I could just use rpg or grenades on robots(who are one of the only challenging enemies).

You complete a few cool action sequences. You get introduced to sergent Chung, hes kinda your typical beefy aug guy, and he unlocks you yet another aug. You get emp'd by some grunt, and you get to learn what snowblind means, just emp short circuiting tech, this idea will barely get build up on, but at least Ross will know why this game is called Project Snowblind. You also get kinda awkward talk Sergent has with tech guy, about being replaced by you, but its delivered in a comedic way(this time it might be intentional) FINALLY you get introduced to the last gun, for this mission , and I just burst out in laughter from getting sniper rifle. I do enjoy more options, but I also find it absurdly funny how many tools the game throws at you. I didnt even get to play with the first few toys! You also get one more action moment, breaking another few robots, and I like how developers did it. Because these robots are like mid game threat, they put the player on the high ground, to minimize damage the player get, its a clever level design, and a way to introduce tougher enemy earlier on.

Onto the new map.See, this game has so many mechanics, that it throws at you, that I complete lost track of some of them, and never used em, and one of those mechanics was hacking robots from distance. You can use icepick,to shoot at a ROBOT, to take control. This map also officially introduces you stealth options, like hacking turrets to kill enemies for you, or VENTS. Vents are back, they're basically a relic of old DX gameplay. Its probably the most boring vents ever, half the time the game doesnt even bother to hide them. So basically the level designs is [b[ the second major difference [/b] between DX games and Snowblind. Btw, one other small relic of old DX design is actually the alarm design, they look EXACTLY like in DX1. As for stealth mechanics itself, its... very generic. You are in line of sight, enemy spots you kinda stealth, no way to distract em by rocks or anything. But its comedically broken. The thing is, the line of sight is VERY inconsistent, sometimes they're blind as a bat, but sometimes they see you even if they chat with each other, and you take vent path. 

What npcs do lack is memory, and ears. I swear I had so many times I just run around, like driving in car(level has a car), then checking out floor for loot, and seeing grunt, UNAWARE of my existence, even saying dialogue npcs say when they find you first. So funnily enough, best way to do stealth here, is to just not take it seriously. "oops they found it, oh well,killing time!" and they cant stop you! Besides robots requiring explosives, early to mid game human enemies are paper thin, so you can just go guns blazing after broken stealth, and alarms dont alert enemies outside the floor

Единственный плюс - на удивление, игра работает почти без закидонов и сторонних патчей. С другой стороны, а оно и задаром не больно-то надо.

Disclaimer: My playtime is a lot longer, closer to 4 hours. One of the fixes for the game made Steam not recognize when I have the actual game running (the menu and actual game are two separate instances for some reason).

Project: Snowblind is an excellent, albeit dated game which has issues running on modern hardware. It reminds me a lot of the Crysis series. Sadly, the game crashes often, sometimes 5 minutes into running since it cannot support multi-core processors, unless you apply a community fix.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2040494150

This guide offers the solutions you'll need to get it running. Do be aware that even with the guide, the game crashes roughly every 1 hour of playtime. Fortunately, it's a short game that does have acceptable saving and short levels. You can save at the start of each level and at fixed mid-level saving zones. Always save when given the chance.

You can get around the 1 hour of playtime thing by just closing and reopening the game every two levels or so.
Do NOT Alt-Tab, it crashes the game. Using turrets sometimes crashes the game too, be aware.

In terms of other technical problems, some hitboxes are peculiar, you can get stuck on nothing or sometimes phase through turrets. There's also broken audio in mid-game menu, an increasingly louder stuttering.
The game's graphics are noticeably aged and there's a blur in certain levels.
Two of the cutscenes in the late-game lacked sound, no clue if it was a user-end issue sadly.

The gameplay is solid if you can get past that. Lots of different weapons, grenades and abilities, as well as multiple options for progressing through levels. You even have a gravity gun... However, the game doesn't offer any incentives to use most of toolkit you have and the levels are rather short. Good for replayability I suppose.

Each weapon also has a special ability/alternate fire mode which is a cool addition, albeit not a very useful one in practice since the enemies are not that strong and you won't be facing too much of a challenge in any level.

Shootting is good, the enemies are not bullet-spongy. In fact, it quite often felt like they died a little too quickly. They react to your shots which is cool. Melee animations are wonky (as in, it doesn't look like a sufficiently powerful punch) but they're pretty strong and useful.

There's locked-on soft aim-assist which may be a malus for some folks. It's not very disruptive but it's clearly present.

The game offers you all the ammo you'll need to progress and is quite generous with pickups in general. There's also health & energy upgrades scattered across the levels which make for neat collectibles.

The story and writing are good, I quite enjoyed it. There's quite a few jokes and neat scenes.

The level-design is excellent, albeit small as previously mentioned. Each level has hackable objects and multiple avenues of approach. The game has 18 levels and I'd say around 4-6 hours of content in its campaign, depending how you play. There's solid variance in the environments as well as good enemy variety.

I like the fact you're not alone in the fight. You're part of a Coalition Force and you got buddies fighting alongside you in many missions. Some parts of your arsenal also allow you to summon temporary allies like shock drones, you can also hack and convert enemy robots to your side. I really love that.

The design in general looks great.
Music is also good.

Overall, I'll give it a 9/10 with the missing point being due the technical problems that it suffers from. That said, I've seen far worse issues in old games like this. It was clearly made by a competent team, the game was intended to be a Deus Ex game at first, and it goes for a bargain price, so I fully recommend it.

Project: Snowblind is a fast-paced, cybernetic first-person shooter that reflects the ambitious experimentation of mid-2000s action games. Developed by Crystal Dynamics and published by Square Enix, it delivers a blend of futuristic military combat, super-soldier augmentations, and light immersive-sim influences wrapped in a compact, high-energy campaign. Although originally conceived as a spin-off within the Deus Ex universe, the project eventually evolved into its own standalone title. That legacy is easy to spot—Project: Snowblind carries the DNA of a game that wants to give players choices and tools rather than funnel them through pure shooting galleries. The result is a hybrid experience: not as deep as a true immersive sim, but far more flexible and creative than the typical shooters of its time.

The game follows Nathan Frost, a soldier who survives a devastating attack on Hong Kong thanks to an experimental procedure that transforms him into an augmented super-soldier. The story wastes little time establishing its stakes: a hostile regime known as the Republic is pushing toward a catastrophic technological strike—“Project Snowblind”—that could destabilize global infrastructure and plunge the world into chaos. Frost, newly enhanced and thrust into frontline operations, becomes an essential weapon in the battle to stop the attack. While the narrative leans heavily on military urgency and action-movie momentum rather than moral ambiguity or philosophical depth, it succeeds in delivering a uniformly tense, tech-noir atmosphere. Futuristic cityscapes, armored corridors, neon-soaked warzones, and high-tech bases all lend the game a distinctly gritty sci-fi flavor.

Gameplay is where the experience shines. Project: Snowblind thrives on giving the player a toolset that encourages improvisation. Frost’s augmentations include cloaking, enhanced vision modes, shielding, temporary slow-motion reflex boosts, and an area-of-effect electrical pulse that can fry electronics and stun enemies. Each augmentation has its own strategic niche, and the satisfying part is how well they combine with traditional weaponry. You might cloak yourself to bypass a fortified checkpoint, slow time to snipe drones mid-air, hack a turret to turn it against its owners, or unleash a storm of EMP energy to disable a swarm of enemies before rushing in with shotguns or rifles. The best moments emerge when you chain abilities and tools together, creating your own solutions to combat scenarios instead of simply shooting your way through them.

Weapons also contribute to the game’s flexible playstyle. The arsenal ranges from standard assault rifles and shotguns to more exotic devices such as flechette cannons, thermal detonators, riot-shield projectors, and deployable attack drones. Each weapon feels distinct, and many serve roles beyond raw damage—some control crowds, others manipulate terrain, and several interact synergistically with augmentations. For a game that is ultimately linear, Project: Snowblind injects just enough variety into its combat encounters to make each level feel like an opportunity to experiment with new tactics.

The level design follows a primarily linear structure, but it frequently offers multiple approaches to objectives. Alternative paths, stealth routes, hidden vents, hackable systems, and destructible objects give areas more depth than a basic corridor shooter. While these options never reach the complexity of a Deus Ex-style sandbox, they still add welcome flavor. The game rewards curiosity and encourages you to look beyond the most obvious path, which helps maintain a sense of agency and replayability even within its constrained structure.

Visually, the game captures the futuristic militarism of its setting with confidence. Although its graphical fidelity reflects its era, the overall aesthetic still holds up thanks to its cohesive design philosophy. Hong Kong’s rain-slicked streets, flickering holograms, industrial installations, and hectic battlefields all contribute to an atmosphere that feels alive and oppressive. The sound design bolsters this mood with energetic combat effects, satisfying augmentation cues, and a techno-infused soundtrack that reinforces the urgency of Frost’s missions.

Where Project: Snowblind falters is in its pacing and depth. The campaign moves quickly—arguably too quickly—and players can reach the credits long before they’ve had time to fully explore or enjoy all of Frost’s augmentations. Many powers are unlocked only shortly before the game concludes, giving little room to play with them in meaningful scenarios. Enemy AI is competent but rarely challenging, often falling into predictable patterns that diminish the need for tactical diversity. Additionally, the game’s initial promise of immersive-sim options occasionally collides with its linear mission scripts, resulting in a hybrid design that feels like it never fully commits to either philosophy.

Multiplayer was once a notable selling point, with support for competitive matches featuring vehicles, gadgets, and augmentation mechanics. However, as with many older shooters, active online communities have faded over time, leaving the mode more of a historical artifact than a practical feature for modern players.

Despite its shortcomings, Project: Snowblind remains a bold and enjoyable experiment—an action game that tries to bridge the gap between pure shooter and flexible sandbox. Even today, its mixture of fast gunplay, satisfying augmentations, and dynamic mission scenarios offers a refreshing alternative to formulaic FPS design. It lacks the complexity of the immersive sims it gestured toward, but what it offers is a lean, energetic, and creatively equipped shooter that never overstays its welcome. For players who enjoy mid-2000s sci-fi shooters or who appreciate games that offer multiple approaches to combat without demanding deep micromanagement, Project: Snowblind still delivers a memorable and highly entertaining ride.

Les sensations sont bonnes : on se sent vraiment puissant, les gadgets futuristes ajoutent de la variété, et l’ambiance cybernétique fonctionne bien. En revanche, le jeu est assez court, linéaire, et la technique a pris un coup de vieux. L’IA est parfois bancale, et la structure très classique pour un joueur d’aujourd’hui.

💭 En résumé : un bon shooter rétro, fun et nerveux, parfait pour les fans de FPS old-school et d’univers futuristes.

🕹️ Note personnelle : 7,5/10 (Divertissant et efficace, mais un peu figé dans son époque.)

Comprei este jogo durante uma promoção a muito tempo atrás, mas por problemas presentes nele nunca fui a fundo jogar. O jogo tem uma má fama de crashar MUITO, quase que durante toda a gameplay para algumas pessoas, e por isso não pude jogá-lo decentemente durante meu tempo usando windows 10. Agora que estou usando linux decidi testá-lo e ver se conseguia ir longe, e para minha surpresa o jogo crashou somente 2 vezes em uma missão onde tentei usar uma torreta (completamente opcional). Então ignorei tal torreta e o jogo rodou super bem sem nenhum crash. Consegui fechar o jogo sem nenhum mod, apenas o jogo vanilla mesmo. Caso você utilize linux recomendo dar uma segunda chance a ele, porém usar versões atuais do proton faz o jogo rodar sem áudio. Sobre multiplayer não sei se ainda existem servidores pois não cheguei a testar. No geral foi um jogo que me surpreendeu positivamente. Nota 7.5/10

So, imagine an 80s, 90s or early 2000s action movie. The usual one, with pretty cool angles and editing, powerful but not unique soundtrack, the main character that can destroy armies singlehandedly, almost without breaking a sweat, and save the day against insurmountable odds, the actor whose main and only skills are being buff, looking serious and delivering the lines in cool voice, and the plot that exists only to create an environment in which the character will do the most insane, cool and dramatic things possible. The type that doesn't get high scores, some people laugh at, others point at and say movies like this are the doom of the industry; that doesn't really get much attention in general and is never talked again by the studio, even though the box office was more or less okay. Now turn that movie into a game - and you'll receive Project: Snowblind.

It is a fascinating idea with some parts being done very well: lots of surpisingly good cinematics; dialogues on every corner; cliche charismatic characters of every kind; numerous amounts of cheesy lines; the clearly good and bad guys; presence of an underlying message that is the only saving grace of the story and probably was written thanks to the lucky accident; the plot with lots of cheap drama.

The endless novel features. Most of the characters can be interacted with, prompting them to spit out their thoughts about situation or some other topic. Environment can be interacted with as well, in the form of destroying some decorations or even moving them; lots of the doors and hatches can be opened and actually will lead somewhere, whether to the next main location or some off way storage with different goods. The surroundings are impressively well detailed, really helping with immersion. There are vehicles which can be operated, terminals that can be hacked and cameras that can be destroyed. Sneak or run and gun - the choice is yours, at least half of the time, when stealthy approach is allowed by the design of the level. Oh, and don't forget to check out fancy physics!

There is a stealth system, a barely working one but still present. Enemies have lines of sight, can hear and notice stuff like gunshots, explosions and even thrown crates, react to it, activate alarm or run to the emplacements, and if they aren't alerted - some interesting information can be heard when they are talking, even though rarely.

The huge arsenal is given to the player. Pistol, automatic rifle, shotgun, sniper rifle, some exciting futuristic stuff - all like in good old days of shooters. In addition to that, there are different types of grenades and some situational gadgets. And an icing on the cake - the abilities system: highlighting enemies, activating energy shield, slowing down time and some other interesting powers - all that is available to the player.

[quote=Obligatory Technical State of The Game Disclaimer][i]...Even the awfully implemented mouse and keyboard controls, rare random crashes, unchangeable small field of view and forced square resolution that can't be tweaked without breaking part of the image aren't enough to kill the joy from using aforementioned gear. There is even a handy guide with descriptions of controls in the folder of the game, in case you'll get confused when playing. But I digress...[/i][/quote]

All that fascinating stuff squeezed to fit into six hours campaign. God, what a bloody mess it is. Feature, upon feature, upon feature. That's what old Call of Duty games would look like if someone decided to mod in every feature from Crysis, and some random personal additions on top of that, just because why not. As result, you end up not using any of that stuff most of the time, because why the hell do that if you can just run and shoot enemies like in every other game? It's fun, yes, but it also makes you extremely overpowered: it's not just easy to get through the enemies, it's difficult to actually lose. It's one of the biggest power fantasies in shooter genre, but it's extremely shallow, short and simple because you can't create good game just by throwing every imaginable thing into a mix. It's oversaturated, it doesn't know what it is. Even multiplayer with lots of gamemodes is present, even though it's dead and there is no ability to play against the bots, unfortunately.

This game is like a showcase. Its developers are screaming: "Look at us! Look at our creation! Witness what great ideas we have, what skills we possess! Imagine what we could have done if we actually tried, cry from that understanding and throw money at us so that we could realize our full potential someday in the future!"

It's not a stealth action, yet it has elements of such. It's not a futuristic heavily abilities-dependant shooter, yet it has elements of such. It's not a plot-oriented story game, yet it has elements of such as well. And it's not your average shooter because it's too complex to be called so.

It's everything. It's nothing. It's a great idea. It's an awkward execution. It's laughable, yet intriguing.

This is a creative freedom in it's pure form, unrestricted and without any meaningful direction. Not bad, but not good either. A great example of what games can be like, and what they shouldn't be. And a fun one, really fun, just because something so saturated can't not be.

Play it, have some dumb fun. Appreciate the chaotic art that can be created only in the field of videogames. Laugh, get surprised, learn, be disappointed. And then never ever repeat the mistakes of glorious bastards from the development team of Project: Snowblind, but take in account and ponder on the actually good ideas which have collapsed under their own weight; burned like the wings of Icarus.

You're probably here because you heard that this was originally supposed to be Deus Ex 3: Clan Wars and you wanted to see what could've been. The similarities are only skin deep. What you have is a game that loves nothing more than to crash, even after fixes. When the game does decide to run, you have a story that is inundated with military cliche and characters that are flatter than cardboard. Being a bargain bin FPS, that isn't always a bad thing. That said, the gameplay is linear, repetitive, and rarely exciting. You can't even enjoy it as a cheap time-waster. With cheap thrills being the bare minimum, Project: Snowblind still manages to fall short. Don't waste a handful of hours of your life that you'll never get back. Look elsewhere for that janky guilty pleasure to play between actual games.

Rogue Trooper, 2006 yılında piyasaya sürülmüş ve benim doğduğum yıl çıkan oyunlardan biri. Bu oyunu ilk kez 2013 yılında oynamıştım. Aradan geçen yılların ardından, 2026 yılında Steam üzerinden yaklaşık 5 saatlik bir oynanışla oyunu yeniden bitirdim. İnsanın çocukluğunda oynadığı oyunlara yıllar sonra geri dönmesi ve o günleri yeniden hatırlaması gerçekten farklı bir his. Eski günleri özlemişim be!

Oyunun dinamiklerini hâlâ oldukça başarılı buluyorum. Özellikle düşmanları bacaklarından vurduğunuzda yavaşlamaları, oynanışa gerçekçilik ve taktiksel bir detay katıyor. Keskin nişancı tüfeğiyle nişan almak da oldukça keyifli. Karakter tasarımları ve oyunun genel atmosferi, çıktığı dönemi düşündüğümüzde gayet başarılı.

Elbette günümüz oyunlarıyla karşılaştırıldığında bazı mekanikler eski hissettirebilir. Ancak Rogue Trooper'ın kendine has atmosferi ve oynanış tarzı, onu benim için özel kılan unsurlar arasında. Bu oyunu yalnızca bir aksiyon oyunu olarak değil, geçmişime açılan küçük bir kapı olarak da görüyorum.

2017 yılında çıkan Rogue Trooper Redux sürümünü henüz oynamadım, ancak onu da deneyimlemeyi düşünüyorum. Bakalım yenilenmiş sürüm, yıllar önceki anılarımı nasıl canlandıracak!

Sonuç olarak: Hem nostalji yaşamak hem de döneminin başarılı aksiyon oyunlarından birini deneyimlemek isteyenlere kesinlikle tavsiye ederim. Benim için yeri ayrı olan bu maceraya yeniden dönmek çok güzeldi.

At first I didnt like this game and I wanted to remove it from my library because I thought it would be just another generic and boring shooter. Thank God I kept playing. Rogue Trooper turned out to be a very fun shooter with likeable characters, enjoyable mechanics, an engaging story and gameplay, cinematic cutscenes, old but appealing visuals and much more. While its not the best shooter I still really liked it and would recommend it to anyone.

I expected Rogue Trooper to be a bit of a brainless romp, but no, that's one of the better, tighter single player shooter campaigns I've had the privilege to enjoy. So many tools and mechanics and approaches to well-considered, varied setpieces. This one has Got It to a degree I wouldn't have suspected.

Rogue Trooper is a 3rd person shooter from my childhood. My first ever playthrough came after I got my first computer system back in 2017/2018 after I had gotten sunk into CSGO and other easier-to-run games.

I enioyed the campaign back then (being a teen it isn't that big a stretch to imagine I fell in love with the simplistic yet addictive combat) and find that replaying it fills me with just as much joy.

The game is very much a product of tis time but that is a good thing. It's janky and counter-intuitive with a old school '2 kool 4 skool'  kind of punch to it. If you enjoy  a sassy and sarcastic dialog you'll enjoy the characters in this. On top of the dialog the women in this game are actually attractive and offer more than just a political mouthpiece for gaming studios.

This is my current 3rd playthrough in total and I am enjoying the first few missions. Since my library is extensive it'll take a while to focus specifically on this but I intend to complete it wholly and with the utmost care.

All in all this is a worthwhile experience and I would reccomend it if you are looking for non-modern games to sink hours into. Sure, it as quick as you make it but you'll find (I hope as I do) that time flies by as you dive within its world.

[h1]Тебе зрадили, а твої вбиті побратими тепер - у вигляді флешок в гвинтівці, рюкзаку та шоломі. [/h1]
Rogue Trooper - типовий шутер нульових, в який нині грати - це як сидіти на незручному дерев'яному стільці: наче й добре, що не стоїш, проте все-одно муляє то тут, то там.
Проте гра присвячена персонажам маловідомого, незаїждженого всесвіту, а тому заслуговує на увагу. 

[h3]📖Сюжет📖[/h3]
В далекому майбутньому, в епоху колонізації землянами нових планет, розгорілася війна за одну з них, що має назву Нова Земля. Військові дії між силами Півночі та Півдня були настільки руйнівними, що біосферу було винищено майже повністю, а повітря стало настільки токсичним, що для продовження війни обидві сторони мусили вдягати захисні костюми і маски. Втім, учені Півдня пішли іще далі і після довгих років дослідницької праці змогли вивести унікальних, генномодифікованих солдатів, здатних перебувати на поверхні планети без додаткових засобів захисту. Ці штучно вирощені вояки-клони росли і розвивались значно швидше за людей і у віці вже 18 місяців мали дорослі, повністю здорові тіла і були готові до бойових тренувань. І, додатково, цій генномодифікованій піхоті не страшна навіть сама смерть! Адже, якщо життя блакитношкірого клона обривається, є можливість вилучити з його тіла чіп, що містить особистість піхотинця і помістити його в зброю, або у нове, вирощене тіло для подальшого ведення бойових дій. 
Ось гравець і приміряє на себе шкурку такого от суперсолдата, на ім'я Роуг (Rogue), який, з декількома своїми товаришами, вирушає на бойове завдання. Проте, як з'ясувалося, один з генералів Півдня вирішує зрадити своїх і переметнутися на бік ворога, через що солдати Півночі влаштовують блакитношкірим хлопцям теплий прийом із сумними наслідками. Роуг вирішує помститися за долю побратимів і покарати зрадника.

[h3]🎮Ігролад🎮[/h3]
Rogue Trooper - це шутер, а отже, перш за все слід розказати про стрільбу та зброю. На вибір тут її декілька видів: штурмова гвинтівка (з додатковим снайперським режимом) дробовик, міномет, гранатомет, лазерна гармата, пістолет та декілька видів гранат. Чогось особливого про стрільбу сказати нічого, вона...нормальна, нічим не виділяється. 
У грі присутній крафт: є можливість збирати з тушок переможених ворогів ресурси для апгрейду, чи створення зброї, а також поповнення боєприпасів та аптечок. Трохи пізніше по сюжету з'являється можливість ставити голографічні приманки для ворогів, або використовувати нашу гвинтівку як турель. Наш Роуг може ховатися за укриттями і звідти вести вогонь, що подекуди є дуже корисним, особливо, коли вороги пруть звідусіль. До речі, про ворогів. Їхній інтелект розчаровує. То тут, то там доводилося спостерігати, як не надто розумні вояки Півночі кидали гранати собі під ноги, або ж ховалися за укриттям таким чином, аби нам було зручніше розстрілювати їхні тушки.  Що ж, принаймні, тут є якесь різноманіття: тут тобі і звичайні піхотинці, і снайпери, і роботи, і бойові літальні апарати...
Є до, речі, який-не-який стелс, а саме, можливість тихого вбивства нещасного НПС зі спини. 
Окремо хочу згадати таку приколньу фішку: якщо вистрілити ворожому НПС в балон за спиною, то власник спершу в паніці забігає туди-сюди, а потім взірветься, розкидаючи тіла своїх союзників. Виглядає весело) 
Але от чого справді не вистачає грі, так це розчленування. Коли вороги розлітаються від вибухів гранат, чи попадань з міномета - їхні цілісінькі тушки виглядають напрочуд нудно і прісно. 

[h3]🎨Графіка і дизайн🎨[/h3]
Як і належить практично мертвій планеті зі знищеною атмосферою, локації виглядають тьмяно та нежиттєрадісно. Дизайн НПС досить цікавий і самобутній, а обличчя головного героя аж пашить брутальністю і готовністю помститися всім і кожному.

[h2] What Is Rogue Trooper [/h2]

Rogue Trooper Is an Action, Third Person, Sci-Fi, Shooter, where you are a GI a genetic modified soldier that wants revenge his comrades , he is hunting a traitor alongside with his fallen comrades (That now are chips in his gun and helmet) that helps the "Rogue Trooper" to fulfill his mission.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


[b] Story: [/b] You play as "Rogue Trooper" a GI soldier that wants to revenge his fallen comrades , all by himself , he visits different locations  and destroys the enemy guns, ships , etc , all thx to his comrades, that are now chips in his guns and helmet, that can give him many tools to complete his mission.


Points: 7


[b] Gameplay: [/b] Rogue Trooper has a couple of guns in his arsenal , all of them take a role , his primary gun is a standard rifle that when you zoom , it transforms into a sniper rifle, you have shotgun, pistol , a rocket launcher etc, All of the weapons serve a purpose and all are fun to use , Rogue Trooper can climb and take cover , which it helps him in the battle , you can find cover and easily take down enemies with the sniper rifle. But , like i said even if the weapons have their purpose, there's not too much , you only have one rifle, one shotgun ,etc.


Points: 7


[b] Atmosphere: [/b] the game takes place in a planet called "Nu Earth" but in this planet, you visit many locations which have different enviroments and details , all the places that you visit are different from each other, you have the big city with a lot of towers , big buildins, you have a dessert , a forest with huge trees, beaches, etc. 
All of them have unique details and doesn't look exactly the same.


Points: 7


[b] Soundtrack: [/b] The soundtrack of Rogue Trooper is mixed , you have good tracks , and others are regular "military tunes" , the best soundtracks are almost at the end of the game, which is fine, but there's not variety and the only songs that you are going to listen are typical military songs.


Points: 6


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[h3] Overall: [/h3]
The game is fun, for the time (2006) in my opinion looks good , is nothing special , but is fun , you can play it and complete it in a couple of hours , if you don't take too long looking at the enviroment , etc (Like i did, that's why i have so many hours) 
But , theres another game called "Rogue Trooper Redux" which is an enhanced version, play whichever version you want , this one is cheaper tho.

Rogue Trooper, developed and published by Rebellion, is a third-person tactical shooter set in the gritty, war-torn universe of the classic British 2000 AD comic series of the same name. Originally released in 2006 and later remastered as Rogue Trooper Redux, the game brings to life the violent struggle on Nu-Earth—a chemically ravaged planet where genetically-engineered soldiers fight a never-ending war. The title follows the lone surviving Genetic Infantryman (GI), Rogue, who sets out on a personal mission for justice after being betrayed by his own commanding officers. This revenge-fueled narrative, bolstered by engaging mechanics and strong source material, makes Rogue Trooper a compelling and memorable experience, particularly for fans of comic-inspired sci-fi action.

From a gameplay standpoint, Rogue Trooper combines third-person shooting with tactical and cover-based mechanics that, for its time, were innovative and well-executed. Players control Rogue, a super-soldier bred for war, enhanced to survive in the toxic atmosphere of Nu-Earth. What sets Rogue apart from typical protagonists isn’t just his genetic enhancements—it’s his sentient gear. His fallen squadmates, Helm, Gunnar, and Bagman, have their personalities digitally preserved in Rogue’s equipment: the helmet, gun, and backpack, respectively. This mechanic is more than narrative flair—it gives the player access to unique abilities such as automated turret fire, on-the-fly ammo crafting, and enemy hacking, all of which add layers of strategy to standard shootouts.

The level design is mostly linear, with open areas that encourage tactical positioning and use of cover, but what truly elevates the combat is the synergy between Rogue and his bio-chip companions. Each encounter becomes a chance to utilize your tools creatively. Whether you're setting traps, creating decoys, crafting grenades, or calling in automated fire from Gunnar, there’s a welcome depth to what might otherwise have been standard firefights. The AI isn’t groundbreaking by today’s standards, but it’s aggressive and varied enough to keep you engaged throughout the campaign. There are also stealth elements sprinkled throughout the missions, giving players alternative ways to approach certain objectives, though the game leans more toward action than stealth overall.

Visually, even in its original form, Rogue Trooper had a distinct aesthetic that captured the bleak, blue-toned atmosphere of Nu-Earth with surprising effectiveness. The Redux version updated textures, lighting, and models to meet modern expectations, but retained the original’s comic-book charm. Character models and animations are functional rather than flashy, but the environmental design helps immerse players in the constant state of warfare and desolation that defines the setting. The blue hues of Nu-Earth are iconic and used purposefully to evoke the toxic, alien nature of the world without becoming visually monotonous.

Narratively, Rogue Trooper does a commendable job of adapting its source material. While it doesn’t delve deeply into complex character arcs or moral ambiguity, it offers a focused and personal revenge story that drives the action forward. Rogue himself is a stoic, no-nonsense figure, a perfect match for the war-hardened world he inhabits. The betrayal at the heart of the story gives the game emotional weight, and the ongoing banter with his fallen comrades—now part of his gear—adds both humor and camaraderie to an otherwise grim tale. The voice acting and writing are solid, managing to convey both gravitas and the darkly sardonic tone often found in the 2000 AD comics.

The campaign is moderately lengthy, offering around 7 to 9 hours of content, depending on play style and difficulty. It’s a well-paced experience that rarely drags, with a satisfying mix of shootouts, set pieces, and light tactical puzzles. The game also includes additional challenge modes and multiplayer options—though these have become less populated over time—which give it some replay value beyond the core story. Despite its age, the Redux edition is a testament to the original game's thoughtful design, proving that good mechanics and a strong setting can stand the test of time.

One of the game’s only real drawbacks is its adherence to older design philosophies that might feel dated to players accustomed to more dynamic cover systems or deeper customization. Movement can feel a bit stiff at times, and mission objectives are sometimes overly straightforward. However, these issues are minor in the grand scheme, and most players will be too absorbed in the combat and world-building to dwell on them. The game also doesn’t offer extensive exploration or branching narrative paths, but it doesn’t pretend to. It delivers a focused, action-packed experience, and it does so with confidence.

In conclusion, Rogue Trooper is a standout example of how to adapt a cult comic series into an interactive format without losing its identity. Through smart mechanics, solid gunplay, and a memorable setting, the game creates an experience that is both entertaining and respectful to its roots. The integration of squad-based abilities via the bio-chip system still feels fresh, and the Redux version ensures that both new players and returning fans can appreciate the game in a more visually refined package. For those who enjoy tactical shooters with a twist, or simply want to step into the boots of a war-bred super soldier on a mission of vengeance, Rogue Trooper remains a rewarding journey through the chaos of Nu-Earth.

[h1] Rogue Trooper [/h1]

[u][i] Halo ama Avatar temalı [/i][/u]

Rogue Trooper, Gerry Finley-Day ve Dave Gibbons'un 1981'de yazmış olduğu bilim-kurgu temalı 2000AD ismindeki bi çizgi romana dayanıyor. Genel olarak sevilse de - herhalde askeri macera hikayesi olduğu için - hikaye kısaca şu şekilde: [spoiler] Nu-Earth diye zehirli bir gezegendeyiz. Burada oksijensiz ve maskesiz yaşamak imkansız. Kuzeyliler ve Güneyliler ( Norts- Southers ) diye bilinen 2 topluluk arasında süregelen ve bitmek bilmeyen bir savaş var. Southers Bilim adamları Nu-Earth'un zehirli atmosferine dayanabilecek 19 adet genetik olarak yükseltilmiş yani modifiye edilmiş yapay zeka ve mavi yaratıklar yaratıyorlar ve bu yapay zekaların da mavi bebeğimsi yaratıklara entegre edip su içinde saklıyorlar. Bunlara 'Genetic Infantryman' deniyor yani kısaca GI. Tabi bulundukları suyu sunucu gibi düşünürsek, yapay zekalarını bir çipe yükleyip yine başka yetişmiş mavi bedenlere aktarabiliyorsunuz. Böylece bir GI ölse bile çipini alıp başka bir GI'ya, silaha, kaska ya da çantaya yükleyebiliyorsunuz. Bir nevi matrix'i andırıyor. Temel mantığı anladıysak gerisi kolay. Bir general var. Bize ihanet ediyor. Çıkartma atacağımız yeri önceden düşmanlara haber veriyor ve orası GI'lar için tam bir katliam meydanı oluyor. Oynadığımız GI olan Rogue kaybettiği arkadaşlarını silahına, kaskına ve çantasına yükleyerek komutanı bulup öldürmeye çalışıyor. [/spoiler] Hikaye kısaca bu şekilde ve pek bir esprisi yok. 

  Oyunumuz Rebellion tarafından geliştirilse de Eidos tarafından yayıncılığı yapılmış. Tabi günümüzde Eidos, Square Enix Europe olarak devam ettiği için Steam sayfasında ismi yazmıyor. - Bu arada Eidos çoğu sevdiğiniz serinin yayıncılığını ya da geliştiriciliğini yapmış bir firmadır. - Oyun adeta buram buram 2006 kokuyor ve ben buna bayılıyorum. Resmen geçmişi anımsadım. Önceden oynadığım oyunları hatırladım. Bana göre bırak Türkiye'yi aslında dünyanın zirve noktası 2000 - 2012 yılları arasıdır. Sadece oyun için değil her anlamda söylüyorum. 

 Oyunda Halo vari bir saf aksiyon ve kendine has mekanikleri var. Mesela rakibinizin sırtındaki tüpe ateş edip onu patlatabilir, çantanızdan silahlarınızı upgrade edebilir ve kendinize mühimmat sağlayabilir, yere mayın döşeyebilir ve sessizce düşmanları indirebilirsiniz. Silah çeşitliliği bu anlamda çok iyi. Zamanına göre görüntü kalitesi bence gayet yerinde. Ses ve müzik nevi şahsına münhasır olacak seviyede - yani kısa ve gaza getiren melodiler - böyle bir oyun için yeterli. Yapay zeka bazen çok iyi bazen çok kötü. Mesela siper alma konusunda çok iyiler ama birini vurunca hepsi sıraya girip ölen kişinin yanında dikiliyorlar ve size kendilerini gümüş tepside sunuyorlar. Fakat düşman çeşitliliği gayet güzel. Ayrıca düşman hasar alıp ölmeyince topallaması ve yürümekte zorlanması gibi detaylar sizi atmosfere daha fazla çekiyor. Zorlayıcı bir aksiyonu ve siper alma sistemi var. Patlayan, yakan, sersemleten ve yapışan bombalar gibi çeşitli bombalarınız var. Siperden kör ateş edebiliyorsunuz. Helikopter ve trenden oluşan aksiyon sahneleriniz var. Ayrıyetten Caps Lock tuşuna basıp silahınıza susturucu takabilir, silahınızı ayaklar üzerine oturtup turret yapabilir, dikkat çekebilir ya da bir hologram oluşturup rakibi kandırabilirsiniz. Açıkçası en çok susturucu ve turreti kullandım. Diğerlerine pek ihtiyaç duymadım. 

Son olarak kendine has mekanikleri ve saf aksiyonuyla - ve bayıldığım 2000'lerden fırlamasıyla - kalbimi çalan bir yapım oldu. Hikayesi ilginç ama işlenişi zayıf olsa da bence mutlaka denemelisiniz. Old but gold 7/10

Носимая винтовка по мере прохождения превращается в дробовик, ракетницу и прочее - нужно только подбирать из павших врагов / особых объектов окружения "исследовательский опыт". С него же аптечки и расходники производятся на бегу, а также осуществляется прокачка инвентаря.
Здоровье частично самовосстанавливается, если некоторое время не получать урона.

Сама движуха-пострелуха часто разбавляется стэлсом, зенитками, рельсовым шутером.
Подкрадывания за спину - есть, рукопашки в лицо - нет!
Автоперезарядка часто портит всё правое дело в особо потных моментах.
Битвы с боссами, считайте, что отсутствуют (две обычные снайперские дуэли, простая укладка, расправа в видеоролике) - а все предпосылки к ним есть!
Прохождение занимает 5.5 часов, если к середине перестать пылесосить карты на опыт, которого и так навалом.
Присутствует и крошильный мультиплеер, в который теперь уже не поиграть из-за закрытия GameSpy, но есть возможность запустить его "оффлайн".
Также можно заглянуть в местную энциклопедию всячины с картинками и описаниями, привязанными к количеству полученного опыта.

Un éditeur qui préfère enterrer ses licences plutôt que de les faire vivre.

EA continue de démontrer ce qui ne va pas dans l'industrie du jeu vidéo : des studios talentueux sont sacrifiés, des équipes qui ont consacré des années à créer des univers et des licences appréciés par des millions de joueurs sont démantelées, et des franchises entières finissent abandonnées.

BioWare fait partie de ces studios qui ont marqué l'histoire du jeu vidéo. Mass Effect, Dragon Age… Des univers, des personnages et des histoires qui ont profondément marqué toute une génération de joueurs. Et derrière ces jeux, il y avait des développeurs passionnés, dont le travail mérite mieux que d'être traité comme des pièces jetables.

Le plus enrageant dans tout ça, c'est cette logique qui consiste à laisser mourir des licences plutôt que de leur donner une nouvelle chance. Si EA ne souhaite plus investir dans certaines franchises, pourquoi ne pas simplement les vendre ou en céder les droits à des studios qui seraient prêts à les faire vivre ? Pourquoi préférer les laisser prendre la poussière plutôt que de permettre à d'autres développeurs de reprendre le flambeau ?

Pour ma part, j'ai décidé de ne plus soutenir cette politique. Je vais donc mettre un avis négatif aux jeux édités par EA sur Steam, non pas nécessairement parce que ces jeux sont mauvais mais parce que je refuse de soutenir EA de quelque manière que ce soit. Bien entendu, plus aucun jeux édités par eux ne sera acheté de ma part également, c'est un peu dommage car certains m'intéressaient mais tant pis.

Adieu EA donc, puisse la licence Mass Effect revenir un jour

Jade Empire is probably the weirdest RPG BioWare has made (MDK2 still takes the cake for oddest game by them), It's oddly charming in a way which is likely due to it's vivid art style, As a big fan of Wuxia, Xianxia and Murim entertainment Jade Empire still manages to hit a good amount of the feelings each of those genres give whilst still being its own thing, Jade Empire builds off Chinese Mythology very well and nothing showcases that more than its wonderful main story, The Companions are a delight which shockingly good voice acting.

Combat Wise Jade Empire delivers on that front as well, It's a blast to toy around with the different styles, One major issue with combat is how unbalanced it is, Some styles are completely overpowered (Leaping Tiger) compared to the others and do in fact make the game a cake walk, I found most styles to be fun though so this wasn't an issue i couldn't fix myself by just enjoying a different style.

Sadly this game does suffer from what a lot of older games on steam also suffer from: Not Working Immediately, You will likely have to fiddle around with it and there is a plethora of guides on the steam community tab on how to fix it! (10 Minutes Top is my estimate) There is also GOG which likely serves it up without any issues at all.

I would recommend checking out the mods for it, They may not be extensive but they are solid and do enhance the experience quite well.

Overall Jade Empire is a great BioWare game that suffered from a poorly timed launch onto Xbox quite literally right before the 360 came out, I truly believe if it released on Xbox 360 instead of the Xbox we would of had a Mass Effect or Dragon Age level series, One of my personal biggest "Gaming What Ifs".

RIP BioWare & Ty for all the good times, Lets hope the IPs get sold to someone better than EA.

5/10 Je ne veux pas être méchant mais c'est un jeu très mid, qui cible sans doute un public enfantin au vu des dialogues. L'histoire est pas mal, sans qu'elle soit à elle même un argument pour l'achat de ce jeu. 

Pourquoi je ne recommande pas ?
1) D'abord le jeu crash, il faut faire quelques manipulations pour pouvoir y jouer. Ensuite c'est un vieux jeu et les combats, qui pourraient être pas mal, sont atrocement frustrants. Se déplacer est une horreur. C'est donc très lent alors que c'est fait pour être rapide. 

2) Les dialogues sont ... miévreux ou totalement bêtes. L'humour marche vraiment bien quand on a moins de 16 ans, pas au dessus. Et le problème c'est qu'il y a énormément de dialogues. Ils n'en finissent pas de parler alors que la situation exige de la rapidité. Et cette surabondance de dialogue gâche tout, car ils ne sont pas bien fait. On est censé avoir des choix, mais très souvent les options que l'on a sont artificielles, ne changent rien, et parfois chaque option est totalement idiot. Je me suis retrouvé de nombreuses fois à choisir par défaut parmi des extraits qui n'avaient aucun sens dans la situation donnée. Bref j'ai détesté. 

3) c'est un vieux jeu d'accord mais .... POURQUOI LES PNJ SE RESSEMBLENT TOUS ???? C'EST CAR ILS SONT CHINOIS ? c'est totalement débile. On a des personnages importants pour les quêtes, puis dans une autre quête on retrouve un perso avec la même tête et la même doublure, mais qui porte un nom différent. C'est hyper destabilisant je ne comprends pas.

Avec tous les jeux qui sont disponibles, je crois que jouer à Jade Empire n'est absolument pas un bon choix, à part pour des nostalgiques. Mais au moins l'histoire est assez courte à terminer. Je l'ai fini en 23 h et en plus j'ai quand même essayé de prendre mon temps.

The BioWare big three on the original Xbox were KOTOR, KOTOR II, and Jade Empire. BioWare had already won me over with KOTOR, so when I saw the same company release this game back in the day, it was an instant buy. I didn’t regret it at all.

For its time, Jade Empire was incredible. The fighting is simple, but still has a learning curve, and it felt fairly interactive compared to a lot of RPGs from that era. Your character is flipping around to dodge attacks, switching between multiple fighting styles, and learning new techniques as you go. Finding and mastering different styles was a huge part of the fun, and I’m happy to say that even in 2026, the combat still holds up. Sure, there are more refined games these days, but this is still a solid play.

The world also still looks good for its age. The environments have a lot of personality, and the story is still very entertaining to unravel. BioWare did a great job with the lore here. I found myself reading every book, scroll, and scrap of paper I came across. It’s a classic good vs. evil story mixed with Asian mythology, and it has that old BioWare charm that made their games so easy to get lost in.

Steam Deck performance is perfect. I didn’t need to rebind the controller, and the game runs great on max settings without any issues.

If you’ve been on the fence about buying this one, grab it during the next sale and wait no more. Get ready to relive the good old days of BioWare with this masterpiece.

[quote][b]Action-RPG воссозданная в антураже Древнего Китая, где Вам предстоит пройти путь от простого ученика боевых искусств до героя спасающего целую цивилизацию. Имеет в себе: атмосферные локации, глубокий саундтрек, множество разносторонних сюжетных линий (помимо основной) и объемную вариативность совершенствования вашего персонажа.

Проект, гармонично переплетающий мифологию и мистику, что позволяет погрузиться в атмосферу древних легенд.[/b][/quote]

[h2]Сюжет[/h2]

Повествование начинается в отдаленной тихой деревне, в школе боевых искусств нашего протагониста, где долгие годы, изо дня в день совершенствуются будущие защитники своего дома и империи в целом.
Но, в силу обстоятельств, гармоничная жизнь "храма" и его учеников нарушается. Деревня была атакована, а заведующий школой [b]Мастер Ли[/b] похищен.
С этого момента начинается обширное путешествие, целью которого становится найти пропавшего учителя и восстановить мир во всем мире, ведь это окажется не обычным похищением, а более глобальной угрозой. Попутно, персонажам предстоит раскрыть тайны своего происхождения и предназначения.

[h2]Геймплей[/h2]

По канонам уважающей себя [b]RPG[/b], нас ожидает выбор "школы" персонажа и его пол:
[list]
[*][b]Нейтральный[/b]
[*][b]Боец[/b]
[*][b]Маг[/b]
[*][b]Ловкач[/b]
[/list]

У каждого из классов, помимо индивидуального распределения шкалы [b]здоровья[/b], [b]маны[/b] и [b]концентрации[/b], есть свой особенный [b]боевой стиль[/b].

Также, на протяжении вашего пути, вам будет встречаться множество моральных выборов, которые будут влиять на ваш путь: "[b]открытая ладонь[/b]" или "[b]сжатый кулак[/b]" (соответственно аналог "добра" и "зла"). Что в свою очередь может повлиять на развитие способностей вашего персонажа в определенную сторону и концовку игры в целом.

Боевая система получилась не самой удачной, но приноровиться на протяжении путешествия возможно. Проходя проект на высокой сложности, приходится вдоль и поперек изучать все боевые стили и механики игры, ведь здесь не дают даже малейшего шанса на ошибку. Одно неверное движение и ваше путешествие будет окончено. А на те самые боевые вариации здесь не поскупились, ведь под конкретный класс оппонентов может не подойти ваш любимый и привычный метод. Поэтому предстоит изучать их и комбинировать в процессе боя.

Может порадовать то, что путешествовать вам предстоит не в одиночку, ведь вас будет сопровождать команда ваших товарищей, большинство из которых вы обретете в процессе выполнения ваших целей. С ними можно побеседовать, получить советы в определенные важные сюжетные моменты и в бою не оставят вас на растерзание врагам. Но, верного спутника можно выбрать лишь [b]одного[/b], остальные будут ожидать в вашем лагере.

Также, хотелось бы упомянуть, что здесь абсурдно [u]огромное[/u] количество диалогов. Провести беседу можно с большинством населения встречающихся вами локаций и я бы даже сказал нужно, дабы не пропустить ничего важного.
Но беседы иногда становятся излишне затянутыми, да и реплики нашего главного героя часто повторяются.

В остальном предстоит: изучать обширные локации, открывать множество сундуков с важными и не очень предметами внутри, читать [b]книги и свитки[/b], делать ответственные [b]выборы[/b], а также выполнять тонны дополнительных поручений.
Благо все эти поручения - это отдельные драматичные сюжетные истории, которые не ударяют лицом в грязь перед основным повествованием. 

Хронометраж - около [b]30[/b] часов

[h2]Атмосфера[/h2]

Колоритный [b]Древний Китай[/b], на этом уже можно было бы закончить описание.
Радует то, что это не просто "сухие" декорации - это дань уважения эпохе того времени и местности.
На пути вы встретите множество элементов, которые будут активно погружать вас в эти времена, например: тематические локации; внешний вид населения и их манера речи; книги, в которых описаны истории городов и выдающихся личностей, которые сделали свой вклад в развитие - науки, технологий, общества и культуры.

Вас ожидает [b]3[/b] основные атмосферные локации:
[list]
[*][b]Две Реки[/b] - та самая отдаленная тихая деревня 
[*][b]Стоянка Тяна[/b] - крупная портовая деревня омывающаяся живописной рекой 
[*][b]Имперский город[/b] - древний мегаполис, культурное сердце [b]Нефритовой империи[/b].
[/list]

На каждой из локаций вам предстоит провести около десяти часов, изучить инфраструктуру и познакомиться с населением. Хотите или нет, но придется погрузиться в проблемы каждого населенного пункта и пережить уникальные сюжетные линии отдельных граждан. И каждый раз, продолжая идти вперед, покидая очередную деревню - ощущение будто уезжаешь из родного города, так уж привыкаешь ко всему и проникаешься историей местности.

И конечно же саундтрек, который гармонично дополняет [b]Восточную атмосферу[/b] и оставляет бриз теплых воспоминаний. Даже стартовый трек из главного меню задает тон масштабного мифического приключения - услышав который ты понимаешь, что ты вернулся домой, в [b]Нефритовую Империю[/b].  

[h2]По итогу[/h2]

Атмосферное Восточное приключение о боевых искусствах, перекликающееся с [b]мифологией[/b] и [b]мистикой[/b] Древнего Китая. Погружающее вас в объемный, запутанный сюжет с множеством неожиданных поворотов, расследований и поисков себя.
Проект может похвастаться гибкой боевой системой, обширным количеством диалогов и квестов, а также колоритными локациями. Останется теплым воспоминанием о том, как в один прекрасный день удалось сдуть пыль с '[b]нефритового[/b]" камня и окунуться в его величественную "[b]Империю[/b]".

C'è un periodo preciso della storia dei videogiochi in cui BioWare non ne sbagliava letteralmente una. In mezzo a giganti colossali come Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic e il primo Mass Effect, c'è questo titolo del 2005 (poi arrivato su PC e altre piattaforme con la Special Edition) che viene regolarmente e ingiustamente dimenticato:
Jade Empire.

​Ogni volta che ci ripenso mi sale un po' di amarezza, perché parliamo di un vero e proprio gioiello grezzo.
L'ho ripreso in mano di recente per una run e volevo buttare giù qualche pensiero a caldo, perché è un gioco che merita davvero di essere sviscerato, nel bene e nel male.

​Il fascino dell'Impero (Punti di Forza)

​Partiamo da quello che ti cattura nei primi dieci minuti: l'ambientazione. Qui siamo immersi in una Cina mitologica, un mondo wuxia fatto di monaci guerrieri, spiriti inquieti, demoni volpe e imperatori corrotti. L'atmosfera è densa, colorata, quasi palpabile. Mettici sopra la colonna sonora clamorosa di Jack Wall (che usa strumenti tradizionali asiatici in modo magistrale).

​Poi c'è la scrittura. C'è tutta la magia della vecchia guardia di BioWare qui dentro:
​I compagni di viaggio: Non sono semplici "spalle" o portaborse. 
Da stella dell'alba alla Volpe di Seta, passando per il cinico Sagace Zu, ogni personaggio ha un background sfaccettato e motivazioni credibili. 
E non dimentichiamo il geniale cameo di John Cleese nei panni di Sir Roderick Ponce von Fontlebottom, una parodia dell'esploratore colonialista britannico che da sola vale l'intero gioco.

​La filosofia morale: 
Qui il sistema di allineamento si basa sulla Via del Palmo Aperto (armonia, equilibrio, vivere nel flusso della natura e aiutare gli altri) e la Via del Pugno Chiuso (autosufficienza, il forte domina sul debole, il caos come motore del cambiamento). 
È vero, a volte il gioco semplifica tutto facendolo ricadere nel classico "eroe vs stronzo", ma concettualmente è un sistema molto più stimolante e adulto rispetto ai soliti GDR.

​La trama: Senza fare spoiler per chi non l'ha mai toccato, ha un bel plot twist e comunque raccontata molto bene.

​Dove la magia si inceppa (Punti di Debolezza)
​Non posso e non voglio fare finta che sia un titolo perfetto, perché i difetti ci sono e si sentono eccome.
​Il problema più grande e divisivo è il combat system. Sulla carta, l'idea di scambiare al volo stili di arti marziali, armi bianche, magie, stili di paralisi e trasformazioni in mostri è fighissima. Nella pratica? Si riduce molto presto a un button mashing un po' confusionario. È legnoso, le collisioni spesso fanno i capricci e la telecamera ogni tanto decide di incastrarsi negli angoli.

Il bilanciamento poi è totalmente sballato: trovi un paio di stili che fanno danni spropositati (come il Salto della Rana o lo stile del Serpente, aggiunto proprio nella Special Edition) e, una volta potenziati quelli, puoi letteralmente asfaltare il gioco ignorando il 90% del resto dell'arsenale che ti sei sudato per sbloccare. ( senza parlare del golem di Giada)

​Un altro scoglio è la linearità. Se venivi dai mondi di KOTOR, l'Impero di Giada ti sembrava un "corridoio decorato". 
Le mappe sono splendide da guardare, ma offrono pochissima libertà di esplorazione, quasi zero verticalità e percorsi molto guidati.
Infine, la longevità: per gli standard dei GDR di quel periodo, la campagna principale scorre via fin troppo in fretta. Siamo sulle 15-20 ore di gioco se non ti perdi troppo in chiacchiere.

​Il senso della "Special Edition"

​La versione Special Edition arrivò originariamente su PC per sistemare un po' di cose rispetto alla release originale Xbox. Aggiunse nuovi stili di combattimento (come l'ottimo Palmo di Ferro), un paio di armi nuove e, in teoria, un'IA nemica leggermente più reattiva ai livelli di difficoltà alti, oltre alle risoluzioni grafiche migliorate.
Ha trasformato il gioco? No. Il feeling legnoso dei combattimenti è rimasto intatto. È semplicemente la versione definitiva e più comoda per giocarlo oggi, tutto qua.

​Tirando le somme
​Jade Empire: Special Edition è quello che definirei un capolavoro imperfetto. Se oggi ti approcci a questo gioco cercando un action-GDR dal gameplay tecnico, profondo e appagante, rimarrai inevitabilmente deluso.
​Ma se riesci a chiudere un occhio sulle meccaniche invecchiate male, troverai una storia che ti prende allo stomaco, un'ambientazione rarissima da incontrare nei videogiochi occidentali e dei dialoghi scritti bene. 

È un viaggio incredibile, uno di quelli che ti lasciano addosso una strana nostalgia.

First played this game when it came out in the early 2000s. Loved it, put hours into it. Got again on Steam recently and once again loving it.

Let's start with the bad, what little there is - the game is over 20 years old. By today's standards it may come across as clunky. The graphics are... well... early 2000s. Not bad for Early 200s and still better than some stuff that comes out today - but still, early 2000s

Now the good: The game was made during Bioware's early golden age and people who played other Bioware games from that era (specifically, SW: KOTOR and SW: KOTOR II) will feel very familiar with both gameplay and appearance. The game melds martial arts and mild magic in the combat mechanics which are real-time. 

The best thing about the game is the story. Bioware had always been able to craft an RPG with a deep, immersive story and Jade Empire is no different. Set in a fictional empire clearly based on the history and mythology of ancient China, you will discover a rich, storied world with breathtaking plots, twists and turns. Your character, a gifted martial arts student raised by a wise old master. discovers that the world itself is in peril. The ghosts of the dead cannot find rest and the cause is no other than the emperor himself, who in his vanity and arrogance, upset the cosmic balance. When the emperor's lackeys kidnap the wise master, it is up to the student to rescue the old man and restore the cosmic balance in an exhilarating tale full of Bioware's trademark twists and turns that leave the player in open-mouthed shock time and time again.

Final verdict: If you liked KOTOR, play it. If you like fast-paced action with little in the way of real story - skip

如果输入密钥发生错误，无法升级至联合版本解决办法：
1. 打开 Windows 设置，搜索并打开 Internet 选项；
2. 切换到「高级」选项卡，下滑找到安全分类；
3. 勾选启用所有 使用 TLS 相关选项，包括 TLS 1.0、TLS 1.1（标注为实验性的 TLS 版本除外）；
4. 取消勾选 检查发行商的证书是否已吊销；
5.完成密钥注册、成功登录游戏。
之后再次打开 Internet 选项，点击「重置」，将网络设置恢复为系统默认状态。

*Runaway* is one of those games where I realized far too late just how terrible it actually is. I can name exactly one thing the game does well: the backgrounds for the individual scenes (excluding, of course, the dreadful 3D-animated characters) which were drawn with great detail and care.

But aside from that? Phew... 
Let’s start with the plot, which is far-fetched and dreadfully clichéd. A guy hits a good-looking woman with his car and then helps her; simply because she’s good-looking. That’s the only reason. He even says as much, out loud, to the camera. Charming, right? He stumbles from one disastrous situation to the next- which wouldn’t be so bad if he were at least somewhat interesting (I’m not even asking for him to be likable). But this guy is just incredibly unlikable. He murders, steals, and lies whenever he can, for no apparent reason.
His sidekick, Gina? She stumbles from one "damsel in distress" scenario to the next (sometimes she’s being kidnapped, other times she’s falling into caves) constantly in need of help and begging our protagonist to take her along and like her. Meanwhile, in every single scene, she wears a different outfit that presents her in a highly sexualized way.

The 3D-animated characters do not blend well with the 2D look of the background, and the dreadfully long, banal cutscenes ( which cannot be skipped or shortened are an ordeal.
Then there’s a whole range of NPCs) all of them eccentric, completely over-the-top, and rather garish. None of them have any depth, and many only appear briefly, but I suppose they’re still passably okay. The game's voice acting (in English) is pretty decent.

But the worst part is the game’s puzzles, which not only require you to meticulously scan the screen for blurry pixels, but are also completely illogical. Examples:

1) In one cutscene, a secret is revealed—a mystery that has been a central focus for much of the game. We arrive in an old area, one we’ve already spent a great deal of time exploring, with no real objective other than to figure out what the object given to us by another character actually is.
And THEN, the game expects you to use a specific mechanic in a location that had already been completely solved—tinkering with a "steam lock"—just so that, somehow, a sheriff’s star pops out?!

Example 2, right at the beginning of the game: We’re in the hospital, standing next to Gina’s bed while she sleeps. We know that some gangsters are after her, but our protagonist is convinced that she’s just exaggerating and having nightmares.
The game expects us not only to climb into the neighboring room for no apparent reason (maneuvering along a thin balustrade outside a 10th-story window) but also to search a pitch-black room for items, all to... do what, exactly? It’s never made clear; in the end, we just set everything on fire and roust Gina out of bed. Nothing is explained here, even simple storylines have to be guessed, and I  needed a guide right at the start just to figure out what the game’s objective was.

Another aspect often overlooked in other reviews is the overt racism present in this game. At certain points, the player encounters the Hopi(an Indigenous people of the Americas) who are portrayed as eccentric, delusional, mystical shamans on the verge of extinction. In reality, however, the Hopi people are very much alive and thriving in the United States; they are not "delusional" at all, but simply ordinary human beings.

Sexism, Racism, Illogical puzzles and clichés: the game offers a fine selection of terrible themes.

To top it off, the game crashed 20 minutes before the end; since there are no autosaves, I would have had to replay the entire final chapter, so I opted to watch a YouTube video instead.

Please do not buy this game, it’s not just ugly on the outside, but on the inside, too.

[H1][b]ANÁLISIS DE [i]RUNAWAY: A ROAD TO ADVENTURE[/i][/b][/H1]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2859508183

Lanzado en el año 2001 por el estudio madrileño Pendulo Studios (que desgraciadamente echó el cierre en 2025), Runaway: A Road to Adventure supuso el resurgir internacional de las aventuras gráficas point & click en una época donde el género parecía casi olvidado. En principio fue editado por la mítica y también extinta Dinamic Multimedia, pero el cierre de esta distribuidora dejó a Runaway en el limbo durante dos años, hasta que FX Interactive acudió al rescate para publicarlo por todo lo alto. Hoy en día es considerado uno de los mejores videojuegos españoles de todos los tiempos y con toda la razón. Vamos a analizarlo por partes:

[H1]Argumento:[/H1]

La historia nos pone en la piel de Brian Basco, un brillante estudiante universitario que está a punto de mudarse a California para comenzar sus estudios de doctorado. Sin embargo, su vida da un giro radical cuando atropella accidentalmente a Gina Timmins, una joven que huye desesperadamente de la mafia tras presenciar un asesinato. La trama atrapa desde el primer minuto gracias a un argumento con un ritmo excelente, diálogos geniales y constantes toques de humor, todo ello respaldado por personajes llenos de carisma, un conjunto que hará que el jugador mantenga el interés de principio a fin. Desgraciadamente la versión de Steam está completamente en inglés (algo surrealista siendo un juego desarrollado en España), pero por suerte tenemos la posibilidad de ponerlo en español haciendo uso de la guía que os comparto arriba (voces y textos), siendo además un doblaje de una calidad sobresaliente.

[H1]Jugabilidad:[/H1]

A nivel jugable es una aventura gráfica de estilo clásico. Encantará a los amantes de las aventuras gráficas tradicionales, siendo muy accesible y fácil de manejar con el ratón, con un manejo muy intuitivo.

En su contra hay que decir que arrastra ciertos defectos propios de la época. Es un juego donde resulta fácil quedarse atascado: en ocasiones la detección de ítems es demasiado exigente, haciendo que cueste horrores encontrar determinados objetos en el escenario (el típico problema de pixel hunting de aquellos años), o bien Brian se negará a recoger o interactuar con algo hasta no haber activado un diálogo previo específico.

No es una aventura gráfica excesivamente difícil, pero sí hay partes en las que puedes quedar atascado y en esta entrega no se incluyó ningún sistema de pistas (cosa que solucionaron a partir de la 2ª entrega), algo que se echa en falta en ocasiones. Por suerte, siempre dispondremos de guías para ayudarnos a avanzar.

[H1]Gráficos:[/H1]

En el apartado visual, Runaway destacó en su época por conseguir encontrar un equilibrio perfecto entre lo tradicional y la innovación. En lugar de dar el salto al 3D completo (algo que seguramente le hubiera hecho envejecer mal siendo un juego de 2001), Pendulo Studios optó por un enfoque mixto novedoso: mezclar fondos 2D dibujados a mano por ilustradores de animación profesional con un gran nivel de detalle y un estilo de dibujo animado / cómic que ha envejecido genial, con personajes 3D estilo cel-shading renderizados en tiempo real, integrándose bien en los fondos bidimensionales sin romper la coherencia artística.

En su contra, he de decir que aunque la estética tipo cómic de los escenarios aguanta el tipo bastante bien, los modelados y las animaciones 3D de los personajes han envejecido mucho peor, resultando algo toscas, rígidas o "acartonadas" al moverse por el escenario.

Esta versión de Steam suele dar varios problemas técnicos como los comentados anteriormente, además de un bug que nos impide seleccionar el modo de alta resolución en la mayoría de tarjetas gráficas y monitores actuales, obligando a jugar en la resolución básica, algo que también podéis solucionar fácilmente siguiendo la guía.

[H1]Sonido:[/H1]
En el aspecto sonoro, Runaway destacó en su momento como una de las producciones más ambiciosas y cuidadas de la industria española, logrando una ambientación con un empaque digno de una superproducción de Hollywood. 

Su gran banda sonora, de David García-Morales Inés, acompaña el ritmo de la aventura aportando ese tono fresco, pop-rock y desenfadado tan característico de la obra. Todo ello se complementa con un diseño de efectos de sonido muy detallado y un doblaje al español de nivel cinematográfico, donde actores profesionales de primer orden otorgaron un carisma desbordante a cada uno de los personajes. 

Lamentablemente, la versión que lanzaron en Steam no incluye de serie las voces en español, algo que me parece surrealista y especialmente grave tratándose de un título desarrollado en España con uno de los doblajes más icónicos de nuestro país. Por suerte podemos solucionarlo también haciendo uso de la guía que os comparto arriba.

También hay que añadir que el audio de las voces tiene un pequeño bug con compresiones irregulares, provocando que en ocasiones suenen frases con una diferencia de volumen o calidad notable respecto a otras.

A modo de resumen, mi lista de pros y contras:

[H1][b]PROS:[/b][/H1]

✅ Uno de los mejores videojuegos jamás creados en España

✅ La estética combinando escenarios 2D con modelados 3D estilo cel-shading

✅ Encantará a los amantes de las aventuras gráficas clásicas

✅ Argumento muy entretenido y bien construido

✅ Gran cantidad de toques de humor bien integrados

✅ Diálogos fantásticos y muy bien redactados

✅ Personajes muy carismáticos

✅ Se puede conseguir a muy buen precio de oferta en Steam

[H1][b]CONTRAS:[/b][/H1]

❌ Resulta incomprensible que la versión de Steam no incluya de serie las voces en español siendo un juego 100% hecho en España

❌ Es fácil quedarse atascado por la rigidez de algunos puzles, se echa en falta un sistema de ayuda con pistas

❌ A veces resulta muy complicado encontrar determinados objetos en el escenario (pixel hunting)

❌ Actualmente da problemas de compatibilidad en ordenadores actuales, por suerte se puede solucionar

❌ Los modelados 3D de los personajes y sus animaciones han envejecido algo mal 

❌ Descompensación en cuanto a la diferencia de calidad de audio en ciertas frases del juego

❌ Carece de funciones de Steam: sin logros, sin cromos ni artículos en la tienda de puntos

[H1]Conclusión:[/H1]

Runaway: A Road to Adventure sigue siendo una obra de culto y una pieza fundamental del videojuego español que cualquier fan de las aventuras gráficas clásicas gozará enormemente, ya que su historia, humor y personajes lo hacen muy disfrutable aún a día de hoy. 

No obstante, la versión que lanzaron en Steam es bastante perezosa: llega con bugs gráficos, problemas de ejecución, sin añadidos de la plataforma y, lo más imperdonable, sin las voces en español de origen. Si decides comprarlo (recomendable especialmente de oferta), se hace imprescindible hacer uso de la guía para arreglar sus problemas y poder así disfrutarlo en nuestro idioma como se merece.
