[i]Another one of my nostalgia trips.

This game is really old. And when I mean old, I mean really, really old. You can see that and feel it everywhere in the game. These days, it really feels like some very interesting and unique indie project. But back in the day, this game was a gem. It was revolutionary in many of the things it did, and for that alone, it would deserve huge praise and a great review.

However, I'm not rating it based on nostalgia, just as I'm not doing with the other games. So let's be fair here.

The game has a lot of positives and negatives. The biggest negatives are the playability, which is not really great, and some mechanics that are hard to understand because we're used to something completely different today. The controls are also difficult to work with, but once you get used to them, they're fine.

One thing that actually aged surprisingly well is the pixelated graphics and their stylization. They still look good even today. And this is a good example of how avoiding hyper-realistic graphics can sometimes be a huge boon for a game's longevity. 

When you look at the game outside of the box of what we expect from games today, it's very unique and well done. The management is very straightforward abut honestly the gameplay in strategic view (on the globe) is not the strongest part of the game. Far from it actually.

But where the game really shines is the tactical combat.

When you land on the ground and fight the aliens, the simple mechanics and AI doesn't really matter. The game just works as Tod Howard would say. The maps could be better designed of course, and there might be more interesting mechanics then just shooting and shooting wile kneeling or throwing a grenade, perhaps some line of sight improvements, but somehow, it all comes together as enjoyable gameplay. You just want to keep playing, continue progressing, hating that your favourite soldiers died and enjoy the game until you reach the end.

And you can have a really good time even today with this super old game. If you think a little outside of the box, give it some leeway because it's really old, and think of it as an indie project, you can still have an amazing experience.

Yeah, I understand that a lot of new players, especially someone who has never played this game, will have a harder time. You will struggle. I might actually recommend watching some YouTube playthroughs first. There are plenty of them.

Then just give it a try.

It's a really great game.[/i]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
X-COM: UFO Defense es el “manual de supervivencia” definitivo para cualquiera que crea que la estrategia por turnos es solo mover soldaditos bonitos y ver numeritos subir. Aquí diriges una organización secreta que investiga, administra y pelea contra una invasión extraterrestre, alternando entre construcción de bases (sí, contabilidad militar) y misiones tácticas isométricas donde un error se paga con funerales en masa.

La primera impresión es clara: esto viene de los 90 y no pide perdón. Es retro, atmosférico e implacable. No te guía, no te consiente y, si te emocionas, te castiga. Es un clásico porque se atreve a ser cruel y porque su mezcla de estrategia, administración y combate por turnos sigue siendo adictiva… aunque te deje con traumas tácticos.

[h2]Informe X-COM: Éxitos de Operación y Daños Colaterales[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
 Estrategia por turnos de la vieja escuela: tensa, táctica y con decisiones que importan   
 Construcción y administración de bases que te hace sentir comandante… y contador al mismo tiempo   
 Ambientación sci‑fi noventera: opresiva, misteriosa y sorprendentemente efectiva   
 Rejugabilidad alta: cada campaña se siente distinta y el juego es “adictivo” por diseño   
 Dificultad implacable: para quien disfruta sufrir con propósito   

Lo No Tan Bueno:
 Cero logros: Steam te mira y dice “¿y tu dopamina de checklist?”   
 Visuales retro/isométricos: encantadores para unos, “¿dónde están mis píxeles?” para otros   
 Es implacable de verdad: si vienes a relajarte, este juego te manda a terapia   
 Enfoque totalmente un jugador: si querías compartir el sufrimiento en co-op… pues no   
 Comunidad activa pequeña (35 jugadores): te tocará evangelizar solo en el chat mental

在上世纪90年代初，Gollop兄弟试图打造Laser Squad 2，最初只是一款等轴测视角、偏小规模双人战术游戏，但因为前作发行商合作糟糕，他们最终找到当时策略游戏巨头 MicroProse，彼时恰逢MircoProse发行的文明系列大火，MicroProse的开发主管认可游戏战术玩法，但提出关键修改意见：" 只做纯战术体量太小，希望能对标文明的宏大规模；增加全球战略管理层面内容，把舞台放在现代地球，X档案当时正火，不妨就采用 UFO 外星人入侵题材。"在大多时候，发行商强制干涉开发商往往会两败俱伤，可这次，恰恰是MicroProse的干预，使得X-COM最终成品的格局远超一款普通的回合制策略游戏。
游戏故事设定十分直白：世界各地 UFO 目击事件频发，外星人不断实施绑架与活体实验。全球各国达成合作，出资组建X-COM以对抗外星入侵，玩家作为最高负责人，任务就是拦截 UFO、肃清登陆的外星人部队，缴获外星装备与生物样本，以敌方科技反过来抵御入侵。剧情没有繁复的反转，核心冲突清晰，不过X-COM真正的魅力不在于剧本，而是一套完整的游戏循环。
游戏分为三大模块：全球战略经营、科研研发、回合制战术战斗，这三套玩法深度绑定，缺一不可，堪称天作之合，要知道维持设计逻辑全程统一是件极难实现的事。事实上绝大多数游戏，尤其是结构繁杂的现代大作，几乎都达不到这种水准，甚至根本没把设计自洽当作追求目标，比如辐射4，开发者试图保留RPG要素，又要引入经营建造，还要兼顾暗黑破坏神式的刷装备系统，结果硬是一样没做好，系统割裂明显，非但没有在前作成熟框架上精进，反倒在设计理念上不进反退，做出各种敷衍了事的折中取舍。 
考虑到大多数人接触的可能是2012年的重启之作，所以以下内容不可避免的会使用重启之作类比，整体上重启之作照搬了原版核心设计，但其中也有不小差别。比如原版中允许在全球战略视图中建造多个基地，你需要选定基地位置，修建营房实验室、工坊、机库等一众设施，调配资金、招募士兵与科研人员。财政系统是持续的压力来源，经费依靠各国政府根据你的防御成效发放；一旦失利，资助额度会持续削减，极端情况下各国甚至会倒向外星人。你也可以变卖多余物资换取资金，合理规划收支、布局全球基地，是长久作战的基础。相比重启作中的单基地设计，初代X-COM是一个更为精致的模拟。
科研体系则是战力提升的核心。战场缴获的外星武器、飞行器残骸，又或是活捉的外星俘虏，都能交由科学家解析。解锁外星科技后，就能量产电浆武器之类的高级装备，弥补人类初始军备的巨大差距。科研进度直接决定战斗上限，被动拖延研究，面对越来越强大的外星部队只会节节败退。
战术战斗是本作最耀眼的核心，也是和重启之作中最大的区别。地面战斗采用经典回合制与时间单位（TU）机制。移动、射击、下蹲等行为全部消耗TU，不同射击模式消耗资源与命中率相互取舍；相比重启之作，初代的监视机制采用一套细腻的计算方式，你可以预留TU结束回合，伏击闯入视野的敌人，系统会通过一套数值计算是否触发反应射击。战场被战争迷雾笼罩，只有士兵视野范围内的地形才会显现，建筑、残骸中随时可能潜藏敌军，每一次探索都充满未知压迫感。外星种族种类繁多，应对不同敌人战术思路截然不同。任务类型丰富：调查 UFO 坠毁点、突袭外星基地、城市反恐救援平民、甚至抵御外星人发起的基地攻防战，基本上重启作里有的，都能在初代里找到。不过虽然说了初代相比重启之作的诸多优点，但不可否认重启之作里的职业系统是个不错的改进，相比之下初代的士兵间差异只采取不同的一套属性参数。
这可能是一部我唯一不想写缺点的游戏，因为X-COM近乎完美，它平衡宏观基地经营与微观回合战术，紧张压抑的氛围、层层解锁的科技树、生死难料的战场，将诸多要素融为一体，体验独特难以复刻。能挑剔的大多也只在于QOL这样的时代性问题，或是平衡性这样的细枝末节，何况现在民间社区开源的OpenXcom已经解决了不少过去的局限性，也是目前游玩X-COM的最佳方式，此外还有像X-COM Classic Remastered这样的平衡性修正模组到ROSIGMA这样的TC模组，每一个经典之作都值得有更优秀的传承和发展，这是玩家和作品本身共同造就的辉煌。

I know that the majority of people who are looking at this game in 2026 and beyond are likely vets who are revisiting a game they played in years past, so I wanted to give a new player's perspective to anyone who might be curious about that point of view. Simply put, as someone who is nearly a decade younger than the game, has never played it before, and has no emotional attachment to it, I was really impressed with how well it holds up. 

I was kind of intimidated at first, with all the various menus and tons of buttons on the battle ui and such, but it turns out its much simpler than it looks. Just start up the game, plop down your base, build some facilities, start your research and manufacturing, load up your soldiers and weapons onto your ship, and get to throwing smokes and shootin aliens. That's the core gameplay loop in a nutshell. You will want to cover more of the globe with radar and capture various aliens (build an alien containment facility!) for research projects as the game goes on. You can build more bases to focus on research or manufacturing (you can sell the stuff you manufacture or transfer it to other bases) if you would like. The tactical gameplay is surprisingly solid for a decades old game, different alien types do a good job actually feeling different to fight and not just like different stat blocks, the ufopedia entries are fun, and I honestly like the dated graphics. It's a very good game, and incredibly impressive for when it was made. The game comes with a manual, so if you wanna learn it the old fashioned way, feel free to do that, but I personally just played the game for a few hours and pulled up the wiki any time I was curious about how something works (for example, the accuracy system is a good thing to read about, as once you understand how it works, your soldiers hitting every shot in a point blank burst despite having only 30% accuracy makes a lot more sense).

Can't really go wrong for five dollars, even better if you grab it on sale for around a buck fifty. If you do pick it up, make sure to install openxcom (I recommend openxcom extended, but the nightly version is also fine) for better compatibility with modern systems, bugfixes, and quality of life changes. I learned after playing it for a while that you can get openxcom to work with steam by downloading the zip version instead of the installer, dropping the files into your steam game directory, renaming the old dosbox.exe to something else, renaming the openxcom executable to dosbox.exe, then pulling all the files from the "XCom UFO Defense\XCOM" folder (it will have GEODATA, GEOGRAPH, etc) into the new "XCom UFO Defense\UFO" folder you just created, and it will launch openxcom when you start the game through steam. If you go into video settings and turn on one of the display filters with a star next to the name (the star means it is using opengl) the shift+tab menu and stuff will start working. I like the Raw (not really a filter, its just the raw pixels but rendered in opengl), Pixellate, and Scale2X filters myself. I wish I had known this earlier because I have like 20 hours of untracked time :( There are also additional settings in the options menu and plenty of mods available that are super easy to install (just drag em into "Documents\OpenXcom\mods" and enable them in the game) so if you are looking to spice things up that's an option. I like a lot of the toggles, as well as the amiga font mod, statstrings mod, and final mod pack, but I would probably not mess with mods or advanced settings too much at least for your first couple hours playing the game. 

My final few pieces of advice to anyone who is trying this game for the first time is that, first, if you are afraid you are doing something wrong because a lot of your soldiers are dying, you are probably not doing as poorly as you think. The early game is kinda like that, so don't sweat it. Use smoke grenades, overwatch fire, and accept that you are going to be taking casualties pretty regularly until you start getting more upgrades and such. Secondly, don't be afraid to pack your soldiers up on the dropship and abort a mission, especially an early terror mission. And finally, make sure to buy flares and put them in your dropship!!!

If you decide to play this game for the first time so many years after its release, I hope you have as much fun as I did :)

This one was plenty of fun! Yeah, it's pretty different from the rest of XCOM, and if you go into it with that lens you might be disappointed. But if you just imagine it as a boomer shooter (as rantinan noted) and free yourself from preconceived notions it's not half bad. Starts off appropriately slow, but escalates appropriately (for the most part).

Environments were crazy nostalgic. Both for how they looked and what they represented (esp. that mall level, forgive me for being a Zoomer but it was hecking frutiger aero).

I did not like that several weapons are more or less useless in the last ten weapons and there was a bit of RNG involved in getting the right weapon (Mass Driver) to drop at the right time. If I played this a second time I wouldn't have even unlocked most weapons, it just makes the game harder because a less useful weapon is more likely to spawn when you really need something with stopping power.

Voice acting wasn't half bad. I even felt a little emotion at the end. And the final image was quite nice.

tl;dr fun for $6 (or less if you get bundled and on sale), plenty of adrenaline, not a bad way at all to spend a couple days

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
X-COM: Enforcer es ese “spin-off” que llega a la fiesta de la Estrategia con gabardina de Acción y se pone a disparar en tercera persona como si nadie se fuera a dar cuenta. En vez de la tensión táctica clásica, aquí controlas a un agente con juguetes futuristas para limpiar calles de extraterrestres, con un enfoque más directo y arcade.

La propuesta estratégica existe, pero más como “microdecisiones” de combate: elegir armas, gestionar recursos de combate y lidiar con oleadas. Si esperas el ajedrez brutal de X-COM tradicional, esto se siente más como damas… pero con plasma y paranoia. La primera impresión: ruidoso, rápido, y con esa vibra de ciencia ficción noventera que hoy se disfruta entre nostalgia y juicio.

[h2]Lo Humano (y lo Alien) de Este Enforcer[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
 Combina Estrategia ligera con Disparos en tercera persona para partidas más “cerebro apagado, dedo activo”   
 Ambientación sci‑fi con extraterrestres: cumple el fantasy de “soy la última línea de defensa”   
 Tiene modos Un jugador y Multijugador, por si alguien más quiere sufrir contigo   
 Va al grano: acción constante, ideal si no quieres menús eternos y cálculos de probabilidades   

Lo No Tan Bueno:
 Cero logros: Steam no te valida la existencia, aunque hayas salvado el planeta   
 Comunidad esencialmente fantasma: jugadores actuales 1… sí, UNO. Felicidades, eres el elegido   
 Identidad confusa: se vende por Estrategia, pero a ratos parece que le da pena serlo   
 Rejugabilidad limitada si buscas variedad moderna; aquí el “loop” manda y no pide permiso

Przynajmniej zagraj kilka poziomów, zanim ocenisz, czy jest do bani, czy nie. Może cię zaskoczyć.

X-COM: Enforcer, developed by MicroProse Software, Inc. and later published under the 2K label, represents one of the most striking departures in a long-running franchise’s history. Known primarily for its complex, turn-based strategy roots, the X-COM series built its identity on tactical depth, atmospheric tension, and global-scale alien warfare. Enforcer, however, strips away nearly all of that strategic DNA, trading careful planning for fast-paced shooting. Released in 2001, it transformed the series into a third-person action game powered by the Unreal Engine—an experiment that, while energetic, alienated much of its fanbase. Rather than commanding squads of soldiers, the player steps into the metallic shell of a lone robotic prototype known as the Enforcer, battling wave after wave of extraterrestrial enemies across a series of linear, combat-focused levels.

The premise is as straightforward as the gameplay: the Enforcer, an experimental combat android built by desperate human scientists, is Earth’s last defense against an overwhelming alien invasion. The story serves only as a frame for the action, unfolding through mission briefings and radio chatter rather than deep lore or strategy. Each level revolves around the same core loop—blast aliens, rescue hostages, and destroy alien portals to stop further waves from spawning. The environments range from city streets to laboratories and industrial complexes, but their structure remains similar: self-contained arenas filled with destructible objects, glowing pickups, and relentless hordes. The simplicity is deliberate, offering instant gratification in place of the slow, methodical pace of earlier X-COM titles. It feels like an arcade interpretation of the franchise—a distilled version that replaces intellect with instinct.

In terms of gameplay, Enforcer delivers a fast, chaotic experience that fits neatly within the early 2000s action-shooter mold. Players move through each map at breakneck speed, mowing down colorful alien swarms with an ever-growing arsenal of energy weapons. The addition of “data points,” collectible fragments that serve as a form of currency, allows the Enforcer to upgrade its gear and unlock new weapons between missions. This gives a small sense of progression, but it’s hardly enough to create long-term depth. The core shooting mechanics are competent, with responsive controls and the occasional set-piece to break monotony, but the repetition sets in quickly. Every mission begins to blur into the next—different backdrops, same alien hordes. There is little variation in objectives or enemy tactics, and the combat, while initially thrilling, lacks the strategic nuance or tension that once defined the X-COM name.

Visually, Enforcer captures a certain charm of its era but has aged unevenly. The Unreal Engine provides decent explosions, particle effects, and lighting for its time, but the environments often feel sterile and box-like. The alien designs are cartoonish and lack the grotesque mystery of the earlier games, and the environments reuse textures heavily. The technical performance, however, remains smooth even on older hardware, which was a strong point at release. The sound design leans heavily on bombastic energy—metallic weapon fire, heavy impacts, and a pulsing techno soundtrack that keeps the adrenaline high. While it succeeds in maintaining intensity, it also reinforces the sense that Enforcer is an arcade shooter at heart, rather than a science fiction strategy title reborn for the new millennium.

As a standalone experience, Enforcer can be entertaining in short bursts. It’s easy to pick up, simple to understand, and full of kinetic, mindless action. Yet this accessibility is also its limitation. The lack of depth, narrative complexity, or meaningful challenge quickly exposes the game’s narrow design. For a franchise built on methodical decision-making and emotional investment in soldiers and missions, this sudden pivot to a solo robot mowing down endless waves of enemies feels dissonant. It’s clear that Enforcer was an attempt to reach a wider audience at a time when the series was struggling commercially, but the result ended up pleasing neither traditional fans nor shooter enthusiasts who already had more sophisticated options on the market.

Looking back, X-COM: Enforcer stands as both a curiosity and a cautionary tale. It’s a snapshot of a time when studios experimented with familiar brands in unfamiliar genres, often with mixed results. The game itself isn’t terrible—it’s serviceable, competently built, and capable of providing a few hours of chaotic fun—but it is deeply forgettable, especially when compared to the lasting impact of the tactical originals. For long-time X-COM followers, it remains an odd misstep, one that pushed the franchise into obscurity for years until its eventual reboot brought the series back to its strategic roots. For newcomers who approach it without context, it’s a decent, if shallow, relic of early 2000s action design. X-COM: Enforcer ultimately serves as a reminder that not every series can—or should—abandon its identity in pursuit of accessibility, and that sometimes the most faithful path forward is the one that remembers what made the name matter in the first place.

I’ll start by saying that I was entertained for a while by this 2001 game, the last of the supposedly original X-COM series. However, as a devoted fan of the original titles, I found it hard to reconcile this game with the X-COM legacy. Unfortunately, it doesn’t capture the essence of the original series, making it difficult to recommend a game that bears the X-COM name yet strays so far from what made the originals special.

The differences are glaring—turn-based strategy vs. a third-person shooter format. It doesn’t feel like a continuation of the same story. If you want to experience the true X-COM spirit, I suggest sticking with X-COM: UFO Defense or X-COM: Terror from the Deep, and skipping the last three games in the series altogether. Of those three, X-COM: Enforcer is the most enjoyable, but I’d rate it a modest 5/10, especially considering its age.

As for the gameplay, it becomes quite repetitive over time. Additionally, some missions feature a sudden spike in difficulty that can be frustrating and hard to explain. I might play for a couple more hours when I’m out of other options, but I wouldn’t recommend purchasing this game unless it’s part of a bundle with the original titles

[b]Egzekutor[/b]
X-COM: Enforcer to trzecioosobowa "strzelanka", która mimo znanej marki przedstawia zupełnie inne podejście do radzenia sobie z nadciągającą kosmiczną zagładą. Oto Profesor tworzy jednostkę "Egzekutora", która samotnie, w trakcie swoich intensywnie ofensywnych działań będzie: pokonywać ogromne ilości obcych, niszczyć ich przekaźniki teleportacyjne, próbować przeżyć określony czas w trakcie zmasowanych natarć, ratować ludzi z miejsc konfliktu oraz chronić wskazane cele. Co jakiś czas sprawdzi się też w Bardziej Osobistych Starciach Specjalnych.
[b]Aktualizacja sprzętu[/b]
Jako Egzekutor prowadzimy działania terenowe pozbawieni wsparcia bezpośredniego - jako takie (w postaci "zrzutów" wspomagających Nasze działania) zapewnia Nam Profesor. "Zrzuty", czyli pojawiające się w Naszym zasięgu bronie i wzmocnienia, zależą jednak od postępów - każda lokacja skrywa pojedynczy pakiet informacji na temat obcej technologii. To przekłada się bezpośrednio na dostęp do nowych elementów Naszego arsenału (w sumie 12 różnych broni i 12 różnych wzmocnień). Zatem poza bronią podstawową (o nielimitowanej amunicji) będziemy mogli skorzystać z: wyrzutni ostrzy, miotacza ognia, strzelby, broni mrożącej, wyrzutni z napędem masowym (coilgun), karabinku fuzyjnego, wyrzutni granatów, wirującego ostrza (broń walki bezpośredniej), broni porażającej, wyrzutni rakiet, działka psionicznego i atomówki. Do wzmocnień pomagających w walce należą: pakiet naprawczy, wspomagacz doładowania, zwiększacz prędkości, intensyfikator obrażeń, system "Łazarz", zwielokratniacz punktów, generator fali bio-magnetycznej, maskowanie, nalot, pole statyczne, dron bojowy i uniewrażliwiacz. Każdy z tych elementów możemy ulepszyć kilkukrotnie, zwiększając ich użyteczność. Poza tym, między kolejnymi operacjami możemy ulepszyć samych siebie w zakresie: prędkości poruszania się, mocy odrzutów (skok), pojemności magazynków, systemów autonaprawczych, opancerzenia czy specjalnych dodatków Profesora. Jest tego dużo a co najważniejsze każde ulepszenie daje faktyczne odczucie wzrostu mocy.
[b]Koszt aktualizacji[/b]
Aby dokonać jakichkolwiek poprawek w Naszej zbrojowni, potrzebujemy odpowiednio dużo zasobów. Tu za walutę służą punkty, które dozowane są w zależności od rodzaju pokonywanych przeciwników. Problemem jest jednak to, że samo ich pokonanie nie wystarczy. Punkty wypadają bowiem z poległych najeźdźców rozsypując się wokoło a do tego możliwość ich zebrania jest mocno ograniczona czasowo. Dodatkowo część takich punktów ląduje w przepaściach czy po prostu z dala od Nas co w przypadku późniejszych etapów - gdzie zagęszczenie wrogów wzrasta i dochodzi próba unikania zmiany broni - ogranicza Nam możliwości swobodnego zbierania ich. Po prostu szkoda, że samo ubicie sektoida, żmija czy mutona nie zwiększa Naszej puli zasobów badawczych bo ostatecznie trudno jest rozwinąć wszystko "na maksa". Na pocieszenie warto zaznaczyć, że każda lokacja skrywa pięć "kluczy" pozwalających rozegrać po wykonaniu zadania etap B O N U S-owy. Stare dobre zbieranie pięciu literek poukrywanych w zakamarkach odwiedzanych miejsc sprawdza się tu znakomicie a do tego takich etapów jest kilka różnych i każdorazowo jest ono losowo dobieranym wydarzeniem - każde jednak pozwala Nam na znaczące podniesienie liczby punktów. Będąc odpowiednio dokładnym możemy uczestniczyć w takich B O N U S-ach jak: zbieranie punktów z ruchliwej autostrady (widok od góry), opróżnianie z punktów magazynu wypełnionego skrzyniami, zbieranie punktów w ringowej potyczce z mutonami, zdobywanie punktów w "Pac-Man'owy" sposób (widok od góry) czy ograbianie kosmicznego bunkra w którym podłoga się stopniowo zapada.
[b]Awaria oprogramowania[/b]
Zanim zacznę wspomnę tylko, że na dobry początek możemy wybrać jedną z wielu dostępnych skórek Naszego Egzekutora. Mimo że nie wpływa to w żaden sposób na rozgrywkę, to każdy element personalizacji jest jak najbardziej pozytywny. Co ciekawe w trakcie rozgrywki odblokujemy kolejne - wszystkie wyglądają ciekawie i mimo że nie zmieniają fizycznie Naszej postury to każda właściwie się odróżnia. Pierwszym co prawdopodobnie będzie Nam uwierać jest sterowanie a konkretnie celowanie za pomocą myszy. Niestety z jakiegoś powodu ruch góra-dół lata jak szalony podczas gdy ruchy na boki są tak jak trzeba - ja poradziłem sobie z tym problemem przypisując centrowanie celownika na drugi przycisk myszy. Problemów jest więcej ale np. już po kilku minutach gry możemy się zorientować że balans dźwięków w grze jest niewłaściwy. W ogólnym rozrachunku nie przeszkadza to aż tak bardzo bo często będzie to jednak miks wystrzałów, wybuchów i dźwięków związanych z podnoszeniem wzmocnień ale jednak przypomina to o sobie przy każdym włączeniu gry. Również już na wczesnych etapach zaczniemy kombinować czy warto jest podnosić broń czy nie bo pomysł na zarządzanie bronią (automatyczna zmiana przy kontakcie) budzi wątpliwości. Autozamiana jest w porządku gdy mamy w ręku broń podstawową ale gdy wokoło pojawiają się co chwilę nowe giwery a Nam zależy na utrzymaniu konkretnego sposobu radzenia sobie z przeciwnościami to już tak dobrze nie jest. Szkoda że niema możliwości wyłączenia z puli danego rodzaju broni (który Nam nie leży) albo że niema osobistej hierarchizacji pozwalającej rozbudować proces decyzyjny takiej zmiany. Pomijając etapy B O N U S-owe w jednej z misji większość czasu rozegramy z perspektywy innej kamery - ani to zza pleców ani od góry. Niby fajnie że coś innego ale jednak mocno ogranicza i tak niezbyt wygodne możliwości rozglądania się.
[b]Wynik[/b]
To na pewno nie jest "ten" X-COM. Mimo wykorzystania znanych przeciwników, którzy właściwie urozmaicają Nam zabawę stopniowo zwiększając poziom trudności, całość rozgrywki trudno powiązać ze znanym Nam formatem. A jednak to nie jest zła gra a nawet bym powiedział, że może być orzeźwiająca bo mimo że prosta w założeniach to oferuje sporo różnorodności, angażuje i jest pełna akcji a na koniec daje przyjemne odczucia. Na tle dzisiejszych gier, które przyciągają lepszą oprawą, X-COM: Enforcer zaskoczył mnie miło wysoką grywalnością.

[h1] Un zombie medio bizarro [/h1]

Stubbs the Zombie in Rebel Without a Pulse (nombre larguísimo) es un juego de acción en tercera persona que nos pone en la piel de un zombi en lugar de obligarnos a sobrevivir a uno. Ambientado en una ciudad retrofuturista inspirada en los años 50, nuestro objetivo es sembrar el caos, comer cerebros y convertir a la población en un ejército de zombies.

El concepto es muy bizarro, con humor negro, situaciones ridículas y una jugabilidad bizarra con distintas opciones para cumplir nuestro objetivo

[hr][/hr]

[h3] Cerebros para todos [/h3]

La principal mecánica del juego consiste en devorar los cerebros de los ciudadanos y enemigos para recuperar salud y habilidades, cada humano que matamos puede convertirse en un zombi que se suma a nuestra horda, creando gradualmente un caos en el escenario.

El juego tiene habilidades muy bizarras: tirarse pedos para aturdir enemigos, arrancarse órganos para usarlos de explosivos, arrancarse la cabeza y usarla como bola de boliche y desprenderse el brazo para controlar a otros humanos.

Esa última habilidad es la más interesante porque permite poseer enemigos y utilizar sus armas para matar a otros humanos desde sus propias filas. También hay vehículos manejables, enfrentamientos contra jefes y situaciones que rompen completamente el tono que uno podría esperar.

[hr][/hr]

[h3] Una ciudad sacada de otra época [/h3]

Punchbowl es una ciudad retrofuturista que mezcla la estética estadounidense de los años 50 con tecnología avanzada, autos voladores, robots y armas futuristas. El contraste le da una identidad visual bastante particular y acompaña perfectamente lo satírica que es la aventura.

La banda sonora también es uno de los puntos fuertes, tiene canciones clásicas de los años 50 interpretadas por bandas contemporáneas, una combinación que encaja muy bien con la ambientación, aunque la música realmente no tiene el protagonismo que debería.

La historia no es tan profunda, tiene un objetivo claro y un trasfondo mínimo, pero cumple decentemente

[hr][/hr]

[h3] No va muy allá [/h3]

El principal problema es que la jugabilidad se vuelve repetitiva después de las primeras horas. Y si, aunque las habilidades son originales, la mayoría de los enfrentamientos terminan girando alrededor de las mismas acciones: aturdir, atacar, devorar cerebros y seguir avanzando.

Los controles pueden sentirse algo toscos, avanzar por el escenario es intuitivo y los aliados zombis no destacan en inteligencia. La dificultad tiene algunos desequilibrios, con enfrentamientos que pueden pasar de ser demasiado sencillos a convertirse en un auténtico dolor de cabeza.

La campaña es corta, igualmente está bien ya que la jugabilidad puede volverse repetitiva luego de 2 niveles.

[hr][/hr]

[h3] ¿Vale la pena? [/h3]

Stubbs the Zombie tiene una propuesta bastante particular, que puede divertir por momentos dado el humor que maneja y a la posibilidad de infestar a todos siendo un zombie medio bizarro, pero también puede ser un juego repetitivo y algo sencillo si lo que estás buscando es algo un poco más complejo.

La verdad lo recomiendo en descuento. Sigue siendo un juego bastante interesante y único que destaca más por cómo se presenta que por la profundidad o el enganche de los que carece.

Stubbs is actually a hidden, even if unpolished Gem. 

I don't even remember where I got this, maybe from a bundle of keys, but at 95% off I think it's a more than fair price for what it offers. And what it offers is a adventure zombie/horde experience where you control a zombie and can convert enemies - though I'd argue it leans heavier into the adventure aspect where you go area to area completing story objectives. As a dabbling game dev, I was really impressed with the enemy AI. Different voice lines for different scenarios depending on the enemy types, dodging out of the way of vehicles, different movement patterns depending on what parts of the body were damaged (some zombies would even crawl towards enemies with only an arm left!). The zombies would gang up on enemies, when an enemy was overwhelmed they'd run away or try and regroup before pulling their weapon out again. Most enemies could be remotely controlled using another ability, and you had access to their normal weapons and movement. Other enemies would notice that, then start targeting you. I was really impressed with how well some of those systems worked. 

Some segments were definitely tedious, and some save points seemed to fail to activate (or activated when I went significantly past them on another life). Some of the humour was definitely of its time (early 2000s like the first ability you unlock) but I was caught offguard with how funny some of the other voicelines were. I didn't have any issues running the game on Win10 with a beefy PC, but some people are reporting issues, so that's worth keeping in mind too.  

Overall worth checking out, especially if you're interested in NPC AI or like the 'infect the town and flip them to your side' fantasy!

[i]Stubbs the Zombie: Rebel Without a Pulse[/i] is a wonderfully weird little game that deserves more attention. Running around eating brains, converting innocent townsfolk into your own undead army, and causing absolute chaos never really gets old. The humor is charmingly absurd, and the premise alone is enough to set it apart from the sea of generic zombie games where you're always the survivor.

Unfortunately, there were a few things that made my gameplay awkward and tedious. My laptop exceeds the recommended system requirements by a comfortable margin, yet the game simply refused to cooperate. (The game would freeze after 20-30 minutes of gameplay, forcing me to have to exit the game and reboot it constantly.) If you're using newer hardware, especially Intel Arc graphics or a recent Windows 11 machine, be prepared to do some troubleshooting.

Once you get it working, it's a blast. Just don't expect it to launch flawlessly on every modern PC. It's disappointing that a remastered release still has these quirks, but the gameplay itself is entertaining enough that I still recommend it. Just keep your expectations in check and be ready to spend a little time fixing things before you spend your time eating brains.

Death Track: Resurrection is a high-octane, arcade-style combat racing game developed by Sky Fallen and published by Fulqrum Publishing that attempts to resurrect a cult classic concept for a modern audience. Set in a dystopian near future where traditional motorsports have been replaced by deadly televised survival races, the game blends blistering speed with heavy vehicular combat, presenting a vision of racing as violent entertainment rather than pure competition. Its tone is unapologetically over-the-top, leaning into spectacle, aggression, and excess as defining features of its identity.

The game’s setting frames racing as a brutal sport staged in ruined, hyper-stylized versions of real-world cities. Tracks wind through futuristic interpretations of places like New York, Paris, Tokyo, London, and Moscow, often incorporating massive straightaways, sharp turns, destructible scenery, and environmental hazards. These locations are not merely backdrops but active components of each race, shaping how players approach speed, positioning, and combat. The sense of racing through collapsed infrastructure and neon-lit ruins reinforces the game’s dystopian atmosphere and helps distinguish it from more traditional racing titles.

Gameplay revolves around a constant tension between speed and survival. Winning is not simply about crossing the finish line first, but about managing boost, avoiding destruction, and eliminating rivals when necessary. Vehicles are equipped with a variety of offensive and defensive weapons, including machine guns, rockets, mines, and countermeasures that can be upgraded over time. These systems encourage aggressive playstyles, as neutralizing opponents often becomes just as important as mastering racing lines. Boost mechanics add another layer of risk, pushing cars to extreme speeds at the cost of control and stability.

Vehicle handling is intentionally arcade-focused, favoring responsiveness and spectacle over simulation accuracy. Cars feel fast and volatile, especially at higher speeds, which can make races exhilarating but also chaotic. Tight corners combined with heavy weapon fire often lead to crashes and sudden reversals of fortune, reinforcing the idea that Death Track: Resurrection is as much about controlled chaos as it is about precision driving. For some players, this unpredictability enhances the thrill; for others, it undermines consistency and mastery.

Progression is structured around multiple game modes that offer different types of challenges. The Scenario mode provides a loose narrative framework, guiding players through a series of events that gradually unlock new tracks, vehicles, and upgrades. Additional modes such as Tournament, Quick Race, Drag Races, and Challenges add variety, allowing players to focus on pure speed, combat-heavy encounters, or specialized objectives. This breadth of modes helps prevent repetition, even if the core loop remains centered on weaponized racing.

Visually, the game reflects its late-2000s origins, but it still delivers a striking aesthetic rooted in its futuristic dystopia. Neon lighting, metallic environments, and exaggerated vehicle designs emphasize speed and aggression, while cityscapes convey scale and spectacle. Although textures and effects feel dated compared to modern racers, the art direction maintains a cohesive identity that supports the game’s tone. Performance quirks on modern systems can occasionally disrupt immersion, reminding players of the game’s age and technical limitations.

Audio design plays a mixed but important role. The soundtrack leans heavily into energetic, electronic, and industrial styles that complement the relentless pace of racing and combat. Menu music and race themes effectively set the mood, reinforcing the idea of racing as violent entertainment. In contrast, in-race sound effects, such as engines and weapons, can feel underpowered or inconsistent, sometimes diminishing the impact of collisions and firefights during critical moments.

Artificial intelligence behavior is aggressive and persistent, ensuring that races rarely feel passive. Opponents actively use weapons, jostle for position, and apply pressure throughout events, often keeping races tightly contested until the final moments. However, this intensity can sometimes cross into frustration, as rubber-banding mechanics and relentless AI aggression may make outcomes feel less skill-driven and more arbitrary. Success often requires embracing the chaos rather than attempting flawless execution.

Multiplayer was envisioned as a core component, allowing players to test their skills against others in online combat races. While the concept fits the game’s design, long-term multiplayer activity has diminished over time, leaving the experience primarily focused on single-player content. As a result, the game now feels more like a self-contained arcade experience rather than a living competitive platform.

Ultimately, Death Track: Resurrection is a bold but uneven revival that prioritizes intensity, spectacle, and aggression over refinement and balance. Its vision of futuristic combat racing is compelling, and moments of high-speed chaos can be genuinely thrilling, especially for players who enjoy arcade-style action and are willing to accept rough edges. While dated mechanics, technical quirks, and inconsistent handling limit its broader appeal, the game still offers a distinctive experience for those drawn to weaponized racing and dystopian flair. For players seeking something loud, fast, and unapologetically chaotic, Death Track: Resurrection remains a flawed but memorable entry in the combat racing genre.

Rating: 6/10

По какой-то причине издатель Fulqrum Publishing решил выпустить обновления для своих старых игр. После долгих размышлений они пришли к выводу, что это будут не патчи, фиксы, достижения, карточки, Steam Cloud или оформления для библиотек, а что-то гораздо более важное — очередной лончер (Fulqrum Launcher).

Хочу обратить внимание: ПК-игроки уже устали от бесконечных лончеров. Это заметили даже крупные издатели, которые начали постепенно убирать лончеры из игр, выпускаемых в Steam. 

Реакция сообщества King's Bounty на новость о добавлении очередного лончера, была столь бурной, что часть тем пришлось удалить. Но вместо того, чтобы учесть обратную связь, вы продолжаете выпускать обновления для всех «своих» игр с добавлением лончера. 

Надеюсь, рано или поздно человек, отвечающий за эту «диверсию», будет уволен, и всё вернётся на свои места.

Дисковое издание этой игры попало мне в руки еще в 2010 году. Тогда мне этот продукт показался слишком сложным, да и слабое железо давало о себе знать. Спустя 10 лет с лишним вернулся к этой игре, немного разобрался, и о чудо, игра проще простого, как в прохождении, так и в освоении её аспектов, в частности управления и получения контента, а то есть, машин. И так в чем суть.

В игре машин мало, но и получить их все у вас вряд ли получится, по той простой причине, что вы не сможете проходить одно и то же соревнование, чтобы фармить деньги. Одна трасса, одно призовое место и один шанс сорвать куш. По этому стоит стараться разрушать все объекты на карте и всегда приходить к финишу первым. И не распыляйтесь на покупку автомобилей. Вы гонщик, а не коллекционер. Купите один, качайте его, и этого вам хватит, чтобы пройти сюжет и чемпионат. Дальше вам денег хватит уже на пару тройку дополнительных машин, чтобы пройти режим заданий. 

По поводу управления. Вы ведете тяжелый бронированный высокотехнологичный болид. Естественно он должен прилипать к дорожному покрытию, а когда сцепления нет - значит вы машиной уже не управляете, ну а в повороты на 180 градусов можно войти и на скорости 200км/ч.

Единственная претензия - ИИ, он слаб. Противник будет по сути у вас всего один, сфокусируйтесь на нем и вы будете побеждать, потому что остальные либо сами разобьются, либо вы их нагоните.

Herkese merhaba! ailenize marketlerden bol bol oyun CD'si aldırdıysanız muhtemelen oynadığınız bir oyundur, benim çocukluğumda baya oynadığım bir oyundu Death Track ve bu oyunla birlikte diğer en sevdiğim oyun da Hard Truck Apocalypse, onu da oynamanızı şiddetle tavsiye ederim! 

Oyundan kısaca bahsetmem gerekirse, yarışırken savaşma oyunu, evet, hem birinci olmaya çalışıyorsunuz aracınızla hem de önünüzdekilere ateş edip roket atıp arkanızdakilere de mayın sallıyorsunuz.

Oyun zor! gerçekten zor, en azından alışana kadar kontrolleri çok zor geliyor, need for speed oyunlarındaki gibi hayalet bariyerler yok ve her çıkıntıya çarpabiliyorsunuz, dönüş yapıyorsunuz diyelim önünüze duvardan bir çıkıntı geldi bam sonuncu oldunuz, bu durum fazlaca sinir krizi geçirmenize sebep olabilir, ve araç kontrolleri de çok sinir bozucu, arabayı fazla çevirirseniz direk kayıyor, yolda önünüze çıkan kırılabileceğini düşündüğünüz şeylere çarpmayın, çünkü kırılmıyorlar, çöp kovası bile olsa duvara çarpıyorsunuz, yollardan nefret edeceksiniz ama post apocalyptic kurgusunu seviyorsanız oyunun hoşunuza gideceğine eminim.

Oyunun ilerleyişinden bahsetmem gerekirse hikaye modunu oynadım ve hikaye modunda haritalarla birlikte araçlar, yükseltmeler ve silahlar açılıyor, bütün haritaları bitirmeden sıradaki haritaları oynayamıyorsunuz herhangi bir modda.

Aracınızı geliştirebiliyorsunuz, aynı şekilde 3 tane silah çeşidi var aracınızda bulunan, 1. ana silah (makineli, lazer ve plasma silahı), 2. ikincil silah (roket atar ve güdümlü bomba), 3. arka silah (mayın veya tekerlekleri patlatmak için diken) bunların hepsinin seviyesi var,
Silahın iki şekilde kullanımı var, biri mouse ile diğeri de oyunun otomatik nişan alması var, ctrl tuşu ile ateş ediyorsunuz, ben onu kullanıyorum, yarış yaparken nişan almaktan çok daha kolay, haritalarda patlatabildiğiniz yerler oluyor, onları patlatırsanız size kalkan veya booster falan veriyorlar, bu boosterları yollardan da toplayabiliyorsunuz ama yıkılabilir yerlerden kazandıklarınız daha uzun süre aktif kalıyor.


Biraz yoruyor insanı oynarken, ama çok farklı bir havası da var, eski bilim kurgu filmlerini hissedeceksiniz oynarken ve sinirlenip sildiğinizde belki yıllar sonra indirip tekrar bitirmeye çalışacaksınız, oyun kısa ama dediğim gibi alışması zor bir oyun ve biraz yorucu, ama kendini aratır çünkü böyle başka bir oyun yok.

Ben bu oyunu öneriyorum ve oynanışı beğenmezseniz bile bulunduğu kurguyu bir denemenizi öneririm.

Как оно играется в 2022? На удивление, весьма бодро! Графика постарела хорошо и смотрится броско, живо. Трассы щедро наполнены деталями, не скупятся на объезды и альтернативные пути. Притом каждый трек - не просто отдельная улица единого города, а свой отдельный биом (!), с уникальными погодными эффектами и оформлением. Единственный недостаток - игра довольно короткая, за пределами сюжетки (да, здесь есть сюжетка с пререндеренными роликами, которые смотрятся доволньо прикольно) делать особо нечего. "Death Track: Resurrection" ist ein Action Fun-Racer.

"Deathtrack" war ursprünglich ein futuristischer Racer aus dem Jahre 1989 von Activision. Für die Zeit war vor allem die Grafik ziemlich fortschrittlich, wenn sie auch heute nur noch wie ein Pixelbrei wirkt. 

"Death Track: Resurrection" stellt sich offenkundig in die Tradition des großen Vorbildes. Allerdings ist dieser russische Racer - im Gegensatz zum Klassiker - beileibe nicht grafisch oder technisch fortschrittlich, im Gegenteil. Zwar stammt das Spiel aus dem Jahre 2009, aber selbst für das Jahr wirkt die Aufmachung altertümlich. Und auch technisch scheint der Titel nicht ganz auf der Höhe. Trotz der schwachen Grafik kann es schon mal zu Rucklern und unschönem Aufploppen kommen. 

Die Zeiten sind hart. In der postapokalyptischen Welt herrscht Dauerkrieg. Kein Grund, deswegen auf Autorennen zu verzichten. Gerade in einer Welt der Zerstörung gibt es genug Wagemutige, die ihr Leben auf der Rennstrecke riskieren.  Wir suchen uns also ein Fahrzeug und eine Strecke aus - wobei zu Beginn sowieso nur jeweils eines zur Verfügung steht,  alles andere muß freigeschaltet werden. Und dann rasen wir aus einer Third-Person-Perspektive gegen mehrere Gegner durch bekannte Hauptstädte und nutzen die auf Dach und Motorhaube installierten Waffen nicht nur gegen unsere Konkurrenten, sondern auch um einige markante Gebäude wie Big Ben im Vorbeifahren dem Erdboden gleichzumachen. Natürlich können wir auch unseren Booster nutzen und Munition oder Schilde aufsammeln. 

An einigen Stellen haben die Tracks Verzweigungen. Wirklich kreativ wird das Strecken-Layout aber nie. Hin und wieder stehen Sprungschanzen oder von Gegnern fallengelassene Spikes in der Gegend rum. Etwas anstrengend wird die Action-Kamera, die bei besonders hohen Sprüngen oder beim Einreißen von Gebäuden das Ereignis in Slow-Motion zeigt. Das Zurückspringen auf die Fahrkamera ist gerne unnötig abrupt und läßt einen gerne mal in der Bande enden. 

Die Strecken haben aber vor allem ein wesentliches Problem: sie sind viel zu lang. An sich sind lange Strecken begrüßenswert, für einen solchen Fun-Racer ist es aber nicht nur ungewöhnlich, sondern auch ermüdend, immer so lange Passagen absolvieren zu müssen. Dafür bieten die Strecken auch einfach zu wenig Abwechslung. 

Das Fahrgefühl ist mit dem Controller einigermaßen okay. Das Fahrzeug reagiert relativ direkt, wenn auch manchmal etwas schwammig. Allerdings gibt es auch in Bezug auf das Handling deutlich bessere Vertreter des Genres. 

Trotzdem kann der Titel durchaus Spaß machen. Für ein wenig Fun-Racing zwischendurch bietet "Death Track: Resurrection" für einen sehr kleinen Preis ein relativ solides Spielerlebnis. Man darf nur nicht mehr erwarten als Mittelmaß.

Death Track: Resurrection

Positives:
+ Finally a Death Track successor
+ The tracks are cool and well made
+ Carmaggeddon style comments and view of the destruction
+ The graphics are ok
+ The sound is ok
+ If you play it right, its also quite fun
+ Parts and weapons upgrade
+ Has a story mode (called "Scenario")
+ Drag Races

Negatives:
- A lot of horrible bugs that never were fixed
- Many errors and sudden quits of the game (making it hard to play)
- You need to force stop the game after you exit (therefore my 128 hours of "playtime")
- If you dont lock the fps to 60, the nitro is bugged
- The AI and difficulty level is very hard and partly unfair
- There is no in-game explaination on how to play this game
- The handling is not the best, quite slow and less responsive than it should have been
- Because of the above, its hard to progress
- The challenge mode is just hard and boring

So to answer the games question: "Do you have what it takes to survive?"
Maybe, that depends how you choose to play, how patient you are and how many retries you are willing to do.


Total Score: 6/10


PS! If you struggle run the game properly try this:
1. Lock your fps to 60 to make the nitro work as it should (use RivaTuner Statistics Server)
2. Go to Video Options and turn off shadows, 512mb video memory, reflections and soft particles. If this does not help enough, also turn of the antialiasing and lower texture quality to medium. 
3 .You can also experiment with windows compability modes: XP SP3 or Vista SP1,
deactivate fullscreen optimization and run it as admin.

This is my highly recommendation on how to play this game:
1. Play the "Scenario" first (which is the main story/campaign mode, that unlocks upgrades)
2. Choose the "Classic" mode (this will make you, but more importantly your opponents unable to respawn)
3. Choose the "Low" difficulty (anything higher will make the game almost unplayable and unfair)
4. Use your money only on better parts and weapons upgrades (dont ever waste your money on new cars)
5. Buy the lazer gun when you can (it does not need new ammo, instead it charges over time)
5. When starting the races, let all the other cars pass you, then start to destroy one by one till you are in first place and the only racer left. You will need some practice and retries, but its the most efficient way to win the races. This also saves your car from total destruction.

Hopefully you now have what it takes to survive

Если же вы наткнулись на эту игру в стиме по совершенной случайности, я бы скорее посоветовал попробовать игру по пиратке, ибо сейчас это очень неоднозначный опыт. Подобный опыт предоставлялся разве что серией Twisted Metal, но в TM геймплей сфокусирован больше на боевом аспекте, ежели гоночном. Однако физика столкновений и геймдизайн DT довольно часто хромает и, как результат, вызывает фрустрацию.

[h1] NecroVision (2009) [/h1] — это тот самый случай, когда игра не становится классикой, но оставляет после себя вполне тёплое и запоминающееся впечатление. Да, она далеко не идеальна. Да, к ней нужно привыкнуть. Но именно благодаря своим странностям и характерному шарму она смогла доставить мне настоящее удовольствие.
[h1] Атмосфера и идея. [/h1]
Самое сильное, что есть в NecroVision — это [b] [i] исходная задумка [/i] [/b]. Первая мировая война как фон для кровавого экшена с элементами хоррора и мистики выглядит свежо и необычно. Траншеи, грязь, газ, пулемёты, солдаты в касках — всё это создаёт [b] [i] мощный визуальный и эмоциональный фундамент [/i] [/b]. Жаль только, что военная составляющая и ощущение позиционной войны довольно быстро уходят на второй план. Фантастика и мистика наступают агрессивно: нежить, демоны, сверхъестественные силы начинают доминировать, и траншейная мясорубка превращается скорее в декорации. Тем не менее сама идея остаётся цепляющей — редкий случай, когда Первая мировая война используется не просто как исторический фон, а как часть игрового настроения.
[h1] Геймплей и ощущения. [/h1]
В основе лежит [b] [i] классический шутер от первого лица в духе старой школы [/i] [/b]. Игра явно хочет быть новым Painkiller — с толпами врагов, брутальным оружием и безумным темпом. До уровня оригинального Painkiller ей, конечно, далеко: не хватает той самой безумной динамики, отточенности и «вау-эффекта» от каждого выстрела. Но именно в этой попытке есть своё очарование.
Стрельба поначалу ощущается довольно корявенькой. Отдача, точность, ощущение оружия — всё это [b] [i] требует привыкания [/i] [/b]. Первые часы можно искренне злиться на управление и ощущение «деревянности». Однако со временем рука приноравливается, и процесс начинает приносить удовольствие. Особенно когда находишь [b] [i] удачные комбинации оружия [/i] [/b] и начинаешь просто рвать орды нежити.
[h1] Баги и шероховатости. [/h1]
Технически игра [b] [i] не самая гладкая [/i] [/b]. [b] [i] Баги встречаются [/i] [/b], и один из самых заметных — постоянные подбрасывания персонажа при столкновении с препятствиями. Натыкаешься на угол, на ящик, на неровность рельефа — и тебя подкидывает. Это раздражает, особенно в напряжённых моментах. Но даже эти шероховатости не убивают общее впечатление. Скорее они добавляют игре того самого «шармового косяка», который часто встречается в проектах середины-конца 2000-х.
[h1] Почему она всё равно работает? [/h1]
[b] [i] Несмотря на все недостатки, NecroVision умудряется цеплять [/i] [/b]. Есть в ней какая-то честная, немного неуклюжая энергия. Она не пытается казаться чем-то большим, чем является. Она просто хочет дать тебе пострелять толпы врагов на фоне Первой мировой, подкинуть мистики и позволить получить кайф от самого процесса. И у неё это получается.
[h1] Вердикт. [/h1]
Если подходить к игре с правильным настроем — [b] [i] не ждать шедевра и идеальной полировки [/i] [/b], а просто наслаждаться атмосферой, идеей и брутальным экшеном — она вполне способна доставить удовольствие. Даже с корявой стрельбой, даже с багами, даже будучи «почти-Painkiller». Иногда именно такие неидеальные, но искренние игры остаются в памяти дольше, чем многие вылизанные проекты.
В общем, NecroVision — это приятный, немного кривоватый, но по-своему обаятельный шутер. Стоит попробовать, если любите старую школу шутеров и не боитесь привыкать к особенностям управления.
[b] Моя оценка [/b] — 6 из 10.

Разгар Первой Мировой войны. Траншеи под Верденом. Тяжёлые сражения. Применение смертоносного газа немецкими войсками. И будто мало этого на поля сражений вылезают сверхъестественные существа. Откуда они взялись? Как обычно напортачили учёные. И не просто учёные, а немецкие учёные двадцатого века.

Игра очень сумбурная. Игроку часто приходится пробегать по уровням и махать оружием во все стороны, потому как ближний бой очень силён в игре и становится только лучше по ходу сюжета.

Уровни зачастую длинные и содержат много секретов. В секретках лежат патроны и аптечки, а в некоторых артефакты, которые увеличивают максимальный запас ярости. Ярость даёт слоумо в предсмертном состоянии. Что можно успеть сделать за короткое время? Набить пару комбинаций, которые восстановят здоровье, и отстрелить мелких врагов по головам.

Помимо сумбура в бою, игра ощущается затянутой. Прохождение занимает 8-10 часов, а усталость от игры начинается уже в середине, когда отходишь от нововведений в виде миссии в мехе и новеньких когтей. Если вам нравятся шутеры, и вы никогда не играли в Necrovision, то попробуйте. Тем, кто не фанатеет от шутеров, играть в неё не стоит.

PainKillerの元開発陣がかつて独立して作ったとされる古典B級FPS。
これを作った人が後に色々なところに分かれていってBulletStormやChernobyliteにつながっていったと思うと感慨深い。
開発史的にも、ゲームシステム的にも、PainKillerとBulletStormのと考えるとすらっと楽しめると思います。

2026年6月時点、Win10を使用していますがゲームエンジンのほうが古すぎて現代のPCスペックに追いついておらずかなり動作が不安定、というか高確率で起動すらしません。
Windows側でディスプレイの解像度を限界まで下げた後、ゲームのグラフィック設定を全てMediumにすると小手先を使わずとも比較的安定して動くようになります。

PainKillerのゲームエンジンを魔改造している都合上、リリース当時の時点でもだいぶ古いエンジンを無茶させてた感じだからね。仕方ないね。

ゲーム内容に関しては、Chapter1～2まではCoDを真似して滑ってる駄作、2中盤～5までは両作、6以降は吹っ切れてPainkillerとかデビルメイクライになります。
なので、序盤1時間は耐えてください。
当時会社都合でPainkillerでストーリーを大幅に削られてた鬱憤が溜まってたストーリーをやりたかった欲求が爆発したのが容易に予想できるので、生暖かい目で大目に見ましょう。

かったるいムービーや演出が過ぎ去れば少しづつ加速的に面白くなります。

PainKillerのの頭悪いシューター感をもっと堪能したいとか、難しいことを考えずにぶっ放したいときにおすすめの一作です。

Tangible proof that you can have a video game that's gets torn apart by it's own mechanics fighting against each other, BUT there are glimpses of a really amazing idea that sometimes works. 

NecroVisioN is a videogame, a videogame that combines the horrors of World War I with.... Zombies? Vampires? Dragons!?!? Developed by The Farm 51, it follows Simon, an American who's somehow in the British Army, as he just rolls with the absolutely bonkers nonsense that he encounters with the most cheesy remarks you could thing of. The game is such a anomaly cause the setting is absolutely off the wall, the gameplay concept is promising but the execution is held back by jank and too many mechanics conflicting with each other, and the tone is absolutely all over the place it's so hard to figure out if the game itself thinks you should take it seriously or not. 

Gameplay of NercoVisioN at it's core is a FPS of it's time mixed with duel-wielding melee gun combat with superpowers. That's one hell of a sentence so let me break it down: Given this came out in 2009, it's very clear that it was trying to rope in people in the Call of Duty audience, given the dark WWI military theme with objectives, the way the player moves, and with all the guns having decently long reloads and ironsights. However on the flip side you also a combo system, bullet time, able to duel-wield both a single-hand gun and melee weapon, carry a insane amount of firepower, and having a kick that would make Dark Messiah be proud. It's two VERY distinct parts of the game that are mashed together and while it often fights against each other, when it does come together, it surprisingly does work really well. Weapons are period accurate so there's a few automatic weapons with long reloads so you often rely on a ton of bolt-action rifles, trench guns, pistols, and of course, melee. Later in the game you do get more fantastical, vampire weapons including SMGs, Auto-Shotguns, Rocket launchers, etc. as well as the Shadow Hand which is basically THE melee weapon of the game, complete with multiple different firing modes. Enemies start basic with German Soldiers but quickly spiral to include zombies, and all the vampire and demonic forces you could thing of including in a WWI setting. Most of the weaker enemies work in larger numbers as not only are they kinda stupid thanks to the jank, their damage can be outweighed with you using all your tools to regain health via combos, and playing smart. It's with the tankier enemies where this starts to fall apart, cause a lot of them can close the distinct with you quickly and deal massive damage. It's where a ton of the game's mechanics start to crack cause devolves from a power fantasy combat sandbox into a shaky button mash slog and it absolutely sucks that it happens this way. If the game simply didn't have realistic movement and had more ways for the player to regain health consistently and/or guard against attacks it would be for the better. Think like a New Doom-esque gameplay loop where you fight certain ways to regain resources to spend in more fights. As it is, It's possible to get through it but not it's as fun as it could and was being. There's also a few vehicle segments with a dinky vampire mech suit and a full-ass dragon and... they surprisingly control well, they're hilariously some of the most consistent parts of the gameplay in the entire package so are surprisingly not as frustrating.

Stylewise, NecroVisioN kinda hits that Painkiller vibe for me which is: it is outdated for todays standards but is exceptionally detailed, and held up a lot of physics and detail. Which is kinda fitting since this game does run on a version of the Painkiller engine. Though one thing that's very different is the sheer amount of bloom and other VERY distracting post-processing effects. The game already is a cluster$%&@ with how much stuff is at pointblank in your face, having blinding effects along with the camera shaking from the movement does not help in the slightest. I could absolutely see this game being a seizure trigger for someone just with the sheer amount of visual noise that you cannot turn off. And it's a shame cause the actual art direction, especially with all the out there monster designs and underground vampire locations are pretty nice.

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Kyezoar/recommended/46250?snr=1_5_9__402] Lost Company Review [/url] 

Overall, NecroVisioN, I think is a prime candidate to be completely remade, not into a different genre, but simply to build it back up as a the weird WWI x Fantasy Melee FPS combo it was meant to be. It's full of so many interesting ideas and gameplay concepts that it genuinely pains me that it's stuck in a incredible janky and sometimes insufferable shell. Cause while it absolutely deserves to be dogged on in some places I do genuinely think it is worth a playthrough if you're curious and ONLY if you're curious and can keep cool when it gets chaotic. And for only 5$ base price AND not needing to get any patching to just get the game running, it's a pretty low bar of entry for a pretty high bar game in terms of going off the wall.

Somos Burkner Simón un soldado estadounidense que se a formado voluntario en las filas británicas durante la primera guerra mundial, mediante un ataque de infantería en el campo de batalla todo nuestro pelotón muere y nuestro protagonista queda confuso y atrapado detrás de las líneas enemigas, cuando Simón retoma el conocimiento intentara escapar entre las duras trincheras, solo para descubrir que los Alemanes han intentado bloquear las salidas, tratando de contener unas fuerzas sobrenaturales. Entonces decidiremos investigar más sobre lo que está pasando, adentrándonos en una aventura siniestra de horror, oscuridad, miseria, nigromancia, muerte y carnicería llevándonos al mismo subterráneo vampírico y al infierno donde se encuentra Mefisto y sus esbirros y parece ser que la culpa de toda estas manifestaciones esta a cargo de un Alemán de nombre Jonas Zimmerman.

El juego cumple, se puede jugar completo en Steam (por suerte) y la aventura entretiene con su tono dramático y sombrío ofreciéndonos paisajes devastadores y deprimentes. Mediante cartas de soldados que funcionan de colección dentro del juego también nos arrojaran luz sobre otras situaciones desde otro punto de vista que encajan bien con el ambiente de desesperanza en la guerra, aunque el tono cambie más a la mitad de la aventura y vamos a encontrarnos con enemigos profanos, vampiros, fantasmas demonios y ogros gigantes. 
Gran parte de la jugabilidad depende de eliminar innumerables enemigos, recorrer pasadizos y encontrar zonas con secretos, acompañados de diversos poderes sobrenaturales y armas para destrozar y desgarrar a los enemigos. Además de la campaña principal podemos jugar unos niveles a base de desafíos que se nos propondrán retos para desbloquear armas y tenerla permanentemente en nuestro arsenal para evitar buscarla individualmente en la campaña
Es un juego de casi 15 años así que gráficamente no se ve tan mal, las voces vienen en total español(España), y realmente no me gustaron las actuaciones de voces que son ridículamente pobres en un ambiente sombrío y melancólico, mucho menos cuando el personaje principal hace chistes. Pero cuando entra en modo nigromante las voces son más potable y se toman las actuaciones un poco más serias. Igualmente es un juego recomendado consigue ofrecer algunas emociones decentes y los jefes están buenos, sobre todo los jefes finales que dan una lucha muy épica.

review:
The best mission in Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare asks you to lie still in the grass while an enemy patrol walks past. In “All Ghillied Up,” Captain MacMillan tells you when to move, and the tension comes from how long you have to wait. The same campaign opens with a raid on a cargo ship that ends in a desperate sprint across a tilting deck. Both missions are over quickly, and both are easy to remember years later.

That variety keeps the campaign moving. The gunplay is snappy, the squad chatter sells the urgency, and switching between the SAS and the U.S. Marines gives the story room to change pace. Some encounters have aged less gracefully. On higher difficulties, repeated grenade throws and waves of enemies can make pushing toward the next checkpoint feel like the only sensible move, even when the game seems to be asking you to take cover.

Multiplayer is the other half of what made COD4 special. Create-a-Class lets you build around a weapon and a handful of perks, while killstreak rewards make every extra elimination feel like it counts. Maps such as Crash give you room to fight over rooftops and alleyways. Shipment takes about three seconds to turn into a complete mess, which is exactly why it’s fun.

**9/10.** The original Modern Warfare is still worth playing for the campaign alone. It’s short, varied, and knows when to give the gunfire a rest so you can hear the boots coming through the grass.

Call of Duty 4 is the genesis of the golden era of Call of Duty. If you know anything about Call of Duty, (You're breathing, aren't you?) then I don't have to say anything else. You already know exactly what makes this game so special. Everything people associate with a good Call of Duty game is right here. There are higher highs the series reaches, sure, but the peaks of the franchise are standing on the shoulders of this game.

To start, the campaign is great. The game is one of the two games in a transition period between the more grounded original CoD trilogy and the Hollywood action series that started with MW2. This means it is great for pretty much anyone. You want high stakes? CoD 4 has it. You want more grounded combat like CoD 1-3? There's levels like that. Hollywood action? There's levels like that. Cool characters? CoD 4 has 'em. If there's anything anyone knows about CoD campaigns, it's that there's a guy called Captain Price in a few of them. There's a reason for that.

The only downside is that the actual meat of the story itself is lacking. If you are the type to be bothered by plot-holes and contrivance in stories, you might get a bit itchy playing CoD 4. Things just sorta happen, and you don't get a lot of context for why it's happening. There's not much environmental storytelling to pick up the slack either. You're encouraged to focus on the task at hand, like a good soldier.

The multiplayer... do I actually have to elaborate on this? It's Call of Duty 4! It's *the* CoD MP. The one that caused a generational addiction and began the takeover of the FPS industry lead by the end of the decade. That MP. Create-a-class, killstreaks, perks, unlocks, prestige, etc etc: it is the blueprint of the CoD MP formula. The only detraction I can think of is that because this is the pioneer game, a lot of the kinks that have since been worked out over 19 years aren't worked out here. So, it can be frustrating or underwhelming if you compare it to newer titles. But, honestly, if you can convince yourself it's 2007 and just play it for what it is without minding what comes next: then this game is just as addictive as it was back then.

The only issue with that mindset is that nowadays, you're rarely gonna find a truly vanilla CoD 4 experience on PC. For one, you need CoD4X to play most servers. For two, servers that are still around often have XP cheats or play on a non-vanilla map or ruleset. (No shade toward Promod, I love Promod.) If you manage to find a vanilla game of CoD4 on PC, cherish that moment.

gameplay, graphics, acting, music, setpieces, direction, pacing--all very well done. The writing, however, isn't good. And that's not because it gets lost with what it's trying to say--actually, the thematic material is good, and consistent throughout. Where it gets lost is with what the hell is actually happening in the story.

South Park writers famously said that if you have a story that can be described as "this, then that," over and over, then you have a bad story. Well, Call of Duty 4 is somehow worse than that: imagine a "this, then that" story, but then take out three or four "this's" or "thats" at random. Not only do the events not make sense, but there are massive gaps in between things not making sense.

Overall game: What I liked most is the nostalgia. It's a perfect remake of the original right down to the controls. The graphics are faithful to original and the gameplay is following what i remember from last time I played this game quite some time back.

Mechanics and controls: Don't worry about mechanics, they are ancient so it will take some time getting used to it. The controls are not as intuitive but if you can find your rythm, it should not stop you from enjoying the game. 
Also, the negative reviews complaining about jump controls are lacking basic reading capability for some reason. To avoid joining that force, pay attention for 90 secs when the tutorial is asking you to do things and you will figure it out (Hint: tap for jump and hold for longer jump, use it wisely!). 

Now time to cook it: Puzzles are same as original so not as complicated for someone who already played the game before. Nothing new or innovating for me personally. If you are a first timer, enjoy the game. 

Bugs, if you want to call it that: What I would warn about? Camera controls are wonky. I mean, usually near walls and ledges, you have to adjust or else you might jump into oblivion. The controls draw direction from both arrow keys and camera unlike current gen games where camera is free looking. That's the challenge i assume for someone who hasn't played this game yet. 

TL;DR - if you played it before, its the same thing. If you didnt play it before, time to learn what it was like gaming a couple of decades back. Enjoy!

Enjoyable Tomb Raider game (until you reach Great Pyramid level, particularly one room),  with a largely smooth transition away from the block based movement and spacing mechanics to dual analog. Anniversary makes big changes with the OG Tomb Raider but still maintains the minimalistic approach, primarily focusing on exploration (and lots of shooting of animals).

[h1]Ремейк, до эпохи ремейков[/h1]
Мы живём в эпоху ремейков. Одни становятся глотком свежего воздуха, а при виде других задаешься вопросом «А зачем?».
Отчасти это связано с Законом убывающей доходности — прыжок с PS3 на PS4 и PS5 уже не так впечатляет, как с PS1 на PS2. 

Тогда за короткий срок Resident Evil, Metal Gear Solid и Tomb Raider преобразились до неузнаваемости. Но это были не просто графические апгрейды. Resident Evil переделал локации, сюжетные моменты и головоломки. MGS The Twin Snakes стал несбалансированным. А Tomb Raider полностью переосмыслили.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]📖 Сюжет — переписали то, что не было сломано[/h2]
Anniversary является ремейком TR1 и в то же время существует во вселенной, начатой с Legend. Лара здесь мотивирована родителями, в то время как в оригинале её родители отреклись от неё — приключения были её собственным решением, вопреки сопротивлению. Здесь она идёт по стопам отца, ищет мать. 

Натла использует это, чтобы нанять её. Отношения с Натлой тоже изменены. В оригинале она наняла Лару, потому что та лучшая в своем деле. Здесь Натла работала с отцом Лары и убила его. Она даже предлагает Ларе место рядом с собой. Но это противоречит оригинальной Натле — злой бабище, которая хотела хаоса, а не власти. Зачем ей делиться силой?

Пьер, Ларсен, другие приспешники — все убиты в катсценах или QTE. Вы не сражаетесь с ними. Вы не формируете соперничество. Вы не получаете катарсис. Anniversary могла бы вырезать Пьера полностью — игра была бы точно такой же.

Лара здесь убивает Ларсена в QTE и смотрит на свои руки в ужасе. Тема вины проходит через игру. Но это не вяжется ни с оригинальной Ларой, ни с новой. В Legend она косила людей волнами. Как будто сценарист хотел добавить глубины, не понимая, как это интегрировать.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]🎮 Геймплей — современно, но ненадёжно[/h2]
Лара автоматически хватается за уступы. Может раскачиваться на шестах, прыгать по платформам, использовать грапл для раскачивания и бега по стенам. Движения стали более плавными, но и более искусственными. Я никогда не был уверен, как далеко прыгнет Лара. Одни и те же вводы давали разные результаты.

Лара «магнитится» к платформам, возможно, из-за камеры. Это заставляет бороться с управлением, особенно когда идёшь за секретами. В испытаниях это становится источником раздражения. Ты не чувствуешь контроля. Успех или провал не полностью зависят от тебя.
Танковое управление было устаревшим, но предсказуемым. Ты знал, что может Лара. Смерти были твоей виной. Здесь — нет.

Чекпоинты частые и самостоятельные. Умираешь — теряешь минуту. Это убирает напряжение. Раньше я был осторожен, боясь отката. Теперь действую безрассудно. Это меняет поведение игрока и снижает вовлечённость.

Бой обновлён. Ручной захват цели, стрельба по нажатию. Враги агрессивнее, атакуют толпами. В узких коридорах это приводит к неизбежному урону. Но есть «адреналиновый выстрел»: доведи врага до ярости, доджни, и в моменте убей одним выстрелом. Работает на всём. Делает напряжённые моменты тривиальными.

Боссы — тот же хэд-шот в моменте. За исключением кентавров, где нужно украсть щиты и отразить их же атаки. Это интересно. Жаль, что такого мало.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]🌍 Локации — знакомые, но обрезанные[/h2]
Вот тут больно. Anniversary берёт четыре культовых региона оригинала — Перу, Грецию, Египет и Атлантиду — и проходит по ним катком ремейка.

Общее впечатление: ты вроде бы узнаёшь места, но это как встретить одноклассника, которого не видел двадцать лет. Черты вроде те же, но что-то не так. Мозгу нужно время, чтобы понять: перед тобой не тот человек, что раньше.

Самый яркий момент как по мне это битва с Т-Рексом. 
Оригинал — динамичная сцена с вариантами действий, можно драться уклоняясь, можно было сражаться издалека. Опять же, для возможностей PS1 нормально. 
Здесь — Носорог из Человека-Паука: агришь, он бежит, доджишь, он стукается о шипы, получает урон. Повтор. 
Разработчики в комментариях говорят, что хотели «улучшить» бой. Но они не поняли, что оригинал был особенным по-своему. В рамках своих механик, а не чужих.

Уровни сжали, выпрямили, сделали линейными. Целые секции вырезали. Вилкабамба превратилась в одну камеру. Затерянная долина потеряла половину структуры. Систему и Гробницу Техокена слепили в один огрызок. Колизей переосмыслили полностью, и он стал единственным местом, где переосмысление усилило эмоции, но остальное — плоско.

Оригинал любил петлять. Выход часто был рядом, но за запертой дверью. Ты исследовал, возвращался, запоминал. Здесь тебя ведут за руку. Из опасной неизвестной цивилизации Anniversary превращает локации в тематический парк: всё расставлено, всё подписано, всё контролируется. Водопады никуда не ведут. Это декорация, а не места с секретами.

Больше всего пострадала Атлантида. Она стала хуже: из «мясной жути» превратилась в крепость Баузера. Ну короче полный пролет. Нужно то было сделать как в DMC5 или как в Silent Hiil’е эти уровни.

Египет — единственное исключение. Он ощущается как Tomb Raider: блочная архитектура, прямые углы, тайлы на полу. Ветераны чувствуют себя дома. Жаль, что так не подошли ко всему остальному.

Поместье Крофт — приятный сюрприз. Паззл-бокс в духе Resident Evil. Час удовольствия. Но опционально.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]🎨 Визуал и звук — технически лучше, эстетически беднее[/h2]
Полигонов больше, текстуры чётче. Но эстетика потеряна. Оригинал был ярким. Храмы строились, чтобы прославлять правителей. Anniversary — приглушённый, серый, пыльный. Всё рушится. Реалистично? Да. Скучно? Тоже да.

Оригинал выигрывал от обратного эффекта жуткой долины. Старые текстуры заставляли воображение работать. Ты не знал, что перед тобой. Это создавало осторожность, опасность. Anniversary всё показывает. Теряется «потусторонняя атмосфера».

[hr][/hr]
[h2]💻 Steam версия — Отличная, но есть нюанс[/h2]

[h2]📊 Вердикт[/h2]
После прохождения первого уровня у меня возник вопрос в голове. А зачем эта игра вообще нужна? Как ремейк – ну такое, как полноценная вторая часть серии – ну камон, у вас вся тематика из TR1 вылизана какая тут в попу «полноценность», как попытка заработать деньжат – вот тут я целиком и полностью понимаю причину.

Ремейк Resident Evil 2 работает, потому что фокусирется на том, какие эмоции вызывал оригинал. Anniversary этого не делает. Она упускает суть Tomb Raider.

Оригинал был неуютным, опасным, загадочным. Ты не был желанным гостем. Ты планировал, осторожничал, знал, что смерть за углом. Anniversary с современным управлением, линейными уровнями, чекпоинтами на каждом углу и чёткой графикой вызывает другие эмоции. Ты не чувствуешь угрозы. Ты чувствуешь себя крутым экшен-героем.

Если судить Anniversary как отдельную игру — она нормальная, крепкая, играбельная. 
Если судить как переосмысление TR1 – просто нет. Это не Tomb Raider. Это Legend интегрировала TR1 в себя, поверхностно походя на оригинал. Без должного переосмысления. Лучше бы они сделали простой сиквел, как Underworld.

Tomb Raider: Anniversary is a retelling of the very first Tomb Raider game, and this one has always caused a lot of discourse within the fandom. Personally, I've always really liked it. To me, this is a great version of the original adventure, and I think most of the changes they made work really well.

Coming out after Tomb Raider Legend, Anniversary was also part of that new direction for the franchise. It was meant to tie this new soft reboot back to Lara's established history, reintroducing her first adventure while showing how the new games could be intertwined with what came before.

And I think they handled that really well.

They changed things, obviously, but not to the point where it feels like they were trying to erase the original. The story feels a little more grounded and developed, the characters feel more fleshed out and less dated, and the whole thing felt incredibly modern at the time. Even now, I think it holds up really well.

The gameplay is honestly amazing.

Getting to revisit those locations from the first Tomb Raider, but seeing them completely rebuilt at a different scale and with different layouts, was such a great idea. You recognize places and moments from the original, but things have been changed enough that you can't simply rely on your memory. It makes the adventure feel familiar and unexpected at the same time.

And having Lara with the grapple hook feels so good. The movement and exploration are such a natural evolution of what Legend established, and it makes these environments so much more fun to navigate.

I also really love Croft Manor in this game.

Compared to Legend, it's not finished yet, which is such a fun little callback to the original Tomb Raider. You have the boxes and crates sitting around the main hall, and they actually paid attention to those little details from the original game. I love when a remake or retelling does that, because it makes you feel like you're looking at the same place through a completely different lens.

That's really what I love about Anniversary.

It's not just trying to recreate Tomb Raider 1 exactly. It's taking that adventure and rebuilding it for a completely different era of Tomb Raider while keeping the heart of the original intact.

There has always been this whole "classic purist" discussion surrounding Anniversary, and I understand why some people prefer the original exactly as it was. But I've never really subscribed to the idea that you have to choose one.

You can enjoy both.

I do.

I love Tomb Raider 1, and I love Anniversary. They are different experiences, and I think that's perfectly fine.

And that's also why I'm so curious about Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

In a way, Anniversary was created to connect the original Lara and her first adventure to the new direction of the franchise. Legacy of Atlantis is taking that idea so much further. The purpose of this game is to bring all of these different timelines together: Classic Lara, the Legend-era soft reboot, and the Survivor Trilogy, finally merging them into one Lara.

We're finally getting to a point where all of these different versions of Lara are becoming one.

And honestly, I'm really curious to see what's going to stay.

What parts of Classic Lara are going to remain? What survives from the Legend era? What elements of the Survivor Trilogy become part of this unified version of Lara? Seeing how they take pieces from all three timelines and figure out what belongs to this one Lara is probably one of the things I'm most excited about.

It's such a different situation from Anniversary. Anniversary was taking one classic adventure and rebuilding it to fit into a new timeline. Legacy of Atlantis is essentially taking Lara's entire history and trying to bring it together.

I can't wait to see how they do it.

For me, Anniversary has always been a great Tomb Raider game.

I like it. I always have.

It's a really good retelling of an iconic adventure, and I love seeing how it fits into Lara's story. And now, after all these years, I'm really excited to see where this idea of connecting Lara's different eras ultimately takes us.
