Championship Manager 2007 is an ancient game from 2007 (as the name implies).  It's a whopping 17 years old at the time of this review.  The game lacks support for any modern gaming display resolutions (or widescreen monitors), hasn't been modernised or updated to run smoothly on modern gaming PCs.  Despite this lack of modernisation, it carries a pretty high price tag for such an ancient game.  This seems to have been put on Steam as a nostalgia gouge, or just a cash grab to try profit from abandonware.

Championship Manager can best be described as Football Manager, but from Wish.  If unsure, the most recent games in this series are mobile apps... and that should tell you everything you need to know about this from a PC gaming perspective.  At this point you might think this review for Championship Manager 2007 is a copy and paste of my review for Championship Manager 2008... and it is, because Championship Manager 2008 is a copy + paste of Championship Manager 2007.  The only difference is they added 1 to the year.  This kind of thing is not okay now, it wasn't okay then, so let's stop that. 

Like the dozens of other football management games, this is a spreadsheet with a screensaver (fine, some people like that), but this is not the best of those kinds of games.  It wasn't then and it certainly isn't now.  It's aged very badly. 

From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.

The game only displays in 4:3 pillarboxed aspect ratio, due to the age of the game, it predates the 16:9 widescreen gaming standard established back in 2006.  It's possible they're marketing this towards people using an old CRT they found in a dumpster, or this game is being specifically marketed towards people gaming on PC's from 1995... either way, this isn't really acceptable in the modern era of PC gaming.  It's obviously not going to look right on a modern 16:9 gaming display.

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.

Championship Manager 2007 is relatively expensive for an abandonware nostalgia gouge, at $5 USD, and it's not worth it.  The game is just too old, hasn't been modernised.  For comparison, the $5 USD asking price for this game could get you games like "Fallout 4", "Payday 2" or "Civilization VI".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.  There's also thousands of free, superior quality games on Steam.  And as the old saying goes, you can't go home again.

I love this game, but I can't give a positive review. I had this game on CD shortly after its release. There was a very irritating and big bug in it. I bought it on Steam again, hoping that it was a complete product after all these years, but it is still here.

Well, after changing the qualifying format to 10 groups, the Euro adds play-offs for the second-place teams, which, as it turns out, make no sense, because despite winning them, we don't get to the Euro. Instead, random teams like San Marino or Andorra play there, which completely ruins the gameplay. Playing as an average team, where we often take second place in the group, we will probably never play in the Euro, unless by some miracle we are drawn.

The second bug is related to the world ranking, where practically nothing changes. Points are obtained very slowly, top teams receive disproportionately more, and even by winning series of international competitions, you would have to win everything for 400 years to reach the top.

There are also a few inaccuracies in the national cups. For example, in the Polish league there is a chance that despite winning the 1/8th or 1/4th cup (I don't remember exactly, but it happened to me 2 or 3 times), our opponent will still play and we will be eliminated.

I would buy it a third time if it worked properly </3

Championship Manager 2008 is an elderly game now and you might wonder why on earth anyone would be playing it in 2020.

Well there's a few reasons I downloaded this game - I have a lot of spare time now we are under lockdown conditions and I wanted something that would run on my 8 year old PC.  Also the price, it was and is a bargain compared to more "modern" games.  Plus I used to play the old Champ Manager games back in the 90s on the Amiga, so a bit of nostalgia there!

Anyway, as you can see I have played this game quite a bit, it says getting on for 2,000 hours but I do tend to leave it running, I've probably played a total of about 50 seasons or so with various teams.

I've won over a 100 trophies with Spurs, taken Gainsborough Trinity from the Conference North to the Championship in 6 seasons and then got sacked when we were relegated (tough Chairman there!) amongst other things.

Overall it's a really solid football management game, you can manage thousands of different sides from massive clubs down to small conference teams.  You have to keep an eye on finances, keep the players happy, look after training and scouting plus strategy etc.

You can do pretty much what you want, buy and sell players, train them, scout, hire staff etc.  What I like about the game is you can decide how much micro-managing you want, I personally don't bother doing the training and just buy/sell players, set contracts, pick the side and formation.  But you can do as much or little of that as you want.

The game engine is pretty believable with the highlights being decent when you consider the age of the game - it's certainly entertaining enough watching your side struggle to score goals.  One niggle is sometimes the defenders/goalkeepers do some pretty dumb things, but it's not a big issue.

What I enjoy is discovering new players when they're young and watching them develop into worldbeaters.  Picking up a non-league player at age 16 for a few thousand pounds and seeing them turn out to be multi-million pound players getting their first international cap a few seasons later.

It's certainly worth the price, I don't feel the need to get a much more expensive up to date game just at the moment.

Now excuse me as I need to get back to managing Spurs, it's 2040 and we're going to try for our fifth Premier League title in a row.

It's a bit easy once you work out the best formation/strategy but I'll let you work that out for yourself!

[h2]顺便聊聊这游戏[/h2]
IO Interactive 2007 年的作品。凯恩是“七人帮”的前雇佣兵，被判死刑，押赴刑场的路上被七人帮劫走，同车的还有精神极不稳定的林奇。七人帮要他把当年“弄丢”的钱找回来，不然就杀了他的女儿珍妮——于是两个亡命徒从东京、哈瓦那一路打到古巴的丛林。

这游戏的卖点从来不是枪法：掩体射击手感一般、队友 AI 呆、画面也早就过时。它好看的是人：凯恩和林奇一路互喷、互相拖后腿，剧情阴冷得没有一个好人，两个结局都让人憋得慌。流程大概六七个小时，促销几块钱，想看故事的话值。

多人“脆弱同盟”的背叛玩法当年很有想法，现在服务器早关了，只剩单人。配上中文，起码能听懂这两个混蛋到底在骂什么了。

Un gameplay daté, mais deux personnages qui mériteraient leur propre film

Kane & Lynch: Dead Men est typiquement le genre de jeu qui peut être difficile à recommander aujourd'hui pour son gameplay... mais impossible à oublier pour son ambiance et ses personnages.

Techniquement, le jeu a pris un sacré coup de vieux.

Le moteur, basé sur les technologies utilisées pour les premiers Hitman, montre clairement ses limites. Les déplacements sont rigides, les animations datées, les gunfights assez rudimentaires et certaines mécaniques semblent parfois avoir été adaptées à un moteur qui n'était tout simplement pas conçu pour ce type de jeu.

Et pourtant...

Quelle ambiance.

Kane & Lynch est avant tout un énorme hommage au cinéma de Michael Mann.

On retrouve cette esthétique froide et réaliste, les fusillades brutales, les braquages qui tournent mal, les personnages complètement paumés et cette sensation d'assister à un film policier beaucoup plus sombre que le jeu vidéo moyen.

On pense évidemment à Heat, Collateral, mais également à toute cette culture du thriller criminel où les personnages ne sont pas des héros.

Kane et Lynch sont deux types profondément dysfonctionnels.

Kane est un criminel vieillissant, cynique et complètement détruit par ses propres choix (rien que les moments où nous sommes au sol et que Kane resasse son passé). 

Lynch est encore pire.

Instable, violent, imprévisible et psychologiquement dérangé, il peut passer du calme absolu à une explosion de violence en quelques secondes.

Et c'est précisément leur relation qui porte tout le jeu.

Les dialogues sont excellents.

Les deux personnages passent leur temps à se détester, se menacer, se manipuler et malgré tout à devoir compter l'un sur l'autre.

Il y a quelque chose de fascinant dans leur dynamique.

On pourrait presque retirer les fusillades et garder uniquement les dialogues : il y aurait suffisamment de matière pour faire un excellent film criminel centré sur ces deux personnages.

C'est probablement la plus grande force de Dead Men.

L'écriture ne cherche pas à rendre Kane et Lynch sympathiques.

Elle cherche à les rendre crédibles.

Ce sont deux hommes abîmés, violents, égoïstes et parfois totalement irrécupérables.

Et pourtant, on finit par s'intéresser à eux.

La bande-son est également une énorme réussite. Merci encore Jesper Kyd. 

Mais surtout, le sound design est incroyable.

Les armes ont du poids, les fusillades sont assourdissantes, les explosions claquent et l'ensemble donne une véritable sensation de chaos.

C'est probablement l'un des aspects qui participe le plus à cette impression de regarder un film de Michael Mann dans lequel on aurait pris le contrôle des personnages.

Le jeu possède également cette photographie particulière : couleurs froides, environnements urbains, éclairages nocturnes et décors réalistes.

Tout est fait pour renforcer cette atmosphère de polar criminel.

Malheureusement, le gameplay ne suit pas toujours.

Les gunfights sont assez basiques, les déplacements manquent de fluidité et certaines séquences deviennent franchement laborieuses avec les standards actuels.

On sent clairement que le moteur des premiers Hitman n'était pas forcément adapté à cette nouvelle orientation beaucoup plus orientée action.

Mais malgré cela, je trouve difficile de réellement détester Kane & Lynch: Dead Men.

Parce que derrière son gameplay vieillissant, il y a une véritable personnalité.

Un jeu imparfait, parfois maladroit, mais qui possède une ambiance que beaucoup de productions plus modernes n'arrivent pas à reproduire.

Au final, Kane & Lynch: Dead Men est presque davantage une expérience cinématographique interactive qu'un grand jeu de tir.

Et son plus grand mérite reste ses deux personnages.

Kane et Lynch pourraient parfaitement exister dans un film de Michael Mann.

Un scénario sombre, des dialogues excellents, des fusillades brutales, une bande-son mémorable et deux personnages complètement détruits.

Le gameplay a vieilli.

Le moteur montre son âge.

Mais Kane et Lynch, eux, restent toujours aussi intéressants.

Un jeu imparfait, mais un sacré morceau de cinéma criminel vidéoludique.

[h1]Мертвы по прибытии[/h1]

Кейн и Линч - два редкостных негодяя. Первый ненамеренно - ну, он так говорит - кинул преступный синдикат, на который работал, за что мужика, собственно, прижали в стиле "или твоя семья получит свинца, или ты вернешь спионеренное". Кейн, очевидно, соглашается на условия. А в качестве надзирателя/няньки к нему приставляют Линча - едва контролирующего себя психа, который страдает от галюнов. В атмосфере взаимной и плохо скрываемой неприязни и недоверия и проходит все короткое и, откровенно говоря, скучное и бессвязное приключение этой парочки.

Несмотря на отзывы о хорошем коопе, давайте смотреть правде в глаза. Во-первых, GFWL, мать его. Как тот, кто натрахался с ним вдоволь еще несколько лет назад, я честно скажу - вот конкретно эта игра долботни с запуском не больно-то стоит. Во-вторых, установить этот древний сервис несложно - проблема в том, чтобы заставить его работать корректно и коопить - у меня с этим не срослось.

И вот как сингловый опыт Kane & Lynch - это игра категории "kinda meh". Однообразное мочилово с ужасным разлетом пуль у всего оружия и дай бог парой-тройкой запоминающихся эпизодов. Коопных механик для такого жанра чудовищно мало - две (лечение и пополнение боезапаса), как и ситуаций, требующих взаимодействия. ИИ - тупой (у союзников и врагов одновременно). Визуально игра не цепляет, при всех попытках в кинематографию катсцен. Единственное светлое пятно - музыка Йеспера Кюда. 

Ну отвалился она из продажи и отвалилась - и черт с ней. Несмотря на год выхода, характерной попытки игр тех лет чем-то впечатлить пресытившегося игрока я лично не прочухал.

[b][h1]Brutal e caótico![/h1][/b]
Kane & Lynch: Dead Men foi desenvolvido pela IO Interactive, mesmo estúdio da franquia Hitman, e distribuído pela Square Enix, lançado em novembro de 2007 para PC, PS3 e Xbox 360. Descrito como um game de ação em terceira pessoa cooperativo.

O jogo nos apresenta Kane, um mercenário condenado a morte que está sendo transferido e que é resgatado por Lynch a pedido do grupo intitulado The 7, após a fuga, Kane é interrogado pelos líderes do grupo que o acusam de traição. Kane, mesmo negando que tenha roubado seus antigos empregadores, se vê obrigado a reaver o dinheiro em 72 horas, e Lynch tem a função de garantir que Kane cumpra o acordo. Com isso a dupla inicia uma verdadeira corrida contra o tempo para reaver o dinheiro dos The 7 e resgatar a filha e ex-esposa de Kane, que foram raptadas pela organização.

A trama é bem consistente, envolvendo bastante ação, dramas familiares, traições e honra entre ladrões. O grande destaque do enredo são os dois protagonistas, com Kane se destacando por conduzir toda o desenvolvimento da história, sendo um personagem violento e durão, mas com uma carga dramática bem forte devido a culpa pelos seus erros do passado, ao seu lado temos Lynch, sendo um contraponto ao Kane, por ter uma personalidade mais caótica e igualmente violenta, com seus próprios dramas pessoais a serem resolvidos. O destaque é justamente o relacionamento dos dois protagonistas, que vai se fortalecendo ao longo da narrativa, conforme vamos conhecendo os seus dramas e conflitos éticos, ambos não são herois, muito pelo contrário, são cheios de falhas, mas no fim se demonstram aliados leais.

A jogabilidade para época atendia as expectativas, sendo bem direta e funcional, hoje nitidamente envelheceu, com uma movimentação truncada e com pouca variedade de movimentos, mas com a ação frenética das missões o gameplay flui tornando a progressão constante. A estrutura das fases é estritamente linear, com o objetivo restrito de se avançar do ponto A ao ponto B, derrotando os inimigos pelo caminho. Há alguns momentos de perseguição e fuga em veículos, mas nada que mude drasticamente a estrutura base do gameplay.

Não há coletáveis, sistema de progressão ou segredos a serem encontrados ao longo dos 15 capítulos da campanha e devido a sua estrutura linear, não há motivo para exploração, tornando o fator replay quase inexistente. O game contava com a possibilidade de se jogar cooperativamente, porém atualmente esse modo está inacessível, devido ao desligamento dos servidores. Apesar dessa limitação, o game permite que o jogador de comandos para o Lynch, assim como para outros companheiros que se unem a dupla durante a campanha, facilitando assim alguns momentos que demandam uma abordagem mais tática durante os confrontos.

Kane & Lynch: Dead Men é um ótimo game de ação, com uma jogabilidade simples, mas que recompensa o jogador com tiroteios intensos e um enredo maduro e interessante, com Kane e Lynch sendo o total oposto dos protagonistas habituais, cheios de falhas e camadas de complexidades. O final, dependendo da escolha do jogador, pode ser devastador, marcando a jornada dos dois mercenários de forma sombria.

[H1] Kane & Regret [/H1]
[H3]painfully mid[/h3]

If you're a video game nerd like me, you'll probably remember the controversy surrounding [b]Kane & Lynch: Dead Men's[/b] release. The backlash wasn't about the game's violence or subject matter. Instead, it became one of the first major controversies to raise questions about whether publishers had too much influence over the outlets reviewing their games.

I remember much of the discussion centering around Jeff Gerstmann's 7/10 review for GameSpot. Looking back, that score feels fair, though I would argue it may have been slightly generous. Today, I'd place [b]Kane & Lynch: Dead Men[/b] closer to a 6/10, and on some days, perhaps even a 5/10.

[b]It's an aggressively average game that rarely rises above its peers.[/b]

The game's squad-based mechanics feel underdeveloped, with AI teammates often creating more problems than they solve. It's clear the game was built with co-op in mind, as many of its frustrations would likely disappear with a human partner. 

The criminal underworld setting, memorable set pieces, and antihero premise give the game some personality, but Kane himself is surprisingly one-dimensional and difficult to care about. Lynch is cool though.

Unfortunately, most of the game's ambition is buried beneath repetitive shooting, weak squad mechanics, and uneven storytelling. The result is a campaign that feels far longer than it actually is, largely because it rarely gives the player anything new to do. One particularly odd design choice is the game's obsession with rappelling. The mechanic appears throughout the campaign and is used repeatedly in the final mission, yet the game never does anything interesting with it, making these sequences feel repetitive rather than engaging.

Only pick this up during a deep sale. despite what my Steam playtime might suggest, much of that was spent with the game running in the background. [h1][b]🎮 Reseña de Kane and Lynch: Dead Men™[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
Kane and Lynch: Dead Men™ es ese shooter de acción en tercera persona que te mira a los ojos y te dice: “¿Quieres una historia de criminales violentos, robos y decisiones horribles?” y luego te empuja a un tiroteo donde media ciudad parece tener licencia para dispararte. La propuesta es simple: campaña con narrativa “adulta”, mucha balacera, y un dúo de protagonistas que no son héroes… son problemas con piernas.

La primera impresión es potente: atmósfera sucia, crimen, tensión, y una vibra de película de atracos que se descarrila a propósito. En lo jugable, es acción directa: cobertura, avanzar, disparar, repetir; con el plus de poder vivirlo en cooperativo (local/online) y hasta en pantalla dividida/compartida con Remote Play Together, porque nada dice “amistad” como gritarle a tu compañero por arruinar el sigilo que nunca existió.

[h2]Lo Criminalmente Bueno y lo Sospechosamente No Tan Bueno[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
✅ 🔫 Acción en tercera persona sin rodeos: disparas, cubres, avanzas. Punto.  
✅ 🤝 Cooperativo real (incluye local, pantalla dividida/compartida y Remote Play Together): el caos se disfruta más acompañado.  
✅ 🎬 Trama con tono adulto y violento: criminales, robos y mala leche; al menos no pretende ser una fábula.  
✅ 🎧 Gran banda sonora y buena ambientación: cuando el juego se pone “cinematográfico”, se nota.  

Lo No Tan Bueno:
❌ 🏆 0 logros disponibles 😴: Steam te mira y te dice “¿progresión? ¿metas? jajaja no”.  
❌ 🎮 Compatibilidad parcial con mando: perfecto para pelearte con el juego… además de con los enemigos.  
❌ 👥 Jugadores actuales: 1: sí, hay multijugador… en teoría. En práctica, es un club privado.  
❌ 🧠 IA / dificultad irregular: a ratos la tensión es buena; a ratos sientes que el tiroteo es una fila para que te disparen.

[h2]Conclusión (Bueno)[/h2]
Kane and Lynch: Dead Men™ es como invitar a dos tipos peligrosos a tu casa: va a ser intenso, incómodo, y probablemente termine con gritos… pero no puedes decir que fue aburrido. Su mayor gancho es el tono: criminal, violento, atmosférico, con una historia que se siente más cínica que heroica (gracias a Dios).

¿Vale la pena? Depende de tu tolerancia a lo “de su época” y tu amor por el cooperativo. La comunidad hoy se siente fantasma (1 jugador actual), así que si vienes por multijugador como actividad social, trae una ouija. Aun así, con 2607 recomendaciones totales, está claro que a mucha gente le funcionó: no por perfecto, sino por tener personalidad y balas de sobra.

Thirty-eight hours in *Kane & Lynch*, and at this point I’m convinced the real achievement isn’t finishing the game , it’s surviving long enough to understand why I kept coming back.

This isn’t the kind of crime game where you walk in feeling like a legend. It’s the kind where you walk in feeling like a bad idea.

From the first few minutes, *Kane & Lynch* makes one thing very clear: this will not be smooth, heroic, or remotely professional. Plans collapse instantly. Gunfights turn into panic. Cover feels optional. And somehow every situation manages to get worse in ways that feel almost artistically disrespectful.

And honestly? That’s exactly why it works.

Most games want you to feel like a master criminal.
*Kane & Lynch* makes you feel like two men who should absolutely not be trusted with a car, a weapon, or a five-minute strategy meeting.

After 38 hours, I’ve spent enough time with Kane and Lynch to realize their greatest superpower isn’t violence , it’s turning every “this can’t possibly get worse” moment into a challenge to fate.

What kept me hooked wasn’t perfection. It was the raw chaos of it all. The grimy atmosphere. The constant tension. The sense that every mission is one bad decision away from becoming a historical event for local law enforcement.

And somehow, against all logic, it becomes weirdly compelling.

By hour 38, I wasn’t playing to win anymore.
I was playing because I needed to know what fresh disaster these two would create next.

Would I recommend *Kane & Lynch*?

If you want polished crime fantasy, probably not.
If you want the digital equivalent of being trapped in the world’s worst criminal partnership — and enjoying every glorious trainwreck of it , absolutely.

It’s messy. It’s rough. It’s chaotic.
And somehow, that chaos has character.

Kane & Lynch: Dead Men nos narra una breve historia de acción y venganza (te la puedes pasar en un día) como si de una peli de Jason Statham se tratara. El juego realmente se enfoca en Kane, aunque se puede jugar con Lynch de manera cooperativa, pero sólo en local.

La historia empieza con Kane siendo rescatado de un transporte de prisioneros gracias a Los7, un grupo de mercenarios del que Kane formaba parte y que por lo visto les traicionó robándoles (lo que se supone una gran cantidad de dinero). Ahora que han dado con él deberá devolverles lo que es suyo o asesinarán a su familia y, para asegurarse de ello, han asignado a Lynch para que supervise y ayude a Kane en su misión, pero un giro de los acontecimientos llevará a Kane y Lynch a enfrentarse en una guerra directa contra Los7.

El juego presenta una historia chula con escenarios muy diferentes: empiezas atracando un banco pero luego te envuelves en una guerra civil en Cuba, incluso asaltando un rascacielos de Tokio. No falta acción en el juego, que además siendo del 2007 contaba ya con destrucción parcial del entorno. Aun así, el juego se reduce únicamente a avanzar y matar, con poco desarrollo narrativo del resto de personajes salvo Kane por evidencias de la trama, pero siendo Lynch uno de los deuteragonistas lo único que sabemos es que es un esquizofrénico que se automedica. Es una historia que va a saco, divertida y con buena dosis de acción.

Pero pese a lo muy corto de la historia, aunque esté chula, se trata de un juego antiguo y hay cosas que no llegan a cuajar del todo. Lo primero de todo es que utiliza el ya muerto GFWL, que personalmente no me ha dado problemas pero a otros usuarios sí (basta con instalarlo aparte y ya), aunque lo que más me ha fastidiado es que el juego presenta un problema de stuttering, el cual parece que hay un fix online pero sólo si juegas con ratón y teclado, yo habiendo jugado en PC lo he tenido que sufrir. Por otro lado a veces hay problemas de audio con las voces que se escuchan flojo. Los aliados, que puedes comandarlos a que ataquen a determinados enemigos y te sigan, a veces se van tan lejos que acaban siendo masacrados, y debes revivirles antes de un tiempo o fracasarás la misión. Y por último el recoil está mal hecho, ya que estando quieto y disparando únicamente un tiro no sabes a qué dirección va a ir la bala.

[h1]6.5/10[/h1]
Pese a los problemas que menciono el juego se deja jugar y se disfruta. Contaba con un multijugador curioso llamado Frágil Alianza en el que se podía traicionar a los aliados para quedarte con el botín del atraco y jugar una especie de Policías y Ladrones, pero con el GFWL y la carencia de red es imposible siquiera jugarlo.

Actualmente la franquicia Kane & Lynch cuenta con este y otro juego más, aunque justamente Dead Men se encuentra descatalogado de Steam porque los desarrolladores van a hacerles mejoras al juego, pero eso data ya del 2021. Se puede comprar la Kane & Lynch Collection en páginas de claves, aunque me salió por 20 euros más o menos, lo que considero caro en relación a la poca durabilidad que ofrecen ambas experiencias, pero entendible al tratarse de clásicos.

Ah, Kane & Lynch. The once over‑hyped, “promising and unique” project I knew about back in the day but never actually played until now, 2026. And wow… this game did not age well.

The Good (well… “okay”)
The core idea behind the story is decent. You can tell the devs wanted to build something gritty, emotional, maybe even psychological.

There are glimpses of what could’ve been a genuinely interesting narrative with complex characters.

The Not‑So‑Good
Graphically and mechanically, the game feels ancient.

Shooting is rough for a good half of the campaign. The ballistic spread is absurd.

Dialogue feels like it was written by a bored 10‑year‑old.

The story has zero direction. Great concept, no execution.

AI is painfully dumb.

Level and location choices are… strange, to put it politely.

The Verdict
Kane & Lynch had a lot of potential. It could’ve been a gritty, emotional crime story with depth. Instead, it’s a blunt, repetitive shooter with an uninteresting plot and clumsy gameplay.

5/10 at release

4/10 today

Honestly, better to stay away unless you’re revisiting it purely for curiosity or nostalgia.

Об этой игре я знаю очень давно, и знаю я её как легендарный шутер от третьего лица. И, проходя игру, я понимал, почему её таковой считают. Из того, что на поверхности, так это графика: для 2007 года её можно назвать эталонной, ну или как минимум близкой к этому. Даже сейчас, в 2025 году, её не назовёшь какой-то вырвиглазной или супер устаревшей — она вполне смотрится наравне с играми вплоть до 2010–2011 года, а это уже о многом говорит. Можно сказать, она опередила своё время.

Второй момент — это режиссура и постановка. Игра выглядит очень стильно и профессионально, так, как будто бы ты играешь в дорогой голливудский боевик.
На протяжении всей игры у меня было ощущение, что я где-то это уже видел. Не буду делать каких-то заявлений, но мне кажется, что многие разработчики вдохновлялись данной игрой — от каких-то уровней до самих персонажей. Брать тех же главных героев, Кейна и Линча: на протяжении всей игры я видел в них Майкла и Тревора из GTA 5. Кейн — гений преступного мира, для которого ограбление банка — это достаточно повседневное дело, и Линч — псих, убивший свою жену, который без таблеток не может протянуть и дня и каждый раз норовит убить важного заложника. Да и сцена с ограблением небоскрёба очень похожа на ограбление ФСБ в той же GTA 5. Атмосфера и эстетика мне очень напомнили Max Payne 3.
А, проходя эпизод с ночным клубом, я не мог отделаться от ощущения, что играю в Джон Уик: толпы людей, синие лазеры, которые едва освещают большое помещение, и редкие враги с фонарями, которые пытаются выцелить тебя из толпы. Пожалуй, это лучший эпизод в игре, очень интересный с точки зрения постановки, так как данную локацию мы проходим 3 раза в разных условиях. Первый раз — просто идём до офиса директора сквозь толпу, выслушивая бредни Линча. Второй раз — похитив директора, мы идём назад и перестреливаемся с малочисленными врагами, пытаясь увидеть их в толпе паникующих людей. И третий раз — мы возвращаемся через шорткат обратно в кабинет и вынуждены снова идти по этому коридору, но в этот раз все посетители разбежались, и нам предстоит сразиться уже с большим количеством хорошо вооружённых бойцов. Крайне интересный эпизод, который, наверное, и ассоциируется у меня с этой игрой.

И всё это звучит как вполне себе отличная игра. В принципе, первая её половина и вправду отличная, но чем дальше в лес — тем больше дров.

Сюжет, пожалуй, самая слабая часть игры. Он переполнен огромным количеством дыр и несостыковок, а порой и откровенного бреда. Буквально в начале игры главные герои грабят банк, чтобы Кейн вскрыл свою же ячейку, потому что он сбежал из тюрьмы и у него не было документов. Зато на следующий день персонажи уже находятся в Японии (да, документы им уже были не нужны для этого), устроили хаос в ночном клубе, похитили человека — и назад в Америку, делов-то. А потом вообще нас закидывает в Венесуэлу, где идёт гражданская война… (да, вот такой вот резкий и непонятно чем обоснованный переход от ограбления небоскрёба в джунгли Венесуэлы). И босс-вертолёт в наличии — куда уж игре начала 2000-х без босса-вертолёта. И уровень в джунглях в стиле Рэмбо имеется — куда уж игре начала 2000-х без уровня в джунглях.
И резкость не только в странном повороте сюжета, но и в смене качества игры: первая половина игры кажется новаторской, интересной и стильной… Вторая половина — посредственной, вторичной и скучной.

Как вишенка на торте — стрельба, в шутере от третьего лица, — и в неё неприятно стрелять. По мне, такого вообще быть не должно. При том что в игре достаточно неплохие модели оружия, неплохой арсенал, отличные звуки, даже присутствует достаточно приятная отдача, стрельба не ощущается дубовой… и может даже показаться, что я её пытаюсь сейчас похвалить… так бы и было, если бы не разброс, который сделали настолько большим, что единственный способ попадать — это всегда сближать дистанцию до минимально возможного расстояния. Ты буквально дальше 5–10 метров ни во что не попадёшь. И так и выходит, что в игре есть один ствол, у которого более-менее всё норм, и ты только с ним и ходишь, всё остальное — просто мусор. Этот небольшой, казалось бы, момент, который к тому же очень легко отрегулировать, перечёркивает вообще всё удовольствие от стрельбы. На протяжении всего прохождения я не понимал: неужели это не тестировали? Неужели до выхода игры никто не заметил слона в посудной лавке? Как это дошло до релиза — я просто не понимаю!

За всё время я около 5 раз начинал проходить эту игру, и каждый раз я её забрасывал на миссии в Венесуэле. В моей памяти она всегда была великой игрой, каждый уровень в ней мне запомнился. Режиссура и стиль игры действительно заслужили, чтобы как можно большее количество людей с этим ознакомилось. Но то количество минусов всегда перевешивало и не давало мне дойти до конца. Можно простить игре, если в неё скучно играть, но интересно следить за сюжетом. Можно простить игре унылый сюжет, если в неё интересно играть. Но тут как раз тот случай, когда в игру неприятно играть, в этот сюжет ты просто не веришь — настолько бреда налепили.
Сегодня я всё-таки её прошёл. Поставил цель — закрыть гештальт. Прошёл игру за 3.5 часа (в среднем прохождение занимает 4–5; я же прошёл быстрее, так как неплохо знаю локации и можно сказать, спидранил), и, конечно, я не жалею о потраченном времени. Оно точно стоило того, чтобы поставить себе эту галочку, тем более что, в принципе, первые 1.5–2 часа прошли больше с удовольствием, чем с негативом.

Conflict: Denied Ops è uno sparatutto in prima persona del 2008 (Pivotal Games, pubblicato allora da Eidos e oggi su Steam sotto Square Enix) e, di fatto, l’ultimo capitolo della serie Conflict.

Nel 2025 ha senso prenderlo solo con l’idea giusta: un FPS vecchia scuola, “rumoroso” e diretto, che punta tutto su ritmo, esplosioni e ambienti distruttibili, non su finezza o modernità. La sua carta migliore resta la distruzione scenica: coperture che cedono, muri che si aprono, esplosioni che vi fanno avanzare a forza. Ancora oggi può divertire, se vi lasciate trascinare dal suo impatto immediato.

Se questa recensione esiste, è soprattutto per un atto d’amore e nostalgia verso un franchise che mi ha dato tanto. Desert Storm (1 e 2) e Global Terror sapevano far sentire dentro una squadra, con più ruoli, più varietà e quella “tattica leggera” che rendeva le missioni più personali. Proprio per questo Denied Ops è stato anche una delusione: ridurre tutto a due soli soldati e due ruoli toglie identità al gruppo e spegne quel senso di team che era parte del fascino della serie.

A questo si aggiungono limiti inevitabili: struttura spesso ripetitiva, feeling da titolo d’epoca e qualche spigolo tecnico. E nel 2025 la co-op online non è una promessa tranquilla: può funzionare, ma non è il motivo giusto per sceglierlo oggi.

Denied Ops vale come “capsula del tempo” per chi cerca un FPS semplice, distruttibile e anni 2000, accettando compromessi. Per chi vuole una co-op moderna e stabile, o uno sparatutto più profondo e vario, conviene guardare altrove. Resta la speranza che qualche azienda videoludica riprenda Conflict: basterebbe tenere quell’anima action, riportare una squadra da quattro, e costruirci sopra gunplay moderno e cooperativa fatta bene.

Conflict: Denied Ops represents a bold but uneven departure from the formula that originally defined the Conflict series. Developed by Pivotal Games and published by Square Enix, it abandons the four-soldier, tactical third-person structure that longtime fans had come to expect, replacing it with a streamlined first-person co-op shooter centered on just two operatives: Lincoln Graves, the quiet and calculating sniper, and Reggie Lang, the loud and heavy-hitting machine gunner. This stripped-down pairing is at the heart of the game’s identity. Instead of managing a full squad with layered tactics, players bounce between—or directly control—these two characters as they infiltrate global hot zones and attempt to dismantle a nuclear threat orchestrated by a Venezuelan general. The result is a game that trades strategic depth for high-octane action, and while this shift brings flashes of fun spectacle, it also exposes limitations in pacing, structure, and design philosophy.

The gameplay emphasizes simplicity above all else. You move through linear missions built around firefights, explosive destructible elements, and the buddy-action dynamic between Graves and Lang. Each agent has a fixed combat role: Graves snipes from afar with precision and stealth, while Lang dominates close-quarters battles with sheer firepower. Switching between them mid-combat is a defining mechanic, enabling players to position one operative strategically before jumping to the other to execute a powerful attack or suppress an enemy line. When playing cooperatively with another human, this system feels more natural, allowing each player to embody a specific role in a way reminiscent of classic action duos. In single-player, however, the experience is inconsistent. The partner AI can behave erratically, leaving you vulnerable during heated firefights or forcing you to micromanage positioning that should feel intuitive. Despite this, the raw gunplay can be enjoyable in bursts, particularly when demolishing walls and cover with heavy weapons, a feature the game heavily promoted at launch.

One of the defining traits of Denied Ops is its emphasis on destructible environments. Many walls, barriers, and structures can be blown apart, creating improvised routes or exposing enemies who thought they were safe behind cover. This mechanic injects energy into encounters and provides a welcome sense of freedom compared to the more rigid battlefield design seen in earlier Conflict titles. Explosions, collapsing scenery, and debris flying across rooms contribute to the game’s aggressive, bombastic tone. In this respect, Denied Ops successfully embraces its identity as an over-the-top shooter rather than attempting to replicate the more methodical pacing of its predecessors. The missions span several global settings—from South America to Russia and Africa—yet despite the geographical variety, the mission flow often feels repetitive due to the simplistic objectives and predictable encounter layouts.

Narratively, the game stays firmly in action-movie territory. The plot revolves around preventing a nuclear catastrophe, but the story never digs deep into geopolitics or stakes. Instead, it leans heavily on the dynamic between Graves and Lang, whose banter alternates between camaraderie and caricature. Their personalities are intentionally exaggerated—the stoic marksman vs. the brash heavy—but while their interactions add some flavor, they rarely elevate the campaign beyond serviceable storytelling. The supporting cast is thin, and mission briefings rarely offer more than functional context. This leaves the narrative feeling like an afterthought, present mainly to give structure to the action rather than to immerse the player in a meaningful world.

From a technical standpoint, the game shows its age. The visuals, while functional, feature muted color palettes, stiff animations, and environments that can appear flat despite their destructibility. Controls feel noticeably better on PC than on console, especially for sniping, but even then, the aiming and movement can feel sluggish at times. Enemy AI is inconsistent—sometimes overly passive, sometimes unreasonably accurate—and these fluctuations make certain encounters feel artificially difficult or awkwardly easy. The audio design, dominated by machine-gun rattles and explosive effects, supports the action well enough, though voice acting and dialogue delivery tend to land in the realm of cheesy rather than compelling.

What ultimately shapes the experience of Conflict: Denied Ops is expectation. Approached as a continuation of the tactical Conflict series, it can feel jarringly shallow. Approached as a short, chaotic co-op action shooter, it becomes easier to appreciate its strengths: the destructible environments, the buddy-system design, and the breezy, popcorn-movie pacing. The game is at its best when played cooperatively, where its limitations fade into the background and its simple, loud, and exaggerated firefights become more entertaining. In single-player, however, the flaws—AI shortcomings, repetitive mission design, and constrained weapon variety—stand out more sharply.

In the end, Conflict: Denied Ops is an experiment that succeeds in ambition but stumbles in execution. It represents a franchise attempting to reinvent itself for a more action-oriented market but losing some of the depth and identity that originally made it stand out. For players who enjoy straightforward shooters with big explosions, easy-to-grasp mechanics, and co-op antics, it offers a still-serviceable dose of entertainment. But for those seeking refined tactical gameplay, cohesive storytelling, or polished design, it remains an uneven entry in the series—memorable in concept, but inconsistent in delivery.

It's difficult to figure out where to start but, let me try and summarise this game.

Conflict: Denied Ops, is a bottom of the barrel, bottom of the bargain bin FPS made by a dev team that clearly had no idea how to make a shooter. Not only are the controls a disaster, the concept is tired even when they were trying this, and the story is almost non-existent, the level design is just atrocious, and the entire structure of the singleplayer campaign is just garbage.

Basically, they messed up everything you can imagine that it is possible to mess up. EVERYTHING is bad.

So let's talk about the shooting itself since it's the most important. It is genuinely almost impossible to shoot enemies in this game. You might be wondering what I am talking about - it's a shooter, so you just aim and click right? Well, yes, except, first up they decided that aim down sights should be LEFT SHIFT instead of RMB, and they clearly didn't think much of aiming, or understand how to make ADS feel good, because instead of your gun being accurate during ADS, your gun is still what feels like pretty much the same accuracy as just hipfire spray-and-pray.

And that accuracy is terrible. TERRIBLE. I am speaking mostly from experience of playing as the horribly stereotypical black army man, because he gets an LMG with a 100 and then later 200 round magazine, and your only alternate is the grumpy white man's sniper rifle, which you might think would be a step up, except in his case you get scope sway that makes you feel like you just drank 16 beers. It makes aiming with it just outright impossible, I think the game may actually want you to like stop, completely stop moving, stand still, and then wait for 5 seconds before taking a single shot, but it's completely impractical to do, because even if you use the stupid gun camera for shooting around corners, you can STILL be shot at, and you REALLY do not want to be shot at by any enemy, ever.

By the way, this is a game where you die from about 4 or 5 bullets, on NORMAL difficulty.

Now let's talk about the enemies. Every single enemy in this game is way better than they have any right to be, they are way stronger than you, to the point in the last couple of levels but particularly the last one, every single enemy becomes a full on black ops soldier with near perfect accuracy. This game also reminded me of certain other games from this era like Rage, where, every enemy can basically interact with the environment and blind fire and do all this stuff that you can't do whatsoever, and you're left literally wondering why you are so weak and being sent on this stupid two-man mission to solo what appears to be multiple armies of guys, all across the world.

So this coupled with the level design sets you up with a predicament where you are constantly up against enemies that, outgun you, outrange you, outshoot you, and after a certain point they ALL take WAY more bullets than you to kill, so in a straight up bullet hose duel, you LOSE. In the last level, basically every soldier is some kind of spec ops guy in FULL black attire, which I guess is to signify they are the MOST elite men ever, which is just great because each guy takes like 15-20 bullets to kill and that's if they all hit, it's insane, these guys just don't die. And again - NORMAL difficulty.

I played on Normal because, sometimes you play these low budget shooters where you just get a bad feeling about them and, on this occasion it proved to be right. I would have probably played on easy just to speed things up, but I couldn't.

Anyway, so aside from the shooting being terrible, there's only like 5 weapons in this game. You get the LMG, the sniper rifle which is more like a DMR, a masterkey shotgun, an underslung grenade launcher, and a rocket launcher for dealing with the MULTIPLE vehicles the game throws at you, all of which you have no business fighting, especially given this rocket launcher fires unguided missiles - and the game throws not only helicopters but PLANES at you. You just literally have to shoot and hope for the best.

In this game, you control two army soldier men. Whichever one you aren't controlling is done by the AI. You can issue some vague orders but most of the time, about 90% of the time, you just want him to follow you around and do his thing.

So one of the most prevalent things in this game is that you will die nearly constantly. But don't worry, if you die, your buddy can pick you up! Provided he doesn't die too. But don't worry, your buddy gets what seems like either a big bonus to his health while the AI is controlling him, or, just very strong health regeneration, or both. Enemies can still very easily kill him, but he is still WAY more sturdy than he is if YOU are controlling him.

This means generally when you are on the ground you absolutely do NOT want to control your buddy, you just want to tell the AI to come revive you - which you can do and it will do, posthaste. Since it has that extra HP, it'll probably manage it. The only problem is the 'get back up' animation for your guy takes FOREVER so it's very common to get revived, begin to stand up, then die again while trying to stand up. Which is just great.

Suffice it to say, the game is incredibly frustrating. The game is full of giant open rooms littered with catwalks and waist-high cover that the enemies all love to hide behind. To the game's credit, the enemy AI is quite good in the sense that it does a good job murdering you, it can even launch what seems like surprise attacks to me where it'll chill in cover, then duck out and blast you if you leave cover, usually killing you instantly.

This is not a lot of fun to deal with though, and thus, it's frustrating.

The level design too struck me as very... amateurish, tedious, since every level is kind of like one long linear one most of the time where you have to just backtrack to the start of the level once you get to the end, which is just awful. Also, it reminded me of Counter-Strike: Condition Zero Deleted Scenes, which was a bunch of singleplayer levels made by a dev studio, for Counter-Strike 1.6, and the original Condition Zero. The idea was, they basically came up with a bunch of 'ingredients' for their level designers to play with, like weapons, satchel charges and scripted events and stuff, within the concept of 'counter-terrorism'. And then they just made a whole bunch of levels, completely unrelated, none interconnected, with these mixed ingredients.

This game had a similar feel, in that every level kind of felt like it was made by a different team, because so many of them ended in weirdly similar ways. Like several different people all decided to make their level end with you shooting down a helicopter or something, and several different people decided to end their mission with 'hold here until your helicopter arrives' and then a different team had a different idea and just had the mission just end.

Anyway I hated this game. It was just bland and terrible. It was not fun, it wasn't funny. Even in the worst shooters, usually you can at least point to some interesting design concepts, or at least enjoy the FPS elements, but this game didn't even have that.

I am not sure, but I have a feeling they were trying to make this game purely for commercial reasons, it feels very cynical and it doesn't feel like anyone who made this was really in it for the passion. It's hard to see this game as anything more than a paycheck to whoever made it. The main game I know of other than this game from Pivotal is Conflict: Desert Storm, and that was a very different, tactical, third person shooter.

It feels like this game, was trying to aim for the Call of Duty crowd, but it falls so pathetically short and it's so misguided that it had no hopes of truly being successful. It feels to me like the death throes of a studio, and they made this game, and the studio shuttered the same year of its release.

So yeah. Avoid this game.

There are games much older than this, that are still fun to play. The problem with this game, is it hits the bucket list of the shooters of the time, but does none of them well. 
The only thing that it does okay, is its destructible environments. Pretty good for the time, boxes and wooden walls rip apart satisfyingly under fire, and there's usually enough explosive barrels/objects around for that classic instant kill. 
There is a scene early on, where you take down a Hind, and it does the typical helicopter death spiral, and comes crashing down towards you. I sat there watching it, expecting it to fly off-screen, realizing too late, it was coming down on my head, bringing beams and parts of the building with it.

Я без шуток. За последнее время, перебирая библиотеку Стима, я видел такой мусор, в который вы, люди, даже бы не поверили. И этот морально устаревший даже на момент релиза, кривой и косой боевик - одна из вершин наиболее отвратительного игрового опыта, который я получал.

Начну с того, что у меня в целом вопросы к милитари-шутерам как к жанру; точнее, мне они просто не нравятся. Здесь, гоняя двух вояк по всему миру ради несения демократии, я потерял интерес к героям и сюжету примерно на первых 15 минутах, даже не вслушиваясь в диалоги - а хер ли, субтитров-то нет, локализации по дефолту нет, а звук в игре не самый выдающийся, чтобы все это вообще на полном серьезе слушать. 

Этот тактический боевик предлагает для управления сразу двух героев, и реализация этого максимально плоха; на удивление, разочаровал союзный ИИ, который даже на средней сложности в большинстве случаев скорее обуза, чем помощь. Добавьте к этому довольно скудный арсенал и набор из 10 миссий, где после каждой вы получите халявный апгрейд. 

Казалось бы - прошел, плюнул и забыл. 

Но какой-то мудак-разработчик придумал миссию на руднике с обороной от врагов на открытом месте под конец... Если что - чуть ли не треть времени на текущем таймере (а, может, и добрая половина) у меня ушло именно на несколько десятков попыток это пройти. И вот, сегодня я это прошел это задание до конца - и следом добил всю игру, пробиваясь еще три уровня через ее кривизну, тупорылость и неинтуитивность.

Конечно, я не игрок в тактические шутеры, это правда; но если в вашем [i]сингловом[/i] тактическом шутере союзники не дотягивают даже близко до уровня напарников из Star Wars Republic Commando (молчу про лаконичность и удобство управления отрядом в последней) - может, не стоит игру делать вообще?

Если вы это купили (скорее всего, просто в большом паке, как и я) - скройте с глаз в библиотеке. Если начали играть, но не уверены в своих силах - ставьте сложность ниже.

Но еще лучше - просто избегайте покупки.

Underworld:

Two steps forward one step back

We got a refinement of all the previous installments, the culmination of the LAU trilogy and the last hurrah before a long hiatus.

Underworld presents us with a more mature  Lara and the pinnacle of her design throughout the series, also the first time she has been motion captured, every ability and movement option has been revised and improved upon.

The game starts in media res before leading us all over the globe in search for Avalon and the conclusion of the story set in the last two games. No level overstays it welcomes and have a good balance of exploration, platforming, combat and some bike riding here and there, although they never drag as in Legend and its even incorporated into proper puzzles.

The jump in visual quality is jaw dropping with some of the best scenery in any tomb raider. (Make sure to turn off fullscreen effects as bloom is way overtuned)

For the negatives sadly the game struggles at times with some slight stuttering.

Collectibles no longer integrate naturally into the enviroments nor offer a reward for engaging with the platforming as they are all inside same looking jars that stop you on your tracks and play an overly grating sfx at pick up.

The animations themselves are top notch although the way they sped up some of them and how the transition between animations can look a little stiff or uncanny at times.

You can tell it was slightly rushed out of the door and the studio was for the most part split with anniversary's development. Still its a great game on its own right, far better than the survivor slop trilogy, and an excellent send off to the saga before a long hiatus.

Также могу отметить, что это самая мелкая игра из трилогии по продолжительности прохождения, что обидно. Также нет DLC, которые выпускались на консолях, почему не добавили на PC - непонятно. Pra mim me dói muito ter que dar uma avaliação negativa para um jogo de uma franquia que tem sido minha favorita desde a infância, ainda mais pelo fato de que o problema não é o jogo, mas sim a portabilidade para PC...

É preciso fazer diversas configurações, para que torne ao menos jogável, um dos mais bizarros é que se você usa algum monitor acima de 60 Hz você precisa travar a placa de vídeo nessa taxa ou em 30 se possível, caso o contrario nada funciona direito, texturas bugam, colisões bugam, comandos não respondem de forma esperada, câmera em espaço pequenos simplesmente enche a tela de screen tearing, ao encostar em determinados pontos (geralmente rampas) aleatoriamente você vai a óbito.

São coisa que uma vez ou outra a gente suporta, mas ao longo do jogo inteiro se torna frustrante, é uma pena mesmo que tenham feito a portabilidade sem se quer um pingo de carinho

2026年体验最糟糕的一部古墓丽影：
1.与新机器设备的极不兼容，修改cpu数量同时锁60帧垂直同步能提高小关卡加载的稳定性，但是无法解决大关卡加载闪退问题，通关需要依靠存档资源
2.优化问题，同样只打汉化补丁的情况下，前作传奇和10周年都能完美4k120帧运行且全程无闪退，后出的地下世界由于制作赶工经常卡顿闪退
3.视角跟随相比十周年的水平退步巨大，爬墙经常出现不受控制的视角乱转后回正
4.宝藏设计最敷衍的一作，路边三个罐子堆一起就算一个收集点是何意味
5.剧情上无功无过，但是感觉有6代黑暗天使的韵味
6.战斗没有前作爽快，随时能换装备的设定导致弹药火力基本溢出，失去了往作收集不同武器弹药和资源管理应战的乐趣
7.后期谜题的引导欠缺打磨，新加入的现场指导功能只是比十周年笔记有用一点

最好的优点：
最早接触到劳拉的版本就是本作开场的潜水服，同人作品给小脑刻下的精神烙印支撑我打完了游戏。
如果官方以后更新了新机器的优化补丁解决运行问题，本作还是值得给个好评推荐

테마파크 같은 유적지를 뛰어다니고 퍼즐을 풀며 길을 나아가는 액션어드벤처게임, 툼레이더 레전드 삼부작의 세 번째 편인 언더월드입니다. 더욱 발전한 그래픽과 라라의 동작들, 조작에 곧바로 반응하는 라라의 움직임, 좀 더 직관적인 동선 유도와 전투 공간 활용 등, 현 세대의 게임 구성 스타일에 발을 많이 걸친 느낌이라 상당히 편하게 즐길 수 있었습니다. 전작들과 출시일 차이가 그리 크지 않은데 상당히 많은 부분이 달라졌네요. 그래도 여전히 뭔가 삐걱대는 카메라시점이 오래전 게임이라는 느낌을 주지만요.

 가장 마음에 들었던 점은, 보스전을 과감하게 없애고 보스전에 해당하는 것은 큰 규모의 환경 기믹 퍼즐로 만들었다는 점이었습니다. 애니버서리, 레전드, 둘 다 보스전의 기믹전투에 상당히 불만이 컸기에, 정말 반가운 변화였습니다. 물론 보스전이 없다는 점에서 오는 아쉬움도 분명 있지만, 기존 방식대로 만들 거면 차라리 이런 형태가 낫겠다 싶네요.
 그리고 그래픽 역시 지금 시점에서 봐도 나쁘지 않은 정도였습니다. 상당히 넓은 공간을 향상된 그래픽으로 둘러볼 수 있게 돼서 주변 환경 구경하는 재미도 좋았구요. 특히 바닷속 환경이 기억에 남네요. 

 삼부작 중에 가장 즐겁게 플레이한 게임이었습니다. 재밌게 즐겼네요.

Tomb Raider: Underworld é um daqueles jogos que me fazem lembrar por que amo tanto essa franquia. A Lara Croft é minha personagem favorita dos jogos, e poder acompanhar mais uma de suas aventuras é sempre uma experiência especial para mim. Uma das coisas que mais gostei foi a jogabilidade. Explorar os cenários, escalar paredes, saltar entre plataformas e resolver os enigmas torna tudo muito divertido. Gosto de como o jogo faz você se sentir realmente explorando lugares antigos e misteriosos, sempre com aquela sensação de que existe algo esperando para ser descoberto. Os cenários são lindos, principalmente os ambientes antigos, as ruínas e os lugares escondidos. É muito gostoso explorar cada canto e descobrir os segredos que o jogo guarda. A sensação de aventura está presente o tempo todo.
  Outra coisa que amo é a própria Lara. Ela é inteligente, corajosa, independente e tem uma personalidade que faz dela uma personagem inesquecível. Para mim, ela é muito mais do que uma protagonista de videogame. Tenho um carinho enorme por ela e pela história dessa franquia.
 A história também consegue prender a atenção, principalmente para quem já acompanha as aventuras da Lara e quer descobrir mais sobre sua jornada. Claro que algumas partes podem ser um pouco difíceis, e certos movimentos exigem paciência, mas isso não tira a diversão. Na verdade, superar esses desafios deixa tudo ainda mais gratificante.
  No geral, Tomb Raider: Underworld foi uma experiência que adorei. A exploração, os enigmas, os cenários e a jogabilidade fizeram com que eu aproveitasse muito o jogo. Talvez eu seja suspeita para falar, porque amo Tomb Raider, mas é difícil não gostar de uma aventura com a Lara Croft.
 É um jogo que me faz sentir aquela vontade de continuar explorando, descobrir todos os segredos e viver mais uma aventura ao lado de uma das personagens mais marcantes dos videogames.

  Para mim, Tomb Raider é muito mais do que uma franquia. É uma das minhas paixões nos jogos, e Underworld é mais um motivo para continuar amando esse universo. 🖤

I remember loving this game when it came out back in the day, but this most recent playthrough has cemented this as being a bottom-tier mainline Tomb Raider game.

Only play if you are a big fan of the franchise and want to see it all.

Underworld fu senza dubbio la punta di diamante della trilogia LAU, all'epoca di fatto acclamata per via della grafica di tutti e 3 i capitoli.
Ma a distanza di 20 anni?

Mentre Legend è ancora oggi giocabile, seppur graficamente datato ma con un gameplay ancora solido e la colonna sonora migliore della trilogia... Anniversary è quello invecchiato peggio, con la sola grafica a salvarlo se comparata con l'originale, ma con un gameplay e una storia a dir poco claudicanti.

Underworld si frappone tra i due e svetta vincitore di poco rispetto a Legend nella trilogia poiché, ovviamente, ha la grafica migliore e un gameplay corretto che risolveva i problemi visti nel secondo capitolo... non del tutto ma si vede che provarono a fare qualcosa.
Inoltre la storia qui prende finalmente piede per bene e prosegue praticamente gli avvenimenti di Legend stesso, Anniversary fu incastrato a forza in mezzo ai due ma il suo plot, se così si può chiamare, stonava non poco.
Menzione negativa a parte per la gestione della camera che qui è veramente da sickness pura,   in pratica va giocato tutto con la modalità mira per non vomitare.

Questo terzo capitolo merita quindi di essere recuperato? Si può dire di si, volendo anche direttamente dopo il primo e saltando il secondo, a meno che non siate curiosi di vedere la grafica del remake del 2007 (e auguri per quella del secondo remake dell'anno prossimo, ci vorrà come minimo una 5090).

Per alcuni questo è ancora l'ultimo, vero Tomb Raider... e Lara, prevedibilmente, è invecchiata bene.

Battlestations: Pacific is one of the best naval warfare games ever made, and there are very few games like it, especially with multiplayer. The multiplayer still works too, so if you can get into the game, there is still a community around it. What makes it so special is that it works as both a strategy game and an action game, letting you command the battle while also personally taking control of ships and planes. I put hundreds of hours into this on Xbox back in the day, and it remains one of my favorite naval combat experiences.

As of 2026, the game is still no longer available to purchase normally on PC. There are still keys available on other websites such as Humble Bundle, which is the cheapest and safest website. There is also another major issue after purchasing it. Because the game is so outdated, it relies on old Windows systems that no longer work properly, meaning the game may not run unless you follow installation guides. It took me a while to get it working, and not every computer will be able to run it successfully. Only buy this if you are willing to work through the guides and understand that getting it running may take some effort. 

Even with the hassle of buying it and getting it running, I still think the effort is worth it. Battlestations: Pacific is a beautiful game, and I genuinely hope it gets revived one day. R.U.S.E. was brought back recently, so maybe there is still hope for this title too.

省流：这是一个十六年前的游戏，重置和舰队决战等优秀mod让它焕发不彻底的新生。尽管它有各种各样的缺陷，但我还是乐意为它打出一个好评（在没有中评的情况下）。

目前购买和游玩方式：只能由cdkey入正——可以看看humble bundle的BSM+BSP捆绑包，我当时是全价70多元入正，也许也能等到打折。游戏需要已经失效的Windows Live，mod通常自带免xlive文件，这个文件本身也很容易搜到。亲测WIN11可以正常游玩。

异常主观的加减分项目：
+单机。对我个人来说很好，非常好。
+存在非常优秀的mod，首推重置和舰队决战。
+沉浸感强，存在日语英字补丁。游戏原版有此功能，却是损坏的，这很令人沮丧。
○画面，特别是特效细看略为过时，重复的音效和音乐也有相同问题。
○兵装的模块化伤害受限于年代和代码做得比较粗糙。
○每一件武器都没有第二个的整身涂装，只能通过mod替换！？！？！
○缺少绝对意义的自由视角，mod的电影视角也无法旋转镜头。
-无存档点设计下经常闪退，在各种意想不到的时候闪退，程序缺乏官方维护，这是最大的问题。
-更具体的游戏问题，一部分问题是由于代码限制导致的：如战役街机模式数据和战场表现（例如飞机飞行高度和海空单位速度）抽象、舰船防空火力太过凶猛（尤其是真实模式下）、航母甲板空置和舰载机编队和编队内飞机数量上限等。
-（上述缺点导致游戏性中最严重的问题是）在这个游戏框架内航母和飞机的重要性远不如战列舰。

以上，我个人愿意为这个游戏在打mod的情况下给出至少75/100的评价，至少我可以连续玩50个小时不感到厌倦——除了程序太能跳出了（玩十局七局闪退。现在要是有这样一款海战游戏，哪怕你就是端一个高清重制版我都买账。

结论：《战斗位置太平洋》多少有些死得太早，以至于没有mod加持的话它在各种方面都已经算得上过时。即使有mod，32位程序也经常出现不稳定和闪退。但在制作组解散、Square Enix不太可能重启这个项目的情况下，TFA正式发售前它的玩法在市面上依然几乎找不到替代品。优秀mod为这个游戏注入了新鲜血液，使得它的即时战略要素，辅以第一人称+第三人称直接操作飞机和舰船的沉浸感放在2025年都依然激动人心。

In 2025, with great regret it is a NO, not because they are bad games by any metric, BUT.......

      Some games are firmly locked within their time and the limitations / style of games dependent on their systems.  Battlestations Midway and it's latter sequel, essentially the story of the same Pacific War but told from a Japanese Pilots perspective rather than the first games American Pilot, were big news for Xbox 360 Owners such as I, due to there no really being very few flying games that weren't totally arcade and based upon Historical events.  So, upon time of release both these games offered something unique for the 360 with the player being able to command a Torpedo Boat, a Destroyer and rain down shellfire on enemy vessels, a Submarine for those torpedo attacks looking through the scope - complete with diving to evade the possible depth charge attacks to eventually controlling and commanding a fleet of ships in your mission to push back and regain the islands.  The best part for me personally was the Carrier gameplay where you could allocate wings of Torpedo Bombers, Dive Bombers and the Fighter Cover. Sending out Spotter Planes trying to catch a glimpse of the enemy fleet and organise an attack catching them unprepared and off guard, whilst always facing the risk you may get caught yourself with your pants down your fighters mid transit whilst the Imperial Japanese Airforce arrived to give your ships an Imperial Rogering ! 
    The campaign managed to hold your interest without becoming repetative. You could fly from 3rd person but what was great for a 360 game was the in-cockpit view and ability to switch to other Aircraft on the mission.  So, a very good Campaign and the games also featured a Multiplayer Skirmish option to extend the games life.  Also the ships, subs and planes all featured easy individual control schemes relevant to their class using the Xbox Gamepad. 
    Sadly though, these games released in that 'Games for Windows Live' period requiring an account registering and linked up to a now totally defunct website. The Graphics are bleeding edge Xbox 360, replaying these games today requires being able to find a work around to by pass the dreaded GFWL - which was do-able but havent attempted for quite some time now.  In complete honesty though, unless you have a particular affinity or desire to relive what these games offered and no longer own your old Xbox 360 copy....... Well, you're better leaving these games as the pleasant memorie you may have of playing them at the time, the Multiplayer won't be available ( unless someone has modded some way to do so ? ) you'll have to battle just to get the game to run on your system AND the BIG BIG final point, times have moved on and there's definitely better more modern games out there to scratch that itch.   A modern ground up version offering all the aspects this pair of game did, would be EPIC though, as the Pacific War doesn't seem to get as much exposure as the European side of the conflict, yet featured the Carrier upon Carrier warfare so many Science Fiction Space Sagas have used as their inspiration and although these games do not really touch upon the sheer brutality of what the Marines had to face out there on those islands, over all these games give a viewpoint from both sides and tell very well a story quickly fading into the dusty pages of history and the bravery of those men who fought there, many not to return.

J’y ai joué il y a longtemps, avant que ce soit sur Steam. J’ai rejoué un peu après… et bon, le jeu a vieilli. Beaucoup. 🚢💨

À l’époque, c’était stylé : des combats épiques, des porte-avions, des avions de chasse qui s’affrontent au-dessus du Pacifique, des explosions partout. Tu pouvais piloter un avion, diriger une flotte, bombarder des îles… bref, c’était la guerre totale et c’était génial.

Mais en y rejouant aujourd’hui, ça pique un peu. L’IA est parfois aux fraises, les graphismes ont pris un coup de vieux, et la maniabilité n’est plus aussi fluide qu’avant. C’est toujours fun, mais ça sent clairement le jeu d’une autre époque.

Bref, un bon souvenir, mais un jeu qui a un peu trop vieilli pour briller comme avant. 😕

If Battlefield 1942 was also an RTS, you'd get Battlestations: Pacific. You can control vehicles like planes, battleships and submarines and then seamlessly switch to a commander role as you order AI-controlled units around from a top-down view of the battlefield. It's arcadey but with realistic elements: You have infinite ammo, but you need to lead your shots. The third-person vehicle combat and RTS hybrid gameplay makes battles dynamic and engaging. Ok so I picked this up on and off a lot of times over a period of 4-5 months and I might not remember to mention some things in my review so I apologize for that, With that out of the way lets dive right in.

Just cause 2 is basically a sandbox game with a story you have the freedom to choose your missions, how you complete them, when you complete them then there are the weapons and mechanics there are a lot of possible ways to play this game you have 3 weapon slots 2 of them are "normal" weapons and the third one is reserved for "special" weapons then you also have a grappling hook which honestly by itself should be the only reason to get this game in the first place.


With the grappling hook you don't just move from place to place rather its a weapon and its extremely versatile for what it is, Want to hang enemies from the wall? Want to tie 2 vehicles together and watch them crash into each other? Want to make enemies fly by pinning them to a chopper? You can do all of that and much more with just the grappling hook.

Then there are the vehicles which are honestly better than whatever GTA has, a lot of them are built to kill even the airborne vehicles like choppers have turrets and cannons with which you rain hell upon your enemies and yes its as good as it sounds its extremely satisfying to decimate an entire military outpost via aerial assault.


Then there are the characters, factions and the story I'd say its pretty mid and maybe even bad on purpose there's this one guy who is supposed to represent an Indian sikh maybe? He is the leader of a faction called "Ular Boys"  and He keeps saying "Serdadu" (Soldier in Bahasa Indonesia and Bahasa Malaysia) after every sentence and it gets pretty annoying, the other two faction leaders aren't any better one of them is a commie slut and the other is a bald drug dealer. Then comes our protagonist Rico and his allies they're portrayed as stereotypical CIA operatives except for Rico who is supposed to show "human" side of the agency. The mission basically is to replace one dictator with another who is friendly to American interests and that's what we're sent to do there.

Lastly the issues, while not a lot I had to tweak a few settings because the game kept crashing even though I have specs that far exceed the recommended hardware and even after that during some cutscenes the game was prone to crashing and the only way to fix that was to replay from the last checkpoint.

I guess that sums it up completely now the question is do I recommend it? Yes, but not at the full price its an alright game but extremely repetitive and sometimes outright boring but still worth playing at least once.

去年通关了正当防卫1和3之后，一直想着抽空把2和4通掉。好巧不巧，去年年底经历了电脑坏掉和新房装修碰一起，老电脑还刚好坏了，玩这款老游戏都卡的要死。直到上个月终于配了新电脑，我才终于有机会把这部小时候玩了几个小时的大作从头到尾玩一遍。作为一款比较老的游戏，它的优化不是很好，虽然游戏内非常流畅，但每次玩十几二十分钟总会莫名其妙的闪退，好在我硬着头皮玩下来了。
剧情上，与前作一脉相承，我们扮演特工里科，去岛国帕瑙找寻老友，推翻残暴的军政府。没啥好说的，四部作品的故事虽然都连着，但是大同小异，套路都一样。主线任务只有七个，基本都是挨个清理据点，最终同反派对峙。没什么槽点也没什么亮点，毕竟游戏主打的就是一个战斗破坏爽，炸炸炸就完事了。
画面上，相较于前作有了极大的提升，我个人感觉和同一时代的显卡危机画质差不了多少，极其广袤的大地图据称有同一时期的GTA4的四五倍大，雪山、热带、海边、山脉等各种风景一应俱全，让人赏心悦目。玩家可以借助飞翼在天空自由驰骋，一步步爬到山顶或者从高空一跃而下。可惜的是，广阔的地图里面除了众多凑数的收集品以外，并没有什么有趣的细节或支线任务，互动性几乎为零，使得地图显得很空洞。
玩法上，凭借着不错的画面表现力，游戏的体验感在前中期是比较好的，肆意屠戮、爆破的感觉确实相当解压。本作的武器不是特别多，手感中规中矩，但作为一款开放世界射击游戏来说还是说得过去的。最有特色的还是手臂上的挂钩，这一经典道具可攻可守，像蜘蛛侠的蛛丝一样灵巧多变。它与降落伞构成的了一套奇特的移动与战斗系统，让主角的机动性达到了“上天入地”的级别，玩家可以用它快速穿梭于丛林、雪山和城市之间，也能在战斗中把敌人、载具从高处拽下，或是将两名敌人连接在一起让它们互撞。配合游戏鼓励制造混乱的开放设计，玩家可以用近乎任意、极其夸张方式摧毁军事基地或交通设施，充满了创造性和黑色幽默。
不过，本系列“炸炸炸”的爽快感只能维持一小会，一旦从中抽离，就会发现游戏在诸多设计上相当粗糙。剧情叙事几乎是摆设、动画呆滞、驾驶手感轻飘等等，一部分原因是时代的局限性，但另一方面也反映出设计的很多不足之处。
我个人评8.3分吧，正当防卫2就像杰森斯坦森的流水动作片，剧情简单无脑，特技和爆炸场面管够。它的核心乐趣在于纯粹的的物理破坏，如果你纯属找乐子，它依然能提供七八小时左右的解压体验。但如果你更看重沉浸式的故事或优秀的关卡设计，那么以现代标准来看，已经显得有些过时了。总的来说，不是很建议购买，找个视频花个十几分钟云一下剧情即可，直接玩三部和四部可以获得更加爽快和刺激的体验。

A game that feels like a Michael Bay game. It is fun for a bit but gets very repetitive quickly and most of the contents are copypaste. The map is REALLY BIG that would make Ubisoft blush. Every location activity is basically the same, grab boxes (with the aid of a hot and cold wifi icon on the top left of the screen which you'll be staring at often and the boxes used for upgrading weapons/vehicles/HP) and/or blow up stuff with red paint on it to get 100% for every location. Even the missions are mostly the same consist of blow stuff up, killing enemies, or vehicle delivery. A lot of other open world games does the gameplay loop similar way too, but at least those are more fun and this one gets boring very fast. I will say as a positive is that at least the locations and regions of the map are diverse enough. But every settlement locations feels the same but with some buildings and structures rearranged. You're forced to blow up stuff and cause chaos to unlock missions to progress he game. There are vehicle related content consist racing or flight piloting. Machine gun will mostly be your primary weapon due to its stats and how easy it is to get ammo for it from enemies instead of buying and pistol/revolver will be the same for your sidearms. I don't know why but you can't navigate the map screen with WASD but force to either drag with left click mouse or use the arrow keys. Also, to mark a location you have to use the SCROLL WHEEL CLICK. You can't rebind the map navigation keys. Also there is no borderless Fullscreen.

The only good thing I'll say about the game is being able to duel wield your 2 sidearms and the grapple hook mechanic. Combine the grappling hook with the parachute will be your main way of fast traversal beside using vehicles. You can do some silly things with the grappling hook like hook an NPC on a vehicle and drag them around, grappling hook climb, or hook link two things together. The grappling hook mechanic also turn the character into pseudo Spider-man, being able to zip around the map and stick surfaces with it.

Over all, 7/10. But I dropped the game. I'd give the game a mixed review if I could. Map is way unnecessarily big and is very repetitive. Getting 100% is mind numbingly boring. Achievements are grindy, tedious, difficult, and/or annoying to get. Don't go for 100% and just focus on missions.

This open world action sandbox game centers on chaotic sandbox destruction across a massive tropical island nation. Players control a secret agent tasked with overthrowing a local dictator through widespread rebellion activities. Traversing the environment relies heavily on a versatile grappling hook and parachute combination. Movement physics allow continuous momentum building across mountains, jungles, and urban centers. Causing general destruction fills chaos meters needed to unlock story missions.

The grappling hook mechanics serve as both a primary traversal tool and a combat weapon. Tethering enemies to moving vehicles or high structures creates endless creative possibilities. Parachuting combined with grappling allows infinite flight across the four hundred square mile map. Hijacking cars, boats, and helicopters mid movement keeps momentum steady during pursuits. Firearms and explosives provide destructive options for demolishing government property.

World design features diverse biomes ranging from dense jungles and snowy peaks to arid deserts and modern cities. Exploring settlements yields collectible weapon parts, vehicle upgrades, and monetary resource caches. Military bases and propaganda installations offer large scale destruction challenges filled with explosive targets. Fast travel options reduce tedious transit times across the vast island territory. Map completion metrics track settlement destruction percentages for dedicated completionists.

Visual presentation delivers bright, sprawling landscapes with impressive draw distances and dynamic weather effects. Explosions and fire physics produce spectacular chain reactions across military installations. Character models and vehicle designs maintain functional clarity during chaotic firefights. Audio design features punchy weapon reports, roaring engine sounds, and dramatic orchestral musical cues. Voice acting captures the B movie action tone effectively throughout cutscenes.

Replayability stems from endless sandbox experimentation using physics tethers and vehicle stunts. Unlocking black market weapon drops expands tactical choices during aggressive assaults. Optional faction missions offer varied objectives across different regions of the island. The overall package provides a thoroughly entertaining open world playground for action enthusiasts. Pure freedom of movement and destruction keeps repeat sessions engaging.

I experienced random crashes at different points during the casino mission, even after restoring the default graphics settings.

Go to Settings → Advanced Display Settings and try the following configuration:

Setting| Recommended Value
Texture Detail| Low
Shadow Quality| Low
Anti-Aliasing| Off
Anisotropic Filtering| 2x
Water Detail| Low
Object Detail| Low
Decals| Off
Particles| Off
V-Sync| Off
High-Res Shadows| Off
SSAO| Off
Point Light Specular| Off
Bokeh Filter| Off
GPU Water Simulation| Off

Also, under Display Settings, lower your resolution to 1920 × 1080 (1080p), especially if you normally play at 1440p or 4K. Even 720p.

Restart the game completely after applying these changes.

Главные особенности игры

• Огромный мир Панау: Вымышленное островное государство в Юго-Восточной Азии Just Cause 2 - Википедия поражает масштабами (площадью в сотни квадратных километров с разнообразными биомами — от тропиков до снежных гор).

Безумная свобода передвижения: Связка из фирменного крюка-кошки на левой руке и бесконечного парашюта позволяет летать над островом почти без остановок.

Культ разрушения: Сюжет здесь отходит на второй план Just Cause 2 - когда разрушаемость стала сюжетной. - DTF, уступая место хаосу. Чтобы продвигаться по игре, нужно взрывать военные базы, вышки и статуи диктатора Малыша Паная, ощущая себя героем голливудского боевика.


Как играется Just Cause 2 в 2026 году?

• Плюсы:
	• Физика полетов, взрывов и зацепления объектов друг за друга всё еще дарит массу веселья.
	• Игра отлично запускается на старом и среднем «железе», так как требования 2010 года по нынешним меркам мизерные.
	• Ощущение беззаботного экшена без душноты современных сервис-игр.

• Гринд: Для 100% прохождения или открытия всех улучшений придется зачищать сотни одинаковых маленьких поселений.
• Устаревшая механика: Побочные активности, стрельба и ИИ полиции и врагов сегодня выглядят архаично.
• Сюжет и диалоги: Наигранная серьезность вперемешку с комиксной абсурдностью воспринимается скорее как комедия.

This is undisputably the father of all open world games. No Grand Theft Auto game comes close to this masterpiece. 
In addition, this is also the best game of the Just Cause franchise in my opinion, despite the "dated" graphics.

While the story is moderate and straightforward, getting towards it's completion is what the game is about. 
Exploring the islands, experiencing different climates, destroying a lot, and I mean a lot of kaboomable stuff, driving, flying, grapple-hooking, racing, unravelling secrets, getting close towards the 100,00 % completion mark, are just a fraction of all the amazing stuff that make up Just Cause 2.

This is quite literally the wind-down-game after a long day of work or to just get your mind free.

To anyone who is reading comments about crashes - while this game isn't prone to crashing, the crashes happened a lot less on Win11 than Win10 from what I have experienced so far, just remember to save the game from time to time.

I can only recommend this game to anyone who wants to experience an actual open world game.

This game has been made with passion and heart and I am afraid that we won't get to see anything comparable anytime soon.

Just Cause 2 is about as deep as a puddle. But a very fun puddle! The game is incredibly simple - go around the map with your grappling hook and parachute, maybe drive some sort of vehicle, shoot some bad guys and blow some stuff up. That's pretty much it, with some subtleties in its implementation throughout.

The game doesn't care how you go about things. The achievements do encourage experimentation but nothing in the game itself mandates it. You can go about things however you want. You can do the missions you want, or you can just faff around in the sandbox. Either approach, or a combination of the two, should let you make progress through the story missions.

The game doesn't take itself seriously and is all the better for it. I would recommend knocking up the difficulty a notch so that encounters don't become rote. Higher difficulties will throw helicopter gunships and rocket launchers at you so gameplay doesn't become mindlessly dull. You can't change difficulty mid-campaign, so bear that in mind.

The map is surprisingly big and diverse. The game updates you with stats on various aspects of completion, like locations discovered and x/n "things" destroyed or collected. Those numbers all look big, but they're not overwhelming because the game doesn't much care if you do achieve 100% of any particular category. And they have to be big numbers so that the map isn't just an empty expanse that's a terrible place to spend time.

Mercenary mode means that you don't need to worry about locking yourself out of progression; all missions *should* be available to you even after the main campaign is finished.

Performance is an issue - decals and some visual fidelity settings will cause the game to crash, but resolving this is a couple of simple toggles, rather than having to install patches. But Square Enix really should address this (and Valve should make them) because it really is unacceptable to sell a game that crashes like this. But when it's not crashing the game looks and performs well.

Make of this game what you will; it's a fun romp!
