After my painful experience with "Sherlock Holmes: The Mystery of the Mummy", the next game in the series was this one, "Sherlock Holmes: The Silver Earring". At first glance the game seemed like a massive improvement over its predecessor, and this motivated me to start it soon after finishing the traumatic experience of completing the first game without using a guide. 

The whole game feels a lot more polished than the first game. It looks better, sounds better, and obviously had a lot more effort and money put into it. However, it was not long before the game revealed its true face...

First things first, the game again needs some tinkering until you get it working properly, but a lot less than the first game. After that, the game starts, and it can at first trick you into believing you are in for a nice and relaxing point & click experience. That is, until you get stuck at the first location because you need to find all the clues. This will take some time, because the game once again has moments where you are required to pixel hunt for stuff, and this first case of it is extremely evil, because the thing you are looking for is in a very tricky spot. You see, when you put your cursor over a door you can enter, it changes into a hand. Guess what it also turns into when you hover over an item you can interact with? Into a hand... That's as far as I'm going with this hint...

After I finally found all the clues, Holmes and Watson (who is present this time) returned to Baker Street, and I had to examine the clues. This was a bit cryptic, but you can figure it out pretty quickly with a bit of trial and error. However, what followed after was awful. The quiz...

You see, the quiz is essentially the way Frogwares wanted to simulate you leading an investigation. You get a set of questions, and you have to answer them and provide the right pieces of evidence to each question from the pool of all the evidence collected. It seemed like a nice idea until you realized that the game doesn't let you progress until you get all the questions right, and it doesn't tell you which one you answered right or wrong. The first quiz took 6 hours of my life. I asked for help from my friend, and he didn't prove so useful, so I asked him to look into the guide to check if the game broke, since there are literally discussion threads on Steam asking if the game is bugged during those quiz moments due to how cryptic and unintuitive to solve they are. After he confirmed everything was alright, I continued to torture myself for hours until I realized, quite admittedly, the stupid mistake I made... The second mistake I made was a lot more stupid, though, and not on my part.

Almost every quiz in the game has a question or two to which the answer is weird, or there are technically more answers to a single question. This feature of the game is so confusing that a lot of people in the reviews quite clearly admit to using a guide.

Moving on from the first level and first quiz, what followed was the second level, the most puzzle-dense level of the game. One I had to brute force, and then I got stuck on the following puzzle and asked for help from a second friend, which enlightened me, and I completed the puzzle that bothered me. For the second quiz, I luckily completed it pretty quickly, and then it was time for level three.

Here I got stuck on a puzzle for multiple hours. You need to open a safe by figuring out a combination with the help of some kind of a code. I again asked for help from the first friend, and this man, after finishing his 8-hour shift, sat down and wrote combinations on a paper until he finally found the answer, writing on the box of his pizza! This allowed me to continue the game. A stealth section followed soon after, and it was as awful as everybody else in the reviews says. It has less to do with hiding Holmes and more with hiding him from the invisible visibility cone of the guard and his dog, and I think that years of experience playing video games helped me to complete this part more than anything else. Quiz number 3, more pain, level 4.

Quite a quick and easy level, except for that timed maze part a lot of people are mentioning. Luckily, I managed to complete it pretty quickly. This part is very bad because it results in an instant game over without an option to retry, which means you can potentially softlock yourself if you save at a wrong time, which happened to one guy who made a thread about it on discussion boards. The fourth quiz again took multiple hours of my life.

Level 5 is short and easy, except for the part where you have to use an item on an item that doesn't show you can use an item on it, because, why not? The fifth quiz is the easiest of the bunch, and by this time you understand how they work. It also has the fewest questions.

Then the game allows you to answer optional questions to solve the crime, but I skipped those because I had no idea, and even after watching the final cutscene that plays right after that, I'm still not sure I completely understand everything.

To conclude, "Sherlock Holmes: The Silver Earring" is a clear example of that saying "two steps forwards, one step back". In a lot of ways, it is a better game than the first one, but the style, atmosphere, voice acting (which can also be quite questionable), and the story don't matter if the game is not fun, and I don't think it is... I wasted dozens of hours of my life on this and once again became obsessed with finishing the game, feeling like I can't play anything else until I beat the game. It was an awful experience, and I don't want to repeat it again. I don't recommend it, and I can see why when you search on the Sherlock Holmes subreddit, the first two games are barely mentioned, and even if they are, they are described as dated by everybody other than the most hardcore genre fans. Fascinating, since IGN reviewed this game also and quite positively at that, calling it easy. Either IGN was a lot better of a company before, or we are just stupid nowadays...

If you still want to play it, have a guide ready, and if you don't want to use it, like me. Well... be prepared for pain. But don't, if you can help yourself. Remember, games are supposed to be fun. This one is not...

A lazy, asset-flipped cash grab that insults the Sherlock Holmes name.

If you are coming to this game fresh off Frogwares' mainline 3D titles expecting an immersive, atmospheric detective thriller, turn back immediately. This is not a real Sherlock Holmes game; it is a cheaply produced, frustrating 2008 hidden-object spin-off stitched together with old materials.

Here is why you should absolutely avoid it:

• Shameless Asset Flipping: Frogwares didn't bother creating new environments for this game. Instead, they heavily recycled crime scenes and background art straight out of Sherlock Holmes: The Case of the Silver Earring (a game that came out four years prior in 2004).

• The Most Infuriating Pixel Hunts Imaginable: A hidden-object game relies on clever camouflage, but this title crosses the line into complete absurdity. You will spend huge chunks of time furiously clicking around low-resolution, blurry screens trying to find dynamic items that are literally the size of a grain of sand—like a specific stray strand of hair or an invisible smudge of dust that is the exact same colour as the floor.

• Completely Unplayable Hint System: Because the items are impossibly small, you will naturally look to the game's hint system. Shockingly, the developers put a strict, non-replenishing cap of seven hints per level. Once you run out of hints, you are left completely stranded, forcing you to have a third-party internet walkthrough open just to make basic progress.

• Lifeless Presentation: There is zero voice acting in this game. The story is told through dry, silent text boxes slapped onto frozen, un-animated character cutouts. It strips away all narrative tension and makes it impossible to care about the case or the characters.
• Terrible Modern PC Optimization: The game is locked to a rigid legacy 4:3 aspect ratio. Playing it on a modern screen forces massive black bars onto the sides of your display. Worse, the audio compression is deeply outdated, resulting in awful crackling sounds over the music loops on Windows 10 and 11.

Final Verdict:

Do not waste $10 on a shallow 2-hour game that feels like a braindead Frankenstein monstrosity. If you want a casual Sherlock hidden-object experience that actually has passion and high-quality hand-drawn visuals behind it, buy Sherlock Holmes: The Hound of the Baskervilles (2011) instead.

Posiblemente el peor juego de SH de Frogwares.
Se aleja mucho de la fórmula de siempre y restringe al jugador tanto en movimiento como en gameplay. Se trata de una aventura centrada en solo dos cosas: búsqueda de objetos ocultos y puzles desde una posición fija en cada escenario y el juego, tristemente falla en ambas cosas por un exceso de dificultad y exasperación. Algunos objetos son imposibles de encontar sin una guía o usando una pista y hay puzles que acaban cansando de tanto que se pueden tardar en resolver.
En cuanto a la historia, falla desde el principio en enganchar al jugador ya que todo lo observamos con la perspectiva de Holmes y Watson, quienes solo dialogan al inicio y al final del juego y lo único que dicen enmedio son mensajitos al terminar un área. Y ni hablemos de los secundarios. Tanto los testimonios como los sospechosos solo se presentan en forma de documentos y fotografías que no permiten mostrar su personalidad y así captivar más al jugador. Las declaraciones de los testigos carecen de peso, lo presentan como algo que debes leer atentamente y marcar como correcto si tiene sentido, pero estas serán correctas siempre, haciendo que el mensajito de "Buen trabajo!" quede muy fuera de lugar
Para acabar, el sistema de deducciones es simple, pero funciona, se trata sencillamente de relacionar objetos similares entre sospechosos, escenarios y partes clave del asesinato. Luego, lo normal sería que el juego te hiciese encontrar todas las conexiones y darte a elegir quién crees que es el asesino, pero solo basta con fijarte en la única persona que estaba en el escenario del crimen a la hora correcta y conectar cosas hasta que el juego dice "Felicidades, has ganado!" de la forma más anticlimática posible. 

Menos mal que he pillado este juego a 1€ con el 90% de descuento, porque por 10€ me parece un abuso

Les analyses au labo sont sympas et rappellent l'ambiance des romans. C'est plus un jeu type "énigmes et objets cachés" que réellement un jeu d'enquête mais on passe un bon moment quand même. Jeu pas gourmand du tout et très fluide, pas de bug rencontré.

I'm normally a fan of point-and-click games and hidden object games, but sometimes these games like to hide objects so well that it becomes almost impossible to percieve. This game is no exception - and while I like the premise of helping solve a mystery as the famous Sherlock Holmes, I can't help but feel entirely detatched from the experience due to a disdinct lack of story 95% of the time. There's more lines of dialogue and story in the final cutscene than there is in the entire rest of the game combined. Probably more words too.

Not only that, but the game is short and has some truly awful puzzles - the ten digit code being easily the worst. Five guesses at a code where the numbers can't repeat and there's ten digits? That requires some serious luck - because even with the best methods you have available, it'd still be a massive crapshoot if you actually win. When the puzzles are skill based, they're not too bad, but when they're random chance like that it completely saps the fun. Short, poor puzzles, infuriating objects, barely any story and feeling of detective work - The true mystery of the Persian Carpet is if the game designer was the real victim in the murder all along.

[h1][b] Reseña de Sherlock Holmes: The Mystery of the Persian Carpet[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
Sherlock Holmes: The Mystery of the Persian Carpet es ese tipo de aventura casual que no pretende revolucionar nada: te encierra en una escena y te dice “encuentra cosas”, pero con acento británico imaginario y una pipa invisible para que te sientas intelectual mientras buscas un botón del tamaño de una uña.

La propuesta es simple y peligrosamente adictiva: apuntar y clic, objetos ocultos, rompecabezas ligeros y una vibra de “soy detective” aunque en la práctica seas un aspirador humano de pistas. La primera impresión es clara: esto es un misterio para relajarte… o para discutir con tu pantalla cuando el objeto “obvio” estaba camuflado como si fuera parte del tejido del universo.

[h2]Lo Elemental y Lo… No Tan Elemental[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
  Temática detectivesca directa: misterio + observación sin relleno innecesario.  
  Rompecabezas y objetos ocultos ideales para sesiones cortas (bien casual, bien “un capítulo y me voy”).  
  Controles de apuntar y clic: accesible, sin pelearte con combos raros.  
  Satisface el “modo Sherlock” aunque sea a base de encontrar cachivaches como gremlin victoriano.  

Lo No Tan Bueno:
  Cero logros: literalmente nada que presumir en tu perfil, ni aunque te sientas el Watson definitivo.  
  Comunidad mínima (3 jugadores actuales): si buscas conversación, vas a hablar con el eco.  
  Rejugabilidad limitada: una vez resuelves el misterio, el “misterio” se convierte en tour guiado.  
  Fórmula rígida de objetos ocultos: si no te engancha este estilo, aquí no hay milagros ni giros modernos.

Sherlock Holmes: The Mystery of the Persian Carpet es como un té negro: clásico, simple, y si te gusta, te lo tomas feliz. Having bounced hard off this one in the past I came back to it with more time and less expectation of what kind of game this is in comparison to the rest of the series.

As other reviewers have said, it is more like a Hidden Object Game (HOG) - though less of a traditional one like Sherlock Holmes and the Hound of the Baskervilles - mixed through with quite difficult logic puzzles and an element of matching crime scene evidence with the evidence from individual suspects.

In this game we are trying to find enough evidence to: 
 - match the murder weapon;  
 - pin down the time of the murder; 
 - finger whom the murderer was; 
after making the collected evidence suitable for comparison. 

This means that a lot of the time we are collecting various ashes (from cigarettes and cigars and other sources), cloth fibres (green cotton, purple satin etc.) and matching shoe prints (and waxes and paints) to the actual shoes. This process at first seemed weird and repetitive to me, but I got into a rhythm of looking forward to the step of putting the cloth or the ash etc. under the microscrope, and then cutting or scraping a piece off to use for comparison at the end of the level.

The game is level based and I played on Casual. This meant no timer (a timer would be horrible, despite the ability to pause) which is explained as Holmes working on his own time and the longer he takes it will alert the authorities who will tell him to bugger off and work on assigned cases. This also meant that the game moved me to each scene, and each review of a suspect or preparing the evidence, so it was very linear. The game mentions 'a new location is available for you to visit on the map', but then instantly takes you to the map and I could not find a UI element or menu option to move between Holmes' lounge, the police station or the map. I am assuming this is because I was in the linear Casual mode. I also feel that I needed this on my first time playing.

There is a difficulty where you are just set free in the world and can move about the various scenes at will, but I imagine that would make this game overall very difficult and I doubt many people would play through to completion, especially with a timer. Perhaps I will come back to attempt this at some point in the future with faint memories of where the objects are that I'm looking for.

The objects are hidden in such a way as to mostly be unfair or downright evil depending on your experience with HOGs. Finding them is hard even with 7 hints that can be used overall per level.. and even playing on Casual I'm happy to admit that I used these at times. The game is probably best enjoyed with a walkthrough in order to see what it has to offer without getting too frustrated. Though even with a walkthrough I imagine it would take a decent couple of hours to play from start to finish.

In terms of value I'm pretty sure I got this one as part of a complete the set bundle, so likely paid a fairly minimal amount so price didn't factor into my feelings for this game at all. I really enjoy the other more traditional HOG's by Frogwares (and their Dracula themed one - Dracula: Love Kills). They are more satisfying to play than this one also as they are a bit newer and have achievements which people like so they feel their time isn't somehow wasted on entertainment designed to spend your time so this game definitely doesn't appeal to everyone, but in the end I definitely enjoyed my time with it.

I think for what it is, for me, this game could only have been better if they had voiced any of the text in the game. Sherlock and Watson, the various suspects would have greatly added to the game, though there is a fair degree of personality that comes through in the text - common spelling mistakes nonwithstanding.

Wikipedia says that this game is 'Primarily an object hunt game', which is true - but it also is quite unique in how it does so. So I will recommend it to people who are open to something different and have the time and patience to put into it because I don't think I've ever played a game quite like this in the last thirty years [despite not mentioning it on the store page, this game was released in 2008].

My rating: 5/10 (neutral). This game will appeal to a niche category of gamers.

"Persian Carpet" offers a commendable variety of puzzles and that's the game's strongest feature. The overarching gameplay goes like this: the player has to find clues in scenes to unlock puzzles; solve those puzzles to reveal more clues; process those clues into evidence at 221 Baker Street to add to Holmes' deduction board; and match the evidence to gain access to the next scene. However, finding the connections between the evidence is the most ambiguous and frustrating part of the game. I never fully understood the logic of the deduction board, and throughout most of the game I randomly paired items until the game rewarded me with matches. Unfortunately, each visit to the deduction board requires a predetermined number of connections before Holmes can advance to the next level and continue the investigation.

Equally frustrating is the 'pixel hunting' mechanic of finding clues in each scene. The player is shown silhouettes of objects to find. Some are easy to spot while others are nearly impossible to see. Some clues are revealed only through interactions with the scene, like rolling back a carpet, prying open a box or repairing an object.

The story and its expanding list of suspects is confusing to follow; but ultimately Sherlock Holmes provides the solution after all the clues are found and matched. The mystery's reveal is adequate but not particularly rewarding after hours of tedious mouse clicking. A professional review of the game notes: "By the time I fingered the culprit at game’s end, all I really felt like I’d solved was the interface, not a mystery."

"Persian Carpet" was included in a bundle of Frogwares Sherlock Holmes games I bought during a Steam  sale. Sherlock Holmes versus Jack the Ripper is easily one of the darkest and most atmospheric entries in the series featuring the famous detective. This time, accompanied by his loyal friend Dr. John Watson, Holmes takes on a particularly disturbing investigation involving the brutal murders committed in London in 1888 by the mysterious and infamous Jack the Ripper.

One of the things I appreciate most about this installment is its unsettling atmosphere. Much of the story takes place at night, leading us through the gloomy streets of Whitechapel and other rather disturbing locations that perfectly capture the fear and uncertainty surrounding the investigation. The dark setting really adds to the experience, creating a constant sense of unease as you gradually uncover more details about the murders.

As far as gameplay is concerned, the game stays true to the familiar formula of the series, offering plenty of logical puzzles with a well-balanced level of difficulty. What I particularly enjoyed were the various deduction tools that help you piece together the evidence and make sense of the investigation. These include deduction boards, timelines used to determine the victims' approximate times of death, and charts that allow you to examine possible motives behind the crimes. Such mechanics make the investigation feel much more engaging, as you're not simply following the story but actively trying to understand what happened and who might be responsible.

It's also worth mentioning that this is probably not the best choice for younger players. Given the nature of the crimes being investigated, the game occasionally features fairly graphic scenes of violence. While these moments aren't constant, they certainly contribute to the darker tone of the story.

Completing the adventure should take anywhere from several hours to well over ten, depending on how quickly you solve the puzzles and how thoroughly you explore each location. Personally, I didn't encounter any significant bugs or technical issues that interfered with my progress, which made the overall experience even more enjoyable.

Overall, I really enjoyed my time with Sherlock Holmes versus Jack the Ripper. It's a well-made detective adventure that successfully combines an intriguing criminal investigation, satisfying puzzles, and a genuinely creepy atmosphere. I especially appreciate how the game encourages you to think carefully about the evidence rather than simply handing you the answers.

If you're interested in detective stories, historical mysteries, or Sherlock Holmes in general, I think you'll find plenty to enjoy here. It's definitely worth playing, particularly if you appreciate slower-paced adventures where observation, reasoning, and attention to detail actually matter.

Highly recommended!

Sherlock Holmes versus Jack the Ripper to jedna z najbardziej klimatycznych, a zarazem najmroczniejszych odsłon serii poświęconej przygodom słynnego detektywa. Tym razem, wspólnie z jego nieodłącznym przyjacielem, doktorem Johnem Watsonem, mamy okazję podjąć się wyjątkowo trudnego śledztwa dotyczącego brutalnych morderstw popełnionych w 1888 roku w Londynie przez tajemniczego Kubę Rozpruwacza.

Tym, co szczególnie wyróżnia tę część, jest jej niezwykle mroczna i niepokojąca atmosfera. Większość wydarzeń rozgrywa się nocą, w ponurych uliczkach londyńskiej dzielnicy Whitechapel oraz innych miejscach, które doskonale oddają klimat niepewności i grozy towarzyszący całemu śledztwu. Twórcom udało się stworzyć naprawdę sugestywną scenerię, która skutecznie buduje napięcie i zachęca do dalszego odkrywania tajemnicy seryjnego mordercy.

Pod względem rozgrywki produkcja pozostaje wierna sprawdzonej formule serii, oferując liczne zagadki logiczne o dobrze wyważonym poziomie trudności. Na szczególną uwagę zasługują rozbudowane narzędzia dedukcyjne, dzięki którym możemy analizować zgromadzone dowody, ustalać prawdopodobny czas śmierci poszczególnych ofiar czy rozpatrywać potencjalne motywy popełnionych zbrodni. Wszystko to sprawia, że gracz może rzeczywiście poczuć się jak detektyw prowadzący skomplikowane śledztwo, w którym każdy szczegół może mieć znaczenie.

Warto jednak zaznaczyć, że ze względu na tematykę oraz pojawiające się momentami dość dosadne sceny przemocy gra niekoniecznie będzie odpowiednia dla najmłodszych odbiorców. Mroczna atmosfera i brutalny charakter przedstawionych wydarzeń stanowią nieodłączny element opowiadanej historii.

Ukończenie całej przygody zajmuje od kilku do kilkunastu godzin, w zależności od tempa rozwiązywania zagadek i dokładności eksploracji. Podczas swojej rozgrywki nie napotkałem żadnych poważniejszych błędów technicznych, które mogłyby utrudnić postępy lub negatywnie wpłynąć na odbiór gry.

Osobiście uważam Sherlock Holmes versus Jack the Ripper za bardzo udaną odsłonę serii, która świetnie łączy klasyczną przygodówkę detektywistyczną z mroczną historią kryminalną. To zdecydowanie produkcja warta uwagi, szczególnie dla osób zainteresowanych zagadkami kryminalnymi, historycznymi śledztwami oraz samą postacią Sherlocka Holmesa. Jeżeli lubicie niespieszne, wymagające odrobiny dedukcji przygody z niepokojącą atmosferą w tle, z pewnością warto dać jej szansę. 

Gorąco polecam!

Frustrating errand simulator that reduces brilliant detective work to tedious item hunts.

If you are thinking of picking up Sherlock Holmes versus Jack the Ripper, it is a narrative concept with massive historical potential that ultimately falls flat under the weight of outdated design. While tracking history's most infamous serial killer across Victorian London sounds thrilling, the actual experience is an archaic chore that will thoroughly test your patience.

Here is what you need to know before diving in:

• Glorified Fetch Quests: The game completely abandons the thrill of active clue seeking in favor of a rigid, chore-based item retrieval system. Instead of solving crimes through pure intellect, you spend the majority of your time pixel hunting for random objects just to satisfy the arbitrary triggers of every character encounter.

• Opaque Direction & Writing: The script does you absolutely no favors when it comes to puzzle logic. The dialogue adds very little notion to what you are supposed to do next, leaving you completely stranded without any clear narrative direction. The story itself lacks any meaningful depth, making the progression feel empty.

• Alt-Tab "Gameplay" Returns: Much like The Testament of Sherlock Holmes, Frogwares heavily relies on obtuse, trial-and-error mechanics that stall your momentum. The complete lack of mechanical clarity forces you to keep a secondary window or mobile browser open, relying on Google and external AI tools just to figure out how to progress the case.

• Severely Outdated Presentation: For a game of its age, the technical presentation holds up incredibly poorly. The game design feels aggressively archaic, the pathfinding is clumsy, the sound effects are gratingly subpar, and the lifeless character animations make the entire investigation feel robotic.

Final Verdict: A structurally flawed adventure game that turns the world's greatest detective into a frustrated delivery boy. If you do not want to constantly run external walkthroughs just to get through a single chapter, save yourself the headache and skip this entry entirely

[h2]这或许是游戏史上，玩家距离1888年那个秋天最近的一次机会[/h2]

作为蛙社最后一部旧时代引擎框架的福尔摩斯系列正传性质作品，我认为《夏洛克福尔摩斯vs开膛手杰克》是一部近乎满分的作品。老实讲这个带点“关公战秦琼”性质的标题虽然有些没品，也许起个更具文学气质的标题会更好一些。但也不得不承认这个标题的确商业噱头十足，且让[b]福尔摩斯vs开膛手杰克[/b]，也确实是后世人对侦破此案的一种美好幻想。

正式游玩之前，由于老游戏没有官中，现在互联网上该游戏的汉化补丁极为稀少，且大多链接已经失效。我只在原ChinaAVG论坛和Steam测评里玩家分享的那个链接里找到了补丁，原ChinaAVG论坛里那个补丁可能因为游戏后续更新已经没法使用了，打了后会卡在主菜单界面进不去游戏，所以建议大家就不要再费力气去全网找了，还是去测评里大佬分享的那个链接去下载。因为游戏没有自动存档，也没有明确的章节划分，切记勤存档！特别是修煤气管道小游戏之前一定先存档，有一定概率会bug无法完成，如果遇到bug读档还有得救。另外本作的解谜倒是不难，但老游戏因为提示少，设计思路也比较古早。有时候一些小游戏可能要花一两分钟摸索，对上设计师的电波后才知道要怎么解。

看得出来蛙社出于对逝者与真实案件的尊重，在制作本作时还是非常的严肃与克制。游戏高度还原了开膛手杰克5案诸多细节，具体到案发时间，案发现场，被害人死状，甚至细节到了证人证词。即便受害者形象采用了相对克制的插画风格，在尸检时还是会感觉有些残忍，甚至最惨的玛丽·简·凯利第5案用了另一种更为克制的表现方式。结局更像是基于现实已知线索展开的一次if推理，最终对峙的镜头虽然受限时代技术略显简陋，但镜头的表现张力非常强，玩到最后还是很震撼的。

严格来说本作没有刻意设计的恐怖元素，也没有真正意义的“jump scare”，但如果完全没有心理准备，[u]大晚上看到被害人插画，和后期有一个照片线索的时候[/u]，可能还是会被吓一跳。有时候我在想，开膛手杰克案的一些细节始末，喜欢刑侦推理的朋友们大多都有所了解。但似乎因为该案距今已经间隔了一百三十余年，过大的时间跨度稀释了我们对这个案件凶残程度的认知。对今天的人们来说，开膛手杰克案似乎变成了一个被反复讲述的“传说故事”，而不再是当年那个血淋淋的，令人不寒而栗的连环血案。

但当通过游戏亲历1888年伦敦白教堂的那个秋天时，才真正体会到：当时贫民区的居民所经历的，是一场如永不消散的大雾般如影随形的恐惧——没有人知道自己会不会是下一个，也没有人知道自己会不会遭遇更残酷的杀害。游戏展现的是官方认定的5起凶案，而现实中因关联性不足的疑似案件还有十余起，无人能确定其中是否也有开膛手杰克的参与。时至今日，对前些年那件披肩证物的DNA检测，也因证据链不全、存在污染风险等客观因素，仅能提供一种可能性。保守来看，此案或许永远无法被真正侦破；即便未来能确定凶手身份，也无法再审判那个犯下残酷血案的开膛手了。

游戏里我们扮演福尔摩斯与华生侦破了此案，让开膛手杰克用余生去偿还自己犯下的罪孽。但现实里的1888年没有福尔摩斯与华生，通关游戏的我想到这里，仿佛自己就站在白教堂区街道的尽头，而开膛手杰克，

[strike]就那样永远地消失在了1888年伦敦白教堂区那个秋天的雾色之中……[/strike]

While I had to edit game.ini file and download files from outside to make the game run, afterwards I haven't encountered any bugs or issues whatsoever during my gameplay. It was a smooth ride and I finished the game in two sittings.

If you enjoyed other Holmes games by Frogwares - personally I only played Crimes and Punishments, Chapter One and the remake of The Awakened so far - I'm sure you'll enjoy this one too. The graphics are obviously dated, but I don't think they're bad. And if you're playing a lot of point-and-click and similar games I'm sure you've seen worse. The editing is sometimes too choppy though, and some scenes transitions are much too abrupt.

The plot is fairly interesting, at least the main one. I personally prefer "From Hell" type of Jack the Ripper (a 1979 Sherlock Holmes movie "Murder by Decree" is close to that btw), but I still enjoyed this particular retelling of the story and the explanation as to why police never caught the killer.

Subplots are less engaging and a lot of the playtime is padded by random, silly quests for various people, especially in the early parts of the game. The story there is a bit ridiculous, dialogues are very heavy handed, and it's clear the creators of the game added these parts only to make the game a bit longer.

Puzzles are rather easy. Though I did struggle a bit with the dates of the battles that took place in US, and the cell opening puzzle was quite annoying. Some puzzles are so deeply explained that the player just needs to follow Holmes' instructions without thinking, sometimes we don't any explanation at all, which is a bit odd. A few pixel hunting moments also occured, but I'm quite used to these, so I didn't mind.

I also played with Polish subtitles (they turned on automatically, and I didn't bother to turn them off) and noticed that there were some typos and misspellings. I am also unsure if the explanation of the Yiddish puzzle was fully correct (I think one letter/number combination was wrong).

In any case, if you like crime stories, point-and-click games and don't mind playing older titles, this one is still pretty fun.

回到游戏本身，全流程大概8-10小时左右，虽然很恨开发者但我没有办法说这个游戏本身不好玩，真的真的很好玩，工业化污染时期伦敦阴暗潮湿清冷的氛围，贫富差距加大遍地的流浪汉，酗酒者，妓女艰难求生，看着游戏里西装革履的绅士和染上梅毒的妓女穿行而过心里也是凄凄惨惨，剧情相当出色，推理过程是绝对严肃的本格推理，收集证据，基本演绎法，需要严密的逻辑，中间穿插了很多有意思的完全不一样的小游戏，这就不得不拉出来阿加莎改编的游戏系列了，比起这个推理来像是幼稚园的推理游戏，真是浪费了阿婆的IP。

A mystery that I had been following since I was a teenager, bent on solving unsolved mysteries. The story places two of England's famous figures into a battle of wits, the titular Sherlock Holmes vs. the first mass media covered killer, Jack the Ripper.

The game is beautifully well-done, giving you the chance to experience the game either as a point-and-click (the original intended way to play) or switch it to first-person to experience the dirty streets of Whitechapel for yourself. 
The game was released in 2009 and it shows, some graphics could use a little more work and some mechanics could be implemented that were not added until much later on.
The story is wonderfully told, from the beginning with Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson being intrigued at the unfortunate murder of Mary Ann Nichols in Buck's Row, to witnessing the horribly disfigured body of Mary-Jane Kelly in Miller's Court. All throughout the tale, Sherlock is attempting to uncover the truth while dodging the police who have warned him to stay out of it.

In the end, the killer is found, but I'll leave that to you.

The puzzles are good, but some can be a bit confusing and will leave you looking up a guide because the instructions aren't always clear. There was a section where Sherlock needed to leave a building undetected, but I had no idea why I was gathering items and putting them together for. Something that could've been prevented had Sherlock mentioned needing to make a distraction.

All in all, great game.

The Sherlock Holmes series finally finds its mark as a casual sleuthing and adventure game.

"SH Versus Jack the Ripper" continues the first-person-view game mechanic that was introduced in "Sherlock Holmes: The Awakened" and refined in "Sherlock Holmes: Nemesis." Mercifully, the complex cyphers and math-based puzzles of previous games in the franchise are mostly gone, toning "Jack the Ripper" difficulty to approximately medium compared to previous games. (Mensa brainiacs and puzzle masochists can turn to the frustratingly difficult object hunting game, "Sherlock Holmes: The Mystery of the Persian Carpet" released after "Nemesis" to get their fix.) 

With "Jack the Ripper" we get two new game mechanics: the deduction board and crime scene reenactments. More enjoyable to me, however, was the expanded use of Dr. Watson as a playable character. Watson carries nearly half the game as he conducts interviews alone, solves puzzles and unearths clues for Holmes' investigation. Holmes, to his credit, acknowledges Watson's contributions and assures Watson that he is indispensable. Both characters are evolving, as is Frogwares' skill as a story teller. Taking the games chronologically by release date starting with the "Mystery of the Mummy's Curse," I found "Jack the Ripper" to have the most enjoyable narrative. I would recommend this game as an entry point into the series.

Not all is perfection, however. First, there is a considerable amount of 'suspension of disbelief' required to accept Holmes' deductions as fact. Second--and somewhat counterintuitive to the first--is Holmes' numerous experiments and tedious recreations to 'prove' his theories. They make for an interesting diversion but are rarely convincing as being solid detective work. And third, there are a few glitches that hobble the game until worked around; for example, using a protractor to draw an elipses on a map of London becomes a trial-and-error exercise to envelope the correct area. Most puzzles can be solved by bashing pieces around until the player is rewarded with a positive acknowledgement by the game.

The crime scenes are creepily faithful to the actual Whitechapel murders. When I was 13 I found a hardback copy of "The Complete Jack the Ripper" by Donald Rumbelow (in an abandoned house, strangely). The book included autopsy photos, the Ripper's alleged letters, and the crime scene photo of Mary Kelly horrifically mutilated on her bed. As inappropriate as the content may have been for my age, the text of the book fascinated me and much is ingrained in my memory more than 40 years later. In "Sherlock Holmes vs. Jack the Ripper" there is an obvious care to be authentic to the murders. Frogwares does not avoid the gruesomeness of the actual events; Holmes and Watson discuss mutilation of female genitals and the removal of uteri and other organs. Ridiculous street characters and a few absurd situations provide levity to the game.

The case follows a few 'red herrings" along the way but by its conclusion settles on one of the most popular theories of the true 'Jack the Ripper's' identity and motives. Does Holmes identify the correct person? In this version he does, of course ... but the public can never know.

This is my fourth Sherlock game from this developer. I like it better than the previous one which was Sherlock vs Arsene Lupin aka Nemesis. I think this is mainly due to the story, which is quite well known as so many adaptations have been made about it.

Overall I think this is by far the easiest Sherlock game out of the first four they released. There are times where it becomes a chore, where you have to go from place A to place B, only to pick up one item to return to place A, then return to place B and so forth. Still I recommend it.

While I enjoyed my 5 hours playing it, I find it hard to recommend this game to anyone.

If you played Shadowgrounds, and didnt like it, you likely wont like this one as well. It is sliiightly better gameplay vise, because I think some AI got improved slightly, enemy placement were harder to fight off, but that could be because I played on hard difficulty this time instead of normal. If you DID like Shadowgrounds, you might be disappointed by how short it is(yes, 5 hours is the whole singleplayer story, theres a few survival maps but I didnt bother with them, since thats not why I liked original shadowgrounds)

And while there was slight improvements in gameplay, there are some downsides too. Like how now you cant use all your weapons from the original game, because some guns didnt make transition into this game(like lightning gun, laser, grenade launcher), and remaining guns that did make the cut(pistol, pulse rifle, flamethrower, shotgun, minigun, rocket launcher, energy sniper rifle) all are divided between 3 playable characters. Two of these characters use pistol, so just like in original game, you'll get bored of using pistol a ton. But this time you WILL be forced to use pistol because sometimes you'll get swarmed by waves after waves of enemies(especially during sniper lady sections). So what ends up happening is that you gonna mostly use pistol, pulse rifle, flamethrower, shotgun, energy sniper rifle. The rest of the weapons are gonna be used very rarely since game rarely gives those guns ammo. Not so fun fact, one of the pistol upgrades is bugged, I think its lock on upgrade, so if you upgrade it, then you cant use pistol anymore... Check forums to avoid it

AND this game has only one official boss fight(and it sucks, cus he's dumb). They got replaced with you being surrounded, and get constantly attacked from everywhere. It was kinda fun, but it gets repetitive.

If you got this game from shadowgrounds bundle when it went for 90% off, I guess its fine to try, or if you have friends to play co op. But besides that I find little reason to recommend playing it, let alone buying it.

Shadowgrounds: Survivor, developed and published by Frozenbyte, is a top-down action shooter that expands upon the intense gameplay of the original Shadowgrounds. Released in 2007, the game returns players to the icy landscapes of Jupiter's moon Ganymede, where humanity faces a relentless alien threat. Combining fast-paced combat, strategic weapon use, and RPG-style progression, Survivor offers a compelling blend of action and customization that engages both fans of the original and newcomers to the series.

Players can choose from three distinct characters: Luke, Bruno, and Isabel, each with unique abilities and strengths. This variety encourages different approaches to combat, as players can tailor their playstyle to their preferred tactics. Adding depth to the experience, the game features an upgrade system that allows players to improve weapons and enhance character attributes. This sense of progression not only rewards continued play but also enables experimentation with different loadouts and strategies, making encounters with alien enemies feel fresh and dynamic.

The environments in Shadowgrounds: Survivor are varied and richly detailed. From snow-laden landscapes and frozen tundras to abandoned research facilities and the besieged New Atlantis colony, the levels provide both visual diversity and strategic complexity. Each setting introduces unique obstacles, requiring players to adapt their tactics to environmental hazards. Dynamic effects such as snowstorms and shifting lighting further immerse players in the tense, claustrophobic atmosphere of the alien invasion, heightening the sense of urgency during combat.

Combat is at the heart of Survivor, and it delivers a satisfying and intense experience. Players face waves of alien creatures using a broad arsenal that includes pistols, machine guns, flamethrowers, and devastating explosives. New additions like deployable Mechs and Sentry Turrets offer alternative tactical options, allowing players to experiment with defensive setups and offensive strategies. The physics-based mechanics, including destructible environments and realistic weapon effects, add a layer of depth to battles, making each encounter both challenging and rewarding.

While the story may not be the primary draw, it provides a strong framework for the action. Players follow the survivors’ struggle to repel the alien threat and escape from the besieged colonies, with the narrative offering context for the missions and encounters. Fully voiced characters and cinematic cutscenes help convey the tension and stakes of the alien invasion, creating a sense of purpose behind the relentless combat.

Graphically, Shadowgrounds: Survivor impresses with detailed environments, fluid animations, and dynamic lighting effects. The atmospheric soundtrack complements the gameplay, intensifying the suspense during firefights and exploration. Together, these elements create an immersive experience that keeps players engaged and invested in the action.

Though highly enjoyable, the game is not without its limitations. Some players may find the gameplay loop repetitive over extended sessions, and while the weapon variety is broad, combat mechanics remain relatively straightforward compared to modern shooters. However, these minor shortcomings do not detract significantly from the overall experience.

In conclusion, Shadowgrounds: Survivor is a polished and engaging action shooter that combines fast-paced combat, strategic depth, and immersive environments. Its diverse characters, upgrade system, and tense encounters with alien forces create a compelling experience for both fans of the original game and newcomers. While it may not reinvent the genre, it delivers a satisfying and entertaining journey through a hostile and vividly realized sci-fi world.

Frozenbyte повертається з Shadowgrounds Survivor, продовженням культового ізометричного шутера, що розширює і покращує оригінальну формулу. Гра пропонує ще більше хаосу, нових персонажів, розширену систему RPG-елементів і можливість виживати у ще жорстокіших умовах. Але чи змогло продовження перевершити свого попередника?

Сюжет: три долі у хаосі вторгнення
Події Survivor розгортаються після Shadowgrounds. Колонія на Ґаніметі захоплена прибульцями, і лише жменька вцілілих намагається вибратися живими. На відміну від першої гри, цього разу ми керуємо не одним героєм, а одразу трьома персонажами:

Лукас Бенч – морпіх із важким озброєнням,

Ізабелла Макандер – снайперка,

Баррі Ґаррен – інженер із турелями та механічними помічниками.

Кожен має унікальний стиль гри, що додає різноманітності геймплею, хоча сюжет усе ще залишається другорядним елементом, більше слугуючи фоновим доповненням до екшену.

Геймплей: більше RPG та стратегічних можливостей
Як і в оригіналі, Shadowgrounds Survivor – це інтенсивний twin-stick shooter, де гравець відстрілює орди прибульців у темних коридорах колонії. Гра відчувається більш динамічною, ніж перша частина, завдяки:
✔ Розширеній системі RPG-елементів – кожен персонаж має дерево прокачки з унікальними здібностями.
✔ Новій системі зброї – тепер можна не просто знаходити нові гармати, а й покращувати їх, роблячи вибір між різними модифікаціями.
✔ Різноманітності місій – деякі рівні вимагають не лише стрільби, а й оборони позицій, що додає стратегічного елемента.

Кожен герой відчувається по-різному: інженер може встановлювати турелі, снайперка вміє ефективно атакувати здалеку, а морпіх просто нищить усе на своєму шляху. Це додає грі глибини, хоча загальна структура місій залишається лінійною.

Графіка та звук: похмурий, але атмосферний sci-fi
Гра використовує той самий рушій, що й перша частина, але з покращеннями у спецефектах. Освітлення та тіні, як і раніше, грають важливу роль у створенні напруги. Дизайн локацій усе ще повторюється, але різноманіття об’єктів і деталей стало більшим.

Саундтрек продовжує підсилювати атмосферу, а звукові ефекти відчуваються потужними – стрілянина, вибухи та крики прибульців додають грі кінематографічного відчуття. Озвучення персонажів залишилося простим, але достатнім для створення відповідної атмосфери.

Новий режим Survival – справжнє випробування
Одним із головних нововведень стала арена Survival Mode, де хвилі прибульців атакують гравця, і потрібно вижити якомога довше. Це чудовий режим для тих, хто хоче просто насолоджуватися екшеном без сюжету.

Висновок
Shadowgrounds Survivor – це покращене продовження, яке пропонує більше варіативності, цікавіші бої та нові можливості. Воно не робить революції в жанрі, але для фанатів ізометричних шутерів та sci-fi жахів ця гра – чудова знахідка.

Оцінка: 8/10
✔ Три унікальні персонажі
✔ Покращена система прокачки та зброї
✔ Динамічний ігровий процес
✔ Напружена атмосфера виживання
✘ Сюжет усе ще другорядний
✘ Локації могли б бути різноманітнішими

[h1]Crítica de \Shadowgrounds: Survivor\ – Cuando la supervivencia parece una tarea de medio tiempo[/h1]

[h2]Resumen[/h2]
¿Alguna vez has sentido que eres el protagonista de una película de serie B empuñando un arma mientras hormigas gigantes tratan de hacerte cosquillas en los pies? Bueno, \Shadowgrounds: Survivor\ te da eso, pero envuelto en un shooter de ciencia ficción donde debes sobrevivir en un mundo marginado por criaturas que claramente no quieren ser tus amigas.

[h2]Aspectos importantes e interesantes[/h2]
¡Luces, cámara, acción! \Shadowgrounds: Survivor\ destaca por poner a tus dedos en el gatillo desde el minuto uno. Entre explosiones, arañas del tamaño de bulldozers y una extraña necesidad de guardar combustible más celosamente que tu propia vida, el juego cumple en entregarte un escenario de película de ciencia ficción. Además, las mecánicas de mejora de armas son como entrar a una tienda de dulces... si los dulces fueran herramientas para exterminar alienígenas.

[h2]Aspectos por mejorar[/h2]
No es por ser quisquilloso pero, ¿podemos hablar del elefante en el cuarto? La inteligencia artificial del juego tiene menos luces que un sótano en apagón. Los enemigos a veces parecen más perdidos que turista sin mapa, lo cual reduce algo de la adrenalina. Además, la historia tiene menos carne que un plato vegetariano en una barbacoa, y con ello menos tracción para enganchar.

Но есть одна маааааленькая деталь. Первая часть воспринимается сейчас откровенно ужасно из-за вороха проблем, причем в чисто игровом поле. Survivor рассказывает историю про то же самое вторжение, но с перспективы трех разных героев, задача которых встретиться и дать финальный бой пришельцам.

И знаете что? Да похорошело почти все. Зачатки РПГ-системы в виде прогрессии героев и их усиления реально полезная штука, как и бесконечный фонарик и карманные аптечки. У каждого чара есть пара уникальных апгрейдов, но самое главное - большой арсенал из оригинала был попилен между этой троицей, благодаря чему приходится пользоваться всеми пушками. Нет проблем в балансе относительно припасов; уровни очень короткие и насыщенные битвами, без шастанья впотьмах. Это, кстати, повлияло на темп игры: прохождение занимает то же время, что и оригинал, но Survivor обладает гораздо более интенсивной динамикой и воспринимается как динамичный забег (в отличии от затянутых глав в оригинале, где доигрываешь кампанию чуть ли не по инерции). Надо еще и отдать должное попыткам разрабов развлечь игрока турельными секциями и покатушками на роботах. Плюс в игре появилась система секретов, открывающих после первого прохождения дополнительные модификаторы вроде ускорения темпа игры, черно-белого фильтра и прочих мелочей разной степени полезности. 

Ощущается как вполне годный клон Alien Shooter, приближающийся к оному по динамике. Здесь, несмотря на устаревание игры, все же оставлю "синий" палец - из-за толковых изменений и просто потому, что понравилось играть в это больше, чем в оригинал.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

While the poor critical reception of Shadowgrounds Survivor compared to its predecessor might lead you to believe it's significantly inferior, that conclusion wouldn't be entirely accurate. In several aspects, Survivor improves upon the original's shortcomings.

Positives:

Combat: Despite the auto-lock feature, the combat remains fast, fluid, and feels fantastic.

Graphics: The graphics showcase a significant improvement, featuring visually appealing environments and character models.

Characters: You have the choice of three unique characters, each with distinct weapon loadouts, traits, and voice acting that surpasses the original. The engaging performances breathe life into an otherwise lackluster story.

Modes: Beyond the main campaign, you can experience various modes, including the new and exciting survival mode.

Inventory and Progression: Unlike the overwhelming inventory of the original, weapons are now categorized by character. 
Additionally, a new progression system lets you level up both characters and their weapons individually, unlocking new perks like before. This streamlined approach is commendable.

Negatives:

Stages: The stages are disappointingly short, and some characters possess overpowered and exploitable special attacks (though admittedly fun). The story feels inconsequential and merely serves as a setup for the emphasized survival mode, suggesting it was an afterthought.

Boss: Even more concerning is the presence of only one true boss encounter, occurring near the beginning of the game. Everything else consists of regular stages and the survival arena. This design choice feels like three steps forward and two steps back, which is unfortunate.

Enemy Variety: Enemy variety hasn't significantly changed since the original, and some enemy types may even be missing. 
While the game throws large waves of enemies at you, which is enjoyable, new enemy types aren't introduced effectively. 
If you're new to the game, some enemy mechanics might initially be confusing.

Flashlight: Lastly, my personal pet peeve, the flashlight remains underutilized. While functional, it retains the same functionality as the original without the need to charge it. In other words, it feels somewhat redundant.
Overall:

Despite its brevity and shortcomings, I found Shadowgrounds Survivor enjoyable. While I can't wholeheartedly recommend it, I wouldn't dissuade someone from trying it either. Ultimately, I wish it offered more content than what's currently available.

[h1][b] Reseña de Gumboy Tournament[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
Gumboy Tournament es ese experimento indie que mezcla carreras con plataformas en una vibra casual: corres, saltas, compites y tratas de no quedar como payaso frente a tus amigos… si logras convencer a alguien de entrar. La idea suena a “party game” de sofá con piques rápidos, caos controlado y rondas para reírte del que se cayó a medio salto.

La primera impresión es clara: esto quiere ser simple, accesible y directo. Un juego para desconectar el cerebro y activar el instinto competitivo básico. ¿El giro controversial? Su mayor enemigo no es la pista… es el lobby vacío. Sí, “multijugador” existe en el menú; en la vida real, los jugadores actuales están en un sólido e inamovible 0.

Aun así, el hecho de tener 302 recomendaciones totales sugiere que, en algún momento, la gente sí la pasó bien. Es como ese bar del barrio que “antes se llenaba”, y tú llegas un martes a las 3 pm y el bartender (tú) te mira a ti (también tú).

[h2]Lo que Acelera y lo que Patina[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
  Mezcla de carreras + plataformas: el combo funciona para partidas rápidas y caóticas.  
  Tiene modo un jugador y multijugador: al menos hay opciones para no depender 100% de la fe.  
  Préstamo familiar: ideal para “prestárselo” a alguien y culparlo si no le gusta.  
  ADN indie: se siente como un proyecto con personalidad y ganas de ser divertido sin complicarse.  

Lo No Tan Bueno:
  0 jugadores actuales: el multijugador es más una leyenda urbana que un modo vivo.  
  0 logros: si vienes a farmear dopamina de Steam, aquí no hay cosecha.  
  La parte “torneo” pierde gracia sin comunidad activa: competir contra el vacío no cuenta como esports.  
  Depende mucho de que tengas gente: si no, el chiste se cuenta solo… y no da tanta risa.

[h2]Conclusión (Aceptable)[/h2]
Gumboy Tournament es un juego casual indie de carreras con plataformas que probablemente brilla cuando hay gente: pique rápido, caos simpático y ese sabor a “una más y me voy”. El problema es que hoy el multijugador se siente como abrir una cancha y encontrarla cerrada con candado… y tú con la pelota en la mano.

Las 302 recomendaciones totales son el testimonio de que no es un desastre absoluto; simplemente está atrapado en ese limbo cruel donde un juego social se queda sin sociedad. Si lo compras por el un jugador, te va a cumplir a medias; si lo compras por competir online, prepárate para practicar el arte milenario de correr solo.

Гамбой Турнир — это как если бы кто-то взял резиновый мячик, накачал его кофеином и заставил участвовать в "Формуле-1" на батуте.
Ты — зелёный шарик по имени Гамбой, который скачет по уровням, как будто у него вместо ног — пружины из ада.
Геймплей? Прыгай, скользи, цепляйся языком за стены — и всё это с физикой, от которой у тебя кружится голова.
Графика — 2006-й: яркий, как жвачка, и такой же липкий.
Минус: через три раунда ты уже не понимаешь, где ты, а где пол.
Плюс: когда ты наконец добираешься до финиша — это как если бы ты выиграл Олимпиаду... на резиновом мяче.Вердикт: 7/10. Идеально для тех, кто хочет почувствовать себя ребёнком с ADHD. Или просто поорать "Я НЕ МОГУ ОСТАНОВИТЬСЯ!".

Gumboy Tournament is a lively and unconventional physics-based arcade game that builds upon the ideas of its predecessor and reshapes them into a more competitive, content-rich experience. Developed and published by CINEMAX GAMES, it centers on controlling a small, spherical character whose movement is governed by momentum, gravity, and environmental interaction rather than tight, traditional platforming inputs. The result is a game that feels tactile and playful, where learning how surfaces, slopes, and speed interact becomes just as important as reaching the goal itself.

At the heart of Gumboy Tournament is its physics-driven movement. Rolling, bouncing, and jumping are all influenced by terrain and velocity, encouraging players to think dynamically rather than mechanically. Smooth ramps can be used to build speed, curved walls can redirect motion, and vertical drops can become opportunities rather than hazards when handled correctly. This emphasis on momentum gives the game a distinct rhythm, where success often comes from understanding flow rather than executing precise button combinations. Early on, the controls may feel loose or slippery, but with time they reveal a surprising level of depth and consistency.

The single-player component offers a substantial campaign with dozens of levels spread across a variety of themed environments. These stages gradually introduce new mechanics and environmental twists, including altered gravity, moving obstacles, and more complex terrain layouts. Instead of focusing purely on reflex-based challenge, many levels encourage experimentation, rewarding players who learn how to exploit physics systems creatively. While the campaign does not rely on narrative motivation, it provides a steady sense of progression through escalating complexity and visual variety.

Where Gumboy Tournament truly differentiates itself is in its multiplayer offering. The game supports multiple competitive modes that transform its physics sandbox into a chaotic arena. Each mode introduces distinct objectives—ranging from territory control and item collection to races and team-based goals—that require players to adapt their movement skills to tactical situations. Momentum becomes a weapon as much as a tool, allowing skilled players to outmaneuver opponents, steal objectives at the last second, or recover from mistakes in dramatic fashion. Multiplayer matches often feel unpredictable and energetic, driven as much by improvisation as by planning.

Visually, the game embraces a whimsical and slightly surreal aesthetic. Environments are colorful and imaginative, blending fantasy elements with abstract geometry that complements the physics-heavy gameplay. The rounded character designs and curved level structures reinforce the game’s focus on motion and flow. Sound design and music further enhance the arcade feel, providing energetic accompaniment during competitive matches and more relaxed tones during solo play, without overwhelming the on-screen action.

Despite its creativity, the game is not without rough edges. The same physics system that gives Gumboy Tournament its charm can also be a source of frustration, particularly for newcomers. Movement can initially feel unpredictable, and competitive matches can devolve into chaotic collisions where precision gives way to spectacle. Balance between multiplayer modes and player counts can vary, and without deeper progression systems, long-term motivation relies heavily on enjoyment of the core mechanics rather than unlocks or narrative hooks.

Ultimately, Gumboy Tournament is a game that thrives on personality, experimentation, and shared chaos. It does not aim to provide a tightly scripted platforming experience or a deep story, but instead offers a playground where physics take center stage. For players who enjoy arcade-style competition, unusual movement systems, and games that reward mastery through feel rather than formulas, it delivers a distinctive and energetic experience. While it may not appeal to everyone, it stands out as a memorable entry in the physics platformer space, especially when enjoyed with others.

The graphics are livable, but they're not that great and make the game look flat. The game does have multiplayer, although I have not personally tried it out since no one has made a server in a good few years, but I imagine that it would have the same gameplay as the singleplayer.



In short, this is a relatively fun, casual game to spend your free time on when you've only got a minute or so and you've run out of dragons to kill. The multiplayer however has been dead for several years now though, so only play for singleplayer or with friends. $3 is too expensive for this game, seeing as of how you can easily buy this game on sale for $.29.

Surpreendentemente simples... creio que até demais para alguns, mas não deixa de ser divertido. 

Você realiza transações comerciais entre planetas, famoso compra barato/venda caro, com algumas exceções em situações nas quais eventos aleatórios positivam ou não determinados produtos ou quando o próprio jogador é capaz de manipular o mercado por meio de determinadas missões.
Há alguns minigames de tiro, ao estilo Quake clássico, bem dinâmico e estilo arena.
Não há uma progressão de personagem, nem personalização do mesmo. A história do jogo é simplista e não há personagens memoráveis, ou talvez o próprio jogo foi feito a ser assim. Como o jogo funciona entre capítulos, o progresso do capítulo anterior pouco influencia no próximo.

O jogo é divertido, mas demasiadamente simples. Vale a pena numa promoção.
an interesting idea, especially in the 2000's but by now has been eclipsed 100 times over by far better games.

Space Trader: Merchant Marine is an ambitious but uneven space-faring hybrid that reflects both the creativity and the limitations of mid-2000s indie design. Developed and published by Meridian4, the game sets out to combine interstellar trading, light role-playing progression, and first-person combat into a single experience where players can choose how to make their fortune. You begin as a relatively insignificant trader navigating a bureaucratic, tightly regulated universe, and the long-term goal is to rise in wealth and influence by exploiting trade routes, completing contracts, and occasionally resorting to violence when profit demands it.

At the heart of the experience is the trading system, which encourages players to travel between planets and space stations in search of favorable prices. Each location offers a range of commodities, and success depends on buying goods cheaply and selling them elsewhere for a profit. In practice, this loop is simple and easy to grasp, making the game accessible even to players unfamiliar with economic simulations. However, the underlying market behavior often feels random rather than reactive, with price fluctuations that don’t always appear connected to supply, demand, or player actions. This limits the sense of long-term strategy, as trading becomes more about trial and error than careful economic planning.

To supplement the trading gameplay, Space Trader: Merchant Marine introduces combat missions and bounty hunting, which place the player directly into first-person shooter encounters. These segments are intended to add variety and provide an alternate source of income, but they are also one of the game’s weakest aspects. Combat is functional but basic, with limited weapon variety, simplistic enemy behavior, and environments that feel repetitive. While these missions can offer a short break from trading menus, they rarely feel engaging enough to stand on their own and often come across as an underdeveloped side activity rather than a fully integrated system.

Progression is handled through money accumulation and incremental upgrades rather than deep character customization. As you earn credits, you can improve your ship and unlock new opportunities, but the sense of growth is relatively shallow. There is freedom in how you approach the game — focusing on commerce, missions, or a mix of both — yet the lack of meaningful branching systems or complex decision-making means that different playstyles tend to blur together over time. What initially feels like an open sandbox gradually reveals its narrow mechanical scope.

Visually and technically, the game shows its age almost immediately. The graphics are dated, with stiff character models, sparse environments, and a user interface that can feel clunky by modern standards. Spaceports and planets serve their functional purpose but lack visual flair or environmental storytelling. That said, there is a certain nostalgic charm to its presentation, especially for players accustomed to older PC games where ambition often outpaced technical execution. The sound design and music are similarly modest, providing atmosphere without leaving much of a lasting impression.

Narratively, Space Trader: Merchant Marine presents a lightly satirical science-fiction setting dominated by excessive regulation and corporate control. The premise of pushing back against an overbearing Ministry through profit and clever maneuvering adds a bit of personality to the universe, but the story is mostly background flavor rather than a driving force. Quests and contracts tend to repeat in structure, and character interactions are minimal, making the narrative feel more like a thematic wrapper than a fully realized storyline.

Ultimately, Space Trader: Merchant Marine is a game defined by its ideas more than its execution. It offers a glimpse of what could have been an engaging blend of space trading and action, but neither component is developed deeply enough to fully satisfy fans of either genre. For players with an interest in retro PC titles, niche space simulations, or experimental hybrids from the late 2000s, it can still provide a few hours of curiosity-driven enjoyment, especially at a low price. However, those seeking a deep economic simulation, polished combat, or modern design sensibilities are likely to find its systems shallow and its ambitions only partially realized.

Rating: 5/10

[h3] На связи Дед и Сандей, сегодня мы бросаем якорь прямо сквозь крышу космической финансовой биржи. [/h3]

[b] Об игре: [/b] шутер от первого лица, в котором больше первого лица, чем шутера. Пять глав, повествующих о Трейдере — с момента "я хочу продавать штуки" и до "я хочу, чтобы мои подчиненные продавали штуки". Данное поделие было создано разработчиками из студии [i] HermitWorks Entertainment [/i] в 2007 году на движке id Tech 3 [spoiler] (и [url=https://hermitworks.blogspot.com/2008/04/space-trader-source-code-release.html] код которой перешёл в "опен-сорс" в 2008 [/url], так что, теоретически, игра бесплатна, но не в Стиме) [/spoiler] и данный продукт стал единственной игрой, когда-либо выпущенной этой студией перед закрытием. Основа геймплея — упрощенное "купи-продай" разные товары у двух типов торговцев (обычные торгаши и контрабандисты) через меню, беготня по небольшим локациям для сбора рандомно спавнящихся ресурсов и, собственно, "шутер от первого лица", которые запускаются в зависимости от контекста ситуации. Причем шутерная составляющая всегда начинается с того, что вы с кем-то разговариваете и после очередной фразы вас просто кидают на арену, где нужно либо перебить всех врагов (это редкость), либо завалить N-ое количество супостатов, чтобы вылез такой же супостат потолще и ну-как-будто поопаснее. На этих аренах тоже лежит куча барахла, которым можно набивать карманы, чтобы продать потом торговцам и бонусом каждый "босс" в игре является лутбоксом — как только его отпинаешь, из него во все стороны разлетаются ящики с предметами, на подбор которых у вас есть ровно 10 секунд. Да, обратный таймер запускается после конца файта на арене и будьте уверены, что утащить что-то с трупа, если вы убили его где-то далеко, вы просто не успеете (благо за сам факт убийства вам всё равно начисляют награду в любом случае). К слову, о таймере. На каждую главу (плюс три дополнительных "челленджа", если основной игры вам не хватит) у вас есть общий таймер, который уменьшается каждый раз, когда вы перелетаете с планеты на планету и только во время перелетов, любые другие перемещения на счетчик не влияют. Сама игра похвастаться большим количеством контента вроде как не может — всего четыре вида оружия (стандартный вонаби-револьвер, узи с глушителем, дробовик и штурмовая винтовка; всё кроме первого нужно снова и снова подбирать на аренах), где-то 20, может 25 моделек персонажей из которых 10 являются противниками, примерно 17 карт, которые используются повторно для разных квестов или стычек (где была жилая зона, там же может в будущем начаться стрельба, кроме одной или двух локаций, которые сделаны чисто под пострелушки), пачка основных заданий и две пачки дополнительных. Основные квесты — набери бабла, принеси N-ресурсов, перебей всех на арене, просто походи туда-сюда и поговори с персонажами. Как уже было упомянуто, в моменты перемещения по локациям есть возможность поднимать множество контейнеров, которые содержат рандомное количество рандомного ресурса и эти самые контейнеры разбросаны просто повсюду, причем некоторые из них буквально спрятаны в места, куда нужно паркурить по балкам, уступам и наклонным поверхностям. [spoiler] (колонны над головой на Европе, под лестницей на Земле, за окном, если сигать с перил последнего торговца на Ганимеде и всё в таком духе) [/spoiler] Есть целая кучка отсылок в именах персонажей (Джон Коннор, который мутузит беззащитных роботов), на постерах (Zalgo в малом баре на Земле), в элементах окружения и описании квестов. 

[b] Личный опыт: [/b] Windows Aero. Это была моя первая мысль, когда я загрузился в игру. Сочетание того, как выглядит меню, локации и персонажи в игре, на некоторое время унесло меня куда-то во времена мультсериала "Повторная перезагрузка", миллиарда тем для WinAMP'а с пузырьками и вот куда-то в этом направлении. Но устарело это даже для своего времени, ведь, как сейчас говорят, "в то время уже первый кукурузис вышел! тогда уже не второй полу-жизнь, а уже второй полу-жизнь эпизод два вышел!". Никакой глубины механик тут нет, сложностей, как таковых, тоже. Если можешь наперед хотя бы на половину шага думать, то пылесось локацию с квестами — выполняй все заказы охотника за головами, не забывая сбывать всё собранное между миссиями — покупай на всю котлету всякой херни со звездочкой (которая отмечает, что данный товар покупать прям рекомендуют) или просто то, что стоит дорого, но у чего упала цена — лети в ближайший порт — продавай всё, че ты там притащил и начинай цикл заново. Сюжет описан выше, это, если убрать мелочи, вообще всё. Но не смотря на то, что сюжет проходняковый, он не прям плохой. Есть какие-то внезапные твисты (пусть и несколько нелепые), есть относительно сносные дополнительные квесты, например [spoiler] взбунтовавшиеся роботы-работники, которые взяли персонал реакторной станции в заложники и вместо рубилова, нужно найти способ добраться до заложников и отключить этих шайтан-тарабаек [/spoiler] Есть странные вещи — вроде (вау, ноухау) есть дополнительный урон от стрельбы в голову, можно подтягиваться на не самые высокие препятствия, даже есть возможность попасть в воду с характерными звуками шлепков по жидкости (зачем?), но ты не можешь стрелять сразу после перезарядки. Снова лупить можно спустя, по ощущениям, половину, а то и целую секунду или вроде того. Начинаешь арену с 100 здоровья и 50 (или 100?) щита и сожрав все аптечки и "генераторы щита", что не прибиты к полу, можно разбухнуть до 200 и 400 единиц здоровья и щита соответственно, что позволяет с любым оружием танковать в лоб что угодно (правда не долго, бьют больно). Некоторые вещи совершенно неочевидны, вроде того, что и как тебе нужно делать, чтобы выполнить свою задачу. С одной стороны, вроде, достаточно просто читать, что тебе говорят персонажи, всегда есть целый ворох НПС, которые могут подсказать, что нужно делать или с чего начать. А потом доходишь до пятой главы и на последних двух-трех перелетах узнаешь, что окаааазывается надо было улететь с планеты, вернуться на неё и там появится тот единственный персонаж, который позволит тебе дальше двигать глобальный сюжет. Я так скажу. Люди говорят, что на распродаже эта штука продается рублей за 10. Если вам нравится инди (ведь от этого поделия очень тянет инди-сценой) и вы с удовольствием бегаете в других играх по карте, собирая какие-нибудь кольца или самоцветы и готовы к несколько туповатым противникам и не самой располагающей к себе стрельбе (хотя мне под конец даже начало нравится), то я бы вам и за большую цену это посоветовал. Скажем, рублей за 15. Вся сюжетка пролетается за 6 часов, плюс-минус ещё часа четыре, если выбивать ачивки. 

[b] Сандей: [/b] подбери, продай, повтори. И так до тех пор, пока не начнёшь чувствовать себя героем какой-нибудь рабочей драмы про перегруженный склад. Галактика полна приключений, но мы почему-то всегда возвращаемся к роли кладовщика с амбициями. И ладно бы это был осознанный выбор дизайна, но нет — это просто то, чем игра по умолчанию заставляет тебя заниматься. А эти переходы в арену из хаба? Это как если бы в любой момент переговоров по громкой связи кто-то вдруг выстрелил в потолок и заорал: "Ижеесинанебеси, всё, понеслась." Победил "босса"? Лови свою награду в виде лутбокса, который не открывается, а буквально взрывается предметами по всей карте, и у тебя 10 секунд на то, чтобы бегать и собирать этот фестиваль абсурда. Сама задумка с таймером (любым из) могла бы работать, если бы это не было так неуклюже. Но кому-то может и понравится. Мне? Нет. Не рекомендую. (но палец выбираю не я, так что...)

[h3] Вот и всё, время сниматься с якоря и выплачивать долг за проломленную крышу. Эх. До встречи в бурных водах. [/h3]

It's clearly unfinished, but what's there works well and is enjoyable for a few hours. It's a fairly simple trading sim with some FPS combat and exploration. Find quests, complete them for money, take advantage of the market, deliberately manipulate the market, etc.

Parts 2 and 3 are the meat of the game and are quite enjoyable.

Introduction (2.5/5):
"Space Trader: Merchant Marine," developed by Hermitworks Entertainment and released in 2008, attempts to combine trading simulation with arcade-style space combat. While it introduces an interesting concept, the game falls short of delivering a fully immersive or satisfying experience in either aspect.

Graphics and Presentation (2.5/5):
The visual presentation of "Space Trader: Merchant Marine" is serviceable but doesn't stand out. The space environments lack the level of detail seen in more modern space simulation games. Character and ship designs are decent, but the overall visual presentation may feel dated compared to contemporary titles.

Gameplay Mechanics (2.5/5):
The game attempts to merge trading simulation with space combat, where players navigate through space, trade goods between planets, and engage in arcade-style battles. While the concept is intriguing, the execution is uneven. The trading mechanics lack depth, and the combat may feel repetitive and disconnected from the trading aspect.

Trading and Economy (2/5):
Trading, a fundamental aspect of the game, lacks the complexity and depth found in dedicated trading simulation titles. The economic system is simplified, and the trading routes may not offer enough variety or challenge to keep players engaged in the long term.

Space Combat (2.5/5):
The space combat component, while providing a change of pace, lacks the depth and sophistication seen in dedicated space combat games. The controls and combat mechanics may feel somewhat basic, and the repetitive nature of battles can diminish their overall enjoyment.

Mission Structure (2.5/5):
The game features a mission-based structure where players take on various tasks, including trading missions and combat assignments. While this adds some structure to the gameplay, the missions may not offer enough variety or complexity to keep players fully engaged.

Sound Design (3/5):
The sound design is satisfactory, featuring space-themed music and appropriate sound effects. While not groundbreaking, the audio elements contribute to the overall atmosphere of space exploration and combat.

Learning Curve (3/5):
"Space Trader: Merchant Marine" has a moderate learning curve, making it accessible to players new to trading simulation and space combat. The tutorial provides a decent introduction to the game mechanics, but the lack of depth in both trading and combat may limit the learning experience.

Replayability (2.5/5):
The game offers a limited level of replayability. While players can revisit missions and attempt to improve their trading and combat skills, the lack of a more dynamic economy or a compelling narrative may limit long-term engagement.

Technical Aspects (2.5/5):
The technical aspects of the game are passable, but some players may encounter bugs or performance issues. The overall polish of the game may not meet the standards set by more recent titles in the space simulation genre.

Overall (2.5/5):
"Space Trader: Merchant Marine" presents an interesting concept by blending trading simulation with arcade space combat. However, the execution falls short of delivering a fully engaging or polished experience. While it may appeal to players looking for a casual and quirky combination of trading and combat, those seeking more depth in either aspect may find the game lacking.
