A Nikopol: Secrets of the Immortals egy 2008-as kalandjáték, ami lassan a feledés homályába merül – teljesen jogosan. Ahogy a játék címében is ott rejlik a titok, valójában a legnagyobb titok az, hogy egyáltalán hogy született meg ez a játék egy olyan név alatt, amelyhez Enki Bilal kultikus képregénye, a La Foire aux immortels kapcsolódik.

Grafika és látvány: Kezdjük azzal, hogy a játék grafikája még megjelenésekor is elavultnak számított. Az élettelen textúrák és a primitív karaktermodellek aligha tudják felidézni Bilal eredeti művének sötét és nyomasztó hangulatát. Az alacsony felbontású képek, a rosszul megtervezett színek és a steril környezetek mind hozzájárulnak ahhoz, hogy a játék teljes mértékben elvágja magát attól a vizuális gazdagságtól, amit a képregények kínálnak.

Történet: A játék narratívája kínosan esetlen, és szégyent hoz az eredeti anyagra. Bár Enki Bilal univerzuma tele van politikai intrikával, filozófiai kérdésekkel és mély társadalomkritikával, a játék mindezt alig tudja átadni. A sztori darabos, szétesett, és alig követhető, miközben a párbeszédek olyan semmitmondóak és szárazak, mintha egy unalmas telefonkönyvet lapozgatnánk.

Játékmenet: A Nikopol játékmenete kínszenvedés. A point-and-click kalandjátékok alapeleme a logikai feladványok és a történetvezetés, de itt mindkettő csúnyán megbukik. A rejtvények nem logikusak, hanem abszurdak és frusztrálóak, amelyek inkább próbára teszik a játékos türelmét, mint az eszét. A játék nem ad kielégítő visszajelzést, így gyakran csak véletlenszerű kattintásokkal lehet előrehaladni, ami a modern kalandjátékokhoz képest rémesen elavult megközelítés.

Hangok és zene: A hangok minősége és a szinkronszínészek teljesítménye egy újabb pofon a játékosnak. A karakterek monotonnak és érzelemmentesnek tűnnek, ami tovább fokozza az egyébként is halott atmoszférát. A zenei aláfestés unalmas és felejthető, alig-alig szól bele a játék világába, ami a legtöbb esetben inkább idegesítő, mint emlékezetes.

Összegzésként a Nikopol: Secrets of the Immortals egy fájdalmasan középszerű alkotás, ami semmilyen szempontból nem állja meg a helyét. A játék egy elszalasztott lehetőség, ami nemcsak a forrást, hanem a játékos idejét is pazarolja. Ha valaki szeretné megismerni Enki Bilal művészetét, akkor messze kerülje el ezt a játékot, és inkább vegye kézbe a képregényeket.

Удивительная и единственная в своём роде вещь. Открыла для себя внезапный кроссовер двух совершенно разных линий: творчества Бенуа Сокаля и трилогии Никополя. В целом, как это часто бывает с кроссоверами, целиком понять это чудо можно только после знакомства с обеими составляющими, иначе будет сильно непонятно.

Как один из квестов Сокаля, эта игра выделяется необычным геймплеем: от первого лица мы перемещаемся по панорамам 360. Решение, возможно, несколько неудобное на фоне уже знакомого формата "2д фон + 3д персонаж", но меня не оставляет мысль, что игра была бы идеальна для запуска на VR. Атмосфера неприятно мрачная (да, её тут многие хвалят, но миры Сокаля обычно в разы светлее и милее), нету традиционного духа авантюриста-путешественника. С другой стороны, Никополь младший определённо оказался самым харизматичным персонажем из всех сокалевских квестов. [spoiler] И самым опасным, раз уж на то пошло. Немного не ожидала от квеста необходимости убивать, хотя не могу осуждать за это Никополя. [/spoiler]

Как часть линейки Никополя, эта игра поражает в первую очередь тем, что она не повторяет оригинальный сюжет, а дописывает пропущенную в комиксе ветку. То есть это полноправная часть сеттинга, даже более каноничная, чем фильм. Что очень мило на самом деле, потому что комикс незаслуженно мало времени уделяет бедняге Никополю Младшему, которому приходится собирать все шишки из-за отца. Здесь он хотя бы раскрывается как личность, [spoiler] и пусть формально, но получает хэппи енд. [/spoiler] Не могу не восхититься всей проделанной им работой.

Ещё из приятных штук, возникших на стыке двух направлений: необычные переходы в кадрах. Вышло вроде не очень эффектно, но сама идея такого графического приёма восхитительна (если отходить совсем уж в сторону, то она была великолепно реализована в Gorogoa, где стала основой геймплея. Для видеовставок, конечно, подходит плохо). 

В целом получился шедевр, но шедевр, так и не обретший популярности из-за своей нишевости, и вдобавок получивший ту же проблему, что и многие квесты Сокаля: техническое решение геймплея было крайне быстро задавлено развивающимися технологиями индустрии, что сильно подрезало козырь в виде великолепной работы художников. "Nikopol: Secrets of the Immortals" is an ancient game from 2008.  It's a whopping 16 years old at the time of this review.  The game lacks support for any modern gaming display resolutions (or widescreen monitors), hasn't been modernised or updated to run smoothly on modern gaming PCs.  Despite this lack of modernisation, it carries a pretty high price tag for such an ancient game.  This seems to have been put on Steam as a nostalgia gouge, or just a cash grab to try profit from abandonware.

This is a Myst clone, basically you're presented with a first person 3D scene that you can look around and interact with, but movement is a matter of "teleporting" between these static scenes.  Not a true FPS game, which makes it again a little obsolete.  The idea is that you're a nice guy in a dystopian alternative world/society, and egytpian aliens crash land with their space pyramid so you need go to sort all that out, I guess.  Hey, even terrible game concepts can work if the gameplay and technical execution are good enough.  Just look at Helldivers 2.  Anyway, it's worth mentioning the graphics here are kind of okay for a 2008 game... but that's just about all this has going for it. 

On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.

The game only displays in 4:3 pillarboxed aspect ratio, due to the age of the game, it predates the 16:9 widescreen gaming standard established back in 2006 (2 years before this launched, so there's really no excuse for not being aware of the gaming environment at the time).  It's possible they're marketing this towards people using an old CRT they found in a dumpster, or this game is being specifically marketed towards people gaming on PC's from 1995... either way, this isn't really acceptable in the modern era of PC gaming.  It's obviously not going to look right on a modern 16:9 gaming display.

The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only  players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 100,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.

The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
A strange point and click adventure game with an interesting story based on a book.

[b]Pros[/b]
+ Strange interesting story
+ Graphics still hold up

[b]Cons[/b]
- Timed puzzles can cause death
- Quite a bit of backtracking

[h1]Overview[/h1]
Nikopol: Secrets of the Immortals is a very strange point and click adventure game based off a book series. I have no prior knowledge of the books so I went into the game completely blind. I have to say the game setting and story is very strange and will keep you captivated enough to see through the end.

[b]Story[/b]
Nikopol has an interesting yet very strange story. It mixes a futuristic dystopian France with Egyptian mythology and straight up aliens. The world building is quite something to behold and everything about the world and story is generally just so strange it will captivate you enough to see it through the end.

[b]Graphics & Sound[/b]
Graphics still hold up and is quite decent, nicely depicting a future dystopian France and strange alien things. Cutscenes use a mix of movie and comic panels creating a interesting and unique style during story sequences. The voice work is actually pretty good with decent dialogue written that fits the narrative.

[b]Gameplay[/b]
The game uses a first person view and allows full 360 exploration within areas and you move between areas by finding paths. Puzzles in the game aren't too complicated though there are quite a few times where you'd find an item that you know you would likely need, the problem is sometimes the game would not let you do things or take items before you make progress in other areas. Another part that can get annoying are the timed puzzles, failure to figure them out or complete them in time will cause your death requiring you to retry the sequence. There are also a few other ways you could end up dying and each time you fail the autosave or reset could put you a little ways back.

Игра в жанре квест с замечательно переданной атмосферой постапокалиптического общества. Человечество успело установить контакт с инопланетянами и пытается выжить на остатках разрушенных ядерной войной городов.  
		
Сюжетом игра обязана комиксам из прошлого тысячелетия. С разницей в 6 лет, начиная с 1980 вышли 3 издания, которые были объединены в Трилогию Никополя. ГГ (Никополь младший) является сыном человека, бросившего вызов фашистскому строю франции образца 2023 года. К этой мысли его отец пришел не сам, надоумил бог из египетского пантеона богов - Хор. На момент происшествия событий, над Парижем завис без топлива космический корабль, на котором прилетел Хор и остальные его братья и сестры. И пока остальные боги искали чем заправить пирамиду, Хор решил закрутить авантюру, тут-то ему и попался старший Никополь. Который при божественной поддержке быстро сделал спортивную карьеру, а потом и политическую, на свою голову… Играя за младшего приходится вытаскивать родителя из сложной ситуации. На этом начинается история ГГ, художника по профессии…
		
Геймплей выполнен в классическом варианте, когда в квесты играли без подсказок суровые геймеры, роняя скупую слезу над прохождением очередной "хрен разберёшь" головоломкой. Никаких подсветок предметов, никаких намеков на решение (кроме витиеватой логики реализованной разработчиками). ГГ кроме художественных наклонностей оказался классическим универсалом - может программировать карты доступа, имеет навыки дешифровки кодов, может хорошо стрелять из снайперской винтовки, состоит на хорошем счету у бога Анубиса. Удачливый такой парень. Графика в целом неплохая, все картинки прорисованы четко и гармонично. Звуковое сопровождение помогает создавать атмосферу.
		
Игру можно порекомендовать только любителям квестов. У большинства остальные геймеров игра вызовет или скуку или в силу сложности прохождения, злость.

[b]Nikopol[/b] n'est pas un jeu tout jeune car il date de 2008, mais étant un point and click on ne peut pas dire qu'il a vraiment vieilli (il était d'ailleurs très beau à l'époque).

Et surtout, il reprend l'univers d'un ponte de la bande dessinée, j'ai nommé Enki Bilal, qui s'associe ici à Benoit Sokal pour nous offrir un classique issu de la trilogie "Nikopol".

Je suis étonné de la note moyenne donnée par la communauté, pour ma part j'ai adoré l'atmosphère, les énigmes furent bien pensées, ni trop dures ni trop simples, juste ce qu'il faut, l'univers empreint d'une guerre entre plusieurs Dieux de la mythologie égyptienne est superbement rendu, le doublage impeccable, bref j'ai beaucoup aimé ce titre.

[u]Le pitch [/u]:
Vous voilà donc propulsé dans un Paris futuriste gouverné par un despote, le dictateur/prophète Choublanc, où une véritable iniquité sociale sévit dans la capitale qui est divisée en deux quartiers, le centre bardé de postes de contrôles et de caméras et où vivent les plus nantis, et tout autour dans des quartiers aussi sales que mal lotis où vivent les gueux.
Depuis peu de temps trône dans les cieux de Paris une pyramide volante très énigmatique, et qui demande à s'adresser aux autorités.

Vous incarnez bien entendu Nikopol, artiste-peintre pris en éteau entre la rebellion (l'ordre) qui prend de l'ampleur et vient à peine de vous recruter, une répression impitoyable dans ce monde archi sécurisé et empli de propagande, et une trame de fond liée à votre "défunt" paternel (qui en réalité fut cryogénisé par une cour martial et enfermé dans la tour Montparnasse), et qui pourrait bien avoir un lien avec cette étrange pyramide volante.

Le jeu n'est pas très long (8 à 10h), bien réalisé, prenant, il est vendu à moins de 5€ sans promo, alors si vous aimez le style et l'univers de Bilal faites moi confiance et ne vous privez pas, vous ne le regretterez vraiment pas, parole de scout!

Reviews for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing

Overall Game
----------------------------------------
KnightShift is a unique blend of RPG and top-down adventure. It can be played as a strategy game, an RPG, or a hybrid mix.

Seemingly very low-budget, KS still brings an interesting, if not intricate, gameplay to the gamer. For those who can tolerate the lower-end graphics and quirkiness of the game (I find it cute how the prince takes a nap, for example, as odd as it is), KnightShift will bring a good round of exploratory gameplay in an indie package that I'd recommend for a fun few hours of Princedom.

Overall Rating: 8/10

Gameplay
----------------------------------------
Warning: There are a LOT of keys/key combinations to remember for this game.

If you're undaunted, the next hurdle to overcome is a slightly awkward mouse control that seems to be reminiscent of Windows 98 mouse acceleration insanity. Once familiarized with it, the mouse awkwardness stops detracting from the interface.

I'm not sure if there were audio cues for some things, but I learned haphazardly that the giant withcraft looking areas are healing spas. This was useful fighting my first few bears. The lesson here is just to explore the areas, as context tooltips don't really exist to assist in understanding what is around you in the game.

Although rough around the edges, the quirky gameplay and level-matched quests can catch you and lure you in for more from this game. The random encounter fights contribute a little to exp farming and provide a balanced challenge as you build up your equipment set and character.

Overall Accessibility
----------------------------------------
KnightShift has dialogue that is not subtitled, making the plot a little inconvenient to follow. I don't blame the developers, who, as a small indie group, made the game because they wanted to, and did so as best they could.

Because I was unable to properly test multiplayer, the overall rating is based on only the subtitles category.

Rating: 7/10

Subtitles/Text
----------------------------------------
KnightShift is an indie game on a unique platform. That said, it's not subtitled or captioned. Deaf/HoH players can still read the text of what was said after by hitting F2 a few times, which cycles through the 'mission log' and flavor text/mission text.

At first I found it annoying, but I find the workaround tolerable and am happy they included it.

Rating: 7/10

Chatting/Communicating
----------------------------------------
While KS has multiplayer capability, I did not test. Based on the keyboard options, I saw no key for chat.

Rating: N/A

Действие игры разворачивается в мрачном будущем на территории Франции. Игроку предлагается с играть за [b] "туловище" [/b] по имени Альсид Никопол (Египтянин, наверное, :), который живет в аварийной пяти этажке, и зарабатывает деньги рисуя картинки на пляже Анапы.

В играх, начало сюжетной линии начинается с простого и понятного, и раскрывается по ходу игры, но тут, наоборот. С самого начало, не понятно, что делать и куда бежать. И только во втором акте игры, когда появляется  [b] "Тюлень", [/b] рассказывающий тебе про какой-то замес и что тебе в этом замесе отведена главная роль, сюжет становиться более понятен.

Расхлебывать замес придется на протяжении 5 игровых актов, попутно решая мелкие [b] "задачки". [/b] Задачки здесь простые и линейные, все выполняется на одно локации, за это можно издателю сказать спс, что не отправляет бегать от одного конца карты к другому. Но все-таки, один геморрой есть, это программирования пропуска. Тут даже «сапер» отдыхает. [b] Большой минус [/b] этого квеста, взаимодействие с предметами. Они не выделены каким-то цветом, и не имеют подсветку при наведении курсора, а как результат, всю игру придется тыкать «палец в жопу». Вот такое тыканье пальцем, превращает решение элементарных задачек, в испытания вашей психики.

Звуковое оформление игр, не плохое, в совокупности с очень качественно и детально нарисованными локациями, в игре создается приятная атмосфера.

Очень долгая подводка:
Как-то скучающий Я, как это обычно бывает, загорелся просмотром фантастики. Под руку удачно попался ролик, что-то типа "Топ хороших, но особо не известных фантастических фильмов". Там упоминалась "Гаттака", "Экзистенция", "Тринадцатый этаж", "Джонни Мнемоник", "Патруль времени" и ещё пара.. Какие-то я уже видел, какие-то открыл для себя впервые (да-да, "спасибо" "Экзистенция" за размышления на пару недель). Так же в этом списке был фильм "Бессмертные: Война миров". Про этот фильм Я слышал и ранее, вроде как в контексте уникального визуального стиля. Я помнил лишь о грязном мегаполисе будущего, висящей над городом Пирамиде, обилии философии и не очень качественных компьютерных моделях Богов Древнего Египта, с "физиологией кукольного Кена" (Рикман, мы помним. F). И в моей голове он отложился как концептуальный французский фильм.

Фильм.
Я оказался прав. Концептуальное французское кино, которое мне понравилось. Понравилось настолько, что я начал "рыть" интернет, в поисках информации. Фильм, конечно, не идеал. Из минусов я бы сразу обозначил некую рваность повествования и хаотичность событий и не совсем внятную концовку. Но всё же, фильм весьма хорош, и Я бы хотел порекомендовать его любителям фантастики и европейского кинематографа. Но это позже. 
Фильм открыл для меня этот одновременно притягательный и, в то же время, отталкивающий мир. Мир так похожий на наш мир всякого победившего.. Мир с философией сопротивления и пророков. Раскрывать детали сюжета Я не стану, считаю, что с фильмом стоит ознакомиться самому, а не читать мои бредни.
Из однозначных и неоспоримых плюсов фильма отмечу каст актёров. А именно выбор Томаса Кречмана на роль Никополя. Великолепное попадание в образ, характер и внешность. Отыгрывает он на всё сто процентов. Пусть этому актёру и не повезло выбраться из ампуа героев среднеоценённых фильмов и человека, что так и не смог взять Сталинград (ну серьёзно, он же не под крестом родился. Почему всё время офицер Вермахта?), но в данном фильме он на столько в тему, что воспринимать его получается только как Никополя.
Фильм Я бы поставил на первую ступеньку. Если хотите познакомиться с данной вселенной - начните с просмотра фильма.

Никополь. Трилогия.

Великолепное комплексное произведение с захватывающей глубокой историей. Крайне рекомендую к прочтению. Сам Я прочёл её с одного захода запоем.
Отдельно хотелось бы отметить потрясающий визуальный стиль (да, повторяюсь, но без этого нельзя). Сюда же, к плюсам, стихи. Поэзия Шарля Бодлера атмосферно дополняет и обрамляет мир, построенный в этом произведении.
Но прочтение визуальной новеллы так же дало ответы на вопросы к фильму. Рваное повествование фильма и некая нескладность истории идёт из того, что сам Энес Билалович, адаптируя, сменил не только основную локацию (считаю минусом, но рыночек..) с Парижа на Нью-Йорк. Но и разорвав на эпизоды собственное творение, склеил из пары кусков фильм-кадавр. А всё остальное попросту выбросил. По итогу оказалось, что фильм не освещает и десятой доли событий новеллы, хоть и является прямым переложением книги на рельсы синематографа. Фильм может быть лишь затравкой на фоне монументальности книги. Он меркнет, но всё же остаётся неплохим.
Вторая ступень. На ней и находится книга. Если вам понравился мир из фильма - ознакомьтесь после него с книгой.

Во время исследования массивов информации по Энки Билалу я наткнулся на упоминание игры (о да! Я наконец-то до на неё дошёл!). Оценки были не высоки, но мы помним про "концептуальное французское кино". Игра в жанре квест.. от неизвестной мне французской студии.. но меня это особо не пугало, иногда в таком отличительно странном находятся алмазы. Тем более игра (о удача!) продаётся в Steam.

Игра.
И да, это алмаз. Неогранённый и небольшой, но настоящий.
Если верить титрам, игру пилила студия White Birds Productions в 2008 году. Гугл говорит о ещё нескольких нестандартных квестах этой студии, о которых Я, конечно, не слышал. И так же титры сообщили, что в студии работает, собственно, полтора десятка землекопов.
Может, качество итогового продукта всё же зависит не от максимально раздутого штата с кучей разных групп?..
Как я понимаю, бюджет был ограничен и выбор у студии заключался в выборе "растянуть и сделать посредственно" или "слепить маленький драгоценный камень в короне жанра point-and-click квест". И как дочитавшие весь этот сумбур до этого места понимают, они выбрали второе. Иначе я бы не расписывал эту портянку.
Игра опирается целиком и полностью на трилогию, не беря во внимание фильм. Третья и финальная ступень.
Теперь по пунктам:
1) Музыка и звуковое оформление не плохи, но не выбиваются из среднего по палате значения. Так же, иногда, она не совсем в тему.
2) ВИЗУАЛ. Насколько же круто оформлено окружение, для столь нишевого проекта. Тут и комиксовая раскадровка в сюжетном повествовании, и живое трёхмерное окружение. Игрок - всё ещё статичная точка обзора на уровне головы Алкида Никополя-сына. НО. Я не припоминаю других квестов, где можно было бы так свободно крутить головой и рассматривать множество мелких деталей окружения. Графика смотрится достойно даже сейчас, всё же Бенуа Сокаль могёт. Отдельное уважение вызывает, что ролики выглядят созданными на движке, отличий минимум.
3) Загадки просто идеальны. Их концепция не в череде загадок, ведущей к финальному решению, а в построении главы или эпизода вокруг загадки. Для меня они образец привязки к миру, логичности и сложности.
4) Сюжет. Вот это не однозначно. Ибо игра - это отдельная самостоятельная история с своей концовкой, построенная на костяке событий и мира книжной трилогии. А точнее первой и второй книги. Но право на жизнь она однозначно имеет.
5) Минусы. Ну во первых игра полностью линейна и проходится за 4 часа (и это я ещё сидел на магнитных картах по 15 минут), но причины этого я описал уже ранее. Лучше ложка мёда чем ведро.. не мёда. Отсутствие широкоформатного разрешения. Эту проблему не решил даже ручной ввод параметров в конфиге. Ну и баги. Встретился с одним, но в двух местах - пропадание солдат. Они просто уходили в инвиз, и проходить эти места приходилось методом тыка. Возникает и решается перезагрузкой.
6) Ситуативный плюс. "Новый диск" неожиданно постарался в своё время и сделал весьма хорошую локализацию, с которой у меня даже не пригорело. Есть лишь пару огрехов в переводе (цезлы).

Чем заканчивается.
Как я уже говорил, если будет интересно ознакомиться, порядок должен быть таким: фильм-книга-игра. И только так.

Nikopol é um point-and-click de temática cyberpunk possuidor de uma trama bem esquisita, baseada em um livro de um famoso escritor francês. A obra inclusive ganhou adaptação para o cinema, mas é tão maluca que é difícil imaginar como seria o filme.

Tudo se passa em um já nem tão distante 2023 (o lançamento é de 2008), quando após uma série de guerras, religião e a política se misturam em uma França agora governada por um líder absolutista, que não só fundou um culto à sua própria personalidade, como também criminalizou todas as outras religiões. 

Naturalmente surgiram alguns movimentos de resistência, e o jogo se inicia justamente quando o jogador está prestes a entrar para um deles, em uma tentativa de encontrar seu pai.

A história, apesar de completamente doida, é intrigante e prende o jogador com seu ar de mistério. Inicialmente parece se tratar de conspirações políticas em uma sociedade totalmente oprimida pelo governo. No entanto, com o decorrer da campanha, as coisas vão ficando cada vez mais estranhas, misturando diversos elementos que não parecem ter alguma relação entre si... No fim das contas, a coisa envolve deuses egípcios, alienígenas, religião, enfim, uma tremenda colcha de retalhos.

O jogo em si é difícil, mas não porque os puzzles são complicados e você não sabe o que fazer... A verdade é que é muito complicado achar os itens corretos no meio da bagunça do cenário. Sem falar do excesso de linearidade que por vezes você está tentando a solução correta, mas por não fazer exatamente o passo a passo concebido pelo desenvolvedor, ela simplesmente não funciona, e faz você perder um bom tempo procurando outra coisa para só mais tarde descobrir que estava certo desde o início, só não havia clicado no pixel correto.

Desta maneira o jogador precisa tolerar bizarrices tais como encontrar alguns documentos que não podem ser lidos, não a menos que você os coloque sobre uma mesinha no local exato onde o puzzle precisa ser resolvido. Ou ainda ter um martelo e precisar usá-lo para quebrar uma parede, mas ela se recusa a quebrar, a não ser é claro que você bata no exato lugar onde o jogo deseja que você bata...

Há também algumas cenas de ação, em que você precisa resolver o problema antes de ser pego pelos agentes do governo, o que, na prática, significa que você tem tempo para resolver a situação. review:
Ciekawy powrót do przeszłości, zagwarantowany przez szczyptę nostalgii z 2008r pt. Crash Time 2.
Na początku fabuła jest papierowa i zastanawiamy się po co ona w ogóle jest, jednak z czasem zaczynamy się w nią wczuwać i czekamy na kolejne sprawy dua policjantów z autobahny...

Jeśli chodzi o wypadki to mamy tutaj giętą blachę, iskry i zniszczenia jak w burnoucie, nie jest mocno graficznie, natomiast czuć wszelkie zmiany następujące przez uszkodzenia pojazdu. Odpadające koła, wisząca maska, wgięta karoseria i wiele więcej.
Nawet dźwięk jazdy po drodze gruntowej jest odwzorowany perfekcycyjnie, aż ma się wrażenie, że ktoś za oknem właśnie jedzie na dworze autem. Dźwięki poszczególno cylindrowo silników aut, dźwięki w tunelu bardzo ładnie odwzorowane. 
Gra bardziej na klawiaturę niż na pada moim zdaniem.
Minusem jest, aby w pełni się cieszyć grą potrzebujemy pełnej klawiatury, ponieważ nie można zmieniać części przypisań przycisków (po prostu nie ma ich wyszczególnionych) - page down, page up, insert, home. Potrzebne są do obracania kamery i posługiwania się mapą. Ekranowa klawiatura coś pomaga ale to nie to samo :P
Kolejnym minusem jest mała liczba pojazdów, jest ich tak naprawdę może z 10, gdzie każdej jego wersji mamy  zwykle po kilka sztuk, policyjne, cywilne, inaczej stuningowane, inaczej pomalowane itp. Minusem jest też to, że mamy narzucone z góry kolory i dana wersja występuje tylko w 1 kolorze/ malowaniu.
Misję są rozlokowane niezbyt intuicyjne. Po mniej więcej 20% gry musimy sami szukać misji w obu częściach mapy, podstawiając odpowiedni pojazd w odpowiedniej lokacji i modlić się o odpalenie się dialogu (nie wiadomo gdzie i jakie auto użyć - speed runy z yt trochę pomagają).
Poziom trudności HARD wreszcie ma jakieś znaczenie - czuć niewybaczanie błędów i potrzebę tryhardu, aby ukończyć misję.
Nie które misję są moim zdaniem przekombinowane jak np. toxic waste, gdzie trzeba wykonać 6 perfekt jumpów w 45sek, walcząc z niedopracowanymi hitboxami. Często używając skrótów tak jak gra nas do tego namawia, natrafimy na kolejne zepsute hitboxy barierek, które nas obracają, czy krawężników, które podbijają nas w powietrze często robiąc beczkę w powietrzu.
Pochwalić należy AI oponentów, bo gdy się rozbijemy, albo są przeszkody na drodze, nie uderzają bezmyślnie tylko przyhamowują i starają się ominąć przeszkodę.
Jednym z poważniejszych minusów jest maksymalne używanie 2 przycisków z klawiatury na raz, oznacza to mniej więcej tyle, że nie skręcimy, przyspieszymy i nie obrócimy kamerą, bo któreś z przycisków przestanie reagować. Bardzo jest to uciążliwe przy misjach z zatrzymywaniem oponentó, gdzie potrzebujemy skręcać i patrzeć, gdzie jadą, czy to użyć ręcznego albo nitro. Najgorsze jest próba nawracania na ręcznym trzymając obroty, auto przestanie skręcać albo nie zaliczy ręcznego.
Skrypt obrotów silnika i zmiany biegów jest zrobiony fatalnie, automat zmienia biegi jakby automat był już na granicy swojego życia,  - hamując skrzynia wrzuca jakby luz i trzeba dać jej z 2sek za nim silnik stwierdzi, że jednak ma zapięty bieg i wróci na obroty. Przy używaniu nitro często potrafi zrobić nie potrzebnego kickdowna żeby tylko po czerwonym polu używać nitro.
Znajdźki wymagają trochę skila, ale da się bez większych przeszkód pozbierać.
Styl jazdy jest typowo arcadowy, wszystkim można próbować driftować po zakrętach.

Czy bawiłem się dobrze? Zdecydowanie, odpaliłem tą grę z nudów i sam się dziwię, że tak się wciągnąłem.

[h1] Even if it is not a very good production, it has a special place for me. [/h1]

The Crash Time series is actually an adaptation of the Cobra 11 (Alarm für Cobra 11) TV show. When I was young, I used to catch it on TV from time to time and it was enjoyable to watch. Even though the game is not very good, I bought it when I saw it because the show has a special place for me. Since the show generally features car chases, it also had an impact on increasing my interest in cars.

[h1] High-Quality Mechanics for Its Time [/h1]

To be honest, the driving mechanics are way ahead of what was expected. Despite being released in 2008, it has nice and realistic car mechanics. Along with this, it also features damage mechanics that most companies did not dare to do in those years. It stands out awkwardly in some places, but overall they made it successfully. Of course, no matter how successful these mechanics are, unfortunately, they are not enough to fill the void in the game's soul.

[h1] An Unimmersive Open World [/h1]

As I mentioned above, the game feels soulless. The 2 biggest reasons for this are that its world is not very satisfying, the color palette is bad, and the story is not adapted properly. It has a soulless atmosphere, and after the first 1-2 hours, the gameplay feels quite empty. After a while, we enter a vicious cycle in this boring world. The missions start to repeat themselves... In short, it looks like most of the budget was spent on mechanics, and they didn't focus much on the atmosphere, open world, and story parts. That's why it turns into a completely empty car driving game.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3695334970
[h1] Conclusion [/h1]

Unfortunately, this game is nothing more than exploiting a brand name. Most game companies try to turn hit brands into games with low budgets, and we end up encountering games like this. They wasted a show that already has a deep story. The game feels fun for a short time, but afterwards, as I said, it becomes repetitive and starts to get boring. A great potential has been wasted.

Ah, Crash Time II. Is it flawed? Absolutely. 
But it's fun.

It has some decent racing fun, the car wrecks look great, and the missions are actually underrated. I especially love the one that's about a bomber, where you have to evade a remote control explosive drone and then eventually use your own. The variety of missions with stunts, car chases, races, and absolute chaos make this game actually pretty worth playing if you just want to have some relatively easy but epic gameplay. If you're new to the racing genre, this actually is not a bad place to start given the game's difficulty. The graphics are OK.
As great as it is, we better discuss the cons. The missions are a bit weird sometimes, making not too much sense. The voice acting is terrible (even the captions can be just as bad, and sometimes the wrong character says the line), but that's a given considering the game's relatively low production quality. It also lacks a proper plot (but I've noticed that most racing games do not even have a plot so the fact there's something at all is actually pretty good). The physics is a bit janky but still works just fine. 
It is important to know that this game is based on a TV show: "Alarm for Cobra 11 - The Highway Police". This actually is the SIXTH game based on the show.

Long story short, it's fun and action-packed, but only if you can tolerate jank. It just so happens that I grew up with this game so I can definitely tolerate it and enjoy it.

I don't get the negative reviews for this one, honestly. This is a fantastic objective based driving game. The graphics are great even for today, and the cars handle like I wish gta 5 would: forgiving in breaking power and grip, but grounded in realism. Not to mention the excelent deformation physics. 

As for the difficulty, I have been playing on normal with manual shifting on controller and found it very forgiving. When I fail I know it's because I messed up, and even then, I normaly pass the missions on first try. The performance is great, runs stable and never crashes. It also does work well with a controller, you just have to bind every button. The story is a good bonus, it's just a light hearted buddy cop adventure with independent missions. I never watched the tv show it's based on, but I can get the appeal. 

Only negative I can note, is that finding the missions is a bit annoying, since some missions start randomly on patrol and some you have to drive into the marked location. I searched a wakthrough online and once I figured out how it works, it was smooth sailing. 

Anyways, if you like games like Driver, Simpsons Hit and Run or The Itallian Job, you're probably going to get a great bang for your buck with this one, especially for how cheap it is.

I’m an idiot. Up until the 50% completion mark, I kept thinking that this was some kind of Dark Souls of racing games and I was wondering why such a fun game had no cult following whatsoever. Without any embellishment, I truly thought that Crash Time II is an incredible love child of Flatout and Burnout. I was quite surprised when I saw the top reviews were negative and the game sat at a mixed score.

Following baddies across town in a miniaturized Germany that still looks on par with most recent indie and AA games, taking them down by some well-executed manoeuvres and ridiculous stunts, or using my map knowledge to halt them at exactly the right spot was thrilling. Having to end my pursuit because I got spun out by a high-speed train, or not being able to follow the AI because a bus inadvertently blocked the autobahn exit, the AI having a good degree of unpredictable behaviour created some great moments of emergent gameplay. Adding the ridiculous challenges to this gameplay formula where you need to jump on top of a skyscraper to take down a helicopter or skipping through some half sunk containers to get across a canal quickly, or using RC cars to blow up trucks made this the Flatout sequel I always wanted, even more than Wreckfest.

There is a sweet spot between tension and comfort. Comfort, in knowing your abilities and the limitations of the tool you have in your hand and tension in having to apply your abilities in difficult situations. Crash Time II hit that exact spot. I like being afraid of my own speed and having to manage my finger on the W button. Crash Time II’s car physics are pretty good and weighty, and busy streets and autobahns make pressing W a choice you have to make. Damage model is impressive too, even today. There is nothing more satisfying and infuriating than resetting progress because I’ve lost a wheel when I rammed into a bad guy without thinking about the consequences.

The voice acting sucked, story was boring at best, and those feeble attempts at humour fell flat on their face because of their innate Germanness. Still, even if I disregarded the gameplay, there was much to love here. Crash Time II perfectly encapsulates not only late 2000’s but also Germanness with its Euroslop soundtrack, missions where you have to stop beer carrying trucks because fermentation process went wrong, and environmentalists kidnapping a nuclear plant manager. Humour often missed its mark, but initial setup for most missions are “we have nothing to do, let’s go grab a coffee/get tickets for the circus/have a race for the fun of it/have a beer with a friend” and this drew a chuckle out of me every time by inadvertently showing how useless the pigs are. I even loved this game’s feeble attempts at humour.

Still, I’m an idiot. I was losing between 5 to 15 percent of my speed anytime during gear changes, even though I was playing with automatic transmission. I didn’t get the reasoning for this design decision, but it made the car fight against what I want to do. This was frustrating, because one wrong move could set my progress back ten minutes and make me replay the same case over and over again. I liked this decision though, because not only I had to conquer my enemies, but I also had to tame the car I was driving. I attributed the loss of speed to gear ratios being wonky and thought that this would be fixed when I unlocked better cars.

Better cars didn’t fix the issue and around 50% completion I came across a dirt race that required jumping over an obstacle at a certain speed. This was simply impossible, because right before the jump I was losing 20 kph and there was no space to gain more speed before the jump. So, I checked out Steam forums for a walkthrough and stumbled upon a thread talking about how unbinding shift up button will cause the game to think you’re shifting up any time you press A to turn left…

There has never been a harder facepalm in the history of men. This game wasn’t challenging at all, let alone being the Dark Souls of racing games. This game was easy as fuck. There was no challenge other than the one I idiotically set for myself. If there is no challenge there is no sweet spot, there is no tension, there is no fucking comfort. The remaining 50% went by like a breeze, without excitement, without difficulty. I unbinded the shift up button again, but the magic was lost and it wasn’t coming back.

I hate Crash Time II for making me fall in love with it under false pretences.

Crash Time 2, developed by Synetic and released in 2009, is an open-world racing game that combines high-speed chases with crime-solving missions. As a member of the Autobahn police, players are tasked with escorting politicians, transporting valuables, and apprehending criminals, all while navigating the bustling streets of a fictional German city. The game offers a mix of arcade-style driving and investigative gameplay, aiming to provide an engaging experience for fans of both racing and action genres.

The driving mechanics in Crash Time 2 are straightforward, focusing on high-speed pursuits and vehicular combat. Players have access to a variety of police vehicles, each equipped with unique attributes to aid in missions. The game's open-world environment allows for free exploration, adding a layer of freedom to the gameplay. However, the driving physics can feel dated, and the AI behavior lacks sophistication, often leading to repetitive encounters and predictable outcomes. Despite these shortcomings, the game's emphasis on speed and action provides a sense of excitement, especially during intense chase sequences.

The narrative structure of Crash Time 2 is mission-based, with players taking on various assignments that contribute to an overarching story. While the plot serves as a backdrop to the gameplay, it introduces a range of scenarios that keep the experience varied. From high-speed chases to tactical operations, the missions offer a blend of action and strategy. However, the storytelling lacks depth, and character development is minimal, which may leave players less invested in the narrative progression.

Visually, Crash Time 2 presents a world that, at the time of release, showcased impressive graphics for an open-world racing game. The cityscape is detailed, and the vehicle models are well-designed, contributing to the game's immersive atmosphere. However, by modern standards, the graphics appear dated, with textures and animations that show signs of age. Despite this, the game's art direction helps in creating a believable environment that enhances the overall experience.

The sound design in Crash Time 2 complements the gameplay, with engine roars, sirens, and crash effects adding to the intensity of high-speed pursuits. The soundtrack features a mix of music that aligns with the game's action-oriented tone. While the audio elements are functional, they don't stand out as particularly memorable, serving more to support the gameplay rather than enhance it.

In terms of longevity, Crash Time 2 offers a substantial amount of content through its diverse missions and open-world exploration. However, the lack of online multiplayer and limited replayability may deter players seeking long-term engagement. The game's focus on single-player experiences means that once the missions are completed, there is little incentive to return, especially given the repetitive nature of some tasks.

Overall, Crash Time 2 is a game that appeals to fans of arcade-style racing and action games. Its blend of high-speed chases and crime-solving missions provides an entertaining, if somewhat shallow, experience. While the game may not offer the depth and polish of more modern titles, it holds a certain nostalgic charm for players who appreciate its straightforward approach to gameplay.

For a game that cost me less than 1 USD, this game is a hidden gem. Absolute steal too. Considering the game's price and age, the production quality of this game is impressive. I may not know much about the Cobra 11 TV show and its characters because I'm not from Europe, but the story is certainly interesting and gives this game a sense of life and personality. Many people have already pointed out the low-budget English voice acting and said it was bad. I believe that the low-budget-ness of said voice acting adds to the game's personality. The dialogue is funny too, I remember one mission in which a criminal mentions "the wrong profession" or something and Semir says "a game designer?"

Speaking of the missions, some of them can be rather basic, tedious or boring at times, but you get hooked onto the story and just want to keep playing through them. They can be confusing to start too especially for beginners. (tutorial is quite long, and you need to look for the red flag beside the car name to be able to start missions, if none show up then switch to the other map). Most of the time you are driving to some location, stopping or destroying opponents and taking part in races, with some ramp platforming stuff thrown in. Limits to car and property damage may seem ironic for a game called Crash Time, but considering you're playing as two cops in Germany, you might understand why. Or not. I personally believe they add some sense of challenge to the game and encourage you not to cause too much damage while on-duty. The literal crash time is saved for when you're off-duty, so when you are, feel free to damage and crash to your heart's content!

Many of the missions are one-and-done deals without much to them, though some of them can be of rather unusual situations. Then you get to the multi-part missions, such as the street racer arc, in which Ben does usual street racer stuff while Semir pretends to be some rich fashion designer car enthusiast or something... all in the name of taking down some group of racers... Wacky stuff indeed. The aforementioned ramp platforming missions are wacky too, from jumping up to the top of a parking garage to save some guys from a plane that crash landed there, to Ben saving Semir from the Russian mafia by... jumping over some warehouses in a junkyard...

The developers certainly made great use of their unlicensed but close enough versions of real cars. What many people complain about when it comes to certain games using unlicensed cars is the lack of an acceptable damage model, if at all. But given this game series is named Crash Time, there was absolutely no reason why Synetic would not give each car a good damage model. An impressive one at that, because what game other than other games in this series and BeamNG allow you to lose your wheels if you crash hard enough? I don't know so if you do, please tell me... Driving physics are also great, with fun, slidy, oversteer-focused physics and a feeling of weight while driving heavier SUVs, trucks and whatnot. I personally prefer these physics over the more arcady physics that most other open world driving games I've played have. Vehicle selection is interesting too, while you have your typical German stuff, you also have access to other unusual machines, like a go-kart, an F1 car, a skid-steer forklift, an American truck (especially in a German setting) a military APC and even an RC car with a bomb strapped to it (referred to as the "drone" ingame).

The maps themselves are also really good considering the game's budget. Plus, their setting is rather unique too. While the autobahn can be seen in a fair few racing games, a detailed open-world German city is not a common sight in racing games, unless you count this series of course. Oh, and the autobahn map is actually beautiful, especially the valley in the middle with an insane elevation change, which will certainly surprise you once you first encounter it. Oh, and you can find a castle there and check it out too! And there's an incomplete bridge going across it that you can jump through! Graphics still hold up well for a game from 2008, even more so for a low-budget title! While the textures may show the game's age a bit, and the UI may seem a bit low-effort, the rest of the game's visuals still hold up well today. The car models are well-detailed, the lighting is very bright and vibrant (though the bloom could become too bright at times) and the cities look interesting, with lots of industrial architecture along with some urban, residential and rural areas.

With all of that being said, PLEASE try out this game for yourself. It has always been cheap and will continue to stay so, even more so during sales when it goes for less than a dollar. The Crash Time series has always been a hidden gem...

(tldr: game can be weird and wacky sometimes, cars are fun to drive and satisfying to crash, graphics still hold up well, price is very cheap so go get it pls)

A superspectacular police chase racing game with responsive controls, wonderful visuals, and astounding vehicular crashes that consistently entertains and thrills at all times.

Positive:
- All vehicles feel and handle distinctly, possessing variability in weight, acceleration, speed, and handling. Although there are no manufacturer licenses, many of the automobiles are fitting replicas of their real-life counterparts, exhibiting style and grace in their mechanical fortitude.
- Despite being about seventeen years old at the time of this writing, the artwork, and especially the city, are exceptionally conceived, representing a fictional major city in Germany accurately and impressively. The open-world roads and highways environment is relatively large and bustling, containing a living and reactive traffic system that is crowded and realistic, and constructed around a sprawling cityscape with green spaces and a lengthy river. The entire area truly is a pleasure to drive around in.
- Missions provide an excellent degree of variation and an outstanding amount of activities to partake in. Such undertakings always entail chases, speed, and law enforcement recklessness. Ranging from pursuing fugitives, causing massive amounts of destruction, to street racing, there is an abundance of fun and excitement to be had.
- As fast as the vehicular action can get, and as populated as the city is, the game runs extremely smoothly and rarely goes below the specified 144 frames per second on maximum settings. Movements are incredibly smooth, and the locomotion of heavy mechanical objects are splendidly fluid. The combination of awesome technical flawlessness and supreme automotive mobility makes for a wholly exhilarating experience.
- Every vehicle and most city structures are governed by physics-based damage models, are fully destructible, and suffer different types of deterioration. Such a synthesis of systems creates extravagant collisions, impressive amounts of wreckage to the parties engaged and bystanders, as well as striking spectacles involving metal and speed.
- Story and plot are based on a German television series (Alarm für Cobra 11 – Die Autobahnpolizei), and while a direct comparison to the source material could not be made as a reference for this review, the plot, story, general writing, and associated voice acting are positively cheesy and campy, but in a thoroughly charming and endearing way. The humor genuinely works cohesively well alongside a crime stopping framework with lines and jokes that are optimistic and easygoing.
- Acrobatics and platforming in some case missions provide an amusing break from the more traditional police work, generating some impractical and totally absurd maneuvers through obstacles and ramps around the city that are exceedingly exciting. Such attempts can often be some of the most challenging driving in the game, and accomplishing them feels highly rewarding.

Neutral:
- Police cases, which appear in their own "Cases" submenu, can only be accessed after a case has already started and after a saving point has been reached. In order for the player to begin as the operative of a case, they must go into a different submenu, titled "The Patrol", drive around aimlessly for a bit, and wait for a summons to participate in a case for the adventure to actually begin. To make matters even more cumbersome, some cases only start if one finds a specific spot in the city, with no actual gameplay associated with reaching that destination. This is an unnecessarily bureaucratic process that could have been implemented in much more sensible ways.
- Weather changes or day/night cycles are nonexistent, as it is endlessly sunny and invariably dry. Regardless of the absence of such effects, traversing the city completing many tasks and assignments is still a joy and a treat. The perpetually favorable meteorological conditions and the continually diurnal status do not hinder the numerous explorations and missions by any means.

Negative:
- The software requires that .NET Framework version 3.5 is installed and activated in order for it to work. This is a much older iteration than what is considered to be the current version at the time of this writing (4.8).
- There is no way to activate vertical sync or to limit the frame rate from within the game. The only way for this setting to be operational is to actuate it externally using one's video card software.

Overall rating: 4.0/5.0

I have zero nostalgia for this game, and I had never heard of it until I randomly bought it for $1 a few days ago.

Gotta say it's truly a hidden gem. In large part due to how the physics are completely nailed (for an arcade game) - it's just plain fun to drive around. The vehicles all feel grounded with a sense of weight, and are so detailed that you can feel their suspension shift and load/unload the tires as you accelerate, slow down, or go up/down inclines. You also have to mind creating oversteer with the gas, as overdoing the gas at lower speeds can help you slide through corners (or help you spin around) - but it can also cause you to lose traction at high speed and cause you to crash, so you always have to be mindful of the car you're driving, and how its tires and suspension behaves in different conditions.

The AI is also fantastic. They are able to navigate the world very well, and do not seem to employ cheating or off-screen teleporting to give the illusion of competent AI, like many other games do. So when you're chasing an enemy car (or being chased) through the entire city, it feels believable and can be very exciting, as many unexpected things can happen -- the AI can try to trick you by randomly looping around and turning 180 degrees around (causing you to blow past them), or by suddenly taking obscure shortcuts and leaving you in the dust, among other tricks.

The difficulty level is also spot on, at least on Normal, and you generally have to sweat to win. For example, some enemies can only be stopped by damaging them to 100%, but you can only significantly damage them by really smashing them into obstacles at very high speeds (otherwise you only nibble-off like 2% health, or cause them to innocently spin-out and not hit anything - and then then you'll run out of time). So you have to let them get well ahead of you, and then plan when & where to build up enough speed to cause them to lose control and smash into something. This strategy is necessary but risky, because your enemy may take a sudden turn and make you miss, or you could end-up smashing into a wall and losing all your health. Or if you mistime your acceleration, your enemy may get an uncomfortable lead, and perhaps an enemy helper car may fishtail you and ruin your run.

So yeah, I expected mediocre jank, but this is a very competently made game with great physics & AI, and a world that's fun and challenging to drive through. Thoroughly enjoyed my time with it, and I loved how it captured the feeling of being in a chase in some cheesy TV show.

[h1] It took me ages to finally find you from my childhood memories. [/h1]

One of the first ever racing games I played in my childhood and I must admit it was extremely difficult for me to find this game since it was too niche even when it came out and the game series never had that big success compared to its competitors. You can tell by the fact that the game is originally based on a German TV series called "Alarm für Cobra 11 - Die Autobahnpolizei", so that is the reason why around 95% of the car list is pure German. Well, I didn't mean they got real BMWs, Audis and such, they did them the same way as the GTA series did to avoid copyright issues due to limited budgets which is also one of the big reasons why this game is so bad-known to this day.

I was worried that my nostalgic rose-tinted glasses would deceive me with how I remembered this game from the past but even to this day it's still fairly fun and has no real other alternatives. Tell me, in what other game you can play as a police detective in a well-made German city where you can drive various types of vehicles, and by that I mean not just your standard saloon or SUV but also a kart, APC, F1 formula car, limo, Optimus Prime-esque truck and more.

Since the game's devs were based in Germany you will be feeling German vibes really well, for example I never saw any other racing game that would have TURNING SIGNALS SET BY DEFAULT or soft-limiter when you wanna hear the engine sound while staying still [spoiler] Turning signals are better to swap with manual shift pedals because automatic transmission is horrible with changing gears and you can fool soft-limiter by setting your gearbox to neutral [/spoiler] or how often do you hear something related to taxes (there's is a literal hint that says "Don't wreck anything. Taxes are high enough already") or the fact that I completed this game 100% with all cars unlocked within 10 hours precisely lol.

I'm not sure why this game has mixed reviews because the game isn't difficult at all, like yeah there might be some annoying levels but you can still complete them after a few attempts, optimization is relatively good, graphics still look really awesome, story is somewhat cringe but it doesn't overwhelm you at the same time.

Overall I find this game a hidden gem today and it's sad to see that the game series died long ago with the studio that made it, I doubt we will have something like this game any time soon.

Un petit jeu bien sympa de l'époque Xbox 360 où l'on incarne le mal à l'état pur, sans prise de tête.

Overlord fait partie de ces jeux au concept simple mais terriblement efficace qui faisaient le charme de la génération Xbox 360. Ici, pas question de sauver la veuve et l'orphelin : on joue littéralement une sorte de Sauron en armure noire, entouré de sa horde de larbins prêts à tout casser sur son passage.

Pourquoi ça fonctionne toujours aussi bien :

Un concept jouissif et décalé : Diriger sa petite armée de créatures (qui s'équipent avec tout ce qu'elles trouvent, des fourches aux citrouilles en guise de casque) pour piller les villages et écraser les héros clichés de la fantasy est un vrai plaisir coupable. L'humour noir fait mouche du début à la fin.

Simple et sans prise de tête : Le gameplay, qui rappelle un Pikmin version diabolique, est super accessible. On avance, on envoie ses troupes au charbon, on améliore sa tour et son équipement, et on profite du spectacle sans avoir à réfléchir pendant des heures.

En bref : Un jeu modeste qui a forcément un peu vieilli techniquement, mais qui reste super fun et rafraîchissant. À prendre sans hésiter à petit prix pour passer un bon moment détente du côté obscur.

Un éditeur qui préfère enterrer ses licences plutôt que de les faire vivre.

EA continue de démontrer ce qui ne va pas dans l'industrie du jeu vidéo : des studios talentueux sont sacrifiés, des équipes qui ont consacré des années à créer des univers et des licences appréciés par des millions de joueurs sont démantelées, et des franchises entières finissent abandonnées.

BioWare fait partie de ces studios qui ont marqué l'histoire du jeu vidéo. Mass Effect, Dragon Age… Des univers, des personnages et des histoires qui ont profondément marqué toute une génération de joueurs. Et derrière ces jeux, il y avait des développeurs passionnés, dont le travail mérite mieux que d'être traité comme des pièces jetables.

Le plus enrageant dans tout ça, c'est cette logique qui consiste à laisser mourir des licences plutôt que de leur donner une nouvelle chance. Si EA ne souhaite plus investir dans certaines franchises, pourquoi ne pas simplement les vendre ou en céder les droits à des studios qui seraient prêts à les faire vivre ? Pourquoi préférer les laisser prendre la poussière plutôt que de permettre à d'autres développeurs de reprendre le flambeau ?

Pour ma part, j'ai décidé de ne plus soutenir cette politique. Je vais donc mettre un avis négatif aux jeux édités par EA sur Steam, non pas nécessairement parce que ces jeux sont mauvais mais parce que je refuse de soutenir EA de quelque manière que ce soit. Bien entendu, plus aucun jeux édités par eux ne sera acheté de ma part également, c'est un peu dommage car certains m'intéressaient mais tant pis.

Adieu EA donc, puisse la licence Mass Effect revenir un jour

[code]Хочется прямо отдельно выделить то, что локации здесь крупные. Очень много времени тратится на банальную ходьбу и Бэктрекинг.[/code]

Визуально игра ничем не выделяется, кроме как решением придать объектам лёгкое свечение. Из-за этого графика местами кажется мыльной.

Локации меж собой различаются, но их наполнение зачастую однообразно. Переключаешься между ними не часто, поэтому окружение легко приедается.
[hr][/hr]
[h2][b]🎮 ИГРОВОЙ ПРОЦЕСС И МЕХАНИКИ[/b][/h2]
Удовольствия от геймплея я не получил. Виной этому — три всадника апокалипсиса:
[olist]
    [*][b]Устаревший движок, враждующий с новыми мышками.[/b] Даже не знаю сколько часов я терпел залипание клавиш. Как долго наблюдал за тем, как прихвостни бегут на смерть или нарезают круги... Хорошо что на глаза попалось руководство с пояснениями. Нужно было снизить Частоту Опроса с 1000Hz до 150Hz. (Пользуйтесь.)

    [*][b]Неудобное управление с глуповатым ИИ.[/b] Прихвостни крайне плохо простраивают пути. Даже если ты их ведёшь, они могут застрять в объектах по дорогах или в упор не видеть лежащий мешок с золотом в ногах. Бывало они обтекали объекты и убегали куда-то в закат.

    [*][b]Однообразие и отсутствие вариативности.[/b] Механик ужасно мало... Все бои и продвижение по локациям ощущались одинаково. Менялись только декорации.
[/olist]

[h2][b]📑 ПРОЧИЕ ВПЕЧАТЛЕНИЯ[/b][/h2]
В первую очередь игру расценивал, как симулятор злодея и комедию. Печально, что ни первым, ни вторым меня здесь удержать не смогли.

Шкала морали здесь как будто бы лишняя. "Порабощая", прямых злодеяний не совершаешь. Только указываешь на своё господство и тебе по доброй воле таскают дань. Смысл жанра в этом случае как-то теряется. Обратная же сторона этого — бездумные убийства и разрушение всего, что только можно. Снова же, не столько злодей, сколько убийца и вандал. Был бы рад увидеть что-то среднее, но увы, имеет что имеем.

Местный юмор может быть временами забавным, но весёлым я бы его посчитал скорее в детстве, чем сейчас. Впрочем, стоит отметить что он необычен, как минимум из-за своей жестокости к миру.


До конца так и не прошёл. Засыпать лучше в кровати, чем во время игры. Да и отсутствие желания возвращаться тоже печальный знак.
[hr][/hr]
[h2][b]⚖️ ИТОГ[/b][/h2]
Преисполненный хорошими воспоминаниями, столкнулся с жестокими реалиями. Слабый геймдизайн с геймплеем и не привлекательные злодеяния с юмором. 

Для ностальгирующих может ещё и пойдёт, но в остальном опыт довольно печальный.

[b] In short: [/b]
If you've ever searched online for a necromancer type game with some form of minion summoning mechanic, Overlord gets mentioned everywhere.
You might not be a necromancer but if you're looking for something to scratch that specific itch, that makes you want to send your minions into villages and cities to plunder, kill and pi** on the innocents belongings while standing next to the burning houses and farms and letting out your most cartoonish "yes! take their stuff! kill them all! muhahaha!" then this is the absolute most perfect title to date. Technically you also gain more minions from killing living things, so you are kind of a necromancer. Keep in mind that you should play it with a controller and even then the controls will challenge your patience here and there.

For a 19 years old classic the visuals of this game aged really well. It's humorous and the big semi-open areas give you plenty opportunity to explore and search for loot and upgrades. Everything you do has an effect on the game, killing random stuff gives you more minions, destroying and plundering gives you gear for your minions and gold. A relatively fleshed out corruption mechanic exists, which gives you the feeling that the world is reacting to you doing evil things just because you want to, which is cool. The gameloop also contains some minor puzzles. There's a lot of game juice here, killing, destroying and even spawning minions feels good and sounds good. Everything you do is fun.

[b] Annoyances [/b]
The cameracontrols and controls in general are the absolutely most horrendous I have ever had to deal with in any game. You should really play it with a controller, since the game was made for it and its really noticeable. Also the mouse and keyboard controls really often bug out and you have to go to the pause menu to reset it. Even with controller it is sometimes absolutely awful to control anything in this game. Most of the time it wont get in your way, it's not a constant annoyance. But it does get in your way on a regular basis.
Another annoying thing is that sometimes you might loose all your minions to something (for example you accidentally sending them to their deaths) and theres no spawntunnel in your vicinity. So you have to walk all the way back to the last spawntunnel and then come back with fresh minions which might just be 2 minutes of playing walking simulator.

[b] Conclusion [/b]
I do think that the fun of the game outweighs the annoyances. The Game is not difficult enough to be really frustrating, when you loose your minions to some control-issues. Also it doesn't really matter if your minions die, they are literally made for being sent to their demise. For 5 bucks this is a no-brainer if you enjoy minionmanagement in videogames or just want to be the evil guy for once.

Encarnar a un señor oscuro y dirigir a una horda de esbirros dispuestos a arrasar con todo a su paso resulta ser una premisa tremendamente divertida y llena de acción. Las comparaciones con Pikmin, la clásica saga de criaturas de Nintendo, son inevitables, ya que la gestión de esta pequeña y caótica legión es el pilar fundamental de la experiencia. Sin embargo, en esta ocasión la balanza se inclina de manera evidente hacia el combate directo, ofreciendo un ritmo dinámico que encaja a la perfección con la temática villanesca y gamberra que propone la aventura.

A pesar de lo entretenido que resulta sembrar el caos, la fórmula se queda un poco a medio camino si la medimos con sus referentes, pues se echa en falta ese encanto tan particular y la genialidad en el diseño de los desafíos. Las situaciones planteadas carecen de la profundidad estratégica necesaria, convirtiendo a los sirvientes en simples herramientas de fuerza bruta en lugar de piezas clave para resolver rompecabezas verdaderamente complejos.

Overlord™ — это необычная приключенческая игра, которая смогла выделиться среди множества фэнтезийных проектов благодаря своему чёрному юмору, оригинальной механике управления приспешниками и нестандартному взгляду на жанр. Вместо роли благородного героя игрок получает возможность стать настоящим тёмным властелином, который постепенно возвращает себе власть.

Главная особенность игры — это управление миньонами. Маленькие демонические существа становятся главным инструментом игрока: они атакуют врагов, собирают ресурсы, открывают проходы и помогают решать различные задачи. Наблюдать за их поведением действительно весело, ведь каждый тип приспешников имеет свои особенности и характер.

Геймплей представляет собой смесь экшена, приключения и лёгких элементов стратегии. Сам Повелитель участвует в сражениях лично, но большая часть успеха зависит от грамотного использования своей армии. Нужно правильно выбирать, каких миньонов отправить в бой, кого оставить для защиты и как использовать окружение.

Отдельно стоит отметить юмор. Overlord постоянно играет с привычными фэнтезийными клише: здесь герои оказываются не такими уж благородными, а зло становится главным действующим лицом. Игра отлично высмеивает классические истории о спасении мира и предлагает посмотреть на события с другой стороны.

Мир получился атмосферным и запоминающимся. Замки, деревни, подземелья и различные фантастические локации имеют собственный стиль. Музыка и общий тон игры хорошо поддерживают ощущение сказочного, но немного безумного приключения.

Однако у проекта есть и недостатки. Управление миньонами иногда может быть неудобным, особенно в сложных ситуациях, когда они начинают вести себя не так, как ожидаешь. Некоторые задания могут показаться однообразными, а ближе к концу игра начинает повторять уже знакомые идеи.

Графика сегодня выглядит устаревшей, а технические моменты иногда напоминают о возрасте проекта. Но благодаря своему стилю и оригинальной концепции игра всё ещё сохраняет свою привлекательность.

В итоге Overlord™ — это отличный пример игры с собственной идеей и характером. Она не предлагает самый глубокий сюжет или сложнейшую боевую систему, зато дарит уникальный опыт, которого почти нет в других проектах. Если хочется необычного фэнтези с юмором, атмосферой и возможностью почувствовать себя настоящим злодеем — Overlord точно заслуживает внимания.

[h1]Dragon In My Dreams[/h1]

[i]There will be a TL;DR at the end.[/i]
 
~

Esteemed, beloved, and highly influential internet creative [i]James Rolfe[/i] once created a documentary titled “[i]The Dragon In My Dreams[/i]” where he spoke about a childhood playground decoration that continued to influence his mentality well into adulthood. He found himself dreaming of the dragon growing up, thinking about it sometimes [b]as[/b] a grown up, and eventually making a return to his childhood playground to reconnect with this aging part of his own psyche. In some ways he idealized the dragon, in others he might have integrated it into his thought processes on a subconscious level, but in all ways it must have been a surreal experience to kneel down before that facsimile of a monster and see it through the eyes of a child once again.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Kc3JqVIIJA 
[b]Second Sight[/b] was [i]The Dragon In My Dreams[/i] for me.

I remember going on a field trip in [b]2004[/b] and learning about it through a magazine. A friend of mine had some gaming articles that his parents had gifted him for entertainment on the bus ride. I got to see [i]action packed[/i] screenshots of telekinesis, dead bodies being used as weapons, guns, and lots of buzzwords designed to make this experience seem like some sort of apotheosis. “[b]Learn the truth[/b]”, “[b]Wanted, dead or alive[/b]”, “[b]most dangerous man in the world[/b]”.
I even saw the TV commercials which, if you saw them in their native [i]2004[/i] habitat, would be incredibly edgy.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EY9HpqclOEQ
Both of these campaigns focused on the bodily violence, the extreme aspects, and the insane imagery. The mental takeaway was always that of complex battlefields, adult themes, grief, and a stitched together man rampaging through an illegal research complex.
Somehow it really impacted my younger self and that cover image, which [i]goes hard as hell[/i], was burned into the back of my brain for years upon years even though my only exposure was from one magazine and a single viewing of the TV commercial.
It’s all there:
The serious red lighting, the dramatic cover that conveys frustration and hopelessness, the title “[b]Second Sight[/b]” promising a mystery, the screenshots of dead bodies being magically levitated, the promise of visceral combat.
The impact stayed with me, but as a child I had no real idea what the product was or had a frame of reference to digest the kind of experience it was offering. My experience with games at that point was primarily 90’s [i]Nintendo[/i] titles and seeing fleeting glimpses of [i]Halo[/i] when older kids were playing it.
For a time afterwards, I began to wonder if [b]Second Sight[/b] was a real thing, if I hallucinated it, if I somehow confused it with [i]Kayne & Lynch[/i] due to the similar colors, beat up protagonist, and similar marketing strategy. I never remembered what the game itself was named.
Flash forward more than 2 decades later and this fully grown dork just so happens to see that cover art on [b]Steam[/b] which triggered [i]Vietnam[/i] style flashbacks (sort of the opposite of what is in the game itself) but, gleeful at my rediscovery of this haunting imagery, I resolved myself to finally face [i]The Dragon In My Dreams[/i] and see what [b]Second Sight[/b] truly has to offer.

~

Uh. It’s not great.
Foremost, I want to get out of the way, there’s no expectation that my childhood memories should be held as an ideal - or even that the marketing itself is accurate - but anyone coming here for a gritty, dire, adult, or profound experience should turn elsewhere.
A big issue is that the dialogue and story are clever enough, but the twists shown may have been mind-blowing for a time where games were generally reserved for sillier titles when [i]Sly Cooper[/i] and [i]Rachet & Clank[/i] were the heavy hitters for narrative design. By today’s standards the “twist” is novel, but nothing too jarring. There are some good plot aspects, but the strong opening quickly loses its momentum and you’ll likely be calling out the cliches or coming up with far more interesting ideas for twists than the developers themselves chose to run with. What you actually get is an A plot that follows a perpetually confused and well-meaning underdog in his search for answers and a B plot that follows a goofy military experience that makes less and less sense until the end of the game itself. The big twist is [spoiler]The A plot is the B plot. That’s it.[/spoiler] Some of the dialogue is nice, the animations are top shelf during the pre-animated cutscenes, but the thrust of the plot is uninspired and there are plenty of cringe-inducing lines proving that “[i]woa! That just happened![/i]” was in scripts decades before today’s slop. It’s sadly a flawed gem. There’s a lot of promise, but the “[i]too cool for school[/i]” vibes make it feel too amateur and goofy to be taken seriously, even though it obviously wants to be playing with the bigger kids on the playground.

Gameplay wise, [b]Second Sight[/b] is tragic. It did not age well, but after playing many games from before and during this era, it was bad even for its time. While there are miniature combat sections, in spite of what marketing will tell you, combat is [i]LAME[/i] and you [i]WILL NOT WANT TO DO IT[/i]. [b]Second Sight[/b] is primarily a [i]stealth[/i] game where some small concealment puzzles are punctuated by a few action setpieces. The catch is that if you are caught, unlike in established “[b]actually good[/b]” stealth titles where powerful enemies confront you, security is on high alert, a mission may fail and reset - instead there is an unending infinite bad-guy spawner. The game itself is saying “[i]Too bad you messed up, now suffer![/i]”. You might as well reset yourself - but as annoying as the all-you-can-defeat buffet of baddies can be, sometimes the optimal solution is to face-tank their attacks and rush past them to complete the level. These things wouldn’t be so bad if getting caught and dealing with threats was organic, but it tragically isn’t. The true horror in this game is the [i]controls[/i] which are at the bottom tier of any game control setup I’ve ever played. The shooting mechanisms are worse than [i]Goldeneye[/i] and the stealth game has awkward tank controls.
When you get caught sneaking, most of the time it’s not because you made a mistake, but generally because the controls are too clunky and unintuitive to execute plans properly.
When you get into combat, most of it is not accurate or interesting because the controls are too clunky and unintuitive to make attacks properly.
It often boils down to standing in the open (or getting lit up like a cigarette while peeking from cover) to charge up psionic abilities or slowly adjust your aim, letting enemy bullets slowly plink away at your massive health bar.

Having to work with bad controls in stealth to try avoiding bad controls in combat to finally continue the generally [i]ok[/i] story with an [i]alright[/i] twist is… well it’s something, but it wasn’t something I can recommend.

Even if the version of the game I imagined back in [i]2004[/i] was better in terms of plot and story, the controls and general gameplay alone were probably why the fans consider this a buried gem to this day without ever having wider appeal.
 
~
 
[h3]TL;DR[/h3]
[i]3.5/10[/i]
[b]Second Sight[/b] is a [i]Flawed[/i] game.
While the premise and presentation appear promising, the gameplay and follow through leave much to be desired. This one needs a modern remaster to be properly enjoyed.

Незаслуженно провалившийся и забытый шедевр начала 2000-х. Игра с необычными и новыми для того времени геймплейными механиками, интересной стилистикой и нетривиальным сюжетом.
Как и во многих играх того времени вас не водят за ручку, объясняют задачу один раз, вскользь во время диалога; много ситуаций ,где нужно подойти творчески, чтобы решить головоломку или пройти определенное место. Игра предлагает несколько способов прохождения,  в зависимости от вашего стиля игры, а именно, на выбор предлагается ряд паранормальных способностей: телекинез, невидимость, пси-атака, проекция. Многие из способностей имеют ,так сказать, вторую фазу, открывающуюся по ходу сюжета. Что интересно, некоторые возможности игрой никак, НИ РАЗУ не упоминаются, но при этом они есть: например, можно открыть кпк на "Tab",  зачем-то есть милишная атака на f, которая ничего не делает, или захват npc со спины. Присутствует определенная нелинейность, несмотря на коридорность локаций и даже различные заставки после смерти гг, с показом альтернативного развития сюжета. По духу больше всего напоминает фильмы про Джейсона Борна.
   Из минусов можно отметить отвратное управление во время прицеливания(видно,что кривой консольный порт бородатых лет), и неоправданно высосанные из пальца квестовые тупняки (а на деле просто неочевидные действия) ближе к концу игры, где нужно 3 раза пробежать весь уровень в обе стороны, чтобы понять, что вообще требуется и куда идти, которые ,такое ощущение, специально придуманы просто чтобы растянуть хронометраж. Все это усугубилось моим принципом никогда не смотреть прохождение, а сидеть пока не снизойдет озарение.
   Я был впечатлен этой игрой, будучи ребенком, когда она бесплатно прилагалась к видеокарте nvidia, и вот будучи дряхлеющим скуфом... я впечатлен вновь.  9/10

For how cheap this game goes for on sale, Second Sight is worth it. Good enough acting, expressive characters, a compelling story, a nice artstyle, and a satisfying plot that doesn't go on for longer than it needs to. Best of all is the gameplay. Access to a fun multitude of powers as you go through the game with John Vattic, the main character. In a lot of aspects it still holds up. My only problems were the cutscene/audio issues where cutscenes would cut off too quickly and the audio would be out of the sync. An issue that especially frustrated me was not being able to close the game and pick up where you left off. You have to finish a level and only get checkpoints in the same session. Whenever you close it, you start from the beginning of the mission each time. Thankfully, chapters aren't painfully tedious and usually last up to an hour each at most. 7/10.
