Second Sight is a distinctive third-person action adventure that reflects both the creative ambition of Free Radical Design and the particular experimental spirit of the mid-2000s era of game development. Originally released in 2004 and later brought to modern platforms by THQ Nordic, the game occupies an unusual space between stealth shooter, psychological thriller, and supernatural sci-fi drama. At its core, it tells the story of John Vattic, a parapsychology researcher who awakens in a high-security medical facility with no memory of how he got there, only to discover that he has developed powerful psychic abilities. This amnesia-driven premise may sound familiar on paper, but Second Sight quickly distinguishes itself through its structure, atmosphere, and its willingness to weave narrative and mechanics tightly together.

The storytelling unfolds across two timelines: a present-day escape from imprisonment and a series of flashbacks to a military operation that preceded Vattic’s capture. These shifts are not mere stylistic flourishes; they serve to gradually recontextualize everything the player thinks they understand. As the plot progresses, conspiracies involving covert research programs, psychic experimentation, and shadowy government agendas come to the forefront. The pacing is deliberate, allowing tension to simmer rather than relying purely on explosive spectacle. One of the game’s greatest strengths is how it builds intrigue through uncertainty, encouraging players to question what is real, what is remembered, and what might still be hidden beneath the surface. The eventual narrative revelations land with genuine impact because the groundwork has been carefully laid.

Mechanically, Second Sight sets itself apart through its integration of psychic powers into both combat and stealth systems. Early on, Vattic’s abilities are limited, but as the story unfolds, he gains access to telekinesis, healing, psychic blasts, charm-based invisibility, astral projection, and even the ability to possess enemies. These powers are not superficial add-ons; they fundamentally reshape how encounters can be approached. Telekinesis allows players to manipulate objects, disarm foes, or create distractions. Possession enables infiltration of guarded areas without firing a shot. Projection offers a reconnaissance tool that reduces risk and encourages planning. The gradual expansion of this toolkit provides a satisfying sense of progression and empowerment.

The game’s level design supports this flexibility. Encounters are often constructed with multiple routes and strategies in mind, whether through vents and side corridors for stealth-focused players or open firefights for those who prefer direct engagement. While firearms are available and functional, they rarely feel like the most interesting solution. The psychic mechanics invite experimentation, and the game subtly rewards creative thinking. At times, however, the balance can tilt too far in favor of psychic dominance, particularly once more powerful abilities are unlocked. Certain confrontations become less tense when enemies can be effortlessly manipulated or neutralized from a distance. Even so, the satisfaction of combining powers in inventive ways remains one of the experience’s highlights.

That said, Second Sight undeniably carries the technical hallmarks of its era. The camera can be temperamental, particularly in confined spaces, and aiming lacks the refinement that later third-person shooters would standardize. Movement animations and environmental interactions occasionally feel stiff by modern standards. Yet these rough edges are less damaging than they might appear because the core design remains thoughtful and cohesive. Rather than relying on twitch precision, the game often emphasizes positioning, timing, and power management. For players willing to acclimate to its early-2000s sensibilities, the underlying systems still hold up remarkably well.

Visually, the game presents a grounded aesthetic that leans into muted tones and institutional architecture, reinforcing its themes of secrecy and control. Research labs, military compounds, and urban backdrops are rendered with a functional realism that suits the narrative’s tone. Character models and textures reflect the technological constraints of the time, but strong art direction and consistent atmosphere help maintain immersion. The audio design contributes meaningfully as well, with a restrained musical score that underscores tension without overwhelming it, and voice performances that lend credibility to the unfolding drama.

What ultimately makes Second Sight memorable is not just its mechanics or plot twists, but how cohesively those elements reinforce each other. The psychic abilities are narratively justified, the fragmented structure mirrors the protagonist’s fractured memory, and the gradual accumulation of power parallels the recovery of truth. Few games of its era attempted such a tight interplay between story and gameplay systems. While it may not have achieved blockbuster recognition, it has earned a dedicated following precisely because of this ambition.

Revisiting the game today reveals both its age and its originality. In an industry that often revisits established formulas, Second Sight feels refreshingly singular. It stands as a reminder of a period when studios were willing to experiment boldly with genre hybrids and unconventional storytelling structures. For players interested in narrative-driven single-player experiences that blend stealth, action, and supernatural elements, it remains a compelling and worthwhile journey. Despite dated controls and presentation quirks, its imaginative design and carefully constructed mystery ensure that it continues to resonate long after the credits roll.

Not as mechanically interesting as Splinter Cell, not as well-written as MGS 2, but still engaging nonetheless. Beautiful showcase of 2004 technology (particle effects! interactible physics objects! floor reflections! ragdolls!) The slow dripfeed of powers and the creative integrations required to solve puzzles keep levels from feeling too similar. There's a sense they had a larger game in planning, one with more interactions between the psychic abilities and the world around you, but what we got works.

However, for a game so focused on stealth, the constant combat it throws at you (along with the infinitely spawning enemies) sometimes makes for a tedious experience. The levels themselves are fairly short, but can turn into a slog if you missed a switch or item to pick up. None of it's necessarily difficult, but this is in part due to the braindead AI. F.E.A.R.'s automated planning and algorithms, this is not.

Second Sight - это не просто реликт давным-давно минувших времён, а один из большинства уникальных проектов типа "игр категории Б". Вот я прошёл игру до конца, что стоило мне титанических усилий, как с точки зрения затраченного времени, нервов и впервые за долгое время был вынужден смотреть прохождение на Ютубе, ибо гений на разработчике оказался сильнее. Игра вызывает довольно смешанные чувства и во время наших приключений, да и после прохождения как такового.

На этой рецензии стоял бы палец вверх, если бы не один значительный момент, а именно - техническое состояние игры. В смысле, это не единственный недостаток, но на остальные ещё можно было бы закрыть глаза и может игра по-другому бы чувствовалась, если бы не то, как она работает (отвратительно). По дефолту игра не работает в 16:9, так что надо лезть в конфиг-файл и прописывать там нужное разрешение. Ну и кайф, всё отлично, можно даже ФПС там прописать, чтобы игра не лочилась на 30, да? Ну так вот - НЕТ БЛYAТЬ. В строке герцовки экрана можно даже миллион написать, сама игра всё-равно будет работать в 15-20 ФПС. Есть различные руководства Стим, в которых написаны методы исправления этого каличного фреймрейта, но имеется также маленькая приписка, что "работает не у всех". Плюс игра вообще-то под консоли пилилась, так что без ограничения кадров можно ожидать разных весёлых вещей, как в 3Дэшных ГТА. 

Что однозначно заслуживает похвалы - сюжет этой игры. Если бы здешняя история была скучной, то я бы через силу и боль так и не допрошёл бы эту игру, но повествование меня затянуло и хотелось узнать, чем же закончится история доктора Джона Ваттика, да и всего мира, если так посмотреть. Путешествия между прошлым, будущим и настоящим, нелинейное повествование и просто добротная история - это то, что делает сюжет этой игры особенным и во многом, очень запоминающимся

Если смотреть на тэги Стима, то игра себя в первую очередь позиционирует, как стрелялка от третьего лица. Что можно сказать о стрельбе, когда у тебя 15-20 ФПС? Ну, ничего хорошего. Разброса у оружия почти нет, автоматы чувствуются одинаково, дробовики убивают врагов с другого конца коридора. Приятно стрелять из снайперской винтовки - тогда в нижнем углу у нас есть небольшая панель, откуда показывают вид из прицела, чтобы было удобнее ставить хедшоты. НО, вспоминаем, что игра так-то - консольная, а значит у нас есть наполовину работающий авто-аим. Не нашёл способа его отключить. В чём проблема? Ну, если врагов в комнате всего 2 или 3, то "переключаться" между ними довольно просто. Однако, стоит в помещении появится ещё каким-то бочкам, ящикам и прочей 3алупe, то автонаведение начинает брать в рассчёт и их, значительно усложняя весь процесс.

Вторым тэгом в Стиме является скрытность ака стелс. Хорошо ли он здесь реализован? Ну, очень спорный вопрос. Это не стелс уровня Бэтмена или Сплинтер Селл - игра нам довольно ясно говорит, что вступать в открытые конфронтации невыгодно и лучше либо решать вопрос по-тихому, либо вообще не показываться врагам на глаза. Second Sight (PS2)
Second Sight, entwickelt von Free Radical Design und veröffentlicht im Jahr 2004 für die PlayStation 2, ist ein ambitioniertes Stealth-Action-Spiel mit einer faszinierenden, erzählerischen Tiefe. Es kombiniert klassische Third-Person-Action mit übernatürlichen Elementen und einer spannenden Story voller Wendungen.
Handlung & Atmosphäre
Die Geschichte folgt John Vattic, einem Mann, der nach einem Experiment mit Telekinese und anderen Psi-Kräften in einer mysteriösen Forschungseinrichtung erwacht. Ohne Erinnerung an seine Vergangenheit versucht er herauszufinden, was geschehen ist. Die narrative Struktur setzt dabei auf Rückblenden, die nach und nach die Wahrheit hinter seiner Mission und seinen Fähigkeiten offenbaren. Die düstere Atmosphäre und die psychologische Spannung geben dem Spiel eine einzigartige Note.
Gameplay & Mechaniken
Second Sight verbindet traditionelle Schleichmechaniken mit übernatürlichen Kräften. Neben Waffen und Nahkampfangriffen kann John seine telekinetischen Kräfte nutzen, Gegner manipulieren oder Objekte bewegen. Das Gameplay erfordert strategisches Vorgehen, da das direkte Kämpfen oft nicht die beste Lösung ist. Einige Abschnitte bieten ein intensives Stealth-Feeling, während andere auf actionreiche Auseinandersetzungen setzen.
Grafik & Sound
Für ein PS2-Spiel hatte Second Sight eine solide technische Umsetzung. Die Animationen und Charaktermodelle waren gut gestaltet, auch wenn sie nicht ganz die Spitzenklasse der damaligen Zeit erreichten. Die Soundkulisse und Synchronisation tragen jedoch hervorragend zur dichten Atmosphäre bei – insbesondere die düsteren, oft mysteriösen Musikstücke.
Fazit
Second Sight ist ein unterschätztes Spiel, das eine spannende Mischung aus Action, Stealth und Rätseln bietet. Die Geschichte bleibt bis zum Schluss fesselnd und die einzigartigen Psi-Kräfte sorgen für eine erfrischende Spielmechanik. Wer auf narrative Tiefe und innovative Gameplay-Ideen steht, sollte sich diesen Klassiker nicht entgehen lassen!

While it is an interesting concept and idea, it's execution is flawed.
It's a more or less forgotten 6th gen third person action-stealth game.

Gameplay wise, you're given an array of psychic abilities, these range from being usefull in most cases, to some that are almost never used, except in areas where an obstacle needs to be dealt with to proceed furter.
Granted 90% of the game, you can ignore the psychic abilities and just use your guns, so they don't feel too impactful, despite the story revolving itself around them. 

The controls are wonky, it's a choice between a third person camera that will glitch out in enclosed areas or a "cinematic camera" that will rather film you in the wrong direction, so you can't see the enemies.
But of the 2, the third person camera is actually usefull.
Shooting is autolock on to enemies and you then have to move the cursor to decide where to hit, however the autolock is terrible, as at times it will lock to the wrong enemies, or explosive barrels in the vicinity.
Making it extremely frustrating, if you're trying to hit something specifc.

You can't save during the missions, so you have to complete the levels in order to progress. 
Granted if you die during the missions,  you do have checkpoints to jumpt to.
There's no mission number either in the main menu, so you just have to sorta guess which mission is the next.
  
The game jumps from being stealth focused in 1 mission, to a combat oriented one in another. 
This is most likely done to make the gameplay more varied. 
Argueably the worst missions are the stealth missions, as the stealth is poorly implemented and the game will just spews out more and more enemies if you get spotted.

Visually it looks dated, but does it's job, the characters however, does look a bit weird, especially in the cutscenes.
It's nothing negative, but it's just an observation. 

Muisc is excellent and helps set the tone for the different levels, however, you're gonna be sick and tired of listening to the singular "combat" track.
the rest of the sound effects falls the line of being okay and neutral, there wasn't really anything that stood out. 

The story is honestly the biggest reason to keep going, because the premise is quite interesting and it is setup nicely and leaves you wondering where it goes next.
And then it just ends on a whiff.

I couldn't really recommend this game, unless you're nostalgic about the game or looking to play 6th gen games for some reason.

Debo admitir que los puntos positivos del juego son únicamente su historia y su variedad de "estrategias" que puedes hacer con los poderes y armas que te otorga el juego. Dragon Nest remains one of my all-time favorite RPGs, and even after all these years, it still stands out as one of the best action RPGs ever made. Few games manage to combine fast-paced combat, memorable dungeons, and a charming fantasy world as well as Dragon Nest does.

The combat is what truly sets it apart. Every class feels unique, and the action is fluid, responsive, and skill-based. Instead of simply clicking through enemies, you have to dodge, chain combos, and master your abilities, making every battle exciting and rewarding.

The world is colorful and full of personality, with memorable characters, engaging storylines, and beautifully designed environments. Whether you're exploring dungeons, taking on challenging nests, or teaming up with friends for raids, there's always something fun to do.

What makes Dragon Nest one of the top RPGs is how satisfying its progression feels. Unlocking new skills, upgrading gear, and perfecting your build gives you a real sense of accomplishment. The cooperative gameplay also creates unforgettable moments, especially when tackling difficult bosses with friends.

Even today, Dragon Nest holds a special place in my heart. It's a game that defined the action RPG genre for many players and proved that great gameplay never goes out of style. If you're looking for an RPG with fantastic combat, engaging content, and countless memorable adventures, Dragon Nest is a classic that's absolutely worth experiencing.

Manhunt es un juego increíble. Para pasar el rato está muy bien y sigue siendo divertido incluso después de más de 20 años. Agradezco que Rockstar haya dejado el juego disponible en Steam, pero lamentablemente no todo son cosas buenas, de hecho, la mayoría son malas.
Le doy una reseña positiva porque me da pena que un juego así siga acumulando críticas negativas, aunque, siendo sinceros, es totalmente comprensible y merecido. El port de PC es horrible, probablemente uno de los peores que he visto en mucho tiempo. No se trata solo de pequeños bugs o fallos menores: el juego es injugable. Y cuando digo injugable, me refiero a que ni siquiera se puede abrir sin que crashee. Rockstar simplemente dejó el juego en Steam y se desentendió por completo. No puedes iniciarlo ni jugarlo sin instalar un parche hecho por terceros. Hay errores de todo tipo: de sonido, de texturas, de diálogos… pero el peor es el crasheo constante como ya he mencionado. Es una pena que el juego vaya a quedarse así para siempre, por lo que agradezco de corazón a los modders y fans que dedican su tiempo a arreglar este tipo de cosas. Me costó muchísimo hacer que funcionara correctamente. 84/100.

🔫 Max Payne – A Timeless Classic That Still Deserves Some Love!

🎮 A Classic Worth Revisiting

Max Payne is an absolute classic, and despite its age, it's still an enjoyable experience today.

There's something special about going back to games like this. The atmosphere, the gameplay and that unmistakable old-school feel remind you why Max Payne became such a memorable game in the first place.

I still had a great time playing through it, and it's fantastic to see that the core experience has aged as well as it has.

🖥️ Modern PC Compatibility – Needs Some Love!

Unfortunately, getting the game running correctly on modern hardware isn't quite as straightforward as it should be.

You'll need a few workarounds, community fixes and mods to get everything behaving properly. The game is also missing some modern features, particularly achievements, and its compatibility with today's hardware and operating systems needs attention.

It's disappointing that a classic like Max Payne still relies on community-made solutions just to bring the experience up to modern standards.

👏 Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive – This Classic Needs Attention!

While Max Payne was originally developed by Remedy Entertainment, the franchise is now owned by Rockstar Games and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive.

I'd really like to see them give the original game some proper attention.

Achievements need to be added, modern PC compatibility needs to be addressed, and the game deserves a little more care to ensure it works correctly on today's systems.

It's not asking for a complete remake or some massive overhaul. Just some basic support and quality-of-life improvements to make this classic more accessible for modern PC gamers.

It's a shame that players still have to rely on community fixes and workarounds when these are things that should have been properly addressed.

🤔 Final Thoughts

Despite the technical hurdles, I still thoroughly enjoyed revisiting Max Payne.

It's a classic that deserves to be preserved and made accessible for modern PC gamers. The gameplay and atmosphere still hold up, but the technical side desperately needs some attention.

Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive, please give this classic some love. Add achievements, improve modern compatibility and make sure Max Payne gets the support it deserves.

This was a good time, and I highly respect it as one of Remedy's first games that laid the foundation for Remedy as we know it. However, this is a game that clearly shows its age, with rough spots in some areas that keep it from being a masterpiece, in my opinion, and it could seriously benefit from a remake.

The main story follows the titular Max Payne, an NYPD detective turned DEA agent, as he attempts to solve his family's murder and, while doing so, finds himself entangled in a conspiracy involving several crime families, a secret society, and the US military.

The combat here is very reminiscent of the older John Woo action movies and features a bullet-time dodging mechanic, and it's simply a good old-fashioned fun time. I found myself jumping into battles and clearing out rooms before the enemies could react in time, which is always satisfying.

The story here was a fun time mainly due to the comic book-style cutscenes presented with a hard-boiled neo-noir style and campy performances from the characters who are clearly just members of the development team, which oozes charm.

The writing was very good, and Max Payne himself was an interesting character with some banger dialogue thanks to the excellent performance from the late James McCaffrey, who is almost always the best part of anything he's in.

With that said, though, not all is perfect, and I do have some criticisms.

Enemy AI is pretty rough at times, and most of their behavior boils down to charging at you mindlessly or camping around nearly impossible-to-spot corners, waiting to one-tap you and end your no-hit streak.

Almost all of the guns in the game suck ass. There's way too much spread, they don't do much damage, and bullet travel is egregiously slow. The only somewhat decent gun for me was the Colt Commando.

Whenever you dive from shoot-dodging, there's a small animation of Max getting up from the floor. This was always annoying because you cannot shoot or do anything during this animation, and there's also no I-Frames either, so you're left completely vulnerable, as the enemies can just one-tap you by the time you get back up.

Because of the silly nature of the performances in the cutscenes, it's hard to really care or take anything seriously, so I ended up not being that invested in the main story even though the writing was great.

Outside of Max Payne himself, none of the characters were all that memorable to me. I know Mona Sax is a major character in the 2nd game, so I'll hold my full thoughts on her for now, but in this game, she did not leave much of an impression on me.

Overall, this is a good game that I can comfortably recommend despite its shortcomings, and it's an interesting look at Remedy in its early days before it became what it is today.

I wasn't sure whether to recommend this or not. I like it, so I will, but you should be aware that it's one of those ancient games that requires a year-long expedition to the far corners of the internet to get running properly on modern systems and fix critical bugs.

If you're willing to go to all that trouble to make it work, you may decide it's really fun. But that will also depend on having incredible patience, because it is brutally, sadistically hard. I simply had to cheat for the last quarter of the game.

Overall, I'd say it's worth it for the presentation and the bullet-time feature, which was novel and well implemented. And I love the film noire story and the way it pokes fun at itself. But it's going to be a major headache to get running if you've never had to deal with this problem that plagues many old-butt games.

This game has no issues on Windows 11 at all! You only need one thing: Max Payne Widescreen Fix. You can easily find it, just ask an AI where to get it and how to install it. It’s pretty easy.

As for the game itself: it’s amazing. First of all, the atmosphere and writing are top-notch. These old games really remind me how developers had to work cleverly with less, as they had fewer models and assets to represent everything they wanted to create in the world. That kind of creativity is part of what makes games an art form.

Of course, beyond that, it’s a “simple” third-person shooter that can feel very hard and punishing. But the good news is that you can save at any point, which makes the challenging parts less frustrating.

One useful combat tip: keep moving! I usually found it much more effective to move left and right while shooting at enemies, because they can miss, too. In many cases, I found constant movement much more useful than the ability to slow down time.

I’m glad I finally tried this legendary, old game. I didn’t have the opportunity to play it when it came out, but I’d heard about it many times. Even though it’s an old game, I fortunately don’t know the story, so I can enjoy it without any spoilers.

[h1]Max Payne[/h1] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3818897770 Pětadvacet let je v herním průmyslu celá věčnost a Max Payne už svůj věk po technické stránce zkrátka neschová. Stal se z něj fascinující, ale nesmírně křehký artefakt minulosti. Zapomeňte na chvíli na to, že je to nekompromisní hard-boiled noir detektiv. Na moderních počítačích je to spíše zmatený „lumík“ na útěku. Abyste ho udrželi při životě, musíte bedlivě hlídat každý jeho krok a prošlapat mu cestu skrze džungli pro něho naprosto neznámého a cizího hardwaru. Ale k věci. Hra má tři hlavní akty, které jsou dohromady rozdělené do více než dvaceti kapitol. A i když tempo v těchto kapitolách ani na vteřinu nepovolí, to, co vás u obrazovky udrží nejvíc, není samotný počet nepřátel ale styl, jakým je celý tenhle sešup do pekel vyprávěn... Scénář hry napsal finský vývojář Sam Lake, vlastním jménem Sami Antero Järvi, ze studia Remedy Entertainment. Právě on vtiskl titulu nezaměnitelný noir styl a stvořil ikonické vnitřní monology plné temných metafor. Kvůli tehdejšímu extrémně nízkému rozpočtu navíc musel hlavnímu hrdinovi propůjčit svůj vlastní obličej, čímž vznikly legendární škleby v komiksových cutscénách.

[b]Max Payne[/b] – po tolika letech už spíše „rozvařený“ než „hard-boiled“... Jako hra si i po pětadvaceti letech zaslouží absolutní uznání za to, jak definovala žánr. Samotné jádro hry sice neztratilo nic ze své geniální noir atmosféry, skvělého bullet-timu a mrazivého příběhu, ale... Jako produkt na současných digitálních obchodech je to polomrtvý pacient, kterého musíte k životu probrat šokem v podobě komunitních fixů. Stojí to za tu námahu? Pro fanoušky noiru bezpochyby ano. Pro všechny ostatní to bude jen frustrující exkurze do herní historie. Když ale konečně ošéfujete padání hry, přinutíte launcher spolupracovat a hlavně - když se z komiksů ozve ten ikonický hlas Jamese McCaffreyho, okamžitě hře všechny ty technické naschvály odpustíte. Remedy tehdy stvořilo nesmrtelnou legendu. Jen škoda, že se o její odkaz dnes musí starat komunita namísto distributorů. 

[h3]Max Payne vs. Win11[/h3]
[b]Noir, který moderní PC nerozdýchá[/b] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3818943704 Koupit si dnes Max Payna na Steamu s pocitem, že kliknete na 'Hrát' a ponoříte se do nostalgie, je čiré bláznovství. Oficiální digitální distribuce vám totiž doručí v podstatě systémově nekompatibilní artefakt...

Problém není ve vašem hardwaru, ale v samotném jádru hry z roku 2001. Původní engine Max-FX totiž spoléhá na technologie, které moderní Windows 11 už dávno pohřbily. Pokud máte (jako já) moderní herní notebook se systémem MUX a dedikovanou grafickou kartou (např. řady RTX) a procesorem AMD s integrovaným Radeonem, launcher hry herní grafiku vůbec neuvidí. S touhle situací moc nepomáhá ani legenda jménem dgVoodoo2, která herní GPU sice umí zpřístupnit, ale samotné nastavení vyžaduje hlubší HW znalosti a je skoro jisté, že hra spadne s hláškou, že nemáte grafickou kartu s podporou DX8. Engine hry je vůči moderním sestavám jednoznačně extrémně náladový. Na některých sestavách může hra kvůli frekvencím obrazovky nad 60Hz rovnou odmítnout i nastartovat. Kupříkladu s moderním wrapperem d3d8to9 se vám může s trochou štěstí podařit hru stabilně rozjet i na 144Hz+ panelu, aniž by obraz protestoval, ale hlavní boj se i tak nakonec přesouvá čistě na audio frontu.

Hra totiž hledá rozhraní DirectSound3D, které v dnešních systémech neexistuje a proto audio stopy v proprietárních .ras archivech zůstanou pro Windows neviditelné. Bez komunitního zásahu – buď stažením předem opravených masivních balíků dat, nebo ručním překódováním souborů skriptem MaxBatch – přijdete o to nejcennější: ikonický noir dabing. Má to však obrovský háček – samotné upravené zvukové soubory bez grafického wrapperu mohou hru brutálně zalagovat a způsobovat různá zacyklení zvuků, protože engine nedokáže bez moderního překladače audio s obrazem synchronizovat. Max Payne na moderním PC zkrátka nevyžaduje jen hráčské dovednosti, ale spíše trpělivost IT specialisty.

Pro mě osobně se jako funkční záchrana ukázala právě kombinace grafického wrapperu [url= https://github.com/crosire/d3d8to9/releases]d3d8to9[/url] a následné stažení již hotových, předem opravených .ras souborů podle přímočarého návodu na webu [url=https://www.specialagentsqueaky.com/blog/how-to-fix-broken-max-payne-sounds-on-windows-10-steam]Special Agent Squeaky[/url]. S tímto kombem hra na W-11 sice v launcheru tvrdošíjně ukazuje pouze integrovanou grafiku AMD Radeon a akceleraci musím mít přepnutou na D3D Software T&L, ale ve výsledku vše konečně běží plynule a mluví přesně tak, jak si pamatuji z roku 2001.[hr][/hr] Max Payne - když musíte, tak musíte. [h1]Max Payne: The shooter that influenced a generation[h1]

Picture this, a man in 2024 got a free integrated graphics PC and wanted to game on it, that man’s close friend wanted to get him a game that could run on it but he wasn’t sure what. So he went with a game he loved, Max Payne. Little did he know he was gonna gift that friend a game he would cherish. I was that man who received max payne. 

The story, while simple is really good. The story is about Max Payne, a cop who lost his family because of the drug V. While investigating the situation Max gets framed for the murder of someone close to him. The story explores the concepts of loss, depression, and how long term grief can ruin someone’s life.

The late James McCaffrey nails his role as Max Payne, making the one liners, and the monologues work. There’s no one else who could’ve played this character as well as he could. If this was played by any other actor this dialouge would’ve came off as cheesy Marvel dialogue.

The gameplay aged really well, The levels are really fun to traverse, every building plays differently from the other, but it could be confusing to figure out where to go in some levels. The only levels I didn’t enjoy were the dream levels, there’s three of them in the game. And they slow down the pace of the game, feeling like they were supposed to be for a completely different game, they’re slow and often involve platforming segments that feel like walking on a tightrope. 

Gunplay is really fun as well, having bullet time, where you can slow down time to have more time to shoot your opponents. This mechanic was fun to mess around with, making gun fights feel exciting watching you shoot them in slow motion. Max’s arsenal of weapons helps the gunplay stand out as well, accommodating many, with a shot gun if you wanna just blast through the room, pistols if you wanna play more careful, and SMGs if you want to just spread bullets all across the room. I like how many approaches to combat there are
The artstyle is great as well, Remedy was about to go bankrupt so this game had to preform so they could stay afloat, so they cheaped out, instead of having mostly cutscenes they took photos and used them to make the game into effectively a comic book, their cheapness somehow paid off and these cutscenes add to the games artstyle, they’re so iconic that people disliked the fact that Max Payne 3 had more traditional cutscene than comic panels

Unfortunately, I’m not sure what side to blame for this. Rockstar or Remedy, but this series has been not well maintained on modern platforms. Max Payne 1, 2, and 3 all have weird issues. Max Payne 1 requires a patch in order to work correctly now. The average person might pick up this game and not even know that a patch is needed and is gonna be confused about this. For an iconic game they sure don’t care about making sure it works out of the box in 2026. Without the patch I wasn’t able to hear any of the cutscene audio. 


Overall though, Max Payne is a fantastic game, you can tell how it revolutionized the shooters of today with its movement like bullet time. It’s a shooter that has and always will be amazing.

[h1] A fun and engaging crime drama with a love-noir twist [/h1]

When asked what my favorite games are, Max Payne 2 is always at the top of my list. I will be as objective as possible and avoid introducing my personal bias when describing the game's objective strengths and weaknesses, though.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] Story [/h2]

This is the game's main selling point. The story in Max Payne 2 is not exactly unique, but it is multidimensional, with the characters in it being mysterious and duplicitous. This is a departure from the first game, where characters were very transparent in their goals and ambitions. And with most of the characters here being returning characters from Max Payne 1, you'll be seeing a lot of familiar faces if you've played the first game.

The game features a detective story with a love story twist. Without getting into spoilers, the game starts as a cop crime story, with Max investigating a series of murders that have been taking place in the city. This quickly spirals out of his control when Mona Sax, who Max met in the first game and is emotionally attached to, appears to be involved. The story turns into a story of duty vs passion when Max starts to get increasingly involved in the case for all the wrong reasons.

The story is the best attribute of the game, but it can also be confusing. Remember when I said that in the first game the characters are very transparent and that in Max Payne 2 they are mysterious and duplicitous? Yeah.... in this game it is safe to say that they over-corrected when trying to make everyone's intentions more two-faced. It is not so much that you cannot know who you should side with and be up against, and more that the specific details of who works for whom on behalf of whom aren't very clear. It is easy to get lost in the narrative noise and in Max's monologues, and even as a fan and as someone who already knows the story inside out, the web of relationships between characters and events can get hazy.

Don't get me wrong, the broad strokes of the story are often very clear - what might happen instead is that you may often find yourself asking things like 'how does doing X help us in what we are trying to do?', while the answers and crucial clues lie in a dialogue line that appears once in the middle of the previous level.

This is definitely a shortcoming, and it is something the game tends to do quite often - it is not hiding things from the player, but it often decides to reveal key details in inopportune moments where the player is more concerned with combat or decompressing from a hard level; And these key details are often only mentioned once as Max making a mental note in the middle of the level.

If you are playing it for the first time, my advice is to pay close attention to the secondary dialogue and especially to Max's monologues in the middle of levels.

Despite this narrative pacing flaw, I think the story works well. It delivers on its promise of a love-noir crime drama, and I think players that empathize with Max will enjoy it. This is definitely not hard to do, because while Max can be hard to identify with, he is a character that is very easy to empathize with.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] Combat [/h2]

The combat feels satisfying - there is enough weapon variety in the game to last the playthrough, and the revamped bullet time gives the player more ways to express themselves. Now Max does not automatically get up after finishing the shootdodge move and keeps shooting while lying down, which is appreciated. Some guns do feel more punchy than the others, though - with the shotguns feeling very weak compared to the rifles. Pistols also don't feel very strong. The rifles on the other hand feel perfect - they hit hard and you can feel the weight of the bullets.

I also appreciate how enemies with kevlar vests don't bleed and can be pretty tanky if you shoot them in the chest where the vest is, but shooting them in the legs makes them bleed and headhots are insta-kills. That's a neat detail.

Physics is the aspect of combat that the game really wants the player to notice, and it will constantly remind you of that by placing enemies on the edge of buildings and in front of cardboard boxes and cans of paint, so that when you kill them you can see their bodies interacting with the environment. It's pretty nice, and while the physics can get wonky sometimes when it interacts with bullet time, for the most part they work pretty well. I also think it may be intentional since part of the game's charm is being funny and not taking itself too seriously during gameplay - this is reflected in the in-game TV shows and funny conversations with side characters like the police officers in the precinct.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] Atmosphere [/h2]

The atmosphere in Max Payne 2 is amazing, though I still think the first game's atmosphere was more palpable. I think the first game's lighting made it so the levels felt darker. In this game the lighting system makes things brighter than before, which I think takes away from the atmosphere that is supposed to be darker.

The first game also had a lot of different levels, while in Max Payne 2 there's not even a single city level. You spend most of your time inside buildings, construction lots and enclosures where the city is still visible, but out of reach - I think that is part of the reason why Max Payne 1 had a better atmosphere, since you could roam the streets in a few levels to take in the atmosphere a bit better.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] Soundtrack [/h2]

The soundtrack is 10/10, just like in the first game. I actually like this game's version of Max's theme more, with the added depth of the cello. The modified main theme is the only song that is repeated from the first game's OST, with all other songs being original creations for this game. The audio quality is also noticeably increased from the first game, which is expected given Max Payne 2 had a much larger budget. The OST is very orchestral, with cellos, pianos and violins being heavily emphasized and giving the game the 'noir love story' theme it is going for.

This is also the game where Poets of the Fall debuted in the Remedy games, with the lyrics to the song 'Late Goodbye' actually being inspired by a poem written by Sam Lake (the game's writer). Since then, Poets of the Fall have repeatedly been featured in Remedy games.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] Overall [/h2]

Max Payne 2 provides a fun experience with an engaging combat system, an amazing soundtrack and a great story that can seem a bit more confusing than it actually is, because of how it is told.

The game is around 6 to 7 hours long, but those hours are packed with emotional beats, twists and turns. It definitely does ask the player to be more attentive, especially when compared to the first game, but it does deliver on its promise of being a love-noir drama and the emotional moments hit hard for players that empathize with Max's struggles. It is absolutely worth getting into.

Essa é uma review meio difícil de fazer pelo simples fato desse jogo me deixar muito confusa. Eu gosto muito dele, e, pra mim, num geral é o melhor Max Payne. Mas, ao mesmo tempo, ele não é ele o que eu tenho apego emocional... 
Mais um exemplo de como a nostalgia pode cegar a gente, eu acho. O 1 foi o primeiro que joguei, quando ganhei um PS2 do meu pai na adolescência. Não joguei tanto, mas a dublagem brasileira e (o rostinho do Sam Lake) me marcaram muito na época. Depois veio o 3, que joguei com o meu irmão. Ambos me deram ótimas memórias, e elas meio que se misturaram com as minhas opiniões e o gosto num geral. O 2 nunca foi tão presente assim na minha cabeça, então apesar de gostar dele, a competição no meu coração é meio difícil. Ainda assim, ele merece uma das minhas reviews idiotas, então vou fazer uma!!

Max Payne 2 melhora praticamente tudo do primeiro; A história é melhor, ainda sendo um noirzinho bem anos 2000 e melodramático pra caramba, mas esse sempre foi o conceito e não seria Max Payne se fosse diferente. Shakespeare segue tirando todas as suas ideias do Max, se fosse eu processaria! Gráficos lindíssimos, jogabilidade legal, trilha sonora maravilhosa, diálogos bons e engraçados e cutscenes melhores que as anteriores (agora eles têm verba!!). Tudo bem mais caprichadinho... Só que tão diferente!
E isso não é exatamente uma reclamação, eu gostei das mudanças, mas na minha percepção eu quase senti como se fosse um jogo totalmente diferente, só que ainda a mesma coisa. Tipo um navio de Teseu. Tanto que eu ainda tenho dificuldade de ver ele como uma sequência direta. Problema cognitivo meu, mas paciência.
A maioria dos personagens que voltaram têm mais profundidade e tempo de tela, especialmente a diva Mona Sax, que virou praticamente coprotagonista, tendo suas próprias fases (que deveriam ser maiores inclusive, amei jogar com ela!!). A história em si eu não sei dizer se gostei muito ou não, ela é um pouco menos mirabolante que a anterior, mas curta e confusa em algumas partes (ou talvez eu não tenha prestado muita atenção, acontece), e as vezes parece ‘reescrever’ o que acontece no primeiro jogo, como por exemplo o relacionamento entre o Max e a Mona. Mas foi por um bem maior porque eles têm uma química incrível, então, dito isso: ainda é uma história boa.

Meus dois centavos sobre a jogabilidade: Aqui ela tá entre o leve e pesado do 1 e 3, então tá no ponto perfeito pra mim. A IA dos inimigos é melhor também. Bullet time segue sendo a coisa mais divertida do mundo. Também achei mais gostoso de atirar nele, mas não me pergunte o porquê pois não sei responder coisas técnicas!!

Agora, momento cachorro boboca: Amo que dá pra interagir com ainda mais coisas também, mesmo que não sirva pra porcaria nenhuma. Tirar refrigerante da máquina, dar descarga em privada, ligar o aquecedor que tem uma placa de “não ligue” e quebrar ele pra ser xingada logo depois... Também é muito divertido ficar na frente das pessoas vendo tv, recomendo! Os canais de tv também são completinhos agora. Finalmente pude ver todos os capítulos de Senhor e Senhora, era meu sonho. Inclusive, o Sam Lake faz vários personagens nos programas que tem lá!

Meu top 1 em quesito jogos do Max Payne, praticamente o bebê urso da Cachinhos Dourados, tendo quase todas as melhores coisas dos outros 2 jogos e formando um equilíbrio perfeito.

"A brilliant, cinematic noir thriller that cleans up the edges of the original, even if it loses a bit of the grit."

Rating: 8/10

Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne is an absolute classic third-person shooter that stands the test of time. If the first game felt like a raw, unforgiving grindhouse film, this sequel elevates the presentation to a slick, high-budget Hollywood neo-noir blockbuster.

The Good:

• Refined Bullet Time: The signature slow-motion gunplay returns and feels much tighter. You no longer need to stand perfectly still to activate it, and getting kills actually extends your meter, keeping the adrenaline flowing continuously.
• Quality of Life Upgrades: Grenades and Molotovs now have their own dedicated hotkey, meaning you no longer have to awkwardly switch away from your dual pistols just to throw projectiles.
• Pacing & Balance: Max is noticeably sturdier here compared to the first game. The difficulty curve is smoother, removing those frustrating moments from the original where you'd step through a door and instantly get one-shotted by a shotgun, forcing you to reload the same room ten times.
• Havok Physics Engine: For a game from this era, the implementation of physics is incredibly satisfying. Blasting enemies into piles of boxes or watching dynamic ragdolls fly across the room gives the combat an amazing sense of weight.
• The Narrative: The shift from a pure revenge plot to a tragic, film-noir love story involving Mona Sax is brilliantly executed through fully voiced graphic novel panels and Max’s iconic, poetic monologues.

The Bad:

• Escort Missions: The game introduces a few segments where you have to protect NPCs, and the enemy AI tends to aggressively rush them down, leading to some needless spike difficulties.
• Slight Loss of Atmosphere: While the graphics, lighting, and models are a massive upgrade from the original, the environments sometimes lose that bleak, apocalyptic, snow-covered dread that made the first game’s setting so haunting.
• Short Campaign: You can easily blast through the main story over a single weekend.

Verdict:

Max Payne 2 fixes almost every mechanical flaw of its predecessor, delivering an incredibly tight, responsive, and cinematic shooter. It is an essential play for any action fan, especially when caught on a Steam Sale.

Rockstar's redheaded stepchild, but my personal favorite game that they have ever made. A childhood staple, it's a story about a kid who takes over a corrupt school not because he wants to own the school, but to stop others from making Bullworth Academy even worse. 

Bully has a world that feels so cohesive with great aesthetics and every NPC being named and having their own personalities is something way more games should be doing. Jimmy Hopkins influenced little squirt angle a ton. "There are a bunch of kids around this place who need a beating, and you're picking on the few who don't" is a quote that really stuck with me all these years. He's like a paladin of vengeance, using his strength to defend those weaker than him, even if he sometimes does some evil himself. (but that might be my Baldurs Gate 3 talking)

Is it perfect? Hell no. Without at least SilentPatch the game runs like garbage, but that's an easy install/find on your favorite search engine. There are certain missions that have aged like milk, story-wise. A primeira vez que joguei Bully deve ter sido com uns 6 anos, com meu irmão mais velho.

O jogo já me ganhou de primeira. Me divertia muito fazendo qualquer coisa dentro do jogo.

Sempre guardei ele com muito carinho na memória, então, quando ganhei meu próprio console, foi um dos jogos que corri atrás. Apesar de ser um jogo "antigo", comparado com os jogos que eu jogava nessa época, cada detalhe do jogo me fazia sentir como se fosse a primeira vez jogando, mas, dessa vez, pude também entender a história. Zerei o jogo no XBOX 360 e depois acabei vendendo o console. Anos depois, ganhei um PS4. Fiquei muitos anos com ele até ver que Bully estava em promoção e decidir comprar novamente. Já era a minha terceira experiência com o jogo em épocas diferentes da minha vida, e todas as vezes ele conseguiu me fazer sentir o mesmo que a primeira vez. Platinei o jogo no Playstation e, alguns anos depois, comprei ele aqui na Steam.

O jogo acerta em tudo que se propõe a ser. Todos os personagens da história são memoráveis, a jogabilidade é divertida demais e a história tem uma mensagem surpreendentemente bonita e memorável para um jogo que se passa em uma escola. As armas, colecionáveis, aulas e missões secundárias são todas únicas e inesquecíveis. O gráfico é o que se espera da época, talvez um pouco melhor.

Só queria que a Rockstar fizesse um remake desse jogo para poder jogá-lo pela "primeira vez" novamente.

[h1]''BEM-VINDO À BULLWORTH''[/h1]

[b]''AVISO: ESSA ANÁLISE NÃO POSSUI SPOILERS''[/b]

🕵 Depois de mais de 20h jogando esse clássico da Rockstar, decidi trazer uma análise sobre um dos jogos mais diferentes e divertidos já desenvolvidos pela empresa. 🕵

[b]📋 Bully: Scholarship Edition:[/b] É um jogo de ação e mundo aberto desenvolvido pela Rockstar, onde acompanhamos Jimmy Hopkins, um adolescente de 15 anos que é enviado para a Bullworth Academy, um internato conhecido por seus alunos problemáticos e pela enorme rivalidade entre os diferentes grupos da escola. Seu objetivo é sobreviver à rotina escolar, enfrentar valentões, fazer amizades e conquistar seu espaço. 

[h1]Jogabilidade:[/h1]

[b]📋 Como é a Jogabilidade?[/b] Bully apresenta uma jogabilidade bastante divertida, seguindo uma fórmula de mundo aberto semelhante à de outros jogos da Rockstar, mas adaptada para o ambiente escolar. Você pode explorar a cidade, realizar missões, participar de atividades, andar de bicicleta e enfrentar outros alunos utilizando diferentes golpes e objetos. O jogo também conta com um sistema de reputação entre os grupos de estudantes, fazendo com que suas ações influenciem diretamente na maneira como os outros personagens interagem com você.

[h1]Ambientação e Atividades:[/h1]

[b]📋 Como é a Ambientação?[/b] A Bullworth Academy é um dos grandes destaques do jogo, trazendo uma escola cheia de personalidade, com diferentes áreas para explorar, personagens e situações inusitadas. Além das missões principais, temos diversas atividades, como aulas de química, inglês, educação física, música e outras, cada uma com seus próprios minigames e recompensas. 

[h1]Conclusão:[/h1]

[b]📋 Minha opnião:[/b] Bully: Scholarship Edition é um daqueles jogos que possuem uma identidade própria, trazendo uma proposta diferente do que estamos acostumados a ver nos jogos da Rockstar. Sua ambientação, personagens, humor e liberdade de exploração fazem dele uma experiência bastante divertida, principalmente para quem gosta de jogos de mundo aberto. É um clássico que merece ser conhecido e que continua sendo lembrado até hoje.

[b]📋 Prós: 📋[/b]
-Ótima ambientação.
-Personagens carismáticos.
-Jogabilidade divertida.
-Boa variedade de atividades.
-História envolvente.

[b]📋 Contras: 📋[/b]
-O jogo é quebrado no PC, tive que baixar mods para conseguir consertar o FPS travado, gráficos, entre outras situações.

Os contras vão da opinião de cada um, essa foi minha análise sincera. Jogue o jogo e tire suas próprias conclusões.

Honestly? This game has soul. Rockstar nailed the whole greasy boarding-school vibe.

The cliques, the pranks, the run-down hallways, the prefects hunting you down. It just pulls you into that world and keeps you there.

Considering it came out in 2008, the graphics and physics hold up fine and surely cartoony art style ages way better than realistic visuals do, and the animations still have plenty of character.

The story is where it lets me down a bit. It's mid at best, honestly leaning toward meh, and the chapter transitions are straight-up abrupt. One moment you're wrapping something up, next thing you're dumped into a new arc like half the plot got cut. The characters are charming enough to keep you going regardless, but the pacing is rough.

One heads-up if you're on PC: install the SilentPatch to prevent frequent crashes. This worked for me on Windows 10: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?l=german&id=1323609222

All in all — it's a blast you can knock out in about a week, and I'd say give it a go.

review:
[h1]Highly recommended, but...![/h1]

Man, I was so hyped to jump back into Bully, or Canis Canem Edit, as some call it. But the game just kept crashing approximately every five minutes. I know there are fan-made patches out there that might fix the issue, but honestly, why should I go out of my way to make a game playable? Those few bucks aren't going to hurt Rockstar one bit, so it's not like I am losing out there. Other than the chance to experience this game once again.

On another note, this game is genuinely incredible. It's unique and has so much depth. Surprisingly. One of my all-time favorites. What really grinds my gears, though, is that Rockstar has apparently tried to make a sequel multiple times over the years, only to scrap every single attempt. It's such a missed opportunity. This franchise has so much potential, and a new Bully game would be something fans would absolutely go wild for. The concept and world of Bullworth are just too good to leave behind. Perhaps it's a lack of commitment from the developers, as well as doubt in the commercial/financial success, they are holding back such a beloved series. I would happily pay full price for a stable, polished sequel. It's just frustrating to see such a fantastic concept languish like this. The original game, despite its flaws, is a testament to what Rockstar can do when they're not afraid to be a little different. Bully offered a fresh perspective on the open-world genre, focusing on schoolyard politics and social dynamics rather than just crime. In comparison to Rockstar's other IPs, Bully was a breath of fresh air, and that's why it remains so special to so many of us. 

Hopefully, one day, they will reconsider and bring Bully back for good.

[h1]The best story in the entire GTA series[/h1]
I've always felt that GTA IV has one of the best stories in the entire Grand Theft Auto series, if not the best. Niko Bellic is easily one of my favourite protagonists in gaming. His story, his past and his reasons for coming to Liberty City make him such an interesting character. There is something about his journey that makes it feel much more personal and grounded compared to other GTA games.

What I especially like is that the story isn't just about crime, money and power. It deals with themes like friendship, betrayal, revenge and the consequences of your past. Niko feels like an actual person with his own struggles rather than just another GTA protagonist.

[hr][/hr]
[b]The other stories[/b]
The two expansions, The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony, deserve just as much appreciation. Both introduce completely different perspectives on Liberty City, with their own characters, atmosphere and storylines.

Johnny Klebitz and Luis Lopez are both great protagonists in their own right. I really enjoyed how their stories connect with Niko's and show different sides of the same city. It makes Liberty City feel like a much bigger and more interconnected world.

[hr][/hr]
[b]Final thoughts[/b]
GTA IV might not have the biggest map or the most content compared to some of the newer entries, but its storytelling, characters and atmosphere are something special.

For me, the entire GTA IV experience, including both expansions, has some of the best storytelling Rockstar has ever delivered.

I really hope Rockstar brings back this level of storytelling in future GTA games.

review:
Llevo bastante tiempo jugando a títulos de mundo abierto y Grand Theft Auto IV: The Complete Edition sigue siendo una de las propuestas más sólidas y recomendables que puedes encontrar en Steam.

Lo que hace que este paquete valga totalmente la pena es la profundidad de su propuesta. La historia principal de Niko Bellic ofrece un tono sensiblemente más maduro y oscuro que el de otros entregas de la saga, con un guion muy bien construido sobre el choque cultural y las contradicciones del sueño americano. Además, el motor de físicas (Euphoria) le da un peso al movimiento, los tiroteos y la conducción que hace que cada enfrentamiento se sienta muy realista e impredecible.

Esta edición brilla especialmente por incluir las dos expansiones, que complementan la experiencia de forma impecable:

The Lost and Damned: Aporta una perspectiva motera muy bien lograda con Johnny Klebitz, centrada en la camaradería, la lealtad y una atmósfera genial de rock y ambiente callejero.

The Ballad of Gay Tony: Le da un contrapunto más ágil y brillante a la ciudad a través de Luis López, enfocándose en la vida nocturna, los clubes y misiones con más acción y variedad de artefactos como el paracaídas.

El cruce entre las tres historias dentro de la misma Liberty City está ejecutado con un cuidado impresionante. Si buscas una experiencia completa, con un gran nivel de detalle y docenas de horas de contenido de calidad, es un juego que cumple de sobra y que da gusto tener en la biblioteca. Totalmente recomendado.

[h1]GTA: Episodes from Liberty City - две истории, один город[/h1]
[h2]О чём игра[/h2]
Episodes from Liberty City - это два отдельных эпизода, каждый со своим героем, стилем и атмосферой.
The Lost and Damned рассказывает о Джонни Клебитце, байкере из клуба «Пропащие», который пытается удержать братство от распада на фоне предательства, наркотиков и войны с другими бандами.
The Ballad of Gay Tony переносит нас в гламурный мир ночной жизни, где Луис Лопес, телохранитель и правая рука клубного магната Тони Принса, балансирует между лояльностью, семьёй и криминалом.
[h2]Чем выделяется[/h2]
Два уникальных стиля: мрачный байкерский боевик и яркий клубный экшен.
Новые виды оружия, транспорт и миссии.
Сюжеты пересекаются с событиями GTA IV, создавая общую картину.
Новые радиостанции и саундтреки, отражающие атмосферу каждого эпизода.
Полноценные кампании, каждая на 8–12 часов.
[h2]Недочёты[/h2]
Некоторые миссии могут показаться устаревшими по механике.
Графика осталась на уровне GTA IV.
Без знания оригинала некоторые сюжетные моменты теряют вес.
[h2]Кому понравится[/h2]
Фанатам GTA IV, желающим увидеть Либерти-Сити с новых ракурсов.
Тем, кто любит байкерскую тематику или клубную атмосферу.
Игрокам, которым интересны мрачные и зрелые криминальные истории.
[h2]Интересные факты[/h2]
- В одной из миссий Луис Лопес участвует в ограблении банка — это та же сцена, что и в миссии Нико из GTA IV, только с другой стороны.
- The Ballad of Gay Tony добавил в серию парашюты, которые позже вернулись в GTA V.
- В The Lost and Damned можно участвовать в байкерских гонках с бейсбольными битами — отсылка к фильму «Дикие ангелы».
- Rockstar изначально планировала выпустить третий эпизод, но позже отказалась от идеи в пользу разработки GTA V.
[h2]Заключение[/h2]
GTA: Episodes from Liberty City - это не просто дополнения, а полноценные истории, расширяющие вселенную GTA IV. Они предлагают два разных взгляда на один и тот же город, наполненный насилием, предательством и гламуром. Если ты хочешь вернуться в Либерти-Сити и увидеть, как пересекаются судьбы героев, это идеальный повод.

Is it fun? No. Does it tell a complete story? Also no. Are the puzzles intuitive and rewarding? No again! But I did play it all the way through and have a great time despite there being almost no redeeming qualities to it. I've owned the physical box of this game for years and only just now played it, so I admit there is some nostalgia to take into account. But even so, the worldbuilding is intriguing! I don't always leave a game feeling like I just explored a world and this one did it for me.

Developed by Momentum Digital Media Technologies and published by Strategy First, Culpa Innata is an ambitious point-and-click adventure that combines science fiction with detective storytelling to create a mystery driven by political intrigue and philosophical themes. Set in a future where the powerful World Union claims to have eliminated crime, poverty, and conflict, the game immediately challenges the illusion of perfection through the shocking murder of one of its citizens in the neighboring Rogue States. Players take on the role of Senior Peace and Security officer Phoenix Wallis, whose assignment begins as a routine investigation but gradually uncovers a web of corruption, hidden agendas, and ideological conflict. Rather than relying on explosive action, the experience emphasizes careful observation, thoughtful dialogue, and piecing together clues that reveal the darker side of a supposedly flawless civilization.

The game's strongest feature is its richly imagined setting. Every location, organization, and conversation contributes to the sense that this futuristic society has been meticulously designed. The contrast between the technologically advanced World Union and the politically unstable Rogue States provides a compelling backdrop for the investigation while encouraging players to question whether absolute order truly leads to a better world. Phoenix is an engaging protagonist because her journey is not limited to solving murders; it also becomes a personal examination of loyalty, justice, and morality. As the story progresses, the narrative constantly challenges preconceived notions about authority, freedom, and truth, rewarding players who pay close attention to the details hidden within dialogue and environmental storytelling.

Gameplay follows the classic point-and-click formula while introducing enough variety to keep investigations engaging. Players travel between numerous locations, inspect crime scenes, gather evidence, question witnesses, solve inventory-based puzzles, and make dialogue choices that can influence conversations and relationships. The game encourages exploration and logical thinking rather than hand-holding, making every breakthrough feel earned. Its extensive cast of characters helps create a believable world where nearly everyone has a motive, a secret, or a unique perspective on the unfolding events. The integrated journal system also proves useful by recording discoveries and objectives, allowing players to manage the increasingly complex investigation without losing track of important information.

Visually, Culpa Innata was an impressive technical achievement for its time. Fully rendered 3D environments, cinematic presentation, and expressive facial animation technology help bring its futuristic world to life. While the graphics naturally reveal their age by modern standards, the artistic direction remains effective because it prioritizes atmosphere over spectacle. The soundtrack complements the investigative tone with subtle compositions that heighten suspense without becoming intrusive, while voice acting adds personality to the large supporting cast even if performances occasionally vary in quality. Together, these elements create a convincing environment that supports the game's slow-burning narrative and immersive world-building.

The game is not without weaknesses, however. Its deliberate pacing demands patience, as conversations can be lengthy and progression sometimes depends on revisiting locations or exhausting every dialogue option. Some puzzles feel less intuitive than others, and navigation across the game's many environments can occasionally interrupt the flow of the investigation. Players looking for fast-paced gameplay or constant action may find the experience overly methodical. However, those who appreciate story-focused adventures will likely view these slower moments as opportunities to absorb the game's intricate lore and carefully layered mystery rather than unnecessary obstacles.

Culpa Innata stands out because it strives to deliver more than a conventional detective story. It uses its murder investigation as a vehicle to explore complex social and political ideas while maintaining the engaging structure of a classic adventure game. Its memorable protagonist, intelligent writing, and thoughtfully constructed world make it a rewarding experience for players who enjoy narrative depth and meaningful exploration. Although certain mechanics and technical aspects have aged over time, the game's ambitious vision and commitment to storytelling continue to make it a distinctive entry within the adventure genre.

Rating: 7/10

Reviewing games I played a long time ago:

A very ambitious aventure game that in many ways was ahead of its time mainly on how non linear it is and the freedom it gives to the player on how to proceed in the investigation. Kinda reminds me of the Blade Runner game.

Saying that, even though I admire it, I remember I didnt really liked that much. I dont think I'll ever replay it again, but I liked it enough to buy it here and be part of my library.

I want to like this game. I think it has some smart ideas (even if they're now outdated), and the plot/story might be interesting, but the interface is terrible.
The clicking to move around the areas is awful, simply frustrating. You can start in one place, walk across a normal pedestrian bridge, and not be able to return to the previous area because the camera angle, or clicking interface, won't allow you to get back far enough to trigger the view of the previous area.  Walking around a simple plaza shouldn't be so difficult.  And I am not even complaining about how long it takes or the repetitiveness of it all. The view angles are horrible, worse than the original Resident Evil game.  You are supposed to explore a little, find some signs around areas, but I can't be sure if I'm trying to move into areas that are blocked off or the interface is so bad that I'm not being given the opportunity to trigger the transition view to move there. On top of that, sometimes you can't re-enter places you just left, which can be annoying if you're just being curious because there can be things to interact with there (that you missed or chose not to interact with in the moment), but I'm guessing that those are also instances where there are no clues or story progression points in that area. If movement was supplemented with the arrow keys, a lot of this could be remedied fairly easily.   
The voice acting is ok. The dialogue is interesting, there is a definite attempt to copy futuristic ideas like those in A Brave New World and Logan's Run. It definitely has an old school societal futuristic/dystopian vibe, and it leans into the POVs of the characters living in it vs. those who aren't as brainwashed. 
The puzzles range from easy (making sense) to esoteric (from "who would think of that" to some pretty crazy leaps of connecting bits of clues). Overall, not too bad, you will probably have to resort to a guide at least 2 or 3 times.  
The user interface for your policing work computer can be confusing and frustrating. You have clues, you can try to use them in your computer to process them, but it is not exactly clear how or where in your computer that you are supposed to do that. And, a lot of the times, when you are allowed access to parts of the computer functions, you can't use the clues or they just give you no info. For a futuristic police information and forensics tool, it's pretty crap. On top of it not being very intuitive.  
And you are sometimes forced to go through awkward/embarrassing (in regards to your character in-game) dialogues with your boss during debriefings. Sometimes all you have is information about someone's sex life, or catty employee gossip, and you are forced to go through them with your boss even though all you want is the "Ask to leave" option. It's silly — especially when your character is always saying "I shouldn't waste their time". But when you actually have something important that you want to try to take to your boss, you block yourself from going to your boss to bring it to them. You can't even call them to bring it up or make an appointment to do so. It makes no sense.   
And there is a strict daily time allotment in the game, you can only spend so much time going places and talking to people before the day ends.  And you are limited to how many interactions you can have with suspects/witnesses. It's not a bad mechanic, it limits exploring (but there isn't a whole lot of exploring to be done), but it would be nice if you had some sort of tool in game to help you measure and manage that time. If it was just a number of actions/locations per business day, then that would be nice to see, but it just seems like a day can pass more quickly than others without having actually done much. 
I could go on. Basically it's a frustrating interface that is an active obstacle to what could be a good point & click game. Point & click games normally have a bit of wasted time involved in them, but this one feels like a bit more than that. It's bad design in movement and area perspectives, it shouldn't be this hard/bad. 
If you know what you're getting into, and you're prepared to deal with it (or know ahead of time what/where you need to do/go to accomplish what's needed), then it could be a good game for you. If you're looking for a fun P&C game, but don't want to deal with unnecessary headaches/frustrations, then maybe this game is a pass for you.

An underrated gem with a unique play style - half point & click puzzler, half detective interview simulator with an impressive amount of fully voiced dialogue options with divergent outcomes (it was actually a precursor to LA Noire, which I believed to be the innovator of this gameplay style before I discovered Culpa Innata) 

The setting is also unique - a post-post-apocalyptic future, where society fell apart but was rebuild with a new world order living by different codes of law and morality to our present. The game does a good job of exploring the differences of the new world with nuance - there are elements of the World Union that seem oppressive to citizens, but also benefits and security greater than we know today. 
Even after finishing the game, I can't fully tell the intended perception from the writers' point of view - sadly the game leaves many questions unanswered intentionally, presumably in the hope they would make a sequel that never came to pass. 

One aspect of the philosophy of the World Union that didn't make sense to me was the Ayn Randian "greed is good" mantra - this phrase is used several times throughout the game, but an explanation as to why the Union believes this was never presented. So, despite being a compelling nuanced world, parts of Culpa Innata do feel underdeveloped (or at least under-explained). 

Visuals and music are great - it feels very retro but in an atmospheric way, reminiscent of point & click classics like The Longest Journey and Syberia. The game's world is a creative and expansive vision of a near-future city, full of "Y2K futurism" interior and clothing designs that will be enjoyably nostalgic for anyone who remembers those times. The music is also very of the time with electronic dance tracks and some experimental use of samples and heavy industrial elements. It feels like music from a Berlin night club, in a good way! 

Final thoughts - a compellingly unique and surprisingly in-depth experience for its genre - far less "on rails" than most p&c titles and with a huge amount of dialogue. I really enjoyed the immersion of the interviewing system, however, I did also get fatigued by the number of times I needed to revisit the same characters to continuously cross-reference new findings. In a sense, the detective experience here could be called "too realistic" in subjecting the player to the repetitive and tedious side of the job. 

Small complaint aside - this is a game that got me thinking more than most and I wish it had got a sequel!

On the other hand rouge states goes on as we are now.
 We play a character raised in world union and strongly belives its edicts. Society and normal people's behaviour changes according to the system's values are very well represented. You cannot skip one lane of dialog, if you right click it skips entire dialog -tree (!! careful). Since you cannot reply dialogue this is awful. In most adventure games , right click just skips one. Altro recuperone, nonché una delle migliori avventure grafiche che abbia mai avuto il piacere di giocare.
Universo, trama e lore affascinanti, ottima scrittura, e personaggi che restano impressi nella mente con un doppiaggio che, seppur spesso riciclato con giusto qualche variazione di timbro e tono, riesce comunque a farteli amare o stare sulle palle, per cui direi che l'obiettivo è stato comunque pienamente raggiunto.

E' la prima (e forse unica aggiungerei) avventura con progressione non lineare che abbia mai visto o provato finora. Il nostro compito è quello di indagare su un determinato avvenimento, ma il modo e l'ordine con cui portare a termine questa indagine è totalmente nelle nostre mani. E' quasi tutto basato sui dialoghi, tranne qualche sporadico puzzle (su questi ci torno tra poco), ma non tutte le linee di dialogo sono giuste o portano a risultati concreti, e quindi potrebbe volerci più o meno tempo sia per arrivare a una determinata conclusione e sia per terminare il gioco del tutto. E non c'è un modo preciso per portare avanti i compiti, con la possibilità anche di saltare interi personaggi o luoghi se si evita di fare determinate cose, e ogni run risulta potenzialmente differente proprio per questo motivo.
Notevoli anche le espressioni facciali secondo me, specie per un'avventura grafica del 2008 con un budget così risicato, che nonostante siano ovviamente indietro rispetto agli standard attuali (e grazie, graziella e grazie al ca**o, aggiungerei), lasciano trasparire ogni dettaglio sui volti legato al dialogo corrente.

Una piccola perla ingiustamente sottovalutata, che però fa a botte con dei puzzle a volte insensatamente astrusi, inutili (letteralmente) o privi di qualsiasi indizio sul come risolverli, e di un sistema di controllo punta e clicca un po' vecchio e totalmente inadatto allo scopo, specialmente considerato che il gioco urla a squarciagola "GAMEPAD!" da tutti i pixel. Il risultato è che il movimento è molto impreciso e risulta legnoso: spesso ho fatto fatica a direzionare bene il personaggio soprattutto per passare in un'altra area, dato che nonostante si clicchi sulla freccia per cambiare schermata/inquadratura si dovrà azzeccare il punto giusto per farlo, pena lo stallo del personaggio.
Il finale è un po' "rushato" per così dire, anche per colpa del fatto che ci sarebbe dovuto essere un sequel: la sensazione che ho avuto è che l'avventura si arresti di colpo quando sta decollando, forse l'unica nota dolente a livello di ritmo del gioco, che altrimenti riesce a dosare benissimo, a mio parere, i colpi di scena e le informazioni date al giocatore (a meno che non siate una pippa e sbagliate tutti i dialoghi, quello è un altro discorso).
Presente anche qualche bug (sempre legato al movimento, non a caso) che può causare il blocco permanente del personaggio (a meno di non fare il fast travel, il che però è controproducente dato che farà avanzare il tempo della giornata) e che quindi costringe a ricaricare la partita; ma a parte questo, nient'altro di rilevante.

Tutta la parte investigativa, che è poi il fulcro stesso del gioco, è talmente ben fatta e pensata che ne avrei voluto di più, ancora e ancora; ma purtroppo, nonostante la durata considerevole, prima o poi era inevitabile giungere a una conclusione.
Peccato che il seguito sia stato cancellato nel 2009 a circa metà sviluppo a causa di un voltafaccia del publisher, apparentemente, con conseguente mancanza di fondi. Proprio di recente però (quando ho deciso io di giocarlo, manco a farlo apposta) un nuovo dettagliatissimo sito del gioco è stato messo online con indizi su un possibile sequel o (si spera di no) remake. Chissà... Speriamo bene.



PS:  Ah, ha anche una intro che è entrata tra le mia preferite. E per l'amor di dio giocatelo in inglese, a meno che non vogliate farvi due risate con il doppiaggio italiano osceno, che ammetto sia stato una bella scoperta trash.

I've experienced the game with the [url=https://www.moddb.com/mods/culpa-innata-uncut-patch]uncut patch[/url]. It's fairly interesting, I liked the main character with her flaws and ingenuity combined with a good heart and strong drive. The dialogs and the various characters you meet were rather good, and sometimes made me laugh. The investigation itself was incredibly slow but compelling enough to want to see it through. However, the intrigue was too simple and didn't "toy" with the player/reader enough, like the best mystery novels that keep you guessing until the end about who is the culprit and what happened. There was also too much peripheral unexplained stuff that ended up having no relevance to the plot at all. The beginning of the opening cutscene is intriguing, right? Well forget it having any real impact on the actual plot, it ends up being just worldbuilding.

Playability-wise I found it atrocious, with the slow panning around often disorienting fixed-camera 3D scenes. There's no hotkey to show hotspots, which would've been very welcome in few specific scenes, the inventory system is slow to use, and the puzzles are the obnoxious minigame kind. I much prefer the item-finding and combining style like in Book of Unwritten Tales or Black Mirror II and III.
The use of the computer for various analyses felt pretty good though, but didn't give you enough freedom to really make you feel you were coming up with ideas on your own.

Graphics are bad but art direction is good and uses its limited means effectively. Music is surprisingly good and adequate.

The woldbuilding was deeper than average but imperfect. Some of the stuff like the Final Bill of Rights makes no sense when you dig into the text's details, and is completely inconsistent with the other rules of this society. Actually there are many other inconsistencies like this such as the upper echelons getting religious-like names in a society that looks down on old religions. And said upper echelons were represented in a very inconsistent way in the game. Overall though, a valiant effort that genuinely made the game more interesting to play, and while there are obvious ideological drives, they were not overbearing i.e. it didn't feel like preaching to join one real-world ideology or another.

The adult elements felt refreshing, especially in the sense that all that overt talk about sex really makes you feel that you're in a different society that doesn't have the same inhibitions as ours. The visuals restored by the uncut patch were very tame (and not that well modeled/animated), but do serve to reinforce the story.

The ending was a rather disappointing cliffhanger - but at least you get to solve the murder case.

Overall, a weak recommendation. It was enjoyable enough to finish it, but I wouldn't play it without a walkthrough to get through the puzzles.
