A game that LOST its roots.

The game passed to another developper and another publisher. Things got worst.

I explain. The designers tried to differenciate things more by building the races in a different way.
In this game we have ONLY two races comparing to the 3 plus the scourge we had in the first Perimeter, the Exodus and the HeartBack.
So, the story says that the new world those races were searching finally found. But the Exodus still can colonize the surface while the HeartBack can build in Water.

If you are a Perimeter Veteran please read the differences below, after the many dashes.

For the Newcomers to this game.

Here we have a simple strategy game. You first build the energy cores and terraform the ground so you can move easily or build upon it. To do that on the easy way build every NEXT energy core to the change of the levels of the ground and press the terraform button of the NEW energy core. In other ways you'll get yourself saying some bad words if NOT smushing the PC or leaving the game completely. The manual terraforming controls are buggy so don't be frustrated. The only thing you'll need the manual terraforming is when you want to get some blue crystals and you'll need to dig the ground.

Every technology as the game says must be researched first. So if you want to build unit factories you need to research them first. So level 2 and 3 factories. The factories create the pop cap. But you can't have as many factories as you want as the preserve energy. The units from the factories have ground and air mode. You change them dependant on what you want to attack or defend because ground units don't fight air.

Generally is a very simple game that tricks your imagination. Nothing more.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If you have played the first Perimeter....

The game differences are Massive.

--There is no Frame here. No main building. No King of Chess. You start building like any other strategy game.
--The energy cores can be built anywhere at start. The terraform process is included in them and can be set at automatic mode or manual. Manual terraforming is crap. You use it only to level the ground where you want and then auto. The controls for the manual are buggy. A very easy way to keep the level of the ground the same(but you lose space) is to build the energy cores to the gaps that the ground changes levels. When you press the terraform button the ground will be in the same level as the OLD energy core. But as you can see in this game you have to be occupied even to that.
--Population cap is related to the factories and is NOT standard as in the first game. Every factory places about 2 more squads and the squad units number is about 1-4 dependant on the unit. Factories preserve energy like in Command and Conquer and NOT like in the first Perimeter when ONLY working. In this way the squad number is limited. 
--You have a Research Center to advance your technology. To build the 3-set level of factories you have to research them as much other techs like PLUS in Weapons or Shields for your units. The first level builds light units, the second level medium units and the third heavy units that are effective in buildings most.
--So we have ONLY 3 units per race that can be changed from ground to air and vice versa depedant of the opponents offensive and defensive. For example fighters confront fighters and the vehicles other vehicles. There is NO unit from the ground to hit the air.
--The chess game that we were playing in the first Perimeter with the capturing of the energy cores or buildings of the opponent is VERY limited here, because the Exodus structures are damaged from water and the HeartBack structures from the normal ground.
--There are NO subterrastrial units on this game.
--Ahh yes, I almost forgot. New power-ups like Nukes,mass terra destruction and such are coming from the blue ingame crystals like OLD techs that you find on the planet's surface. To get those crystals you'll need to build an energy core on them and MANUALLY terraform the ground in DIGGING mode.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Slamit pinball big score est un jeu de flipper qui propose une unique table sur le thème du policier et du voleur. Pour accéder à celle-ci, il va falloir être rusé et prendre sur soi. Allez, je suis sympa, je vous fais gagner du temps : tout d’abord, n’allez pas dans les options voir la configuration des touches car vous allez revenir à votre espace bureau, manu militari. Le jeu crashe à chaque fois. Ensuite, pour démarrer une partie, il faut appuyer sur la touche « 1 » de votre clavier pour signifier que vous insérez au moins 1 crédit puis la lettre « S » pour Start. Ça y est, vous y êtes ! Bon courage ! Parce que c’est difficile ! 
La distance entre les raquettes est assez importante, et si la bille passe par la roue du centre, de gauche à droite, vous passez être quasi sûr qu’elle va filer droit vers la sortie centrale, autrement dit faire un avion ou une cave. De même, les garages sont monnaies courantes, je ne compte plus le nombre de fois où je lance la bille qui file direct dans un des couloirs latéraux, géniaaaaaaaal… 
C’est vraiment dommage car tout ce qui fait un bon flipper est présent : des rampes, des multibilles, des bumpers, des cibles tombantes, des missions qui se joue parfois au fronton, des trous gobeurs, une raquette supplémentaire, des rollovers,… On peut secouer la machine, c’est même conseillé pour une fois. 
C’est joli, il y a des bruitages, des lumières, les touches sont classiques (les MAJ droites et gauches, et ENTREE pour lancer). Mais décidément, c’est trop dur ! Et dommage qu’il n’y ait qu’une table si difficile d’accès ! 
A recommander pour les aficionados.

9/13/2021 - A new perspective on this game, considering many games came out after this:

WOW, is all I can say about this creation. Before anyone asks, no, I'm not changing my stance, because of what's happened since, but with a concept like freeform nudging, this is WAY ahead of its time. 

We have had many different pinball games with great physics, but most of them fall short. Pinball Arcade steers the ball as part of its nudging, FX3 suffers from nudge passing especially on recreations, and mainly, nudging overall is incredibly simplistic with single press, full-strength nudging. Even VPX suffers similarly to FX3. Pro Pinball is an exception with analog-based keyboard nudging, but Slamit takes it a step further, utilizing custom nudges depending on how many keys you pressed and which ones. For a 2009 game that utilizes custom strengths, lights, and other options, the work they poured into this is seriously impressive.

Given the current conditions, however, I can't recommend this due to problems on modern-day systems, including choppy framerates (Steam's in-game FPS disagrees somehow...?). This is no fault of the developers, however, and it's a truly tragic tale to be told and why there's no support behind SlamIt. One of the lead devs actually died in a car crash shortly after it released. If you want to get this game for preservation's sake, go for it. Otherwise, steer clear and look for a more enjoyable pinball experience.

I hope this project (or the SlamIt nudging system at least) is revived one of these days, in this series or another.

this table has some clever features, but it also has myriad problems that never got fixed. among them:
- each of the camera positions are junk 
-the flippers are short as hell, making shots hard to aim for
- the bumpers never hold the ball long enough to get anywhere close to Super Jets 
- the Bank random feature tends to not work
- the safe kickout often sends your ball straight down into the drain, and 
- there is no physical "glass", so the ball can potentially fly off the playfield with no chance of recovering it (along with some other game-ending bugs).

the rules of the game are completely confusing. sometimes you hear the announcer shout "calls activity!" and you're expected to make a shot, but the shot never seems to be lit up in a way that you can identify it. other times you see a letter scroll across the display (covering up all other information, natch) and sometimes you manage to add it to "Big $core" in the middle of the playfield, but it's unclear how or why that happens. 
and, most of the main modes add their score to your bonus, so combining them with a decent bonus multiplier basically makes anything else you can do to score irrelevant.

but, the table's layout is actually very cool! the artwork is decent, and there is a good mix of standard and gimmicky shots. the u-turn / dial in the center is neat, but underutilized. also, the hidden ramp that rises and leads the opened safe makes for a cool jackpot shot. 

with some work, and a ruleset that actually made sense, this could have been a wicked game, which is a shame.

other high points: the game is actually pretty good looking (the flasher effects are very well-done), the sound is alright overall, and the voice acting is so hilariously bad that you think about it days later and smile.

This is a definitive "DO NOT BUY". You can harangue this game into working, but even on modern hardware produced years after this game was released, it will still run at a terrible frame-rate. That is unfortunate, because the table layout and game itself are actually interesting.

If you want to play pinball, there are thankfully more options on Steam now. Pinball FX2, Pinball Arcade, and Worms Pinball are all more worthy of your time.

TLDR: Als Teil der Reihe empfohlen, aber wirklich nur für nostalgische Fans oder Personen, die einige nervige Dinge (s.u.) vertragen können und die es nicht stört in der (nicht originalen) englischen Fassung zu spielen. Alle anderen sparen es sich lieber.

Die Ankh Reihe ist für mich eine große Kindheitserinnerung - es sind die ersten Spiele an die ich mich bewusst erinnern kann. Deshalb habe ich mir kürzlich aus nostalgischen Gründen die komplette Reihe für ein paar Groschen geschnappt. Den ersten Teil auf Steam kann man auch echt - mit ein paar kleineren Einschränkungen (Review siehe dort) - mit gutem Gewissen für Oldschool Adventure Fans empfehlen. Beim zweiten Teil sieht das aber leider etwas anders aus. 

Was ist gut?
Die Story gefiel mir und es war schön, die Figuren aus dem ersten Teil wiederzusehen. Es gibt ein paar neue Locations. Es gibt noch eine zusätzliche spielbare Figur und die Passage in der man zwischen Assil und Thara tauschen kann, war gut gemacht. Einige Rätsel sind recht originell. 

Die Rätsel:
Es gibt definitiv ein paar gute Ideen ( die 10 Kochgebote fand ich durchaus eine witzige Idee, außerdem die Taverne in der man alle glücklich machen soll zu Beginn ), aber leider ein paar Probleme mit dem Gamedesign, Questlog und der Logik. Vorallem in dem Steinbruchsegment musste ich vieles nachgucken, da ich einfach nicht verstanden habe, was das Spiel von mir will, da ich Dinge unbeabsichtigt in der "falschen" Reihenfolge gemacht hatte und somit manche Questlogeinträge in mir nur ein "aber warum ?" auslösten. So wurde ich auf einmal gebeten "Dinge zu finden die ein Charakter an ein Seil hängen kann". Ich hatte zwar aus Trial- und Error mal ein Seil irgendwo runter geworfen (ohne zu wissen wozu). Da ich eine Sache nicht angeklickt, und dazu den Dialog noch nicht geführt hatte, war mir diese Aufgabe sehr schleierhaft, bis ich nachgeguckt hatte, worum es ging und warum überhaupt etwas an das Seil gebunden werden sollte. Oft kombiniert man (in meiner Erfahrung) blind Dinge und rafft erst später wozu.
Dazu natürlich diese typischen Point und Click Sünden wie "Finde einen Hammer und einen Meißel" wenn man in der Werkzeughütte daneben eindeutig welche liegen sieht, die jedoch nicht anklickbar sind und die Utensilien dann mit 5 Umwegen anders beschaffen muss. Na ja, das ist verschmerzbar, man kennt es auch aus anderen Spielen.

Sprachfassung 

Ein deutlich größeres Problem für gerade dieses Spiel. Wie schon einige andere beschrieben haben, findet sich hier auf Steam (im Gegensatz zum ersten Teil) nur die englische Sprachfassung. Die deutsche muss man sich manuell selbst extern auf Umwegen organisieren. Da ich mich da nicht ausreichend technisch auskenne, habe ich mir den Aufwand gespart und die englische gespielt. Grundsätzlich bin ich jemand, der gerne und viel auf Englisch spielt, also dachte ich "halb so wild".
 
Aber bei einem Spiel, das original auf Deutsch ist und so stark auf Wortwitz und kulturellen Anspielungen beruht wie Ankh, macht es eben doch einen Unterschied. Einige Witze funktionieren nicht (die "Katze im Sack" oder die Anspielung auf das Lied "Flugzeuge im Bauch" als Copyright Infringement z.B.). Sie machen auf Englisch exakt gar keinen Sinn, und man hat einfach große Fragezeichen in den Augen, wo der Witz sein soll, bis man sie sich im Kopf rückübersetzt. Die englischen Sprecher sind auch finde ich schlechter gecastet, was besonders auffällt, wenn man direkt vorher den ersten Teil auf Deutsch gespielt hat. 
Vorallem bei Thara,  merkt man, dass die Sprecherin wohl überhaupt kein Briefing erhalten hat, in welchem Kontext eine Aussage fällt und die Betonung oft gewürfelt scheint. Manche Aussagen klingen unpassend sarkastisch, oder wie Fragen obwohl es keine sind, ernst obwohl sie ein Witz sind usw. Als kleiner Pet Peeve, könnte man noch ergänzen, dass das Wort "Ankh" teilweise im selben Dialog fünfmal unterschiedlich ausgesprochen wird (z.T. wie das "a" in "Thanks", z.T. wie in "car"). Darüber hinaus gibt es manchmal sprachliche Fehler in den englischen Untertiteln ([spoiler] zum Beispiel die Aussage von Seth er könnte jemanden mit seinen "bear hands" umbringen, war schon wieder unfreiwillig komisch [/spoiler]. Das alles ist zwar schon ziemlich ärgerlich, aber immer noch nicht das Ende der Liste von Problemen mit dem Spiel.

Das Technische

Man soll ja mit dem Positiven beginnen: Komplett gecrasht ist mir das Spiel nicht. Yay. 
Sonst war aber eigentlich alles dabei:
1. Fehlende Dialogzeilen (sowohl fehlende Audio als auch kryptische Zahlencodes statt Antworten (z.B. Dialog mit arab. Botschafter zu Beginn, wenn man ihn auf das Harem anspricht); 
Andere Audiodialogzeilen wiederum erscheinen an falschen Stellen, die zu unfreiwilliger Komik führen, wenn Figuren etwas komplett anderes als da steht, das völlig abstrus ist, sagen.
2. Bereits erfolgte Handlungen werden vom Spiel "vergessen" ([spoiler] Als man der Palastwache das Couscousgericht kochen muss, weist einen diese auch nachdem dieser "Quest" abgegeben wurde nochmal darauf hin, dies zu tun und im finalen Kapitel steht diese Aufgabe verwirrenderweise auch NOCHMAL im Questlog, auch wenn es an der Stelle absolut nicht gefordert wird [/spoiler] ). 
3. Kleinere und größere Glitchereien. Charaktere verschwinden und tauchen spontan wieder auf. Thara unterhielt sich mehrfach mit Schmuel, Ephraim und co. obwohl sie überhaupt nicht da waren. Assil ist mir im letzten Kapitel einmal komplett weggeglitcht und stand auf einmal in der Küche, auch wenn ich den Aufzug noch gar nicht plotmäßig freigeschaltet hatte, wo ich ihn auch nur mit Mühen wieder rausbekam. 

Quality of Life:
Es gibt auch hier keine Hotspotanzeige und keine Schnellreisemöglichkeiten, man klickt also viel blind rum und läuft noch mehr hin und her. Allerdings sind Cutscenes inzwischen skippbar und man kann die Dialog- Musik- und Effektlautstärken einzeln verstellen, also ein kleines Upgrade. 

Fazit: Ich tue mich schwer auf dem Ja/Nein Bewertungssystem von Steam "Nein" zu drücken, da mir die Ankh Reihe sehr am Herzen liegt, auch wenn ich es objektiv eigentlich müsste. Es gibt aber durchaus auch Gründe das Spiel zu mögen und ich hatte ja an vielen Stellen meinen Spaß. Aber ja, es könnte auch viel besser sein , wären allein schon mal das Problem mit der Sprachfassung nicht und die Technik stabiler. Für einen Euro im Sale fühlt man sich wirklich nicht um sein Geld betrogen, aber man muss wissen worauf man sich einlässt.

"Ankh 2: Heart of Osiris " is an ancient game from 2007.  It's a whopping 17 years old at the time of this review.  The game lacks support for any modern gaming display resolutions (or widescreen monitors), hasn't been modernised or updated to run smoothly on modern gaming PCs.  Despite this lack of modernisation, it carries a pretty high price tag for such an ancient game.  This seems to have been put on Steam as a nostalgia gouge, or just a cash grab to try profit from abandonware.

This is an Egyptian themed "me too!" entry trying to do a slightly more recent spin on games like Sam & Max Hit The Road and Day of the Tentacle, but the charm isn't there and the puzzles are convoluted yet unrewarding.  It's also really dated and lacks support for 4K resolution and other modern PC attributes, making this a bit of a failure.

The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only 12 players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 100,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.

So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?

"Ankh 2: Heart of Osiris " is relatively expensive for an abandonware nostalgia gouge, at $5 USD, and it's not worth it.  The game is just too old, hasn't been modernised.  And as the old saying goes, you can't go home again.  Even when it was new, this was never a triple-A game.  This is the kind of game that went almost directly from the warehouse into the cheap bargain bins at the front of the shop.  Now, on Steam, without any modernisation?  This is impossible to recommend.  This is also competing with over 14,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.

Ankh: Herz des Osiris ist der zweite Teil der Reihe. 
Die Ereignisse aus dem ersten Spiel werden hier nun fortgesetzt.

Die erste Szene beginnt auf dem Friedhof Kairos, wo zwei düstere (und uns wohlbekannte) Gestalten entlangspazieren. Sie sprechen vor einer Gruft mit Osiris und wollen ihm das eben gestohlene Ankh überreichen. Der Totengott hat auch schon einen Plan – er will seinen Diener erwecken, damit dieser seine Ankunft in der Welt der Lebenden vorbereitet. Plötzlich springt Assil herbei und möchte allen erzählen, wie er es geschafft hat, sie zu finden.
In der zweiten Szene finden wir Assil übel zugerichtet in einer dunklen Seitengasse auf. Thara hat mit ihm Schluss gemacht und zu allem Überfluss wurde auch noch sein Ankh gestohlen. Sein Wächter-Status ist damit dahin. In seinem Inventar befindet sich ein Brief von seiner Verehrerin, der Tochter des Pharaos. Damit erklärt sich, warum Thara nichts mehr von ihm wissen wollte. Also macht Assil sich auf, um beides zurückzugewinnen – das Ankh und die Liebe seines Lebens! 

Im Prinzip hat sich zum Vorgänger nicht viel geändert. Wir steuern hauptsächlich Assil und suchen nach bekannter Point-and-Click-Manier nach Objekten, die man betrachten oder gar aufnehmen kann. Hauptsächlich? Ja, denn das ist die große Neuerung: Im weiteren Spielverlauf können wir auch Thara bei ihrer Mission helfen oder den Pharao höchstpersönlich durch die Gegend lotsen.
Durch die Interaktion mit anderen - bzw. aus dem ersten Teil bekannten – Charakteren ergeben sich aufschlussreiche und teils lustige Dialoge. Auch hier kann man nichts falsch machen, es sei denn, man hat vergessen, Dinge miteinander zu kombinieren ;)

Ein paar Fehler sind auch hier wieder mit dabei gewesen, aber nichts Gravierendes. Die Ladezeiten zwischen den Szenen waren nur etwas nervig. 

Vom Spielspaß her ist Teil 2 gleichauf mit dem ersten. Die Entwickler nehmen sich selbst auf die Schippe, parodieren geschichtliche Ereignisse und wissen, wie man vorhandene Charaktere/Umgebungen mit Neuerungen gezielt einsetzt. 
Mit dem Deutsch-Patch macht es gleich doppelt Spaß – auch wenn keiner versteht, warum die deutsche Vertonung nicht mit angeboten wurde.

Während Ankh 1 seine Fans überzeugt hat, schwächelt der Nachfolger etwas. Die Witze sind wohl doch nicht so angekommen wie gewünscht. Auch hier sucht man Errungenschaften vergebens. 
Trotzdem gebe ich hierfür eine Empfehlung raus. Es ist ein größtenteils gelungenes Sequel.

This game gets a thumbs up from me but barely. It's a decent little point and click adventure that was actually rated pretty highly during its time by the German gaming press but does not hold up particularly well.

Let's start with the pros though:

- Decent voice acting
- Graphics are OK for a game from 2007 and the early days of 3D adventures
- It's not too long and can be finished in well under 10 hours
- You get to play as different characters and, in imho, all are more fun than the 'hero'
- The game is usually heavily discounted on Steam and can be had for about a dollar at times

Now for some of the negative:

- The story is a direct continuation of the previous game and will make even less sense if you haven't played that one already
- But even then, it doesn't make a whole lot of sense and feels more like a set up for the finale in part 3
- It's not as funny as it thinks it is - most of the jokes fell flat for me
- The puzzles are hit and miss, they are either painfully obvious and trivial or rather obscure and convoluted
- The biggest challenge are not the puzzles but rather objects hidden in the background that are very easy to miss (this was most annoying in chapter 4), one item did not appear to be there (visually speaking) at all and I only found it on mouse over by accident
- No option to highlight interactive objects
- Game tends to just quit when you try to switch back to it from ALT+TAB - so save often!

This seems like a lot of negative and yes, mechanically the game isn't great. It's a decent game though if you liked the first one or (German) point and click adventures from that era.

[h1][b]Ankh 2: Herz des Osiris – Assil, Thara und der Fluch des Patchs[/b][/h1]  
[b]Spielzeit:[/b] 8–10 Stunden – je nach Verzweiflung über Mondrätsel und Sprachpatch.  
[b]Empfohlen:[/b] Für Retro-Fans, Liebhaber von trockenem Humor und Abenteuerlustige mit Geduld für technische Umwege.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Einleitung: Der Humor zieht in die zweite Runde[/h2]  

Nach dem Erfolg des ersten [i]Ankh[/i]-Teils schickt Deck13 Assil wieder auf Abenteuerreise – diesmal in [i]Ankh 2: Herz des Osiris[/i]. Was mit einem gestohlenen Ankh, einer kriselnden Beziehung zu Thara und einer Prise ägyptischer Magie beginnt, entwickelt sich zu einem weiteren humorvollen Abenteuer voller Rätsel, skurriler Charaktere und witziger Dialoge. Leider nur auf Englisch erhältlich, es sei denn, du bist technisch so versiert wie ein Nilbau-Ingenieur und wagst dich an einen Sprachpatch.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Hauptteil: Der Fluch des Humors und der Mondrätsel[/h2]  

[h3]Humor und Story:[/h3]  
Der Humor hat im zweiten Teil eine Schippe Frechheit draufgelegt. Die Dialoge sind spritziger, und Assils Begegnungen mit den abgedrehten Nebencharakteren sorgen für viele Lacher. Die Story selbst knüpft nahtlos an den ersten Teil an und bietet eine interessante Mischung aus Abenteuer, Beziehungsdrama und ägyptischem Mythos.  

[h3]Grafik und Atmosphäre:[/h3]  
Grafisch bleibt [i]Ankh 2[/i] dem Stil des Vorgängers treu. Es gibt kleine Verbesserungen, aber die große Revolution bleibt aus – typisch für ein Spiel seiner Zeit. Die farbenfrohen Umgebungen und liebevoll gestalteten Charaktere sorgen dennoch für nostalgischen Charme.  

[h3]Synchronisation:[/h3]  
Einmal mehr ist die deutsche Synchronisation ein Highlight: Oliver Rohrbeck (Ben Stiller) und Thomas Danneberg (John Cleese) verleihen den Figuren eine unvergleichliche Persönlichkeit. Sie machen das Spiel zu einem akustischen Genuss – vorausgesetzt, du bist bereit, die deutsche Version über einen Sprachpatch nachzurüsten.  

[h3]Rätsel:[/h3]  
Auch diesmal bleibt Deck13 der klassischen Point-and-Click-Tradition treu: kreative Rätsel, die oft zum Nachdenken anregen – und manchmal auch zum Fluchen. Wer beim ersten Teil mit den „Mond-Rätseln“ (absurd komplexe oder unlogische Lösungen) klargekommen ist, wird hier ebenfalls gefordert.  

[h3]Musik und Sound:[/h3]  
Die Musik untermalt das Geschehen solide, ohne dabei zu stark aufzufallen. Die Soundeffekte hingegen unterstützen die Atmosphäre gut. Es ist wie eine österreichische Sachertorte ohne Schlagobers: lecker, aber nicht herausragend.  

[h3]Technische Details:[/h3]  
Auf modernen Systemen läuft das Spiel einwandfrei. Es ist fast beeindruckend, dass ein Spiel aus der Mitte der 2000er Jahre so stabil auf Windows 10 funktioniert – da könnte sich manch modernes Spiel ein Beispiel nehmen.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Pro & Contra[/h2]  

[h3]Positiv:[/h3]  
[list]  
[*] [b]Verbesserter Humor:[/b] Frecher, bissiger und unterhaltsam.

Serious fans of the point-and-click genre may appreciate this one, but players who only occasionally visit this kind of game would do well to look somewhere else. 'Ankh 2' is tagged on Steam as a comedy, but genuinely humorous moments are quite rare. It isn't a particularly intuitive game, and the narrative mechanics are far too inflexible.  I can remember one moment, for instance, when I had to shoo away an aggressive cat. I had in my inventory a piece of chicken but trying to use this to complete the objective resulted simply in my character shaking their head and saying, very robotically, "Hmm... this doesn't work." 
There are some fun moments in 'Ankh 2', but no more than can be found in any other average  point-and-click game. At £3.99 you certainly won't feel cheated by the developers, but don't expect more than a few hours' enjoyment.

Сиквел Ankh вышел довольно противоречивой игрой. Разработчики сделали заметный прогресс в плане шуток и сценария, но в то же время сделали значительный шаг назад в плане игрового процесса и технической части. Движок тут ну очень кривой и забагованный, модельки персонажей то и дело исчезают, и в целом игра умудряется выглядеть хуже чем первая часть. С геймплеем та же проблема, я жаловался на чрезмерное злоупотребление пиксельхантингом и бэктрекингом в оригинале, но если там это еще было терпимо, то в Ankh 2 разработчики превзошли себя. В этой игре одни из самых бредовых и маразматичных загадок, что я видел в квестах, а в сочетании с еще большим количеством бесцельной беготни кругами по местным локациям и сливающимися с фоном предметами и активными точками, комбинация выходит просто убийственная. Подсветки активных точек так и не добавили, поэтому без руководства к прохождению на игру вполне реально угробить 10+ часов в попытках понять извращенную логику дизайнеров уровней.

Ankh 2 вытягивает юмор и атмосфера - игра стартует довольно вяло, но ближе к середине сюжет разгоняется и начинает выдавать действительно смешные сценки. Если первая часть серии была просто местами забавной, в этот раз сценаристы действительно постарались - после феерической зарисовки "Фараон и Говорящий куст" я простил игре далекий от идеала геймплей и технические проблемы. Ну и финал Ankh 2 на мой взгляд вышел более удачным, да еще и концовка немного отличается от выбора в финальных диалогов. В общем, если убрать время, затрачиваемое на поиски нужной вещи на экране или попытки понять, что клетку с попугаем нужно открыть с помощью игральных карт, то выходит весьма неплохой юмористический квест.

Could've been good but too many annoyances made this game pretty unplayable.

There are parts I really liked about this game, the story are actual puzzles were enjoyable. But that's about it.

Technical glitches up the wazoo. Uggg. It completely crashed on me so many times and a couple of times after an event happened the game glitched, with dialogue popping up like it hadn't happened and I couldn't go back, couldn't go forward. So lame. Also, talk about clicking on super tiny specific things or one tiny hidden area of the screen to find an exit. I literally had to move my cursor slowly across one oasis scene trying to find the one small spot that finally popped up as an exit.

I've seen plenty of sequels that want to rely so heavily on building up to the third installment that the story goes missing (I'm looking at you, Dragon Age II!), but I've rarely seen a second game that uses the first as it's crutch. Mainly because that's such a stupid idea, and yet that's pretty much what Ankh 2 seems to be doing a lot of. I've never played the first, but with how many things are mentioned for happening in the first game and how little is explained at whatever the hell is going on when I jump in the game, leaving me with this subliminal message to get Ankh 1 (Which I won't, because of how pestered I was).

 In the end, I was left with my imagination to fill in what happened in the Ankh 1... and that's not a good thing to do. 

If you make a sequel, it should have elements of it's predecessor, but still be able to stand on it's own. Come on Ankh 2! Look over at Mass Effect 2, Arkham City, and Assassin's Creed II. They're doing it just fine! Even Final Fantasy can make a game that stands on it's own... about 15 completely different ways, though. 

But that isn't the only thing that made me dislike Ankh 2. The game's graphics, while cartoony and colorful, have poor texturing and the game likes to do the occaisional zoom in on some of the objects, which made me sneer at my laptop screen.

On top of that, the story is urine poor (I'm allowed to say "urine", right?). There are a few jokes that hit me with the "nostril snort and slight smirk" reaction, but these are very few. Most of them are incredibly cheesey- just like the voice actors. And they're all pretty much rubbish. Except for Moses. He was decent. But everyone else was very obviously acting. 

The story also wants to hit these serious moments and build up this particular love triangle when I had no absolute belief in either because of how odd the former stood out like sore thumbs and how forced the latter felt. Along with that, the story's biggest flaw is caused mainly by the gameplay which is about as slow as a donkey with two broken legs and no carrot in front of it's face. Characters- even when running- are hardly going that fast and always maintain the same animation- which is alright for a casual scene. But in suspense, action, and intense scenes- these really bring all that feeling down to a screeching halt. 

Along with the occasional game flops, like screen glitches and crashes. There was one point that I had played four hours worth of the game and was close to beating it, and I accidentally saved just as the game broke on me, and I ended up having to go all the way back and rush to where I left off.

Another huge problem is the logic of this game. Sure, it's like many point-and-click puzzle games (where the most specific, strange things can solve puzzles, even when other objects in your inventory could suit the job just as easily), but honestly. How was I supposed to know that a doll with it's head popped off should hold a candle? Or that I should use the Eleventh Commandment Tablet as a wrecking ball? OR that I can split a coconut with a cuckoo-clock's bird and use said coconut to revive a parrot?

And my final complaint, is more of something I just noticed when I was getting towards the end of the game. How to Thara and Assil have the magic ability to telepathically communicate to each other during puzzles so that one on the opposite side of the stadium knows that they need to direct a sunbeam produced by another and reflect it right back at them?

I'm going to play Ankh 3 not because I want to, but because foolishly bought both and now it's just sitting there, staring at me in my inventory- and the slight charm of this game which existed as much as a fly's fart in the midst of a tornado. To those looking to play this game, play at your own risk. If you like puzzles... play at your own risk. If you like parodies of Egyptian society... I suppose you'll like this. If you like weird B-movie stories... I guess you'll like this too. But only buy it on discount. I'd never pay the full price for this.

Pros
- Decent voice acting although the accents don't really fit the epoch.
- Nice graphics for the time
- Humorous dialog 
- Show hot-spots tool (hold X on keyboard)
- Supports Full-HD and WUXGA seems to v-sync OK with no tearing.
- There is a basic hint system; you're controlling two characters and if you have one character talk with the other then they will sometimes provide some basic clue or instruction for what you should be doing or focusing on (or you can also press the tab key which will bring up a basic todo list.)
- Subtitles can be disabled for a more immersive experience.
- Plenty of points of interaction with commentary from protagonist. 
- Mostly playable with the mouse although you will need the keyboard to exit/save game as well as use the hot-spot reveal tool.

Cons
- Left mouse button is for observation and right mouse button is for action which is opposite of pretty much every other point and click adventure game.
- While the voice acting is good some of the lines especially from the main character (Assil) are recorded at a really low volume. Other lines are too loud. 
- When there is a dialogue scene the game tries to go for a dept of field kind of a effect but it just makes everything look blurry (edit: you can disable this annoying effect by turning off "Full Screen Effects" in the settings.)
- Lots of backtracking for puzzle solving and the various animated sequences are mostly un-skippable

Overall its not bad, but does have a lot of annoyances. Might be worth it on sale if you like this genre.

This game gets a thumbs up from me but barely. It's a decent little point and click adventure that was actually rated pretty highly during its time by the German gaming press but does not hold up particularly well.

Let's start with the pros though:

- It's not too long and can be finished in well under 10 hours
- The game is usually heavily discounted on Steam and can be had for about a dollar at times
- It finally has on option to highlight objects on screen (press X)

Now for some of the negative:

- The story is a direct continuation of the previous game and will make even less sense if you haven't played that one already
- But even then, it doesn't make a whole lot of sense and some puzzles seems to be there just for the sake of having them
- It's not as funny as it thinks it is - most of the jokes fell flat for me
- The puzzles are hit and miss, they are either painfully obvious and trivial or rather obscure and convoluted 
- Game tends to just quit when you try to switch back to it from ALT+TAB - so save often!
- The accents from the voice cast are all over the place and don't make a whole lot of sense
- They make a big deal of being able to switch between characters early on, but only use it in the first chapter and then never again. The switch to Thara at the end does not count as you can't switch back to Assil at that point.

This seems like a lot of negative and yes, mechanically the game isn't great. It's a decent game though if you liked the first one or (German) point and click adventures from that era.

Das Spiel ist mittelprächtig.

Das Spiel ist der dritte Teil der Serie um den Held Assil im alten Ägypten.

Fortsetzungen gelingt es ja nicht immer, die Höhe der vorhergehenden Titel zu halten und so ergeht es uns auch mit Ankh 3.

Assil und Thara sind nun ein harmonisches Paar, bissige Seitenhiebe sind passé. Nur das Ankh, der heimliche Held dieses Spiels, hält die Fahne des bösen Humors aufrecht. Dabei gibt es Momente, wo ich wirklich auch mal schmunzeln oder lachen konnte, aber es war selten.

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=917891130

Das Spiel beginnt ermüdend langweilig. Erst ab dem 3. Level (von insgesamt 8) ging es richtig los. Die Götter entpuppen sich als gelangweilte Gruppe von Snobs, die in eine Art Luxushotel residieren. Es wird aber viel zu wenig aus dieser Idee gemacht.

Die Geschichte ist entsprechend ziemlich flach, trotz des bombastischen Titels. Immerhin wird aber ein altägyptischer Mythos neu und spaßig interpretiert. Der Kampf der Götter erweist sich aber im Grunde als ein Wettkampf zwischen dem Ankh und Seth, der nach anfänglichen Herausforderungen dann überraschend schnell beendet werden kann.

Wir begegnen fast allen Bekannten aus Ankh 2 wieder, was vielleicht witzig gemeint, aber nicht sonderlich witzig war. Die Figur der Mumie hat mir dabei noch am besten gefallen.

Typisch für ein Point & Click muss man Objekte einsammeln, kombinieren und an der richtigen Stelle einsetzen. Dabei waren einige Kombinationen und Verwendungsmöglichkeiten etwas oder ziemlich unlogisch und abweigig.

Andere Arten von Rätseln gab es fast nicht. Manchmal musste man den Gesprächspartnern gewisse Dinge entlocken, indem man die richtigen Fragen stellt (die waren gut) oder die richtigen Antworten gibt (1 Mal und das war schlecht). Aber ansonsten habe ich keine Rätsel bemerkt, keine Minispiele oder ähnliches. Bei mancher Gelegenheit hatte ich das Gefühl, als wäre etwas geplant gewesen (weil man zwei Rezepte einsammelt), das man dann weggelassen hat.

Auch das Rätsel (das man schon aus Ankh 2 kennt), überrede x Personen, an Assil/Ankh zu glauben, wurde dermaßen simplifiziert, dass es traurig ist.

Toll fand ich (von der Idee her) das Rätsel mit dem Escher-artigen Irrgarten, auch wenn es dann relativ leicht zu lösen war.

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=917892053

Die zu Beginn des Spiels eingeführte Möglichkeit, zwischen Assil und Thara zu wechseln wurde tatsächlich nur in Level 1 und 2 verwendet und nur ein einziges Mal wirklich gebraucht! Das finde ich enttäuschender als wenn sie die Möglichkeit gar nicht angeboten hätten.

Insgesamt bietet das Spiel also gänzlich durchschnittliche Rätselkost. Einige Objekte sind schwer zu finden, aber es gibt eine Taste, mit der man sich interaktive Objekte anzeigen lassen kann. Allenfalls einige abwegige Lösungen können einen manchmal zu einer Lösungshilfe greifen lassen.

Die Spielzeit wird dann kaum mehr als 8 Stunden betragen.

Die Grafik ist ähnlich der der Vorgänger der Serie, mit dem typischen Comic-Stil.

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=917891461

Ich kannte Ankh 1 und 2 mit deutscher Synchornisation, die mir sehr gut vorkam. Insofern fand ich die englische Vertonung von Ankh 3 etwas enttäuschend.

Die Bedienung des Spieles ist genreüblich, allerdings muss jedes Objekt nach jedem Versuch erneut aus dem links oben angezeigten Inventar geholt werden, was Trial-and-Error-Passagen etwas umständlich machen. Gespräche und Zwischensequenzen lassen sich überspringen.

Ich hatte keine Probleme, das Spiel unter Windows 10 zu spielen.

Pro & Contra:

+ Einige witzige Figuren, Unterhaltungen, Situationen
+ Einige vernünftige Rätsel/Lösungen

o Uninspirierte Geschichte

- Einige abwegige und unlogische Lösungen für Rätsel
- Zu wenig Tiefe, was Rätsel und Geschichte angeht

Wertung: 06/10

Can I just say how odd it is that Ankh 2 and 3 have such epic-sounding titles, but are reduced to nothing more than standard puzzle solving with heavily-skewed logic and tons of stiff, dry humor. To be honest, in some respects  I like Ankh 3 more than Ankh 2. What about Ankh 1, you may ask? I've personally had enough to do with these games that I have no desire to see how it all started. Why do I like Ankh 3 more than Ankh 2? Probably only one reason- the worlds are more colorfully and creatively designed. They're prettier to look at. But Ankh 3 does about everything else worse than Ankh 2. The story is cluttered and messy, with tons of ideas picked up then dropped (you get drunk and have a random dream of shooting a chicken out of rocket launcher that has no context, no build up for the story, and no humor to it). The puzzles are even more incredibly strange and painful to solve because they make no bloody sense. The new voice actors are leagues worse than those of Ankh 2. And, as I complained in Ankh 2, Ankh 3 relies too much on it's predecessors. 

It doesn't make any self-aware game jokes like Ankh 2, but there are a lot of reoccuring characters and ideas brought up you'll have no idea of what they are unless you've played at least Ankh 2. And the story tries to take all these silly shenanigans and cliche humor (especially from the ankh. Yeah, it can talk in this one and I hate the bloody thing. I forgot why it was so damn important halfway through the game, and just wanted to toss it), and make it seem big, climactic and important but seeing where everything was built off of, I had no reason to think anything like that.

TL;DR: If Age of Empires and Warcraft III had a high-functioning special-needs child, it would be BC Kings. 

BC Kings is a very mediocre RTS. Gameplay-wise, it looks like Warcraft III but uses most of Age of Empires II’s mechanics; even using a lot of that game’s sound effects. Players build a base and either destroy the enemy base or accomplish other objectives in the campaign. Units have different niches and there’s a wide-variety of resource types, but the game is not entirely balanced so it’s easy to just cheese a handful of units to win most games. Flying units, ranged units, spearmen, and a handful of fast-moving units are all you need to beat most levels so long as they’re available. 

The campaign, to its credit, offers a variety of different scenarios (like a Stone-Age D-Day invasion level) and can be creative when it comes to mission design. There’s even a level where you can take control of a single character from the 3rd person and essentially play a mini-RPG. Otherwise, the story and setting are ridiculous to a self-aware point and it’s nothing too special.
 
The game’s soundtrack is repetitive and it sounds like the developers took a bunch of generic-sounding “ancient” music rejected from previous media to throw into the game. The rest of the sound effects are alright as many are ripped straight from AOE. 

The graphics are also mediocre. They look like a fuzzy, stutter-y WC III clone are very outdated for 2008. Even so, the blood and gore effects are alright. 

Overall, this game has its moments and I’ll give it props for being unique and featuring interesting mechanics; like its sub-map feature where each mission has multiple maps players can explore. It takes place in an underexplored time-period and it’s very tongue-in-cheek. The game likes to crash when switching between maps or loading up sometimes, but I haven’t had the serious issues others have had on Windows 11. If you want to try an obscure, cheap RTS, it has enough to keep you entertained. Otherwise, skip this title if you want to play a real RTS.

BC Kings developed by Mascot Entertainment and published by Strategy First is a prehistoric-themed real-time strategy title that attempts to merge traditional base-building mechanics with light role-playing elements and a narrative-driven campaign. Set in a fantastical version of the Stone Age, the game follows the journey of Mradin, a tribal hero seeking to reclaim his homeland while uncovering secrets tied to ancient myths and rival factions. The premise alone distinguishes it from many other RTS titles of its era, replacing medieval castles or futuristic battlefields with primitive settlements, mystical creatures, and stylized tribal warfare.

At its foundation, the game adheres to recognizable real-time strategy conventions. Players gather resources, construct buildings, train units, and expand territory while preparing for confrontation with enemy tribes. The economic loop revolves around collecting essential materials that fuel construction and technological advancement. A broad tech tree allows access to numerous upgrades and specialized units, encouraging strategic diversity in army composition. Over sixty unit types and dozens of structures provide a sense of scale, even if not all options feel equally viable in practice. Magic abilities and special powers introduce additional tactical considerations, allowing players to influence battles beyond raw numbers alone.

What sets BC Kings apart is its attempt to incorporate adventure-style progression into the RTS formula. The campaign features a series of story-driven missions interwoven with optional side quests that reward Shell-coins, a currency used to enhance hero abilities and statistics. This system gives players an incentive to explore maps more thoroughly rather than rushing primary objectives. The narrative unfolds through in-game sequences and dialogue exchanges, lending the experience a semi-episodic structure that emphasizes character development. While the storytelling is relatively straightforward and occasionally simplistic, it provides a framework that makes the campaign feel more cohesive than a collection of disconnected skirmishes.

Mission design varies between standard base-defense or elimination scenarios and more experimental objectives that require puzzle-solving or specific tactical maneuvers. Some maps emphasize terrain awareness, rewarding players who exploit chokepoints or hidden paths. Others introduce scripted events that shift the battlefield unexpectedly. These variations prevent the campaign from feeling entirely repetitive, though pacing can fluctuate depending on mission length and objective clarity. Certain scenarios may feel drawn out, particularly when economic buildup becomes slow or when AI opposition lacks dynamic adaptability.

Visually, the game reflects its late-2000s origins. Character models and environmental textures are modest by modern standards, with simple animations and interface layouts characteristic of the era. The prehistoric fantasy aesthetic, however, gives the world a distinct flavor, combining tribal motifs with mythical elements. Settlements are constructed from wood, stone, and bone, and units are equipped with primitive weaponry that reinforces the thematic identity. While not technically impressive today, the art direction captures a certain charm rooted in its unique setting.

Combat operates through standard RTS mechanics, with units engaging automatically once in range. Tactical depth comes from balancing melee and ranged forces, managing spell usage, and positioning troops effectively. Hero characters serve as focal points on the battlefield, offering stronger abilities and upgrade potential compared to standard units. However, unit responsiveness and pathfinding can occasionally feel clunky, revealing some of the game’s mechanical limitations. Enemy AI ranges from manageable to predictable, meaning experienced strategy players may find the challenge uneven.

Multiplayer functionality is included but has largely faded into obscurity due to limited active participation in recent years. As a result, the game functions primarily as a single-player experience today. Its longevity depends on players’ interest in revisiting classic RTS structures rather than competitive online play.

Ultimately, BC Kings stands as a distinctive but imperfect entry in the strategy genre. Its fusion of base-building, light RPG mechanics, and prehistoric fantasy worldbuilding demonstrates creative ambition, even if execution does not always match its conceptual scope. While its dated visuals, occasional balance issues, and mechanical roughness may deter players accustomed to modern RTS polish, it retains appeal for those curious about lesser-known strategy experiments from its era. For enthusiasts willing to embrace its quirks and appreciate its narrative-driven campaign structure, it offers a nostalgic journey into a uniquely themed battlefield shaped by tribal warfare and mythic undertones.

Rating: 6/10

BC Kings — это мобильная стратегическая игра, которая сочетает элементы карточных и тактических боёв в фэнтезийном мире. Игра позволяет игрокам создавать и развивать свою армию, захватывать территории и сражаться с другими игроками или ИИ в реальном времени.

Основные особенности:
Геймплей:
В BC Kings основная механика строится на коллекционировании и использовании карт-юнитов — героев, существ и заклинаний. Игроки собирают коллекцию карт, формируют мощные Deck-и, и ведут сражения на тактической карте, выбирая правильную стратегию для победы.

Стратегия и тактика:
Благодаря системе карточных боёв и разным классам юнитов, игроки могут разрабатывать тактики, учитывать слабости врага и учитывать различные ситуации на поле боя.

Развитие и прогрессия:
Игровой процесс включает построение базы, развитие ресурсов и усиление юнитов. Есть система уровней, улучшений и открытий новых карт и возможностей.

Многопользовательский режим:
Есть режим PvP, где можно сразиться с реальными противниками со всего мира. Также доступны кланы и события, объединяющие игроков и стимулирующие соревновательный дух.

Графика и дизайн:
Визуал — яркий, мультяшный стиль с привлекательными моделями героев и красивыми анимациями боя.

Что интересно:
Глубина стратегического выбора благодаря разнообразию карт и тактик.
Возможность коллекционировать новых героев, улучшать их.
Простая механика, подходящая для мобильных устройств.
Регулярные события и обновления, добавляющие новые возможности.
Минусы:
Иногда бывает важна фарминг и донат для быстрого прогресса.
Может казаться сложной для новичков из-за богатства карт и стратегий.
Многопользовательский аспект требует хорошего интернет-соединения.
Итог:
BC Kings — это привлекательная карточная стратегическая игра для мобильных устройств, сочетающая элементы коллекционирования, тактики и PvP-сражений. Игра понравится тем, кто любит разрабатывать стратегии, собирать уникальных героев и соревноваться в реальном времени.
Игра отлично запускается в Linux (через Proton). Моя детская игра, все удовольствия и эмоции от игры сохранены. Я доволен.

BC Kings is an ancient game from 2008.  It's a whopping 16 years old at the time of this review.  The game lacks support for any modern gaming display resolutions (or widescreen monitors), hasn't been modernised or updated to run smoothly on modern gaming PCs.  Despite this lack of modernisation, it carries a pretty high price tag for such an ancient game.  This seems to have been put on Steam as a nostalgia gouge, or just a cash grab to try profit from abandonware.

As a matter of fact for me (and for some other gamers, as the discussion forum shows), the game is broken for many players and is likely to not work at all.  When launching into any missions, the game crashes to desktop immediately for me.  So if you do buy this game, be warned there's a good chance it might not even work. 

The game itself is a lame ripoff of Warcraft 3, only awful.  There's a badly done caveman skin slapped over it, in case that's a more interesting genre than ripping off Tolkien like Blizzard did.  Anyway, zero points to Gryffindor for such a lame premise for a game. 

The game only displays in 4:3 aspect ratio (although you can force it to a 16:9 stretched resolution... which looks even worse), due to the age of the game, it predates the 16:9 widescreen gaming standard established back in 2006.  It's possible they're marketing this towards people using an old CRT they found in a dumpster, or this game is being specifically marketed towards people gaming on PC's from 1995... either way, this isn't really acceptable in the modern era of PC gaming.  It's obviously not going to look right on a modern 16:9 gaming display.

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.

Because the game is broken and unplayable for me, it may also not work for other gamers.  This is a solid reason to approach this game with some skepticism.

So, should you buy this game?

BC Kings is relatively expensive for an abandonware nostalgia gouge, at $4 USD, and it's not worth it.  The game is just too old, hasn't been modernised.  And as the old saying goes, you can't go home again.  Even when it was new, this was never a triple-A game.  This is the kind of game that went almost directly from the warehouse into the cheap bargain bins at the front of the shop.  Now, on Steam, without any modernisation?  This is impossible to recommend.  This is also competing with over 11,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.

I will say I played this game when I was a kid so I defiently get a lot of enjoyment from it because of nostalgia. HOWEVER the game itself isn't bad. It has an interesting premise, that being cavemen fighting aliens, so if that sounds interesting to you go ahead, it's fairly cheap and quite fun. The game mechanics are nothing special, just the standard RTS formula. There are some additional mechanics, such as being able to unlock new  weapons and abilities for your heroes, and not by an experience based leveling system, but rather getting points from finishing optional side quests in game, which usually aren't a hassle and revolve mostly around exploration, rather than having to chase around a time limit or such. The graphics are definetly WarCraft 3 inspired and not really the best on a technical level but they're servicable and easily readable (for example the more units are damaged the bloodier they get, or resource points become smaller and smaller the emptier they are).

Overall it's an OK experience, nothing incredible but I mean c'mon, it's a 2008 indie release by a Russian company. For what it is it's a pretty good game, an interesting story and I would definetly recommend it to people who enjoy RTS games.

I found it interesting that the game has sidequests that give you points to improve the hero and weapons of the game.

Ah, [b]BC Kings[/b]... Such a weird title. But not because it's a weird game, or something. It totally isn't. It's pretty generic one, actually. It's just the whole idea is pretty much crazy. The whole story of this game is that one guy [i]really[/i] wanted to make his own [b]WarCraft[/b]. Or [b]Age of Empires[/b], since this game may look like both of them at the same time. Anyway, that's why [b]BC Kings[/b] is so strange. It's pretty much a story about [b]Marcell Baranyai[/b] making his own old school [b]RTS[/b] in late [b]2000[/b]s.


What's so weird about it? Well... think about it. [b]RTS[/b] isn't an easy thing to make. It's not like one of those [b]Hidden Objects[/b] games, or something like that. Not one of those types of games that you can mass produce without putting too much effort into it. You need to make a proper [b]AI[/b], you need to make interesting missions, you need to balance things out... It's a pretty complicated process, really. And here we have one person doing all of it. Man, [b]Mr. Baranyai[/b] even did part of [b]3D[/b] graphics and voiced all of the characters! How cool is that? The guy literally made most of the stuff all alone here! You may expect him and his game to suck, thanks to that, but the funnies thing is – [b]BC Kings[/b] is actually pretty cool. No, really, screenshots may look poor, but it's actually a pretty solid [b]RTS[/b] title. If you like the genre and have nothing new to play on your radar, you should probably check this one out. It has everything that you enjoy in such games and all that actually [i]works[/i]. Which is a [i]huge[/i] success for one person.

The problem is, as you may guess, this game can't really compete. Even with much older titles that actually had more people and bigger budget behind them. Any years old [b]RTS[/b] can easily destroy this one. Not because this one is bad. But because... it has nothing special about it. It's just your generic something without its own face. It copies every single aspect of the big games like [b]WarCraft[/b], or [b]Age of Empires[/b] series and doesn't really add anything new to the formula. Aside from prehistorical setting that is. Which also doesn't feel that good thanks to a lot of [i]really[/i] stupid humor ([spoiler]aliens and “[i]I'm your father[/i]” jokes included[/spoiler]). So... why? Why trying to make something that was already made in a much better way? I guess it's just because [b]Marcell Baranyai[/b] just [i]wanted[/i] to make something like that. Like he played all those awesome games from the past and wanted to make his own. But... even though [i]technically[/i] he succeed, [b]BC Kings[/b] isn't something you recommend to everybody. It's a very niche product for hardcore [b]RTS[/b] players, who already played every other [b]RTS[/b] out there and still want something they didn't play before.

For many people this title may deserve a downvote. It looks dated, it feels dated, it has literally nothing new in it, it comes with a lot of copy / pasted concepts from the popular [b]RTS[/b] titles (at some points it feels [i]exactly[/i] like poor man's [b]WarCraft III[/b]), while story is just stupid and not really fun. So... yeah, I can see the reason for all those negative reviews. In their own way they're actually right. And still, I don't want to give this game a negative review. Not only because it's a big success for its maker, who put a lot of hard work into it. But because it actually works pretty well. If you don't mind dated graphics, generic gameplay and poor humor, you totally [i]can[/i] enjoy it for what it is. Like you can enjoy cheap bubble gum. You won't want to chew it for long and you certainly won't want to return to it, but... it won't hurt you to enjoy it for some time. If you're an old school [b]RTS[/b] fan with a free weekend... It may actually be pretty enjoyable experience. Technically, it [i]is[/i] a poor man's [b]WarCraft III[/b], but... who said it can't be enjoyable at all? The price is just right after all.

На первый взгляд, BC Kings - посредственная и неинтересная RTS, сделанная чуть ли ни одним человеком. Так думал я в начале, а потом мне нравилось всё больше и больше. Не поймите меня неправильно, BC Kings средняя стратегия, но в ней есть некоторые интересные вещи, которые цепляют.

Сюжет - полный рандом. На землю падает некий метеорит, который приносит за собой здоровую красную голову и армию мутантов. Они начинают кровопролитную войну с неандертальцами, а учитывая баланс сторон, ещё и равную.  Главными героями являются Мрадин и Гезник (Гейзник, Гишик, Гешик, whatever) - люди племени Укха, которые готовы дать отпор мутантам(и не только им). Основная цель кампании - дойти до главного лагеря, перегруппироваться и нанести смертельный удар главе мутантов. Казалось бы, куда абсурднее, но под конец происходит столько рандомных неожиданных поворотов, что уровень этой самой абсурдности достигает своего максимума. Снежный человек, уровень в аду, последняя миссия вообще в этом плане переплёвывает всё. Озвучки в кампании нет, а русский язык в игре сломан, так что надо играть на английском, благо там всё понятно и легко, никогда не было затруднений в понимании происходящего.
 
По геймплею всё просто, ибо это RTS аля Warcraft 2. Две расы (Неандертальцы и Мутанты), которые отличаются лишь модельками и ресурсами, коих пять видов: дерево, камень, кости динозавров, еда для людей и какая-то кислота для мутантов. Если на карте нет какого-то определённого ресурса, то можно построить специальные мельницы, которые перабатывает одни ресурсы в другие. Также в кампании есть прокачка героев за монетки, которые зарабатываешь проходя квесты или просто находишь на карте. Одну такую я подобрать не смог, ибо она находилась на островке, на который нельзя было высадиться, так как транспортный корабль почему-то не видел берег. Прокачка героев сводится к оружию для Мрадина, а ещё здоровью, регенерации, броне, силе удара и скорости удара для обоих героев. Карта в кампании обычно делится на несколько уровней, что несомненно плюс к разнообразию, но есть одна проблема. Если перейти в другую локацию во время какого-то исследования, игра может вылететь. Благо по умолчанию автосейв каждые три минуты, так что не особо бесило.

Три уровня развития главного здания. Чтобы защищать свою базу от нападок, кроме стен ещё можно строить башни. Причём в каждой из них можно поселить пятерых стрелков, из-за чего они становятся очень мощными. Также есть какая-то ловушка, которую я никогда не использовал.

Нужно строить дома, чтобы увеличить численность населения (+7 каждый). Из военных построек есть казармы, питомник, мастерская и священное место (у мутантов какое-то другое название, ну суть та же). В казарме можно нанимать обычных воинов и стрелков, а позже и усиленных. В питомнике есть два типа быстрых наземных юнитов, которые почти не различаются, ибо второй просто усиленная версия первого, а ещё убер имбовых летающих юнитов. В мастерской можно нанимать катапульты (жирный камнемётчик на телеге у мутантов) и копейщиков, которые могут оседлать мамонтов(мутантских животных у мутантов) и стать достаточно сильными. Также там можно купить уже готовых наездников, но это достаточно дорого. В священном месте продаются лечащие юниты, которых можно научить кастовать различные заклинания. Также есть порт, в котором продаются транспортный и боевой корабль. 

В плане боёв всё слишком просто. Минимум тактики, максимум раша. Максимальное число войск, которое можно выделить, равно тридцати шести. Создаёшь 36 воинов ближнего боя, 36 стрелков, 5 катапульт и на всякий случай 5 медиков - ты почти победитель. Это канонично именно для кампании. А если ты играешь в обычную игру ради победы, а не ради интереса, то можешь просто создать 36+ или больше тех самых летающих юнитов и игра почти закончена, ибо они нереально имбовые. Стоят копейки (150 пищи), бьют очень больно, а сбить их могут только стрелки, башни и другие летающие юниты. Совсем не интересная, но очень действенная тактика. Мне  больше нравится создавать наземных юнитов и биться ими, но есть небольшая проблема - они постоянно застревают друг в друге. Из-за этого очень неудобно контролировать армию на узких участках и коридорах. 

Из интересного ещё стоит отметить уровень, который можно пройти в режиме мясного шутера от третьего лица. Это было неожиданно и круто. 
Подводя итог, хочу сказать, что игра средняя, но на мой скромный взгляд достойная внимания фанатам RTS. Забавный сеттинг, не менее забавный сюжет, сбалансированные расы с ужасными летающими юнитами, интересные фичи типа многоуровневых локаций и шутера. В целом интересная, но достаточно проходная стратегия.

Tut mir echt weh, das schreiben zu müssen, aber für mich ist der Teil einfach unspielbar. 

Das Übersichtsfenster bei den Kämpfen ist viel zu klein, man muss Schiffe erst kennzeichnen, die Konvois finde ich für die Stufe "einfach" als viel zu stark, die Duelle sind einfach unnötig und viel zu schwer (besiegt ist besiegt!); Piratenorte muss man erst mühselig ausfindig machen, anstatt dass in nem Steckbrief der letzte Aufenthaltsort angegeben wird; das Geld geht bei Fahrten viel zu schnell flöten (war dauernd im minus) und konnte dann nicht mal reparieren, Crews und Kanonen muss man teils wochenlang zusammensuchen. 

Und das für mich wirklich allerletzte: Schiffe sieht erst man wenn sie eine Länge entfernt sind und wenn man ausweicht kann man trotzdem alles verlieren und wenn man bei Kämpfen flieht hat man automatisch verloren. Das ist alles total unlogisch und macht es teilweise fast unmöglich Schiffe zu finden//zu attackieren oder an feindlichen Städten vorbeizukommen. Als ich im Szenario den ersten Piraten vernichten musste bin ich mehr als 10!! Minuten im Kreis gefahren weil ich ihn nicht angreifen konnte. 

Im Hollandszenario als man die Städte annektieren musste hat vor allem das dazu geführt dass ich die Frist nicht einhalten konnte und dann einfach verloren hatte. Da hätte man auf der Stufe einfach auch nochmal mehr Zeit geben können, zumal der Rangaufstieg um an Geld zu kommen ewig dauert wenn man Feinde so schwer angreifen und besiegen kann. Und falls man es doch schafft, will der Gegner ein Duell. 

Kurzum: Gute Idee, aber völlig schwachsinnig umgesetzt von den Entwicklern. Ich würde mich in Grund und Boden schämen, so nen Stuss zu veröffentlichen und dafür noch Geld zu verlangen. Und dass sage ich als jemand der die gesamte Tropicoreihe komplett abgeschlossen hat und schon 20 Jahre Erfahrung in dem Genre hat. 

Fazit: Mangelhaft, durchgefallen.

Порт Рояль 2 - это игра из той эпохи когда даже стратегии были с душой, а не просто клепались что бы срубить бабла.
В данном случаи имеем прекрасный пример захватывающей стратегии которая остается ЛУЧШЕЙ в серии не смотря на выход более новых частей. Сюда же добавляем постоянную вражду между государствами которая влияет на экономику и ваш торговый успех. Ну и так же нельзя не упомянуть про очень годно сделанные морские бои, захваты земель и даже строительство и развитие собственных колоний.

Port Royal 2 – Идеальный олдскульный таймкиллер с продуманным геймплеем

Провел десятки часов в этом морском стратегическом симуляторе – и до сих пор возвращаюсь! Если вы любите классику жанра без лишних наворотов, но с глубиной, эта игра – для вас.

Почему Port Royal 2 до сих пор актуален:
Олдскульный шарм – простая графика, понятный интерфейс и ностальгическая атмосфера морских приключений. Никаких микротранзакций, только чистая стратегия!

Простота и глубина – легко начать (купи корабль, торгуй, воюй), но сложно освоить. Нужно балансировать между торговлей, пиратством и выполнением миссий.

Продуманная экономика – цены на товары меняются, спрос зависит от города, а пираты не дремлют. Каждое решение имеет последствия!

Недостатки (но они почти милые):
Графика устарела – если ждёте 4К-текстур, это не сюда. Но стиль есть стиль!

Иногда слишком уж хаотично – когда все пираты Карибов решают напасть на вас разом, это… стрессово.

Нет мультиплеера – но зато можно бесконечно покорять Карибы в одиночку.

Итог: 9/10 – отличная игра для тех, кто ценит проверенную временем стратегию без лишней мишуры. Если хотите почувствовать себя капитаном эпохи парусов – это ваш выбор!

P.S. Совет: начните с торговли ромом – это прибыльно и весело. А потом купите фрегат и станьте грозой морей!

Эта игра, как старый непутевый друг, который вернулся, чтобы поклянчить у тебя пару соток. Техническое состояние ужасное, интерфейс издевательский, что подкашивает не самое приятное управление ещё больше. Но потом, ты вспоминаешь, каким приятным сюрпризом оказалась игра, которая не имеет к ужасному фильму, оскорбляющему участников реальных событий, почти никакого отношения, и рука тянется к кошельку. На данную тематику очень мало игр, а эта, несмотря на все огрехи, все таки достаточно интересная. Если просто - это "В тылу врага", но в сеттинге войны в Афганистане. Но тут не получится отснайперить одним юнитом роту врагов или одной коробочкой прочистить всю карту. Ландшафт вносит свои коррективы, техника сильный козырь, но потерять ты можешь его за одно мгновение, а личный состав строго ограничен и его учишься беречь (последнее особенно тяжело - ИИ крайне любит выставить солдата в полный рост под кинжальный огонь). Хотя последнее, даже придает определённой остринки и можно списать на панику и человеческий фактор - давай, спасай раненных. Не твоя вина, что они появились, но делать что-то надо. Неоднозначный, но запавший в душу проект.

Its full of bugs but I'm surprised this game got localization patches in 2024. It's basically a retail total conversion mod for Men of War. Its innately kind of novel for being about the Soviet-Afghan War which almost never gets representation in media outside of Russia. This game also has a memorial tab dedicated to real soviet soldiers so I guess that sums up the politics of this game. Its also an adaptation of a fictional film of the same name. 

It has cool skeumorphic UI. Thats nice. All the character voices are in Russian. The graphics are definitely dated and the models and environments do not look so good up close on the highest settings, but could be worse. 

Save often, because this game is brutal even on the easiest difficulty. Enemies with RPGs will very quickly destroy APCs and Tanks and some of the mission objectives are innately deceptive and playing aggressively is an easy way to lose everything fast. If you get yourself in a bad position it is very hard to correct your mistake. This is one of THE MOST PUNISHING and unfair singleplayer RTT games I have played. I don't blame people for savescumming in this game because of the sheer amount of trial and error torture present in this. 

Mine CLEARING is NOT FUN because instead of having a GROUPED MINEFIELD you have to CLEAN dozens of MINES individually and SOMETIMES THEY randomly explode and this process can take MINUTES to clear whole strips of ROAD. Yeah F you too. 

The pathfinding for vehicles is broken and they constantly get stuck on things, so you spend much time just trying to get things unstuck and these problems are as obvious as encountering the bulk of them in the first mission. Which is painstakingly frustrating. 

It also plays the Soviet Union national anthem when you win a mission.

DO NOT RECOMMEND. Not even for fans of the Soviet-Afghan war, you guys deserve better than this.  Too punishing, too clunky, you babysit vehicles. The Pause-Plan mode doesn't allow you to do anything useful. I guess this game really does encapsulate the real torture of the actual war.

Developed by Lesta Studio and Новый Диск and published by Strategy First, 9th Company: Roots of Terror is a real-time strategy game that draws heavily from the Soviet-Afghan War, placing players in the role of Soviet paratroopers during one of the conflict's most recognizable military operations. Instead of creating a fictional war story, the game attempts to capture the harsh realities of combat by following soldiers from their demanding military training through the fierce battles that culminate in the defense of a strategically important mountain position. This historical backdrop gives the campaign a more serious tone, focusing on discipline, survival, and tactical planning rather than larger-than-life action.

The campaign unfolds across a series of interconnected operations that allow players to select missions from an operational map before engaging in tactical combat. Each mission introduces different objectives, environments, and enemy situations, preventing the experience from becoming repetitive. Success depends on understanding the strengths and weaknesses of a wide roster of military units, with more than eighty unit types available throughout the game. Infantry squads, armored vehicles, and support elements each play distinct roles, encouraging players to think carefully about positioning, reconnaissance, and coordinated attacks instead of relying on overwhelming force. The progression system also rewards preserving experienced troops, giving veteran units greater value as the campaign advances.

One of the game's strongest qualities is its emphasis on realism. Morale has a direct influence on battlefield performance, meaning soldiers under intense fire can panic or become less effective if poorly managed. Vehicles feature localized damage, making careful targeting an important tactical consideration rather than simply reducing enemy health bars. Environmental destruction and detailed battlefields further contribute to the sense of immersion, with explosions and collapsing structures helping battles feel dynamic despite the game's age. While the graphics are unmistakably from an earlier generation of PC gaming, the rugged mountain landscapes and military equipment still succeed in conveying the difficult conditions faced by soldiers operating in Afghanistan.

The gameplay is rewarding for players who appreciate deliberate strategy, but it also carries several frustrations that reflect its era. The interface can feel cumbersome until players become familiar with its controls, and unit pathfinding occasionally struggles in complicated terrain. Certain missions are significantly more difficult than others, sometimes requiring repeated attempts and careful resource management to overcome. These challenges can be satisfying for experienced strategy fans, yet newcomers may find the learning curve intimidating. Technical issues on modern hardware may also require minor adjustments, although the core tactical experience remains intact once everything is running smoothly.

What ultimately separates 9th Company: Roots of Terror from many military strategy games is its commitment to recreating a historical conflict with a focus on tactical authenticity instead of spectacle. Every mission reinforces the importance of planning, maintaining troop morale, and making thoughtful battlefield decisions under pressure. The campaign successfully creates the feeling of participating in a larger military operation while allowing individual engagements to remain tense and meaningful. Although its aging presentation, dated interface, and occasional technical shortcomings prevent it from matching more modern strategy titles, its solid mechanics and historical foundation still make it a worthwhile experience for players interested in realistic real-time strategy games and military history.

Once I got over the camera issues and slow start, this was one of the best RTS campaigns I ever played.

Before each mission, the game lists all the men you've gotten killed so far in the campaign, with respective name, skills and medals. That small touch really changed my perspective on taking casualties throughout the story (plus there's a bonus mission for keeping certain soldiers alive until the end).

Overall it's a simple but quite tactically rich game, the missions are diverse and well designed. I particularly enjoyed how vital scouting is when attacking or patrolling, as enemy ambushes and strong points will wipe out your whole platoon in seconds.

Ammo management also provided some cinematic moments: in "last stands" your men end up having to share their last mags among themselves. A few times I had to send a guy crawling through hell to grab a few mags from enemy bodies and bring it back to share with everyone. Good stuff.

So this is perhaps the only movie tie in game which is better than its movie. Deserves a remake.

[h2]📜Описание[/h2]
[b]«9 рота»[/b] — это RTS, выпущенная в 2008 году по мотивам одноимённого фильма Фёдора Бондарчука. Игра рассказывает о реальных событиях: 8 января 1988 года 9-я рота 345-го гвардейского воздушно-десантного полка попала в окружение на высоте 3234 и в течение двух дней сдерживала атаки четырёхсот моджахедов и пакистанских наёмников. Из 39 человек шестеро погибли, 28 были ранены, двое посмертно стали Героями Советского Союза. В игре вам предстоит пройти путь от новобранца в Ферганской долине до участия в той самой битве. Поддержка русского языка есть, причём аутентичная — с матом, дедовщиной и прочими армейскими прелестями. Стратегия нелинейная, с двумя тактическими уровнями, более 80 типов юнитов и системой боевого духа, от которой у вас самого дух захватывает.

[h2]🎨Графика и звук[/h2]
Графика на момент выхода была очень приличной, сейчас — ностальгическая. 3D-модели техники и солдат детализированы, окружение проработано: горы, кишлаки, ущелья. Физика разрушений — отдельный вид кайфа: здания складываются, техника взрывается, «Град» выносит всё, включая надежду на победу. Анимация боя реалистичная — солдаты падают, перебегают, перезаряжают. Звук — главное достоинство. Аутентичные звуки выстрелов, взрывов, крики «Аллах акбар!» и «Духи!» создают полный эффект присутствия . Музыкальная тема из фильма узнаваема и добавляет пафоса. Озвучка русская, живая, с характерными для армии выражениями. Боевой дух солдат влияет на их эффективность, и вы это слышите: когда дух низкий, они ноют и стреляют в молоко. Плюс: атмосфера через звук передана великолепно. Минус: графика, конечно, устарела, но для фанатов это часть шарма.

[h2]🎮Геймплей[/h2]
Игра сочетает два тактических уровня: карта операций (глобальная стратегия выбора миссий) и тактические карты, где вы непосредственно управляете войсками. Миссии нелинейны — можно выбирать, куда идти, какие задания выполнять. У вас есть отряд, который набирается опыта с каждой битвой: выжившие становятся элитными солдатами, терять их жалко, а терять приходится. Управление — классическое для RTS: выделил, кликнул, отправил. Но есть нюансы: система боевого духа работает жёстко — если солдат долго обстреливают или видят павших товарищей, они могут побежать. Приходится использовать командиров для поднятия духа. Механика расчёта повреждений реалистичная: один выстрел из гранатомёта может уничтожить БТР, а пулемётная очередь — скосить отделение. Более 80 типов юнитов: от «вертушек» до «духов» с «стингерами». Миссии сложные, без сохранения в бою — можно потерять час прогресса, если не сохранились на карте операций. 

[h2]📖Сюжет и атмосфера[/h2]
Сюжет следует за фильмом, но добавляет игровую свободу. Начинается всё в учебке в Фергане: дедовщина, муштра, привыкание к мысли, что ты теперь не человек, а расходный материал. Потом — Афганистан, боевые выходы, и наконец — высота 3234. Атмосфера — тяжёлая, гнетущая, но не без героического пафоса. Игра не романтизирует войну, но и не превращает её в чёрнуху. Диалоги — живые, с чёрным армейским юмором. Черный юмор здесь в том, что даже в игре вы понимаете: ваши солдаты — это не просто юниты, они имеют историю, и когда погибает ветеран нескольких миссий, вы чувствуете это. Игра поднимает тему цены победы: вы выигрываете сражение, но теряете людей. И финальная миссия — это буквально «стоять насмерть», где вы не можете победить, только выжить как можно дольше. И это честно.

[h2]✅Плюсы:[/h2]
[list]
[*] ⭐ Реализм и аутентичность — основано на реальных событиях, детализация техники и быта.
[*] ⭐ Система развития солдат — вы привязываетесь к бойцам, терять их больно.
[*] ⭐ Два тактических уровня и нелинейные миссии — есть выбор и свобода.
[*] ⭐ Отличная озвучка и звук — полное погружение в афганскую атмосферу.

[h2]❌Минусы:[/h2]

[*] ⚠️ ИИ иногда тупит — союзники могут стоять под огнём, а враги — игнорировать очевидные угрозы.
[*] ⚠️ Устаревшая графика — для 2026 года это уже ретро.

[*] ⚠️ Отсутствие системы достижений для истинных коллекционеров прекрасного.
[*] ⚠️ Отсутствуют дополнительные материалы в Steam вроде обоев или карточек.
[/list]

[h2]😈Заключение:[/h2]
[b]«9 рота»[/b] — это честная, жёсткая и душевная RTS для тех, кто помнит фильм, кто уважает историю и кто не боится сложностей. Если вы любите современные стратегии с подсказками и сохранениями каждые пять минут — игра вас сломает. Если вы готовы к вызову, хотите почувствовать себя командиром, отвечающим за жизни своих людей, и готовы переигрывать миссии по десять раз — берите не думая.
