Antes de termos cobertura automática, mira assistida e regeneração de vida como padrão, existia Island Thunder. E meu amigo… que jogo tenso. Se você vacilasse um segundo, tomava um tiro e voltava pro menu principal com humildade. Era na raça, no ouvido, e no binóculo.

Mas vamos ser justos: esse jogo é MUITO antigo. E levando isso em consideração, dá pra dizer que os gráficos e a mecânica eram inovadores e desafiadores pra época. Era o tipo de FPS tático que não segurava sua mão — você precisava planejar, calcular cada passo e ficar atento a cada sombra. A ambientação nas selvas cubanas era densa, tensa e cheia de surpresas (quase todas letais).

Porém, se teve um ponto que incomodou — e não foi pouco — foi a IA do inimigo, que parecia ter um GPS embutido. Você tava atrás de uma pedra, bem escondido, e mesmo assim tomava um tiro cirúrgico de um NPC que nem deveria saber que você existia. O raio de percepção dos inimigos era surreal, e isso quebrava um pouco da imersão. Era mais “Ghost Paranormal Recon” do que “Ghost Recon”.

E falando em desafios, a interface e os controles eram um capítulo à parte. Confusa, travada, cheia de atalhos que pareciam saídos de um teclado alternativo. Sério: quem em sã consciência coloca o botão de recarregar como “Z”? Tudo bem que era outro tempo, mas pô… o “R” é de “Reload”, né? Coerência, Ubisoft!

Apesar desses tropeços, Island Thunder ainda tem seu charme bruto. As operações são sérias, a tensão é real, e completar uma missão sem perder um soldado te dá um orgulho que poucos jogos entregam hoje. Era estratégia acima de tudo — e cada decisão contava.

Recomendo com carinho pra quem viveu essa época ou quer entender como era o tiroteio raiz, sem radar, sem mira automática, e com inimigos que aparentemente tinham visão de raio-x. Island Thunder não era só um jogo, era um teste de nervos… e de paciência com a tecla “Z”.

Lançado como uma expansão de Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon, Island Thunder transposta os jogadores para as selvas e costas de Cuba.

Jogabilidade: segue exatamente o mesmos elementos do jogo base sem adições.
	
Gráficos: seguem exatamente o mesmos elementos do jogo base sem adições.

Conclusão: a expansão do jogo tem o foco em adicionar mais missões e prolongar a jogatina, mas não altera em nada os elementos e a essência do jogo base, dessa forma, mantenho a minha avaliação do jogo base como referência devido ao seu fator histórico.

The games premise is about a fictional war which in hindsight wasn't far from what happened in our real world, where you take control of a team of up to 6 men split up in squads of up to 3 (Alpha, Bravo and Charlie squad. each squad can hold up to 3 members so you can have the teams split up in for example 3,2,1 or 3,3,0 or 2,2,2 or if you feel very brave you can also only take 1 soldier in the field)

Overall the campaign is quite short but varied and completing every bonus objective marked with a X gives you a unique soldier with a special load-out. after your done with the main missions you can hop into firefight, for some re-playable action where you hunt down all enemies on the map on both maps made for the mode and the previous completed campaign maps.

The length of the game was fantastic, the pathing does mess up sometimes, and aimbot through terrain does not return. Enemy placement makes sense for the most part, except maybe in a couple of missions, but it can be forgiven. 

I didn't care about the story in the previous two games. But this one does have an above average narrative, which ties perfectly with the missions presented. Nothing special, but alright.

If you would wish to play only one of the 3 OG Ghost Recon games, I'd say this is the way to go. And yes...they have cutscenes for every mission...I just wanted to mention that for no reason whatsoever

Ahoy fellow gamers and fur-friends! It's Kiba Snowpaw here, your frosty Ice Wolf from a chilling planet, trying to thaw out by warming up to some classic video games. Despite the icicles on my fur, I've been gaming for years! 36+ of them to be exact. 🐾❄️ Gaming is my escape from a loud mind and life's icy hurdles. But let's dive into the world of Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon: Island Thunder. 🕹️

🎮 Background:
Ghost Recon has been around since the good ol’ days of the PS2 and Xbox 360, introducing us to the complex realm of military tactical simulators. Remember Operation Flashpoint? Ah, memories! My buddy Shilka and I used to debate which game was better. But back to Ghost Recon.

🌴 Island Thunder - More than Just a Breeze:
Island Thunder, the final expansion to the original Ghost Recon, feels like the pinnacle of not just Ghost Recon but also tactical FPS games. The AI in this expansion? Woah, sharper than the icicles on my cave's roof! The setting - lush jungles that provide opportunities for strategies, ambushes, and dynamic gameplay. So, why my mixed feelings?

👍 PROS:

    Visual Delight: For a 2002 game, the graphics are surprisingly crisp! Aesthetically pleasing, one might say.
    Strategic Gameplay: It’s not a run-and-gun situation. As a commander, you've got to strategize, think, and be one with your team. Every bullet counts!
    Team Dynamics: Lead up to 3 teams! It's tactical but accessible for newbies.
    Stability: No glitches, crashes, nada! Smooth sailing, or should I say, smooth gaming?
    Content: They've added a sprinkle of new weapons, character models, mission cinematics, and more. Also, enemy variety? Chef's kiss.
    Engagement: The single-player story is immersive, though brief. The community, while sparse, still carries a torch for the game.

👎 CONS:

    Dead Multiplayer: Sad wolf hours! The multiplayer realm is a ghost town. 😔
    Inflexible Mechanics: No jumping?! Come on, sometimes a wolf wants to leap!
    AI Discrepancy: Enemies have eagle eyes, sniping you from distances unseen, while our Ghosts sometimes... well, they can be a bit "derpy".

In-Depth Critique:
Island Thunder takes the beloved Ghost Recon formula and amplifies it, sometimes to its detriment. While the tactical strategy elements remain its strength, the spike in difficulty can be frustrating. More often than not, I found myself bellowing at my screen, "How did they even spot me?!" 😡

But through the lens of a hardcore gamer - there’s beauty in this challenge. The satisfaction of finally completing a mission after countless retries? Unmatched. On the other hand, casual gamers might feel the cold bite of frustration.

Impact & Comparison:
Ghost Recon as a series set a high bar for military sims. Island Thunder, while possessing unique attributes, also carries some of the older games' baggage. Compared to its predecessor, Desert Siege, it's a tad more vexing, but the charm remains intact.

Final Howl:
Ghost Recon: Island Thunder is both a nostalgic trip and a lesson in patience. While the gameplay can test your limits, the satisfaction of victory is pure euphoria. The blend of strategy, realism, and challenge makes it worth the dive. Yet, for some, the learning curve might be a steep, icy slope.

Rating: 🎮🎮🎮🎮 8/10 - A challenging blizzard that'll test your tactical prowess.

Ghost Recon Island Thunder is the second and last expansion pack for Ghost Recon, released in 2002, the same year as the first pack. It adds 8 new missions, some weapons, and additional multiplayer content.

Although I have already reviewed this game together with Desert Siege in the Ghost Recon review, I am writing about it separately here as it is a standalone game. The multiplayer is not very active, so the focus is mainly on single player missions. The expansion adds a few minor changes, such as new enemy units and some additional equipment, but they do not significantly change the gameplay. Players still need to give clear orders to their teams, as units will not act on their own, and missions require careful planning to complete.

Overall, Island Thunder is similar in style to the original game and previous expansions. The missions are structured to provide some challenge, and while the expansion does not introduce major changes, it still provides additional content and a focused single player experience

The second expansion of Ghost Recon. Island Thunder is by far the best one out of the expansions and way better than the original.

I'd say that it is an okay tactical FPS for the price. 

In my opinion underrated ( or should I say overhated? ) . It's not perfect but neither were its predecessors. The main criticism is the AI's behavior not being consistent, that they are either too good or incredibly stupid. But after playing Raven Shield I came to the conclusion that the AI was pretty much the same there too.


There are some things that the game improves though. The briefings are short and straight to the point, that makes the story more comprehensible. To sum it up, it is very similar to other Rainbow Six titles - terrorist organizations attack different parts of the world and the main villain is in possession of a bio weapon. So the gameplay loop is pretty much the same  - stop terrorists, defuse bombs and rescue hostages. This time we are limited to one squad, so only 4 operatives per mission. It's kind of a downgrade for some players, but it's a non-issue for me since I barely used the other squads in the third game. 



Some other improvements are the graphics* and level design. I find it genuinely impressive how clean the game still looks, especially the textures and models. The shadows look good too but sometimes they are buggy and can be seen through walls. Environments look more realistic and have some destructable items. The layouts of the levels are generally linear, but I prefer it that way because there is a sense of progress and more diverse environments ( instead of storming just one main building ).



Some negatives :



- There was no reason to limit the player to be able to control just one character. Yes, Chavez is the squad leader but he doesn't talk and there are no cutscenes. We only hear the guy from the briefing call us by his name, but other than that he feels like another npc. So if you die, it's game over. Kinda challenging but since we can quicksave infinitely, that challenge is undone.

- Guy on the radio ( I don't know his name, he is our superior I think ) needs to shut up. Talking about the mission and directing the team is alright, but no need to tell me that I am wounded or that my teammate is down. Like, I freaking know that, I am literally there in the gunfight. " You are wounded! " I FUCKING KNOW


* note : the screenshots on the store page do not do the game's graphics any justice, it actually looks better than that.

Woah! I knew that most people disliked this game, but I decided to give it a chance anyway and it's terrible.

They removed most of the tactical elements of the previous entries. There is no planning, level design is extremely linear. You cannot even change your teammates. If you die, you lose, you do not get to control the remaining members of your squad. You can still give some commands to your squad, but it's very limited, basically, "go there", "follow me", "stop".

The worst thing about this game is that there are dozens if not hundreds of enemies in every mission and you have very limited ammo for your primary weapon. Unless you take a machine gun, you most likely will run out of ammo. You cannot take enemy weapons laying on the ground either... I guess it is designed in a way that they expect you to change between your primary weapon and your handgun constantly, but it's inconvenient and unfun. Also, half the weapons are useless because they are only situational like shotguns, or grenade launchers. You can only have one primary weapon for an entire mission, so you will not pick a shotgun because there will be many long distance fights.

The A.I. of your teammates is awful, sometimes they do not react if someone is shooting at them, they do not hide or shoot back just wait till they run out of health and die. Their pathfinding is horrible, they commonly tend to get stuck somewhere far away behind.

The grenades. You have to hold the button to increase the distance of your throw, but in no scenario would you want the short weak throw. So you just waste time to make a long throw, and half the time, you are in emergency and these slow throws are just absurd. Even the shortest "quick throw" takes ages, you are likely to be killed by the time you throw a grenade. It's ridiculous.

The game is fundamentally badly designed. Even though the shooting has some fun, the gameplay is barely functional. I have beaten 3 missions and I think it's enough for me to see that the game is unlikely to improve later on.

[h1][b] Reseña de Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Lockdown™[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Lockdown™ es acción táctica en primera persona con vibra militar: entras, planeas (o eso intentas), disparas con “seriedad profesional” y rezas para que tu equipo —o tú— no convierta una operación quirúrgica en un festival de balas perdidas.

La propuesta es clara: un shooter más metódico que el típico “corre y dispara”, con enfoque en tensión, control de espacios y decisiones rápidas. La primera impresión en Steam hoy es… curiosa: es como encontrar un clásico en una vitrina, con 3 personas mirándolo en tiempo real. Sí, 3. Tú, otro valiente, y probablemente un bot con nostalgia.

[h2]Lo Táctico y Lo Que Te Táctica la Paciencia[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
  Acción militar en primera persona con enfoque táctico: menos arcade, más “piensa antes de asomar la cabeza”.  
  Se presta para jugar en serio: el ritmo y el estilo favorecen la coordinación (especialmente en multijugador/cooperativo).  
  Tiene modos para un jugador y multijugador: variedad de intención, aunque no siempre de ejecución.  
  Préstamo familiar: ideal para pasarle la “experiencia” a un amigo y ver si sigue siendo tu amigo después.  

Lo No Tan Bueno:
  Comunidad actual microscópica: 3 jugadores activos… encontrar partida puede sentirse como buscar señal en un sótano.  
  0 logros: Steam te mira y te dice “¿progreso? no conozco ese concepto”.  
  En un juego táctico, el multijugador es parte del alma… y con tan poca gente, el alma anda en modo fantasma.  
  Se nota que es un título de otra época en estructura y presentación: si vienes con estándares modernos, prepárate para ajustar expectativas.

[h2]Conclusión (Aceptable)[/h2]
Lockdown™ tiene ese encanto de shooter táctico “a la antigua”: más serio, más lento, más de pensar. Si buscas acción con disciplina, aquí hay una base respetable. El problema es que en 2026 el juego no compite con su puntería, compite con su contexto… y su contexto dice “3 jugadores activos”. Eso no es una comunidad: es una junta vecinal.

Con 486 recomendaciones totales queda claro que a mucha gente le dejó buen sabor en su momento. Pero hoy, si vienes por multijugador/cooperativo esperando vida, te vas a comer un silencio incómodo. ¿Vale la pena? Sí… pero con condiciones: o vienes por el modo un jugador y la curiosidad histórica, o traes amigos y los obligas con cariño.

Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Lockdown™ — гигантское разочарование после шедевральной третьей части.

[h2]Сюжет[/h2]
Для начала хочется сказать пару слов о сюжете. Лично мне он показался максимально посредственным. Хоть он и получился длиннее, чем сюжет «тройки», но также он вышел слегка несвязным. К примеру, про вирус «Легион», о котором говорят даже в описании игры, вспоминают немного в начале, а затем практически до самого конца он нигде не фигурирует. Также хочется сказать, что если в прошлой части мы постепенно выходили на зачинщика, и у него была чётко прописанная мотивация, то здесь имя главного антагониста называют в предпоследней миссии, и персонажа никак не раскрывают. Из-за этого историей трудно проникнуться, а за отсутствие какой-либо минимальной финальной кат-сцены — сразу минус балл.

[h2]Геймплей[/h2]
Хочется также сказать несколько слов о геймплее. Стрельба в игре стала значительно приятнее, но при этом очень сильно деградировала тактическая составляющая. Начнём с брифинга. Если раньше мы получали информацию с трёх разных точек зрения (общая информация о задании, тактические обстоятельства, психотип врагов и их подготовленность, а также новостная сводка о прошлой миссии), то здесь всё свелось к стандартному рассказу о произошедшем. Также из игры полностью убрали систему планирования. Вы можете настроить только снаряжение отряда — и всё. При этом нельзя проложить маршрут, выбрать, кого взять с собой на задание.

Вследствие отсутствия тактического режима локации из просторных превратились в линейные туннельные уровни, где тебе просто необходимо идти по заранее заданному маршруту, чтобы перейти на следующую такую же локацию. Сильно деградировали и сами миссии. Если раньше, скажем, спасение заложников требовало серьёзной тактики (ведь их могли убить), то здесь все спасения происходят одинаково: вы зачищаете комнату с террористами, которым абсолютно всё равно на заложников (которых всегда двое), после чего проводите людей до точки эвакуации. И таким вы занимаетесь практически на каждой миссии. Также хочется отметить обилие багов и тупое поведение ИИ — как у противников, так и у союзников, и особенно у заложников.

По итогу могу сказать: если вы пришли к этой части после условной «тройки», то, скорее всего, разочаруетесь, поскольку она больше похожа на новую часть Call of Duty, чем на Rainbow Six.

Well....I now know why this game has been sitting in my backlog for so long.
About all the good I can say is that the graphics are pretty damn crisp and will give you that mid-oughts nostalgia.

The bad?
They somehow managed to make an R6 game while making any tactical element useless. Setting up a room clear more often than not ends up with my team dead as they all go one way and get rolled from the other. Other times my teammates will walk one by one into a gas grenade and die one after the other. The tactical beauty of the first R6 has been utterly neutered on it's way to consoles. I'm amazed at having to kill close to a hundred enemies a level while thinking if I had to kill half as many per level in the original.

Without tactics what you do have is an absolutely punishing FPS. Enemy AI is pretty dim as they will sometimes look away while a firefight is happening in the room but, with only three hit points, if they zero in, you're dead in a second. This is compounded by times when there's multiple enemies in a room and with only three flashbangs a mission, you're having to kill four or five enemies by yourself. Quicksaving before opening any door or ordering a clear becomes mandatory.

You can change loadout but honestly, between what attachments a weapon can use and how much ammo a weapon can hold, I found being able to choose between dozens of different guns to be absolutely pointless.

Ding must've gotten a concussion between games because the bloom is wild. Single shot is the only way you'll hit something but is slow enough it can get you killed. You'd think moving and shooting would be an option but the bloom expands to half your screen. This is compounded by how much quicker enemies move than you, making some firefights a god damned game of whack a mole. Moving the cursor affects bloom as well, compounding the frustration. Near the end of the game the enemies get spongy so unless you can hit the head (and the bloom will make sure you do not), you're going to waste a lot of ammo. When you're engaging at a distance, you'll also be wasting a lot of ammo.

Speaking of, the game gives you a tip at one point about how it's quicker to swap weapons than to reload but if you've already began the reload animation it will not allow you to change weapons. Nothing more awkward than mid-firefight mashing the change weapon key and nothing happening while getting shot at.

Maps are boring. No music and all you can do is find hostages to bring to a point or use a computer. So throughout the sixteen missions, you are looking for three things and that's it. The gunplay is basic so it gets repititive fast. It essentially becomes a manual rail shooter.

The story is.....pretty meh. The amazing part is on completion of the final objective in the mission you get booted out to the menu with some credits and.....that's it. No thank you, no cinematic, no cutscene, nothing. 

Overall: Lockdown managed to remove anything that made R6 great and leaves you with a FPS that's more frustrating than fun. I wouldn't recommend this game free. Go play the original, Vegas or Raven Shield.

I enjoyed playing Lockdown on the PS2 back in the day. It had a decent single player mode, and some fun online play. I recently picked the PC version up on a Steam sale, and while it's sad that the online play is long gone, the single player mode is fun so long as you take it for what it is. Lockdown was first developed on the PS2 and Xbox and released in September of 2005. This PC port was released 5-months later. This means that Lockdown is a "consolized" version of Rainbow Six if you will. If you take the game for what it offers, you'll probably find some enjoyment out of it. However, if you're looking for the deep tactical features of previous games, things like pre-planning every step of the mission step-by-step, you'll be sorely disappointed with R6: Lockdown. 

There is a little tactical feel in giving commands to your teammates throughout the missions, even if teammate AI is dumber than a box of hammers, but those deep tactical-FPS elements that made R6 and Ghost Recon so good have been watered down for a more straightforward, and what I would call, Hollywooded-up experience where the game moves from set-piece to set-piece as a means of progression. This is opposed to having a more open exploration with tactical planning feel to it like the previous games. The game is a very linear experience overall. Perhaps a precursor, if you will, to design elements later found in Rainbow Six Vegas.

Hardcore Rainbow Six fans were probably sorely disappointed with Rainbow Six: Lockdown when it hit, but I would liken it to SWAT: Global Strike Team which was released on the PS2 and Original Xbox where it's a streamlined, consoled-up version of a deeper tactical franchise. I, personally, have always enjoyed Lockdown for what it is. It is a shallow shell of the Rainbow Six games that came before, but I've always been able to enjoy it for what it offers, and not hated it for what it doesn't. When it comes to PS2 Tom Clancy Games, it's still way better than the PS2 port of Ghost Recon 2 and G.R.A.W., but not better than the PS2 port of Rainbow Six 3, which is, surprisingly, a solid port of the Xbox version of Rainbow Six 3 which is also different from Rainbow Six 3: Raven Shield

For PC gamers looking to dive into a deep, Red Storm-developed tactical FPS, this isn't the Rainbow Six for you. However, for those with nostalgia for playing Lockdown back in the day on the PS2 or Original Xbox, or those who don't mind a more shallow, "consolized" tactical FPS game, Lockdown is worth picking up for cheap. I think I only spent around $2.50 for it, maybe less on a Steam sale, and I'll get more than my money's worth out of it. It's just a shame that it can no longer be played online, because it's online play was actually pretty fun on the PS2 back in the day. The official UBI servers are long gone, but I know people tunnel the game through Lan to play it online still. I've never personally looked into how to do it, but there are still ways to play it online if you have your heart set on it.

The Bottom Line: This is a bad Rainbow Six game, but not a bad game in it's own right. Hardcore R6 fans should skip this one, but if you're a forgiving gamer, or a nostalgic PS2/Xbox owner who played this back in the day, Lockdown is enjoyable for what it is. If you find it cheap enough, you'll get your money's worth out of it.

От Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Lockdown™ после прохождения я получил двоякое впечатление. 
С одной стороны имеются интересные задания с интересными локациями и с возможностью кастомизации и управления нашим отрядом. А с другой стороны имеем ужасную и кривую стрельбу и тупых противников. Разве что стрельба из пистолетов более приятная.
Перед началом каждого задания по своему вкусу выбираем снаряжение для нас и нашей команды. От огнестрельных пушек до специального оборудования и снаряжения. Поэтому буквально для каждого члена отряда можно специализировать свою роль в задании. Вроде бы круто, но в купе с тупыми противниками, эти подготовленные роли не имеют никакого смысла. Достаточно всего будет просто идти по заданию и по пути устранять противника. Тем не менее осторожность при прохождении задании все же не помешает, так как враг бьет достаточно сильно чтобы погибнуть за пару выстрелов
Стрельба из основного оружия в игре крайне не приятная. Все как будто очень криво и расхлябано. Не знаю как так получилось у разработчиков, но стрельба из пистолетов ощущается куда приятнее. Поэтому большую часть времени я проходил задания именно с пистолетом.
Пусть и локации линейные, но они сделаны крайне неплохо и разнообразно. Приятно было погулять по разным локациям во время прохождения задании, если конечно игра сама не принуждала продвигаться по сюжету.
И в целом я бы пропустил Lockdown™, так как она по мне не самая удачная часть серии и вряд ли заслуживает внимания.

Umiera się po jednym strzale, co wnosi niezwykle dużo irytacji do gry. AI towarzyszy jest bardzo złe, do tego często nie chcą wykonywać rozkazów w wyraźnie powiedziany sposób. Przykład: chcę wydać komendę otwarcia drzwi i wyczyszczenia pomieszczenia, które jest halą. Towarzysze biegną na pałę pod ogień nieprzyjaciela, i od razu giną. Ich możliwości taktyczne są bardzo ubogie. Fabuła jest tak skomplikowana, jak wykałaczka. Jest ktoś, kto w pierwszym poziomie kradnie gaz, a który to w ostatnim się odnajduje, pomiędzy tym fabuła to 30 sekund bieda briefingu między poszczególnymi poziomami. Nie pokuszono się o cutscenki. Poziomy są bardzo liniowe, zawsze jest jeden poprawny sposób. Nie ma żadnych rekomendacji jaką broń zabrać, granaty, tłumik, nic. Same bronie są ładnie wykonane. Jednakże dodatki do nich są bardzo szczątkowe, przez co niebezpiecznie szybko wkrada się nuda. Niestety, nie puszcza ona przez całą grę. Ogólnie ujmując całość nie jest dobra. Lepiej zainwestować czas i pieniądz w części o podtytułach Vegas, oraz serię SWAT, która radzi sobie z tematem znacznie lepiej.

Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Lockdown takes the established counterterrorism formula of the series and pushes it toward a more immediate, action-focused style. Developed by Red Storm Entertainment and published by Ubisoft, the game follows the elite Rainbow unit as it responds to a series of international terrorist incidents that eventually reveal a larger biological threat involving the Legion virus. The premise provides a suitable framework for a globe-spanning campaign, giving each operation a sense of urgency even though storytelling generally remains secondary to the missions themselves.

The biggest difference between Lockdown and the earlier Rainbow Six games is its approach to tactical combat. The series traditionally placed considerable importance on planning, careful movement, team coordination, and punishing consequences for mistakes. Lockdown retains portions of that identity but streamlines the experience considerably. Missions are more direct, firefights happen more frequently, and quick shooting skills play a greater role. This makes the game easier to understand for players accustomed to conventional first-person shooters, but it also removes some of the strategic complexity that made the earlier installments distinctive.

Close-quarters combat is where the game performs best. Many encounters take place inside buildings, corridors, rooms, and other confined environments where threats can appear suddenly. Moving cautiously and checking dangerous areas before advancing can still be valuable, and the atmosphere becomes particularly effective when the player does not know exactly what is waiting behind the next doorway. These situations provide glimpses of the tense tactical identity associated with Rainbow Six, even when the overall mission design favors a faster pace.

The equipment selection adds another tactical layer. Alongside conventional firearms, players have access to specialized tools and devices designed for particular situations. Lock fusers, laser trip mines, virus grenades, and other equipment provide alternatives to simply entering every encounter with guns blazing. These gadgets help reinforce the fantasy of operating as part of a technologically equipped counterterrorism unit, although the streamlined mission structure means the player is rarely required to develop exceptionally complicated strategies around them.

Squad interaction remains important, but it is considerably less elaborate than what veterans of the more simulation-oriented entries might expect. Giving orders and using teammates intelligently can make encounters easier, especially when clearing dangerous locations. However, artificial intelligence occasionally exposes the game's age. Teammates do not always behave with the precision expected from highly trained operatives, while enemies can alternate between dangerous reactions and predictable behavior. These inconsistencies can weaken otherwise suspenseful encounters.

The campaign's presentation has also aged considerably. Character models, environmental geometry, textures, animations, and visual effects clearly belong to an earlier generation of PC shooters. Nevertheless, the darker environments and enclosed locations complement the counterterrorism theme reasonably well. Rather than relying on spectacle, Lockdown often creates tension through restricted spaces and uncertainty about nearby enemies. Its visuals may no longer impress technically, but the underlying atmosphere remains effective in certain missions.

Audio contributes substantially to that atmosphere. Environmental noises, footsteps, voices, hostages, weapons, and subtle sounds around the player's surroundings can provide clues about nearby activity. When played carefully, these details encourage the player to listen before entering unfamiliar areas. Gunfire has enough impact to make close-range engagements feel dangerous, while ambient sounds help prevent quieter portions of missions from becoming completely lifeless.

Lockdown also experimented with multiplayer through a class-based structure featuring specialized operative roles and a selection of competitive maps, including returning locations inspired by classic Rainbow Six content. These systems were meaningful attractions when the game was contemporary, but multiplayer should no longer be considered its primary selling point. Anyone purchasing it today is better served by treating the campaign and its historical significance as the central attractions rather than expecting a thriving modern online community.

Steam Deck compatibility is Playable but less straightforward. The game does not have an official Steam Deck Verified rating, so it should be treated as unsupported rather than as a guaranteed handheld experience. Because it is an older Windows PC title, compatibility may depend on Proton behavior, configuration adjustments, community controller layouts, and possibly manual troubleshooting. The original control design was built around keyboard and mouse, which can also require customization for comfortable handheld use. Players wanting a completely effortless Steam Deck experience should therefore approach it cautiously.

What ultimately holds Lockdown back is not that it completely fails as a shooter, but that it occupies an awkward position between tactical simulation and accessible action. The faster combat can be enjoyable, yet simplifying the planning and strategic elements makes the game feel less unique. Players expecting the deliberate preparation and unforgiving realism associated with classic Rainbow Six may be disappointed. Conversely, those who prefer a more straightforward military shooter may appreciate being able to enter missions without spending extensive time preparing elaborate tactical plans.

There is still value here for players interested in the history of tactical shooters. Lockdown demonstrates a period when the franchise was experimenting with ways to reach a broader audience while retaining recognizable elements such as squad commands, specialized equipment, counterterrorism operations, hostage situations, and dangerous close-quarters encounters. Not every experiment succeeds, but the result has enough personality to remain interesting as a product of its era.

Overall, Tom Clancy’s Rainbow Six Lockdown is a competent but uneven tactical action game whose streamlined design makes it simultaneously more approachable and less strategically rewarding. Its confined firefights, useful gadgets, atmospheric audio, squad mechanics, and international counterterrorism theme can still provide entertainment, but dated artificial intelligence, aging presentation, reduced tactical depth, and uncertain Steam Deck operation limit its modern appeal. It is most worthwhile for Rainbow Six enthusiasts curious about the franchise's evolution or players who enjoy revisiting older military shooters and can tolerate their technical and mechanical limitations.

První Tomova duhová šestka, se kterou jsem se v době vydání mohl setkat na pirátské platce. Jako sérií nepolíben a absolutní neznalostí o čem vlastně má titul být na mě nezanechal žádné negativní vzpomínky až na  hardcore požadavky a méně horší technický stav. Hlavní ale je, že mě to bavilo. Tak opět po letech a již doplněním vzděláním a dnes již daleko lepším technickým vybavením se opět vracím s novými poznatky do své eseje. Bohužel jádro Duhové šestky zde horko těžko budeme hledat. Taktické plánování nebo přepínání členů naprosto chybí, oblasti a mapy jsou malé, prázdné a místy hloupě poskládané. Technický stav také není  
 v nejlepším stalo se mi místy, kdy jsem byl nucen restartovat misi vícekrát neboť rukojmí zmizel nebo se nenačetl daný skript. Během hraní máme pocit, že to celé je někde na půl cesty. Na druhou stranu, když pomineme, že se jedná o R6 tak hra samotná zas tak špatná není a má jen špatné označení. Nemohu si pomoc, ale během průchodu hrou jsem se nemohl zbavit pocitu, že se jedná spíš o titul Ghost Recon. Dnes už se můžem jen dohadovat co se dělo v průběhu vývoje. Závěrem můžu dodat když pominu že se jedná o R6 tak vlastně je v vcelku dobrá oddychovka, která zabaví na pár hodin a i dnes se hraje plynule a vypadá pěkne. Takže Tom Clancys ''Ghost Recon'' : Lockdown 7/10

Я, владелец аккаунта, в здравом уме и твёрдой памяти, по своей воле пишу данное ревью третьего апреля 2025 года. Я прошёл эту игру за 8.8 часов, и это время провёл с пользой, осознавая, что игра не идеальна, несмотря на то, что вышла 3 августа 2005 года.
Есть несколько плюсов и минусов, но не буду вдаваться в подробности каждого. Выделю ключевые моменты.
Плюсы:
Графика – несмотря на 20 лет с момента выхода, игра всё ещё выглядит достойно.
Вариативность – большой выбор тактик и оружия. (имхо Sound Scanner это просто ваууууу)
Цена – игра стоила всего 300 тенге (или около того).
Минусы:
ИИ – крайне тупой, иногда застревает в пустых местах или игнорирует приказы.(Хотя,я бы тоже не хотел следовать приказам какого-то придурка у которого 8.8 часов опыта в этой игре)
Дизайн карт и миссий – однообразие: иди по коридорам, отключи что-то, спаси заложника. Всё по шаблону.
Цена – игра стоила всего 300 тенге (или около того)
Заключение:Несмотря на все недостатки, мне понравился тактический геймплей. Когда я отдавал приказы о штурме через дверь с кувалдой и флешкой, на мгновение почувствовал себя настоящим командиром спецотряда.
Оценка: 8 тупых ИИ из 10.

As a kid, I would sit on a sofa, holding a PS2 controller in my hands, playing Rayman: Raving Rabbids. Those times were simple, without the trepidation about worrying my future. Here I am once again revisiting the game. I thought I would have never replayed it. A thought crossed my mind, RRR flashed before my eyes, summoning me to review this spin-off Rayman game.

RRR consists of 45 mini-games according to AI (yes, I didn't count it using my fingers). While some stages reused a fraction of them, the overall quality of them is still held up pretty well. The player plays as Rayman, who has been caught by Rabbids during a picnic. After Rayman is sent behind bars, he buckles down to musing on a way of getting out of this solitary cell. 

The controls are slightly clunky on M&K, they are either smooth as butter or the unlubricated gears grinding against your table. Nevertheless, the controls are pretty straightforward considering RRR is supposed to be a kid-friendly video game. It irks me that the arcade shooter mini-game is taking part in half of the final stages of multiple in-game days. Those graphics are soothing, needless to say; cartoon art style at its advantage, in which they stand out quite nicely. Not much to say about the music. Rhythm games are often offbeat. I, personally, would give it a six out of ten. If I'm being stingy about scoring, five sounds reasonable.

6/10

The first game in the "Rayman" Rabbids series. Some say these white devils bastardized the franchise and sent ubisoft on a path to destruction, but those who grew up with them came to enjoy them for some god forsaken reason (i fall in that latter camp, for full disclosure.)

It's a minigame collection, short and simple. I'd say though it's not bad compared to what was coming out at the time, and even at a discounted price it'll give you some good chuckles and roughly 4-6 hours or so of gameplay. Minigames are your basic party game stuff but nothing generic or outright shovelware. there's a few minigames strewn about that suck, but thankfully you only need to do 3/4 per section to beat the game (and 1 of those 3 will always be a rhythm game that is piss easy.) 

speaking of the soundtrack, it's licensed music that is by the books pop music but it's ubisoft's own covers. not bad, to a point where i think i'll have madonna's "girls just wanna have fun" stuck in my head because of this title.

story and atmosphere are pointless but a little humorous. rayman's essentially forced into indentured servitude by being the court jester for the rabbids and a big black muscular one we never see again. over time they come to love him more and more as a performer until he.... does something i don't wanna spoil. 

the minigames' theming and gameplay are kind of half the reason i enjoy the title. its kind of quirky and definitely of the time, stuff like simple mario party type games, racing, or an on rails shooter, nothing ever tries to be too difficult (unless you wanna do the challenges) because it's not here for you to have a challenge. your here to play minigames and laugh at the screaming rabbits.

This steam port hasn't been updated since launch, but surprisingly it runs well on windows 11 without config. i HIGHLY recommend a controller for this game. steam lies to you, you can enable a controller in the options menu and i played with an 8bitdo pro 2 in xbox mode with windows 11. no experience with trying on steam deck.

Nothing is true, everything is permitted

Prince of Pers- Digo, Assassin's Creed 1. Quase 20 anos depois e, caramba, que jogo interessante.

Eu gostei muito mais do que achei que fosse k. Todo o estigma que colocam nele: "ah, é ruim", "ah, é repetitivo", "ah, é travado". E sim, ele é repetitivo, mas isso não estragou a experiência pra mim, pq ele é muito redondinho, sabe? Tudo que eu mais gosto em AC tava lá desde o começo.

E, de verdade, eu adoro esse pacote que a UBI trouxe logo de primeira.

A movimentação, que é muito precisa mesmo hj em dia, e que eu prefiro muito mais do que vi nas minhas singelas 4 horinhas de Shadows. Os lançamentos, o uso do grab, aquele movimento pra passar por entre os gaps, nusssssssss. Muito gostosinho. Fora que subir qualquer estrutura alta nesse jogo é quase um puzzle — algo que foi herdado pela trilogia do Ezio, mas que sumiu nos ACs mais novos, tirando o Origins.

O combate é legal, mas é onde ele fica repetitivo mesmo. Se tu já jogou algum AC, vai tirar o combate dele de letra, pq é uma versão mais simples do que a gente (depois de anooos de franquia) já conhece. Mas é super estiloso desde aquela época.

Mas a parte mais legal do jogo é a construção de mundo. E eu nem tô falando dos visuais incríveis de Jerusalém, Acre, Damasco e outras localidades do jogo. Mas sim de tom e atmosfera.

AC1 é muitooo apegado a alguns temas e é quase totalmente focado em tateá-los com um zelo filosófico. Sabe o "Nothing is true, everything is permitted"? ENTÃO. O jogo pega isso e esticaaa até tu entender direitinho. Ou não tbm, pq esse jogo é cinza AF nesse sentido.

Amo alguns diálogos aqui tbm, carregados de nuances. Em específico, um lááá pro final do jogo, com uma pessoinha sem um dos braços, que mostra muito bem tudo que o jogo fala. E, melhor ainda, a evolução do Altair como um dos melhores personagens dessa franquia até hj.

Map 14/20 (les villes sont assez cool à découvrir surtout leurs ambiances, mais outre les quêtes principales et quelques quêtes secondaires redondante elle n'est pas extraordinaire)

Ambiance Sonore 14/20 (ost très cool et ambiance global sympa)
Durée de Vie 15/20 (ni trop long ni trop court)

Overall 13-13.5/20

Le début d'une licence légendaire, qui a malheureusement bien périclité depuis, sous la coupe à l'époque d'un studio de passionné, l'immersion dans l'histoire tout comme dans l'environnement des premières croisade est exceptionnel, la justesse historique permet d'apprendre des faits sur cette époque sans être assommé par des pavés, l'évolution d'Altaïr est prenante.
Les seuls défauts seraient la nécessité de télécharger un patch pour y jouer sur steam, caper a 60 fps sinon les collisions du perso rendent le jeu injouable et les bannières collectibles qui sont trop nombreuse et de facto, beaucoup trop chiant à faire ainsi à la limite la raideur de la caméra qui est parfois désagréable (surtout pour le parcours), le jeu n'est pas le jeu du siècle (notamment due au collectibles et quêtes secondaires assez redondante mais sinon en terme d'histoire, de gameplay, de doublage... tout était excellent et c'était un plaisir de le refaire sur pc après l'avoir fait enfant sur ps3.
Je recommande fortement

Assassin's Creed, el primerito, es un juegazo que marcó a toda una generación.
La historia es épica. Juegas como Desmond Miles, un hombre del presente que es secuestrado por una empresa llamada Abstergo y lo meten a una máquina llamada Animus para revivir los recuerdos de su antepasado, Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad, un Maestro Asesino de la Tercera Cruzada en Tierra Santa.
Altaïr tiene que recorrer las ciudades de Jerusalén, Acre y Damasco para eliminar a 9 objetivos templarios y recuperar el honor de la Hermandad de los Asesinos. Y mientras vas avanzando, vas descubriendo que hay algo mucho más grande detrás de todo, una guerra secreta entre Asesinos y Templarios por un artefacto muy poderoso.
Las dinámicas están excelentes, eso de estar saltando en las casas, subirte a las diferentes estructuras de la ciudadela, correr por los techos, escalar torres y saltar al pajar, se siente increíble. Y lo mejor es ir sigilosamente matando a tus enemigos, mezclándote entre la gente, siguiendo a tu objetivo sin que te vean y eliminándolo en el momento perfecto.
Es un juego que lo jugué hace tiempo pero que siempre se recuerda con cariño, porque fue el que empezó todo, el parkour, el sigilo y esa historia que te deja picado.
Si nunca lo jugaste, tienes que jugarlo para entender de dónde salió esta saga tan grande. 9.5/10.

Unfortunately this game is too obsolete and annoying these days to warrant any recommendation. Certainly at its prime, when it was all brand new, it sparked entire series out of itself and a way to make games as well but if it released today it would barely pass as an Indie game or proof of concept with what it was trying to accomplish.
Just watch the dialogue/scenes on YouTube, maybe a summary and skip straight to AC2.
Why?
Because the writing and narrative are the only good things it has to offer, and there are other means to experience it. Especially when the game throws so many logs at your legs.

For starters the game refuses to launch normally on modern systems and you will have to launch it from the game directory. IF that works for you of course. It did for me and I just renamed the .exe's to track my play time (overlay doesn't work).

As soon you get past your first assassination in Memory Block 1 I regret to tell you that you've seen all the gameplay the game has to offer. From then you will be doing the exact same things 8 more times if you don't get mortally bored any time earlier.

Over time it just gets more annoying to do: Rescuing citizen usually means fighting entire garrison as more guards keep joining the fight. Population of Karen tier beggars, drunkards and madmen seems to outnumber the normal people. Moving around on the streets becomes almost impossible in later chapter while roofs are teeming with archers. 
For a game about people working from the shadows the quiet approach to most things seem not possible by design. Instead you will spend 90% of your gameplay time just fighting the endless swarms of guards. Pre-final battle is a gauntlet of soldiers. Final battle is another fight with a swarm. Everything you do in this game will devolve into a brawl against 20 guards minimum very quickly. And combat system is not great. Very methodical with just fishing for parries, forever. I've endured worse but that's entirety of gameplay.

Revolutionary at the time climbing is not good in this entry. It's very slow, Altair often refuses to grab stones and ledges clearly put there to be grabbed. It's notorious and works against you about as often as it doesn't. I swear the only time I played the game NOT thorougly pissed was when watching cutscenes...

Despite insane amount of collectibles with 0 in-game aid to find them there is 0 reward for them. That "additional memories" block on level select? That's not a level, just an indicator. I do enjoy a nice collectathon but with no kind of reward but a filled progress bar is just insulting. Hours of padding for already repetitive slog of a game. Whole Kingdom area is just a vomit of collectibles with nothing else. This zone shouldn't even exist in the game.

.
So, now. By skipping the actual game part of the game you do gain quite a lot:
The whole vibe of the Animus is great, so is Abstergo and the scenes in the Present.
On-Engine cutscenes are also just great. In fact, seems like all budget went for creating the atmosphere, camera angles and all that cinematic feeling for everything. Because of that there is notable aim for realism which shows in the climbing, while its sequel AC2 makes climbing much faster, more fluid movements and noticeably more stylized visuals.
If you still insist to play it no matter what and assuming it launches for you in the first place - just do the bare minimum to continue the main plot. Collectables are worthless, literally. That way you will see the best bits and skip the boring chores the game is stuffed with. IF you can stomach the combat gauntlets by the end, can't forget about those >.<

[h1] For anyone who is unable to play the game: [/h1]
[h2] Fixes that worked for me [/h2]
[h3] Fix 1 [/h3]
Right click the game in your steam library and select [u] properties [/u] , then go and click [u] browse local files [/u] . This shall give you access to the installed files. Now you shall see two main applications that go like AssassinsCreed_Dx9 or AssassinsCreed_Dx10. Click anyone of them (I clicked Dx10) and the game shall launch.
[h3] what this fix does [/h3]
This fix directly launches the game via its installed files without utilizing steam so whilst you play like this you cannot access steam features ie; screenshots etc
[h3] Fix 2 [/h3]
[u] physically disconnect your PC from the internet [/u] Either turn off your wifi or ethernet (In my case I physically unplugged my ethernet cable). Use steam in offline mode and the game shall run perfectly fine 
[h1] Why the F*CK AM I FACING THESE ISSUES? [/h1]
Well the answer is simple, Ubisoft could not give two flying ***** about it's fans and decided not to update the games verification system. This issue occurs because when you launch AC1 on steam the game tries to contact [b] Legacy Ubisoft servers during startup (gconnect.ubi.com) [/b] which have been shut down and no longer available. This failed connection crashes the game and thus turning off the wifi or non-steam launch helps tackle it 
[h1] Actual game Review [/h1]

[h1]ШТОШ![/h1][hr][/hr][h3]Assassin's Creed - это игра, которая для меня навсегда останется настоящими "Истоками". Это монументальный памятник эпохи, который в далеком детстве подарил десятки часов погружения в этот мир, заставив безоговорочно поверить в скрытое противостояние ассасинов и тамплиеров в Святой Земле. Каждый раз, когда в наушниках начинает играть таинственный и тревожный эмбиент Джаспера Кида, по спине пробегает табун ностальгических мурашек. Шаг за шагом, сквозь пыльные улочки Дамаска, Акры и Иерусалима, мы проживали эту грандиозную сагу. И сегодня, запуская оригинал, я вспоминаю те самые первые, чистые детские ощущения, когда прыжок веры с колокольни заставлял замирать сердце, а концепция генетической памяти в Анимусе казалась чем-то запредельным и гениальным.[/h3]
[u]Я не гуру обзоров по играм, НОООО, вот чем я хотел бы поделиться за время моего игрового опыта:[/u][hr][/hr][h3]Геймплей[/h3] Для своего времени это был прорыв, заложивший фундамент индустрии, пускай игра и предлагает лишь красивую иллюзию открытого мира. Местный честный паркур заставлял думать как скалолаз и  рассчитывать траекторию прыжков между уступами на стенах. А чего стоит легендарный скрытый клинок! В игре он является не просто оружием, а ультимативным инструментом, позваляющий делать мгновенное убийство цели в прыжке или или планировать безликое убийство из толпы. Всё это дарило невероятное чувство превосходства, хотя в открытом бою приходилось переключаться на меч. Механика социального стелса с растворением среди монахов до сих пор ощущается самобытно. Однако игровой процесс страдает от монотонности: все расследования перед ключевым убийством сводятся к одинаковому набору из подслушивания на лавочках, кражи записок и избиения информаторов, но вспомните, нам ведь многого и не надо было, это сейчас все зажрались и душатся от всего подряд...  Сюжетная линия Альтаира прекрасна в своей строгости — здесь нет спасения мира ради дешевого пафоса, только холодная философия Кредо и последовательное устранение девяти целей. Линейное повествование жестко ведет вас по списку жертв от предательства до финала, заставляя вслушиваться в их предсмертные монологи. Отрезанный палец ради скрытого клинка, суровые выговоры Аль-Муалима и постепенное возвращение ранга мастера создают великолепную взрослую историю о фанатизме, слепой вере и поиске истинной свободы.[hr][/hr][h3]Сюжет[/h3] Сюжетная линия Альтаира прекрасна в своей простоте и строгости! Тут нет спасения мира ради дешевого пафоса... Только холодная философия Кредо и последовательное устранение девяти целей - как возможность доказать, что ты все таки достоин. Линейное повествование жестко ведет вас по списку жертв от предательства до финала, заставляя вслушиваться в их предсмертные монологи. Отрезанный палец ради скрытого клинка, суровые выговоры Аль-Муалима и постепенное возвращение ранга мастера создают великолепную взрослую историю о фанатизме, слепой вере и поиске истинной свободы.[hr][/hr][h3]Атмосфера[/h3] Палящее солнце Святой Земли передано отлично, а города визуально заметно отличаются друг от друга. Золотой Дамаск, туманная и полуразрушенная синяя Акра, а горная крепость в Масиафе дарит потрясающее чувство отрешенности от остального безумного мира. Настоящий восторг испытываешь на точках обзора, когда после синхронизации под пронзительный крик орла камера делает величественный оборот, и перед тобой открывается захватывающий вид на весь город. Мрачный саунддизайн, гипнотические мотивы, крики глашатаев и звон стали идеально передают паранойю убийцы.[hr][/hr][h3]Графика и оптимизация[/h3] Визуально игра выдает свой почтенный возраст, но благодаря уникальному цветовому фильтру для каждого региона и отличной анимации движений она до сих пор выглядит весьма сносно. На современных ПК все работает идеально плавно, однако устаревший движок подкидывает свои нюансы. Готовтесь столкнуться с полным отсутствием современных разрешений экрана в меню и головной болью при подключении геймпада, игра наотрез отказывается распознавать триггеры новых контроллеров без фанатских фиксов.[hr][/hr][h3]Остальное[/h3] Игра полностью переведена на русский язык, не смотря на имеющуюся плашку в стиме. На сюжетную линию уйдет около 10-15 часов, если не тратить время на сбор сотен разбросанных флагов. Для Steam Deck имеется плашка - "Можно играть", но придется воевать с раскладкой управления и мелкими шрифтами. Цена на распродажах за этот кусочек истории сейчас чисто символическая, так что покупка полностью оправдывает себя как дань уважения великим истокам.[hr][/hr][h3] На фоне недавно нашумевшего ремейка Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag Resynced, доказавшего возможность крутой пересборки классики с нуля, фанаты засыпали форумы вопросами. Но Ubisoft прямо заявила, что других ремейков в разработке сейчас нет. И все же я бесконечно верю, что эта контора пNд0р@с0в соберется с силами и сделает полноценный ремейк первой части на новом движке Anvil, а не продолжит штамповать ленивые копии ради попыток повторения успешного успеха.
Этот мир стал для меня началом общего игрового пути, и никакие конвейерные сиквелы не смогут затмить те самые первые детские воспоминания.[/h3]

Pros:

- 🖥️ Beautiful world designs of the each historical locations, very vibrant and detailed, makes you want to explore every nooks and crannies.

Cons:

Shame that Ubisoft got infected by the Woke Cult later on so the writing as well as the gameplay gone down the shitter. Avoid anything after Assassin Creed Unity!

Combat system is exremely balanced & polished for a game this old. Although it may feel exaggerating, this game is one of the best games i've played interms of combat design. The only nitpick i have is since the game is almost 2 decades old it's designed for those old hardware you will face isssues like game freezes and hard stuck issues.

Game suggestion:
Keep an eye for those zombie patients and begger ladies who come after you and irritate the hell out of you. Don't even have an idea how many of them i've killed for pestering me all the times.

NOTE: Solutions to play the game without any issues;
1. When you try to play the game while being connected to the internet it will route to the servers which don't exist but the game constantly tries to connect to those non existent servers and hard freezes in th process. There are some fixes in the internet you can find or check out the guide in the forums of assassin's crred community. 

2. Whenver you switch to other tasks while playing the game you'll get issues like screen shifting and forces you play in widnowed mode. To eliminate it there are 2 options one is free tool called "NOMOREBORDER" but if you want paid and polished one search "BORDERLESSGAMING" in steam. download & install the application of your choice then select the game and select borderless window mode. 

3. Enable steam input if you want to enjoy the game with controller. if you are keyboard & mouse user turn the highprofile off which helps you a lot when you are in combat and running from those guards who chase you like death gods.

4. Turn Vsync on which somehow eliminates leap of faith(It is nothing but jumping off scene from those watch watch towers once you reached it's peak for quick traversal) issue

Finally, My review in one line is go for it, if you think of starting this AC franchise, you won't regret it.

It works fine for me, but many people have cited controller issues and crashes on start-up, so keep in-mind that you may have to tinker with this to get it working properly. The largest problem that I've seen is that the game will occasionally crash to desktop after an hour or two of playtime.

That aside, the game is exactly like the original 2008 release, just with some graphical polish. The game still looks breathtaking at times even though its 18 years old, the combat feels nice, the platforming is fun and intuitive, the guards (while dumb at times) do a decent job at pursuing the player, and the setting of the late 12th century Israel and Syria in the midst of the Third Crusade is a very neat decision. The game takes place in the cities of Masyaf, Acre, Damascus, and Jerusalem. Altair investigates these cities and performs hits to restore his rank in the Order. The game is a tad repetitive, but it's also not very long. Even if you go out of your way to do every mission and view tower (which you DEFINITELY don't have to do, but I've been enjoying the exploration), I'd say it'll probably take you around 20 hours give or take.

Rainbow Six: Vegas 2 is effectively an upgrade of its predecessor in nearly every way. You have a lot more options in terms of weapons and playstyle, better cover mechanics, character customization, a levelling system that encourages you to take risks and try new angles of approach, an improved team control. It's basically R6:V but better in nearly every way. The story isn't as grand as the first game and there are some strange decisions (like, why does the second to last map force you to fend off a small army alone? Could they not provide a replacement team?) but generally it's serviceable and there are a lot of fun maps to play. 

My primary problems have to do with the audio mixing, which is all over the place. Sometimes civilians are really quiet even when you're standing right in front of them, and your allies will often speak as if they're talking over the radio despite being next to you, which makes it kind of hard to parse what they're saying sometimes. It's not a big deal since it's a nearly 20-year old game and it doesn't really impact gameplay at all, but it is a bit distracting sometimes. A bigger problem I had was when I booted up the game for the first time there was simply no audio at all, and even weirder it wasn't just the game itself; it seemed to ENTIRELY kill the audio even on other apps when I had the game open. I eventually fixed it by having the game run in Windows compatibility mode (This seems to be a known issue for Windows 11) but it was still a very strange bug. 

My only other issue is that I don't like that the snake cam is removed on terrorist hunt mode. it gives a mixed message where the game wants you to play tactically instead of running in guns blazing but it removes one of the most important tools for doing so.

Recommended. A tactical squad campaign in a lost genre, where tagging targets, ordering breaches and methodical room clears pair with constant three-track XP progression across a bomb-threat Las Vegas told in parallel with its predecessor.

Loadout depth is massive, checkpoints are gracious, and the stealth-then-firefight rhythm of the convention centre and monorail levels is the formula at its best. Three XP tracks (Marksman, CQB, Assault) tick constantly, unlocking gear as each grows, and a carry-over save from the prior entry grants bonus experience.

Squad AI jams teammates in doorways and ignores orders, solo missions strip the safety blanket, and the final gauntlet spams respawning enemies and grenades across seven-attempt frustration. Roughly seven hours of an extinct genre worth revisiting.

Hey kiddo, Handsome Jack here... and I just played Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Vegas 2, and apparently somebody looked at the first game and thought, “This is good, but we could put even MORE terrorists in Las Vegas.”

Excellent.

You know what I like about Vegas 2? It understands that a good employee doesn't just run into a room screaming and hoping for the best. You actually have to think. Breach the door, check the room, give your team orders, pick your targets, use cover, and then turn the whole place into a very professionally managed crime scene.

That's leadership.

Of course, you can also ignore all of that and sprint directly into a hallway full of terrorists.

That's not leadership.

That's a performance review.

The cover system still feels great, the weapons are satisfying, and having AI teammates who can actually follow basic instructions makes me feel like the world's greatest tactical commander. “Breach this door.” They breach it. “Throw a grenade.” They throw it. “Shoot that guy.” They shoot him.

Kiddo, do you have any idea how rare competent employees are?

And then you've got Vegas itself. Casinos, hotels, streets, rooftops, bright neon lights, and heavily armed lunatics occupying all of them. You can't walk through the city without somebody trying to kill you.

It's the Las Vegas tourism board's worst nightmare.

The customization is also a nice touch. You can create your own operator, change your gear, and gradually improve your soldier through the progression system. It's basically an employee development program where the promotions are measured in bullet accuracy.

The campaign is fun, the co-op is even better, and the terrorist hunt modes are fantastic when you just want to kick down doors and remove problems from the building.

The biggest issue is that it can feel a little dated. The AI isn't always brilliant, some encounters can become repetitive, and there are moments where the game gets a little too predictable.

But honestly, kiddo, the core formula still works.

Plan.

Breach.

Shoot.

Clear.

Move.

Repeat.

Beautiful.

And the multiplayer? Absolute chaos. Tactical players trying to coordinate while some lunatic runs around with a shotgun and somehow manages to win.

I hate that guy.

I respect that guy.

I want to fire that guy.

9/10, kiddo.

BEST of the BEST - this game beats all shooters. The game is old so I had to setup my xbox one controller manually. 

Below are the instructions for setting up your Xbox One controller to use the game's native controller support on PC. This gives you the same controller feel as playing on the Xbox console. I have over 1,000 hours in the game, and this setup feels perfect! See below for the setup instructions.

CONTROLLER SETUP 
- find this file and open it: C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Rainbow Six Vegas 2\KellerGame\Config\PCKellerJoysticks.ini
- when you open the file in notepad and make joystick zero to look like this:
[Joystick0]
ProductName=Controller (Xbox One For Windows)
UseXInput=True
VendorID=1118
ProductID=767
------------------------

you are done. now go test and make sure the controller works:

- make sure your controller is plugged in directly to usb. (it's not able to play wireless / bluetooth)
- go into game options using mouse & click on 360 controller option to enable it. when it says on, your controller should allow you to move around the menu.
- if controller doesn't work, restart your computer, open steam, plug in your controller to USB (wireless does not work,) open game, and then test again. 
- if it still doesn't work, edit the file again (PCKellerJoysticks.ini) & try all these numbers for the product ID and one should work: 673, 721, 736, 733, 742, 746, 767

It's quite easy so don't let it scare you. There is a reason why many people still buy this game today and play it every day. This game is one of the best and got lost over the years because games changed their way of how they make money.

[h1][b] Reseña de Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six® Vegas 2[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six® Vegas 2 es ese shooter de acción “táctico” donde te venden que cada decisión importa… y luego te recuerdan a balazos que te equivocaste por asomarte 0.3 segundos de más. Es un juego de disparos con enfoque por escuadras, mezcla de sigilo opcional y tiroteos intensos, con ese sabor a “antes los FPS te pedían cerebro, no solo reflejos”.

La propuesta es simple: entrar, limpiar, avanzar, repetir… pero con el plus de que te deja jugar en cooperativo y multijugador, y además meterle personalización al personaje para que tu operador se vea único mientras hace exactamente lo mismo que todos: cubrirse y sobrevivir. Primera impresión: clásico duro, atmosférico, y con más orgullo que tutoriales modernos.

[h2][Táctica de élite vs. Caos en el casino][/h2]

Lo Bueno:
  Jugabilidad táctica y basada en equipos: aquí sí importa cubrirse, asomar con cabeza y leer la situación.  
  Cooperativo que le da vida: jugar acompañado convierte cada misión en “operación seria” (o en desastre organizado, igual se disfruta).  
  Dificultad con colmillo: no te regala victorias; te las hace sudar como si fueras pasante en fuerzas especiales.  
  Ambiente “realista” y con tensión: entre pasillos, luces y cobertura, se siente ese ritmo de asalto metódico.  
  Personalización de personaje: porque si vas a fallar una entrada, al menos hazlo con estilo.

Lo No Tan Bueno:
  0 logros: sí, cero. Steam te mira y dice “tu dopamina te la ganas trabajando”.   
  Comunidad miniatura (23 jugadores): encontrar partidas puede sentirse como buscar vida inteligente en un desierto… con balas.  
  Enfoque dividido (primera/tercera persona): a ratos se siente menos “táctico puro” y más “acción con traje serio”.  
  Para ser un clásico difícil, no siempre es amable: si vienes de shooters modernos, te va a dar una cachetada de realidad.

[h2]Conclusión (Bueno)[/h2]
Rainbow Six® Vegas 2 es como ese veterano que no necesita gritar para imponerse: te obliga a jugar con cabeza, a respetar coberturas y a entender que “correr como héroe” es una forma elegante de pedir respawn. Como juego de acción táctica, sigue siendo divertido, tenso y sorprendentemente adictivo cuando te metes en su ritmo.

Ahora, hablemos del elefante en la habitación: 23 jugadores activos. Eso significa que el multijugador puede sentirse como un club privado donde todos se conocen… y tú eres el nuevo al que van a borrar del mapa con cariño. Aun así, con 5190 recomendaciones, queda claro que la gente no lo recomienda por nostalgia barata, sino porque el juego todavía tiene dientes.

(Ignore the hours, I've played this game too many times to count as a kid, and had to play this round in admin. You'll see why down below because it will also happen to you.)

[h2] Game Errors + Glitches: [/h2]

[h3] AlertForDebug [/h3] 
You will most likely encounter the "AlertforDebug" error on first launch that will then immediately crash your game. If your game is not launching (or, it launches once, but not again) you'll have to change the game path in the boot.txt file to something like this: 

E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Petz Horsez 2

This is what my path looked like, but obviously the location the game/main file is going to be different for you. You can find the location by going to the game in your library, selecting gear icon on the game page, then "browse local files." You would copy that entire file location into that line of gamepath in boot.txt.

[h3] Saves [/h3] 
When you save for the first time, it MAY add a duplicate Petz Horsez 2 folder within the MAIN Petz Horsez 2. You'll know if this happens if you get the AlertforDebug error again when launching after exiting your first session. 

What you'll have to do is move the separated save file within that duplicate folder back into the MAIN Petz Horsez 2 folder. You can delete that leftover secondary folder once you confirm the save folder is moved into the main one. Make sure gamepath still correlates to the main folder (so when game launches, the system will know where to look for the save files in that main Petz Horsez 2 folder.)

[h3] If game is STILL not launching [/h3] 
If this is the case, right click the commonplayer.exe in the Petz Horsez 2 folder and go into properties, then compatibility. Select compatibility mode to run for Windows 8.  Then, select "Disable fullscreen optimizations" + "Run this program as an administrator." Hit apply and okay. W/ this option, you should be able to run w/ steam, otherwise right click the .exe file and run as admin.

[h3] Secondary Objectives. [/h3]
 Once you're actually in the game, you'll eventually see that there are secondary objectives for the player to complete. If 80% of these objectives are completed, then you will get different  (and better) endings. Most objectives unlock after you interact with the task, [b] HOWEVER!! [/b] Certain tasks do NOT show in the notebook and are NOT counted if you do them in the tutorial chapter: [u] Open laptop, Open library, Catch figurines, Communication activity, Lunging activity, Entering in the farm lounge, Going to the town hall place. [/u] 

If these are done in tutorial, they do not count. If this happens you would have to manually go into the file and change it. Conversely, there are tasks that do not show in the journal, but DO count towards the secondary objectives: [u] reach endurance level 3, reach agility level 3 [/u]

I recommend you scale the game to your screen so it doesn't stretch everything, that made it look weird for me when I first launched it. Also, time is a valuable resource in game so it's not a particularly cozy or casual game.

Petz Horsez 2 developed and published by Ubisoft is a horse-care and ranch simulation that blends animal management, light storytelling, and equestrian competition into a single, slow-paced experience. Originally released in the late 2000s and later made available on Steam, the game carries a distinctly nostalgic identity, reflecting a period when lifestyle simulation titles were designed around routine, responsibility, and gradual progression rather than streamlined convenience. At its heart, the game invites players to immerse themselves in ranch life, raising horses from foals to capable competitors while balancing daily chores and long-term goals.

The foundation of the experience revolves around caring for your horses. Players feed, groom, clean, and monitor the health of each animal, ensuring that their physical condition and morale remain high. These tasks are presented through interactive mini-games that simulate brushing coats, washing hooves, or distributing feed. While repetitive over extended sessions, these routines are essential to the core philosophy of the game: building a bond through consistent attention. Unlike more arcade-styled animal games, progress here feels earned through patience. Watching a young horse gradually improve its abilities after hours of care and training fosters a sense of accomplishment that mirrors real-world dedication.

Training and competition add structure beyond barn chores. Horses can be prepared for various equestrian disciplines, including jumping and cross-country events. Training sessions serve as skill-building exercises that influence performance during competitions, and success in these events rewards players with prize money and unlockable items. These competitions offer a shift in pacing from quiet ranch maintenance to more focused, performance-based gameplay. While the riding mechanics are relatively simple by modern standards, they provide enough challenge to make preparation meaningful. Winning a tournament feels less like a quick arcade victory and more like the culmination of careful preparation.

The game also weaves in a light narrative element centered around restoring and preserving a struggling ranch. Story segments appear through brief cutscenes and character interactions, providing context for the player’s efforts. Although the narrative is not particularly complex, it adds emotional framing to the otherwise cyclical gameplay. Rather than tending to horses in isolation, players are working toward sustaining a legacy and keeping the ranch operational. This gives purpose to the daily repetition and reinforces a sense of long-term investment.

Visually, the game reflects its era. Environments capture pastoral charm with open fields, rustic barns, and countryside backdrops, but character models and horse animations show their age. The horses themselves, while varied in breed and coloration, sometimes lack the anatomical realism and fluid movement seen in more recent equestrian titles. Nevertheless, there is a quaint appeal in the stylized presentation. The atmosphere remains gentle and calming, reinforced by soft background music that complements the rural setting.

One of the defining characteristics of the game is its deliberate pacing. Progress unfolds gradually, requiring sustained engagement with daily care routines. For players who appreciate tranquil, methodical simulation experiences, this rhythm can be soothing and immersive. However, for those seeking faster progression or more dynamic systems, the repetition may feel cumbersome. The interface and control scheme also reflect older design sensibilities, occasionally feeling less intuitive compared to contemporary simulation titles.

Despite these limitations, the game maintains a dedicated audience drawn to its blend of responsibility and relaxation. It captures a specific fantasy: living among horses, nurturing them from infancy, and guiding them toward competitive success. The emotional satisfaction comes not from dramatic storytelling or high-intensity mechanics but from steady improvement and quiet dedication. For players who grew up with equestrian simulations or who enjoy cozy management games centered on animal care, it offers a heartfelt, if imperfect, journey into ranch life.

Ultimately, the game stands as a nostalgic reminder of an era when simulation titles prioritized routine and immersion over convenience. While its technical aspects show their age, its core appeal—building bonds with animals and investing time into meaningful progression—remains intact. It may not satisfy players seeking modern polish or complex systems, but for those willing to embrace its slower rhythm, it delivers a charming and earnest equestrian adventure grounded in patience and care.

Bought this game for nostalgia’s sake and managed to get it to work on Steam Deck. With some tweaking of the controls and getting used to, it’s more than playable. 

That being said, it’s pretty boring. Progressing a horse’s skill takes a lot of training and the rounds are rather repetitive. Dressage is especially bad for this — it’s too little engagement and each round lasts way too long, and there’s barely any variety. 

There’s no user guide (wiki understandably isn’t complete), if you missed an explanation, you’re out of luck. I seem to remember training foals is the only way to age them up and have yet to have any progress with that. Over a decade ago when I first played this game, I had the same problem. Trial and error aren’t great options just out of the sheer number of mind-numbingly boring mini-games you have to go through to test what activity influences which stat. 

The controls and camera are rather clunky even for its time. 

That being said, the game is super charming. The series always had great characters and pretty deep stories. Part of what made the series so great is talking to the characters in your free time and getting to know them better, though in this particular game this aspect has kind of suffered. 

The town the story takes place in is beautiful, even though it’s pretty hard to navigate (atrocious camera angles!). All the little details are great, and don’t get me started on the cozy apartments — shame you can only stay in one during one walkthrough. 

Hard to decide if I could even recommend this game. I don’t think the story and the environments are worth the exercise in frustration that the gameplay is, but if you’re not a completionist, it’s could be a fun game! I’d come back to it every now and then to do those tedious training rounds (and quit when I see how many times I have to repeat them to progress). 

Like the characters, the story is another strong side of the game. It’s not exactly a great detective mystery, but I remember it being pretty engaging when I first played. 

All in all, it’s a very nostalgic horse game for me, and I’m glad you can still make it work on newer systems.

- The controls are JANKY and there's no way to change the keybinds to WASD.
- If you turn before you try to walk, you won't be able to walk. You have to walk forward and then turn while you're walking if you wanna turn.

THE GOOD:
The last truly great Heroes game before the series went full brain damage. Gorgeous (for 2006) 3D maps, six distinct factions that actually feel different, long meaty campaigns, and that pure “one more turn” heroin that made the series legendary. Battles look dramatic, the music slaps, and exploring the map while stacking armies never gets old. Still holds up as one of the best pure turn-based strategy experiences.

THE BAD:
Dialogue is pure cheese. Some missions are padded. Loading times and occasional bugs remind you it’s from 2006. The AI can be a bit wonky, and pure veterans of III will miss certain deeper systems.

THE UGLY:
You will lose an entire army because you got greedy on the adventure map. You will rage at a poorly timed bad luck streak. And yes, some of the voice acting is so dramatic it loops back around to comedy. Still worth every second.

THE VERDICT:
8.5/10
Classic turn-based fantasy strategy

This game is a lot of fun at first, but it becomes incredibly tedious over time.

I love the core concept, and I genuinely enjoyed the earlier campaigns. By the time I reached Zehir and the Academy campaign, though, I realized I wasn’t having fun anymore. The game had become a massive time sink.

The biggest problem is how poorly the mission objectives are explained. The game often gives you little or no indication of what you should prioritize, which direction you should take, or whether you’re operating under a hidden time limit. You can spend hours exploring, building your hero, and playing what seems like the logical strategy—only to discover that you were supposed to rush the objective from the beginning. By then, the enemy has become overwhelming and your only realistic option is to restart the entire mission.

That isn’t satisfying difficulty. It’s old-school trial and error combined with missions that can take hours to complete.

I don’t need a game to hold my hand, but it should at least hint at the right direction and clearly communicate mechanics that can permanently screw up a campaign. Heroes V frequently punishes you for decisions you had no reasonable way of knowing were wrong at the time.

If you have endless free time, enjoy consulting walkthroughs, and don’t mind repeatedly restarting missions after discovering that you went the wrong way or built your character incorrectly, then go for it. For me—and probably much of a modern audience—we simply don’t have time for that shit.

Before starting, ask yourself: Are you willing to lose several hours because the game poorly explained—or completely failed to explain—what it expected from you? Do you enjoy replaying the same long missions until you discover the specific strategy the designers secretly intended? Are you a masochist?

If the answer is yes, this game may be perfect for you.
