I did not have the time nor the computer needed to run this game upon its original release. This would have been a game I loved, and likely replayed several times had I played it at that time.

(IN SHORT: For less than the cost of a cup of coffee, even with the aged edges and two crashes, it was worth seeing the credits roll. I'm looking forward to completing the next two games).

The game certainly shows it's age, but one needs to judge it by the standards of its time. As an older gamer trending toward playing older games when I have time, it was worth the couple of bucks (which was for the entire series) and 7-9 hours to complete (the 47 hrs played were after I left the game running multiple times). This game likely sat in my library for over a decade, whenever it was Steam released, and I am happy I finally played through it. After a couple of decades of massive open world games, I am happy to see the credits roll in an old classic like this without needing to invest in dozens or even hundreds of gameplay hours. I like that the team attempted to create a more realistic approach to replicating a firefight which often relies on gaining fire superiority over one's enemy thus keeping the enemy pinned, but it doesn't always translate well during gameplay in this oldie. Establishing fire superiority and utilizing maneuverability were how I was trained to fight in the Army.

Unfortunately, I did experience two areas in the game that produced a repeating script error followed by a crash. Only one of the areas required me to find an answer on Google to troubleshoot, which consisted of me simply needing to leave my squad behind for a short run in a specific mission, so it could have been far worse.

For less than the cost of a cup of coffee, even with the aged edges and two crashes, it was worth seeing the credits roll. Looking forward to completing the next two after I playthrough Homefront.

My first time knowing about the existance of this series was playing Brothers in Arms 2: Global Front on my first smartphone back when I was a teen. More than a decade later, I finally experience the series proper, starting with Road to Hill 30.

I got to say, this game was a breath of fresh air than the standard WW2 FPS titles from COD and MOH. Like many had point out, it's a squad based tactical FPS than requires using some planning to progress rather than just going ham using brute force. As Sergeant Matt Baker, you take part in the Normandy Campaign completing missions by leading a squad of 2 teams (each for the majority consisting of 3 bros). The teams you are given are a gun team and an assault team for the most part. In some missions, you will get a tank (or two) as part of your squad to command.

As mentioned, the game is tactical...kind of like a mini RTS but you are on ground doing the commanding. You get to direct your bros to take cover, lay covering fire, close in to assault an enemy position or follow you around. How you use them is by observing the map for opportunities, which you can toggle to get a bird's eye view from your position or you can cycle to the views on your teams, enemy, or the checkpoint positions to get a general layout to plan your move. I admit the I rarely use the map view cause the navigation can be a bit wonky. Also unlike COD, your bros are VALUABLE and are your lifeline, it's best to keep most of them alive when progressing toward the end of the mission. Them dying (don't worry they will come back next mission unless scripted to die) early will actually make things difficult. I am often forced to manually do checkpoint restarts most of the time when that happens.

The bread and butter tactic for most of the campaign is usually straightforward, let the bros give covering fire to pin enemies down while you go or position another team to flank the pinned enemies. Speaking of pinning enemies with covering fire, I like the system where there will be a circle on an enemy team showing their status via three colours When the circle is red, they are a threat and free to shoot you, so suppressing them by firing will cause the circle to progressively turn grey like a clock. When it is grey, they are pinned and are forced into cover (also making it harder to kill them face on), that's where the flanking opportunity can be seized to take them out. Once you get the general idea, completing objectives is really fun. Though the sudden difficulty spike at the [spoiler] clearing the warehouse part in the Push into Carentan mission [/spoiler] was not me finest hour.

However, I have one gripe, the gunplay. Oh boy, it's absolutely terrible. I feel like I am a stormtrooper shooting each time I click the left mouse button. The recoil is so high you will miss most of your shots. Aiming down sight is like using a sniper rifle in COD, where your breathing causes the aim to keep swaying which means you will ALSO miss most of your shots...and you can't hold it. Enemies can be also quite spongy, from what I feel like, which make things worse. I get that they are going for realism but man, even at point blank close range you still can miss shots, that sucks man. But don't let me pointing this out deter you from getting this game, it's still a great and fun game. 

As for the story, I like it. It's pretty grounded in reality where Sergeant Matt Baker just a guy overwhelmed by the heavy responsibility of keeping his men alive in this hellish war. And oh boy you will tragically lose some bros permanently in the story. For the most part, I find it funny how he is a silent protag like COD protags in mission cutscenes yet is able to shout commands in gameplay [spoiler] until the ending...where we also finally get to see his face [/spoiler]. He also fully speaks when giving the opening narration for each mission that are sometimes existential and depressing. Another praise from me is that this game really make you remember who are the bros in your squad as well as the commanding officers. I like how is a nice change from the one man army and epic cinematics I am used to. I look forward on how the story progresses in the next 2 games.

Kolejna z mych ulubionych gier z dzieciństwa. Gra potrafi złapać za mordę klimatem, ale jednocześnie potrafi człowieka doprowadzić do szewskiej pasji. Zacznijmy od tego, co najlepsze, czyli oprawy. Grafika jest przepiękna w swojej swojskości, a otwarte przestrzenie, wioski, pola i lasy mają w sobie coś takiego, że człowiek czuje się niemal jak u siebie w domu. Wszystko ma swój urok i pomimo upływu lat nadal potrafi zachwycić. Do tego dochodzą realistycznie odwzorowane bronie, satysfakcjonujące strzelaniny, ciekawe cele misji i przyjemny system dowodzenia oddziałem, który pozwala poczuć się jak prawdziwy dowódca, a nie kolejny Rambo biegający po polu bitwy. No i fabuła, która jest absolutnie przepiękna, pouczająca i potrafi zostawić człowieka z refleksją na temat wojny, braterstwa i tego, ile kosztuje przetrwanie. Dodatkowe informacje o wojnie dostępne w menu to świetny dodatek, który pozwala dowiedzieć się czegoś więcej, zamiast bezmyślnie napier... strzelać ;)) do wszystkiego, co się rusza. Soundtrack również robi robotę i doskonale podkreśla klimat całej przygody. Niestety, kiedy przechodzimy do samej rozgrywki, zaczyna się festiwal absurdów. Przeciwnicy są momentami takimi gąbkami na pociski, że można wpakować w nich pół magazynka, a oni dalej stoją, jakby właśnie dostali delikatnego klapsa. Tymczasem gracz i jego drużyna potrafią padać od kilku trafień, co tworzy niezbyt przyjemną dysproporcję. Granaty? W większości przypadków szkoda na nie amunicji, której przecież nie ma, bo granaty są praktycznie bezużyteczne, chyba że wylądują centralnie pod nogami przeciwnika. Do tego dochodzą nieśmiertelni wrogowie, którzy potrafią w trakcie przeskakiwania przez płot prowadzić ostrzał, jakby właśnie trenowali do igrzysk olimpijskich w strzelaniu. Sztuczna inteligencja naszych sojuszników to osobna historia. Czasami człowiek zastanawia się, czy oni w ogóle wiedzą, po co tam przyszli, bo przeciwnicy potrafią zachowywać się rozsądniej niż nasi własni ludzie. Taktyka również szybko zaczyna nużyć, ponieważ większość starć sprowadza się do powtarzania podobnego schematu. tj. ciągłe, ale to ciągłe flankowanie. A wisienką na torcie jest celowanie, podczas którego bohater trzęsie rękami jak narkoman na głodzie, podczas gdy Niemcy potrafią pruć do nas bez najmniejszego przycelowania i trafiać z chirurgiczną precyzją. 
--
Na koniec warto wspomnieć o jednej rzeczy, która może odstraszyć osoby grające na nowszym sprzęcie. Gra potrafi się wykrzaczyć, zawiesić albo odmówić współpracy, ale niekoniecznie dlatego, że jest zwyczajnie zepsuta. Problem leży między innymi w starym silniku, który nie zawsze radzi sobie z wydajnością współczesnych komputerów. Rendering potrafi odbywać się tak szybko, że silnik nie nadąża z prawidłowym przetwarzaniem poszczególnych elementów, a skrypty odpowiedzialne za wydarzenia w misjach mogą zostać pominięte lub wykonane w niewłaściwej kolejności, bo komputer próbuje załatwić wszystko natychmiast. Nie traktuję tego jako klasycznego minusa samej gry, bo trudno winić ją za to, że współczesny sprzęt potrafi wyprzedzić założenia, pod które została zaprojektowana. Warto jednak mieć to na uwadze, jeśli planujecie wrócić do tej perełki po latach. Czasami trzeba trochę pokombinować z ustawieniami lub ograniczyć liczbę klatek na sekundę, żeby wszystko działało tak, jak powinno.

Consider it maybe at a heavy discount if you want.

I beat the game in under 9 hours, the game has a decent story, a paratrooper squad in the first 8 days after D-Day killing and getting killed, not really any hero antics or 1 man army stuff. Has some really great quotes, my favorite being at the start of the game before the drop 
"I never asked to be squad leader, but I had no choice. Now I've got thirteen soldiers under my command. Thirteen men depending on me to make the right decisions and not get them killed. Thirteen families relying on me to bring their husbands and sons home. Thirteen. Thirteen is not a lucky number."


However the game is mechanically very flawed with 3 issues:

1: Glitches and crashes, multiple times it crashed at the very end of a level, including the very last level in the game, at one point I thought I was going to have to restart as the guy you have to speak to got stuck on the curb in the street but for some reason I don't understand you can alt tab with the game running and he gets unstuck

2: Terrible gunplay- Your character sways like they are another drink from blacking out which makes aim difficult, when you are on target the guns are very inaccurate, struggling to hit stationary germans who are standing and shooting back, when you do hit the guns don't seem to do very much damage, unless you hit the head you need multiple hits with every gun besides the sniper rifle which you get on like 2 levels. This adds alot of unneeded challenge as in most other shooters you could just take the guy's head off when they stand up to shoot, or potentially just snipe the guy at the machine gun.

3: Wild difficulty spikes and poor level design, one level forces you to run through an open field under fire because germans just keep respawning, I spent probably 100 rounds from the above mentioned sniper dropping them before the game hinted I needed to just move. On one level I needed to hit 2 separate tanks with multiple panzerfausts and the 2nd tank can see the box you grab them from meaning you have to gamble on the tank not hitting the cannon round. On the final level you have no grenades which can be used as executioners for tanks nor any anti tank weapons, at multiple points having to just run down the road infront of a tank and pray it misses with the cannon.
It's fine but the gameplay is fairly repetitive at times as you look to flank the enemies while your squadmates give you covering fire and basically rinse and repeat for the entire campaign.

[h2]Иллюзорный шутер[/h2]

По началу, когда запускаешь Brothers in Arms будучи незнакомым с серией, получаешь примерно то, на что рассчитывал: боевик средней руки про Вторую мировую войну с какой-нибудь "своей фишечкой" и дефолтными для этого поджанра управлением, картинкой, сюжетом и геймдизайном.

[i]Казалось бы, что можно сделать не так...[/i]
А вот можно. Разработчики не смогли сделать интересные ситуации как в первых CoD с разнообразными уровнями (типов миссий ровно две — либо сражения в кустах, либо в городском ландшафте, попытку в какое-то разнообразие смогли выдавить из себя ровно один раз при обороне церкви) или разноплановые ситуации, как в MoH. А растягивать игру-то надо, иначе будет пробегаться за 4 часа.
Поэтому BiA начинает [u]создавать иллюзию сложности[/u]. В каждом сражении начинаешь чувствовать себя криворуким долбоёбом, который не может с "гаранда" попасть в 30 метрах. А разгадка кроется в трёх нюансах:
— стрельба сделана абсолютно рандомно, и судя по всему, шанс "успешного" выстрела скейлится от сложности. Для иллюзии прицел "реалистично" водит туда-сюда, играем мол, за рядового вояку а не суперсолдата. Вот только это нихрена не так, попасть можно целясь выше\ниже цели, как и промазать если навестись чОтко в жбан. Разброс при стрельбе от бедра почти на уровне Sniper Elite 1, где стоя прямо перед стеной и выпустив очередь из МП40 может сложится ощущение, что стрелял из дробовика, насколько шизанутый разброс.
— неимоверно кривые хитбоксы солдат за укрытиями. За какой-то тележкой можно прострелить в шлем, за какой-то насыпью нет. Вкупе с предыдущим фактором становится ещё веселее. 
— ну и ложка говна в бочке дёгтя, которая раскрывается если накрутить себе читом через консоль снайперку в миссиях, где её не должно быть: [u]уязвимость врагов строго предопределена разработчиками.[/u]
Если "вот тут и сейчас" игра не считает, что игрок должен кого-то убить — он никогда не убьёт. Просто потому что враг или за "неуязвимым" укрытием, либо на "недосягаемом" (30 метров, ага) расстоянии. И стреляя с обычного Томпсона это толком не понять, зато подобрав снайпу можно гыгыкнуть, выпустив 10 пуль в разные части тела и наблюдая нулевой эффект. Потому что бот или слишком далеко, или не пройдена КТ служащая разблокировкой его смертности.

А всё ради того, чтобы игрок не пытался вывести игру на собственном скилле, юзая "фишку" игрульки — "подавление". Это когда мы приказываем своим болванчикам стрелять по вражьим болванчикам, чтобы те сренькнули и мы пошли в обход с фланга расстреливать беззащитных тупых актёров. Почему актёров? Потому что они не пытаются быть злобными врагами, а просто играют свою роль.
Пехота никогда не попадёт в игрока с первого выстрела, даже если вышли в упор; пулемётчики до определенной границы в "конусе поражения" только создают вид свистящих пуль, на самом деле никогда даже не царапая (зато если шагнуть чуть дальше той самой грани, то сразу ваншот); танки не умеют сдавать назад и не рыпаются даже если пристрелить безоружного, блять, командира на башне. 

Т.е. вся игра сведена к одной простой цели: заебать игрока своей "фишечкой". Встречаем врагов, приказываем своим ботам набить шкалу подавления, бежим в обход рашить немчур. Всё, успех. Ну кроме миссий где танки должны биться с танками, это просто рулетка "у кого сильнее будет тупить ИИ", поэтому проще разбираться самому.

Сделали бы разрабы просто шутан про ВВ2, где все эти фокусы с отрядами и подавлением добавлены как соус, а не гарнир без нихуя — было бы съедобно. А так получился какой-то театр, где по 10 минут надо сидеть и стреляться рандомно летающими пульками, либо идти по строго заданному разрабами маршруту даже не пытаясь в "тактику", а окружающие боты по обе стороны изображают вид бурной деятельности. В результате ни нормально пострелять (дальше своего носа без оптики никого не убить), ни поиграться в стратежку (все решения прямолинейны и шаг влево шаг вправо почти всегда равны смерти).

Что точно хорошо, так это техническая часть. Заводится без проблем и патчей в 2к\180фпс, не лагает, не вылетает, не багуется.

TLDR:
Revolutionary for its time, Road to Hill 30 has aged gracefully in its story, but shows its age in shooting mechanics.

Pros:
- In an oversaturated genre, Road to Hill 30 sets itself apart through an intense and emotional storyline with some of the best voice acting in gaming history.  You'll genuinely care about Baker and his squad.
- Gritty combat feels frighteningly realistic, despite its age.  Ragdoll physics, impactful explosions, and armor/heavy weapons that can change the course of a battle instantly.  
- Map design is based off real world battles/locations and it feels very genuine.
- Incredible soundtrack, effects, and ambiance.

Cons:
- The shooting is frustrating due to weapon sway and exaggerated recoil.  I get they wanted to make the player feel like they were frantically in a battle and 'only human', but the reality is dumping a Thompson mag into 3 unsuspecting Germans should be possible... in Road to Hill 30, it isn't.
- Some brutal difficulty spikes feel unfair (even on easy).
- While the AI for enemies can catch you off guard for a game this age, the friendly AI leaves much to be desired.  Your brothers will run headfirst into MG-42 fire without warning or take cover in front of barriers...
- Requires some tweaking to get running on modern monitors. 

Overall: 8/10
Still holds up pretty well

Here I am yet again, replaying this game and the whole series for what has to be the 100th time.

Brothers in Arms was actually one of the first physical games I ever owned for my old big box computer, and I don't think I realized back then just how much this series would end up influencing me.

This game is a huge part of what made me fall in love with military history, strategy, World War II, and especially the Airborne and paratrooper units. 
That interest stayed with me for years, to the point where I eventually enlisted as a paratrooper myself and served for three years in my own country.

I also remember watching documentaries about the events and the unit on the History Channel around the same time, seeing the real history behind what I was playing, hearing from people connected to those events, and then going back into the game made the whole experience feel so much more meaningful.

I've replayed Road to Hill 30 more times than I can count, and somehow the story still gets to me. 
You genuinely become attached to the characters and the squad, even though the gameplay is relatively simple by today's standards, the combination of commanding your men, maneuvering, suppressing enemies, and actually having to think about what you're doing still feels incredibly satisfying.

But what really makes this game special isn't just the mechanics, It's the atmosphere, the characters, the history, and the feeling that you're following a group of soldiers through something much bigger than themselves.

This game was part of my childhood, but it also genuinely shaped one of the biggest interests in my life.

If you're a World War II nerd like me, especially if you're interested in the Airborne, military history, or tactical games, you owe it to yourself to play Brothers in Arms: Road to Hill 30 and the whole series really.

Hra je velmi dobrým odrazem stavu herního průmyslu v počátcích 21. století, kdy byly velmi populární druhoválečné hry a různé natahovací mechaniky. To ale není nic špatného, jenom bych s tím hned od začátku počítal.

Rozhodně Vás ale čeká velmi zajímavé a neobvyklé vyprávění příběhu, doplněné historickým kontextem a jinými bonusovými materiály, které rozhodně obohatí Vaše historické znalosti z této doby. Pokud se Vám navíc podaří vžít do hry, bude pro Vás ztráta vojáků opravdu něco znamenat, jako kdybyste byl skutečný seržant Baker. To jsou ale věci okolo a samotná hratelnost je prozatím trochu v mlze, což je ale účel. Ačkoliv je hra na pozadí úžasná, její herní mechaniky pokulhávají. To je primárně způsobeno repetitivností, kdy vše nové objevíte už asi v první třetině hry a po zbytek už jde o to samé, jen doplněné zajímavým příběhem.

V samotné hře je velmi malá variabilita, což je u taktické hry tohoto typu trochu škoda. Ačkoliv ovládáte jednotky, máte prakticky pouze dva typy – útočný a potlačující. Přesně takto se sice nejmenují, ale je asi jasné, jak fungují. Tím, že se souboje točí kolem mechaniky „potlač, obejdi a zabij“, se hra stává velmi jednotvárnou, čemuž nepomáhá ani stejnorodé prostředí, kde skoro každá mapa vypadá úplně stejně. Postupem času se nepřátelské jednotky stanou až nesnesitelně přesnými a možnosti krytí nedostatečnými. K tomu připočtěte, že ke konci hry mají Vaši vojáci často problém s hledáním cesty (pathfindingem), a vzniká tak obrovská frustrace z celého zážitku.

Rozhodně ale nechci hru vykreslit jako špatnou, jde opravdu o odraz doby, kdy hry byly na sílu těžké a konce často rozbité. Co je ale naprosto unikátní, a ještě jsem to nezmínil, je možnost rozkazovat na bojišti tanku. Ten slouží jako třetí jednotka, kterou máte v několika misích k dispozici, a ačkoliv je tato mechanika také často rozbitá, působí opravdu unikátně. Viděl jsem to pouze v tomto díle a následujícím, nikde jinde.

Pokud se chcete dostat do této herní trilogie, doporučil bych spíše začít zatím posledním dílem – Pekelnou dálnicí (Hell's Highway), jelikož je výrazně propracovanější a hratelností dostupnější. Pokud Vás to chytí, běžte i do tohoto a druhého dílu.

P.S.: Hru jsem hrál s komunitní češtinou. Jelikož oficiální překlad chybí, mohu tuto verzi vřele doporučit.

    [b] Графен [/b] ужасный даже для 2005 года (фир, колда 2, нфс мв и тд).

Что бы вы понимали, я включил читы и просто ходил в упор врагов расстреливал, что бы пройти быстрее уровни и посмотреть сюжет. ДАЖЕ В УПОР я попадал где-то 60% пуль. Как работают патроны я так и не понял, вроде бы у тебя магазины, вместо общего кол-ва пуль, но при этом можно раз 5 перезарядится и только потом магазин потратится. 

    [b] Унылая тактическая составляющая [/b] По сути все, для чего она нужна это либо приказать своим гномам стрелять на подавление и самому обходить, либо наоборот. [h1]O jogo tem realmente alguns pontos bons:[/h1]

[b]Atmosfera e Realismo:[/b] Focado na história real da 101ª Divisão Aerotransportada, o jogo traz uma ambientação crua, sem o heroísmo exagerado de outros shooters da época. A tensão da guerra é palpável, você não não tem música é apenas o barulho da guerra que da uma ótima imersão.
[b]Jogabilidade Tática:[/b] O sistema de "Fixar e Flanquear" transforma o tiroteio em um verdadeiro jogo de xadrez militar, confesso que não é pra todos, eu particulamente gosto.
[b]Narrativa e Personagens:[/b] Acompanhar o Sargento Matt Baker e o peso psicológico de liderar seus homens [b]EXTREMAMENTE BURROS[/b] cria um vínculo genuíno com o esquadrão. Você realmente se importa com quem morre como uma babá.

[h1]Vamos aos pontos negativos:[/h1]

- A inteligência artificial dos aliados às vezes falha, deixando seus homens expostos ou travados em coberturas ruins.
- Comandos de esquadrão em ambientes muito fechados ou cheios de destroços podem ser um pouco desajeitados.
- O ritmo do jogo é lento por natureza; se você entrar querendo correr e atirar estilo Call of Duty, vai morrer em segundos.
- Os gráficos e as texturas, embora revolucionários para 2005, envelheceram bastante e podem parecer datados hoje em dia. Mas eu ainda acho lindos, principalmente na parte do por do sol ao lado do rio.

[h1]O que poderia ser melhor?[/h1]

[b]Maior variedade nas mecânicas de combate:[/b] Depois de entender a lógica de suprimir e flanquear, quase todos os confrontos seguem a mesma fórmula.

[b]Uma precisão um pouco melhor nas armas:[/b] O "spread" (espalhamento dos tiros) é tão realista que às vezes irrita, fazendo você errar tiros bizarramente curtos, e da uma estranha sensação de que a mira não serve de nada.

[b]Um puta spoiler de quem morre com 1 minuto de jogo [/b]

[h1]Devo jogar?[/h1]

Com certeza. É um clássico indispensável para quem busca um shooter militar estratégico, maduro e focado em liderança real de esquadrão. Nota 8.5/10. “Suprimir, flanquear e rezar para o estilhaço não te pegar.”

Bônus:

- "Eu vou pega-los por trás. Por aqui. E por aqui. E depois, eu vou dar a volta... e vou entrar com tudo pela frente. O que? Vocês estão rindo de quê?" Baker explicando suas táticas ao esquadrão.
- DOUBLE TIMEEEEE
- Baseado em relatos e fotos reais de vilarejos da Normandia.
- Nada de regeneração automática de vida no meio do tiroteio: errou, pagou caro.
- A física dos tiros e o impacto dos cenários destrutíveis eram impressionantes para a época.
- "Suprima aquele ninho de metralhadora AGORA, soldado!" gritos de desespero ao som de morteiros

Obrigado Gearbox Software e Ubisoft <3 Foi uma experiência incrível!

За 75 гривень (або 30 зі знижкою) це дуже і дуже хороша гра. Але є деякі але, а також пару застережень.

Графіка: дуже стара, не красива для більшості зумерів, але все одно стильна та ідеально передає атмосферу, кривавість також входить у набір хоча і навіть не близько до калл оф дьюті блек опс чи Waw.

Сюжет: Історія у грі дуже хороша, вона передає переживання головного героя і його настрій та реакцію на те що відбувається навколо нього. Персонажі прикольні і мають свої особливості за якими цікаво спостерігати, гра вміє нагнітати атмосферу та показує війну по справжньому (хоча і з обмеженнями)

Геймплей: Тут починаються головні проблеми, наприклад стрільба яка є дуже поганою, на це можна підзабити через вік гри але зброя не влучає 60%-75% набоїв в упор і часто саме це буде причиною вашої смерті (особливо в останній місії), але така стрільба частково потрібна була щоб зробити керування своїм загоном ефективним та цікавим. Гра дуже репетативна але знову ж таки тоді нічого краще не могли придумати для цієї гри, більшість часу гравець керує загоном солдатів який є кращою зброєю ніж сам вогнепал гравця і керування ними вимагає одних і тих самих дій протягом всієї гри (тактика ніколи не змінюється). Керування бійцями зрозуміле і просте, але вони іноді туплять (для мене це далеко не так часто траплялось як для інших людей тому є підозра що вони просто погані командири, але у фінальнії місії в мене згоріла дупа від дурості юнітів, а також я втратив деяких бійців на інших рівнях через їх нездатність ефективно зайняти укриття). Вороги у грі дуже погані, вони не різноманітні (можна опустити це через вік гри), а також неймовірно швидкі і точні, вони влучають у ціль швидше та краще за гравця і реагують занадто швидко, навіть коли ще не помітили гравця. Пройшов я гру на високій складності (максимальна розблокується тільки після проходження на високій), на цій складності в мене майже не виникло проблем окрім однієї з останніх місій де я просто не міг зрозуміти який маршрут треба обрати і гра не активовувала деякі скріпти через високий фпс, а також в останній місії в мене згоріла срака бо там повний абсурд і потреба у великій удачі. Тому краще грати на середній якщо ви поганий гравець чи просто легко піддаєтесь злості.

Технічний стан: загалом все нормально, але довелось обмежити ФПС на одній з місій до 60 бо інакше боти не могли активувати скріпт так як застрягали на бордюрі.

Висновок: Гра точно варта своїх грошей, але тільки якщо гравець готовий терпіти технічні обмеження ігор того часу та жахливу стрільбу.

Помню как в детстве играл в неё, и тогда она казалась мне лучше и в плане сюжета и геймплея, но видимо игра плохо состарилась, стрельба никакая, командование топорное, союзники которыми командуешь бывает не выполняют команды. В общем игра хороша для своего времени, но сейчас не стоит в неё заходить, даже если хочется ностальгии, только испортите свои воспоминания о ней.

Oui oui mille fois oui. C'est ça qu'on veut comme jeu. Et pas des jeux fan service bourré de micro transactions. Que les developpeurs reviennent à cette tradition de faire des jeux pour que les gens s'amusent et non pour qu'ils dépensent.
J'avais ce jeu sur XBOX première du nom quand j'étais gamin. Quel plaisir de le refaire sur PC. On pourrait penser que c'est la nostalgie qui parle et c'est en partie vrai. Mais BiA c'est bien plus que de la nostalgie.

C'est avant tout une histoire, l'histoire de la plus grande opération militaire de tout les temps. Parmi tout ces milliers de soldats vous êtes le chef d'un petit groupe que vous devrez diriger pour tenter de les faire survivre dans cet enfer qu'a du être le bocage normand. 
BiA n'est pas un FPS classique ou vous avancez et tirez. Ici la stratégie est primordiale, à vous de placer vos hommes au bon endroit et de donner les bons ordres, car vous ne pourrez pas foncer seul et tête baissée pour vous emparer d'une place forte. Pour diriger vos hommes c'est simple, vous avez un groupe d'appui-feu et un groupe d'assaut. A vous de switcher entre les deux pour établir vos stratégies, mettre la pression à l'ennemi (car oui les ennemis arrivent par groupe, comme vos hommes et ces groupes d'ennemi ont une jauge de moral) et décidez si vous allez les flanker ou les charger. Attention, vos hommes peuvent mourir aussi (pas de manière définitive je vous rassure, vous retrouvez vos hommes à la mission suivante) et vous retrouvez avec des hommes en moins mettra votre mission en péril. Bref le gameplay est original, bien pensé et plaisant à jouer. On aurait aimer une IA un peu plus agressive qui vous met aussi des coups de pression et qui tente aussi de vous charger ou de vous flanker mais pour le reste rien à redire. 

Graphiquement les plus jeunes diront que ça date un peu, et à raison le jeu est sorti en 2005, mais pour du 2005 c'est plus que correct. Vraiment il faut se rendre compte que pour l'époque un jeu avec cette patte graphique c'est exceptionnel, c'est pourquoi je vous invite à passer outre les graphismes dépassés. 

Au niveau de l'histoire on tient une petite pepite, chaque niveau est entrecoupé de fond noir ou votre personnage parlera de sa vie, de ses compagnons d'armes, puis petite cinématique avec vos hommes qui discutent de sujet legers avant que ça ne se mette à tirer, exploser ou que votre commandant vous donne votre ordre de mission. Chacun des personnages à une personnalité bien distincte, et on finit par s'attacher à chacun d'eux au fil de l'histoire, et vous aurez un pincement au coeur lorsqu'ils passeront l'arme à gauche (et oui la guerre est cruelle et ne fait aucune distinction, tout le monde ne reviendra pas vivant)
Mais le coup de génie dans l'histoire de BiA, c'est que chaque niveau est inspiré d'une opération réelle qui à vraiment eu lieu dans l'histoire de la vérité véritable. Car oui la 101eme aéroportée à vraiment existée et à vraiment été parachutée sur la Normandie. Gearbox à voulu rendre hommage à ces hommes qui ont risqué leurs vies pour délivrer un pays qui n'était pas le leur, et de côté la c'est réussi. Petit bonus, pour les férus d'histoire, vous pourrez même débloquer des documents, des photos, des vidéos making-of et interview qui explique comment les équipes de Gearbox se sont inspirées de la réalité pour créer certains niveaux, et même des archives de cette époque là. 

Bref ce jeu est injustement méconnu et fait partie de ces jeux que l'on doit faire au moins une fois dans sa vie.

A fantastic gameplay concept that gets bogged down by terrible execution. I look forward to trying later games in the series, where the formula has hopefully been improved. When it's fun, it's very fun, but most of the time it's a tedious, frustrating slog. Nostalgia blinders is the only explanation for this game's popularity.

-Mechanics/Map Design:  Unfair and uninteresting. The suppression-and-flank mechanic is the only one that works in this game, and they banked everything on it. Too bad you can rarely take advantage of it. It's like getting a really cool car that always breaks down. The "hallway" nature of maps makes it impossible to really take advantage of it most of the time, so you just end up shooting at one another behind a wall anyway or making a dangerous charge. You could say this was meant to force you to take losses, which would've been interesting, but the game cripples you for doing so. Enemies are either incredibly incompetent or deadshot snipers shooting a panzerfaust from the hip while running. It's not fun.

-Checkpoints:  This game is in desperate need of a quicksave system or more frequent checkpoints. Given the unfairness above, trudging through the same 20 minute sequence repeatedly is boring and frustrating.

-Embarrassing Story Presentation: The wannabe Saving Private Ryan/Band of Brothers vibe is cringe. The actors did a decent job, the writers less so, and the director did the worst. Character deaths have very little impact because the game only throws some exposition at you instead of building a bond with your squadmates. Some are introduced for moments only to be killed in a sappy, dramatic scene, but you barely know who they are besides an NPC with bad pathing. So many things don't fit or become obnoxious. Soldiers yell constantly for instance, even when you're just standing there in complete safety, because there's no context marker on their lines, which they're forced to give every so often. The whole thing comes off as bad fan fiction and sloppy.

-Weapon Accuracy:  Yes, the point is to command your units rather than do most of the fighting yourself. However, even a battle rifle is less accurate than a shotgun, shots spreading randomly until you're within 10ft of the enemy. This is not an exaggeration. This was done to force the suppression mechanic, but it was a weak method of doing so.

If you enjoy long playing games for WWII submarine warfare, this is the game for you. It requires patience and working toward using tactics to attack, use your crew and complete missions in a timely manner. Highly recommend.

Silent Hunter: Wolves of the Pacific is a detailed naval warfare simulation developed by Ubisoft Romania and published by Ubisoft. As the fourth installment in the long-running Silent Hunter franchise, the game shifts the focus of submarine warfare to the Pacific theater of World War II. Unlike earlier entries that centered on German U-boats in the Atlantic, this installment places players in command of United States Navy fleet submarines operating against the Imperial Japanese Navy. The game aims to recreate the tension, strategy, and long periods of anticipation associated with submarine warfare while maintaining a strong emphasis on historical authenticity. Through its combination of complex simulation systems and immersive presentation, the game attempts to capture the responsibilities and challenges faced by real submarine commanders during the war.

The campaign spans the years between 1941 and 1945 and places players in the role of a submarine captain tasked with disrupting Japanese naval operations across the vast Pacific Ocean. From the moment players begin their first patrol, they become responsible for navigating enormous distances while searching for enemy shipping lanes and convoys. Missions are not presented as simple scripted scenarios but instead occur within a dynamic wartime environment where ships travel along simulated trade routes. This system allows each patrol to feel unpredictable, as players may encounter merchant vessels, heavily defended convoys, or powerful warships depending on their location and timing.

The gameplay revolves around the careful operation of a submarine and the strategic decisions required to survive in hostile waters. Players must manage navigation, monitor sonar contacts, calculate torpedo firing solutions, and control the submarine’s depth and speed. A key part of the experience is the tension created by stealth-based gameplay. Submarines are extremely effective when undetected, but they are vulnerable once enemy forces become aware of their presence. Approaching an enemy convoy requires patience and precise maneuvering, as a single mistake can expose the submarine to escort ships equipped with sonar and depth charges.

One of the defining mechanics of the game is the torpedo attack system. Players must carefully analyze enemy ship movements before launching an attack. This involves estimating the target’s speed, distance, and direction in order to determine the correct firing angle. On lower realism settings the game can assist with these calculations, but players who choose higher realism levels must perform these tasks manually. Successfully striking a ship with torpedoes can be incredibly satisfying, particularly when a well-planned attack sinks multiple vessels within a convoy.

However, the aftermath of an attack is often the most dangerous moment of a mission. Once torpedoes hit their targets, enemy escort ships begin searching for the submarine responsible for the attack. Destroyers equipped with sonar sweep the surrounding waters while launching depth charges in an attempt to destroy the hidden submarine. During these tense encounters, players must remain calm and maneuver carefully through the depths while avoiding detection. The constant threat of depth charge explosions creates some of the most intense moments in the entire game.

The career campaign serves as the centerpiece of the experience. Players begin as a relatively inexperienced submarine commander and gradually rise in rank through successful patrols. Each mission contributes to the broader war effort by weakening enemy shipping lines and disrupting supply routes. Radio messages throughout the campaign keep players informed about major wartime events and shifting naval strategies, reinforcing the sense that their actions are part of a much larger conflict. This dynamic campaign system helps maintain immersion by allowing the war to evolve around the player rather than forcing them through a predetermined sequence of events.

Crew management also plays a significant role in the gameplay. Each submarine is staffed by a crew responsible for operating sonar equipment, loading torpedoes, maintaining navigation systems, and performing repairs. Over time, crew members gain experience that improves their efficiency and responsiveness during combat situations. Skilled crew members can reload torpedoes faster, detect enemy ships more quickly, and handle emergency situations with greater effectiveness. This system adds another strategic layer to the game, as the performance of the crew can determine whether a mission ends in success or disaster.

The game offers several different submarine classes used by the United States Navy during World War II. Each vessel has unique characteristics such as speed, durability, and torpedo capacity. As players progress through the campaign, they may gain access to more advanced submarines with improved technology. These upgrades reflect the historical development of submarine warfare during the war, as American submarines became more effective through technological improvements and refined tactics.

Visually, the game delivers a convincing depiction of naval warfare for its time. The submarine interiors are fully modeled, allowing players to move between compartments such as the control room, torpedo room, and sonar station. Watching crew members operate equipment inside the submarine helps reinforce the sense of commanding a functioning warship rather than simply controlling a vehicle. Above the surface, the ocean environments are vast and atmospheric, with dynamic weather conditions that can influence visibility and combat tactics. Storms, fog, and nighttime patrols all add additional challenges to submarine operations.

Sound design is equally important in creating immersion. Much of submarine warfare depends on listening for subtle audio cues, and the game reflects this by emphasizing sonar pings, distant engine noises, and the creaking of the submarine hull under pressure. When enemy destroyers begin dropping depth charges nearby, the sound of explosions echoing through the water creates a powerful sense of urgency. These moments are often accompanied by the tense silence of underwater navigation, reinforcing the feeling of isolation deep beneath the ocean.

The game features a wide variety of enemy ships, each with different levels of threat. Merchant vessels carrying supplies are common targets and can often be destroyed with minimal risk. However, convoys protected by destroyers or cruisers present a much greater challenge. These escort ships actively search for submarines and will aggressively attack once they detect a threat. Deciding when to attack and when to remain hidden becomes a crucial tactical decision during longer patrols.

Overall, Silent Hunter: Wolves of the Pacific remains one of the most respected submarine simulation games ever created. Its dynamic campaign system, realistic gameplay mechanics, and immersive presentation combine to create an experience that faithfully recreates the tension and strategy of underwater combat. While its complexity and slower pacing may not appeal to every player, those who appreciate historical simulations and tactical naval warfare will find it to be a deeply engaging and rewarding experience. Through its careful attention to historical detail and gameplay depth, the game successfully places players in the role of a World War II submarine commander navigating one of the most dangerous theaters of the war.

Do not play this game unless you play with the GWX Knight's Cross Edition megamod, which makes the game playable on modern systems and widescreen monitors.
I've owned this game since its original release back in 2005, before steam existed. So let's just say Steam's estimate on my hours played is woefully inaccurate. I also play with the aforementioned (free) megamod and SH3 Commander which makes it playable outside of the Steam Client. My real playtime must run into a few thousand hours.
When SH3 first game out in 2005 it was a fairly mediocre U-boat sim upgraded from its predecessor. But the vanilla game felt like an empty world, with empty ports, and although more immersive than its earlier renditions, it needed a lot of work. Then from the Subsim modding community came the Grey Wolves Expansion (GWX) which turned the game into far and away the best submarine simulator game ever made, if you don't mind playing the German side in the Battle of the Atlantic during WW2.
SH4 shifted focus to the American side in the Pacific War, which just wasn't as interesting, and then SH5 went back to its roots giving us much better graphics, but a much crappier game that was more or less abandoned by the developers as soon as it was released. Even with megamods such as The Wolves of Steel (TWOS) keeping SH5 alive, it just wasn't the same.
Never mind, we still had SH3 and the GWX expansion, right?
But as time went on, computer systems got better, operating systems changed, monitors went widescreen, and SH3 even with GWX began to get old and not as functional on modern computers without an awful lot of work. For quite a few years it had slipped by the wayside and became all but a distant memory of how good things had once been.
Fast forward to 2026 and thanks to the Subsim modding community's passion and dedication, the full glory of SH3 with GWX is perfectly playable again, and fully upgraded to widescreen monitors with the GWX Knight's Cross Edition megamod. SH3 is back on top!
Do not play this game without it.

Silent Hunter III is a highly detailed World War II submarine simulation developed and published by Ubisoft, with development led by Ubisoft Romania. Released in 2005 for PC, the game quickly became one of the most respected entries in the long-running Silent Hunter franchise and remains widely regarded as one of the most immersive submarine simulations ever created. Unlike many action-focused war games, Silent Hunter III emphasizes authenticity, patience, and tactical thinking. Players are placed in the role of a German U-boat commander during the Battle of the Atlantic, experiencing firsthand the challenges of underwater warfare in one of the most dangerous and strategically important theaters of World War II.

The game begins with the player assuming command of a German submarine in the Kriegsmarine, the naval arm of Nazi Germany. The campaign typically starts in the early stages of the war, when German submarines were highly effective against Allied shipping. From the outset, the player is responsible for leading their submarine and crew through multiple patrol missions across the Atlantic Ocean. Rather than presenting a rigid set of scripted missions, the game uses a dynamic campaign system that simulates naval activity across the entire Atlantic theater. Convoys travel between ports, naval escorts patrol shipping lanes, and the war progresses according to historical timelines. This system creates a living battlefield where every patrol can unfold differently depending on the player’s actions and the unpredictable movement of enemy ships.

During each patrol, players are assigned a designated grid sector of the Atlantic to monitor. Once there, they are free to operate independently within that region, searching for enemy merchant vessels and convoys transporting supplies to Allied nations. Much of the gameplay revolves around locating targets using hydrophones, visual observation, and careful navigation. Because the ocean is vast and ships may travel for long periods without encountering anything, players must remain patient while scanning the horizon or listening for distant engine noises through sonar equipment. These long stretches of quiet tension are interrupted by moments of intense action when a convoy is finally located.

Combat in Silent Hunter III focuses primarily on torpedo warfare. Successfully attacking enemy ships requires careful planning and accurate calculations. Players must determine the speed, distance, and direction of enemy vessels in order to calculate the correct torpedo firing angle. The game offers varying levels of realism that allow players to either automate these calculations or perform them manually using traditional naval targeting methods. At the highest realism settings, the process becomes a complex and rewarding simulation where every torpedo fired is the result of deliberate calculations and precise positioning.

Approaching a convoy safely is often the most challenging part of an engagement. Merchant ships are typically protected by escort vessels such as destroyers and corvettes, which are equipped with sonar and depth charges designed to hunt submarines. Players must maneuver carefully beneath the ocean’s surface or approach at night while surfaced to remain undetected. Once torpedoes are launched, escort ships will immediately begin searching for the submarine responsible for the attack. Depth charges may be dropped in rapid succession, creating powerful underwater explosions that can damage or destroy the submarine if it fails to escape. These moments of desperate evasion are some of the most intense sequences in the game, as players dive deeper into the ocean and attempt to move silently while avoiding detection.

The game also places a strong emphasis on crew management. Each submarine is staffed with a crew responsible for operating various stations such as navigation, sonar detection, torpedo loading, and engine maintenance. Crew members gain experience over time, improving their efficiency and reaction speed during missions. As the campaign progresses, players can assign crew members to specific tasks and promote them based on their performance. This progression system adds a personal dimension to the campaign, as players become invested in the survival and success of their crew over multiple patrols.

One of the most immersive features of Silent Hunter III is its fully modeled submarine interior. Players can move between several compartments of the vessel, including the control room, torpedo room, and radio station. Watching crew members operate equipment while alarms sound and orders are shouted during combat helps create the feeling of commanding a living submarine rather than simply controlling a vehicle. This design choice greatly enhances the sense of immersion, particularly during high-stress moments such as depth charge attacks or emergency repairs.

The visual presentation of the game was highly impressive at the time of its release. The ocean environment is vast and atmospheric, with dynamic weather conditions and realistic day-night cycles affecting visibility during patrols. Stormy seas can conceal submarines from enemy detection, while clear skies and calm waters may expose them to aircraft patrols or escort ships. The ship models themselves are carefully detailed, representing various types of Allied vessels that players may encounter during the campaign.

Sound design plays an equally important role in creating tension. Submarine warfare often depends on subtle audio cues, and the game captures this aspect effectively. The creaking of the submarine hull, the hum of diesel engines, and the distant sounds of propellers moving through water all contribute to the atmosphere. When destroyers begin searching for the submarine, the unmistakable ping of enemy sonar echoes through the water, signaling that danger is close. The thunderous blasts of depth charges exploding nearby are among the most nerve-wracking moments in the entire game.

Enemy encounters vary greatly depending on the situation. Players may attack isolated cargo ships transporting supplies across the Atlantic, or they may attempt more dangerous assaults against heavily defended convoys. Each target requires different tactics, and deciding whether to engage or avoid combat becomes an important strategic decision. Attacking a convoy can yield significant rewards but also carries a much higher risk of detection and destruction.

Despite its many strengths, the game’s depth and realism can make it challenging for newcomers. The interface includes numerous instruments, charts, and systems that players must learn to interpret correctly. Navigating the submarine, calculating torpedo solutions, and coordinating the crew requires time and practice. Additionally, the slower pacing of submarine patrols may feel unusual for players who are accustomed to faster-paced combat games.

However, these elements are also what make the experience so compelling for simulation enthusiasts. The long stretches of quiet patrol build suspense, making the moment when a convoy finally appears on the horizon incredibly satisfying. Executing a perfectly timed torpedo attack after hours of searching creates a sense of accomplishment rarely found in other games.

Overall, Silent Hunter III remains one of the most influential submarine simulation games ever produced. Its dynamic campaign system, detailed simulation mechanics, and immersive atmosphere combine to create a uniquely authentic depiction of World War II naval warfare. Although its complexity and deliberate pacing may not appeal to every player, those who appreciate historical simulations and tactical strategy will find it to be an exceptionally rewarding experience. Even years after its release, the game continues to be celebrated as one of the definitive submarine warfare simulations in gaming history.

Silent Hunter: Wolves of the Pacific – U-Boat Missions is a submarine warfare simulation expansion developed by Ubisoft Romania and published by Ubisoft. Designed as an expansion to Silent Hunter 4: Wolves of the Pacific, the game expands the original experience by introducing a completely new campaign centered around German submarines operating far from Europe during World War II. While the base game focuses primarily on American submarines in the Pacific theater, this expansion shifts the perspective to the German Kriegsmarine and its long-range operations in the Indian Ocean. By introducing new missions, submarines, gameplay systems, and strategic elements, the expansion significantly broadens the depth of the original simulation while maintaining the series’ reputation for realism and attention to historical detail.

The campaign is set during the later years of World War II and focuses on the historical operations of the German “Monsun Gruppe,” a group of U-boats deployed to Southeast Asia to disrupt Allied shipping routes. These submarines operated thousands of miles from Germany, launching patrols from ports in territories controlled by Axis allies such as Penang, Singapore, Jakarta, and Surabaya. Players take on the role of a German submarine commander tasked with navigating the vast waters of the Indian Ocean and targeting Allied supply lines. The campaign unfolds across a dynamic wartime map where convoys, escorts, and patrols move across the ocean as part of a living strategic environment. This historical setting gives the expansion a unique identity within the series and highlights a lesser-known aspect of World War II naval warfare.

The gameplay remains firmly rooted in the complex simulation mechanics that define the Silent Hunter franchise. Players command every aspect of their submarine’s operations, from plotting navigation routes to managing torpedo attacks and maintaining stealth during dangerous encounters with enemy ships. Depending on the chosen realism settings, players can automate many of these tasks or handle them manually for a deeper simulation experience. At higher realism levels, submarine warfare becomes a careful exercise in calculation and patience. Players must determine torpedo trajectories, estimate enemy speeds and distances, and launch attacks with precise timing to successfully hit their targets.

One of the defining aspects of the game is the tension created by underwater stealth. Submarines are powerful but fragile vessels, capable of devastating attacks yet extremely vulnerable if detected. Players often spend long periods tracking convoys while remaining hidden beneath the ocean’s surface. Using periscopes, sonar, and hydrophones, commanders must gather information about enemy movements before launching a carefully planned attack. Once torpedoes are fired, the situation can quickly become dangerous as escort ships begin searching for the submarine. Destroyers equipped with sonar and depth charges can transform a successful attack into a desperate fight for survival.

The dynamic campaign system plays a crucial role in maintaining immersion. Rather than presenting a strictly linear sequence of missions, the campaign simulates an ongoing war where enemy ships move across the map independently of the player. Convoys travel along trade routes, and naval forces respond to changing circumstances across the theater of war. Players receive updates through radio transmissions describing major events occurring elsewhere in the conflict. This system creates the feeling that each patrol is part of a much larger global struggle, adding narrative context to the player’s actions.

The expansion introduces several new gameplay features that enhance the strategic dimension of submarine warfare. As players gain experience and increase their rank, they gain access to additional resources that can support their operations. These resources include reconnaissance aircraft capable of locating enemy convoys and allied naval forces that can be directed to assist in attacking heavily defended targets. This strategic support system allows players to influence events beyond their own submarine, introducing a broader tactical perspective that was less prominent in the original game.

Another notable addition is the introduction of specialized crew members known as heroes. These characters are inspired by historical naval figures and provide unique bonuses to the submarine’s performance. Some heroes improve torpedo accuracy, while others enhance crew efficiency or increase survivability during emergencies. Managing these crew members becomes an important part of the campaign, as their abilities can dramatically affect the outcome of dangerous encounters.

The expansion also adds new submarines and equipment representing the German navy’s technology. These vessels differ in speed, durability, and weapon systems, allowing players to experience different approaches to submarine warfare. Later stages of the campaign introduce more advanced technology reflecting the evolving nature of naval combat during the final years of the war. Improvements such as enhanced radar systems and upgraded detection equipment add new tactical possibilities, particularly when tracking enemy convoys across large areas of ocean.

Visually, the game presents detailed environments both inside and outside the submarine. Players can move through various compartments of the vessel, observing crew members performing their duties while monitoring instruments and equipment. On the surface, the game recreates the vastness of the ocean with dynamic weather conditions, shifting waves, and realistic lighting that changes with the time of day. Storms, fog, and darkness can all affect visibility, influencing the tactics players use during patrols and attacks.

The sound design contributes significantly to the game’s atmosphere. Submarine warfare relies heavily on sound, and the game reflects this by emphasizing audio cues throughout the experience. The distant hum of ship engines, the echoing pings of enemy sonar, and the creaking of the submarine hull all help create an immersive sense of tension. When destroyers begin dropping depth charges nearby, the explosive blasts reverberating through the water create some of the most intense moments in the game.

Encounters with enemy ships provide a wide variety of tactical challenges. Players may attack vulnerable cargo ships carrying vital supplies or attempt riskier assaults on convoys protected by multiple escorts. Each type of ship behaves differently and requires careful consideration when planning an attack. A lone merchant vessel may be destroyed with minimal risk, but convoys defended by destroyers can become extremely dangerous engagements where stealth and patience are essential for survival.

Overall, Silent Hunter: Wolves of the Pacific – U-Boat Missions is a substantial expansion that enriches the already detailed world of Silent Hunter 4. By introducing a new campaign perspective, additional mechanics, and deeper strategic systems, it provides a fresh experience for players who enjoyed the original game. The combination of historical authenticity, immersive simulation mechanics, and tense submarine combat makes it one of the more compelling naval warfare experiences available. While its complexity may limit its accessibility for casual players, dedicated simulation fans will find it to be an engaging and rewarding portrayal of World War II submarine warfare.

I am only just embarking on my first proper mission so I cannot comment on how that will go, but from my protracted time in the submarine school I think SH4 is really enjoyable and I would recommend it. The graphics are not up to today's ultra-high realism standard but the game is still highly immersive. On my first exercise I stupidly surfaced more or less right next to an enemy destroyer and it was a genuinely scary experience! The walk-around interior in the stock game is by default limited to the control room and conning tower, however you can easily conduct a mission using the charts, sonar, radar, periscopes and the torpedo data computer in first-person mode. I personally think is a big plus point and if you turn off 'automatic targeting' then your campaigns will be about as hard as they probably were in real life. Sinking a ship with just the deck gun is particularly satisfying and the sinking animation itself is very impressive. You can even dip the external camera under the water to see the vessel heading for the sea bed, complete with collapsing bulkhead and exploding boiler noises. Dipping the camera underwater when you are in shallow water is also a sobering experience as you see rocks looming out of the murk just a few feet from the hull. Although you play as the captain, selecting a new course may still result in the sub staying on it's existing heading if you have allowed the crew in the control room to fall asleep. Selecting the right crew with the right skills for each station is an important aspect of the game. I do recommend installing a couple of basic third-party mods, one to provide a larger protractor on the chart display and one to make the telegraph and compass dials larger and easier to read. There are plenty of other free mods covering things like changing the chart style to adjusting the field of view of the periscopes. You'll find these mods on the Subsim Radio Room forum where there is also a great community of seasoned Silent Hunter players who, in my experience, are more than happy to help newbies.There are also 'mega-mods' for SH4 like FOTRSU and TMO which dramatically modify the gameplay and increase both the graphics and operational realism level for each mission. On a side note I also think the music is great... I mean really good. The musical theme changes dynamically to suit the action and it never seems to get tiresome although you can of course turn it off. I did think for a while that the fuel gauge was broken as it never seemed to move but it turns out that subs can travel 11,000 nautical miles on a full tank so it takes a while for the gauge to start going down. Sadly, you can't shoot the seagulls with the anti-aircraft gun, but that's the only downside I have found so far.

Attack conveys of shipping while avoiding destroyers and aerial attacks. Planning an attack can be a time-consuming and stressful exercise: Tracking your targets with the periscope, positioning your sub and choosing precisely the right moment to fire your precious torpedoes.

For added realism, you can programme the Torpedo Data Computer (TDC) yourself using target speed, Angle on the Bow (AOB), torpedo running depth and impact triggers. There's plenty of information on this over at the subsim website as well as tutorial videos on YouTube.

Working this all out with a notepad and protractor next to the computer is an experience worth trying, as a successful hit feels even more sweet given all the effort you put in! You also get a small sense of what it must have been like for the submariners who did this in real life, and the the dangers they faced.

In SH3 you are in command of a revolutionary German U-boat in terms of technology and use of minimum resources/manpower. 概略
　第二次世界大戦下に太平洋で戦ったドイツ海軍モンスーン部隊が主役の拡張パック。

・操作性
　操作は非常に簡易化されてはいるが予備知識を要求される部分が多く慣れるまでは接敵から雷撃までが困難で最低限の知識が必要。

・難易度
　難易度は前述の予備知識を要求される部分が多いので難易度の選択は出来るが初心者向きではなく英語力も必要なため敷居は高い。
　
・ビジュアル
　現在のゲームと比べれば見劣りする部分も多いが綺麗な部類で波や天候の表現は素晴らしい反面、陸地の表現が非常に簡素で部分的に評価が難しい。

・サウンド
　潜水艦ゲームとしては音のバリエーションが少なく可もなく不可もなくと言った所でプレイには支障はないが贅沢を言えばもっと音源が欲しかった。

・システム
　全体として司令部からの命令を受諾し特定の海域で哨戒や船舶攻撃を行い戦果に応じて帰還時にポイントを付与され魚雷の補給や改修を行うと言うシンプルな物で歴史的海戦の再現等は無く全体に満遍なく艦船がスポーンするので食いっぱぐれは少ないが史実再現としてはよろしくない。

・マルチプレイ
　マルチプレイの機能自体はあるが現状でマッチングを期待するのは非常に難しい。

・現状での不満点
　・プレイ環境によってはクラッシュが頻発する。
　・スポーンバグなど不具合が多い。
　・キャンペーンでの史実再現度が低い。

総評
　前作と比べると出来る事が減っていたりと評価が分かれるが潜水艦ゲームとしては完成度が非常に高く古いゲームながら潜水艦が好きな方にはお勧めできる内容となっている。
　しかし古さ故にアップデートやマルチプレイには一切期待が出来ずＭＯＤ等も更新や開発が止まっているのでオススメと評価しますが価格と内容を割り切って頂ければと思います。

Wirklich ein recht schwieriger Taktik-Shooter mit teilweise realistischen Ansätzen. Realistisch ist aber nicht die KI. Das war schon immer ein Problem von Red Storm Entertainment. Die schießen zwar sehr schnell und sind teilweise sehr treffsicher, jedoch ist die Wegfindung bei deinen Team und den Feinden manchmal etwas problematisch. Die KI scheint etwas Situationsbedingt programmiert zu sein. Also wenn sie unter Beschuss sind, dann legen sie sich auch mal hin oder gehen zu Bäumen. Das wirkt aber eher wie eine Wahrscheinlichkeitsberechnung der KI.

Die Schnellladen-Funktion und das Schnellspeichern sind die besten Freunde, wie gesagt, aus heutiger Sicht ist es wirklich schwer. Auch die Steuerung ist ziemlich umständlich und nicht mehr zeitgemäß aus heutiger Sicht. 

Bei diesen alten Werk merkt man wirklich, dass die Story noch mit Tom Clancy zutun hat. Es wirkt militärisch und durchdacht. Kleiner Funfact: das Spiel ist aus dem Jahre 2001 und handelt grob darüber das im Jahre 2008 das Land Georgien von Russland überfallen wird. Здешняя сюжетная кампания представляет собой набор сценариев в различных декорациях, определяющих цели в конкретной локации: зачистить вражеский лагерь, взорвать объект, освободить пленных, уничтожить бронетехнику и прочие активности.

Поведение и реакция врагов в большинстве случаев реализованы превосходно. Противник очень метко стреляет (как правило, один выстрел означает смерть), старается не высовываться понапрасну и занимает выгодное положение, чтобы вести огонь. Анимации при попадании в ногу/руку/туловище неприятеля — моё почтение. Ползущий в кусты соперник с простреленной ногой производит сильное впечатление. В общем, я рад, что решил начать ознакомление с серией Ghost Recon с самой первой части. Не прогадал.

Вот существует "The last hero of nostalgaia" - соулс для маленьких. А вот эта игра - это тактический шутер для маленьких.
Я пытался играть в арму и не смог, а тут, сам прошёл все миссии без гайдов или просмотра каких-нибудь фишек и хитростей! Возможно, за это стоит сказать спасибо возможности бесконечно использовать сохранения с загрузками, ведь нет нужды каждый раз после провала начинать с самого начала, и тому, что локации не огромные, а миссии чётко прописаны, вследствие чего запутаться или потеряться просто-напросто не выйдет.
Но у игры есть много минусов, которые перекрывают весь фан от игрового процесса, и самый первый и главный... Увы, она старая, очень, очень старая.
За последние 10 лет я прошёл много старых игр, и какие-то из них прошли проверку временем и остались в моём сердечке, какие-то совсем не понравились, а какие-то оставили смешанные чувства, и это один из таких случаев.
Играть вроде весело и занимательно, но! До чёртиков неудобно... Оружие не ощущается, у него нет отдачи, разброса тоже практически нет, все пули летят чётко в цель (с редкими отклонениями) на любом расстоянии, и даже урон не срезается.
Также в игре присутствует выглядывание из-за углов, но выпад настолько небольшой и медленный, что пользоваться им лучше всего в положении лёжа, ведь так моделька реально меньше и выпад какой-то нереально огромный, но лёжа неудобно передвигаться, всё сложно...
Многими видами оружия я не пользовался, так как они привязаны к классу, а постоянную команду я собрал уже в пятой миссии. Гранаты, клейморы и сканер тоже обошли меня стороной, ими неудобно пользоваться.
Из-за всего вышеперечисленного стрельба по болванчикам ощущается монотонно и скучно. Когда противники не ваншотят всю команду фиг пойми откуда, перестрелки превращаются в обычный отстрел мишеней, которые в лучшем случае ложатся и притворяются мёртвыми (после потери бдительности они начинают стрелять), а в остальное время... они стоят на месте и пытаются попасть в нас, пока мы просто делаем тычки по головам, либо выбегают толпой и смотрят куда попало, но только не в нашу сторону, что приводит к тому же отстрелу моделек по мере их появления на экране... скуууучнооо.
В то же время как раз из-за ИИ противника возникают трудности, но лишь потому, что довольно часто в перерывах между тупыми выходами - они читерят. Попросту несправедливые убийства.
Или, например, была локация с туманом, и мои тиммейты сказали, что нам будет трудно что-либо за ним увидеть, но и враги тоже должны замечать нас с трудом, ОДНАКО! Я реально не видел врагов, а они... стреляют прям сквозь туман и всё чётко в цель )
Но это ладно, я проходил "Far cry 1" на максимальной сложности, так что читерский ИИ не смог испортить игровой процесс (спасибо сохр. и загр.), тем не менее, повторять такой опыт само собой не захочется.
Также стоит отметить, что вражеский ИИ более "продвинутый", нежели ИИ наших напарников. Если ими не управлять лично, то они с вероятностью в 70% умрут во время стычки. Иногда они вытворяют такое, что гордость берёт, однако чаще всего они просто помирают, и вам придётся суматошно переключаться между всеми бойцами, чтобы сохранить им жизнь. Ещё у них имеются проблемы с переходом через какие-нибудь двери, когда ты ведёшь их через тактический интерфейс. Запрещал им стрелять, а они всё равно начинают (даже без угрозы для жизни). Да и само управление в тактическом интерфейсе не позволяет в полной мере контролировать отряды: они то и дело игнорируют какие-то приказы или тупят в текстурах и без личного управления не могут вылезти.
Также не хватает управления конкретным человеком в отряде, из-за чего, чаще всего, твои напарники просто выбегают под пули, хотя "командир" приказал сидеть в доме, и хотелось бы, чтобы все были в укрытии, но нет... Вообще, в игре есть прикольная тема с бойцами, и заключается она в том, что наших напарников могут ранить, и если они выживают, то 1 миссию они пропускают и лечатся, а вот если умрут, то просто выпадают из списка, и игра подкидывает нового оперативника.
Можно подумать: ну умер и умер, а нет! В игре есть прокачка! И если вы улучшили своего бойца, а он умер, то новый будет без этих улучшений, и это капец как обидно, но... Всегда есть но... Сохранения и загрузки позволяют спокойно забить на эту "механику", чем я и пользовался. Может, однажды я и пройду игру как задумано, но для первого раза это было бы слишком!
Печально, что в игре не расписали, за что отвечает конкретное улучшение, но, загуглив, я выяснил, что мои предположения были верны на 75%, так что... Несущественный недочёт.

I really wanted to like the original Ghost Recon. I can see why it became a classic, and the idea behind it is still great: multiple squads, different classes, planning routes, covering sectors, positioning your men and approaching every firefight tactically.

The problem is that the game constantly sabotages its own tactical gameplay.

Cover and terrain feel completely unreliable. I've had enemies shooting at me through rocks, while my own AI teammates were happily firing through the ground at enemies they somehow knew were there. At that point, what exactly am I supposed to do with all this tactical planning? If I can't trust a massive rock between me and the enemy to actually be a massive rock, positioning becomes meaningless.

Squad management doesn't help either. The game gives you several teams and expects you to coordinate them in real time, but actually controlling them is incredibly clumsy. The tactical map is overloaded with micromanagement while simultaneously lacking the precise and convenient commands you actually need. Instead of feeling like I'm commanding trained soldiers, I feel like I'm babysitting several groups of suicidal idiots.

And that's the most frustrating part: Ghost Recon demands patience, careful positioning and tactical thinking from the player while its own AI and engine frequently refuse to play by the same rules.

I don't mind old graphics. I don't mind hardcore difficulty. I don't mind dying from one or two bullets. In fact, that's exactly what I wanted from this game.

What I do mind is being killed through terrain, watching teammates engage enemies through the ground, fighting the squad controls more than the actual enemy, and then being told that this is "tactical realism."

There is a genuinely great tactical shooter buried in here, and I understand why people loved it in 2001. But playing it today without nostalgia, I found myself fighting the game itself far more often than fighting the enemy.

Eventually I realized I wasn't having fun anymore.

Not recommended.

It’s been 25 years since this gem first dropped and it still absolutely SLAPS!

It is incredibly eerie how accurately the original Ghost Recon foreshadowed real-world geopolitical events. Pretty sure Tom Clancy had a time machine, because he nailed the 2008 Russo-Georgian conflict seven years before it happened. The modern-day tactical warfare games we see today only exist because games like Rainbow Six and Ghost Recon built this town.

It's 2026 and the atmosphere is still top-tier, the music is iconic, and the gameplay truly makes you feel like a commando deep behind enemy lines. Sure, the graphics look like they were rendered on a toaster by today's standards, but the game is pure lightning in a bottle. It's ambitious, massive in scale, and has a story that honestly belongs on the big screen.

Word of advice: do NOT play this on Veteran or Elite right out the gate unless you enjoy digital masochism. The enemy AI possesses literal X-ray vision, will snipe you through dense fog from a mile away, and completely deletes any sense of fairness. Meanwhile, your own squad AI starts off with the situational awareness of a potato. Where is the fun in that? Play on Recruit first. This allows for a much more balanced firefight while you level up your squad's attributes. Once they actually learn how to aim, stealth, then you can attempt the harder modes.

Since the game is old enough to rent a car, you might have some issues getting it to run on modern rigs. If it crashes when loading a mission, just download the d3d8.dll file and drop it into the main Ghost Recon folder. If you are playing on an ultrawide monitor, grab the "Widescreen Fixer" so it doesn't look like a stretched accordion. Now you're good to go!

[h1]El origen del 'FPS' táctico definitivo[/h1]

El Ghost Recon original de 2001 es una lección magistral de cómo crear tensión sin fuegos artificiales. A diferencia de los shooters modernos de acción desenfrenada, aquí el ritmo es pausado, metódico y tremendamente gratificante. Controlar a los diferentes pelotones desde el mapa estratégico, planificar las rutas de asalto, dar órdenes de flanqueo y avanzar con pies de plomo por bosques o colinas abiertas ofrece una sensación de simulación militar que pocos juegos han vuelto a replicar.

Sin embargo, es justo detallar sus costuras dentro del texto. Es un juego extremadamente implacable que no perdona ni el más mínimo error. La dificultad es despiadada: la IA enemiga te detecta entre la maleza a kilómetros de distancia y te mata de un solo disparo antes de que te dé tiempo a reaccionar. Además, al ser un título de 2001, sus gráficos han envejecido de forma muy evidente y jugarlo hoy en día en monitores panorámicos requiere retocar archivos de configuración o usar mods de la comunidad para ajustar el FOV, la resolución y la sensibilidad del ratón. Pese a la curva de aprendizaje, es un clásico imprescindible.

I have played this game since it's release in 2001. It is now 2026.
I originally played on GameSpy on the IGS ladder, ranking with the best players globally.
Our team (Virtual Fighters) were on the top of the ladder, multiple times.

Everything is perfect about this game. Campaign, quick mission and multiplayer modes are all excellent. There is still yet to be a tactical shooter that gets even close to GR. in my opinion.
If you want to play multipalyer, you still can. LAN is easy, and online you just do some port forwarding on your router settings. There aren't many dedicated servers out there anymore, but you can still find people to play with in 2026.

You really should get the expansion packs Desert Seige and Island Thunder to complete the game. They feature some excellent additional single player Campaigns, and they add more maps for multiplayer too.

Also, for multiplayer games, make sure you (and your friends) download "Super Grid maps" and "Total Random Respawn" add ons found on ghostrecon.net. It was actually compulsary to have these add ons installed when playing on the IGS ladder.
Grid maps places numbered and lettered grids on the command map, so you can pinpoint locations for your team mates on comms & chat. Total random respawn means that players aren't respawning in the same place every time they respawn.

A really neat feature in multiplayer "Team" mode is being able to have up to Four different teams. So you can play a 2v2v2v2, for example. Good for the big maps.

For both Single Player and Multiplayer modes, in the game options screen, I highly recommend to turn the threat indicator off, for the best experience.

The game may seem a bit slow and difficult at first, but after a few tweaks with your controls, and when you fully understand how to play and know how to use the equipment and maps effectively (especially in multiplayer mode), you'll be hooked!

P.S. Sensors are your friend.

Let's be clear: this game did not age like fine wine.
It aged more like vinegar mixed with manure.

The AI is all over the place, and for all the wrong reasons. The enemy's aim is so godlike it feels like playing CS:GO on a cheater server. You raise your head or peek around a corner... BLAM! You're dead. One shot, one kill.
Random mooks standing in the open, armed with an unscoped AK-47 that's been around since the Vietnam War, are perfectly capable of headshotting your elite sniper clad in ghillie, hidden in a bush 500 yards away.

On the other hand, your teammates are pure, concentrated idiocy: they will remain in the open or come out of cover in the middle of a firefight. Sometimes they will cross your line of sight at the worst possible time. They will block doorways and won't move for any reason. They seem unable to stay focused: you'll often see enemies stroll right in front of them while they look in the opposite direction for no apparent reason. You will soon get accustomed to the red message signaling that one of your comrades has kicked the bucket, usually in the stupidest way imaginable.

This becomes even more frustrating when you realize that saving and loading is an exercise in patience (a.k.a. a pain in the ass). You can save whenever you want during a mission, but you can't load.
You have to quit the mission, go back to the main menu, select Campaign, select the mission, select the save file, load it, and... TA-DA! You're finally ready to get shot again.

Why? Because f**k you, that's why! Early 2000s devs probably thought this game had to be played as some sort of hardcore experience: something like "if you die, you either go back to the beginning or push through and deal with the consequences". There are no mods or patches (AFAIK) that address this (minor-ish) issue, just a few workarounds that might save you some time. I don't think many people out there finished this game without save-scumming the fuck out of it, but that's just the way it is.

In other words, it takes A LOT of patience to play this game 25 years later...

...however, that said, it can also be a rewarding experience.

This game is a relic from a long-lost, pre-Call of Duty era when games didn't need to appeal to everyone. They didn't have to offer the most bombastic and cinematic experience possible. They could simply be made for the people who actually loved the genre.

You won't find a heavily scripted action game here, and that's okay. What you will find is a challenging, clunky, 25-year-old tactical shooter with some very noticeable issues. You may not like it, but it's a window into a gaming world that simply doesn't exist anymore.
