In a time of AAA developers who release the same shit with a different paintjob and 10 more microtransactions every year to milk frat bros who are willing to buy it, it's always a pleasant surprise to find a decent game that slipped under everyone's radar like my cries for help.

Hinterland is a medieval fantasy game about managing your town and taming the wilderness. Not because you want to help your common man, heavens no, but because the king of assholes demands such. There's dozens of different classes to choose from, but they're all basically the same 2 guys. A politician who's good with management and money, or a warrior who can't count higher than the number of times the Mighty Ducks have won the Stanley cup. There's also two unique spins on this: the zombie that everyone distrusts because necromancy is still seen as an evil thing in the media for some reason even though it's about healing people, but doesn't eat and can heal outside of town and the orc who can eat the monsters they kill. Given that this is a game where enemies don't respawn however, this isn't a helpful trait in the long run.

The problem is, the warrior is the only good choice. Money only serves a purpose early-to-midgame, to hire townies to help you help them survive in the middle of fucking nowhere. You can't place orders on powerful equipment, no, the merchant only serves to let you sell your junk for 1 gold each. Regardless of what it is.

"What's that, mayor who's paying for my housing, clothes, armour, weapons, and is killing goblins every day to keep me safe? You have the legendary Backscratcher of Strength? Ehhh best I can do is 1 gold."

You can also give a bugle to the merchant to make him better at his job, but it sure as hell doesn't seem to DO anything. Unlike most workers, he doesn't sell any sort of stock, and he never gives you more than 1 gold for anything, so what's the fucking point? You don't even need to talk to the guy directly, as soon as you have a merchant, you can just drop all your unwanted shit on the floor like a 3 year old taking their winter coat off and it mysteriously turns into money.

Ultimately, money only serves to get you equipment so you can be a better fighter, but if you already know what you're doing because your character is a seasoned veteran who stood guard at the royal outhouse for 20 years and had to kill a chihuahua-sized rat once, you're going to find better equipment growing on trees anyway! A winning strategy I've found is running to high level areas, avoiding all the baddies, stealing the endgame loot, and hoofing it back to town where some level 1 pricks won't know what fuckin' hit 'em.


Another weird thing is that the game seems to be having an identity crisis. Is it an RPG or is it an oldschool arcade game where people actually give a shit about high scores? I swear half the townies don't do anything at all other than contribute to your score at the end for having a diverse array of meats and funny hats. As such, replayability boils down to you knowing what matters and what doesn't - necromancers to create an army of skeletons for you, doctors to make you health potions, and farmers to feed the former two.

The thing about the necromancer is...well, there's two things. One, the game tries to push a Black & White morality thing where you can either choose to build a temple of good or a temple of evil. But the temple of good doesn't do anything useful!
"Hey, I can pray to the gods and give your townies, who may or may not be completely safe depending on what you selected for the raider setting, a little more health regen!"
"Or I could just raise an undead army for you--"
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
THIS GUY, EVERY TIME.

The second thing is, unlike blacksmiths who mentally check out after learning what steel is despite better armours existing in the game, necromancers can stop what they're doing and research more powerful skeletons indefinitely. If you leave the game on long enough, you will have a killsquad of invincible spoopy bois who can, and will, kill God. Are we sure this isn't a *J*RPG?

Ultimately, Hinterland is fun but it's not for everyone. It's a confused mess of conflicting design philosophies, many of which haven't been a thing for over 30 years, but you won't need to take out a third mortgage on your house to buy it and it will run on a potato. If you would like to establish complete dominion over a region out of sheer spite because the king is a racist who hates the undead, this is the game for you.

[h1]“Soldiers! I have summoned you together for the last time.”
~[i]John S. Mosby[/i][/h1]

So, history, huh? A lot of history right here. And not only because it's a game about [b]John S. Mosby[/b], also known as [b]Grey Ghost[/b]. Even though yes, as a huge [b]American Civil War[/b] geek, I must say, it's a pretty interesting thing to see. I mean, let's just admit it - Confederate army gets a lot of hate nowadays. And it's not like I can't see why. With all that racist bull going on around us (even [b]Black Panther[/b] director [b]Ryan Coogler[/b] got detained by police just because he's black), it's hard not to see those monuments and flags as sum of all evil. But at the same exact time... we should not forget that those are also an important reminder. It's really important to see history for what it really is – a history. In a way, it's like looking at your personal past. Not only it made you who you are right now, it's also important to embrace it and learn from it. Just because it's the only way to become a better person and achieve something great in the future. So, personally, I was always very interested in this part of history. It was sure bright and obviously, it was [i]extremely[/i] important for us all. And, of course, when you're interested in something, having a computer game about that? It's always cool. So yeah, here it is. A computer game fully dedicated to [b]John S. Mosby[/b], Virginia Cavalry commander.

And you know what? I [i]loved[/i] the idea. Not only because of what I've said above, but also because of how it was about Mosby's Rangers. Those were a partisan unit, which was known for its lightning-quick raids. They used to strike fast and then disappear without a trace, blending in with local townsmen, leaving Federal Army wondering what did just happen. Those were like ghosts. Hence [b]Mr. Mosby[/b]'s nickname. And as for the name of this game, [b]Mosby's Confederacy[/b] was a name given to a part of Virginia, in which  Mosby's Rangers used to operate. In other words, long intro aside, it's a historical strategy about  Confederate Army's partisans. And when it's about something like that? There's just so-o-o much potential. Which brings us to another part of history. Most recent one.

I'm talking, of course, about [b]Tilted Mill Entertainment[/b]. Like [b]Petroglyph Games[/b], which was founded by ex-[b]Westwood[/b] employees, [b]Tilted Mill[/b] was used to be [i]huge[/i] in their previous life, when they were known as [b]Impressions Games[/b], creators of legendary [b]Caesar[/b] series and its spin-offs. Unfortunately to us all, the same old thing happened to them. They were bought by a big publisher who tried to do things their way, which eventually led to them being closed down (pretty fast in this exact case). After that, they tried to get back to business and even ended up working on [b]Caesar[/b] series again, but... let's just say that their former glory was no more. Their first game, [b]Children of the Nile[/b], while being pretty much [b]Pharaoh[/b] in [b]3D[/b], [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/letande/recommended/17100]was rough, clunky and didn't feel anything like the original[/url]. [b]Caesar IV[/b], which used the same exact approach (remember what [b]Impressions[/b] did in their games during [b]Caesar III[/b] times, that's what they tried to do again in [b]Caesar IV[/b]), didn't do much better. And after not being able to do better even in [b]EA[/b]'s [b]SimCity Societies[/b]? It looks like nobody was interested in working with them anymore. So, what did they do? They went indie. Doesn't sound bad, but... let's just say [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/letande/recommended/17140/]it didn't go well either[/url]. Their [b]Hinterland[/b] ended up being way too ugly, way too limited and too poorly made to be considered as a real deal even by indie audience. Now what do we have here? Well, aside from browser-based [b]Pharaoh[/b]-like game (because yes, they were [i]that[/i] desperate) and a final attempt to return to good ol' [b]Caesar[/b], which ended up in development hell, [b]Mosby's Confederacy[/b] is their final game. And... it's not hard to see why.

See, technically, it's very similar to [b]Hinterland[/b]. For example, it's made with [b]GarageGames[/b]'s [b]Torque Game Engine[/b]. Which isn't a bad thing per se (I mean, it's an engine from [b]Tribes 2[/b] game), but... we've all seen what [b]Tilted Mill[/b] did with it in [b]Hinterland[/b]. Let's just say (oops) they did it again. Heck, [b]Mosby's Confederacy[/b] looks like it's using the same exact assets and even menus look the same. Which is far from being a good thing, of course. Gameplay-wise, though? It's pretty different. While [b]Hinterland[/b] was more like [b]Soldak Entertainment[/b]'s [b]Depths of Peril[/b], [b]Mosby's Confederacy[/b] is more like [b]Total War[/b]. If we can compare those, since the scale here is much smaller. Which makes sense, of course, keeping all the historical background in mind.

Naturally, in this game we're partisans. Like in [b]Hinterland[/b], there are three resources here, one of each is reputation. And, of course, you use it to raise people's support in towns. And it's a very important thing, since you recruit soldiers in those towns and the support determines how far away those soldiers will be able to move. In other words, if you have strong soldiers in one city, but the mission you want to use them in is too far away? As long as your support rate is too low, you won't be able to use them. There's more. You'll be able to use reputation to build hospitals to heal your soldiers (those will level up, so, it's very important to keep them alive), you'll be able to drill soldiers for better morale, you'll be able to upgrade their weaponry and, of course, you'll be able to build bigger munition caches and stables.

And that's our other resources – munition and horses. Don't forget, guys, Mosby's Rangers were cavalry unit. So, having horses [i]is[/i] important. But you can't just buy them. Instead, you'll need to take them from Union Army. And that's where strategy map ends and tactical battles begin. Like I said, this game feels a lot like “[b]Total War[/b] lite”. The actual missions are done in a real-time manner. You select a certain amount of units to take with you and you make a swift move against Federals. Missions can vary from capturing certain things or buildings to killing a certain amount of enemies, while [b]John S. Mosby[/b] himself acts as a commander, which gets the new skills with every level and provide bonuses to his troops. All in all, though, missions here are very, [i]very[/i] basic, so, don't expect much. Maps are too small and feel pretty much the same, there's not enough variety, while the game is also way too slow. Seriously, [b]Mosby's Confederacy[/b] is one of those games that I just can't play without speed hacks. It's just way, [i]way[/i] too slow for me to tolerate.

And that's the biggest problem with this game. I mean, main concept? Loved it. Even though this game doesn't try much to re-create real historical events, it still captures the original historical idea. It [i]is[/i] a game about [b]Mr. Mosby[/b] and his rangers. The problem is – it's just... way too poor. Yet again, [b]Tilted Mill[/b] proved that browser strategy is the best thing they can do with what they have. On paper, [b]Mosby's Confederacy[/b] had everything to become a good game. Right motif, right concept, right approach... But when you actually play it? Having only three resources and playing slow, limited and repetitive missions on maps that all feel the same? It just... isn't good enough. Maybe not as bad as what we had in [b]Hinterland[/b], but still, very bad. And that's probably why [b]Medieval Mayor[/b] game, in which [b]Tilted Mill[/b] decided to re-discover [b]2D Caesar[/b], is still on hiatus. The guys have all sorts of the right ideas. They just don't have what it takes to turn them into reality. Dixi.

Good game. Probably the best real-time Civil War game I've played since Sid Meier's Gettysburg. The combat is a little simplistic for some tastes, but it rewards common sense and patience, as well as good planning prior to starting the mission. The game starts slow and easy, but it quickly becomes difficult near the end of the campaign if you aren't careful with your resources and upgrades. People who are hesitant because you are playing as a confederate shouldn't worry. The game doesn't contain any revisionist elements and does not romanticize the unjust cause of the Confederacy. It is simply a tactical strategy game that challenges you to be a better leader than Mosby was, fighting against overwhelming odds with limited resources. And it is quite fun. 

The only thing I really disliked is that the game has limited replay value. There is no scoreboard to compare your fame points between campaigns. There are also no options to spice things up, such as choosing from different difficulty settings. Every campaign is basically the same, except they give you random missions and troops. 

Still, the campaign can last 6 to 7 hours which is pretty good. The game has some flaws, but the good things stand out more. But because it's sort of a love-it-or-hate-it game, I recommend you buy it when it's 75% off.

[i]Přídavek je vlastně vylepšená původní hra především po technickém stavu a s větším důrazem na optimalizaci zaručující menší náročnost. Příběh není o tolik kratší a přitom stejně zábavný i působivý s daleko filmovějším nádechem a atmosférickou hudbou. Mechanikami téměř indentická s originálem  kromě pár přidavků ve zbraních anebo vozidlech. Bohužel postrádá remaster verzi jako ostatní díly a u moderních systémů bez opensource spouštěče nefunguje včetně jiných potíží. [/i]

[h1]Uhlazenější Lingshan[/h1]

Jaká je definice rozšíření ke hrám nebo tzv. DLC? Představa může být jakákoliv. Můžou to být pouze nově kosmetické věci, kratší příběhy a někdy samostatná hra, která velikostí oproti předloze tolik nezaostává. Když přidáme navíc vylepšení celkového technického stavu původní hry, svádí to k zamyšlení. Crysis Warhead přichází pro roce a Crytek se především zaměřil na optimalizaci anebo dalších technikálií, s čímž originál dosti bojoval a bylo důvodem vysokých hardwarových nároků. Zároveň nám objasní dění alespoň jedné postavy z prvního dílu, jež jsme za celou hru téměř neviděli.

Psycho zastává další post člena týmu Raptor. Pamatujte jednu hlavní věc. Je to Brit, troubové! Stejně jako Nomád i on má své úkoly ke splnění, akorát na opačné straně ostrova, kde Korejská lidová armáda přesouvá tajnou zásilku. Cílem bude tento balíček získat, ale úplně stejným způsobem půjde vše od deseti k pěti. Trochu podivně působí předěl mezi žánry v rámci příběhu. Konkrétně naše postava nijak zvlášť nekomentuje oné změny a situaci přechází normálně oproti Nomádovi. Vzápětí přibylo daleko více filmových scén a všiml jsem si i hudby. Zatímco u původního dílu byla nevýrazná, zde udává důraz mnohem lépe. Hlavně díky bubnům navozující větší atmosféru ostrova kdesi v Pacifiku. Do příběhu se promítá i jistá vedlejší hloubka naší postavy a jiného charakteru v předělech mezi misemi i během nich.

Podobně jako první díl kladou důraz na sandboxové pojetí, i když s vyšším poměrem lineárnosti. Hratelnost zůstává stejná, přesto obzvláštňuje průchod více různorodými aktivitami než pouhým chozením v džungli a likvidování cílů. Například bráněním pozic či eskortou. Rozšířen byl arzenál u zbraní. Vedle pistole přibyla jakási verze UZI, granátomet, a také protipancéřoví i pěchotní miny. Jejich využití jsem téměř nenašel. Spíše působí experimentálně, jakoby pro kreativní řešení likvidace než pragmaticky. Nejúčinnějším způsobem stále vévodí neviditelnost, tiché zabíjení a střelba do hlavy. Naopak využití u nového elektromagnetického granátu dává smysl. Jednak dokáže vyřadit schopnosti nano-obleku nepřátel, ale také škodí mimozemským Cephům. Hlavně u nových pozemních jednotek tzv. "Ceph guardianů", kteří poskytují štíty ostatním pěšákům. Dále máme nové létající oranžové varianty fungující stylem bombardéru. K vozítkům přibyl nový a opancéřovanější vůz s lehkým rychlým kanonem.

Ovšem velkou část práce odevzdal vývojářský tým u stavu hry. Její optimalizace a opravu chyb. Hra zachovává stejnou úroveň grafiky, ale mnohem stabilnější i hardwarově méně náročná včetně lepších snímků. Smutným osudem zůstává fakt, že Warhead nedostal svůj remaster, který by si jistě zasloužil už jen z důvodu nových systémů. Engine má s nimi problém a z mé zkušenosti je nehratelná neustálým padáním. Proto jsme musel spouštět hru pomoci C1 launcheru, který pomáhá odstranit chyby a zajišťuje kompabilitu. Avšak nespolupracuje se Steamem, takže oné nahrané "hodiny" myslím vysvětlují celou situaci. Z nepochopitelných důvodů byla vyžadována i instalace anti-cheat programu pro Wahhead. Ten sice nabízí multiplayer, ale opět jako samostatnou hru oddělující singleplayer.

Аддон в качестве отдельной игры для первой части Crysis, где события игры происходят параллельно ей с Психом, членом отряда «Хищник». По ходу игры мы пытаемся отследить и перехватить контейнер с неизвестным содержанием, предположительно ядерной боеголовкой. Мы успеем побывать в джунглях, внутри ледяной сферы и снова за ее пределами в процессе вторжения цефов.
Аддон недолгий, различий в геймплей на самом высоком уровне сложности по сравнению с первой частью особо нет. Добавили пару новых видов оружия (ручной гранатомет, пистолет-пулемет и имбалансную плазменную пушечку под конец игры, жалко что не дали поиграть с ней подольше…)
Игру сделали явно линейнее в сторону большего количества экшена, переигрывать ее конечно же можно, но уже не так интересно. Катсцен насыпали как на полноценное кино.

Единственная беда в том, что на удивление по сравнению с оригинальной первой частью в Стиме, эта версия дико конфликтует с современным железом и ОС. Пришлось понижать настройки графики до DX9 и отключать сглаживание. В противном случае игра вылетала перед запуском геймплея. 
А так она хотя бы (!) выдерживала 5-10 минут перед вылетом. Иногда игра вылетала при ручном сохранении. 8/10, это все было терпимо.

Отличное дополнение к первой части, но она очень любит вылетать на мощных компах, это очень бесило. Однако игру стоит пройти тем, кто хочет узнать как разворачивалась история с другой стороны и побыть ещё на графонистом острове.

Crysis Warhead — Обзор

Crysis Warhead — это самостоятельное дополнение (standalone expansion) к оригинальной игре 2007 года, разработанное студией Crytek Budapest. Если оригинальная Crysis была известна прежде всего как «тест для видеокарт», то Warhead стал работой над ошибками, сфокусированной на более динамичном и зрелищном геймплее.

Сюжет: Один день из жизни Психа
В отличие от оригинала, где мы играли за молчаливого Номада, здесь главным героем выступает сержант Майкл Сайкс по прозвищу Псих. Сюжет разворачивается параллельно событиям первой части. Пока Номад бродил по джунглям, Псих выполнял свою миссию по перехвату контейнера с неизвестным грузом на другой стороне острова. 
История здесь более личная, мрачная и сконцентрированная. Псих — более эмоциональный и агрессивный персонаж, что делает повествование более динамичным по сравнению со сдержанным Номадом.3 источника

Геймплей: Больше экшена, меньше инопланетян
Разработчики услышали критику фанатов, которым не понравилась вторая половина оригинала (скучные уровни внутри инопланетного корабля).

Действие: В Warhead гораздо больше перестрелок с людьми (корейцами KPA), масштабных взрывов и скриптовых сцен. 
Оружие и техника: Арсенал расширен, а управление техникой стало более отзывчивым. Появились новые виды инопланетной техники, с которой предстоит сражаться.
ИИ: Искусственный интеллект противников (как людей, так и пришельцев) был значительно улучшен. Враги лучше координируют действия и активнее используют укрытия.3 источника

Графика и оптимизация
В 2008 году Crysis Warhead снова стал королем бенчмарков. Графика была доведена до совершенства, при этом оптимизация стала значительно лучше, чем в оригинале. Игра выглядела потрясающе и при этом шла стабильнее на массовых конфигурациях того времени. Журналисты отмечали, что на «среднячках» Warhead выглядел и работал лучше, чем оригинал.3 источника

Плюсы:

Графика: На момент выхода — эталонная (оценка 10/10 от многих изданий).
Оптимизация: Игра работала значительно плавнее оригинала.2 источника
Атмосфера: Саундтрек и звуковое сопровождение получили высокие оценки за создание напряжения.2 источника
Исправление ошибок: Это тот самый Crysis, который должен был выйти изначально — более сбалансированный и динамичный.3 источника

Минусы:

Линейность: Игра стала более коридорной по сравнению с оригиналом.
Отсутствие новизны: Это «те же щи», что и в оригинале, просто более качественные и отполированные. Уникальных инноваций дополнение не принесло.3 источника

Итог
Crysis Warhead — это идеальный Crysis. Студия взяла формулу, которая сделала их знаменитыми, убрала из нее затянутые моменты с инопланетянами в невесомости и сфокусировалась на том, что у них получается лучше всего — на невероятно красивых и динамичных перестрелках в джунглях. Это обязательная часть коллекции для любого поклонника серии и классики шутеров.3 источника

So Crysis Warhead is a standalone game/expansion for the original Crysis, and in many regards I just sort of lump this in with my analysis of the main game. But, there are some differences between the two, which will be detailed here:

The Positives:
The main character of Crysis Warhead is Psycho, who was one of the three characters in the original game that was memorable in any way shape or form. This game takes place during the same timeframe as the original game, when Psycho is separated from the rest of Raptor Team and goes on a series of missions to acquire a high-value target from the North Koreans, which at the end of Warhead leads right back into Psycho's return in the original game's ending. Psycho is given a little more depth here, but it's presented a little weirdly, with a black screen and voiceover flashbacks giving hints to his backstory with his friend and fellow soldier O'Neill. Again it's not Shakespearean or anything, but Psycho does have a few character moments, that while not exactly groundbreaking storytelling, are more than anyone got in the original game.

Gameplay wise there are several improvements, noticeably there are a few new weapon choices for the player to use, which overall makes combat more interesting and simply by the virtue of having more variety, is better, though you'll still largely be using the mainstay weapons of the FY71, the DSG-1 sniper, and the Gauss Rifle at Delta difficulty. The new submachine pistol, grenade launcher,  and nanogrenades are excellent additions, making firefights against Nanosuited Koreans and armored opponents easier and more interesting.

The Negatives:
The negatives of gameplay are sort of inconsequential, but still should be written about; the new flashbangs and claymore mines are practically useless in my opinion, why they were added I have no idea. On Delta Difficulty, some levels are basically impossible to complete, the mission where you have to defend a train being the absolute worst, as you will have to micromanage your suit's armor ability and swap between mounted guns on all side of the train to fight off high-health helicopters, Korean ATV's, and gun emplacements the whole level through. Genuinely unfun at Delta difficulty, you have been warned, you will die over and over again on that level.

When talking about performance, I had severe crashing issues replaying this game on my rig. This was immensely annoying, but the cause was due to several reasons with the way the original Crysis and Crysis Warhead were built, as these games were made for single-core CPU's. There is a Steam community thread with a discord link to community patches for all the Crysis games, including Warhead, that I believe are basically required at this time, here is the link: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2823052004

Once you install that patch, crashing goes away permanently.

Overall, I rank this an 8/10, for a standalone expansion for the game it's solid to stand on its own two feet and gives us a little more to the character of Psycho, while providing great action setpieces and giving us more of the original Crysis 1 gameplay.

Самостоятельное дополнение к оригинальному Crysis, которое сместило фокус с неторопливого исследования тропического острова на ураганный, плотный и голливудский экшен от лица харизматичного сержанта Майкла «Психа» Сайкса.

Плюсы
Динамика и плотность событий: Игра избавилась от затянутых паузовых переходов оригинала. Напряжение держится от начала и до конца: взрывы, погони на военной технике, постоянные перестрелки и минимум ходьбы по пустому острову.

Харизматичный главный герой: «Псих» ощущается куда живее и интереснее стерильного Номада из первой части. Его реплики, поведение в катсценах и реакция на происходящий хаос добавляют игре характера.

Улучшенный арсенал и техника: Появление двух пистолетов-пулеметов, гранатомета и новых видов транспорта (включая катер на воздушной подушке) отлично разбавляет боёвку.

Более адекватный баланс боев с инопланетянами: В отличие от унылых коридоров оригинального Crysis, сегменты с пришельцами здесь сделаны куда более драйвово и не так сильно проваливают темп игры.

Минусы
Сохраненный «танковый» отклик управления: Хотя динамику боев подняли, базовая физика перемещения осталась той же. Нанокостюм по-прежнему ощущается тяжеловесным, а герой местами управляется как неповоротливая бронетехника с инерцией.

«Зрячие» враги и туповатый ИИ: Корейские корейцы все так же способны замечать героя сквозь кусты на приличном расстоянии и моментально агриться всем лагерем.

Короткая продолжительность: Кампания проходится буквально за 4–5 часов, оставляя ощущение пусть и яркого, но очень быстро закончившегося аттракциона.

Заключение

Crysis Warhead для меня оказалась скорее нейтральным опытом. Это неплохое дополнение к первой части, но проходить его после всей трилогии — не лучшая идея.

Главная проблема в том, что игра сильно отличается от второй и третьей частей: здесь заметно меньше механик, устаревшая графика и в целом ощущается возраст игры. Особенно это бросается в глаза после современных ремастеров первых трёх частей. К сожалению, Warhead так и не получила ремастер, поэтому после прохождения трилогии возвращаться к ней довольно тяжело.

Отдельный минус — техническое состояние игры на современном железе. Похоже, с оптимизацией есть проблемы: за относительно короткое прохождение, которое заняло у меня около 4 часов, игра вылетела 5 раз. Для такой продолжительности это довольно неприятный показатель.

Сюжет идёт параллельно событиям первой части, но лично меня он практически не зацепил. Персонажи прописаны довольно слабо, из-за чего не возникает ни особого сопереживания, ни желания переживать за их судьбу. Сам Псих тоже показался мне странно раскрытым: то он ведёт себя как своеобразный шутник, то внезапно проявляет благородство, а иногда просто выходит из себя и начинает творить откровенную дичь.

В итоге Crysis Warhead — игра скорее на один раз. Если хотите пройти её, рекомендую делать это сразу после первой Crysis, а не после всей трилогии. В противном случае устаревший геймплей, графика, слабый сюжет и технические проблемы будут ощущаться особенно сильно.

This game built my childhood in a way few others ever did. I honestly lost count of how many times I finished Crysis Warhead from start to finish; even on Delta difficulty.
The graphics were incredible for their time and still look fantastic today. Out of the entire franchise, this is the one I love the most. It feels simpler, tighter, and more professionally designed than the later games.
The story is excellent and Psycho is a badass protagonist. One of the biggest unique things about Warhead is that it actually had third-person cutscenes. something that never happened before or after in the series.
As a kid, the way enemies would cloak and the isolation of those frozen forests, the mine, and the train tunnels scared the hell out of me. That sense of dread is still with me to this day because of how impactful this game was.
The shooting and weapon customization felt amazing. Stealth was pretty much useless though. enemies would always path toward the exact spot you shot from, even with a silencer. But honestly? I didn’t mind.
The soundtrack is epic as hell, especially during the boss fight, the ending, and those final cutscenes.
Although it was a short game, Warhead will always have a special place for me. Absolute classic.

Crysis Warhead (2008)
Esta reseña es breve teniendo en cuenta la reseña del juego base. Es la expansión clásica de FPS de PC sucediendo simultáneamente a los sucesos del primer juego desde la perspectiva de Psycho. Si bien es más corto, justamente ese puede ser el elemento que puede hacer que Warhead sea igual o mejor de bueno que el juego base: su diseño de niveles me parece constantemente pulido y más refinado, las frustraciones del juego base aparecen más reducidas y la calidad se siente más concentrada. El anfibio con mayor armadura es justamente la respuesta a mi problema de vehículos demasiado débiles y es más viable usarlo en una misión bien diseñada de ir por el mapa con el mismo mientras se combate y dispara. Eso pasa en general, diría que hay misiones mejor dirigidas con ideas interesantes: hay un trecho que perseguimos a alguien con un vehículo sobre el hielo, un nivel de un tren que tenemos que defender dinámicamente como podamos, mejor variación a veces con cephs y coreanos en combate simultáneamente. Incluso se le agrega un par de enemigos a los cephs para darles un poco más de variedad. Aparte de nuevas herramientas útiles como el lanzagranadas o las granadas PEM.
La verdad no tengo mucho más que decir que no sea redundante, me fue muy divertido en su corta duración, incluso lo postuló como el mejor Crysis: Bien condensado y ejecutado.

The shooting is still good, the nanosuit is still fun, and CryEngine 2 still makes that island look impressive. Psycho has some personality too. “I’m British, you muppet!” still makes me laugh.

My problem is what they did with the campaign. The original gave me room to watch patrols, explore the jungle and work out my own approach. Warhead keeps pushing me toward another firefight while I chase the same bloody container around the island. I can choose how to attack, but I miss having more choices beyond attacking.

A shorter campaign is fine. A thin story with less atmosphere and less breathing room is harder to forgive. Psycho has a few strong character moments, but the game rushes past them before doing enough with them.

If you want another helping of Crysis combat, there’s enjoyment here. I still think the original is the better game.

Обзор будет отрицательным побольшей части из-за постоянных вылетов и отсутствию 100% способа избавиться от них. Выключение оверлея Steam и NVIDIA, принудительное включение FXAA через панель NVIDIA и отключение встроенного сглаживания (вроде тут MSAA), понижение разрешения игры, смена названия исполняемого файла x64, включение совместимости с Windows Vista и 7 – никак не помогли с вылетами в этой игре. Максимальное время которое я смог провести за одну сессию составило полтора часа. Тогда я подумал что смена типа сглаживания решили эту проблему, но нет, просто повезло.
Сама игра мне понравилась, очень затягивающая. Сюжет игры происходит параллельно первой части на другой части острова. Тут, играя за Психа мы должны отбить невредимого цефа у корейцев. Цель всего этого спин-оффа показать нам какую миссию выполнял Псих и как он в конце первой части доставил цефа на авианосец.
Игра за Психа никак не отличается геймплейно от 1 части, но тут нам подкинули новые автоматы, гранатомет и плазменную пушку, которая максимально хороша против цефалоподов. Катер на воздушной подушке прикольный, но встречается только раз за всю игру. Добавили больше кат-сцен от третьего лица, которые еще вставлены по всему прохождению сюжета, а не только в финале как в номерных частях. На момент 2026 года игра не сказать что плохо выглядит, текстуры на различных поверхностях не суперобъемные, но четкие. Хотя тут заслуга еще QHD разрешения на котором я играл. По-хорошему игру следовало заремастерить и включить в ремастер 1 части для большей целостности общей картины происходящего, но в этой вселенной Warhead так и остался старой игрой с постоянными вылетами.
В общем игра хорошая, но на современном железе и ОС показывает себя отвратительно.

This game has always been a curiosity for me. I never played Crysis when it first came out on PC as my computer at the time was nowhere close to being able to run it. I did eventually play the Xbox 360 port and even had a decent time with Crysis 2 and 3 when those came out, but Warhead was always something I never got to experience. Now that I have, I can confidently say this can easily be skipped.

First off, the game is extremely short - like maybe 3-5 hours if you're taking your time. I know this is technically a standalone expansion, but for a non-sale price of $20 this feels steep even today. I also had to jump through a ton of hoops to even get the game to run. Yes, this is one of THOSE games that just does not play well with modern hardware and operating systems. After I did get it running though, the game would frequently crash. I'd wager a good hour of my playtime was spent replaying sections of levels because the game would just stop mid-cutscene or crap itself as I'm about to enter combat.

Despite the technical issues I had, I just don't think the game is really worth it as a game either. It feels a lot more linear than the original Crysis, with very few secondary objectives and virtually nothing new in terms of gameplay. As far as I can tell, there's like on unique weapon that you use during the last boss fight but everything else is stuff you did in the base game. The cutscenes are super janky and awkward to the point they feel unfinished. I was genuinely wondering if my game was bugged or something but when I looked up gameplay on YouTube the cutscenes really are that bad.

If you're desperate for more classic Crysis gameplay, maybe buy this on sale for $5, but don't think you're missing out on anything like I did if you skip this. The story is threadbare and does nothing to add to the original. The gameplay is the same, the maps feel smaller, and the overall experience is way too short. And that's only if you can get the game to run properly.

Recommended. A compressed, action-packed companion piece told from the brash Briton's side of the alien invasion, and the momentum never pauses for breath.

Seven roughly thirty-minute missions chain beach resorts, harbour infiltration, hovercraft pursuit, frozen alien tunnels and a freight-train chase into an airfield finale with an infinite-ammo plasma cannon. The mode-selected suit returns, sprinting no longer drains energy, armour only drains when shot, ammo auto-picks-up, and cloak routes still let entire missions be ghosted. Controller support works surprisingly well for a shooter of its age.

A checkpoint-less VTOL defence stretch turns one death into a long redo, the hovercraft container chase dead-ends repeatedly, and vehicle controls are awkward. Textures betray the years up close. The sprint was always the point, and it lands.

I mistakenly thought that Crysis Warhead is a sequel to the first Crysis, turns out it isn't. It's not a prequel either as the timeline of the events is parallel with the first game. To sum up the story - you basically play as Psycho after the Raptor team was separated. If you played the original you'll see Psycho at the end who brags about bringing an alien to the ship. What happens in Warhead is that it shows the process of tracking and eventually capturing it. The whole campaign is basically you trying to prevent the Koreans from taking the alien with them. The ending is pretty cool but I would prefer if there was a boss fight against Lee. I mean that guy is the main reason we went through all that trouble. Instead we see Psycho give him a proper ass whooping in the ending cutscene.


The gameplay is pretty much the same. Though the nanosuit's hud says " Sykes mod " there is nothing special about it, it functions the same as Nomad's nanosuit. There are however a couple of new weapons and vehicles to play with. Dual wielding submachine guns is pretty cool, not a huge fan of the grenade launcher though. I like how they kept the level design non-linear, meaning you can take different paths. You can in fact miss a lot of areas if you just choose the straightforward path. But I found out that playing on the highest difficulty kinda forced me to explore the map a little more, either to find cover or ammunition and I was surprised that I never saw those areas in my first playthrough. There are also some collectibles that unlock a funny ending.

The graphics look great. You may notice a couple of outdated textures on some terrain, but the overall look still holds up. To my surprise it also looks and runs great on the Steam Deck too. Worked flawlessly without tinkering. Played it on " Gamer " ( or High ) settings.

I really like the Crysis franchise, and I decided to buy Warhead on Steam for that exact reason. To me, the biggest strength of this game is that it is a legitimate Crysis experience — something I feel was somewhat lost in Crysis 2 and 3. The freedom of approach and the island environment have stuck with me since 2008 and they are still the core of the experience here.

The big issue nowadays is just how old the game is. For me, the game would simply crash out of nowhere, straight to the desktop without any warning. It's an annoying instability, but alright... it's Crysis, and I already bought it knowing its age.

At the end of the day, it's still a good game for anyone wanting that raw, original franchise experience, but I still prefer the first one.

Un éditeur qui préfère enterrer ses licences plutôt que de les faire vivre.

EA continue de démontrer ce qui ne va pas dans l'industrie du jeu vidéo : des studios talentueux sont sacrifiés, des équipes qui ont consacré des années à créer des univers et des licences appréciés par des millions de joueurs sont démantelées, et des franchises entières finissent abandonnées.

BioWare fait partie de ces studios qui ont marqué l'histoire du jeu vidéo. Mass Effect, Dragon Age… Des univers, des personnages et des histoires qui ont profondément marqué toute une génération de joueurs. Et derrière ces jeux, il y avait des développeurs passionnés, dont le travail mérite mieux que d'être traité comme des pièces jetables.

Le plus enrageant dans tout ça, c'est cette logique qui consiste à laisser mourir des licences plutôt que de leur donner une nouvelle chance. Si EA ne souhaite plus investir dans certaines franchises, pourquoi ne pas simplement les vendre ou en céder les droits à des studios qui seraient prêts à les faire vivre ? Pourquoi préférer les laisser prendre la poussière plutôt que de permettre à d'autres développeurs de reprendre le flambeau ?

Pour ma part, j'ai décidé de ne plus soutenir cette politique. Spore is genuinely one of the most iconic and nostalgic comfort games out there! ❤️

I grew up playing this game after a friend introduced it to me when we were little, and I remember how much fun I had exploring everything it had to offer. As the years went by, I eventually forgot about it until recently, when I stumbled across it again. Naturally, I had to give it another go, and before I knew it, I had spent HOURS playing! 😂🎮

There is something truly special about Spore. The concept is so unique, creative, and incredibly entertaining. Where else can you start as a tiny organism in the ocean, evolve into your own creature, build a civilisation, and eventually work your way towards exploring an entire galaxy? 🐠➡️👾➡️🚀

One of my favourite things about this game is the freedom it gives you. You can create your very own alien creatures, customise their appearance, experiment with different abilities, and watch them evolve throughout different stages of life. Every little decision makes your experience feel unique, and the possibilities are just so much fun!

The journey from a tiny little creature to becoming an advanced space-faring civilisation is such a brilliant concept. Exploring different planets, discovering new species, encountering other civilisations, and venturing further into the galaxy makes the game feel like one enormous adventure. 🌍🛸🌠

What makes Spore even more special to me is the nostalgia. It takes me straight back to my childhood, reminding me of simpler times when I could sit down, play for hours, and completely lose myself in a game. It is one of those experiences that never really gets old, no matter how many years have passed.

I honestly believe Spore is one of those timeless games that deserves so much appreciation. It is creative, relaxing, funny, adventurous, and endlessly entertaining. Whether you enjoy space exploration, creature creation, evolution, or simply experimenting with something completely different, there is something here for everyone.

I would HIGHLY recommend giving this game a try, especially if you love a good space adventure and enjoy having the freedom to create your own little universe. ❤️

Some games are more than just games; they become childhood memories that you carry with you. Spore is definitely one of those games for me. 🥹

Here's to creating weird aliens, evolving into strange creatures, and conquering the galaxy one planet at a time! 👽🚀😂

Yes, I am aware that Mirror's Edge is beloved by many, and I have no aim to tell people that they are wrong. In fact, I think there are certainly things to like about mirrors edge. The art style clean and stylish, and ties thematically into the world of the game. The visuals are very impressive for the game's age. The music is excellent, and great to listen to casually while I'm working. The voice acting is excellent. And of course, I have to recognize that at the time this game released, it was probably more impressive and groundbreaking in ways I don't recognize now.

With that being said however, in my opinion I was disappointed with Mirrors Edge. For starts, the game is very short. With only 10 levels, it took me just over 4 hours to complete the whole story. Sure, a game's length isn't everything, but the levels here felt very similar to one another. With the exception of maybe 2 or 3 levels, most just felt like the same concept: Go off to find a piece of the story, get ambushed, flee until you can lose the pursuers. Is that like saying mouse game has too much cheese reference? Maybe. But this is how I felt. 
Again, however, this could be excused if the freerunning was satisfying, rapid, and exciting. Sadly, again I was disappointed. It felt easy to get hung up on objects, for jumps to not work as expected, rolls to slow you down, or misleading direction to cause you to slip up or fall. 
From what I've played of the sequel, it seems to have fixed many of the complaints I have about the series debut, so that's excellent! Again, I have no hate toward fans of this game or the game itself, but it felt like it let me down on what it was selling me.

Ein Spiel, das sich traut, etwas anderes zu machen. Statt mit Waffen durch die Gegend zu ballern oder Gegnerhorden zu erledigen, geht es hier darum, möglichst flüssig über Dächer zu rennen, Hindernisse zu überwinden und der eigenen Verfolgung immer einen Schritt voraus zu sein.

Das Spielgefühl ist dabei die größte Stärke. Wenn man erst einmal im Rhythmus ist, von Dach zu Dach springt, über Geländer rutscht, Wände entlangläuft und im richtigen Moment die nächste Bewegung ausführt, entsteht ein richtig angenehmer Flow. Die Ego-Perspektive macht das Ganze zusätzlich intensiv. Man sieht die eigenen Bewegungen, spürt förmlich die Höhe und bekommt bei missglückten Sprüngen gelegentlich einen kleinen Adrenalinschub.

Auch optisch hat das Spiel einen unverwechselbaren Stil. Die sterile, helle Stadt mit ihren weißen Fassaden und den kräftigen Farbakzenten wirkt selbst heute noch eigenständig. Der Soundtrack passt hervorragend dazu und unterstützt die Atmosphäre, ohne sich ständig in den Vordergrund zu drängen.

Die Geschichte ist eher Mittel zum Zweck. Sie liefert einen Rahmen für die Flucht und die einzelnen Missionen, bleibt erzählerisch aber hinter dem eigentlichen Spielgefühl zurück. Auch die Kämpfe gehören nicht unbedingt zu den Highlights. Manchmal wird man aus dem flüssigen Parkour-Rhythmus gerissen und muss sich mit Gegnern beschäftigen, statt einfach weiterzulaufen.

Dazu kommt eine gewisse Eingewöhnungszeit. Die Steuerung verlangt Präzision, und gerade am Anfang landet man öfter als geplant im Abgrund. Manche Passagen können außerdem etwas frustrierend sein, wenn man den richtigen Weg nicht sofort erkennt.

Trotzdem bleibt ein eigenständiges Actionspiel mit einer hervorragenden Grundidee. Wer Parkour, Geschwindigkeit und ein ungewöhnliches Spielgefühl mag, sollte sich das nicht entgehen lassen.

I thought I enjoyed this game previously, but upon replaying it just now it's borderline abysmal. The graphics are beautiful, the city is very well realised and dense with details and the sound design is top notch. But the pacing is atrocious. You're never given more than 4 or 5 minutes of parkour puzzle solving before you're interrupted and pressured to run like hell to avoid gunfire and pursuing enemies. It's unnecessarily stressful and heartpounding. I don't mind have a few sections of intense getaways, but it happens multiple times in every single level. And again, the high intensity action moments come and go just as quickly as the comparatively peaceful parkouring. There are far too many ventilation shafts and elevators too. I think this is a good example of why constantly attempting to keep the player on their toes is not always a good thing.

It's worth checking out for the history - it's a very influential and well-remembered game, but I think it aged poorly. Play on easy mode, the combat is awful and frustrating and really detracts from the main event, which is the parkour. The parkour, when you're not being interrupted by combat, getting lost, or falling to your death because of clunky controls, feels very good. But I think since this game came out, the players and developers of platforming games have come to realise that tight, flowing controls are more fun than realism. The story is serviceable, nothing special.

One good thing I WILL say is that the environments are gorgeous, especially if you're into 2000s futurism like me. Obviously the beauty of the environments is supposed to be a symptom of the oppressive authoritarian government, but pretty is pretty. I wish I got to see more funky architectural concepts and less generic city rooftops and vent crawling.

It's definitely not worth the current price, especially for a game over 15 years old and less than 6 hours in length.

Y'know, being a non-parkour gamer and playing this for the first time, it's aged very poorly mechanically. Criticizing it is pointless, it's almost 20 years old, literally around my age, criticizing it with "today's standards" would be using experiences from games born from this game, it's silly.

That being said, I would say that parkour side of things, pretty good, only some parts being VERY frustrating due to weaker guidance and enemy gunfire. I know I said that mechanically, this game didn't age well, but I only really mean combat and difficulty. Easy means enemies kill you in 4 shots, normal means like 3 shots, hard means 1 shot. By today's standards, hard should be 3 shots. Look up a steam guide on how to change the FOV and if you get frustrated look up Mirror's Edge Tweaks, it made the last chapters bearable for me. Now let's get to praising.

With a 20 year old game, it's nostalgic. Back when games still had a lot of room for innovation instead of needing to be opportunistic or chase trends like friendslops or rogue likes, Mirror's Edge has exactly that feeling. The assets of a giant studio with only a handful of mechanics. Beautiful world where the player feels...less free to control. In a way, it almost feels realistic compared to modern first person video games. (Spoiler for mechanics) My favorite, absolute favorite part of the game, is falling to death. That sounds funny, but today's games would NEVER do this unless influenced by Mirror's Edge. Much rather just teleport the player back to checkpoints for efficiency. The first time I experienced it, it felt fresh and somehow, I felt like I was teleported back to the early 2000s, I could smell the mixture of clean air but overly clean, like ammonia and window cleaners, like the whiteness of the buildings was speaking to me. I wouldn't say I "recommend" this game, but I love this game.

Це добротна, якісна гра ще з тих часів, коли в них вкладали душу та ідеї, а не просто "аби зробити" чи "виключно заради прибутку". Гра 2008 року, але такі ігри доволі повільнр старіють, і навіть в 2026 я отримав багато задоволення від проходження.
Сюжет розповідає про кур'єрів, які доставляють товар на своїх двох та долають небезпеки та перешкоди на хмарочосах. [h1]Mirror's Edge[/h1] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3824691514 Hrana zrcadla je nejdůležitějším a nejzranitelnějším místem celé struktury, protože skrze ni může dojit k narušení ochranných vrstev a postupné korozi zrcadla. Žádné "Na ostří nože" - to je slovo knife, případně žiletka jako "Razor's Edge". Ne, nic takového. Hlavní hrdinka hry, Faith, situaci v úvodní cutscéně sama definuje slovy: [quote]„Existujeme na hraně, mezi nablýskaným povrchem a realitou. Na hraně zrcadla.“[/quote][list][*][b]Zrcadlo ([i]The Mirror[/i])[/b]: Představuje samotné futuristické město. To je na první pohled dokonalou, nablýskanou a čistou utopií plnou skleněných mrakodrapů. Lidé v něm vyměnili svá osobní práva a svobodu za absolutní bezpečí, pohodlí a komfort.[*][b]Hrana ([i]The Edge[/i])[/b]: Kurýři (tzv. Runneři), mezi které Faith patří, odmítli tomuto systému podlehnout a byli vytlačeni na okraj společnosti. Žijí na „hraně“ systému – vidí skrze falešný odraz dokonalého města (zrcadla) a znají jeho skutečnou, totalitní a zkorumpovanou realitu.[/list] Mirror's Edge od DICE je i po letech unikátní parkourový zážitek bez přímé konkurence. V roli kurýrky Faith unikáte totalitnímu režimu po střechách sterilně čistého, dystopického města. Hlavním tahákem je adrenalinový pocit z plynulého pohybu (flow) z první osoby, kdy skáčete z budov a odrážíte se od zdí. Nadčasový vizuální styl sází na minimalistickou paletu barev s ostrými kontrasty, což hře dává nezaměnitelnou identitu. Skvělou atmosféru navíc podtrhuje vynikající ambientní soundtrack od Solar Fieldse. V tomhle měště je Víra (Faith) tím, co narušuje tu falešnou čistotu na hraně zrcadla. Ale i tak si nemohu pomoct a vidím silnou paralelu s jistou ikonickou značkou... Podobnost mezi hrou Mirror's Edge a světem Æon Flux je až zarážející a obě díla sdílejí velmi specifickou estetickou i tematickou DNA. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3824692261 Oba tituly spojuje vize zdánlivě dokonalé, sterilní utopie, která ve skutečnosti skrývá totalitní útlak a kontrolu obyvatelstva. Hlavní paralely mezi oběma světy lze shrnout v těchto bodech:[list][*][b]Vizuální styl[/b]: Obě díla sázejí na futuristickou, minimalistickou architekturu plnou čistých linií, zářivě bílých ploch a ostrých, kontrastních barev. [*][b]Protagonistky[/b]: Běžkyně Faith i tajná agentka Aeon jsou atleticky extrémně nadané ženy v rebelské roli, které se vymykají systémové kontrole. [*][b]Akrobacie a pohyb[/b]: Klíčovým prvkem obou děl je parkour, extrémní akrobacie a plynulý pohyb, který hrdinky používají k překonávání překážek a vládních jednotek. [*][b]Informační odboj[/b]: Faith v Mirror's Edge funguje jako kurýr doručující zprávy mimo sledovanou síť, zatímco Æon bojuje v odboji proti totalitní radě vědců. [*][b]Iluzorní bezpečí[/b]: Město v Mirror's Edge i městský stát Bregna v Æon Flux se prezentují jako čistá, bezpečná a idylická místa pro život, vykoupená však absolutní ztrátou soukromí a svobody.[/list] V té době byl trh doslova zaplavený generickými 3D akcemi z pohledu třetí osoby a Æon Flux se sice snažila zaujmout akrobacií, ale v jádru to byl přesně ten typický spotřební produkt, který doprovázel hollywoodské premiéry. Navíc je to PlayStation a Xbox exkluzivita. Pokud vás baví tento specifický subžánr „čistého a jasného“ dystopického sci-fi (které na rozdíl od tradičního Blade Runnera nesází na špínu, tmu a neonový déšť)… tak tyhle díla rozhodně patří k nejlepším zástupcům z nultých let. I když nemusí být po chuti úplně každému. 

Ale zpátky ke hře. Rozhodně je lepší mít gamepad na hraní, ovládání je koneckonců na gamepad přímo ušité. Na Xbox 360 a PlayStation 3 vyšla tahle hra v listopadu 2008, zatímco PC verze dorazila až v lednu 2009. PC verze však dostala skvělou extra péči – studio DICE do ní jako bonus přidalo tehdy revoluční technologii Nvidia PhysX, která na počítačích zajistila realističtější trhání pláten, rozbíjení skla a pohyb kouře. Tohle vše tedy z téhle hry dělá ideální kousek pro Steam Deck, nebo jiný PC handheld. Jestli máte možnost, tak rozhodně to vypalte na 4K všechno na max... https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3828987842 Paradoxně i když koncept hraní téhle hry vypadá na první pohled snadno a hra sama o sobě není nijak extra dlouhá a grafická stylizace je nadmíru minimalistická, tak samotný gameplay vysloveně vyžaduje schopnost rychlého rozhodování a čtení prostoru z pohledu první osoby. Což následně znamená, že jsou nutné i dobře načasované kombinace QTE reakcí - podle toho co se na parkůrové trase zrovna před postavou objeví. A levely nabídnou né vždy jen jednu možnou cestu. Celý parkour v Mirror's Edge je vlastně jeden velký, nepřetržitý řetězec rychlých reakcí, kde každá překážka představuje okamžitou výzvu: „teď vyskoč“, „teď udělej skluz“, „teď se otoč o 180 stupňů“. Jakmile člověk mine jedno okno pro správný stisk, okamžitě ztratí rychlost a celé plynulé „flow“ se rozpadne. Z tohoto pohledu je to skutečně mechanicky velmi blízké tomu, jak fungují QTE pasáže – jen s tím rozdílem, že vám hra neukazuje ikony tlačítek na obrazovce, ale musíte ty správné podněty číst přímo z okolního prostředí a architektury města.[hr][/hr] [b]Parkůr par excelence... (… [i]i když né pro každého[/i].)[/b]

As a child, I was obsessed with parkour. Weaving your way through and across obstacles that weren't actually intended to be traversed, but to keep out, obstruct -- parkour is the ultimate expression of freedom, of movement in an urban environment. It's beautiful. Naturally, my fascination for this sport carried over into my love of games. For a large part of my childhood, I found that outlet in the early Assassin's Creed titles. I had also heard and seen much of Mirror's Edge, but I never had the means to play it. So I contented myself with the iOS version and became obsessed with the game's theme song, "Still Alive". Eventually, EA announced a soft reboot in 2016 that proclaimed to be the return of a cult classic that seemed doomed for obscurity. I bought, played, and loved it on Day 1, even though I recognized the game's many shortcomings.

The years passed, and even when I got the means to catch up on the original, I put it off. And so it sat in my Steam library, waiting for the day when I would finally free it from my backlog prison. Now, I finally did.

Mirror's Edge is every bit as magical as I had imagined: the movement, the level design...they are extraordinary. And yet, they would be nothing without the brilliant visual style and sound design they are wrapped in. The contrast of colors is harsh and blinding, reflecting the sanitized and corporate reality of the city. This is accentuated by the fact that there's almost no HUD at all, only the occasional red glow to indicate your goal. I love how tactfully it guides you through the game without ever diminishing the need to find your own path. But you will fail and fall to your death, and the game will let you feel the fragility of a human body. Parkour is dangerous, and that danger only makes it more exhilerating. In that vein, Mirror's Edge is a challenging game, one that isn't a smooth ride on a first playthrough; but then again, it doesn't seem to have been made for a first playthrough, but for a second, a third, a fourth. For the true beauty of this game lies in knowing it and flowing through it on memory. The game may only be 4 hours long, yet it's the ideal length for this exact structure.

In 2026, Mirror's Edge appears as a relict from its time that, much like early Assassin's Creed games, could never be made by AAA developers today. There are still great games coming out (get out of here, doomers), but they will never ever be the same as games from the 2000s. Especially not when it comes to parkour.

Un éditeur qui préfère enterrer ses licences plutôt que de les faire vivre.

EA continue de démontrer ce qui ne va pas dans l'industrie du jeu vidéo : des studios talentueux sont sacrifiés, des équipes qui ont consacré des années à créer des univers et des licences appréciés par des millions de joueurs sont démantelées, et des franchises entières finissent abandonnées.

BioWare fait partie de ces studios qui ont marqué l'histoire du jeu vidéo. Mass Effect, Dragon Age… Des univers, des personnages et des histoires qui ont profondément marqué toute une génération de joueurs. Et derrière ces jeux, il y avait des développeurs passionnés, dont le travail mérite mieux que d'être traité comme des pièces jetables.

Le plus enrageant dans tout ça, c'est cette logique qui consiste à laisser mourir des licences plutôt que de leur donner une nouvelle chance. Si EA ne souhaite plus investir dans certaines franchises, pourquoi ne pas simplement les vendre ou en céder les droits à des studios qui seraient prêts à les faire vivre ? Pourquoi préférer les laisser prendre la poussière plutôt que de permettre à d'autres développeurs de reprendre le flambeau ?

Pour ma part, j'ai décidé de ne plus soutenir cette politique. Je vais donc mettre un avis négatif aux jeux édités par EA sur Steam, non pas nécessairement parce que ces jeux sont mauvais mais parce que je refuse de soutenir EA de quelque manière que ce soit. Bien entendu, plus aucun jeux édités par eux ne sera acheté de ma part également, c'est un peu dommage car certains m'intéressaient mais tant pis.

Adieu EA donc, puisse la licence Mass Effect revenir un jour

评测后面steam有版本选择方法，前面为我自己的重温体验。游戏虽然无论在当年还是现在玩都可称为神作，但宇宙阶段的问题实在是太大太大了，对于习惯要一周目通关的玩家来说及其不友好。

前几个阶段和记忆中一样好玩，城市阶段头一次体验了小时候没玩的经济型城市打法，还蛮有意思的，由于没有攻击手段，我本来以为只剩另外一个势力之后要用技能里的各种炸弹来打，没想到直接就算过了。捏人捏物没有记忆中的自由了，最大的限制倒不是复杂度条，而是主体部件只能居中放置，外加部分可动部件不会连带相连接的部件一起动，导致我宇宙阶段捏的高达变得非常鬼畜。

说说宇宙阶段吧，这个阶段是非常具有时代感的自动填充马桶，哪怕是加上了DLC的一些手搓下船冒险部分还是无聊透顶，推进器的几个进度锁还逼得玩家只能一点点花时间磨，过于痛苦了。实际上宇宙阶段游玩方式的骨架搭的非常好，只要加一些自动化的内容变成类似模拟经营立马就能跑得通了，里面那些有趣且独特的行星改造相关内容也终于能玩得起了。

以现在的玩法，宇宙中的Grox实在是太tm多了，加上银河中心减移动距离的debuff，不停地去使用重置飞船状态的秘籍都很难冲得过去，游戏里甚至没有真能用来直接通关的自带秘籍，加上老游戏的网上的修改器基本不是失灵就是会导致游戏闪退，我只好把游戏文件改了，修改方法和链接我也放在指南里吧。由于我只是将飞船血量修改到超级大，想要进银河中心还是需要玩家自己玩到拥有四级引擎，所以用这个东西应该也不算缺失了什么体验，只是用来让玩家进入宇宙中心再出来找地球的。如果在搞到四级引擎之前就受不了了，可以游戏内ctrl+shift+c唤出控制台输入moremoney来快速来钱推进流程进度。

很好奇如果不修改一直玩到找到地球需要花多长时间。

终于是重新完整体验了一遍童年神作，无憾了。
---------------------------------
虽说是为童年补票，但现存steam版本问题真的很大，本体和两个DLC都是作为游戏上架的，花了半天才搞懂怎么完美体验完整版（当然狗屎EA已经把服务器关了，下载玩家线上上传的作品已经不可能了），所以打个差评辱骂EA。

为了完整体验，首先必须要三个全部下载，但下载后你会发现本体打开只是本体，外观dlc打开就是本体＋外观，宇宙dlc打开就是本体+宇宙，所以我们需要打开外观dlc的文件目录，从其中的BP1_Content文件夹中找到名为BoosterPack_01.package的文件放入宇宙dlc的本地文件DataEP1文件夹中，这样就能通过宇宙dlc入口打开全部内容。

同时，你会发现游戏即使通过右键游戏属性，通用里的高级启动项输入“-locale cs-cz”获得简中汉化仍有大量未翻译或者“BAD DATA”，还有很多该有UI的地方是白框。所以想要获得舒适体验，参考知乎“告白气球YZ”的回答，应在3dm下繁体汉化，再下载3dm简体中文补丁润色美化版（具体链接可以去知乎获取，我也在每个版本都写了带链接的指南，看的话顺手点个赞吧 ）。找到孢子本体文件的位置，把解压好的zh-tw直接复制粘贴在Spore/Data/Locale文件夹里，不要替换原文件使用方法说的en-us，然后将美化版里的文件覆盖zh-tw里的文件，右键游戏属性，通用里的高级启动项输入“-locale:zh-tw”。这样的版本虽然有些地方会有简繁掺杂的情况，但该有的信息应该都有并看得懂了。

唉，要不是突然想怀旧，谁愿意费劲去鼓捣这些EA本就该做的事情啊。

想要更好的体验似乎宇宙版还有解锁 30帧的小技巧，但之中没有什么动作属性的游戏我也不是特别重视 高帧数，就这样吧，该方法在评测高赞里应该也能找得到。

“Im commander Shepard and this is my favorite review on the citadel” – commander Shepard – probably – if I gave him a discount.

DEEP DIVE - And that brings us to the reason we're here.
Your Shepard, your story
One of the things that makes Mass Effect so special is that this is YOUR Shepard, and this is YOUR story.
You can choose between two pre-designed versions of Commander Shepard — the only two Shepards I'll personally recognise as canon — or create your own character from scratch.
You choose one of three psychological profiles and one of three military backgrounds, each of which unlocks unique dialogue, encounters and story details throughout the trilogy. You also choose from six classes — Soldier, Engineer, Adept, Infiltrator, Sentinel and Vanguard — each offering a distinct playstyle that carries across all three games.
Want to be a biotic powerhouse who throws enemies around like ragdolls? Go for it. Prefer manipulating technology, sneaking around the battlefield invisble and sniping your foes or simply shooting everything that moves? There's a class for that, too.
And these aren't just cosmetic choices. Your background can affect how Shepard responds to certain situations, while your class fundamentally changes how you approach combat. Different builds can make subsequent playthroughs feel surprisingly different.
All three games feature extensive dialogue, fully voiced characters and, importantly, a fully voiced protagonist. Yes, even Shepard speaks! (something even the legendary Baldur’s gate 3 doesn’t do!)
There's an enormous amount of optional dialogue for those who want to immerse themselves in the universe, but you can also skip conversations when you want to keep things moving. The result is a cinematic RPG that offers plenty of depth without forcing you to experience every conversation on every playthrough.
Then there's the character import system.
Your Shepard carries over between all three games, along with your decisions and their consequences as well as some possible bonuses (money, levels, resources etc). Characters you save, relationships you develop and choices you make can have repercussions several games later. It's an incredible achievement, and one of the biggest reasons this trilogy feels like one continuous adventure rather than three disconnected games.
Your decisions aren't just dialogue options that disappear when the conversation ends. They become part of your story.
And that brings us to replayability.
Different classes, backgrounds, psychological profiles, relationships and major decisions give you plenty of reasons to return. You can experience the same overarching story and still discover new interactions, different outcomes and details you missed the first time around.
For some perspective, a typical playthrough on Normal difficulty takes me around 24 hours per game to complete everything. My latest run, however, was on Insanity difficulty, and I made a point of reading all the planetary descriptions along the way. That pushed each game to roughly 50 hours.
That's around 150 hours for one trilogy playthrough!
And I've done this more times than I care to admit.
Technically high replayability. Practically MASSIVE.
Mass Effect 1 — Where it all began
First and foremost, the gameplay is a third person cover shooter, hwoever with additional “abilities” you use to supplement your weapons with. Think gears of war, only much…much rougher, but the game is so much more than its poor third person shooter mechanics. When I first played Mass Effect, I fell in love with it from beginning to end. With the benefit of hindsight and many subsequent playthroughs, however, I can see that it's easily the weakest entry in the trilogy.

This was BioWare still finding its identity. You can feel the influence of Knights of the Old Republic throughout the experience, particularly in the combat and RPG systems. The dialogue and world-building are already fantastic, but the combat feels clunky, and the weapons and abilities aren't nearly as satisfying as they become in the sequels.
Biotics, essentially this universe's version of the Force, are a particular highlight. Playing a biotic character makes you feel like a genuine space wizard, and that's awesome. (through all 3 games I find myself using “pull” while yelling “Get over here” in scorpions voice from mortal combat and then Hadouken or something as equally stupid when I combine biotics for an explosion… very satisfying) The opening story grabs you immediately, but once you reach the Citadel, prepare to spend HOURS there. It's fantastic on a first playthrough, when you're absorbing the lore and meeting the characters, but on subsequent runs, though, it can feel like one very long walking simulator mixed with detective work. (its feels the same as having to endure the start of fallout 3 or 4 on multiple games)
The main missions are excellent, and the side content shows just how ambitious BioWare was (you often receive writing prompts that read more like a cut scene they wanted to implement into the game). Unfortunately, you can also see where that ambition ran into limitations. Side missions reuse a small selection of buildings and environments, and planetary exploration in the Mako can become tedious once the novelty wears off.
I loved exploring planets when the game was new. Back then, the scale of the universe felt incredible. These days, after years of playing other open-world games, those same sections feel considerably less exciting. That's not necessarily the game's fault; gaming has simply moved on.
The game also lays the groundwork for companion loyalty missions, with personal quests involving Garrus (killing dr saleon), Tali (geth data), Wrex (family armor) and Liara (confronting Benezia). These early missions are a glimpse of the brilliant character-driven storytelling that would become a defining feature of the sequels. This was the idea in its infancy as you can actually complete all these quests without even taking them with you haha.

The Legendary Edition also omits the Pinnacle Station DLC. It's not essential content, but the combat simulations offered a useful opportunity to experiment with weapons and builds, so its absence is disappointing.
Despite its flaws, Mass Effect 1 establishes the universe, the characters and the stakes that make the entire trilogy work. It's a little rough around the edges, but without it, we wouldn't have the masterpiece that follows and despite its short comings there are still segments that bring me goosebumps to this day!

for the record i mostly played this on ea games (rip origin) so i have way more hours in this than shown
if you play a lot of games, its hard to really miss mass effect from the list. as a whole the series is both famous and infamous, but id say the original is known for more good than bad. its a good game, and by far has the greatest worldbuilding in the series, in my opinion, and also takes the most advantage of being an exploration into sci-fi as a genre. it also had one of the biggest outrages over a bisexual character, that being liara, from its era. thats probably the area where id say the game is most brave though haha - as a whole the game isnt necessarily anything too new to the genre, especially given the sheer amount of contemporary sci-fi games that you will likely have seen or played by this point. that being said, mass effect absolutely had one of the biggest impacts on the genre in gaming and genuinely deserves the praise; the story is enjoyable and doesnt feel too contrived, the characters all have their own niches to fulfill and are genuinely more complex than you might expect at first, and the romances (while much more so in the succeeding entries) arent as immature as youll find in other games containing this sort of "romancing" system.
given this, i do think its important to mention the clear immaturity the game shows that improves in certain ways across the series. the characters are fairly developed given their era, but certainly not all of them. who the hell cares about kaiden man. is that even his name? i dont really care. hes painfully boring and--if you play with a female shepherd--awful to talk to if you do not plan on romancing the guy. even then, he doesnt get any more interesting. and ashley is fairly annoying, but it is for a reason. i mention them because you do have to interact with these characters quite a bit, and are one of the most important human characters in the game. the side characters are very interesting, along with the main cast, though.
in addition, the choice system isnt as fantastic as a lot of people seem to claim. i feel like people truly aggrandise how much gaming has progressed since the 2000s. of course the extent of what can be done has improved, but i feel like its often forgotten just how much people made do with what they had. with that said, the choice system, acknowledging this, is not that great. its impressively simplistic and dumbs down most moral choices to "good" (paragon) and "bad" (renegade.) this continues throughout the series, though i believe the choices become more interesting over time. its enjoyable to play, but if youre a hardcore roleplayer that enjoys having a complicated main character then this isnt the most impressive thing out there. i can respect the iconicity of it though, and its still very enjoyable.
even though i criticise the choices in of themselves, the characters which influence and are influenced by them are actually pretty good in my opinion. id argue that mass effect, in at least some senses, did revolutionise this intertwinement of choice based story progression alongside the shooter aspects, which were more at home in games that didnt contain that sort of thing. this is more of a side note, and its pretty well joked about, but i find the facial expression system they used to be particularly impressive, honestly. its not really relevant but you should look it up if you dont know and are interested. the way the dialogue is laid out and the pacing, camera angles, and extensive voice acting, are so characteristic of the series and so beloved & iconic that i genuinely believe you are missing out by having not played the games. i think that goes for everything in mass effect though. its just such an integral part of the culture of video games that i think its a worthwhile experience.
the first game is the most different to the other two, which accustom much more aggressively to the game industry standards at the time. the first mass effect takes more precedent in its worldbuilding than the story (though the story isnt awful either) and is much more traditional in the sci-fi aspects of that worldbuilding. id argue it definitely rivals star trek or star wars. the gameplay is also much less developed (which is to be expected), and quite frankly just less enjoyable for me. this doesnt make it bad though. it isnt very complicated and still pretty fun, but doesnt really spring to mind when i think of fun third person shooters. i appreciate the use of the squad members a lot, but it isnt really necessitated in the easier modes.
overall i believe this game is clunky in some aspects, and wildly impressive in others, but overall worth it. its an enjoyable game if you arent opposed to sci-fi and weird voice acting. also garrus and wrex are my favourite squad members in any of the games, and they get introduced here so automatic buy. i criticise it, but mostly out of love

Самой сильной стороной первого Mass Effect, как и всей серии, является его лор, сюжет и персонажи, которые уже успели сделать вселенную  Mass Effect одной из самых узнаваемых и проработанных научно-фантастических вселенных из когда-либо созданных. В целом настоятельно рекомендую к ознакомлению, тем более если вы планируете играть во вторую и третью часть, первую нужно проходить обязательно ведь она во многом является прологом к последующим частям и знакомит с лором этой вселенной.

review: Mass Effect ist ein tolles Sci-Fi RPG, das mit seiner interessanten Welt und Charakteren punktet. Besonders die Hauptfigur Commander Shepard sticht als das perfekte Mittel zum Ausleben der Heldenfantasie hervor. Jennifer Hale spricht im Englischen den weiblichen Shepard grandios. Die Geschichte ist stringent und mündet in einem epischen Finale. Nur das Gameplay kann durch seine Altbackenheit etwas abschreckend sein und die Mako-Sequenzen, in denen man ein Fahrzeug auf den Planeten steuert, sind schlecht gealtert. Man muss sich etwas an sie gewöhnen. Dennoch hat Mass Effect nicht umsonst seine Ära geprägt und sollte wie alle Teile der Trilogie von jedem gespielt worden sein. Was Dank der Legendary Edition nun in seiner besten Form möglich ist.

Score: 4/5
I recommend playing the packaged and remastered trilogy instead, primarily due to the enhanced visuals.
I play Mass Effect for the character stories/relationships, not for riveting gameplay or realism.
Micromanaging your inventory is a key part of the game, and is anti-fun.


Writing ranges from bad to great. The character relationships, growth/exploration/backstories, and interactions/dialogues are mostly on the positive side, often great. The setting/world building is evocative and mysterious. But the main quest's anti-immersive don't-take-this-seriously galactic military adventure is riddled with plot-armor and space opera crap, along with a moderate amount of contrivance and cool set-pieces and explosions. Branching narratives are good within the context of this entry, but have major issues when considering how the later entries integrate, or ignore, your choices from this game.

At the time, the visuals were cutting edge, close to the most photo-realistic RPG/story-focused game I had played.
However, the character visuals aged very poorly when compared to the remastered trilogy thing.
The buildings/vehicles/environments/enemies almost all hold up though.

Audio/SFX/music are all between good and great. Male Shepard's VA, Mark Meer, is rough. Not sure if it was bad direction, or that he wasn't taking the character/role seriously enough, but I was very frequently annoyed or had my immersion broken when playing male Shepard. Even when it meant I was unable to explore what is arguably the best character content in the trilogy. Female Shepard's VA, Jennifer Hale, did an excellent job, with her performance allowing me stay immersed in the goofy setting for such a long time.

Gameplay and balance are rough. Inventory micromanagement and menu navigation is an unpleasantly time-intensive part of this game, with unnecessarily restrictive stored item/resource limits. Cooldowns are awful, ruining most of the ability-focused classes. One of the classes is significantly better than all the others, not relying on many abilities, and as such is one of the least interesting to play.

Pacing is pretty slow, but grinding is not required. There are a limited amount of encounters in the game, so at most you can seek out every encounter/optional quest and you still won't be able to hit max level. The story and character interactions are also doled out fairly slowly, but do build up significantly over the course of a playthrough.

Mass Effect ist für mich bis heute eines der stärksten Sci-Fi-Rollenspiele überhaupt.

Natürlich merkt man dem ersten Teil sein Alter an. Das Kampfsystem ist etwas sperriger als in den Nachfolgern, die Inventarverwaltung kann nerven und manche Planetenmissionen wiederholen sich recht deutlich. Trotzdem hat das Spiel eine Atmosphäre, die mich bis heute sofort wieder einfängt.

Der eigentliche Star ist für mich die Welt. Die Normandy, die Crew, die Citadel und die vielen fremden Spezies wirken nicht wie bloße Kulisse, sondern wie ein glaubwürdiges Universum mit Geschichte, Konflikten und eigenen Regeln. Man fühlt sich wirklich, als wäre man Teil von etwas Großem.

Besonders stark sind die Figuren und die Entscheidungen. Ob man mit Garrus, Wrex, Liara oder Tali unterwegs ist: Die Crew bleibt im Kopf. Dazu kommt die Geschichte rund um Saren und die Reaper, die von Anfang an eine Bedrohung aufbaut, die weit größer wirkt als die eigene Mission.

Auch wenn spätere Teile spielerisch moderner sind, hat der erste Mass Effect für mich einen ganz eigenen Charme. Er nimmt sich Zeit für seine Welt, lässt einen entdecken und schafft es, aus einer scheinbar klassischen Weltraumgeschichte etwas wirklich Besonderes zu machen.

Für mich ein Pflichtspiel für jeden, der Sci-Fi und Rollenspiele mag. Etwas angestaubt an den Kanten, aber atmosphärisch und erzählerisch immer noch großartig.

I love Dead Space and it's music/ambience, it is a game I may not have been around for to play it. But I have began to love it since a few years ago. It is such a good horror. It's the 2000's effect where stuff was somehow better and worse. It just hits.

There’s a moment in Dead Space when you open your inventory to see how much ammo you have left and realize you’re still listening to the room around you. The game keeps running while Isaac checks his supplies, and suddenly even sorting through a few items feels like something you should do with your back to a wall. The USG Ishimura is full of little details like that. A light flickers, something rattles behind a vent, and you find yourself aiming at an empty corridor just in case.

The Plasma Cutter gives combat a rhythm of its own. Taking a leg off a charging Necromorph buys you a second, but it can still drag itself toward you while you deal with whatever else has come through the vents. Stasis gives you enough time to line up a shot when things get crowded. Some of the best fights end with you looking at your remaining ammo and wondering how a room that small cost you so much.

The Ishimura is the real star. The engine room sounds like it could shake itself apart, while the vacuum sections strip away most of the noise and leave you listening to Isaac breathe. The campaign can wear that atmosphere thin when it sends you off to fix yet another piece of machinery. The zero-gravity asteroid defense sequence is the clearest stumble, with a turret that makes for a frustrating change of pace.

**9/10.** The original Dead Space is worth playing for the way it makes ordinary things feel dangerous. By the time you reach the end, the sound of an elevator arriving can be enough to make you raise your weapon.
