Unstoppable Gorg is delightfully corny in so many ways, from its visuals, to its music, to them going to the trouble of making black and white live action film of people acting for the stuff in between missions. There are various towers with different purposes and enough variation between them to make it worthwhile to select certain towers over others depending on upcoming enemy composition, etc. I really like not only the idea, but much of the execution for the game.

However, my one hangup with it is what probably sets it apart the most from other tower defense games: tower mobility. You place a tower on an orbital ring, and can typically place others on the same orbital ring, on the opposite of that ring, or even on the side of it. Then you click the left mouse button on the tower and can spin it around to the other side of your defense point to take out incoming enemies. 

The big issue for someone like me is that I'm pretty darn ADD, and anyone who suffers from it to my extent may find themselves getting overwhelmed by incoming attack waves while trying to keep track of the [i]simultaneous[/i] attacks from different sides, from different enemy compositions, while having to try to spin the right towers on the right rings into the right spots to defend.

It's just too much I have to keep up with at the same time to be capable of doing so. If towers were stationary and the game was designed around that instead, this could be a massive hit with me, but as it is, this feature makes the game incredibly difficult even on lower settings. Anyone with a huge attention span and dexterity who can keep up with and react to a lot of things happening on-screen at once would probably dig this game if they're into TDs and cornball stuff, while those with attention span or dexterity problems might do well to avoid what would otherwise be a pleasant experience.

Now, this game... what a shame. It had everything going on for it: Excelent 60's sci-fi B-movie atmosphere, good graphics, good soundtrack and the right idea. This should've been a "must play" TD game, right?

But no, it's not. Far from it, because the gameplay is just utter crap. First of all the TD mechanic is SUPER restrictive and completely un-intuitive, sure it looked like a nifty concept, but the execution is below subpar. It's like the game is actually a puzzle and it's forcing you to find the correct and only strategy to win each map because god knows there's no room for having fun with different setups.

On top of it, the towers themselves are honestly quite boring and the game doesn't really add anything new to the genre, except for that awkward, weird and ultimately failed rotationary orbital system that forces you to find the correct solution and micromanage like crazy as well.

And again, it's a shame because the rest of the package is really cool. I mean, it's cheesy as hell, but that's intended, and it really works... So in the end, I'm afraid I can't recommend this, as much as I'd like to, purely in terms of gameplay and fun. It's not very fun to play, honestly. 

But hey, if you're a fan of weird cheesy 60's low quality sci-fi flicks, you might want to check this game and enjoy it on a purely aesthetic way.

If you're looking for your next TD fix, stay away from this.

[h1]At the Time of Writing[/h1]
[b]Game:[/b] Unstoppable Gorg
[b]Price:[/b] $9.99*
[b]Genre:[/b] tower defence
[b]Time Played:[/b] 16 hours**
[b]Personal Enjoyment Rating:[/b] ☺☺☺☻☻

[h1]General[/h1]
Tower defence is pretty much my favourite genre of game, and although this one won't be making my top favourite TD game list, I found it to be perfectly enjoyable. It certainly held my interest long enough for me to complete the game.

Although it doesn't offer the sort of playtime that Defense Grid does, I found it a nice change to have a game that is a full meal rather than an uneatable feast. I love to have uneatable feasts, but there is something to be said about having a satisfyingly full meal which comes to an end.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Your standard tower defence concept of waves of enemies which you must stop otherwise you lose the level. Build different towers which have different stats (range, damage, damage type, expense) and upgrade them.

I like it when tower defence games bring in a slightly different twist and then also execute it fairly well. Not some silly bit of fluff that doesn't change the game in any way. Unstoppable Gorg has you place your towers in set locations, however they are generally on moveable rings which allow you to position your towers as needed. You can even click and drag to slowly keep your beefed up tower in range of the enemy for as long as possible.

This ring mechanic is very interesting, and although some levels take it a little further - by either making a ring spin continuously or locking the ring from being moved - I felt that this concept could have been developed a lot more. If it had been, and to the point that it required you to do some real strategising in order to win the level, then this game would have got four happiness out of me.

Speaking of strategy, I should talk about the difficulty level of this game. There have been other reviews which say that the difficulty is much too hard. This was actually something which prompted me to purchase the game, but I was disappointed on that score. The four difficulty levels are: easy, moderate, hard, unstoppable. I did not find that there was a very noticeable difference between moderate and unstoppable, which was odd. I'm afraid that as a long-time fangirl of tower defence games I'm probably reasonably good at them, but when the unstoppable difficulty never posed much of a challenge for me (except for just one level out of 21***) I'm really not convinced that this game is very hard.

[h1]Controls[/h1]
Nice and simple. One can use just the mouse, but the game also has things linked to hotkeys. Each tower type relates the the number keys, and you can toggle the speed of the game between fast and normal with the spacebar with esc essentially being your pause button.

[h1]Storyline[/h1]
I find it funny that this game does try to provide a storyline. I know that I don't "get" this sort of humour at all, but I do recognise that they put quite a lot of effort and work into the little movie clips.

Before and after each level, you get a short B-movie style clip. They make me think of Star Trek Voyager (Captain Proton) and Thunderbirds. It's an extremely basic, banal storyline, but it is entertaining to see all the custom spaceship models they created, the "special effects" and the silly costumes.

One thing I really wish they'd done was to include some sort of 'click to continue' button for the clips, because some of them were essentially newspaper articles and there was no where near enough time for my dyslexic self to read them. I wasn't desperate enough to read them to go to the lengths of snapping a screenshot.

[h1]Sound[/h1]
Rather one dimensional I thought. There are pretty much two tunes (maybe three, I wasn't counting) and they get played over and over and over again. Although I didn't find it annoying, I certainly didn't find the music to be very engaging.

There is one sound effect which is relevant to gameplay - the sound of a tower that's about to explode. 

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
Enjoyable enough a look. I can't say that the graphics are ground breaking, or that they particularly help to create an exciting new visual universe to immerse yourself in. The visuals let you know what sort of tower you're looking at, what sort of enemy is coming your way, and the path that the enemies will take.

However, I will say that there were a couple of rather enjoyable "bases" to defend, in the form of the moon, and planet earth.

[h1]Pros[/h1]
[b]+ [/b]different "moving ring" mechanic
[b]+ [/b]silly B-movie style clips
[b]+ [/b]fully consumable length of game
[h1]Cons[/h1]
[b]- [/b]not very challenging
[b]- [/b]silly B-movie style clips

While fun at first, and made better by an interesting play mechanic, this game is frustrating to say the least (and not a in a buggy way, purely in terms of play).  I'm a huge fan tower defense in general but this game feels a little unbalanced and too hard to be accessible to the masses that I imagine they intended to sell this one to.

For 99 cents or some other low sale, give it a try, but don't feel a need to pay retail for this one. It is largely disappointing...and did I say frustrating.

Tower Defence games have so far passed me completely by.  They just don't seem all that interesting, an exercise in game over.. again.. game over.. again.. etc.. but not in the fun "Super Hexagon" way.  Setting all those towers, and then failing at the very end, when the very last minion makes it past your last carefully-laid planned route, and deals the death strike that spells a do-over.. Gah.  The worst kind of time sink...

Unstoppable Gorg attempts to shake the tower-defence up a bit.. The levels are short, the number of towers small, and their placement is quite crucial.  It also adds an interesting twist: You can spin the towers around to face enemies coming from a different way.  Like Space Run, Unstoppable Gorg takes the Tower Defence idea and adds in a few little twists.  There's just enough here to make it stand out a little from the crowd.

Ok, game mechanics to one side, the rest of the game is pretty good.  It draws heavily from 1950's Sci-Fi imagery and schtick.  It does a phenomenal job of it too.  All the painstaking hours of cutting footage and re-creating that wobbly-saucer-on-a-string feeling really pays off.  The storyline is as cringe-inducingly 50s as it can be.   One thing which made me giggle was the brief appearance of a few 10-Base-T BNC terminators acting as the engine pods on a very dated-looking "War Rocket Ajax".. *cough*.. I mean "Invincible" :) .. about 40 years too early, :)

Unlike some games which seem to peter out in the FMV in later levels, and just give text or voice instructions (low budget maybe?) only to spring back to FMV for the final "death scene", each level begins and ends with a "Galaxy News" transmission.  . Each one is lush, well filmed and voiced.  Right up to the end, the game feels "fleshed out", there are no 'thin' parts, if you see what I mean.

The game plays very well at lower difficulties: the placement and timing of the 'towers', erm, I mean satellites, doesn't matter too much. You can get away with making mistakes.  As you get to higher difficulties, however, the fun starts to turn to the usual Tower Defence Grind Syndrome: placement and timing are crucial.   The "orbital slots" are very carefully placed by the level designers, and it requires the right satellite, with the right level of upgrade placed in the right order, and the slots have to be spun into the right position at the right time.  Getting a level finished can require playing it repeatedly over and over and over until the placement and spinning becomes muscle-memory.  

There are only 22 "single player" levels, so even grinding won't make the game stretch to the buttock-achingly 400+ hours you get out of Skyrim or something.  The levels come with research and a selection of satellites that you can select a subset of.  Most levels obviate the satellite choice, and some leave it a little open for you.  I never found much use for the "sweeper" or the "webber", they just seemed to take up a slot and not do enough to justify it.  Replacing them with a missile or ray gun would do far far better!  I'd increase their range and effectiveness a tad.

One strategy which I totally missed through my first playthrough was selling satellites.  Enemies come in waves, and I'd build my satellites to eventually counter all the waves.  Once I realised that selling satelites and reconfiguring for a next (more powerful) wave was an option, a whole new avenue of play opened up.  So, as you can see, there's quite a lot of replay value too.  The game invites you to try to get better, and beat it on harder levels with better strategies.  It's not punitive, and doesn't rub your face in defeat too much.  I quite like it.  It's a friendly-feeling game, which you can pick up, play, and put down.. or stare-at for hours-on-end (as I did).


Don't recommend it to anyone who doesn't like a bit of rinse-repeat gameplay that typifies these sorts of games.  It's better than most, though. It can make you scream when, after a long battle, you see you lost two medals because you lost 1% of your ship's complement to a stray asteroid some time while distracted killing the mothership.


I do wholeheartedly recommend this to anyone who has a laptop and sometimes just has a spare few hours (on a train, in an airport, or lying in bed waiting for sleep to kick in), and wants to have a bit of retro-movie fun, and doesn't mind a bit of action/puzzle.

A silly tower defense game.  Fortunately, I happen to like silly tower defense games.
It offers a decent variety of towers and enemies, always a key ingredient.  (Although I found some of the tower types more or less indispensable, and others pretty worthless.)  You get money from killing enemies, but also from building generators, so there is that tension between investing and beefing up your defenses.  

Lastly, the game brings us something new: orbiting towers.  All your defenses must be placed at preset points in 2-4 rings surrounding your ship/station.  These rings are fixed in distance from the center, and the build points are fixed in distance from each other, but the entire ring can be rotated.  This lets you move your towers into position near the enemy's attack paths (highlighted by glowy dotted lines), or even follow a wave around to keep it in range longer.  Since the levels are in space, with no real 'terrain', this is a good way of doing things.

One of the game's strongest points is actually not the system itself, but the whole aesthetic.  The entire thing, down to the last detail, is done over to look like a cheesy, low-budget, 40s/50s sci-fi movie/TV show.  The costumes in the live-action cutscenes, the flying saucer enemies, the robots that look like they were patched together from old car parts, the towers that look like they're made of cardboard and tinfoil, and the buttons & iconography on the menus all appear just like you'd expect them to.  I've never played a game that did something similar, and while I wouldn't want it to become a trend, it really works here.

This one was a pleasant surprise. I think everyone is sick of tower-defense games by now, but this one has a pretty interesting mechanic. You place your defense sattelites on building spots on orbits. Each orbit can be freely rotated, but only the entirety of the orbit can be moved. So you can click and drag your towers to make them follow the critters, but you run the risk of moving other towers on the same ring *away* from enemy paths. Similarly, you might end up moving support towers near enemies where they have no business being. So it's a bit more involved than just placing towers and clicking "go". So that's fun! The difficulty seems alright, too. I can generally make "Moderate" at first try. "Hard" and "Unstoppable", not so much. There are a few nuisances - like having to reassign Research Points at the start of *every* mission - but nothing too grating.

The writing is pretty nice. Obviously, a game like this isn't going to have astonishing Deus Ex-esque plot - actually, the fact that there's a plot at all surprised me. It's deliberately patterned after horrible old sci-fi movies, which is nice if you like it. (I very much do!) If you don't, well, you can skip the cutscenes and you won't lose anything. 

So on the overall, I'd say this is well worth it, if you can get it for less than 10 dollars. A few things made me roll my eyes - really, you don't need to tell me five times about what enemies are vulnerable to - and obviously it's a bit rough around the edges, but nothing big. I could see this do nicely on mobile devices. How about an Android port?

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

I don't know who needs to see this in 2023, but don't bother with this game. If you want a marble game, there are better options. In my experience of playing through its very short main queue of levels, I would say Spectraball's design came through as thoroughly uninspired, clunky, and sometimes frustrating. The level design in particular has you going through extremely linear paths with repetitive, confusing obstacles, and platforming challenges that feel a bit miscalibrated at times. All of this is made just a little bit worse by the slightly awkward physics, as well. The music feels, to my ear, equally uninspired, as well as the visual style, which features cliche environments and sterile level backgrounds. Not that they couldn't have made a nice looking game with those choices of environments, but they just... didn't. I won't touch on the mini-games by the way, because I was too bored with the game to bother trying them out.

Maybe buy Spectraball if you just love marble games and want to kill time. It's not horrible, and it's probably worth the $0.49 they're charging right now for the few hours of mediocre entertainment it can offer.

Anyway, I have more I could say, but this review is probably pointless to post these days anyway. I just felt like writing about this game for a minute. Go play Venineth if this game looks appealing to you because of the apparent style it was going for. Venineth is extremely cool and good and puts Spectraball to shame.

Mediocre but fun marble platformer, recommended for marble enthusiasts - 6/10

Spectraball is a marble platformer with 7 stages and a few minigames. The first few levels are fairly well made and have an interesting atmosphere to them, unfortunately the later levels get a bit boring and repetitive. 
The "puzzle" tag confuses a bit, as there is no real puzzling involved, besides from minor pathfinding, so do not expect puzzles like I did. The minigames are fun, although they won't entertain you for a long time.

Overall the games biggest flaw is lacking optimisation: 
- the controls feel clunky, often times not properly registering a jump 
- the red boosters often used are very buggy leading to not getting the speed and failing a jump
- some levels feel unfinished, especially the minigames could have some more work done

There are not many games in the genre so try it out, even with all the flaws it can be good fun. I wish the game would be have been optimised a bit more.


100%-Achievement-Difficulty: Middle to Hard. You have to finish all stages in a row without falling off, although you can restart the current level from the beginning if you fall off. Still pretty hard, especially the last stage.

"Spectraball" ist ein Kugel-Plattformer.

Wir steuern unsere Kugel durch insgesanmt 7 Level, die alle eine eigene Ästhetik haben. Ob Lava, Space oder Schnee, für jeden ist etwas dabei. 

Die Level bestehen aus meist nicht so einfachen Parcours. Häufig muß man Stellen ausprobieren und per Trial and Error herausfinden, wie man denn am besten weiterkommt. Gut, daß zumindest meistens die Checkpoints in sinnvoller Entfernung zu finden sind. 

Dabei gibt es alle möglichen Herausforderungen. Von schmalen Brettern, die über Abgründen schweben über drehende Untergründe bis hin zu Stachelfallen findet sich alles, was man in dem Genre erwartet. Immer wieder treffen wir auch auf kleine Rätsel, Schalter, die wir erst drücken müssen oder Kisten, die wir verschieben müssen. Dabei droht immer der Absturz und der Respawn am letzten Checkpoint.

Die Steuerung funktioniert gut und sollte am Besten durch ein Gamepad stattfinden. Die Physik ist nachvollziehbar. Die Kugel hat eine mittlere Schwere und wir können auch kleine Sprünge mit ihr machen. Eine Besonderheit, die man in dem Genre selten findet: per Tastendruck können wir die Bremse reinhauen und unsere Kugel sofort anhalten. Das ist zwar nur an sehr wenigen Stellen im Spiel wirklich notwendig,trägt aber doch insgesamt zur Kontrollierbarkeit bei.

Die Grafik ist für einen in die Jahre gekommenen Titel aus dem Jahre 2008 in Ordnung. Die Musik ist allerdings ein wenig nervig. Ein bißchen schade ist allerdings, daß das Spiel nicht allzu lang ist. Schätzungsweise hat man das Game in etwa zwei Stunden durch.

Dafür sind die Level durchaus abwechslungsreich und interessant gestaltet. Man findet immer wieder eine neue Parcour-Variante.

Ein gewisses Problem ist aber die Kamera, die sich leider mit Gamepad nur viel zu schnell bewegen läßt. Da man sich immer in Blickrichtung bewegt, werden vor allem Kombinations-Passagen, in denen man die Kamera drehen muß, um sich überhaupt zu orientieren, unnötig nervig. 

Ähnlich gelagert ist auch die Problematik, daß man bei schnellen  Passagen, bei denen man weite schnell weite Strecken inklusive Richtungsänderungen vollziehen muß, reichlich unübersichtlich sein können. Man sieht teils gar nicht wo man hinrast und braucht allein deswegen mehrere Versuche.

On dirige la boule avec les flèches, on saute avec un bouton, on stop la balle avec un autre (cooldown entre chaque coup de frein), et roule ma boule. Les niveaux sont au nombres de 8, plus 3 mini-jeux plutôt dispensables. Chaque niveau est assez ouvert, et c'est au joueur de retrouver le bon chemin, de trouver des interrupteurs +/- cachés, afin d'atteindre le point de fin de niveau et de pouvoir enchainer le suivant.

C'est plutôt sympa, mais pas mal de défauts quand même: déjà, c'est relativement moche, mais bon le jeu a 8 ans je ne suis pas sûr d'être objectif. Ensuite, la caméra est calamiteuse, et pour peu qu'on la place mal c'est carrément toute l'action qui se cache derrière un pan de mur (noir, pourquoi mettre des textures sur l'envers du décor). Aussi, le chemin à trouver est parfois vraiment trop bien planqué, et demande au joueur de s'arrêter, de faire pivoter la caméra sur tous les axes pour essayer de repérer par où passer afin de déclencher la suite. Certains aimeront, moi ça m'a un peu gavé dans ce genre de jeu où je recherche vitesse et précision. Enfin, 2h pour le finir (les mini-jeux sont vraiment moisis), et à part pour tenter le scoring, aucun intérêt à le relancer. Gros manque de finition de manière globale donc.

Spectraball combines elements of platforming, puzzle solving, addictive gameplay, and stunning visuals to deliver an experience that sets a new standard for the genre. In addition, Spectraball utilizes Steamworks, offering full support for achievements and stat tracking.

Неплохой платформер, в котором нужно сквозь многочисленные препятствия довести шарик до конца уровня. Играется все это лучше, чем выглядит на скриншотах - я ожидал увидеть беспросветный трэш, а в итоге прошел всю игру. В Spectraball все завязано на физике, нужно уметь разгоняться и выбирать правильную траекторию, любое неверное движение отправляет к последней контрольной точке. 

Игра в меру сложная, но уровней всего 8 штук, не считая 3 бонусных испытания, так что пройти все можно за пару часов. Однако если вам важны ачивки, то даже не вздумайте в это играть, потому что потому что я не представляю как можно завершить все этапы в этой игре без единой ошибки. Так что ради получения "идеальной игры" в профиле придется изрядно попотеть и потратить экспоненциально больше времени.

В целом, Spectraball явно не стоит полной цены, играть интересно, но контента явно маловато. Уровни имеют совершенно разный внешний вид, но хотелось бы чтобы разница была не только визуальная, но и геймплейная. Например, я ожидал что на "космическом" уровне будет более низкая гравитация, но в итоге физика шарика не претерпела никаких изменений. Но если брать Spectraball на распродаже, то как развлечение на пару часов она сойдет - благо что игра получает -90% скидку довольно часто.

[h1]Описание:[/h1]
Вторая часть где нужно расставлять разные предметы, чтобы они взаимодействуя между собой достигали поставленной цели. [h1][b] Reseña de Crazy Machines[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
Crazy Machines es básicamente un laboratorio de “¿y si…?” donde tu cerebro hace de ingeniero, tu paciencia hace de mártir y la física hace de juez corrupto. Es un rompecabezas casual con corazón de estrategia: te suelta piezas, mecanismos y situaciones para que armes una reacción en cadena digna de caricatura… o un accidente industrial.

La propuesta es simple y adictiva: resolver niveles diseñando máquinas locas que cumplan un objetivo. “Casual” porque cualquiera puede entender qué quiere el juego; “Estrategia” porque si colocas algo un milímetro mal, tu invento pasa de “genialidad” a “bola de chatarra” en 0.3 segundos.

Primera impresión: entretenido, con ese encanto de juguete de escritorio. Segunda impresión: el juego te mira fijo y te dice “no, no era así” mientras tu creación explota por quinta vez. Y sí: eso es parte del encanto… y del castigo.

[h2]Lo que Funciona como Reloj (y lo que se Atora con Grasa)[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
 Rompecabezas con enfoque en física: cuando sale bien, se siente como un mini triunfo científico   
 Ideal para un jugador: perfecto para perder la noción del tiempo a solas (y culpar a la gravedad)   
 Mezcla casual + estrategia bien marcada: fácil de entrar, difícil de dominar   
 Satisfacción de “reacción en cadena”: ver tu máquina funcionar es puro dopamine hit   

Lo No Tan Bueno:
 Cero logros: Steam te mira y dice “¿y tu medallita, campeón?”   
 Comunidad/actividad bajísima: ahora mismo hay 1 jugador… o sea tú y el eco   
 Sin señales claras de soporte moderno (descuento histórico N/A): vibra de “existimos y ya”   
 En un juego de física, a veces el ensayo y error se siente más “prueba y resignación”

[/table]

[h2]Conclusión (Bueno)[/h2]
Crazy Machines es un buen rompecabezas de física para un jugador: directo, entretenido y con ese placer culpable de armar algo ridículo y verlo funcionar… después de fallar quince veces. Si te gustan los retos de lógica con enfoque de “máquina de Rube Goldberg”, aquí hay material para que tu cerebro trabaje y tu orgullo se tambalee.

Ahora, seamos controversiales: en Steam, un juego sin logros se siente como ir al gimnasio y que la báscula no prenda. Y con 1 jugador activo, la vibra es de “club exclusivo” pero sin club. Aun así, sus 111 recomendaciones indican que, cuando conecta con alguien, lo deja satisfecho (o al menos lo deja terminar el nivel).

Захотілося пограти в якийсь пазл, і перше що спало на думку саме ця гра, в нас більш відома під назвою "Заработало!", яка свого часу (ще в школі) пройшлася по руках всіх хлопаків мого класу.

 "Crazy Machines: The Wacky Contraptions Game" пропонує нам вирішувати пазли (задачки) основані на фізичних властивостях об'єктів, спочатку надаючи короткий, іноді комедійний, коментар до цього пазлу. Тобто, на статичному екрані знаходяться різні об'єкти взаємодії, в моменті (із зупиненим часом), якщо натиснути кнопку старту, то час запуститься і об'єкти почнуть впливати одне на одного (м'яч який був у повітрі почне падати під дією сили тяжіння, свічка під котлом почне нагрівати воду й вироблятиметься пара, батарея почне подавати електричний струм на підключену лампочку...), проте на те це й пазл, що нам дають його не зібраним. В коментарі перед пазлом пояснюється, що саме нам потрібно зробити: закинути м'яч в кошик, ввімкнути сирену, запустити ракету... і якщо просто за запустити час, то ціль виконано не буде, тож ми знов зупиняємо час, що повертає всі об'єкти в початкове положення, й за допомогою додаткових об'єктів з бічної панелі намагаємося вплинути на ті об'єкти які вже є на екрані, таким чином, щоб виконати завдання.

 Найпримітивніший зразок пазлу тут, це м'яч, що падає під силою тяжіння, та дошки в бічній панелі, які треба розставити так щоб за допомогою кута відбиття направити м'яч в кошик.
Вже більш складні приклади, включають в себе перетворення механічної енергії в електрику за допомогою генератора, кінетичної енергії в механічну за допомогою парового котла й парової машини, використання шестерень, конвеєрів, гармат, важелів... і багато чого іншого.

 Хоча, насправді пазли доволі (надто) прості. До того ж, дуже часто можна вирішити пазл не тим способом яким задумували розробники, що ще й "зайві" об'єкти на панелі залишаться. Як приклад: в одному із пазлів треба було натиснути важіль, і розставлені предмети натякали на каскад взаємодій між різними об'єктами, як в фільмах чи мультиках, де падає м'ячик, штовхає доміношки, ті падають одна за одною і вкінці штовхають цвях, який проголює повітряну кульку, що тримала один кінець полички, тож поличка хилиться, через що з неї з'їжджає коробка, яка падає на кнопку запалу паяльної лампи... я ж просто взяв підшипник, встановив його над важелем, і коли запустив час, то він впав на той важіль і перемкнув його.

 Вже після проходження всіх 102 експериментів (вони ж - пазли), я усвідомив, що тут є ще 103 абсолютно інші експерименти. Бо як виявилося "Crazy Machines: The Wacky Contraptions Game" (в Steam продається просто як "Crazy Machines") насправді є збіркою в яку входять "Crazy Machines: The Inventor's Workshop" (перші 102 експерименти) та "Crazy Machines: New Challenges" (додаткові 103 експерименти), між якими можна перемикатися в меню "Змінити Лабораторію".
Одразу зауважу, що ці "додаткові експерименти" (New Challenges) значно цікавіші і трохи складніші за перші (The Inventor's Workshop). До того ж в них використовуються нові об'єкти, серед яких є самохідний робот, дирижабль та генератор сили тяжіння... що до останнього, то тут також додалися пазли в невагомості та із місячною силою тяжіння.
З іншого боку, в "New Challenges" для деяких пазлів немає працюючого прикладу вирішення пазлу (відкривається після того як ти вирішиш цей пазл своїм способом).

 Та найбільшою проблемою цієї гри виявилася, соромно зізнатися, відсутність російської локалізації, на яку здебільшого і спирався ностальгійний фактор: в "Заработало!" професор (що іноді з'являється в кутку екрана й промовляє якусь фразу) і справді був озвучений чи не краще за англійську версію. До того ж, англійський опис пазлів в "The Inventor's Workshop" використовує надто зарозумілі слова, чого немає в описі пазлів з "New Challenges".
Ще в "New Challenges" є пазл, який чомусь вирішується сам собою, без використання об'єктів що доступні на панелі. А також раз мені вдалося зламати гру повісивши її (якось поламав фізику об'єктів).
Ну і проблемою є відсутність широкоформатного режиму.

 Зате тут присутній режим конструктора, де ми можемо створювати свої власні експерименти. Він для тих в кого є вільний час, проте поклацавши, мені здається, що там можна робити і справді круті пазли. Та й його інтерфейс доволі зрозумілий інтуїтивно.

 Не дивлячись на те, що "New Challenges" дещо покращує ситуацію, я все ж  не можу порекомендувати "Crazy Machines: The Wacky Contraptions Game". Бо, нехай навіть залишивши частину простих пазлів на початок гри, для ознайомлення гравців, все одно більшість пазлів надто прості, і їх вирішення навіть не здатне викликати радість.

Игра представляет из себя симулятор построения машин Голдберга из относительно небольшого набора объектов, следующих условно физическим взаимодействиям. Так тепло от свечки нагревает паровой двигатель, а батарея приводит в движения электромотор. Игра очевидно довольно старая, но техническое состояние у неё приемлемое. Так хотя пару раз она у меня вылетела, я смог пройти её до конца. Также я как и многие другие столкнулся с крайне неприятным багом физики магнита на уровне 4, из-за которого прохождение уровня стало очень сложным.

В игре есть два режима, свободное конструирование и решение 102 головоломок. Остановлюсь лишь на головоломках, так как большинство людей только этим и будут заниматься в игре. На каждом уровне необходимо, используя ограниченный набор предметов, построить такую машину, чтобы после запуска уровня она без твоего вмешательства выполнила некое действие. Разработчиков в целом хочется за уровни похвалить. Головоломки довольно разнообразные и почти не тратят твоё время растягиванием. Но скудность набора взаимодействующих объектов начинает всё же ощущаться после 50-60 уровней. Также баланс уровней вызывает вопросы. Некоторые из них требуют крайне чудных решений, а некоторые довольно нудных, требующих расположения объектов с точностью до пикселя. Из-за этого к последним уровням ты уже устаёшь от игры, хотя в целом я свой игровой опыт считаю положительным.

Кроме игрового процесса игре нечего предложить. Тут есть крайне условная история, заключающаяся в том, что мы помогаем безумному учёному с его делами, попутно получая новые учёные степени. Но это сделано лишь, чтобы объяснить цель каждого уровня. Музыка тут посредственная, как и визуальный стиль.

Несмотря на явный возраст игры, её ядро - игровой процесс, до сих пор воспринимается свежо и интересно. Поэтому я рекомендую игру к ознакомлению, если вам нравится решать физические головоломки.

Прим. Машина Голдберга - любой сложный механизм для выполнения простого действия. В этой игре в половине случаев цель передвинуть объект из одной точки в другую.

Хорошая игра, но всё-таки на порядок хуже The Incredible Machines (откуда, не секрет, Crazy Machines ведрами черпает вдохновение). Тезисно опишу плюсы и минусы.

Плюсы:
1. Что греха таить — интересные пазлы. Это, безусловно, основной пункт.
2. Игра без особых багов (прошёл полностью и вылетов, зависании и каких-то других очевидных проблем не встречал).
3. Сносное управление. Провода и веревки тянутся нормально (есть другая часть серии где с этим проблемы).

Минусы:
1. Физическая модель. Это как плюс, так и минус, потому что иногда какую-нибудь пушку нужно выставлять буквально с точностью до пикселя, иначе ядро, вылетающее из дула, будет лететь черт знает куда. Прыгающий мяч может как внезапно решить вам пазл удивительным образом, так и тупо скакать у стенки, потому что вы поставили его на 3 пикселя левее, чем нужно. Я понимаю, что это был правильный шаг, и топтаться на месте без физической модели в наше время (да и во времена выхода этой игры) глупо, но проблемы с ним есть.
2. Мерзкий маразматичный дед (местный маскот), который частенько не может внятно объяснить суть задания. Я понимаю, что это такая фишка, но как же он бесит, причём бесит по всем фронтам: своим видом, голосом (благо отключается) и, конечно же, тупыми пространными текстами вместо чётко поставленной задачи. В TIM, на которую я постоянно ссылаюсь, тоже были маскоты — молодой парень-ученый со своим котом, но их было совсем немного и он совершенно не раздражали. Также суть задания в TIM объясняли кратко, очень точно и, иногда, с тонким юмором. 
3. Глупая музыка, но это уже субъективно.
4. Технические проблемы со звуком (по крайней мере у меня на win7x64): звук почти невозможно отрегулировать, он очень громкий, ползунок в настройках не работает почти на всей длине, звук можно только сделать очень громким, очень тихим и выключить. НО! Даже если поставить звук очень тихим, то не обольщайтесь. Не все звуки захотят с этим мириться. Кто-то захочет сыграть на  п о л н у ю  громкость, порадовав вас и всех вокруг!

В итоге, эта хорошая игра. Но эта хорошесть формируется только на костях старой отличной игры The Incredible Machines, чтобы испортить которую нужно очень постараться.

Seu objetivo é criar máquinas funcionais, usando física e pensando bastante para passar cada nível.
Cada máquina tem um objetivo específico, como acender todas as lâmpadas num determinado ponto da tela ou fazer com que a bola de basquete acerte um alvo específico.
As primeiras fases são fáceis, para acostumar o jogador a mecânica do jogo, mas conforme você vai avançando, vai lidando com desafios cada vez mais complexos, inclusive com itens a mais e itens inúteis, que são colocados a sua disposição apenas para lhe confundir.

O jogo ainda conta com um modo onde você pode criar suas próprias máquinas, apenas para se distrair. Eu particularmente não vejo muita graça nesse modo de jogo, mas para quem curte ficar viajando nas próprias ideias, da para criar umas geringonças interessantes.

Helldorado is a real-time tactics game developed by Spellbound Entertainment and published by THQ Nordic that brings players back into the unforgiving world of the Wild West. It serves as both a continuation and a spin-off of the Desperados series, carrying forward the same blend of stealth, strategy, and squad-based action that defined its predecessors. Set in 1883, the story begins in Santa Fe and follows bounty hunter John Cooper and his team as they uncover a conspiracy involving kidnappings, corruption, and a dangerous web of enemies. The game captures the grit and lawlessness of the frontier while layering in complex tactical challenges that demand careful thought and precision.

The narrative builds directly off the events of Desperados II: Cooper’s Revenge, but it functions well enough as a standalone experience for those unfamiliar with earlier titles. Fans of the series, however, will appreciate the return of familiar characters and the continuation of lingering story threads. Missions draw players through classic Western scenarios: train heists, jailbreaks, ambushes in dusty towns, and tense standoffs in saloons. These scenarios are not mere backdrops but carefully designed arenas filled with opportunities and hazards, pushing players to adapt and think creatively.

Gameplay remains rooted in squad-based tactics, with six different characters each bringing unique skills to the table. Cooper is skilled with pistols and knife throws, while others specialize in explosives, disguise, or crowd control. The game introduces “combo actions,” where two characters can combine their abilities to create more effective results, such as pairing stealthy takedowns with distractions or using explosives in tandem with environmental traps. The option to switch between an overhead tactical view and a more zoomed-in third-person view allows for different play styles, making missions feel dynamic and layered. This dual perspective system also supports a cinematic quality, especially when combined with the built-in “movie mode” that lets players record and replay their exploits.

One of the defining characteristics of Helldorado is its punishing difficulty. The game expects precision and patience, often requiring players to study enemy patrols, experiment with different strategies, and repeat sections multiple times until they succeed. Even early missions are uncompromising, and success relies on mastering each character’s strengths and learning how to coordinate the group effectively. For some, this steep difficulty curve creates an engaging and rewarding experience where victory feels earned through skill and persistence. For others, the trial-and-error approach can feel tedious, making progress seem more like grinding through obstacles than enjoying tactical depth.

The presentation captures the essence of the Western setting with a good variety of locations, from desert towns and sprawling ranches to railroads and New Orleans-inspired streets. While the visuals were serviceable at the time of release, they show their age today, with stiff animations and occasional clunky camera angles. The audio design, however, enhances the atmosphere with a solid soundtrack full of Western motifs, environmental effects that make towns and saloons feel alive, and gunfire that punctuates tense situations. Voice acting is functional, though uneven, with some performances enhancing immersion while others sound unrefined.

Replay value comes from the flexibility of missions and the variety of ways players can approach objectives. Different combinations of characters, the use of combo actions, and experimenting with stealth versus more aggressive strategies provide room for creativity. Difficulty settings also allow players to test themselves further once they’ve mastered the basics, though the harsh learning curve ensures that only dedicated players are likely to push through to the end. Some repetition does creep in, as certain maps are reused with altered objectives or enemy placements, but the overall mission variety helps offset this.

Helldorado stands as a niche but worthwhile entry in the real-time tactics genre. It doesn’t try to simplify its systems or compromise its challenge, making it a title best suited for players who enjoy meticulous planning, stealth-heavy gameplay, and the satisfaction of overcoming tough scenarios. It may lack the polish and accessibility of more modern strategy titles, but for fans of the Desperados series or Commandos-style tactics games, it delivers a demanding and atmospheric Wild West adventure. For those willing to embrace its unforgiving nature, Helldorado offers a satisfying mix of strategy, tension, and Old West storytelling.

A very nice, highly tactical game with an unusual difficulty curve (not really a curve), some patches are exceptionally hard and require pin point timing and planning where as some scenarios you can simply run in and punch. I got into the series when I got a demo of the 1st game "Desperado: Wanted Dead or Alive" free with a box a cereal (what a great promotion). I remember spending hours and hours silently knocking out every enemy in the one demo level and hiding their bodies in various outbuildings. This game still has the same great core game play with some less welcome mechanics bolted on such as the 1st person mode and movie export mode. This title improves upon the originals planning system in which you can set up satisfying combinations involving all your people silently taking down how a town. Some people may be put off by the large quantity of quick-saves and loading, but in this tittle I see it as slowly creating a masterpiece stroke by stroke. All in all I highly recommend this title or if you can get hold of it cheap, then "Desperado: Wanted Dead or Alive"

Wenn mich aber ein Soldat entdeckt, schießt er innerhalb von einer Millisekunde sein komplettes Magazin auf mich, ziemlich absurd imo. Desperados 1+2 hat dem Spieler die Freiheit gelassen zu spielen wie man möchte, Ballern oder Schleichen. In Helldorado hat man diese Möglichkeit nicht. Man hat teilweise hunderte Soldaten auf einem Gebiet (z.B. Level 6) und muss einen nach dem anderen schleichend mit Fäusten oder verführerisch (Kate) ausschalten (bewusstlos schlagen und fesseln). Das ist ein paar Minuten ganz witzig, aber danach nur noch Grind und anstrengend. Allein für Level 6 habe ich ca. 6 Stunden gebraucht. 
Echt schade, hatte mich nach den guten Vorgängern auf Helldorado gefreut, bin dann aber doch etwas ernüchtert und enttäuscht.
Fazit der Reihe: 
Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive 5 Sterne
Desperados 2: Cooper’s Revenge 4 Sterne
Helldorado gerade noch 3 Sterne und eine Empfehlung nur für absolute Fans denen der hohe Schwierigkeitsgrad und die ewig langen (Schleich) Levels ohne die Möglichkeit zu Ballern nichts ausmachen.

"Helldorado," Spellbound tarafından geliştirilen ve THQ Nordic tarafından yayınlanan bir Wild West temalı aksiyon-macera oyunudur. Oyun, 1883 Santa Fe şehrinde başlayan şok edici bir kaçırılma olayının ardından, oyuncuların marauding kanunsuzları durdurmak için zorlu görevlerde yer aldığı bir hikayeye odaklanır. İşte bu oyun hakkında daha fazla detay:

Hikaye: Oyun, Santa Fe şehrinde yaşanan sarsıcı bir kaçırılma olayıyla başlar. Oyuncular, kanunsuzları durdurmak ve hain şantaj ve intikam hikayesini engellemek için zorlu görevlerde yer alır. Görevler arasında çalınan ganimeti ele geçirme, saloon kavgalarından kaçma, hapishane kaçışları ve çatışmalar bulunur. Bu vahşi batı macerasının ana teması intikam ve adalettir.

Wild West Atmosferi: Oyun, PC platformunda gerçekçi vahşi batı mekanları sunar. Fırtınalı yağmur yağışından kanlı gün batımlarına ve güzel eski New Orleans'a kadar farklı atmosferlerde görevler sunar.

Akıllı Düşmanlar: Oyunda 60 farklı düşman türü bulunur ve bunlar gelişmiş bir yapay zeka sistemine sahip olup taktiksel davranışlar sergilerler. Bu, oyuncuların çeşitli düşman türleriyle mücadele ederken stratejik kararlar almalarını gerektirir.

Çoklu Karakter Oynama: Oyuncular, altı farklı karakteri kontrol edebilirler. Her karakter farklı uzmanlık becerileri, yetenekler ve silahlarla donatılmıştır, bu da oyun deneyimini çeşitlendirir.

Film Modu: Oyunda kahraman hareketlerinizi kaydedebileceğiniz bir Film Modu bulunur, böylece oyun deneyiminizi kaydedebilir ve arkadaşlarınızla paylaşabilirsiniz.

Tarihi Silahlar ve Ekipmanlar: Oyunda 1880'lerin silahları ve ekipmanları bulunur, bunlar arasında altıpatlar tabanca, av tüfekleri, tüfek, yay ve ok, derringer, bıçaklar, tomahawk ve dönemin diğer silahları yer alır.

Teknoloji: Oyun içinde taktiksel görünüm ve eylem görünümü arasında sorunsuzca geçiş yapabilirsiniz. Ayrıca, Bloom ve HDR renderleme, PhysXageia teknolojisi gibi bazı teknolojik özelliklere sahiptir.

"Helldorado," gerçekçi bir Wild West deneyimi sunan, çeşitli karakterlerin kontrolünü sağlayan ve taktiksel bir oynanış sunan bir aksiyon-macera oyunu olarak öne çıkar. Oyunun hikayesi, atmosferi ve çeşitli görevleriyle oyunculara heyecan verici bir vahşi batı deneyimi sunar. Ancak, incelemelere göre, oyuncuların oynanışı ve düşmanlarla mücadelesi hakkında daha fazla detay edinmek için kişisel deneyimleri ve oyun içi mekanikleri incelemeleri tavsiye edilir.

资料片比本篇强，不过强的有限，看在故事完结了就打个好评吧。
1.修了一大堆本篇恼人的小问题，比如寻路这类的，起码整个流程这帮人不会老是卡在一块了。
2.各种动作速度明显加快，起码我愿意用库伯的飞刀了。
3.增加我非常喜欢的联合行动，比如医生和库伯能来套西部双枪，主动出击比盟军的被动防御强。这种高观赏性低操作度也算一条不错的路径，但由于关卡设计要么缺人用不了要么用不上有点遗憾。

总之还是推荐找个视频看看剧情就得。

Изначально данная игра задумывалась как переиздание второй части, но в итоге превратилась в полноценный аддон, с сюжетным продолжением.

Ещё при разработке второй части (по словам разработчиков), издатель в лице Atari, не выплачивал бюджет по шесть месяцев, из-за чего пришлось уволить половину сотрудников и сильно порезать игру, а с аддоном разрабов вообще кинули и тем пришлось заняться сомоиздательством. Вот только права на название Desperados остались у Atari, поэтому игра и вышла под названием Helldorado: Conspiracy.  
Как по мне игру серьёзно доработали (относительно второй части) и многие косяки были поправлены, но пресса игру разгромила, а продажи оказались мизерные - студия Spellbound оказалась на грани закрытия, и только контракт на разработку Gothic 4:Arcania спас студию, но оказался её последней игрой, впрочем это уже совсем другая история.

Интересный факт: На территории СНГ игра выходила под названием Десперадо 3: Cхватка в прериях, дело в том что издателем был Руссобит-М, ныне почившая компания. В начале нулевых они вообще занимались тем, что брали фанатские моды и продавали их под видом официальных дополнений, так что для них это обычное дело.

[u]Overview:[/u]

Helldorado is the sequel to Desparados 2, however given almost identical layout and gameplay, it's probably better to call it DLC. That being said, the modifications to this entry in the series make the game somewhat fun and I would (just about) recommend this to those who are into the stealth genre and looking for a decent play.

[u]The Good:[/u]

+ The precision of the game play is quite a bit tighter than the previous titles. Although some take downs will require a lot of saving and loading, they are made easier by the responsiveness of your characters.

+ The combination moves add depth where the previous title was lacking: they bring more versatile ways to overcome difficult situations and allow you to play more efficiently.

+ The sound track is actually appropriate for the setting unlike the previous title where it was Kate and John's date music playing every mission. The tracks themselves are pretty nice.

+ As with every title in this series, the graphics are fantastic and really bring the environment to life. 

+ The addition of mission awards is a nice idea. I definitely recommend playing this game on the hardest difficulty just to get all the gold medals.

+ You can often choose your own path / strategy to reach an objective if you're creative enough with your arsenal of weapons

[u]The Bad:[/u]

- The story is yet again so generic that you may as well watch Fistful of Dollars in the background or some other more entertaining (literally any other) Western story.

- Trial and error game play will definitely not be for everyone. I personally didn't have too much of a problem with it because it seems to be somewhat inevitable in stealth titles, but having encounters which require pinpoint accuracy is going to be frustrating. 

- The AI is not incredibly smart. They're not completely brain dead but they're usually more of a hassle than a challenge. 

- Path finding is sometimes a bit broken from top down view. Asking them to run somewhere specific, like through a door, means that you better load anyway because they're going to run into the street first for some reason and then do what you asked them to do.

- The voice acting is recycled from the previous game which means these stereotyped, bland and boring voices accompany your journey. Presumably to save money on the voice acting but then why not just use the voices from the first game which actually sounded authentic?

- Although they have [i]improved[/i] upon the gadgets you have to take down enemies, there is still definitely room for improvement. Not knowing which guards will be leave their post, can be seduced, and so on, prior to attempting to make them just wastes time. 

- I was rather disappointed no new characters were added. In fact, my favourite character [spoiler]just ends up fucking off into the woods before the game ends for a bullshit reason which could have waited,[/spoiler] so I think the game could have had more effort put into this part.

 - The game is rather too short for its price tag. Ideally it should have been twice as long so all the mechanics could have been explored in depth rather than having to rush using them all. 

[u]Conclusion:[/u]

Overall, is this game breaking any boundaries? Hell no. But it is definitely a good game to dig at, piece by piece, for a casual play. There are some disappointing areas, but overall I don't think they outweigh the solid game play Helldorado offers. Metacritic probably got it right here:

So, [b]Helldorado[/b]... You can call it [b]Desperados 2.5[/b] because, well, that's what it is. Comes with a pretty funny story, though. See, at some point [b]Spellbound Entertainment[/b] ended up being so obsessed with making [b]Commandos[/b] clones that one of them ([b]Chicago 1930[/b]) failed pretty hard. Why? Well, for many reasons, I guess. It didn't get enough press, it was far from being the best game from [b]Spellbound[/b] (even though it sure had a certain charm and came with a bunch of fresh ideas, it was still the worst in my opinion), while there were already too many of such games on market. As funny as it sounds nowadays (the entire sub-genre pretty much died with [b]Spellbound[/b], until [b]Mimimi[/b] picked it up and gave it a new life in their [b]Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shōgun[/b]), [b]Spellbound[/b] alone used to produce a new game of that kind every bloody year, while there were also [b]PYRO[/b], who started the entire thing and some other minor games. Like [b]KOREA: Forgotten Conflict[/b]. It was like with all those games from [b]Ubisoft[/b] nowadays. At some point people were like “[i]Seriously? Another one of those? Seriously?[/i]”. It was also somewhat buggy, so... yeah. It failed. And when it did, [b]Spellbound[/b] started to fire people.

Unfortunately, with a brand new team behind [b]Desperados 2[/b], they also lost the only thing that used to make their games so cool. I mean, seriously. The original [b]Desperados[/b] team? The guys knew what they were doin'. They loved [b]Commandos[/b] and they wanted to improve it and explore the new horizons. Like, personally, I really wanted [b]Vampire Hunter[/b] game to happen. All that while [b]Desperados 2[/b] team just... blew it. They've ruined pretty much everything that the original [b]Desperados[/b] did right, while the new game turned out so cheap and ugly that it felt unfinished. So, naturally, even though [b]Spellbound[/b] already worked on the expansion and almost finished it, [b]ATARI[/b] said “Nope, we don't need any more of [i]that![/i] Thank you very much.” What did [b]Spellbound[/b] do? Well, they tried to save the project. The best they can. They eventually found the publisher and released the expansion as a stand-alone game called [b]Helldorado[/b]. Because why the hell not.

So, that's pretty much the story here. It's called [b]Helldorado[/b], but all in all, it's an expansion to [b]Desperados 2[/b]. Or [b]Desperados 2.5[/b], call it any way you want. But enough about that. Already wasted quite a lot of time on that, so... let's look at the game itself, shall we? Well, we shall, but... the funniest thing is – there isn't much to talk about here. I mean, what do you expect? The game started as a bloody expansion and, well, it feels that way too. For both good and bad (mostly bad, though, mostly bad...) it's still [b]Desperados 2[/b]. Can't say nothing's changed, though. Quite the opposite. The character models were heavily improved and are now highlighted in the way similar to the first game (which is a good thing since it makes them easier to see and control), the goals are way better explained now and even have marks on the ground to make things easier for you, while the new “combo” system that allows you to give the same task for all the characters who can perform it is pretty cool and useful. Just select all the guys and send them to kick the heck out of the bandits. Then just sit back and enjoy the brawl. Like I said, useful.

Aside from that, though, what we have here is pretty much the same [b]Desperados 2[/b]... thing. The story picks up right when [b]Desperados 2[/b] ended (yes, it begins with that weird scene about the [b]Doc[/b]), but it's still cheesy as heck and absolutely terribly written, while gameplay still feels cheap and rough. Heck, they even forgot to put one of the important libraries on disc! Not really a problem with the [b]Steam[/b] version (you may still need to install the legacy [b]PhysX[/b] drivers, though), but I still remember the day when I tried to launch the game from disc for the very first time. I mean, come on! How many games miss the important libraries on physical media? Did you even test the bloody thing, [b]Spellbound[/b]?

Sure, the game is totally playable in its current state, but, like with the original [b]Desperados 2[/b], you'll hardly want to waste your time on it. You like the genre and already finished everything else from [b]PYRO[/b], [b]Spellbound[/b] and [b]Mimimi[/b]? Then, and only then, you may consider wasting your time on this game. Otherwise, pick up anything else (literally, anything, even [b]Chicago 1930[/b]) and it'll be [i]much[/i] better than this. Dixi.

The ugly:

- few creative solutions on missions

Mata Hari transforms the legendary dancer and suspected spy into the centerpiece of a traditional point-and-click adventure filled with political maneuvering, romance, espionage, and deception. Developed by 4Head Studios and published on Steam by Viva Media, the game draws inspiration from the turbulent period surrounding the famous historical figure without presenting itself as a strict recreation of her life. Instead, it embraces the mythology that grew around Mata Hari and constructs an international spy story in which charm, observation, intelligence gathering, and manipulation are essential tools for survival.

The historical European setting is one of the experience's strongest qualities. Taking place during an era of growing international tension, the story captures a world where elegant social gatherings and glamorous lifestyles coexist with secret intelligence operations and political instability. Mata Hari moves between these contrasting environments while becoming increasingly involved in dangerous assignments. This gives the narrative an appealing sense of duality: she can command attention as an exotic performer while simultaneously operating within a hidden world of agents, secrets, and competing national interests.

Gameplay remains firmly rooted in classic adventure-game traditions. Players explore locations, examine objects, gather useful information, engage characters in conversation, and solve problems that stand between Mata Hari and her objectives. This is not an action-heavy interpretation of espionage. Success generally comes from understanding situations and determining how information, objects, or relationships can be exploited. Players who enjoy carefully investigating environments will therefore get considerably more from the experience than those expecting frequent combat or fast-paced stealth sequences.

The espionage theme allows the puzzles to move beyond ordinary inventory manipulation. Mata Hari participates in intelligence-gathering activities involving period-appropriate techniques and technology, including code breaking and telephone tapping. These elements help reinforce the fantasy of operating as a spy during the early twentieth century, when surveillance required physical access, specialized equipment, personal connections, and considerable patience. The historical limitations of the technology actually benefit the adventure format because they naturally create opportunities for puzzles.

Several mini-games are distributed throughout the four-chapter story, with eight different activities intended to provide variety between conversations and exploration. These sequences represent different aspects of Mata Hari's unusual life and work, although their entertainment value is somewhat inconsistent. Some provide a pleasant change of pace, while others can feel like interruptions to the stronger investigative portions. They nevertheless demonstrate an effort to make the adventure more mechanically diverse than simply moving between locations and selecting dialogue options.

Mata Hari's career as a dancer also becomes part of the gameplay rather than serving merely as background information. This is important because it gives the protagonist an identity beyond being another fictional secret agent. Her public celebrity, personal relationships, romantic encounters, and clandestine activities intersect throughout the story. The game understands that her greatest weapon is often her ability to influence people rather than overpower them, making social interaction a natural component of its espionage fantasy.

Player decisions contribute to the outcome, and multiple endings provide some incentive to revisit the story or consider choices more carefully. The branching structure is relatively modest compared with contemporary narrative games, but it remains meaningful within a traditional adventure format. Mata Hari's loyalties, relationships, and actions can influence how events ultimately unfold, reinforcing the underlying themes of trust and betrayal. The possibility of different conclusions also suits a historical character whose actual activities remain surrounded by controversy and conflicting interpretations.

The visual presentation has naturally aged. Character models, facial expressions, and animations lack the fluidity expected from modern narrative adventures, and some interactions can appear rigid. However, the environments retain a degree of charm thanks to the period-inspired architecture, clothing, interiors, and European atmosphere. The game frequently feels like an illustrated espionage novel brought into interactive form, and that stylistic personality can compensate for some of its technical limitations.

Pacing will probably be the largest dividing point for modern players. Considerable time is spent talking, examining locations, collecting clues, and working through puzzles. Anyone accustomed to older PC adventures will recognize this rhythm immediately, but players expecting the excitement implied by the word "spy" may find the experience unexpectedly slow. Danger is primarily communicated through narrative circumstances rather than continuous action. Patience is therefore an important requirement.

Puzzle design can also show its age. Certain solutions require experimentation, and the intended path forward is not always immediately apparent. This occasionally results in frustration when progress depends on discovering a particular interaction rather than solving a clearly presented logical problem. At its best, however, the game rewards observation and deduction, especially when its puzzles incorporate espionage techniques instead of relying exclusively on arbitrary item combinations.

The writing and historical context ultimately carry much of the experience. The combination of romance, political tension, secret missions, dangerous acquaintances, and competing loyalties provides an appealing foundation for a spy adventure. While the characterization and dramatic presentation do not reach the standards of modern cinematic games, the unusual protagonist gives the narrative a personality that separates it from more conventional adventure stories.

Steam Deck users should approach Mata Hari as an older PC game without an official Steam Deck compatibility rating. It is neither officially Verified nor designated as a supported Deck release. Running it through Proton or using community configurations may produce different results depending on the setup, but players should not purchase it specifically for handheld use expecting guaranteed functionality.

Mata Hari is ultimately a niche but interesting adventure that benefits greatly from its protagonist and historical setting. Its aging technology, occasionally awkward puzzles, inconsistent mini-games, and leisurely pacing make it difficult to recommend universally, yet its combination of espionage, romance, dancing, code breaking, surveillance, conversation, and branching outcomes remains distinctive. For enthusiasts of classic point-and-click adventures who enjoy historical intrigue and are comfortable with older design conventions, it offers an unconventional journey through the glamorous and dangerous mythology surrounding one of espionage history's most recognizable figures.

Già le recensioni (poche), presenti su Steam erano parecchio discordanti sul prodotto, però ho voluto tastare con mano questo Mata Hari. Avventura grafica punta e clicca, con un gameplay abbastanza standard, ma che porta dietro di se nomi importanti nella storia del genere e in quella che fu la vecchia Lucasarts.
Infatti, Hal Barwood(sceneggiatore), e Noah Falstein alla programmazione, riescono a sbagliare quasi tutto, facendoci capire, come anche vecchi professionisti dell'epoca gloriosa che fu, possono andare in declino.
Partiamo subito con le uniche note molto positive: il comparto tecnico, con sfondi ottimamente disegnati e personaggi 3d ben animati. In generale si respira quella che è l'atmosfera della prima decade del 1900'. Allo stesso modo le musiche sono di buona fattura, e il tema portante dell'opera non da fastidio.
I veri problemi iniziano con tutto il resto del lavoro svolto: la trama è un'occasione mancata, anche per via di una caratterizzazione del personaggio di Mata che quasi umilia la sua storia. Tutto quello che lei fa è andare a letto con uomini, fare qualche balletto( in cui si attiva un minigioco), e ovviamente quello della spia. Spiace che la sceneggiatura viene infarcita di personaggi veramente esistiti nella sua vita, sia nel bene che nel male. L'unica piccola nota è il finale romanzato di brutto, che non mi è dispiaciuto.
La vera nota dolente, che quasi mi ha fatto droppare il titolo, è il gameplay. La giocabilità è qualcosa di atroce.Gli enigmi sono  di una banalità sconcertante, se poi si pensa che dietro ci sta proprio Falstein autore di Indiana jones TFOA. Tutto il gioco sta nel dover andare da un punto ad un altro a raccogliere qualche info, tornare indietro, ritornare li ,andare di qua. Tutto questo casino si svolge attraverso un continuo e nauseante uso della stazione dei treni, dove ogni santa volta dovrete ripetere gli stessi passaggi: andare stazione- comprare biglietto- eseguire un minigioco dove non bisogna farsi prendere dalle guardie( per fortuna si può skip questa cosa, grazie la cielo!)- arrivo a destinazione- prendere un info- e poi nuovamente ritornare alla stazione rifacendo le medesime azioni prima descritte. Tutto questo per un numero imprecisato di volte.
Ogni tanto verrà fuori qualche minigioco di abilità o logica che si può risolvere manualmente come anche skipparlo tramite un pulsante rosso presente su schermo.
Caratteristica peculiare di Mata Hari, è che in base ad alcune azioni: superare guardie, compiere missioni specifiche, guadagneremo dei punti spionaggio, o pnt denaro. Ma tutto ciò sapete a cosa serve? Esatto, a nulla!
Il gioco in conclusione, vi dirà solo che potevate fare di meglio per aumentare il vostro score, ma tutto ciò è fine a se stesso, di una rara inutilità.
In un periodo,in cui le avventure grafiche sono tornare di moda, e con tutta questa qualità che trovate su Steam, non vi consiglio assolutamente di comprare questo Mata Hari. Investite i vostri soldi su ben altro, e cerchiamo di ricordarci del duo Barwood-Falstein pensando ai vecchi fasti di un tempo.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
A very different point and click game focusing very heavily on story and dialogue more akin to a interactive story book.

[b]Pros[/b]
+ Interesting story
+ Different

[b]Cons[/b]
- Mostly dialogue
- Less point and click more story book

[h1]Overview[/h1]
Mata Hari is an older point & click narrative that focuses far more on telling its fictional story based on the real life person Mata Hari, a Dutch dancer that gained popularity in Paris for her exotic dancing.
The game is pretty simple as a point & click with short bouts of puzzles and it focuses very hard on story telling instead of the gameplay, due to being so heavy on dialogue the game also becomes very long from all the talking.

The story itself is rather interesting as it shows a more realistic nitty gritty world of espionage with less of the fancy spy movie stuff we are accustomed to. It may be very boring to many as there's just mostly dialogue and also very different to those accustomed to point & click games with the scarcity of puzzles where many are instead solved through talking. I can say the puzzles themselves are actually quite good and some are also challenging. Other than a few puzzles there are also some dancing mini games that I found to be simple and kind of annoying albeit different, they aren't that important to the story at large and just cements more of the character and could even be skipped.

Only pick this up if you wish to have more of an interactive story book than an actual point & click game.

Nejsem moc zběhlý v historii, o Mata Hari jsem věděl akorát to, že byla během první světové války dvojitou špionkou. Videoherní zpracování není samozřejmě žádným přesným dokumentem, i tak jsem se těšil, co se o této historické postavě případně dozvím.

Příběh je zajímavý, minimálně v první polovině hry, kdy se Mata Hari postupně sbližuje s různými vlivnými lidmi a získává od nich informace. I když mi přišlo, že je získává až podezřele snadno. Z historických pramenů jsem věděl, že skutečná Mata Hari byla nakonec popravena, proto mě [spoiler]celkem překvapil happy-end v závěru, kdy byla její smrt jen fingovaná a ona žila dál[/spoiler].

U adventur mám rád, když jsou v nich přítomný mezihry a zde jich je celkem dost. Ta nejčastější - tancování - je ale celkem nudná, zvláště pak hledání inspirací různě po lokacích. Jednou jsem tu inspiraci hledal asi čtvrt hodiny. Zbytek je celkem fajn. Dost mě bavila ta s cestováním mezi městy. S pozdější potřebou častějšího cestování jsem byl ale celkem rád, že se [spoiler]vždy zpřístupnila i možnost rychlého přesunu bez minihry[/spoiler].

Během hraní jsem však narazil i na řadu nesmyslů a příběhových děr. Například je potřeba odposlechnout telefonní hovor v Madridu, jenže Mata neví, jak na to. Tak odcestuje do Monaka se to naučit a následně se přes Berlín vrátí zase do Madridu. A kupodivu, ten potřebný hovor stále probíhá. Stejně tak je divné, že když je Mata v Paříží a potřebuje někomu v tomto městě zavolat, tak musí odcestovat do Berlína, kde je jediný přístupný telefon.

Vzhled jednotlivých lokací vypadá celkem fajn, hlavně Paříž. Akorát mi to přišlo celé takové statické. Plus si myslím, že by nebylo na škodu, kdyby zde bylo více lokalit. Je fajn, že je možné se v rámci obrazovky přesouvat na dvojklik, bohužel to ale nefunguje i pro východ z obrazovky. Tam musí Mata vždy dojít. Ze začátku jsem pak celkem bojoval i s volbou témat k rozhovoru, ale časem jsem si zvykl. Jsem rád, že je zde přítomna funkce zvýraznění interaktivních předmětu. I díky ní jsem tak naštěstí neměl moc záseků.

Celkově považuji tuto adventuru za mírný podprůměr. Délka je spíše kratší, ale to lze vzít i jako klad, protože to aspoň rychle uteče.

In the past, point-and-click adventure games used to be my favorite genre. However, most of the games I played didn't have a translation to my mother's tongue, preventing me from fully enjoying the experience. Nevertheless, I have always appreciated the gratifying puzzle-solving mechanics.

As time passed, there was a natural transition from 2D to 3D graphics, accompanied by other technological advancements. Consequently, many other titles were introduced, including this particular release. The game's story is intriguing as it is based on real events from the past. The question remains: Is it a good at all?

The story follows a linear path but is divided into different segments or chapters, each separated by a significant leap in time. The graphics, considering the time of release, are satisfactory. The sound effects and music are also adequate, and I have no major complaints in that regard. The voice acting, although a bit cheesy, doesn't bother me personally. In terms of gameplay, the developers attempted to combine various mechanics. It's not solely a point-and-click adventure game; there are also puzzles to solve and even rhythm segments, exploring Mata Hari's background as a dancer. Additionally, there is a points system that may have some impact on the outcome.

To be completely honest, the execution of the game falls short of greatness. I find it difficult to relate to any of the characters, and most of the time, I found myself yawning instead of genuinely enjoying the experience. If given the choice, I would provide a neutral assessment of this game. However, since that option is not available, I have to settle for a negative review.

An underwhelming espionage adventure across Europe which is based on a true story, but just isn’t that interesting or entertaining to play.  The story is ok and uses a few famous names but isn’t that engaging, partially due to the constant back and forth nature and the long time span it covers.  

There’s very little actual game play, focusing on conversations and light puzzles and with very few hot spots in each scene, they become hard to detect.  The backgrounds are beautifully drawn, which is a good thing as you’ll be seeing the same ones a lot, but the 3D polygonal characters are dated, move awkwardly and don’t fit with the scenery at all.  You can also see where they’ve cut corners with basic animations missing, repeating characters and visiting the same scenes again and again.  The mini-games add some variety but are poorly implemented, becoming boring quickly and the scoring system, which offers some replay value, has no bearing on the game.  The voice acting is mostly good but the music tracks often play over themselves.  

Overall, it’s a short and functional adventure game with some charm, but little to really recommend.

"Mata Hari" est un point'n click sorti en 2009 et j'imagine qu'à l'époque, il devait déjà apparaître comme terriblement désuet avec son gameplay remontant à l'Antiquité du jeu vidéo, ses graphismes naïfs et ses énigmes old school absolument insupportables pour le joueur d'aujourd'hui (mention spéciale à ces espèces de circuits-puzzles que l'on rencontre plusieurs fois dans le jeu pour notre plus grand malheur ; heureusement, les développeurs ont eu le bon goût de permettre au joueur de les zapper au bout de quelques minutes de prise de tête infructueuse et de continuer l'aventure comme si de rien n'était). En fait, "Mata Hari" aurait sûrement été un véritable carton s'il était sorti en 1993. Ces constats impitoyables doivent sûrement vous amener à vous demander pourquoi, dans ce cas, je recommande ce titre en lui mettant un pouce bleu tourné vers le haut. Parce que "Mata Hari" a les qualités de ses défauts. Son aspect suranné lui donne en effet un charme certain et il s'avère, en fin de compte, plutôt agréable de parcourir l'Europe de la Belle Epoque en compagnie de notre danseuse coquine et espionne futée (à moins que ce soit le contraire : danseuse futée et espionne coquine). Le twist final est, de surcroît, fort sympathique. Enfin, le petit casse-tête récurrent consistant à se déplacer de gare en gare tout en essayant d'échapper aux agents lancés à nos trousses n'est pas mal du tout. C'est sans doute ce qu'il y a de meilleur dans le jeu. Il aurait pu faire un bon jeu de plateau MB ou Ravensburger en 1988.

Mata Hari is a point-and-click adventure set in the early 20th century, inspired by the life of the famous dancer and spy. The game blends espionage, mystery, and historical intrigue as you follow Mata Hari through Europe, performing exotic dances while secretly gathering information for various intelligence agencies.

Gameplay focuses on classic adventure mechanics: exploring detailed environments, solving puzzles, talking to characters, and completing espionage assignments. The game offers a mix of dialogue-driven investigation and light mini-games that reflect Mata Hari’s double life—part performer, part undercover agent. While the puzzles are generally accessible, they’re engaging enough to keep the story moving at a good pace.

Visually, the game presents elegant period environments, from smoky cabarets to secret intelligence offices. The music and atmosphere successfully capture the pre-WWI era. While some animations and mechanics feel dated today, the charm of the setting and the unique protagonist make it stand out among adventure titles of its time.

Pros:

Stylish historical setting with a unique protagonist

Accessible puzzles and classic point-and-click gameplay

Interesting espionage storyline

Charming environments and period atmosphere

Cons:

Dated graphics and stiff animations

Some puzzles may feel too simple for veteran adventure players

Story pacing can be inconsistent

Mini-games vary in quality

Verdict:
Mata Hari is a charming and atmospheric adventure that offers a unique take on spy storytelling. Fans of classic point-and-click games and historical themes will find plenty to enjoy, even if some mechanics show their age.

In a walk through it says there are different endings depending on the amount of Wealth, Spycraft, and Skills you get at the end of Chapter 4. Do not worry about getting Skill or Wealth. You can farm them later before Chapter 4.

FIXES
Make sure you download this Directx on your computer if the game would not start. Many people had a problem running the game due to not having the right directx in the forum.

SPYCRAFT
The maximum Spycraft is "1000" finding hidden papers and doing secret objectives. You can get it finished by Chapter 3. If you haven't gotten it already you have done something wrong. You are not required to max it or get any of it.

SKILL
The maximum Skill is "10000". It doesn't really effect the game other than ending supposedly. You can farm it by going back and forth between "Monaco" and "Paris station" in Chapter 3 as they are the easiest stations. Otherwise you can just keep using express routes after talking to all the spies in the train stations.
