O meu conhecimento sobre Silent Hill vem dos dois primeiros filmes, dos mapas criados por fãs para Left 4 Dead 2 (do Steam Workshop) e um pouco da história dos dois primeiros jogos. Não se preocupem, pretendo jogar os outros jogos Silent Hill disponíveis para PC eventualmente.

A única coisa que me deu mais dificuldade neste jogo, para além de uns poucos puzzles confusos, foi o sistema de combate. O combate é algo uma beca caca, sim, mas eventualmente apanhei o jeito.

Deixando o combate de lado, gostei da maioria das cenas do jogo, especialmente da banda sonora. A banda sonora é excelente, desde o menu principal aos créditos. Descobri que o génio por detrás das músicas é o Akira Yamaoka, que trabalhou em todos os jogos Silent Hill, bem como em alguns outros jogos de terror, por isso posso ver que ele nunca falha.

A atmosfera é sinistra e bem feita, achei-a assustadora e assombrosa, com a sua típica e marcante névoa. A banda sonora também contribui para isso, juntamente com os sons de fundo, como os monstros a andar por perto e a aproximarem-se de nós, ou até mesmo os gritos a ecoar à distância.

Agora, em relação à história, também gostei. Ela tem vários plot twists e, claramente, nem tudo o que parece é. Há muitos pontos do enredo que também vos podem confundir, mas as perguntas acabam por ser respondidas, seja avançando na história ou até mesmo lendo os documentos que se podem encontrar por aí (sobre o que aconteceu em Shepherd's Glen, as famílias fundadoras da cidade, toda a questão dos rituais e a Ordem).

Há outra coisa que descobri depois de terminar o jogo: este tem cinco finais diferentes. Tudo depende de três escolhas que vocês fazem ao longo do jogo: [spoiler]se escolhem matar a mãe de Alex, se escolhem perdoar o pai de Alex e se escolhem salvar o Wheeler.[/spoiler]

Consegui o final em que o Alex [spoiler]acorda no hospital psiquiátrico, como se toda a história tivesse acontecido na cabeça dele. O pai dele tinha dito antes que o Alex nunca tinha sido soldado do exército e que foi internado num hospital psiquiátrico, por isso faz sentido. Além disso, ele acorda no quarto 206, e encontrei notas que mencionam um paciente no quarto 206 "agendado para uma lobotomia transorbital amanhã". Presumo que seja, de facto, o Alex.[/spoiler]

No geral, não percebo o ódio por este jogo. Talvez para os fãs de Silent Hill seja merda, talvez as pessoas não tenham gostado da jogabilidade ou até mesmo da história, ou seja simplesmente porque o port não foi bem feito (embora o patch que referi antes melhore a qualidade de vida do jogo). Talvez o jogo não seja assim tão bom de todo, mas estou a fazer uma análise baseada na minha experiência e no meu nível de diversão.

O jogo foi feito após o desmembramento oficial da Team Silent, o que já significa que é mais uma bomba depois de Origins (Shattered Memories ainda se salva porque mantiveram no Wii e PS2). O port para pc é horrível, compensa mais você jogar num console desbloqueado ou bloqueado, com o jogo original.
Quanto a história, ainda "tenta" manter um padrão Silent Hill, mesmo não sendo algo "grandioso" quanto os 4 primeiros jogos, se compararmos com os atuais títulos (F, Short Message, Ascension e Townfall), que basicamente não possuem ligação ZERO com Silent Hill. A história do jogo tem ligação com Silent Hill, porque pelo menos, existe HQs e notas dentro do jogo que explicam o porquê de Sheperd Glenn estar do jeito que está. Por mais que eu não goste dos jogos dessa era, eu ainda vejo certo valor nesses jogos, até mesmo no infeliz do Downpour, porque sabe que Silent Hill é o ponto central da narrativa, ao mesmo tempo que a cidade passa a ser uma personagem, ainda é o cenário principal. Não é uma "síndrome" que se espalhou pro mundo, uma idéia de "deixa outros desenvolvedores expandir a franquia", muito menos uma visual novel interativa, esquecendo totalmente da cidade que é a premissa central da franquia. 
Mas infelizmente, o jogo envelheceu muito mal mesmo.

This game must be played with Unknownproject's Homecoming patch. It is truly an unplayable PC port without it. With it, it is probably objectively the best version of the game. Performance/FPS drops can & will happen from time to time, but the frequency is quite low and is still preferable to the PS3 & Xbox 360 versions which cannot even hold a steady 30FPS on real hardware, and both have some other emulation issues on PC. I tested this game both on my main system and the Steam Deck, the game could generally hold 60FPS locked at max settings on both systems.

Besides that, this game is just honestly really bad. In aspects, it is camp & funny bad. It feels more like a sequel to the Silent Hill film from 2006 than any other game in the franchise. A flim that itself is not good in my opinion. This leads to a very "Hollywood" and goofy feeling to the storytelling. This game's story really is very basic and on the nose. It also just wants to reheat the nacho's of this franchise and retell the same aspects of the plot that other games do significantly better. And of course the stupid Pyramid Head (2006 film version) cameo in this game is infamous, and for how insignificant he is to the game, pointless as well.

The combat is not exactly difficult in this game, but it is not fun at all. Basically, every enemy has 1-2 melee weapons that will work well against them and likely stunlock them. When you find it, you just spam hit them until they die and move on. You are just as susceptible to being stunlocked and have your health taken from 100% to 0%. What this means, is that the game boils down to running up to an enemy and hitting it first, if you hit it first with the correct weapon you have basically won the fight. Ranged weapons work fine against most enemies, but are very lacking in punch and therefore feel quite boring to use. Boring is a good way to describe every aspect of how this game plays. 

Puzzles are nothing special, but one in particular (a stupid slide puzzle) can basically get you progress locked until you load a save if you slide it in the wrong order. I wasted an hour of my life this way.

This game is not very long, just over 12 hours for me to beat, but it took me a year and a half to beat this game because of how much of a slog it was. Aspects of it are quite entertaining in a camp way, but most of this game is just NyQuil. Even the entertaining aspects are quite disrespectful to this series. I would not recommend this game to anyone honestly, it is just not a good experience at any price point.

Игра просто неиграбельна на пк. Мало того, что сама игра не сказать чтобы выдающаяся, так и она просто не работает адекватно: вылеты, проблемы с балансом звука, не стабильные фпс (снял лок через мод с нексуса). Сначала было более менее, но после середины начались вылеты после смерти, а игру я начал на харде (тоже больше ошибка проходить эту игру не на нормале) и на нем умираешь довольно часто из-за дубовой боевки. As someone who has always been able to piece together every part of the story and understand what was going on behind the scenes in every game I have ever played, this game left me with a profound sense of bewilderment. However, this was due to its meaninglessness rather than any particular achievement on its part.

Every single character in the game, without exception, does nothing but prattle on instead of telling you what happened to the town. You could ask, "What time is it, I wonder?" and the likely answer you would get would be, "It's too late... Too late for everyone..."

I have always hated having to follow a little child around, one of the biggest clichés in horror games and in this game, we once again find ourselves in trouble while chasing after some stupid child.

Leaving aside the countless gaps in the game's story, I wasn't the slightest bit satisfied with its ending. In fact, I was rather surprised when the game ended. For someone who has expectations but very little patience, this game isn't particularly appealing.

Silent Hill: Homecoming is a dark, unsettling survival-horror game with a strong focus on psychological tension and disturbing creature design. The story follows Alex Shepherd as he returns home to search for his missing brother, uncovering secrets that grow more disturbing as the game continues.

The atmosphere is the game’s biggest strength. Fog-covered streets, abandoned locations, eerie sound design, and the series’ signature Otherworld imagery create a constant feeling of dread. Combat is more action-focused than in earlier Silent Hill games, but it still requires careful timing and resource management.

Some puzzles and story elements are not as strong as the series’ best entries, and the combat can feel uneven. Even so, Homecoming offers a creepy and memorable experience for horror fans who enjoy dark stories, tense exploration, and Silent Hill’s unique nightmare-like world.

Silent Hill: Homecoming è uno dei capitoli più divisivi e sottovalutati della celebre saga survival horror di Konami uscito nel 2008 e sviluppato dagli americani di Double Helix Games, il titolo segna il passaggio del franchise all'era occidentale, portando importanti cambiamenti rispetto ai capolavori del Team Silent

Trama e Atmosfera
Vestiamo i panni di Alex Shepherd, un soldato che torna nella sua città natale, Shepherd's Glen, dopo essere stato ferito in guerra. Al suo arrivo trova una città deserta, avvolta da una nebbia innaturale, e scopre la scomparsa del fratellino Joshua la ricerca del fratello lo condurrà inevitabilmente negli abissi della vicina Silent Hill la narrazione riprende i temi classici della serie: il senso di colpa, i traumi familiari, il fanatismo religioso e la scomposizione della realtà nell'Otherworld la storia regala colpi di scena efficaci e finali multipli ben orchestrati.

Gameplay e Combat System
A differenza dei protagonisti passati, impacciati e spaventati, Alex è un addestrato ed esperto di combattimento corpo a corpo:
● ​Sistema di schivata: Possibilità di evitare gli attacchi con tempismo e contrattaccare.
​● Migliore gestione delle armi: Attacchi leggeri, pesanti e mirata libera per le armi da fuoco.
● ​Enigmi ambientali: presenti e ben inseriti, anche se complessivamente meno complessi rispetto ai primi capitoli.
​● Design dei mostri: eccellente. Creature come Scarlet o il Sepulcher offrono alcune delle boss fight visivamente più riuscite e inquietanti della serie.

Se cercate il terrore psicologico puro e lento dei primi tre capitoli, Homecoming potrebbe sembrare un po' troppo d'azione se però viene preso per quello che è  un horror d'azione con una splendida colonna sonora, mostri memorabili e un'ottima atmosfera macabra — rimane un capitolo estremamente valido e ingiustamente sottovalutato.

Puzzle Chronicles is if Dungeons & Dragons was a match 3 game. 

The matches are very slow moving, and like most match 3 games, a lot of winning is based on luck, which in a story driven game is a real hindrance. 

You gain experience and money each fight and when you level up you can increase some stats. You get a pet that can be upgraded by playing a mini game, though it only seems to be in the first area, and I can't go back there, so my dog monster is stuck. I'm assuming there's other places eventually but I'd have to actually play it enough to get that far.

The problem is, I get the feeling the game wants me to grind, and that's nothing but tedious in a slow moving game based on chance. Heck, it's tedious in most faster paced and more fun games.

I got to a spot where the enemy had some broken abilities that he was using constantly that tipped the scales in his favor severely. The best I could do is delay my impending loss. So my options are to grind and hope that helps, which it won't cuz all abilities that might help are tied to my pet monster leveling up - search for treasure that might help, but more often than not, I find something I already have. (Yes, you do get all sorts of gear to equip to help buff your character) - or I can just keep trying to fight the bad guy until I actually get lucky enough to win.

None of that sounds remotely fun to me, so I'll be moving on.

It's honestly not a bad game, just a bit too tedious and maybe a little too hard for a game based around luck.

J'ai longtemps hésité vu les nombreuses critiques mais j'ai profité d'une promo et pour 3€ et des poussières je ne regrette pas du tout mon achat. Le graphisme date un peu c'est vrai (mais c'est aussi pour ça qu'il est soldé) mais on sent malgré tout que cela a été développé par un vrai studio et pas en mode garage par deux copains. Le héro change d'apparence en fonction des armes équipées, il y a de nombreux lieux et de nombreux ennemis avec chacun des attaques spéciales. L'aspect répétitif du jeu est normal pour un puzzle game RPG où les combats sont basés sur le fait de faire des groupes de couleur, donc forcément oui, on bouffe du puzzle mais ceux qui n'aiment pas ça doivent acheter un vrai RPG pas un puzzle RPG. Concernant la difficulté, il y en a un qui s'est dit bloqué au deuxième lieu, il y a un boss à la fin de chaque lieu (qui correspondrait à un niveau dans un jeu de plateformes), donc oui forcément le boss est plus dur à battre et il faut s'y prendre à plusieurs fois. Et parfois il faudra farmer des petits ennemis pour upper son perso et son stuff afin de pouvoir battre le boss. C'est le principe d'un RPG, on farm l'xp au combat et on level up son perso et pour ça dans ce jeu on enchaîne les puzzles. Après, j'avoue que le jeu n'est pas simple d'accès, c'est pas jeu casual, il faut un bon niveau d'intelligence et dexterité clavier/souris car la rapidité est cruciale. Je l'ai fini en mode normal et il y a un niveau plus facile. Apparemment certains n'acceptent pas de perdre quelques combats, pour moi j'y ai vu un challenge à relever. Ce jeu demande un peu de persévérance. La mécanique du jeu est originale et il m'a fallu pas mal de combat pour arriver à comprendre toutes les subtilités. Certains se sont plaints de l’absence de didacticiel, mais en fait il y en a bien un proposé au début et je conseil fortement de le faire, il n'explique pas tout mais sans la base, la mécanique du jeu n'est pas intuitive. Après, je pense que c'est un jeu one shot, c'est pas le jeu que vous allez poncer en long en large et en travers et rejouer des dizaines de fois mais c'est un jeu auquel vous pourrez jouer un bonne 30aine d'heures pour le finir un fois en mode histoire. L'histoire n'est pas folle, c'est du déjà vu mais elle se laisse écouter et apporte un objectif à jouer, les voix ne sont pas dingue, mais c'est traduit en français et c'est plutôt cool déjà vu le prix. Concernant le côté Puzzle, c'est une sorte de mélange entre puzzle et tetris. Il y a plusieurs forme de puzzle dans le jeu mais je vais vous décrire la principale (celle des combats). C'est pas un écran plein où il faut inverser deux objets pour former un groupe. C'est plutôt comme tetris un écran vide avec des objets qui arrive en flux continu. Sauf qu'au lieu d'être verticale (avec les objets qui descende du haut de l'écran vers le bas), ca se joue de gauche à droite, avec les objets qui arrive par la gauche et qui vont s'écraser à droite. C'est du haut fait que votre ennemi joue lui de droit vers la gauche et qu'on partage le même plateau de jeu que l'ennemi. Il y a un séparation qui bouge en fonction des combos qui fait qu'on va gagner ou perdre du terrain sur l'adversaire et donc avoir accès à plus ou moins d'espace pour jouer. On peut ainsi piquer ou se fait piquer des objets qui sont sur la ligne proche de la séparation quand le plateau avance. C'est assez déroutant et déprimant quand on se fait bouffer un objet sympa mais une fois qu'on a compris le coup ca donne de l'intérêt au jeu. Je disais les objets mais en fait c'est toujours 3 gemmes de couleur alignées (une barre droite de 3) qu'on peut faire pivoter 4 fois (soit pour passer d'horizontale à verticale soit pour inverser l'ordre des couleurs) ou deplacer (pas de gauche à droite comme tetris mais vers le haut ou le bas vu qu'on joue à l'horizontale) . Il y a 4 couleurs dans le jeu. Donc par exemple va apparaitre une barre avec 1 gemme rouge, 1 gemme verte, 1 gemme bleu. A vous de la faire pivoter ou de la déplacer pour qu'elle s'écrase de sorte à former des groupes de gemme de la même couleur. Par contre, ca n'explose pas quand il y a un nombre (par exemple dès qu'on en rassemble 3), ca explose et ca génère un effet quand on colle une gemme particulière (dite d'attaque) de la même couleur à un groupe de gemme. Par exemple, vous avez réussi à rassembler 15 gemmes de la couleur rouge, lorsque vous faite attérir une gemme d'attaque rouge sur le groupe, ca fait disparaitre les gemmes et ca génère l'effet. Et les gemmes qui était "dessus" (a gauche vu qu'on est en horizontale), vont descendre pour éventuellement faire des effets en cascade. C'est donc un mixte intéressant mais qui demande un peu d'expérience savoir quelle est la meilleur déplacer les barres de gemmes de couleur qui arrivent en flux continu. Concernant le côté RPG, pour ne pas vous enlever la surprise, je vous laisse découvrir mais on retrouve les classiques d'un rpg même si chaque principe est réduit à sa plus simple expression et reste assez limité. Il ne faut pas s'attendre à des millers de caractéristiques, Je pense qu'un fois qu'on a compris la mécanique du jeu, on ferait évoluer son personnage de la même façon à chaque partie, c'est pas un RPG que vous allez recommencez avec des classes/caractéristiques différentes. Il y a une quête principale ou globalement vous n'avez pas d'autre choix que de suivre l'histoire donc c'est pas un monde ouvert ou vous faite ce que vous voulez dans l'ordre que vous voulez. Il y a quelques quetes secondaires obsolète mais ca va pas chercher plus loin que d'aller combattre et de ramener l'objet à celui qui vous a donné la quête. Ca me semble normal dans ce style de jeu que le côté RPG soit pas profond, sinon faut acheter un vrai RPG, le coté RPG donne un petit piment et un petit objectif à enchaîner les puzzles pour tuer le temps et stimuler son cerveau. Sinon, la seule vraie critique que j'ai lu et que je rejoins c'est le fait qu'on ne peut rien customiser (on peut pas couper le son par exemple, moi qui joue toujours son coupé avec de la musique j'ai du faire un écart mais le son est discret), on ne peut en effet pas changer les couleurs (donc pour à éviter pour les daltoniens par exemple) et changer les touches, donc faudra s'adapter mais au final, c'est pas compliqué (flèche directionnel pour se déplacer, CTRL pour pivoter, et au lieu d'utiliser l'espace qui n'est pas pratique pour accélerer la descente de l'objet quand vous etes satifsait de sa position, il faut utiliser le clic droit (et pas gauche) de la souris. Le clic gauche servant à déclencher les effets spéciaux lorsque la jauge est pleine). En conclusion, si vous aimez les puzzles games RPG, que vous n'êtes pas trop difficile, que vous acceptez de jouer à un jeu au style graphique démodé et que aimez vous prouver à vous même que vous êtes capables de percer les secrets des mécaniques d'un jeu pour arriver à être bon, je vous conseille ce jeu (à acheter bien sûr en solde à prix réduit). Pour ceux qui veulent plus d'infos sur le contenu et quelques tips pour vous aider à mieux vous en sortir plus vite, vous pouvez lire la suite. On retrouve les classiques d'un RPG, le personnage a des caractéristiques à développer mais il n'y en a que 4 (d'ailleurs attention, je ne sais pas si c'est un problème de traduction, mais la description des caractéristique lorsqu'on passe un niveau n'est pas claire voire fausse, il faut aller dans le sac a dos et changer d'onglet pour voir exactement l'effet de chaque caractéristique, c'est beaucoup plus parlant et juste). On gagne de l'expérience en combattant ou finissant des étapes de la quête et on gagne des niveaux pour les caractéristiques quand on atteint des palier d'xp, classique. 3 / 10. Tech demo.

Puzzle Chronicles is probably the worst title in the Puzzle Quest set of titles, right behind Puzzle Kingdoms. For the most part it feels like a tech demo, an unfinished beta release of the full product. It focuses more on 3D characters models, but forgets the fun and general enjoyability along the way.

The game has some basic ideas pinned down, but the execution is less then perfect. It's tedious, monotone, downright boring and grind-ridden at many times. What boggles me very much is how much the series has decayed from title to title.

One of the worst part of this game and sadly, a core element, is the combat system. Unlike previous titles there's no concept of HP, just a bar that goes towards one of the players. A reminiscence of classic arcade split-screen titles. Still, this particular implementation is totally unfair and favors snowballing. It's harder to come back and win if the bar is closer to your side of the screen. Also, while previous titles promoted a concept of strategy by understanding tile movements, this game is purely RNG based. You can win and loose the same battle in a matter of seconds, on any difficulty. The sad part is that this is a wanted mechanic as you will get a award for constantly failing battles. Promoting bad mechanics and animosity towards the player gets a -1 in my book.

Speaking of difficulty, the game in extremely hard and unfair at the beginning and becomes unusually simple by the end if you focus on getting equipment with rage bonus. The Warbeast and it's abilities are mostly useless and more so as you cannot respec it's skills. 

Minigames are unimpressive. Rehashes of the same concept. Most are optional and the ones that aren't are a bit forced.

Overall, a very drab and mediocre experience that goes on and on, in a forced manner. 4 / 10 from my part and a -1 for bad intentions towards the player, means a solid 3 / 10. Just skip this game and play either of the Puzzle Quest games or a different Match x game altogether.

Not memorable, but a good time waster, and the puzzle bits are actually kind of fun once you get the hang of them (and moreso near the ending, when things get a bit more complicated). They are more Tetris than Match-3, and a few battles were actually quite exciting (and I had to manage my equipment to better handle them).

The biggest annoyance was the world navigating. While it takes only a few seconds for the character to walk form A to B, the actual walking is completely pointless, and there is lots of walking from A to B. It is even more irritating because the game shows you were you have to go by having a sparkling effect walking from A to B... So often you have to wait for the "effect" to go, and then immediately after you spend the same amount of time "going" there yourself. Maybe I missed a key which would skip all this walking?

Another annoyance: loading times are a lot worse than they should.

But again, mostly, an enjoyable experience, and actually less grindy (near the end) than Puzzle Quest. I would say 78/100.

I don't generally bother with reviews, but this game is a fun little time-waster.  If you're a fan of Robert E. Howard's character Conan of Cimmeria that has been the subject of novels, comic books and movies then you'd probably like this games story-line as it borrows heavily from the numerous Conan origin stories.  Also the puzzle gameplay is not terribly complex.  Just enough to feel like you aren't just going through the motions and that some level of skill and planning is needed to win.  The artwork in the game is well done and fits the story well.  Also the game in my experience has proved to be very stable.  I have encountered no bugs, crashes or other bs that a lot of games subject players to.  So if casual puzzle games with cool artwork tickle your fancy, this is a great buy especially if you catch it on sale.  As always have fun :)
edit 12/30/2019  Having read some of the other reviews here and the complaints about gameplay...  there is something you need to know about this type of game, it is a casual game but that does not mean that you run from each mandatory encounter skipping all "non-mandatory" side quests and all exploration in a rush to complete the game as quickly as possible.  It is simply not how this type of game is meant to be played. You should play the mini games several times to get some extra items and make your character stronger, take the time to level your character in the optional dungeons, use the trainer to boost your skills when you have extra gold.  This type of game is not a race to the end but rather a pretty journey that you take your time with.  Level your character, get better gear, learn the puzzle system, give yourself time to feel powerful, it's just about having fun and being someone you will never get the chance to be IRL.  The reality is that it doesn't take that much time to become completey OP and roast al comers so you can enjoy the story.. you just have to work your character a bit as mentioned previously.  There are even secret battles to be found if you just take a little time.. I mean I just pasted Anubis earlier tonight! if you know anything of ancient Egyptian god beliefs then you know that's pretty cool.  My point is don't buy into the whiners, I have played many puzzle games and this one, although perhaps not as in-depth as some I have played, certainly deserves its place in my Steam Library

A somewhat predictable RPG, Puzzle Chronicles suffers from some mildly bad voice acting and fairly repetitive battles - once you learn how to play it's Tetris-esque combat and mini-games, it's pretty much just rinse, repeat, get better gear. The story has some amusing moments, but do not be fooled: you need to disengage your brain to play this game. I think the Puzzle Quest series does a better job of engaging you with its story, and has similar mechanics to progress with.

That being said, it's nice to play a puzzle that isn't "match 3" and while the combat is repetitive (and despite what some think, you [i]can[/i] make a comeback from some very bad looking situations), it's different and interesting enough that while you're progressing the story and facing off against different enemies, it doesn't get tedious. It's worth a play, and will keep you engaged if you're after something light.

I think the only unfortunate thing for me is that there is little incentive to play and get the final achievement (it's just grinding), and not enough of a community to really get anything going for the multiplayer since it's a little older now.

Puzzle Chronicles is a puzzle roleplaying game developed by Infinite Interactive and published by Konami Digital Entertainment Inc. This is yet another title in Infinite Interactives growing stable of puzzle games. You are a hero on a quest through the savage lands of the Ashurin Empire in search of your tribesman who have been taken by slavers. Your hero will combat fierce beasts and battle hardened warriors during your travels as you attempt to rescue your people, raise an army and topple the Empire. This being a R.P.G., you have the ability to customize your character but sadly this time there are no character classes to choose from. As you do battle your hero will accquire experience points which will allow you to upgrade a set of skills to suit your particular playstyle and liking. There is also an abundance of gear to collect or craft ranging from mighty weapons, enchanted armor, amulets, etc. to further enhance your character.

One nice thing about Puzzle Chronicles that sets it apart from Infinite Interactives other games is that this title is not a match 3 game. The closest title that I can liken this to is some sort of sideways Tetris game. Stacks of colored gems instead of blocks enter the battlefield from the left side falling towards a wall that divides your area from your opponent's area. You can rotate the gem stacks and place them any way you choose to. Destroying these gems builds power also called "rage" in this game for your weapons and companion warbeast's attacks. That's right...you can accquire a doge, known as a warbeast, to accompany you on your quest. As you battle, you and your opponent are in a constant tug of war over the wall dividing the battlefield between the two of you. The fight ends when one combatant has no more room to maneuver the gem stacks entering their area because the wall has been pushed too far across their part of the battlefield. The gameplay sounds simple enough but when that divider wall is steadily taking space from your half of the battlefield and the gem stacks just keep coming as your opponent attacks and attacks you really start to feel the intensity of this game. Did I forget to mention the cool little animated fight sequences of your character and your opponent that take place just above the gem battlefield? Besides the story driven battles there are also some mini-games that you can compete in to unlock items and provide even more enhanced abilities.

Graphically I like this game. It has a really nice looking artstyle to it as far as the cutscenes for the story goes and the animated fight sequences that occur as you puzzle battle are impressive and fun to watch. The musical score, like the scores in all Infinite Interactive games, is brilliant and does it job amply but none of the tracks really stand out of the pack to me. Most of the score has a middle-eastern sound to it and is executed quite well though. The sound effects, however, are very well done. Gem explosions and battle sounds are loud and crisp as they should be. The voice-overs in the cutscenes are excellent and do a great job of enhancing the story.

While not my favorite puzzle R.P.G., Puzzle Chronicles does have a nice story that I felt compelled to see through to the end and I also found the deviation from the typical match 3 gameplay to be quite refreshing as well. With that said, one thing about this game that really bothered me is something that I mentioned in another recent review for a match 3 puzzle title...the lack of a good tutorial. Puzzle Chronicles suffers horribly in this failing as you'll quickly find yourself lost after the "so-called" tutorial ends. You'll have to search the internet for some fan written guides or just play the game and learn things by trial and error which can be quite frustrating. However, once you do learn how to play and what everything means then you can finally start to enjoy the game. This title definitely won't be everyones cup of tea but if you're looking for something a little different in the puzzle game genre then I suggest that you give this title a try.

Puzzle Chronicles is nothing but a time-sink, but what more do you expect from a puzzle game? Well, it better not be good art direction or writing, because this game has neither. The gameplay could be compared to 'Battle Tetris' in the form of a tug-of-war, but more often than not comes down to pure luck as to how well you will do in a fight. One try you will be obliterated in a few drops, the next time you will obliterate them. After playing for a few hours (and it took me 14 to finish, doing all side-quests but nowhere near the amount they expect to get all the awards) you will lose a fight and find yourself thinking "I lost? But I already wasted so much time fighting, and now I have to do it again?", and that is ultimately that it is, a waste of time. You will fight your way through it for the sake of completing it, not because it is fun or challenging. Over 14 hours I got half my stats up to around 50, and the other two were still in their teens. For replayability the awards expect you to get them all to 75, with similar expectation for your dog compaion (which serves as your special attacks). 

On the plus side, there is content. Lots of content. There are arenas to unlock, where you can sight certain enemies as many times as you like (ie. grind) and plenty of mini-games, which all take the form of a more traditional tetris-meets-bejewelled set-up, which can net you levels, your dog levels, crafting two items into a higher-tier item, or random loot. So if you're looking for some competative-ish tile-matching and want plenty to keep you going, this is for you, as long as you can look past the ugly art and insuferable main character. Certainly not something you would expect from Konami, and I would by FAR recommend Puzzle Quest over this, in all regards.

I mean... if you took one look at this and said "This might be decent"... you need to get your head examined.

I bought this in a humble bundle 5+ years ago for $11 with like a bunch of other better games, just got bored enough to go and give it a whirl... something mindless while I killed some time... yeah brutal.

It's as bad as it looks... if you cherish the memory of the original game, don't even bother, it takes a huge diarrhea dump all over it. Graphics are cell phone quality trash and so are the animations and game play... can't say much about the music because it's a bunch of ambient noises for the most part and like wooshing air sounds in the flying sections.

I figured it might have some promise in the music category, seeing as they tease you with a remix of the original song from the very first Rocket Knight game in the first level. I was expecting some cool Sparkster music mixed in as well but after the first stage the music basically goes silent... what a joke.

I don't even understand the logic of the devs on the game's mechanics either, for the most part it all makes sense and has some good quality of life stuff... except they decided to make Sparksters ranged attacks consume his rocket boost bar and have it's own dedicated button. 

I remember in the first game he would just shoot out blades of air at a distance for the cost of nothing cause he was just awesome that way... nothing like gimping the hero for the sake of game play mechanics, however, I digress...

The real offense is that in the original game, Sparkster could dash in any direction he damn well wanted.... in this version? Left, Left-Up, Up, Right-Up and Right... that's it... no down-ward or down-ward diagonal dashes for him this game... I just don't get it... There's actually a stage where this tech would have come in insanely handy to break floor boards to find power ups but instead they have you ricocheting off of walls and ceilings... Meaning, the animation for this tech exists, but they limit it to only showing when you bounce off of walls and ceilings... this game is just trash.

It looks like trash, it plays like trash, and it takes a giant dump all over the memory of the original games. These games were sleeper hits at the time, cult classics that grew in status over the years. I remember always loving Rocket Knight Adventures and Sparkster when I was a child, so much so that I purchased them both and still own them to this day and they're worth quite a bit of $_$... this game? Isn't worth the time it took me to write this review... but meh... I was feeling generous... stay the hell away from this junk.

Rocket Knight trás de volta toda a essência da franquia consagrada no Mega Drive. Desta vez com gráficos repaginados e uma dificuldade mais acessível se comparada ao do original. Entramos novamente, na pele do gambá mais destemido dos 16-Bits, para salvar seu mundo. A jogabilidade é bem similar aos primeiros jogos da franquia, tendo alguns bons ajustes para se adaptar a modernidade. Não se trata de um jogo muito difícil, como eram seus antecessores, sendo assim, é possível zerar em pouco tempo, dependendo de sua habilidade nos momentos mais difíceis, que são alguns. Podemos coletar cristais azuis e vermelhos durante as fases, além de corações de vida e outro item com o rosto do protagonista, que nos dão uma vida a mais. O jogo conta com conquistas, e um total de catorze fases para zerar. É uma releitura e ao mesmo tempo, sequência, de muita qualidade, e muito recomendada para fãs de jogos de plataforma.

Looking through the Steam reviews before I booted up the game I thought I would be playing a bad game based off of how many negative reviews I saw. My opinion was further confirmed when I couldn't boot up the game because my anti virus was stopping it from starting up. I turned it off and thought to myself, "Ok let's see this mess". Imagine my surprise when I was treated to a short but challenging platformer that was actually pretty fun. Don't get me wrong, the games no masterpiece but it has a fun although somewhat clunky movement system with the jetpack and some really fun ideas after the first world. The first world is very basic but it teaches you the mechanics of the game, after the first world the challenge starts to ramp up, and new ideas are constantly introduced. The last world especially tests your platforming skills. The drill attack can be  a bit clunky at times if you're playing with a controller, sometimes it'll go straight up instead of diagonal but that was only a minor gripe. Some of the later enemies are especially frustrating but it fits the game well being a revival of a retro series. The game also has some levels where you're flying which is a nice change of pace. Overall I think if you're a fan of the original. or platformers in general, it's worth picking this game up on a sale.

I'm kind of torn on this one. I'm a big fan of Rocket Knight Adventures of the Genesis and Sparkster on the SNES. They are iconic games that demonstrate Konami on top of their game, featuring gorgeous and vibrant graphics, rocking soundtracks and bombastic and energetic gameplay. Rocket Knight, on the other hand, seems like a pale imitation that doesn't manage to reach anywhere near the heights set by its predecessors. I think this is best observed through the redesign of the main character himself. The original Sparkster was squat in build with a cartoony and expressive face, a hero who looked ready to take on the world and whose boisterous charm and appeal was apparent in every frame of animation. The new Rocket Knight's eyes are no longer large and reminiscent of anime but beady and cold. I can't put my finger on it but he somehow looks sickly. I really can't help but feel like I'm no longer playing the same character I was playing in 16 bit.

It actually took me a long while to even get around to playing this through, as the demo had originally turned me off and I felt no inclination to come back to it. But eventually I picked it up on the cheap and decided to give it another shot. To be fair, the game does get better as you progress through it. There are some decent gimmicks that make levels feel unique. The controls are mostly fine. The game is also fairly short and doesn't outstay its welcome, which I genuinely appreciate.

If you're looking to recapture the joy you felt playing throuigh Sparkster's 16 bit adventures, you won't find it here. However, if you're looking for an average action-platformer that will keep you occupied for a couple of hours then you could do worse than this.

I only managed to play through the first few levels of Rocket Knight before I felt like I had seen everything the game had to offer. Everything about this game is perfectly middle of the road. The graphics and animations are fine, but nothing special. The gameplay is your stereotypical action platformer. The level design has some basic secrets and the occasional interesting moment but is generally the same as your standard platformer. The game isn't necessarily bad, it has just been outdone in every way by countless other platformers.

All the best platformers have [i]that[/i] mechanic. You know the one. Mario's head stomp. Sonic's spin dash. DKC's animal buddies. Super Metroid's screw attack. Meat Boy's clingy wall jump. The simple thing that makes traversing their worlds unique. The one that gives you that little thrill of satisfaction every time you use it. 

Rocket Knight's jetpack must certainly rank alongside those classics. When you squeeze the right trigger, launching your opossum avatar across the screen like an avenging angel riding a missile, it feels [i]amazing[/i]. The game knows its strengths, giving you great sprawling levels in which to dart around, careening off solid surfaces like a pinball made of fire and steel as you hunt down gems and enemies.

Other aspects don't [i]quite[/i] hold up to the central mechanic. The enemies themselves aren't anywhere near the heights of Donkey Kong Country's Kremlings, the soundtrack is merely servicable, and the story gets the job done with minimal fuss. The package is an excuse to blast through an alternate reality where the early-to-mid 90s never ended; where all you needed for a classic was [i]that[/i] mechanic, and a game to put it in.

But what an excuse. They don't make games like this anymore, so if a trip back to the 90s sounds like any kind of fun, you won't regret picking up Rocket Knight in the slightest.

There's too much wall bouncing using the jetpack to go farther compared to the original (which also had vibrant colors) and that can be frustrating in last levels (missing will damage you).  However, the game can still be fun to play, much like TMNT reshelled, which had drab graphics/dull music on a solid engine.  The flying levels were at least fun though, felt like a shoot 'em up.

This is an old game, and I don't think it aged well.  My review toss-up nudges me to not recommend it over games like Recore, Blaster Master Zero 2, Skyvolt Zack, and Adventures of Pip, which look much better and have more gameplay mechanics.  You can even air dash in those (except Adventures of Pip which has unique jumps/pixel detonations and that's a fun mechanic), so it's hard to give this game an edge when the graphics/music are forgettable compared to even the original Rocket Knight Adventures.

Rocket Knight is a beat'em up platformer adventure game.  You play as Sparkster a rocket powered oppssum trying to save his people from pig overlords.  The game's level design and stage variety is top notch.  Each level has 4 parts which cycle through various game modes to keep the game interesting.  You have your standard platforming collectathon, a gradius like space ship shooter, an infinite faller, and some very interesting boss battles.  

The rocket mechanic makes playing as Sparkster very fun. It feels great to chain together a few bounce and ultimately cut through a far away enemy.  Sparkster had great mobility, running through the game world was reminscent of Crash Bandicoot or Sonic.  In the later half of World 2, this is subverted when they take away your unlimited rocket powers, but I think it was done well and didn't overstay it's welcome.

The main weakness I found was the collectible aspect, the game locks it's collectible achievements behind a 100% wall, but offers no feedback on how many you still need until the stage is over.  If you're a completionist this can be a real pain replaying the stage multiple times.  

Overall I enjoyed the game, it's an overlooked gem in an overly saturated genre.

Biozone is a subpar platformer shooter where you play as a cyborg named Agent Brass and you defeat aliens.

Of the 15 levels you go through, they all look pretty similar to one another. There's just about 3 different level backgrounds, which two of them almost look like they could just be palate swaps of one another. For the enemies, there aren't too many different kinds of enemies, so they get fairly repetitive over time. The same goes for weapon variants; you have a primary gun and you can pick up grenades and just a few different primary gun power-ups, but it's not very much to keep it different. The controls are okay for what they are. Climbing up things can be a bit annoying, but it works. As far as your usual controls go, you can also pick up and throw boxes, you can roll and climb, as well as use a jet pack once you find a station that'll fill your jet pack. There are 4 bosses you come across through the game and they put up a decent challenge with the exception of the final boss, which is a bit tedious to overcome.

The visuals as I mentioned are pretty repetitive in style and the music is okay to listen to, but it's all fairly the same as well.

Overall, I don't recommend this game as there's nothing that would really want me to play this game. Even with the power-ups and grenades, this game can basically be done with just the basic gun alone and that's exactly what this game is, fairly basic. The one thing I'll give it is that the explosive barrels have a fairly cool explosion.

If you grew up trying out games during trial periods on WildTangent, there's a chance you ran into Tank Universal.

I remember that I used to play this game from beginning to end with no focus on the story at all. Only the visuals and the gameplay were all I was focused on. I did not remember it being slow and I was researching how to increase the framerate.

And then it donned on me. Even though games today manage to go 60fps and beyond, playing this game at 30fps is oddly...better. Combined with the visual computer fuzzy screen appearance and the TRON atmosphere, 30fps felt more than just an engine limitation. It was for an artistic direction.

With that being said, the game is incredibly fun. The story plays out fairly simple. The character names are creative to the point I don't know if they're based on anything, but a breath of fresh air.

The main character, George, is meant to be relatable even if he takes a back seat after...well, sitting down participating in the Tank Universal game. I kinda wished his character was more fleshed out inside the program, the feeling of not wanting to get sick and just live, experience life in its joy and adventures. But I felt he was underplayed as we, the player, control him.

The visuals really tell you everything. It's meant to look dated. It's inspired by TRON. Gameplay compliments it by feeling punchy, static-like, atmospheric combat. And that helps serve as an identity to the game. 

Overall, it's a very simple game, but it has so much artistic flourish in it that is underrated. I feel the creator did an amazing job creating a small game that has kept me interested in replaying after all these years. Seriously, if you look past 30fps as an engine limitation, you're going to see what make it fun and exciting.

You're probably reading this because you liked the tank scenes in the movie Tron.
Not coincidentally, Meridian4 made Tank Universal because THEY liked the tank scenes in Tron.
And I bought it because I like the... well, you know. And it definitely has a certain Tron vibe, only instead of Jeff Bridges, the protagonist is a bored, incapacitated old man. Compelling!

Am I glad I bought it? Yes, because now I don't have to wonder if I was missing out on something great. So IS Tank Universal great? No. Is it worth your time as a die-hard Tron fan? Possibly. And if you've never seen Tron? Less, um... possibly.

Ask yourself:
"Do I enjoy Tron-inspired games where the primary mechanic is mentally calculating how to hit moving targets from a moving vehicle on sloped sufaces with a relatively slow-moving projectile that is affected by gravity (even though the existance of gravity in a digital world makes no sense)?"
If the answer is "yes" and you have $5 to spare, buy Tank Universal.

But also ask yourself:
"Am I deeply annoyed by incoherent/irrelevant storylines, especially when I'm forced to endure them in lengthy, unskippable cinematics?"
"Do my eyes roll back into my head during tedious, unnecessary travel sequences through static environments with no interaction?"
"Do I have a hard time letting go of my nagging sensation that a game, for some unknown reason, isn't as good as it could have been?"
"Did I hate Tron?"
If the answer is "yes" to any of these, consider passing over Tank Universal. Maybe the tank moved a little too slugishly, or maybe the upgrading & leveling system lacked the right incentives or rewards. I could never figure it out. The game always felt like off-brand Legos: that kind that fit together, though not quite right, and never with that secure, satisfying "click" of precision. Don't get me wrong, it's still fun, but why didn't Grandma just buy EXACTLY what I WROTE on my *** **** LIST!?!?

First off: INSANE PROPS to the SINGLE CREATOR of this game. The outstanding work and dedication is astounding. 

Tank Universal: a simple game with a silly 80s-esque plot, 80s-esque style and... well ok, it's basically Tron with tanks. And it's AWESOME; a real chill, tubular time. This game is better than the second version by a long shot. Stay retro ;)

One aspect I personally appreciate is stronger mission and map design--the maps and objectives are more unique and tailor a wider range of experiences, "challenges," and enjoyment, whereas the second's sandbox feeling lacks character.

Another thing accomplished in this is sensible damage output and input. You may gain the sense you're invincible if you play on easy or normal, but you can still get caught off guard if you're not thinking about damage or strategy when necessary.

The aesthetic accomplished in Tank Universal 1 is superior as well. Though graphically inferior, it accomplishes more with simplicity and an imitation Tron texture on people, tanks, environments, weapons, etc. Sound effects fit more in this version. Some crossed over into the second, but all sounds related to tanks were changed, which messes with your memory.

Tank movement is heavier in this version and the upgrade system is simpler. I like some of the faster responses and full 16:9 resolution from the second game, as well as the tank upgrade system. The story in this first version takes itself less seriously as well, yet it has some moments of impact or interest.

Overall, an incredibly memorable game. I actually got Steam as soon as I found out the name of the game--I hadn't played it in over 10 years since my Wild Tangent days, and it's no longer on that. It's just as much fun now, if not more, because I'm an adult with somewhat better motor skills and strategy. A pity there aren't more skirmish options.

Честно говоря, я ожидал чего-то намного худшего от этой игры. На поверку Tank Universal оказался инди-клоном Tron 2.0 средней паршивости, у которого конечно хватает проблем, но играть можно. Игровой процесс разделен на 2 части - пешие забеги и танковые бои. По поводу первых ничего хорошего сказать нельзя, оружия почему-то на этих этапах никакого не дается, поэтому приходится только бегать по пустым локациям до следующей контрольной точки. А вот танковые бои вышли поинтереснее, в наличии несколько типов врагов и укреплений, различные бонусы вроде мин и ракет, да и задачи игра пытается подкидывать кардинально разные. Основной костяк танковых этапов - это позиционная война, где нужно захватывать точки на внушительных картах и постепенно ослаблять оборону вражеской базы, пока соперничающая сторона пытается делать то же самое. Так как игра короткая (всего 20 уровней + эпилог), то и приесться все это действо мне не успело.

Беда Tank Universal в том, что дизайнеры уровней из-за своей явной неопытности наделали кучу мелких, но довольно раздражающих ошибок. Например, сюжет в игре не без интересных моментов, но катсцены по большей части затянуты и cрежиссированы довольно хреново, а пропустить их нельзя. Скорость передвижения слишком низкая, как "на ногах", так и в танке, и из-за размеров уровней часто в игре не происходит вообще никакой движухи. На танке можно включать ускорение, что заметно улучшает темп игры - но проблема в том, что на включение буста тратиться "осколки", которые в ограниченном количестве выпадают с убитых врагов. Так что если сильно спешить, то в итоге останешься без заначки на ракеты и бои будут сложнее. 

Вот так и выходит, что вроде местами играть без шуток интересно, и визуальный стиль с музыкой неплохие, и видно что в целом разработчики как могли старались сделать как лучше. Но в итоге несбалансированность игрового процесса и заунывные пробежки по пустым уровням только портят общее впечатление от Tank Universal. Так что рекомендую ее только тем кто ностальгирует по играм разновидности "типичный шутер из 00ых" и Tron 2.0 в частности, но только с большой скидкой на распродаже. Главное, не стесняйтесь уменьшить сложность игры в опциях на легкую и спамить в консоли (клавиша ~) команду give_shards для бесконечного ускорения. Вот тогда играть намного веселее и скучные моменты можно проскочить, сосредоточившись на главном что есть в этой игре - танковых боях.

This game was my early childhood. I only came across it one day when i was just 11 or so years old, and back then i loved it and to this day i still do. Whilst the game isn't your perfect game or anything too innovative i like to think this game was the key point where it marks in gaming history when Indie games hit the gaming market in force. as this game came out 1 year prior to Notches famous game minecraft.

During the Indie era i can remember all of the different games that came out and this one amoung the many that have faded back into the echos of history this one still resonates with me. Perhaps cause it was the first i came across and it dazzled me at first with its different graphic set which by the way outdated in this era is a nice departure from the heavy and extremely overly detailed and Memory consuming games is a nice change of pace as the practice of less is more is a legitimate practice in the gaming industry.

However there are flaws such as lack of other game modes as the survival mode dosn't satisfy the secondary game modes that are provided though it is good for some time killing if need be. and the Story is rather slow at first because the game breaks down its story into sections where your not told the entire story until you progress through the game, which very much reminds me of how some novels work out, if anything the story plays out as a first-person perspective novel. just you can pilot a tank and interact with the game and see everything that is narrated in the story.

Whilst i wouldn't recommend this game to your average gamer i still like the game too much to not recommend it to anyone who is bored with the modern formulaic game play of most FPS games, it works as a nice departure from the current trends of the gaming market and brings you back to a time when the gaming industry was a more primal and pioneering.

For me its a legacy game that i enjoy to this day and whenever i get a chance that isn't spent on other games i enjoy i always find myself starting a new playthrough on a different difficulty setting

Space Ark :
Note : 4,5/5
Space Ark est un casse-brique mais avec des particularités bien à lui. La "balle" est ici un animal qui rebondit sur une sorte de trampoline. Tant qu'il est dans les airs, vous pouvez le diriger dans sa phase ascendante ou descendante. Du coup, sous ses airs très mignons, très kawaï, le joueur doit faire preuve d'une dextérité redoutable car il faut à la fois diriger la trampoline et la "balle". De plus, vous ne devez pas vraiment casser les briques mais plutôt en toucher un maximum à chaque passage. Et chaque level vous impose non seulement de toucher toutes les briques, mais ne les comptent que si vous en touchez 3 ou plus. De surcroît, il vous impose un quota. Si l'un des deux critères n'est pas rempli, le niveau est perdu!
La maniabilité est bonne à la manette, la difficulté des levels est très progressive.
Space Ark s'adresse clairement aux compétiteurs et aux stratèges dans l'âme.Mais tout indiquait pourtant qu'il visait un public enfantin!  La musique est entraînante, les bruitages adorables, il y a des arcs-en-ciels et des étoiles un peu partout, les bouilles des animaux sont à tomber avec leurs grands yeux...
Mais si vous cherchez à récolter toutes les médailles d'or (et je ne vous parle même pas des succès Steam) , il va falloir sacrément vous motiver! Et vous arracher des touffes de cheveux en pagaille... Car en plus de sa difficulté présente, Space Ark est bugué. Déjà le jeu se lance uniquement en mode fenêtre. La case plein écran est bien là dans les options de démarrage, mais elle est grisée. Cela n'empêche en aucune façon de jouer mais nuit un peu à la visibilité. En plus du mode "campagne", il existe un mode time attack et survival. Là où ça ne passe pas, c'est que j'ai été éjecté du jeu par 2 fois après avoir terminé une série en time attack. Du coup, pas de médaille et l'obligation de recommencer la série au départ. J'ai vérifié sur le hub de la communauté Steam et je ne suis pas le seul. Après tant d'année depuis la publication du jeu, ce n'est pas acceptable. D'autant que le jeu vous invite réellement à progresser pour débloquer des niveaux dans les 3 modes, ce n'est pas comme un jeu de flipper où on choisit une table ou une autre par exemple. C'est vraiment dommage car on remarque bien via les menus de sélection qu'il y a une bonne durée de vie!
En conclusion, Space Ark a réellement tout pour plaire et pour toutes ces qualités, je lui une bonne note. Attention, il se destine à un public vétéran des casse-briques. 
Malheureusement, son bug de progression en fait un jeu pas tout à fait fini, qu'un simple patch aurait pu solutionner! Et donc, je ne peux le recommander.

The problem is, author F. Scott Fitzgerald didn't see the Jazz Age as all about hip music and sparkly clothes. He associated the entire period with materialism ("I want things! Lots of things!") and immorality. For many of the post-World War I era's newly wealthy, materialism and immortality were the name of the game. The novel's star is Jay Gatsby, a young, rich man in love with a society girl from his past. A girl who, as it happens, is married to someone else.

And that's not the only reason why Gatsby still feels fresh today. The novel's very title has become a kind of buzzword for periods of excess and fake luxury. The economic collapse of 2008 brought back distant and unwelcome memories of the stock market crash of 1929, casting the boom times of the 1990s and early 2000s as the modern-day version of the Roaring Twenties.

In both cases, though, unsustainable boom times led to devastating crashes with profound cultural consequences. In the 1920s, it had been a bubble in stocks that brought easy prosperity, while in our own time the bubble had been in the housing market. In both times, easy money meant that many people could begin to dream of living out their days like Jay Gatsby, with life as just one grand party in a seersucker suit. But as that vision of easy luxury crashed and burned (in both 1929 and 2008), newfound hard times required a redefinition of the American Dream.

And while Gatsby is a work of fiction, Fitzgerald's real life contains some suspicious similarities. (Gulp.) Narrator Nick Carraway is both mesmerized and disgusted by Gatsby's extravagant lifestyle, just as Fitzgerald claimed to feel about the "Jazz Age" excesses that he himself adopted. As an Ivy League educated, middle-class Midwesterner, Fitzgerald (like Nick) saw through the shallow materialism of the era. But (like Gatsby) Fitzgerald came back from World War I and fell in love with a wealthy southern socialite.

So I got this as part of an indie bundle of 8 other games for $1.50, and upon looking at the store page, I became worried.

Barely touched on steam for two and a half years and already had mixed reviews, I approached this game today with caution. The opening was cute. I liked the pop-art style intro. It reminded me of something like Little Big Planet.

Then I saw those things up close.
Those...creepy, soulless eyes...begging to die.

Space Ark is basically an Arkanoid game (hooray for puns), where you bounce your Little Big Planet knockoffs around and about hitting objects this game calls "DNA" and  helping these creatures restore there planets to its (un)rightful glory.

I was very skeptical about how this game would be, especially with how the screenshots were kind of a turnoff. But honestly, this game wasn't too bad. In fact it got a little challenging, because not only are you controlling your yoga ball around the stage, but you also have control in navigating your sock puppets that you call "animals."

Granted, it's not as challenging as other arkanoid games that you can find here on steam, such as Ionball, but if you like to have color in your environment and like bouncing up and down cute...soulless...evil...creatures, then you'll enjoy this game.

Though at a price tag of $5, I say wait, look for a sale, or look somewhere else.
This game is worth no more than your typical dollar app, and shouldn't be priced any higher than that.

Other than that, I (personally) can't recommend this game to anyone I know that is into arkanoid but likes this type of theme.

p.s. This game cannot be played at full screen, so that's another thing to note about.

Both widescreen and controller enabled, Space Ark is a game that every indie fan should own.

Eternity's Child is an indie platformer made by unknown studio Silver Sphere. The story revolves around... I don't know. The game starts with an intro in form of wall of text that is scrolling, and it's scrolling pretty fast, you won't get enough time to read it.

So, let's speak about the story as how I felt it through the gameplay. You're something between bunny and elf, with emo bat-elf friend who is shooting laser balls. You are jumping through unique grotesque world full of weird mechanical enemies that are evil. To save the world, to get a heart of your lovely bat-elf and... whatever, you just collect gems with your girlfriend and shoot at mechs.

Let's talk about gameplay. It's praiseworthy the developers put their time into their own engine but it's not much praiseworthy that it plays terrible. You control movement with keyboard, shooting with mouse, nothing surprising, but the whole movement and jumping feels bad - you are now sure of platform edges and objects react with a lag.

Though the game is not even finished (and don't expect it'll ever be), it offers several levels that will make you ask your conscience for not doing anything else. It also has a level editor (beta), but I must admit, I didn't dare to try it.

If Eternity's Child was supposed to be an art project (with removed gameplay), it could end up being pretty nice and interesting "experience". The environment feels weird but that's definitely something positive I can tell about the game. Sadly, there is also some confusing visual design on places - there'll be too many things on the screen and you won't be sure what's supposed to be platform (to jump on) and what's just on the background.

[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
Overall, this is one of the worst platformers I've played lately, it has terrible gameplay and unfinished content. Unique visual style can't save it when everything else is bad. Don't even think about buying it.

This game is a love letter to every wannabe game designer who's played Mario and completely missed what makes it such a brilliant game. The jump physics are floaty and hard to control. The camera is sticky and often forces you into leaps of faith. Platforms are arranged with no rhyme or reason, and it's often visually ambiguous where you can stand and where you can't. Enemy AI makes no sense: sometimes swarms of enemies will gleefully dive-bomb you from off screen, and other times the same enemy types will sit perfectly still, ignoring you as you shoot them. You have health, but levels are mostly made up of insta-death pits. The story mocks itself and the game's arbitrary mechanics right from the first level. Even more embarrassingly, the first thing you see in the game is the fact that two-thirds of the game's content (the second and third acts) are listed as "Coming soon!", despite the game having been released seven years ago (as I write this). Looks pretty but impossible to play with the awful controls.  It's broken in its current state and should be removed from Steam until fixed.  I wish I could have my money back.

It's a nice game and has some interesting ideas like the very complex and badly explained shooting mechanics which allow for about 5 different kinds of bullets. The enemies are very overwhelming and hard to kill which is only more frustrating when you have to worry about dificult platforming. The level sometimes glitches out and doesn't end so you are stuck there until you lose all your lives.

I would have liked more context. Every level seems to be be "collect 2 gems" having no idea why collecting a gem is worth risking your life against a hundred enemies. It's a very pretty world made with a lot of care but I would apreciate it more if I felt I was doing something there.

It's also impossible to tell if you are damaging an enemy or they are immortal. Some enemies will follow you forever and take about 30 seconds to kill so you are forced to shoot anything you encounter for at least 30 seconds to find out if they can be killed. It is also very unfair since enemies will pop out of the ground beneath you making their attacks undodgeable and the platforming often has very little logic to it meaning a lot of trial and error and cheap deaths.

It's not unplayable but there are too many issues for me to recommend it.

This game is just plain awful. 
I really don't recommend this game. It's basically unfished it even has levels in the games code that were never used. 
The problem with this game is that they sold this with the promise of more content in the future. Then completely backed out and left this game unfished. There are actually menu options for these chapters and they're just blank. 
Essentially Luc Bernard sold us a game in beta and never finished it. Imagine buying a game in early access to then have the developer announce they weren't going to finish the game and just left you all with a buggy beta mess.

Of course you ask: "But what of the content that is in the game?"
It's... average at best. The level design is not interesting at all and all levels are just "find 3 gems and get to the exit." If that sounds boring it's because it is. There is no story in this game save for some scrolling of text and then some poorly written, and unfunny banter between the two main characters in the game. I spoke to Luc Bernard about this before in the past, when his game had just been release and he claimed that the game was going to have a deeper story but his collegue thought it was "too cheesy" and so they dropped it. Oh wonderful.
The combat is mostly just shooting some rather bland enemies with boring designs and poorly coded AI. Hell there is a robot bird enemy in this game that will stop chasing you or attacking you if you move past his "activation point."

I hear what you're saying: "But this game is just so gosh damn beautiful." 
Absolutely. Excluding the poor monster design Luc Bernard has done some rather pretty artwork. But it's all ruined by the awful sprites. The beautiful mind that is Luc Bernard chose to stick with ragdoll physics instead of actual animation. 
Oh speaking of physics! Do you like falling damage in your 2D side scrolling platform games? Because Eternity's Child has it. 

So to sum up.
-Painfully average level designs
-Below average gameplay
-Mixed presentation
-Unfinished game 

Is it worth it for the price? No. Absolutely not. Don't even give this man money because he doesn't deserve it. 
Use your money to buy a better game on Steam. Because there are loads more better indie platformers and other games.

I never thought I'd play a modern video game that reminded me of Action 52, but here it is.
I don't even know where to start with this terribly unfinished game. First: Who are these characters? What is going on with the story? IS there a story?? I found there is supposed to be a plain text crawl explaining the story & characters of this game (a lazy move on part of the designers there, one of many), but when the game starts, there is no such thing. Everything you do has no context as to why you're doing it. The bubbles that slowly describe the game's few controls on the first stage are so slow that you're trying to read these things as you're endlessly shooting stuff that wants to fly right into your face and at weird angles, even for a platformer. 
The controls are a total mess, you slide off platforms if you don't angle your blurry jumps just so, if you can see where you're jumping that is. The camera likes to stick on your character's position in such a way that you are often jumping blindly into who knows what, more likely than not, it's something that will kill you. Jumping is iffy at best with having to learn the trick to getting a decent jump without slipping off edges or even getting to a higher up platform. This would be fine if there was a way to grab platform edges, there isn't.
I don't understand the point of having two characters to worry about if the one you actually move doesn't do anything else but that, the flying girl shoots at enemies & nothing else. This is really unnecessary & could have been done better with just one character doing these things.
Many, many sections of the game, both while playing & in the menus, appears to be either really buggy, unfinished, or both. I'm betting on both. Even for an episodic game (which I can see why the sub-sequent chapters never saw daylight), there should have better effort on cleaning this game up, at least so someone knows wtf is going on when they start playing. Again, an intro would have been nice here. Another odd happening is that I got a totally different level 3 on later playthroughs, sometimes happening before I was done in the last area. No warning, just a new level out of nowhere. I even fell through solid walls a few times.
I can say good things about the art style of this game, it's vibrant, pretty to look at & a gothic sort of cute. It's pretty much ruined by the camera motions & animation style they used in this game; very bland, lifeless & marionette-like. Plenty of other games pull off a 2-D world with life & emotion, why didn't this game?

Seriously, save your money. Maybe buy this as a gag gift for a friend if it's on sale for $1. Try the buggy demo, but do -not- pay money for this disappointing and unfinished fragment of a game.

Years after purchasing it, I still feel burned by this game. Don't let the fabulous artwork fool you, this game will bore you, infuriate you, or both, depending on your patience level. Also, if you're like and thought the story sounded intriguing, know that it's barely present and features deeply pretentuous, unengaging writing that will have you ignoring it pretty rapidly. 

It's rare to see an indie game this disastrous actually get released. What's galling is that with a lot of polish it could have been something special, but it feels like the designers ran out of time, money, or patience and just threw it into the marketplace.

No matter what you're looking for, this game will disappoint you.

[h1]仙境不是童话，是爱丽丝的创伤解离幻境[/h1]
真正疯狂的是这个世界。
闲暇之余花16h过完一周目，我随爱丽丝游历了她的仙境，只不过，地狱这个词更适合用来形容本作爱丽丝的精神世界。用掉脑袋切切切开如人心般黑色的虫子，喷涌而出的鲜血夹杂着爱丽丝复仇的渴望，十余年精神病院的折磨摧残着她，亲人与真相一同被当年的大火烧尽，留给爱丽丝的是灰烬、绝望和无尽的苦痛。正如同维多利亚时期，女性、创伤幸存者、孤儿面临的困境，“疯人院”不是疗愈场所，而是人间地狱。假如一个人是医生、是绅士，那他可以随意为患者贴上“歇斯底里、精神失常”的标签，通过催眠、暴力手段篡改、抹除病人记忆。游戏中“歇斯底里”模式便是对此的讽刺，当年的医学界将女性情绪苦痛定义成一种病，而在这里，反倒成了爱丽丝不可磨灭的意志带来的反抗力量。放到当下延伸：它质疑了一个问题--[b]谁有权定义你是不是疯了？谁有权决定你该忘掉什么？[/b]

娃娃屋的设计是我认为本作最精妙的地图设计，麻辣马很好地通过家具等环境细节设计，将孩子们（幻境中玩偶）的精神苦痛表现出来。关于东方地图的元素同样令人惊喜，我完全没有想到中国的皮影戏能够完美与本作融合，每个地图主题都有独特的玩法，强大的游戏设计创新力放在现在也是一股清流。战斗、解密和跳跳乐大约各占三分之一，关于跳跳乐，有些地方可能略有卡脚，但多尝试几次总能过。本作总体瑕不掩瑜，大部分内容上，工作室已经做到了最好，作为一个老游戏，放到当下给我的震撼依旧不减。

其他不多赘述，相信每个玩家都能在体验过后有不同的感悟。用柴郡猫结尾处一句话结束：“只有野蛮人才把痛苦的忍耐力作为价值衡量，忘记疼痛很容易，记住，会令人十分痛苦。

但重获真理是值得忍受磨难的。”

10 из 10. Все еще отличнейшая игра, достаточно разнообразная и интересная, с уникальным внешним видом и хорошим геймдизайном. Кому-то могут показаться душными некоторые места, но это норма для такой игры.

Каждый уровень разнообразен и отражает шизу Алисы, особенно круто что это отражается через платье. Новые враги появляются даже на последних уровнях, каждый со своими особенностями. Очень много секретов, большинство из которых довольно сложно найти. Достаточно простая боевка, которая идеально вписывается в игру.

К сожалению, у игры очень странные технические проблемы на сегодняшний день. Помню, как проходил ее лет десять назад и не помню ни зависаний ни вылетов. Но сейчас даже с установкой фиксов от коммьюнити, все равно есть зависания, вылеты и очень странные баги управления, распространяющиеся даже на геймпад. Увы. Можно играть только лишь если готов терпеть эти неудобства, но саму игру они не делают хуже.

American McGee, que mente deliciosamente perturbada você tem!

Alice no País das Maravilhas sempre foi uma das minhas histórias favoritas. Existe algo maravilhoso em um universo tão absurdo que permite a diferentes artistas explorarem sua criatividade sem praticamente nenhum limite.
E então temos American McGee, que aparentemente olhou para toda aquela fantasia e pensou: "Sabe o que está faltando aqui? Trauma."
E QUE GENIALIDADE!
Alice: Madness Returns é uma interpretação grotesca, melancólica e absolutamente fascinante desse universo. Aqui, o País das Maravilhas não é apenas um lugar de criaturas excêntricas e acontecimentos impossíveis, mas também o reflexo de uma mente profundamente marcada pelo sofrimento.
Gosto de pensar que, enquanto a Alice de Tim Burton parecia estar prestes a explodir por trás de sua aparência delicada, a de American McGee já explodiu há muito tempo e agora está tentando recolher os próprios pedacinhos.
E a direção artística?
O jogo consegue transformar o grotesco em algo estranhamente belo. Os cenários são criativos, perturbadores e tão ricos em personalidade que eu me peguei admirando lugares que, em qualquer outra circunstância, me fariam querer chamar a vigilância sanitária.
O HOMEM CONSEGUIU ME FAZER GOSTAR DE UM MAPA FEITO DE VÍSCERAS. VÍSCERAS!
Isso não é apenas talento artístico, é algum tipo de feitiçaria que deveria ser estudada.
Outro detalhe que adoro é como Alice troca de vestido conforme avançamos pela história. Gosto de interpretar essas mudanças como representações visuais de sua jornada, acompanhando as diferentes etapas de seu amadurecimento e de sua tentativa de compreender a própria mente.
Sobre as armas...
Temos um moedor de pimenta que funciona como uma metralhadora, uma cabeça de cavalo gigante utilizada como marreta, uma chaleira que dispara projéteis explosivos e, é claro, a lendária Lâmina Vorpal.
É simplesmente magnífico!
Quem precisa de armamentos convencionais quando você pode resolver seus problemas psicológicos distribuindo pancadas com a cabeça de um cavalo de brinquedo?
E o melhor é que essas armas não existem apenas para serem bonitas. Alguns inimigos exigem abordagens específicas, incentivando o uso de diferentes equipamentos e tornando os combates mais variados e interessantes.
Os efeitos visuais também merecem elogios. Mesmo sendo um jogo de outra geração, Madness Returns continua impressionando pela criatividade e pelo cuidado com sua apresentação.
A narrativa, por sua vez, é um verdadeiro banquete para quem ama a obra original de Lewis Carroll. As referências estão por toda parte, reinterpretadas com uma dose generosa de horror psicológico, drama e melancolia.
E é justamente essa combinação que torna tudo tão especial.
O horror não está ali apenas para chocar. Ele ajuda a representar a dor, as memórias e a tentativa de Alice de compreender sua própria realidade.
É uma obra que consegue ser delicada e brutal, fantasiosa e cruel, bela e repulsiva ao mesmo tempo.

Veredito: American McGee pegou um dos universos mais fantásticos da literatura, mergulhou tudo em um pesadelo psicológico e conseguiu transformar o resultado em uma obra de arte.

My first time knowing about the existance of this series was playing Brothers in Arms 2: Global Front on my first smartphone back when I was a teen. More than a decade later, I finally experience the series proper, starting with Road to Hill 30 and completing it. I made my piece about Road to Hill 30, now its Earned in Blood's turn.

Unlike most sequels where the story of the 1st game straighaway continues in the 2nd, Earned in Blood's story is actually about the same with Road to Hill 30 where you were in the shoes of Sergeant Matt Baker. The difference this time is that the story is told from the perspective of Corporal (later Sergeant) Joseph "Red" Hartsock, one of Baker's team leaders and a bro. He tells a contrasting narrative to Baker's and like Baker's experience...the campaign ain't glorious for Red either. It's a story of a man who gradually understands the toll of being a squad leader after having issues with his leader's (Baker) ability to lead. Some victories...are earned in blood.

Gameplay wise, is pretty much the same as Road to Hill 30, where you command your teams to tackle the objective. Covering fire and flanking is the prime bread and butter tactic that applies in every situation. I notice that the AI has improved somewhat, as they seem to be smarter in avoiding fire and able to find the safest routes to the position you order them. As for the gunplay, thank God it's a vast improvement over Road to Hill 30. The breathing mechanic is present when aiming down sights, but the chances of your shots landing are significantly higher when compared to Road to Hill 30. I describe the gunplay of Road to Hill 30 as a stormtrooper simulator.  Seems like Red is a better shot than Baker lol.

Next, I find the difficulty of the missions are actually easier than the ones in Road to Hill 30...initially. Maybe it's because I am pretty used to the system that I found them much easier to do. However, around mid to late game, the difficulty spiked to the point where it's retty challenging, leading me to die alot just so I keep my squad alive. Despite my skill issue...I had my share of fun retrying to get the best result to proceed to the next checkpoint moreso than in the 1st game. The bros I lead are worth dying for.

I give Earned in Blood a 9/10. A classic FPS that is a must have for the WW2 buffs. That said, onward to Hell's Highway!

[h1]Brothers in Arms: Earned in Blood[/h1]

[hr][/hr]

[b]Brothers in Arms: Earned in Blood[/b] es un divertido y desafiante [i]shooter[/i] en primera persona ambientado en la Segunda Guerra Mundial, específicamente durante la campaña de Francia. A diferencia de muchos juegos bélicos de su época, este título apuesta por un enfoque táctico que obliga al jugador a pensar antes de actuar.

[h2]Jugabilidad[/h2]

El mayor atractivo del juego es su sistema de combate táctico. No basta con correr y disparar; es necesario coordinar a la escuadra, dar órdenes de supresión y ejecutar maniobras de flanqueo para derrotar al enemigo. Estas mecánicas están muy bien implementadas y continúan siendo el punto fuerte de la saga.

[h2]Lo bueno[/h2]

✔ Sistema táctico profundo y entretenido.
✔ Ambientación convincente de la Segunda Guerra Mundial.
✔ Enfrentamientos intensos que premian la estrategia.
✔ Mantiene la calidad de [i]Road to Hill 30[/i].

[h2]Lo no tan bueno[/h2]

✘ Presenta pocas novedades respecto a su predecesor.
✘ La campaña es relativamente corta.
✘ En algunos momentos la dificultad puede resultar frustrante.

[h2]¿Secuela o expansión?[/h2]

Aunque incorpora nuevas misiones y nos permite vivir la historia desde otra perspectiva, el juego no evoluciona demasiado respecto a [i]Brothers in Arms: Road to Hill 30[/i]. Por momentos se siente más como una gran expansión o un DLC que como una secuela completamente nueva.
