**Street Fighter IV – A Strong Return to Form**

Street Fighter IV marks a triumphant return for the iconic fighting franchise, blending classic elements with modern mechanics that cater to both veterans and newcomers. Released in 2008, this installment revitalized the series and brought the thrill of competitive fighting games back to the forefront, making it a noteworthy entry in the genre.

One of the most striking aspects of Street Fighter IV is its art style. The 3D character models, combined with hand-drawn backgrounds, create a visually captivating experience that stands out among fighting games. The vibrant colors and dynamic animations bring the characters to life, immersing players in the diverse worlds of each fighter. The presentation feels fresh while still honoring the franchise's roots, appealing to both long-time fans and newcomers alike.

The gameplay mechanics are another highlight. Street Fighter IV successfully integrates traditional gameplay with innovative features like the Focus Attack, which adds depth to combat and encourages strategic thinking. This mechanic allows players to absorb an opponent's attack and counterattack, offering new layers of strategy that enhance the fighting experience. The game also includes a robust roster of characters, each with unique moves and styles, ensuring that players can find a fighter that suits their playstyle.

The accessibility of Street Fighter IV is commendable. The introduction of a simpler control scheme allows new players to jump in without feeling overwhelmed, making it easier to enjoy the game’s depth. However, for seasoned players, the complexity of the traditional controls remains intact, ensuring that the competitive scene remains robust and challenging.

That said, the game isn’t without its flaws. Some players have noted that certain characters can feel overpowered or unbalanced in competitive play, which can lead to frustration during matches. Additionally, while the online multiplayer mode offers exciting competition, issues with matchmaking and lag can occasionally detract from the overall experience.

In conclusion, Street Fighter IV is a strong entry in the series that successfully blends classic gameplay with modern innovations. Its stunning visuals, engaging mechanics, and diverse character roster make it a compelling choice for fighting game enthusiasts. While it has its share of balance issues and online hiccups, the overall experience is enjoyable and rewarding. Whether you're a veteran of the franchise or a newcomer looking to dive into the world of fighting games, Street Fighter IV offers a satisfying experience that is well worth exploring.

I wanted to like this game. I promise. I really wanted to be the cool, niche gamer - playing the underrated gem but… I just couldn’t do it. This game has issues and it did not mesh with me.

[h1]NOT QUITE MY TEMPO[/h1]
Alright, let me put it down in plain text.

The swinging kinda sucks. I might be spoiled by the new Spider-Man games that have 10+ years of technology on Bionic Commando but I don’t think so. Swinging was fun on the PS2 Spider-Man games but here, it’s just lame.

When you reach the peak of a swing, the momentum vanishes jarringly, there's sometimes no anchor points for your hook after leaving a swing, and you can’t jump out of a swing to boost momentum. Perhaps there are upgrades later in the game but I didn’t get this far unfortunately.

The Capcom collectible bubble things also jarr me. I found one pretty soon after the intro and arm-collection cutscene and it kinda took me out of the immersion. A thin criticism but it’s how I felt nonetheless.

The combat was rough. I would zip to enemies that I’ve hooked, and then just ride them forward indefinitely, until the game decided I could let them go. There didn’t seem to be a ‘kick’ or ‘release’ button. Probably just a little glitch but this caused me a few deaths.

This isn’t an open world game and that’s fine. I don’t expect to be able to explore every corner of the city. But the world borders were too punishing on the hard difficulty. I’d swing or walk a literal [i]metre[/i] out of line, and the radiation symbol would pop up on my screen. Before I knew it, dead. I feel like it could use some tweaking.

Combat was also just finicky overall. I fought a few robot dudes, but without ammo for my guns. This means I had to awkwardly dance around them with the swinging, until I could kick them in the back. Even then, I still wasn’t really doing some damage and it was just lukewarm fun overall.

I can overlook lame combat if there’s a fun gimmick or immaculate vibes but for Bionic Commando, everything was just okay. It was all lukewarm and below.

[h1]THE STUFF I LIKED[/h1]
This game might have [b]the coolest menu known to man[/b]. I am not joking. The menu for Bionic Commando has very dangerous amounts of sauce.

It’s basically one of Doc Ock’s tentacles pointing directly at you, with the menu items (resume, options etc.) orbiting around it. You get to really satisfyingly point it at the options and when you confirm to proceed, the tentacle thing wriggles forward and you can still see the ring of the last menu in the background, further down the tentacle.

I’m honestly not doing it justice with my shoddy description, please look it up. Mind you, the menu has to be felt to be believed. It’s just so much fun to fiddle with. Maybe a weird thing to hyperfixate on but that’s me I’m afraid.

In retrospect, the menu definitely isn’t as iconic as Persona 5, as immersive as Fallout or as stylish as Batman Arkham Asylum’s pause menus… I like it though :)

Oh and one other thing I liked. I stopped at the bottom of a stairwell and could hear the guards upstairs talking as they hadn’t aggro’d yet. Very sweet touch that didn’t have to be in the game. It’s charming polish like that that can make crappy 7th gen games really survive the years.

[h1]SOZ[/h1]
Being a 17-year-old game, there’s a natural cult fanbase for this game. I read the other reviews - people who played it as a kid because the front cover looked cool in 2009 are enjoying it now for nostalgic reasons and that’s great. I will never try to take that away from anyone.

My favourite game is Gravity Rush and I know it wouldn’t be if I played it for the first time today. So while I can’t recommend picking up Bionic Commando, I respect its position in gaming history as that obscure swinging game for the 7th generation.

With 6 more months in the oven, I think this game could’ve been a bit of a classic hit. It’s just missing that base level of polish and flow that I was gasping for.

I’ll admit there’s probably more fun to be had if stuck at it and really got used to the swinging, but I’m just not willing to do that. My free time shrinks with each passing year and Bionic Commando didn’t hit those initial milestones for me. Sorry to the fans.

Maybe I’ll see you again one day my odd friend. Hopefully at GDQ.

Pour l'anecdote, en 2009, je me souviens des grandes affiches publicitaires dans le métro concernant ce jeu. Et bien que je ne me sois pas procuré le jeu par manque de temps et d'argent, j'étais toujours intrigué par ce titre qui me donnait envie d'y jouer.
Maintenant j'ai enfin pu y jouer et voir ce qu'il valait, et clairement, le moi de l'époque aurait probablement adoré ce jeu car, honnêtement, ce jeu est très bon.
Le vrai seul point négatif qui m'énerve est le didacticiel qui nous apprend toutes les fonctions et utilisations du bras mécanique, pour au final utiliser le bras que pour ce balancer et débloquer les autres techniques vers la moitié du jeu. C'est frustrant car c'est clairement le cœur du gameplay ! Attraper un ennemi et le lancer au loin, ou attraper des voitures et les projeter sur des ennemis plus puissants change littéralement la donne du combat et évite de trop utiliser l'arsenal qui, de base, n'est pas très fourni en munitions. D'ailleurs, il n'y a que peu d'infos concernant l'utilisation de certaines armes.
L'histoire est clairement nanard et certains personnages n'ont que très peu de temps d'écran pour apprendre à les connaître.
Mais comme je l'ai dit plus tôt, c'est un très bon jeu de plateforme-aventure qui aurait mérité de continuer sur cette lancée, surtout maintenant quand on voit certains jeux bac à sable qui jouissent d'une grande liberté d'exploration et d'action. Recommended. A grapple-first third-person action game where a bionic arm serves as movement, melee and tool at once, and where superb swinging traversal outweighs imprecise targeting and a cheap late-game difficulty wall.

Swinging through Ascension City remains delightful throughout, and combat rewards creativity: enemies die to thrown corpses, punched objects and zip kicks layered over conventional pistol, shotgun and RPG gunplay. Collectible dossiers build genuinely interesting faction lore, and the corridors stay short enough that the air between them matters more.

Grapple targeting locks onto everything, so zip kicks meant for soldiers latch onto the ground beside them, and late-game swarms, energy-throwing biomechs and a worm boss with a lengthy redo on failure feel like padding. No final boss arrives, just a climb from Vulture to Vulture. Judge it as a movement game first and it outperforms its reputation.

Supuestamente el juego es una secuela de un juego lanzado en 1995 para Nintendo, pero esta vez la historia se cuenta 10 años después de lo sucedido en el primer título: 

Nuestro protagonista es Nathan Spencer, el primer Bionic commando de una empresa militar llamada T.A.S.C. que se dedica al desarrollo de soldados de tecnología biónica. Spencer tiempo atrás desobedeció órdenes directas en una misión que resulto en la muerte de varios agentes de T.A.S.C., por lo que fue acusado de traición en una corte marcial y sentenciado a muerte.
Con el paso del tiempo varias organizaciones con trabajo en la tecnología biónica comenzaron a tener conflictos entre sí, por lo que se resolvió bajo una directiva presidencial política terminar con los programas de soldados biónicos bajo el lema "bionic purge". T.A.S.C. fue cerrada, pero muchos de sus agentes escaparon en lugar de entregar sus tecnologías biónicas.
Tras una paz de 5 años se produjo un atentado con bombardeos radioactivos sobre la ciudad de Ascensión City por parte de fuerzas terroristas, nuestro viejo amigo Joseph Gibson miembro de la F.S.A. (protagonista del primer juego) y quien metió en cana a Spencer, pero hoy consejero militar, decide ir a buscar y reclutar a Spencer para enviarlo a las ruinas a investigar a cambio de perdonar su condena y dar con el paradero de su esposa desaparecida... El juego al terminar deja un final abierto, secuela que veo que capcom no esté muy interesado en desarrollar porque sigue robando con remakes de resident evil.

Francamente es un título ya viejo, no es un juego malo, ni un juego bueno, Pero se ve lindo gráficamente y la mecánica de balanceo del personaje es fluida e intuitiva lo que hace que el juego sea divertido, un par de logros en Steam no hubieran estado nada mal para darle alguna rejugabilidad y ponerse a buscar todos los coleccionables.

Le studio GRIN, fermé au moment de la sortie du titre, n'a clairement pas eu l'intention de réinventer la roue niveau histoire, celle-ci reste assez basique mais en ce sens, elle est fidèle à l'esprit de l'époque où est née la licence, les années 80's, le cadre est vite posé et ça va droit au but, le tout avec naturellement une mise en scène plus ambitieuse et une très bonne narration visuelle à mon sens.
Ils ont réussi également à super bien adapter Bionic Commando à la 3D et même si le temps est passé, je trouve de mon côté que l'utilisation du grappin reste super fun et procure des sensations grisantes, le déblocage de nouvelles capacités au fil de la progression ne fait qu'accroître le plaisir donné par la partie action/plateforme de l'œuvre.

J'ai toujours autant de bons souvenirs quand je repense à ce Bionic Commando, le gameplay, des passages et niveaux, ainsi que plein de bruitages et musiques qui me sont resté en tête et chaque nouvelle partie me confirme les raisons de tout ça.

Bionic Commando è un action TPS molto particolare che si regge quasi interamente su una sola idea: il braccio bionico e la mobilità basata sulle oscillazioni.

Il gameplay è sicuramente il punto più riuscito del gioco. Muoversi tra gli edifici, lanciarsi, afferrare oggetti e usarli come armi crea un sistema di combattimento diverso dal classico sparatutto in terza persona. La distruzione ambientale e alcune situazioni scriptate ben costruite danno anche momenti abbastanza memorabili.

Tuttavia, il gioco mostra diversi limiti. I controlli non sono sempre precisi e il sistema di aggancio del braccio richiede pratica, con alcune situazioni in cui la risposta non è perfettamente affidabile. Anche il comparto tecnico non è sempre solido, con animazioni, collisioni e IA non sempre convincenti.

Le armi sono la parte funzionale ma chiaramente secondaria rispetto al braccio, mentre alcune missioni risultano ripetitive nel lungo periodo. La storia è poco incisiva e i personaggi non sono particolarmente sviluppati, rendendo la narrazione meno interessante rispetto al gameplay.

In generale, è un titolo con un’idea forte ma non sempre rifinito nella sua esecuzione.

Only got because it was in a bundle with Rearmed, which was the same price (or lower I think actually) as the game by itself. I came in with an open mind, knowing how infamous this is, while also hearing some say that the swinging mechanics were actually kinda good, but no, this game doesn't feel that polished, the combat feels pretty lackluster. There's not even an aim button, so the shooting kinda feels unfocused and a bit inprecise, and it also doesn't feel like a real gun, more like a toy with how it feels and sounds. The combat with the arm isn't that much better, either, just some basic punch attacks and a zip attack which is kinda neat. The swinging is fine, but also pretty unrefined. Honestly, I'd say it kinda feels like a prototype from like months to a year from completion or a game made by someone who was described what an action adventure shooter game was from a game of telephone. Oh, and a minor issue I had is there's no keyboard and mouse controls, so I couldn't map my controller's gyro to the mouse for gyro aim. Then there's the story, the most infamous part, yeah, it feels like it's trying way too hard to be tough and edgy, that it just feels shallow. There's a reason everyone made fun of the wife arm. However, I felt like the ideas presented would have been a good translation of Bionic Commando into 3D if properly fleshed out. With Capcom reviving some dormant franchises, I'd actually like to see them take another try at this, just tone down the edge and make it feel more like the Rearmed games.

Эта игра от ныне покойной студии GRIN - один из самых недооцененных экшенов эпохи Xbox 360 и PS3. В 2026 году она все еще остается уникальным «симулятором человека-паука с пушкой», аналогов которому по физике перемещения практически нет.

Механика крюка: Это то, ради чего стоит играть. В отличие от большинства игр, где крюк-кошка - это просто телепорт к точке, здесь честная физика маятника. Ты должен чувствовать инерцию, вовремя отпускать трос и закручивать прыжки. Когда ловишь ритм и пролетаешь над пропастью между небоскребами, не касаясь земли, - это чистый восторг.

Вертикальный геймплей: Дизайн уровней в разрушенном Асценшн Сити заставляет тебя постоянно смотреть вверх. Битвы происходят в трех плоскостях: ты можешь притянуться к врагу, зашвырнуть в него автомобиль или обрушиться сверху мощным ударом.

Брутальность и импакт: Спенсер ощущается тяжелым и мощным. Твоя бионическая рука - это не только транспорт, но и смертоносное оружие. Возможность схватить кусок бетона и запустить его в вертолет или использовать врага как живой снаряд дает отличное чувство превосходства.

Графика и масштаб: Для 2009 года игра выглядела монументально. Огромные затопленные кварталы, гигантские роботы-боссы и эффекты частиц до сих пор смотрятся достойно благодаря хорошему арт-дирекшну.

Почему 8 из 10 (Сюжетный поворот): История Натана Спенсера довольно клишированная, а финальный твист про «личность» его руки вызвал у игроков в свое время либо нервный смех, либо полное недоумение. Это был смелый, но очень странный сценарный ход.

Линейность и ограничения: Несмотря на кажущийся простор, игра жестко наказывает за попытку уйти в сторону. Радиационные зоны - это невидимые стены, которые убивают тебя за пару секунд, что немного портит ощущение свободы полета.

Итог: Это хардкорный и механически глубокий экшен. К управлению нужно привыкнуть, но как только ты освоишь крюк, игра раскроется как один из самых драйвовых боевиков своего времени.

[h1]Un juego con grandes ideas pero que se queda a medio camino[/h1]

Bionic Commando es, en muchos sentidos, un título que se siente como "uno más del montón". Tenía un potencial enorme que no se llegó a aprovechar del todo; aunque tiene momentos épicos y escenas memorables, estos son demasiado escasos para el conjunto del juego. En general es divertido, pero la estructura se vuelve bastante repetitiva con el paso de las horas.

Uno de sus puntos más fuertes es la dificultad. Es un juego que no te regala nada y llega a ser muy desafiante por momentos, algo que los jugadores veteranos agradecerán. En cuanto a la duración, tiene un punto medio equilibrado, aunque su nula rejugabilidad hace que sea una experiencia de una sola pasada.

En términos generales no es un mal juego, pero tampoco llega a ser notable. A mí, dentro de todo, me gustó y me entretuvo, pero queda en la decisión de cada uno si adquirirlo o dejarlo pasar. Si lo encuentras en oferta, puede valer la pena para experimentar su mecánica del brazo biónico, pero ve con las expectativas moderadas.

Bionic Commando (2009) is pretty funny, even though it feels like it takes itself too seriously. It’s unclear if that was intentional or not, but either way it ends up being hilarious. There are a ton of F-bombs and a lot of different tropes that make it kind of entertaining in a weird way.

It’s also funny how a lot of the NPCs are on a first-name basis with the protagonist. They say “I’m going to F*** You up Spencer” all the time, like they have a personal gripe with him, and something about that just lands.

The game runs pretty well overall, but it does feel kind of janky, especially with the grappling. There are moments where the character gets stuck on a wall trying to jump off, and won’t unlatch unless the game is paused. Not sure if that’s user error or the game, but it happens more than once.

Combat actually feels really good at times. Headshots make that clean “ding” sound that’s super satisfying, and the sniper getting one-shot kills just feels great every time. It’s also super cool being able to grab soldiers with the bionic arm and toss them off cliffs.

The ‘90s action movie ridiculousness really stands out. The pacing is well done, it doesn’t take long to complete, and it never overstays its welcome. There’s also that old-school vibe where it feels like every main bad guy is European.

The character model from the tutorial would have been a better choice, more like the older Spencer from Bionic Commando Rearmed with the red hair and cool sunglasses. That version looks way better than the one with dreads in this game.

Originally picked up alongside Bionic Commando Rearmed for just $3.51 total for both games. 

I got the platinum trophy on PS3 back in 2010, and coming back for that nostalgic hit does not disappoint. The PC version looks phenomenal after all these years. It’s surprising there aren’t Steam achievements in this one.

A remake would actually be really interesting, especially if it leaned into a more fluid swinging style like the Insomniac Spider-Man games. Capcom feels like a perfect fit for that kind of gameplay, and it would be great to see them explore that concept. 

Overall, it’s a mix of janky gameplay, ‘90s action tropes, and unintentionally funny moments, but that kind of makes it memorable.

I honestly can't recommend this game. It triggers some nostalgia, kind of reminds me of the era of games like gears of war, but that's it. I can't even play the games I used to love anymore because the standard has been raised so much and my patience has dwindled along with that. Nowadays, video games are held to strict standards in both story, gameplay and graphics, all these old tropes of "hardened army dude doing army dude stuff and being uppity and hardcore and cracking bad jokes" are so overdone that people couldn't possibly be more tired of them. This is the kind of crap I'd expect to see from a low budget cheap movie rather than a decent game.

I didn't have any issues with phasing through stuff but the bionic arm mechanic feels clunky and the combat couldn't be more boring, it feels like there's no skill involved whatsoever, just button mashing. It just doesn't feel like smooth gameplay and has some weird relics of past games where you pick up ammo and stuff floating off the ground, which really just looks ugly. You can't even pick up other guns and after just half an hour I tired of the grappling mechanic and very few things you can do with it. It doesn't even look cool, kinda silly that everything this half machine army dude has is legs that can jump high and fall from high places and an arm that is basically just a childrens grappling toy powered up, couldn't they have added other mechanics to the arm, like built in firearms, bombs, firethrowers or whatever the hell else? But no, it just grapples, pulls and throws.

I don't see many people enjoying this kind of game nowadays, it's more akin to something a kid would enjoy around 1995-2010, not even children would bother with this game due to its bad story and piss poor mechanics when there are so many games that flow much smoother and is a joy to play.

Of course, not saying every more modern game prevails at everything, but at least they tend to be awesome when it comes to 1-2 things, like graphics being beautiful, mechanics flowing great and gameplay being fun or the story being immersive. This game fails at everything, choppy dialogue, extremely boring 2D-esque characters, bad art (when it was released it was ok though), clunky and messy controls/mechanics and it's not even cool.

Maybe some people would appreciate it for what it is or go back to play it for nostalgia's sake, but I would actually recommend people planning to play it again for nostalgia to leave it alone, I've made the mistake of playing games I loved as a kid again and hating them now because they actually sucked by today's standard, sometimes it's better to leave things in the past and not ruin the memory you had of the great times you had as a kid.

I have a love/hate relationship with this game.

First, I'm not recommending anyone buy this game; I will give my feelings on the game itself below, but the most important thing you must know is that the game is very unlikely to run as-is on any modern machine. It will very likely crash to desktop. I had a few false starts downloading different old drivers, and then finally got it running after finding an altered game executable elsewhere that doesn't break due having more than 4 cpus. It's pretty unacceptable that Capcom continues selling this game in a broken state.

Now for the actual game.

I love that they reimagined a classic NES title that already had a unique mechanic (no jumping, movement is only possible for grappling claw techniques), and iterated on it, creating an intricate and both frustrating and satisfying movement system, while retaining much of the original game's charm. The grappling takes some getting used to, but once it starts clicking it becomes really cool moving through levels. The boss fights are generally more like hazardous puzzles which makes them interesting (at least the first time, there are some repeats with small tweaks). I appreciate that they removed much of the confusing stuff from the NES game, which I think caused a lot of people back then to write it off as too difficult.

But there's problems. Lots of times the game's movement and physics feel rather janky. You can occasionally attach to surfaces that don't seem like they should work, and when the game has to decide if you should land on a surface or not because you are super close it feels like it can be a coin flip. I actually had the game crash to desktop once because i tried moving around some moving platforms and my assumption is that there was too much going on for the game to decide where to put me. The fact that enemies all respawn when you re-enter rooms feels unnecessarily rude, and hazards, while not instantaneous death, are often extremely punishing and for the most part just kill you without a way to recover in two hits instead of one.

One part that I found both fun and frustrating were the challenges. They were fun when they helped you learn a new way to move around, or when you know what to do and want to get lower times. But some are sufficiently complicated and require quite a bit of experimentation or at times what feels like luck to even complete, let alone set a good time on.

Overall, the game has aged okay, but you'll need tons of patience to make it through to the end. But like I said before, don't buy it unless you are willing to sign up for some extra work to even run the game first.

I completed Bionic Commando Rearmed on Windows 11. I encourage you to read this review if you intend to do the same, as it [b]does not launch properly on Windows 11[/b].
[h3]WINDOWS 11 NOTES[/h3]
After installing, the game will silently crash on launch, without even citing an error.
Doing the following two things fixed it for me:
1: Install legacy NVidia PhysX drivers which the game relies upon.
The following link should take you to NVidia's site.
https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/physx/9_10_0224/physx-9-10-0224-driver/
I have seen other users use up to version 9-13 as well.

2: Restart your computer -- Mine did not work until I restarted after the install.

3: Write over the game's installed EXE with a patched version.
The file is hosted on a Google Drive (use at your own risk, but I experienced no problems):
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1C7cJgaaf5-NQ1iqbRiHCm7Oot21LE2KS/view
This patched EXE will also fix some issues that prevent the hacking minigame from working properly on high-resolution monitors.

[h3]REVIEW[/h3]
I did not play this in co-op, and I doubt any of my friends would be interested. Might be fun, hard to say.
To be frank, as I finished Bionic Commando Rearmed, I started feeling more negatively toward it. But I'll give it a very shaky thumbs up because it's got the job of adapting jank NES gameplay to modern controllers. It was always gonna be weird. And once I got used to the game's controls, I did find myself having a lot of fun with mechanics that felt novel, particularly compared to today's games which often follow the same cookie-cutter solutions for game mechanics.
If you're a fan of mechanical novelty, it might be worth a play for you. But my recommendation still comes with caveats.

This game was an early XBox Live Arcade title for the 360, and I was actually working at Microsoft when it was in testing there, so I heard a bit about it from testers. I heard mixed reviews. Perhaps it was for nostalgia of that time that I wanted to go back and finally give it a shot.

First getting into it, the first thing you'll notice is the dated visuals. It looks better than an NES game, and the 2D art for the portraits is surprisingly good, but the tiling textures and basic lighting don't really hold up.
The next thing you'll notice is the odd controls, It may be a turnoff at first. "Guys are shooting me and I can't JUMP over the bullet?? You may think you have to face-tank the shots, and the game will generously provide you with HP from killed enemies, so you can get through most of the game this way. But you can actually deflect bullets with your robo-arm.
I did begin enjoying the novelty of the robo-arm mechanics. At first it feels unnecessarily picky and awkward to use. But once you get the hang of it, you can be surprisingly nimble. This is where the game actually shines -- but you'll need to train and abandon some of your expectations.

The real problems of this game come with the combination of jank and precision-difficulty. This is particularly noticeable in some of the new content in the form of dozens of challenge chambers. At first these are breezy and fun to speedrun to hone your grappling skills. I actually imagined I would grind through them all to get 5 stars, because I was having fun!
But as you continue to play them and unlock more, you'll find that a lot of the levels seem to rely on jank and techniques that you'd never intuit, and are certainly never tutorialized. I'm pretty hardcore about my games and I frankly just gave up on them and I still couldn't tell you how they're even possible. Not because of the skill required, but because I literally have no idea how they could work mechanically. Now, it's possible that even if I knew how these were supposed to be done, they'd be too hard for me and I'd give up. But as it stands I wasn't learning from failure. It was just confusing as to what I was supposed to do!

The final level is a long and punishing slog, punctuated by a bossfight that must be won in a very specific way which is not taught very clearly. This sorta colored the whole experience and made me almost leave a negative review. Fans of the original will also complain that the final level really diverges from the original, so it fails on that front as well.

The rest of the content is serviceable. Varied level designs. Each boss is presented twice, and is harder the second time. You get quite a few guns and they're pretty unique. Tons of secrets that I didn't find. If you like this game there's a lot to do. For me, I was happy to put it down once I beat my skull through the final bossfight.

Right click on Bionic Commando Rearmed in your Steam games list. Hover over manage, then click browse local files. A file explorer window will pop open. Locate bcr.exe in that file explorer window and right click it. Click on properties. Now click on the compatibility tab. Check the box that says "run this program in compatibility mode for:" and select Windows XP Service Pack 3. Click apply. Click the button below that says "change high DPI settings." Check the box that says "Override high DPI scaling behavior." Choose "application" from the dropdown menu. Click okay. Then click apply and okay. The game should now work. Launch it and enjoy.

I remember when Bionic Commando Rearmed first came out on the PlayStation 3. I bought it right away and absolutely loved the music, the gameplay, and just the overall feel of it. Later, when I switched to PC, I was so excited to see it was available there too. It was the same with the other Bionic Commando game—the one with the dreads. I bought both of them back when they originally released on PS3.

Back then, I remember Rearmed being incredibly difficult, and I never managed to beat it. Coming back to it now reminded me why I liked it so much. The controls feel really tight, and the swinging mechanic is still one of the coolest movement systems in any platformer.

This was actually the first game I played on my ROG Ally X. Ironically, I could never get it working properly on my desktop PC, even after trying a bunch of tutorials online. The handheld had no issues, so I ended up playing the entire game there.

One thing I really like is that this isn’t a Metroidvania. You simply pick a level, beat it, and move on. Every stage feels like its own platforming puzzle, and the bosses are puzzles too. It’s not just about having fast reflexes—you have to figure out each boss’s mechanics before you can beat them, which makes every fight feel rewarding.

There are around 19 levels. Some are full stages while others are shorter transition areas, but I actually like that structure because I can jump into a level, focus on beating it, and call it a day instead of wandering through one giant interconnected map. Defeating bosses also rewards you with new weapons and upgrades, like bazookas, pistol upgrades, machine guns, and character enhancements, so it always feels like you’re making progress.

Now for the part where I have a love-hate relationship with the game: that final level. It honestly felt as long as, if not longer than, all the previous stages. It reminded me of the old Gauntlet games where you have a limited number of lives and just keep inching a little farther every attempt. I had to memorize every section. The Albatross stage in particular really was the albatross around my neck—I genuinely thought I wasn’t going to beat the game because of it.

Even after getting through all those sections, you only have so many lives left for the final boss. Eventually I got consistent enough to reach the boss with five lives almost every run, but then I had to learn the boss itself, which is also extremely difficult. The frustrating part is that it takes so long to get back to the fight that practicing the boss is a challenge in itself.

When I finally beat it, though, it felt amazing. It wasn’t one of those “I’m just glad it’s over and never want to play it again” moments. It was the kind of victory that feels earned. I’m pretty sure if I went back now I’d beat that final level much faster because it’s one of those games where persistence and learning the patterns eventually pays off.

I also played the game on the hardest difficulty available for a brand-new save file. I know there’s an even harder difficulty that unlocks afterward, but this was the toughest setting you can choose from the start, and it felt like the perfect challenge.

Overall, I loved Bionic Commando Rearmed. The soundtrack is fantastic, the controls are incredibly tight, the swinging mechanic is still one of the most satisfying movement systems around, and I really enjoyed the level-by-level structure instead of another Metroidvania. It’s a challenging game, but one that always feels fair once you learn it.

It’s also a shame that Bionic Commando Rearmed 2 isn’t available on Steam. I’ve heard it’s not nearly as good, but I’d still like the chance to play it because this game reminded me why I liked the series so much in the first place.

Been over a decade since i last played this game on my ps3. I saw it on sale for $3 and decided to give it another go. After downloading the fix for the video card, it started up and i relived my nostalgia. i feel the game still holds up today.

First up, I want to point out that the amount of set-up I had to do for this one is ridiculous. The game didn't boot at first until an older version of NVidia's Aegia PhysX was installed. Do not buy this on Steam unless you're willing to do some set-up to get it running. As for the actual game, Rearmed is yet another remake/reimagining of the 1988 NES original. I think Rearmed does a better job updating it for modern audiences than the GB game by adding in more bosses, a decent minigame when hacking enemy computers, and some fun challenge rooms. There's also some additional content in the endgame that I won't spoil, but upped the difficulty pretty significantly. The biggest issue I have with this game is easily the visual style. I get what the game was going for (a literal 3D reimagining of the NES game), but it comes across as very cheap. Having played some of Capcom's other revivals, such as Strider (2014), Ghosts 'N Goblins Resurrection, and Mega Man 11, I think those games do a much better job at carrying their respective series' visual styles forward. The music was alright but nothing special. I cannot recommend getting this game on Steam due to the major issues present with getting the game to run at all on a modern PC, despite the fact that I did enjoy the game overall.

Despite the annoying required workarounds of downloading and installing additional drivers to get the game to run (a typical issue for many of Capcom's poorly optimized games), I still give Bionic Commando: Rearmed an overall recommendation.

This is an old, but largely faithful remake of the original 1987 NES classic. It does in fact run wonderfully on the Steam Deck, though as mentioned previously, you need to first follow a number of steps to get it to work. It isn't a surprise that Capcom is willing to let gamers buy a product that (figuratively) comes out of the box broken. Only purchase if you don't mind putting up with the hassle of fixing the game yourself.

With that said, if you own a Steam Deck and want another way to experience one of Capcom's most beloved cult-classics on the go, this is a solid bet. It's clear that Grin (now Overkill Software) went to great lengths to preserve the spirit of the original. All of the NES levels are faithfully recreated in 3D with a wonderfully remixed soundtrack that is completely taken from the 1987 classic. Even the story more closely follows the original Japanese version (originally titled Hitler's Resurrection in Japan) rather than the English language release, in which your mission is to the stop a resurrected Adolf Hitler. While BC: Rearmed never directly says his name out loud, they do strongly imply that Hitler is the resurrected leader of the Imperial Army. To avoid controversy back in the NES days, Capcom had changed his name to "Master D" for the international release.

The only parts of BC: Rearmed that are significantly different from NES version are the boss encounters. Aside from one or two of the boss battles, the rest are completely different from the NES version. I wouldn't say this is a bad thing though. There is a good level of variety to the bosses in Rearmed that makes them a difficult but fun challenge to overcome, particularly if you are playing on the Hard or Super Hard difficulty settings.

The game is filled with all kinds of jokes and references that fans of the NES game will appreciate. They even managed to preserve the infamous exploding head scene at the end of the game, something I hadn't expected but greatly appreciated as a big fan of the NES game myself.

The only unfortunate part of BC: Rearmed on the Steam Deck (for me) is that it can't connect to the 2009 Bionic Commando game. By collecting all 12 secret Yashichi items hidden throughout the levels, you are supposed to be able to unlock Spencer's retro outfit in the 2009 Bionic Commando game. However, no matter what I do, the game just doesn't detect my BC: Rearmed save file.

In any case, to anyone who is a fan of retro games or retro remakes and doesn't mind fiddling around with folders or game files, I can whole-heartedly recommend Bionic Commando: Rearmed. It is definitely worth a purchase.

Bionic Commando Rearmed is one of those rare remakes that fully understands why its source material mattered in the first place. Developed by GRIN and published by Capcom, it reimagines the 1988 NES classic with modern production values while preserving the defining mechanical twist that originally set it apart: there is no jump button. Instead, players control Nathan “Rad” Spencer, a soldier equipped with a mechanical grappling arm that becomes both his primary means of traversal and a central combat tool. In a genre historically defined by jumping precision, removing that convention could have crippled the experience—but here it becomes the foundation for a deeply satisfying and uniquely rhythmic action-platformer.

The first thing that stands out is the visual overhaul. Rather than recreating the original in pixel art, Rearmed adopts a 2.5D presentation with fully modeled characters and layered environments. The stages feel vibrant and kinetic, with dynamic lighting, destructible objects, and detailed backgrounds that add scale and atmosphere without cluttering the play space. The art direction strikes a careful balance between nostalgia and modernization; longtime fans can immediately recognize the level layouts and iconic enemy types, yet everything feels sharper, more animated, and more alive. Explosions burst with weight, metallic surfaces gleam under gunfire, and bosses loom with far more menace than their 8-bit ancestors ever could.

The grappling mechanic is the heart of the experience, and mastering it is both the greatest challenge and the greatest reward. Movement in Rearmed is momentum-based, requiring players to think in arcs rather than straight lines. Swinging across gaps, clinging to ceilings, and launching oneself forward using carefully timed releases creates a sense of flow that becomes exhilarating once internalized. Early sections may feel awkward as players adjust to the absence of a traditional jump, but as skill develops, traversal transforms into an almost acrobatic dance. The level design smartly reinforces this progression, gradually introducing hazards such as spike pits, moving platforms, and enemy placements that force creative use of the arm rather than brute force shooting.

Combat complements the traversal rather than overshadowing it. Spencer’s firearms range from rapid-fire rifles to heavier weaponry, and the bionic arm itself can stun, grab, and even deflect certain threats. Encounters often demand multitasking—swinging to avoid incoming fire while lining up shots mid-air—creating a layered tension uncommon in standard run-and-gun titles. Boss battles are particular highlights, expanding upon the original’s concepts with more elaborate attack patterns and cinematic flair. They test spatial awareness as much as reflexes, reinforcing the idea that positioning via grappling is just as important as firepower.

One of the most substantial additions beyond the original campaign is the suite of Challenge Rooms. These time-trial obstacle courses strip combat down to its essentials and focus almost entirely on movement mastery. They function as both skill tests and addictive replay content, encouraging players to shave seconds off their runs by refining swing timing and momentum control. For players who thrive on optimization and mechanical precision, these challenges dramatically extend the game’s longevity. Local cooperative and competitive multiplayer modes further add variety, allowing friends to tackle levels together or compete in skill-based arenas, though the absence of online multiplayer is a noticeable limitation in a modern context.

The audio design deserves equal praise. The soundtrack reinterprets the iconic NES themes into energetic electronic compositions that amplify the action without losing their retro DNA. The music dynamically supports the pacing—escalating during boss encounters and driving forward momentum in traversal-heavy stages. Sound effects carry satisfying punch, from the metallic snap of the grappling arm attaching to surfaces to the concussive impact of defeated enemies. Together, the audiovisual presentation elevates the remake beyond simple nostalgia, making it feel contemporary while honoring its roots.

Difficulty is unapologetically old-school, and this may be the most divisive aspect of Rearmed. Precision is demanded, and mistakes are often punished swiftly. However, the challenge rarely feels unfair; instead, it feels instructional. Each failure tends to highlight a gap in timing or positioning rather than arbitrary design. This philosophy mirrors classic arcade-era sensibilities, but with modern checkpointing that keeps frustration manageable. Players accustomed to more forgiving platformers may find the learning curve steep, yet overcoming it delivers a tangible sense of growth and accomplishment.

Narratively, the game follows Spencer’s mission to rescue Super Joe and dismantle an imperial threat, retaining the campy militaristic tone of the original while smoothing out localization and presentation. The story is straightforward, serving primarily as a framework for action, but its familiarity contributes to the remake’s authenticity. Fans of the classic will appreciate the respectful recreation of iconic moments, while newcomers receive a cohesive, self-contained adventure.

In the broader context of retro revivals, Bionic Commando Rearmed stands as one of the strongest examples of how to modernize a beloved title without diluting its identity. It does not simplify its mechanics to appeal to a wider audience; instead, it trusts the original design philosophy and enhances it with thoughtful refinements, expanded content, and polished presentation. The result is a challenging, mechanically distinctive action-platformer that feels both like a time capsule and a forward-thinking reinterpretation. For players who appreciate skill-driven gameplay and the satisfaction of mastering unconventional mechanics, it remains a standout title in Capcom’s extensive catalog and one of the most successful classic-to-modern transitions of its era.

Как ветеран по борьбе с Биоклингом, выросший на веревочном движении, я могу заверить вас: Bionic Commando: Rearmed - это гораздо больше, чем просто ремейк. Это ода золотой эре платформеров, тщательно переработанная для нового поколения, не теряя при этом ни капли того, что сделало ее предшественницу классикой.

Мои дорогие воспоминания проникают в новую графику:
Знакомая боль, но с подтяжкой лица: Графика, конечно, преобразилась. Это больше нет кубиков 8-битного чарма. Но это преображение с уважением. Мир все так же мрачен и индустриален, но каждая деталь проработана до совершенства. И да взрывы выглядят просто великолепно.
Музыка, что берет за душу: Музыкальное сопровождение, переработанное тем же человеком, что и оригинал. Каждая нота вызывает ностальгию мгновенно, заставляя вспомнить все те часы, что были потрачены на телевизоре.

Геймплей который остался тем же, но ощущается свежее:
Взрыв из прошлого: Управление осталось неизменным. Натан Спенсер все так же беспомощен, когда не может схватиться за точку. Это может разочаровывать новичков, но ветераны, как мы, считают это частью его шарма. Это вызов требует мастерства.
Сложность которая проверяет навыки: Не ждите прогулки по парку. Rearmed остается одной из самых сложных игр, в которые я играл. Однако, каждая смерть кажется справедливой, а каждая победа заслуженной. Преодоление сложного участка дарит непередаваемые ощущения.

Новые дополнения, для тех кто помнит оригинал наизусть:
Загадки и головоломки: Разработчики включили головоломки, которые требуют использования биоонической руки изобретательным способом. Это отличное дополнение, заставляющее смотреть на мир под другим углом.
Кооператив: Прохождение игры с другом, используя кооперативный режим, дарит новый уровень безумия и веселья. Совместная раскачка и взрывы - это незабываемое приключение.

Remake, remaster, secuela espiritual o lo que urja. Bionic comando es una saga atípica de plataformas, que renuncia al salto en pos de un gancho y su peculiar movilidad. Entrar a la saga, o al menos a este juego es tosco. Infinidad de rarezas pueblan el movimiento; el impulso vertical se mantiene pero el horizontal no, el rango y funcionamiento del gancho son precisos pero extraños y poco intuitivos, así como los controles de primeras, y entender que espacios son transitables y cuales no es un ejercicio de pensamiento lateral, viendo como estamos acostumbrados a un formato particular en lo que refiere al género. Dicho esto, el movimiento funciona. Una vez entendido, moverse y maniobrar por el entorno es satisfactorio, y aunque encadenar salto es tosco, dominarlo se siente muy bien. Por desgracia, el resto del juego no está tan bien. Diría que el diseño de niveles es horroroso, pero lo que realmente es, es hostil. Castigador. Implacable. Cualquier salto puede ser tu ruína. Abundan los fosos sin fondo. Spencer es frágil como el solo, y el contacto con un enemigo o proyectil puede tirarle fácilmente a un foso o unos pinchos, ruina asegurada. No son pocos los enemigos puestos al final de un salto, que generan situaciones de daño asegurado, o mismo en la caída. Tampoco ayudan los minijuegos, ni el hackeo ni las hordas de enemigos, que aunque interesantes al principio, se repiten muy rápido. Es frustrante además que los hackeos sean forzosos, cuando lo que obtienes, información de los enemigos y salud (Indispensable para un jugador novato como yo) sean probablemente inútiles para un jugador experimentado o si llegas bien de salud en un segundo intento contra el jefe. Sin embargo, nada de esto sería un problema de no ser por las vidas. Una mecánica arcaica que se ha colado en este juego, para mal. Si no existieran, el juego sería asequible, sirviendo los cambios de pantalla y jefes como checkpoint. Gracias a las vidas, un par de muertes te devuelven otra vez al principio del nivel. Por encima de todo, Bionic Comando Rearmed es frustrante. Todos los malos aspectos de su núcleo jugable, con los de su diseño de niveles crean una experiencia abominable, donde vas a ver todo tu progreso tirarse por la borde por un mal salto o un enemigo que no habías visto. Me gustaría que me gustara este juego, porque mecánicamente tenía y tiene ideas muy originales, pero a excepción de a un fan de los clásicos, o de lo retro, o de lo difícil (en general), no veo a nadie, mucho menos a mi, disfrutando de este juego.

Bionic Commando: Rearmed – Vzpomínky s moderními svaly

V roce 1988 nám studio Capcom naservírovalo na konzoli NES dnes již kultovní hru Bionic Commando. Tento titul se od tehdejší konkurence výrazně odlišoval, protože jste v něm nemohli skákat. Místo toho jste se po herní mapě pohybovali díky své bionické paži. Tento koncept byl naprosto revoluční a Capcom si to uvědomoval, proto se rozhodl titul oprášit a v roce 2008 vydal Bionic Commando: Rearmed, kompletní remake původního dílu s grafikou hodnou moderních konzolí.

Grafika a zvuk

Ačkoliv je Bionic Commando: Rearmed postaveno na moderním enginu, tvůrci se rozhodli zachovat 2D pohled a styl pixel artu, který je však obohacen o 3D modely postav, nepřátel a prostředí. Vše je tak krásně plynulé a hra působí velmi svěže. A to nejlepší? Soundtrack! Tvůrci vzali původní 8bitové melodie, oživili je a přidali i nové, moderní zvuky, které se k herní atmosféře perfektně hodí. Výsledkem je parádní kombinace nostalgie a moderního dynamického zvuku, která vás vtáhne do hry.

Hratelnost

Co se týče hratelnosti, v jádru je hra stejná jako její původní verze. Stále se nemůžete hýbat jako ostatní postavy a musíte se spoléhat pouze na svou bionickou paži. Tento mechanismus je geniálně propracovaný a tvůrci se ho nebáli rozšířit. Nyní můžete paži používat k zachytávání předmětů, odrážení projektilů a spouštění různých mechanismů. Hra tak nabízí mnohem víc než jen pohyb po mapě, a i když se vám zpočátku bude paže zdát trochu neohrabaná, po několika hodinách si na ni zvyknete a budete s ní dělat opravdové divy.

Hra vám také umožňuje vylepšovat si zbraně a bionickou paži, což sice není nic převratného, ale je to příjemný bonus, který hře přidává na rozmanitosti.

Multiplayer

Bionic Commando: Rearmed nabízí jak kooperativní multiplayer, tak i klasický deathmatch. V kooperaci si můžete zahrát celou kampaň s kamarádem a je to skvělá zábava, protože se můžete navzájem podporovat a strategicky využívat prostředí. Co se týče deathmatche, jedná se o standardní mód, který neurazí, ale ani nenadchne. Pro mě osobně je nejlepší volbou právě kooperace.

Verdikt

Bionic Commando: Rearmed je skvělý remake a důkaz, že i po 20 letech může být hra stále zábavná. Pokud jste fanoušci původní hry, tak je pro vás tento titul povinností. Pokud jste nováček, nemáte se čeho bát, protože hra je dostatečně přístupná i pro nové hráče. Bionic Commando: Rearmed není jen obyčejný remake, je to pocta originálu, která však nabízí dostatek novinek, aby oslovila i moderního hráče. Hru vřele doporučuji a věřím, že si ji užijete stejně jako já.

Hodnocení: 9/10

《生化尖兵复刻版》全方位评测

前言

　　Capcom在FC时代推出的经典横版过关游戏——生化尖兵(也叫“希特勒复活”或“希魔复活”)，给我们留下了一段难忘的童年回忆。即为经典那就总要重现一下，很明显Capcom也知道这个道理，所以《生化尖兵复刻版(Bionic Commando Rearmed)》应运而生了，本作由GRIN工作开发，值得一提的是，这个开发团队曾经参与过育碧的《幽灵行动 尖峰战士》的PC版开发工作。

　　这款游戏不仅会在家用机上出现，PC也被列入了登陆平台名单，如今已经发布，相信已经有很多怀旧的朋友沉醉其中了，当然Mel也是其中的一员，下面就让我们一起来体验一下这款经典复刻游戏。

注：另外一款全3D版《生化尖兵：重装上阵》暂无PC版发售计划，再次不多做介绍，如想了解可以在本站搜索早期的新闻。

　　故事背景 【评分：8】

　　198X年，纳粹党的绝密文件被发现，使我们了解到未能实现的计划——“信天翁”计划的存在。帝国军总统 怀兹曼对这份文件虎视眈眈，欲攫为己有并实现这个计划。联邦军为了阻止这个计划，派出了英雄——超级乔（Super Joe）。但后来失去了联系。一个勇敢的人，背负着拯救乔的使命奔向帝国……

作为复刻版，故事背景自然沿用原作(不然就不是复刻版啦)，从游戏的开始画面可以勾起人们强烈的回忆。本作的剧情较为简单，在今日看来甚至有些俗套，但经典就是因为他存在于过去，给过去的我们带来过一段特殊的感受。

　　所谓复刻版就是利用当今的技术，在不影响原作精髓的基础上，将其重现，生化尖兵复刻版完全符合这个标准，游戏的开头动画，场景设计完全忠于原作，而画面却有了质的飞跃(这是必然的)，游戏人物、场景全部3D建模，仍然保留横版过关的游戏形式，让玩家在最棒的画面中重温经典，这一设计绝对让大部分老玩家备受感动。

　　画面整体采用鲜亮明快的色调，使游戏游戏时感觉较为轻松，场景虚实把握的出色，远处的油井、电塔等建筑若隐若现，被一层淡蓝所包围。近景则比较细腻，光影效果也非常出色，人物、建筑的影子都会随着光源而变化，而且还采用了全屏泛光技术，使画面更加柔和

游戏中加入了物理效果，汽油桶丢出的抛物线，敌人受到攻击倒地、掉下等表现很真实，并且掉入水中的话会泛起一股水花，但是也许为了配合整体的卡通效果水并没有制作成为真实的效果。人物的动作也进行了相应的处理，人物的运动都更加符合物理规律。

另外本作的人设也邀请到曾为拳皇(Kof)、饿狼传说等游戏只做原画的森气楼担任，加强了本作的怀旧情节。

　　作为一款复刻版游戏，如此的画面表现方式，以及多处现代游戏制作技术的运用都为本作增光不少，并且又不失原作的经典元素，可以称得上是恰到好处。

　　当然为了更加调动玩家在游戏时的怀念，本作在开头采用了FC时代的MIDI音乐，当然进入到游戏中后，音乐也将进化的更加丰富，但仍然保持原作风格，可见本作在各个方面对于“复刻”这个词的强调。

　　在游戏的音效方面则只做得更加细腻，人物走在不同场景、不同地板将会发出不同的声响，甚至人物掉到水中的音效十分真实，另外子弹发射的效果也更有感觉，而子弹射击到的目标不同发出的声响也不同，在音效方面真可谓是做到了滴水不漏。

　　操作&上手度【评分：7】

　　对于玩过 FC版《生化尖兵》的玩家来说，上手就容易多了，本作的游戏方式完全照搬原作，经典的机械臂设计，可以让诸位回味当年飞檐走壁的快感。

而没有接触过旧作的朋友可能在初期会有些不习惯，因为本作中没有“跳”的设计，或者说跳跃被游戏控制，而并非玩家自由使用，因为游戏中的跳是在地上设计一个风扇将主角吹起，所以通常情况下玩家只能依靠机械臂进行攀爬，这就增加了游戏的乐趣，在上手以后，你会感受到主角在场景中上蹿下跳的爽快感。

在游戏中允许玩家的机器臂抓挂的地方非常多，在游戏中需要多尝试，以度过难关。除了增加主角的机动性，机械臂还可以抓取一些物品比如战利品还有油桶等，可以说灵活运用机械臂是整个游戏中最重要的要领。

游戏中的关卡设计分为两种，一种是横版卷轴，一种是纵版(就像魂斗罗那样的设计)，在纵版关卡中，玩家不能在使用机械臂跳跃，机械臂则变为防御武器，主角将会抡起机械臂来当掉飞来的子弹或者击飞身边的敌人(不会致命)。

　　总的来讲本作并不算太难，很多地方只要玩家稍动脑筋就可以通过，因为没有跳跃键，部分玩家操作会不太习惯，通过教学关，玩家可以很快上手，并掌握大多数的基本技巧。

　　总结【综合评分：8.3】

本作是一款不可多得的PC游戏，作为一款FC游戏的复刻版，相对传统的PC游戏，更加适合放松休闲，画面表现舒服，游戏节奏爽快，作为茶余饭后的活动项目不错，当然也是各位将要步入“大叔”阶层的FC老玩家追忆童年幸福时光的重要线索。

The majority of the negative reviews are about the fact the game requires you to download a fixed executable to run it. I found that to be very easy to do, there are steam guides for that and frankly, it's sadly not that rare when it comes to older titles.

Once you get past that issue, the game itself is rather charming. It seems to be made with a controller in mind, though I found the keyboard controls to be more than manageable for the most part which is good.
The gameplay itself is defined by the titular bionic, which, truth be told, is a little clunky to manage with a keyboard. Its quite unique but takes some getting used to. The "parkour" mechanic built around it is interesting and well-used, though again, you'd find it more enjoyable with a controller.

The levels are fairly straight-forward. The bosses are fun and challenging while still being fair.
There is a checkpoint system which is quite welcome. You have a base of three lives per level, but you can usually find an extra one hidden around. Checkpoints seem well-placed thus far.
Some of the levels, such as Level 6 and Level 7 and Level 8 (Don't worry, you aren't forced to take them back to back, you can choose in what order to take the levels that are part of a section), which are... hellish, to say the least the least. A true gauntlet to test what you've learned. They're beatable though... with enough attempts anyhow. Much easier with a controller.
The amusing (and infuriating) part is that the difficulty comes not from the enemies themselves, nor the bosses, but from landing those parkour sections properly. Sections which, mind, should, in theory, be rather simple...
I think each of those levels took me half an hour, if not more.

Note the presence of an inventory screen which offers some neat flavor info on each level, as well information on the amount of lives, weapons and upgrades you have. Keep it in mind while playing.
One other important trick, remember that shooting your bionic arm at a projectile will nullify it, thus ensuring you don't take damage from it. This is very important in other particular section. Keep that in mind too.

The patrol levels that occur when you get caught by enemies do overstay their welcome. They are sadly too repetitive as there are few maps, the encounters offer no rewards and they are simple to beat.

The soundtrack is filled with bangers and the overall gameplay loop matches the expected classic.

Overall, no complaints.

This is one of the worst games I have ever played.

I really didn't expect much of this game. I was told actually that I shouldn't play this game, that I should try Rearmed 2, but that's not on PC, so I may as well try this game.

This is going to be a bit more incensed than my usual reviews because this game made me angrier than any game I have played in recent memory, to the point where I simply hit ALT+F4 and quit out because I was so mad.

Bionic Commando Rearmed is a giant pile of garbage. It has a terrible upgrades system for your weapons, none of which you know anything about, it doesn't tell you what's in each stage, it doesn't even tell you really what weapons are expected to do, it doesn't even tell you, how many lives you have at any given time, it gives the player ZERO information, and the only reason you would actually understand even how to play this game in the first place and how you are meant to progress, is because you played Bionic Commando... ON THE NINTENDO ENTERTAINMENT SYSTEM AKA THE NES AKA THE FAMICOM!

LIKE SERIOUSLY??? YOU GUYS DECIDED TO ENTIRELY 100% RELY ON PLAYERS HAVING PLAYED AND UNDERSTOOD WHAT THE FIRST GAME IS, AS IN A GAME THAT CAME OUT ABOUT 40 YEARS AGO AT THIS POINT??? YOU COULD SPARE THE TIME TO DO CRAPPY TUTORIALS ON HOW TO LITERALLY USE YOUR ARM WHICH THE GAME SHOULD BE TEACHING YOU VIA THE LEVEL DESIGN, BUT YOU COULDN'T LITERALLY TELL PLAYERS "HEY YOU GET A WEAPON AT THE END OF EVERY LEVEL AND LOOK OUT FOR THE UPGRADES YOU CAN FIND ONCE IN A WHILE SECRETLY HIDDEN IN STAGES" OR WHATEVER??? 

HOW ABOUT A MAP, OR A MINIMAP, OR ANYTHING?!? NO!? OH WELL THAT'S FINE, I GUESS I BETTER LOOK UP A GUIDE THEN - AKA I HAVE TO USE EXTERNAL SOURCES TO LEARN THINGS ABOUT THE GAME I AM TRYING TO PLAY BECAUSE IT JUST WON'T TELL ME ***ANYTHING***!!!

I mean, sure the game came out in 2008, not 2025 when I am writing this review, but... that's still 2008. This is clearly a pretty low budget title, but I don't care, it's here on the Steam store and I'm gonna rip it apart for wasting my time and money.

But anyway, I think this just goes to show, and set the stage here, for the design decisions of the people who made this game: they HAD ABSOLUTELY no idea WHAT they were doing. I think they even have admitted this. There are videos on YouTube, speedruns done by the developers of this game where they're like, "yeah uh well Capcom approached us and uhh well we were like sure and uhh yeah" and that's like the level of commentary they have for their own game.

Now, I wanted to be fair to this game, really. I thought, well hey, it's probably not going to DESTROY me with greatness, no, I might think it's like, OK, but instead, I got this fucking mess.

So let's talk about like what's so terrible about the game. So first up, the game has a lives system. This is just... not exactly FUN, to deal with, really. But coupled with the absolutely hostile level design, clearly designed with no oversight or really anyone telling the level designer what is good and what is bad and so on? We ended up with this, a Bionic Commando game where you spend a very surprising amount of the game not grappling things or climbing things or whatever.

An example of what I mean is, the game is just full of corridors where it's like, you could swing if you really want to put in the effort to time your grapples perfectly, but it doesn't really help, and it's not fun to do because you can't get very big swings going. There are several corridors where, the room is just full of enemies and any one of them hitting you would interrupt your swing, they're like gauntlets, you just have to run through on your feet spamming the shoot button.

Then the last couple levels just go fucking nuts with rooms where you aren't doing any grappling at all, you're just like VERY SLOWLY waiting in front of a lightning wall or something so you can wait so you can wait for the next one to go down so you can pass that lightning wall and oh my god I want to have DIED.

I cannot understand how they were like, yes, let's copy the Oddworld games, let's make it so you aren't shooting or grappling like a Bionic Commando game should do, instead let's have you dodge stage hazards like crushers, (mincers in Abe's Oddysee), gas clouds, and lightning walls (literally a lightning wall in Abe's Oddysee). I just wish I could swear more to show just how angry I am at all this. It's not fun.

I could just repeat that for an entire paragraph, maybe I should, because that's the bulk of my feedback here. "It isn't fun."

I just was thinking this CONSTANTLY throughout THE ENTIRE GAME, when I wasn't thinking, oh hey I am extremely angry right now. I am genuinely furious, because of what this game is putting me through.

Oh and the best part is, like Contra actually kind of, you basically can never tell what's coming up until it scrolls on screen, at which point it usually is one of the incredibly annoying spread shot turrets that just bathe the entire screen in bullets and you generally don't have an answer except, hoping the 'bouncy shot gun' fires up at it, or maybe the ceiling is low enough for you to grapple to it.

The game is also FULL of bottomless pits, because of course, gotta have those in there. There are many many many rooms in this game, probably most of them, where it's like you're just trying to platform without a jump button, over an endless abyss, so if you ever make ONE mistake, you usually die. Mistimed a grapple even slightly? Well, that was your one shot, you die. There's no handholds, there's no safety platforms (except once in a while), nothing. 

Some of the actual normal levels are completely unreasonable, like it's honestly stunning what they expect you to even do, sometimes it's not even apparent what they want you to do to, you're just left going well, if I grapple onto that thing, maybe something will make sense, and sometimes it does, and sometimes you're just left like... what do you even WANT from me here? It feels like there's much less freedom in your grapples and the way you explore levels.

By the way, I am fully aware that since this is something of a remake SOME of these levels are kind of based on the original levels from the NES game. MANY of them however are completely original, and they are usually the worst ones. I know one screen in particular where the entire room is basically just kaizo blocks, that room was patched out of the XBLA release, because it was so awful to go through.

I should mention too this game actually has 'challenge rooms' so you can 'challenge' yourself with the mostly pretty unpleasant controls and the glitchy, buggy grappling mechanics that work except when they don't. Great. Just great. You can even find these as rewards for exploring optional areas in levels, but... like... a big problem there is, I don't know what I am going to be rewarded with, when I am exploring. And if I find like an item that makes my weapons stronger, I am happy! If I find a CHALLENGE ROOM, I get very very very angry. Like, I wasted my time, and my lives getting here probably, FOR THIS?

By the way, you may notice I have nothing to say about the story, or dialogue. It's bad. The game doesn't seem too invested in it, so I'm sure not going to get invested. The dialogue is atrocious, high-school grade trash. The writer thinks he's funny. I wasn't laughing.

It's not worth the frustration. SKIP THIS GAME. DO NOT PLAY IT UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES.

One of the best remakes out there. If you loved Bionic Commando on NES, you will love this. If you've never played Bionic Commando, you're in for a real treat. But let me cover some caveats before I explain more about the game. These caveats (especially #1) are why the game has mixed reviews. Which is a shame, but the reality of trying to play a game that's nearing 20 years old.

1) This game won't run on Windows 10 without some work. I don't know if it runs on Windows 11. If you're willing to troubleshoot, check the Discussion page first for latest information. For me, I had to install 2 PhysX packages and download a hacked EXE that allows the game to run on more than 4 cores. 

2) The movement in this game is unique. It's a platformer, but your character can't jump. Instead, you have to aim a bionic arm to move vertically. The game centers around this completely. Every level is a bit of  puzzle and a bit of a platformer, because not only do you need to figure out how to traverse the level, you need to get the timing on the arm throws correct. This is the core of why the game's so great, but some people don't like it. The character is not snappy and responsive until you've climbed high enough on the skill ceiling to make him that way. But there is a lot of depth to this system, including knocking bullets out of the air, and performing other tricks with the bionic arm.

3) I think you must use a controller to play the game. I'm currently using a Switch controller with Steam support force-enabled. The prompts are all X-Box style, of course. This game is from 2008!

Now, why is the game so great, beside what I've already mentioned? The music is bangin, the level design is flawless, the enemies are paced just right, are fun, and are not bullet sponges. Everything about this game feels master-crafted. This was a perfect remake back in the dark ages of NES remakes. I would say this is the grandfather of the great NES remakes. And because of the unique arm mechanic, you won't find another game out there like it. Every level has a boss, and the boss fights are fun. Note that this is a relatively linear game with levels, not a metroidvania or open-world style game. It's not an exact copy of the NES game; like any great remake, they improved it but kept the core intact. If you want to know even more, there should be some old school reviews online from back in the days when game review sites were actually pretty decent.

TLDR; if you like unique platformers, and you're not afraid of a little troubleshooting, it's more than well worth a buy -- until Capcom remasters it. (And sadly, they probably never will.)

Después de jugar su secuela quise probar este título para indagar en los orígenes del personaje, y termine encontrándome con literalmente un juego de los 80s con gráficos actualizados como leí por ahí, lo cuál conlleva a que tenga una dificultad y jugabilidad acorde a la época, y es que el juego es difícil de dominar debido a sus limitantes.

Los niveles son diversos y se acompañan de unos colores preciosos y cálidos muy agradables a la vista, al igual que su estupenda banda sonora y su estética tal como lo esperas de un juego de plataformas clásico, y después de ver como era el original me parece que hicieron un trabajo estupendo.

Ahora lo más complicado, es aprender a jugarlo xd, ya que el gancho tendrá varias mecánicas que deberemos dominar si queremos tener una buena experiencia, y sobretodo superar el último nivel que al ser el más largo es el más complicado y aquí si se te acaban las vidas tendrás que hacer todo el nivel de nuevo. Todo el juego se basa en un ensayo y error constante por lo que se exige paciencia. 

Pero una vez que ya dominas el gancho y las limitaciones del personaje (como no poder saltar) a la perfección, vas a disfrutar como nunca, con jefes divertidos a la par que complicados, plataformas desafiantes, gráficos y música gloriosos, y sobre todo, una gran dificultad digna de un juego de la NES que es lo que te ofrece está carismática aventura, por lo que si es lo que estas buscando sin duda te lo recomiendo, si quieres sufrir y pasarla bien como yo lo hice, o si buscas algún reto. Si no es así pues no creo que sea tu juego y vería otras opciones.

P.D. También tiene un modo coop y un multijugador aunque no probé ninguno de estos :p. Además de una sala de varios retos más complicados que el juego en sí xd.

Bionic Commando Rearmed is a really mixed bag of a game and a poor port, but it’s still an okay remake of a classic game, but what is the story. 

The Imperial Army has just struck a major blow to the FSA, as their greatest soldier Super Joe has been captured by them, all hope seems lost as the Imperial Army conquers the land, increasing their power but it’s not over as a young man named Nathan "Rad" Spencer is charged to rescue super Joe and help bring down the evil Imperial Army. It seems impossible for one man to do it all, but with Nathan’s Arsenal and his bionic mechanical grapple arm this young man, this Bionic Commando ma have what it takes to do the impossible and save the world.

Okay let’s talk about the likes, the gameplay is okay I do like the grapple hook even though it could be quite frustrating at times,  it is very versatile and the game really pushes the whole bionic grapple hook thing to its maximum not just with traversing levels, but beating bosses. The weapons are good each one has its own feel, we have your standard pistol and shotgun, but we can also get a machine gun as well as a bazooka and some can be a little bit multi-purpose especially the shotgun, there is also upgrades, but they are scattered throughout the game.

The story is good, it’s a very simple stop the fascists from taking over the world, it does have a good amount of Comedy and some light hearted moments but there is one problem with it but that's for dislikes. The graphics are good with a nice use of shell shaded bright colors that makes each level an area stand out along with a variety of rich environments, characters and enemies that are all visually appealing.

The levels were okayish each level is a bit diverse with some interesting scenery, but it does make you want to stop and look at each one, but there is a problem with them all, but like I have said that’s for the dislikes. The enemies and bosses were good each one has their own unique looks and feel, especially the bosses as each one was quite unique, although they do reuse bosses but I didn’t really mind it. 

The characters are good they're simple but you definitely come to like them, especially Nathan the Bionic Commando as he has this pretty kick-ass classic super soldier kind of feel to him and the helicopter pilot Haley I liked her as well as she is cool with a great sense of humor. The music was good that fit the game quite well with some nice tracks to listen too. The little bonuses in the game are good, I liked the little bios for the different enemies, characters and the world, there's also a challenge mode you can do but I never played it.

Okay let’s talk about the dislikes, now there's this huge and I mean huge problem with the game and it lies in the port itself, the game does not work on newer PCs, it just doesn't.To the point where I actually gave this game a bad review because I thought it was unplayable, but thanks to the fixes/walkthroughs on how to fix the game precisely Katros and Master Squid I was able to play it, but it's still bullshit that we even have to have these walkthrough/fixes for a game that Capcom should have patched it themselves before releasing it.

Now I said the levels were a mixed bag and that's because the game can have some pretty bad difficulty spikes, especially when grappling on certain levels like especially level 6 and 12 are particularly annoying. Now before anyone says I should get good, I'm a fan of Dark Souls games and I've played difficult games before, but the parts of this game feels very much bunk and requires a good bit of luck to beat, I don't know maybe it's my controller but I feel like it's the game itself.

Now the problem with the story is that they really should have just called the leader Hitler like come on I can understand why in the original game they had to scrub most of the overall Nazi references like changing Hitler’s name to the leader and stuff like that, but I feel like you don't have to do it for this game like call the leader Hitler and keep the more overt Nazi stuff in it, I don't know it just feels like if they did it would make fighting the bad guys even more fun, I don’t know like just using subtext feels kind of cheap. Also this game doesn't have achievements which I feel like it should.

Now that you all know this Bionic Commando Rearmed is a really mixed bag of a game and a poor port, but it’s still an okay remake of a classic game, it has okay gameplay, a good story and good characters. 

So do I recommend this game, kind of yes kind of no if you do get it I suggest wait till it's on sale, also to have a lot of patience especially when fixing the game so you can be able to play it on newer PCs. Honestly I hope Capcom or maybe Nightdive Studios can do a proper port of this game that also includes the original bio Commando and bio Commando rearmed 2.

Arkadaşımla birlikte deneyimledim. Onun yardımı olmasaydı oyunu oynayabilmem pek mümkün değildi; bu vesileyle kendisine bir kez daha teşekkür etmek isterim. Eski oyunları günümüzde sorunsuz oynayabilmem her zaman kolay olmuyor ve bu oyun da ne yazık ki istisnalardan biri değil. Arkadaşımın desteğiyle karşılaştığım bazı sorunları aşarak bölümleri herhangi bir aksaklık yaşamadan tamamlayabildim. Yine de oyunun yıllar içinde aldığı güncellemelerle bugün hâlâ oynanabilir ve diri tutulması, hem seriye sadık kalanlar hem de benim gibi sonradan katılan oyuncular için güzel. Elbette birkaç pürüzü modlar ile gidermek mümkün olsa da geliştiricilerin bunları neden ele almadığını düşünmeden edemedim. Yeniye ve daha fazla getirisi olana verilen önemin bunda payı olduğunu tahmin etmek zor değil.

Dönemi için oldukça başarılı sinematiklere sahip olan oyunda, özellikle son bölümlere yaklaşana kadar ciddi bir potansiyel gördüm. Arkadaşlarımla konuşurken kendimi sık sık RE4 ile kıyaslama yaparken buldum. İki kişinin aynı anda oynayabilmesi güzel ve kendine has bir deneyim sunsa da günümüz remake'lerinde alıştığım tek kişilik deneyimin ve yenilenmiş oynanışın bana daha çok hitap ettiğini söylemeliyim. Ek içeriklerle kendi çizgisinin dışına çıkması da oyunun dünyasını güzelce genişletmiş. Hatta bu değişimin yalnızca oynanışta değil, hikâyenin ilerleyişinde de gerekli bir hâle geldiğini düşünüyorum. Denemeye değer bir eski oyun; bazı pürüzleri aşabilirseniz size güzel vakit geçirecektir.

A mixed bag of a game.

Gameplay wise, I didn't mind a lot of the janky controls, and the aiming mechanics were fun, as I've only played the modern games so far. However, not allowing you to move or cancel when reloading was really annoying and is one of my biggest gripes. As well as this,  not being able to pause while accessing the inventory is even more annoying and made many encounters in the game unnecessarily stressful.

The Sheva ai isn't as bad as I thought it would be, but in certain sections made the game fairly frustrating, for example: if she runs out of ammo, she can essentially soft-lock you out of certain sections of the game or walking into insta-kill attacks forcing you to restart the checkpoint. I do think I would have benefited playing coop, so the above may not be as fair, but a mainline game shouldn't require that imo.

The rest of the game is definitely a product of its time, RE doesn't always need to be survival horror, but I felt the franchise's core identity was missing without having something in place of it.

The narrative itself was fine, but if you remove Chris it doesn't stand out from any other 2000s action shooter. 

Overall, it was a decent time, and if I could put a mixed review I would, but the more I played the more I wanted to get it finished and done with.

6/10

I really thought I'd love this game, but it's genuinely so horribly outdated. The controls are awful. They are so bad I had to get a mod to make the game somewhat more enjoyable. This game has some of the worst controls I've ever seen. The story just feels so repetitive. Run around in Africa, shoot a bunch of practically invulnerable zombies, run out of ammo, repeat. And don't even get me started with how excruciatingly boring the puzzles are. Especially in the ancient ruins. I'm so glad that's over.

 It gets so stale at points and I really wouldn't recommend this at full price considering how outdated some features are.

 There is one positive about this game though in my opinion, and that's the villain. I love his ability and his personality. But unfortunately, that's not enough to recommend this game enough. I still could see others loving this game, but for me, it's very average.

The checkpoints are really bad in this game. If you end up dying, or your teammate. Most times you have to restart the mission which you were already 10 minutes deep into. A lot of times I can't even save my useless teammate due to the enemies blocking the path to them. And it's not like I could kill them to get past, as all of the enemies' skulls are made out of titanium (Metaphor), and take ten 9mm bullet headshots to kill. And this was on the easiest difficulty by the way. I chose the easiest difficulty so I could have an enjoyable time, but no. I'm expected to take out an entire group of enemies when I can't even pierce their 5 inch thick titanium (Metaphor) skin. It's almost like all of the enemies are pre-prepped to be installed with the latest bullet proof armour technology, while all the pistol ammo is actually Nerf darts in disguise. I couldn't see a casual player having a fair playthrough in the slightest, especially with the horrendous controls.

I feel like I've really gone harsh on this game review compared to any other games that I've reviewed. But I genuinely felt so many negative opinions on the game while playing. And believe me. I wanted to love this game. 

4/10
