No puede ser que jugar Half-Life (1998) se sienta mejor que esto.

La obra de H.P. Lovecraft, a mi parecer, no está bien retratada en ningún medio, salvo en el de su origen. Por otro lado, las obras inspiradas en estos mitos sí resultan interesantes de ver, siendo una de las más sonadas Bloodborne.
Así que encontrar un juego bueno es bastante difícil, por no decir imposible, ya que, por lo que investigué, existen cuatro juegos bajo el nombre de Call of Cthulhu, siendo uno de ellos Dark Corners of the Earth.

Si tuviera que destacar algo del juego, sin duda sería su ambientación. En los primeros tramos se nos pide investigar en la ciudad de Innsmouth, donde claramente no somos bienvenidos, y eso se hace notar gracias a una ambientación pesada y, hasta cierto punto, terrorífica. Sumado a que, para ese momento, no tenemos armas, se crea una sensación de incertidumbre y desprotección que potencia todo lo anterior.
Pero el juego no logra mantener esa sensación. En capítulos posteriores se vuelve un shooter mucho más convencional y toda esa ambientación nunca se recupera, ni siquiera en los últimos tramos, que son los mas centrados en los mitos.

En cuanto a la historia, básicamente trata sobre un detective que viaja a Innsmouth para investigar el caso de una persona desaparecida. Todo esto está conectado con un tiroteo entre sectarios ocurrido meses antes, que lo dejó bastante afectado, siendo este el presagio de todas las cosas horribles que viviría después.
Fuera de esa premisa, la historia cumple. No es nada del otro mundo, pero deja de ser interesante una vez que la ciudad pasa a un segundo plano.

En cuanto al gameplay, el juego requiere cambiar teclas. Literalmente se interactúa con la S y se camina hacia atrás con la X. El uso de armas es correcto, no existe una mira como tal, pero se puede apuntar y, en general, funciona bien.
Ahora bien, el juego muchas veces peca de ser más críptico de lo que debería. A eso se le suma un spawn que, por lo que pude ver, es infinito, haciendo que recorrer algunos mapas termine siendo un desgaste constante de recursos. Una de las soluciones termina siendo cargar la partida y volver a intentarlo, algo de lo que se abusa mucho en el juego, del ensayo y error.

Dark Corners of the Earth no es el juego que esperaba, ni mucho menos una aventura 100% divertida. Tiene muchas asperezas que terminan desgastando la visión que uno puede tener sobre él. Aun así, reconozco que vale la pena jugarlo por ser algo medianamente bueno dentro de la escasa cantidad de obras ligadas directamente a Cthulhu.

This flawed game has the best introduction you could ask for in a Lovecraft game. An intriguing mystery with allutions to great cosmic secrets is how it begins, though with some admittedly hilarious and disonent line delivery on the part of the main character. But that is also where it falls apart. The first 20 minutes or so make a distinct enough impression that it may be worth a relook by the remaster gods of old and perhaps give this game a total rehaul. The shooting and stealth elements are busted, the investigations are incredibly easy, but the framework of this game can hold something great. 

Worth getting on sale.

Awesome game. Needs a community patch to run well (and not crash) on modern hardware but honestly so worth it. Some people say the game starts well and drops off hard, I think they couldn't be more wrong. Environments are well crafted, storytelling is great and the action is serviceable, fun even. I really like the quite unique player damage + healing system, its a nice touch. Special mention of course to the sanity mechanic, likely a primary influence for more modern greats such as Amnesia.

All in all, you gotta put up with a main course of jank but the dessert is so worth it. A classic that any horror enthusiast should experience.

Great game, bad technical state.

I love Lovecraft, so I couldn't just ignore this game. I installed it and ran into problems almost immediately. The game is in a horrible technical state. It crashes, and some of the in-game events don't work properly.

There are community-made patches and bug fixes available, but unfortunately, they didn't fix everything for me. After installing them, the game was at least playable, although it would still crash whenever I alt-tabbed. That's not a huge problem for me, though.

I was really trying to get into the game, explore the story, and experience the Lovecraftian atmosphere. And honestly, from what I played, the game is really interesting. It does a great job capturing that Lovecraft vibe.

But after a couple of hours, the stability problems started coming back. Then, the next time I launched the game, my mouse simply stopped working. I couldn't rotate the camera at all, which made the game impossible to play.

It's honestly really sad because I was enjoying what I saw.

I really think games like this shouldn't be sold on Steam in this state. You buy a game, install it, and it simply doesn't work properly on a modern PC. Like, what the hell?

So unfortunately, I can't recommend this game, even though I think the game itself is genuinely interesting. You need community-made fixes just to get it into a playable state, and even then, you may still run into problems.

Спустя 20 с лишним лет и бесконечное количество попыток я наконец-то прошел эту игру. И не скажу, что нахожусь в восторге. Скажу больше - она меня морально вымотала, как самый потный сосалик. Даже после "Bloodborne" мои руки так не тряслись. 

Но это ни в коем случае не плохая игра. Нет. Просто она как будто не до конца сформирована. Я знаю, что её выпустили после банкротства студии, но я б не удивился, если б узнал, что её банально не доделали. 

Начну с плюсов. Во-первых, сюжет. Это не прямая адаптация произведений Лавкрафта, а скорее компиляция его самых удачных и узнаваемых работ - тут и "Дагон", и "Тьма над Иннсмутом", и "Зов Ктулху" и "Хребты Безумия" и тд. Вы в роли детектива Уолтерса приезжаете в маленький городок Иннсмут, чтобы найти пропавшего клиента; и в ходе поисков невольно ввязываетесь в движуху между последователями культа Дагона и ФБР. А потом вообще раскроете тайну своего прошлого, но к сожалению это знание не принесет вам счастья (если что, это не спойлер, в начале игры прямо показывают, чем закончит наш герой). И сюжет реально интересный. Не гениальный, но легко бы лег в основу какого-нибудь романа. Полностью вам ничего не раскроют, но, камон, всё по заветам Лавкрафта, ведь нет ничего страшнее, чем тайна. 

Первые пару часов в игре самые удачные. Иннсмаут - маленький, но невероятно атмосферный город. Узкие улочки, темные улицы, уродливые жители, старые дома с заколоченными окнами и протяжный морской ветер. По этому городу просто интересно бродить, смотреть по сторонам, и гадать, что же скрывается за его фасадом. Ну а после начинается по-настоящему напряженная погоня и прятки, которые до самого конца держат в напряжении. Ведь малейшая неосторожность - и прости прощай. А чекпоинтов тут крайне мало. 

Вся фишка с шизой, которая якобы является особенностью геймпля - геморрой. Всё понимаю - герой нервный, всего боится. Но, блин, когда посреди перестрелки или во время самых потных моментов экран становится мутным, а всё видимое превращается в карусель - это невероятно бесит. Пару-тройку раз я точно помирал из-за таких приколов, потому что просто не знал, где враги - а они не промахиваются. 

А вот когда дают в руки огнестрел становится уже не так страшно. Так как интерфейса практически нет, приходится полагаться на внимательность и интуицию, ведь каждый патрон на счету, а герой, увы, довольно хлипкий. 

Почему я раннее сказал про несформированность? Потому что игра скачет между жанрами и до конца не может определиться, что он такое? С одной стороны, скучно не бывает: сначала прячетесь, потом стреляете, потом решаете головоломки - и тд. С другой - ни одна механика не доведена до вменяемого уровня. Стелс кривой, перестрелки портят глупый ИИ и возрождающиеся враги (а ресурсы не бесконечны, ага), головоломки превращаются в долгую и унылую прогулку по запутанной локации в поисках невероятно важного предмета, который ещё поди-сыщи (да-да, пиксельхантинг как он есть) - а нужно ещё найти куда его вставить. 

Квинтессенция этого ужаса - финальный уровень, который представляет собой лабиринтообразные пещеры с неочевидными загадками и моментами, до которых практически невозможно догадаться. Ну откуда я знал, что в одном из закутков вбитый в стене кристалл - который легко пропустить - так важен!!! Я час бродил по туннелям, ломая себе голову, что я упустил. И ведь гулял бы так и дальше, если б не гугл. 

Ну и самая главная проблема этой игры - баги. В руководстве лежат фанатские патчи, но даже с ними нет никакой гарантии, что вы пройдете игру без проблем. У меня, например, постоянно ломались скрипты (особенно на корабле) и были вылеты. А финальная секция вообще вымотала меня до предела. Побег из гибнущего города - притча во языцех среди фанатов Ктулху. Пять минут беспрерывной беготни от падающих камней в надежде, что скрипт не забагует и вы спокойно пройдете до портала - а забаговать он может где угодно - испытание для самых настоящих мужчин. Даже костыльные решения вас не спасут - чистая удача и ничего более. Когда у меня это получилось - не знаю, с какого раза - я почувствовал, будто поднялся на самую высокую гору, вымотав себя до предела. 

В общем, игра далеко не идеал. Даже отличной назвать её не могу. Скорее где-то между "хорошо" и "нормально". Мне понравился сюжет, атмосфера; местами было действительно страшно, напряженно и интересно. С другой - кривой геймплей, баги, игры разума и неочевидные головоломки, решение которых не приносит удовольствия. Но я рад, что закрыл этот гештальт, а значит могу с чистой совестью жить дальше. 

6.5 из 10

Two things:

1) This game is unbelievably broken and buggy on PC. You cannot just download this and run it. You'll have to go find mods/community patches. At the time I played this (2014), it wasn't too difficult a task. I've heard it's gotten harder with each subsequent OS.

2) Underneath the terrible PC port, there is a really special game here. If you can look past some jankiness, you will find one of the most atmospheric Lovecraftian games with some great, unique mechanics that were ahead of their time.

I recommend this game for the true hidden gem seekers. If you are willing to power through the setup, you'll have the opportunity to play a game that deserved a far bigger audience than it got (for those unaware, it released right at the end of the OG xbox's lifecycle after development hell and was doomed to obscurity).

There is some value in having the opportunity to play such an atmospheric/ambitious game, knowing that so few others will ever experience it. It is a niche sort of drug.

I could just gush about Dark Corners forever.
It's not a "good game" by today's standards, and I imagine people will have trouble playing it. If you love psychological survival horror, though, this is one of the progenitors. It's a lot of fun and quirky in how it immerses you in the story.
The graphics have not aged well, but everything bears a solid and creepy aesthetic. The story is a bit of a mash between several of Lovecraft's well-worn classics with the heaviest influence clearly being The Shadow Over Innsmouth, and (unless I'm mistake) most of the game is based on the TTRPG so you're working with some solid foundations.
The game is buggy, I know a few playthroughs have been thwarted in the past by glitches. I recommend mod fixes where possibly and patience when they aren't. I've been told on multiple occasions that GOG has the fixed iteration of the game, so I would recommend it there rather than steam - one of the infamous glitches of the "artillery section" is likely to plunge you out of the end of the game if you're not careful.

If you're a fan of atmospheric horror, this game is an absolute masterpiece! Even after all these years, "Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth" delivers an experience that few games have managed to match.

The atmosphere is incredible. Innsmouth feels genuinely oppressive, mysterious, and unsettling, and the sense of dread never really goes away. Instead of relying on cheap jump scares, the game builds tension through its world, sound design, and storytelling. You constantly feel like something is wrong, and that's exactly what makes it so unforgettable.

The story is one of the best Lovecraft adaptations ever made. It captures the feeling of cosmic horror perfectly, slowly revealing terrifying truths that kept me hooked from beginning to end. The famous hotel escape sequence alone is worth experiencing, it's one of the most intense moments in gaming history.

I also loved that combat isn't the main focus. You're vulnerable, your character can panic, and sometimes the smartest option is simply to run. It makes every encounter feel meaningful and keeps the tension high throughout the adventure.

Yes, the game shows its age, and it has a few technical rough edges, but none of that took away from what makes it special. Its atmosphere, storytelling, world-building, and unforgettable moments easily outweigh its flaws.

This is a true cult classic and, in my opinion, one of the greatest horror games ever made! If you enjoy Lovecraft, immersive storytelling, and games that leave a lasting impression, don't hesitate. It's an experience you'll remember long after the credits roll...

Highly recommended !!

Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth became a guilty pleasure game for me because I know that it is an incomplete mess.

Lets get the most important thing out of the way first:

The PC port for this game on Steam is broken.  The port was made primarily by a single developer so I don't blame them considering the company faced financial struggles at the time. You will have to patch the game and even then it will still have bugs that are not solved to this day. One bug I could not find a fix for was whenever I had blood splatter on my screen from taking damage the game would lag.

Most of these fixes are linked on the PCGamingWiki:

Retail EXE to utilize all settings using DCoTEPatch.

Widescreen Fixes Pack to fix HUD, aspect ratio and cutscenes.

dgVoodoo 2 to fix crashing when alt-tabbing the game.

DCoTEPatch is absolutely mandatory for bug fixing, enabling extra features and increasing FOV.

Once all of the patches are applied you will have to use the Steam launch command to make Steam launch the game using the retail EXE.

Now I can get to the game itself.

I did try the game a while ago and I believe I got up until the boat section before I gave up. This time around I completed the entire thing. The game feels very ambitious, unfortunately a lot of the game was cut probably due to the scope being too large and some financial troubles. What's left is a game that is inconsistent and barely holds together.

Arriving at Innsmouth sets the stage well. The inhabitants are really creepy looking and the town itself looks lost to time. A significant part of the game takes place there and it feels very different to the last half. It is more of a slow burn, asking people for clues, stealthing past guards and solving puzzles. The chase that takes place in the hotel is commonly mentioned as a highlight for people and I understand why.

Unfortunately the stealth is not great. The game has very bare bones stealth mechanics and it is extremely inconsistent when enemies spot you resulting in a lot of trial and error. It takes quite a while before you get a gun and once you do it becomes less of a stealth detective game and more of a straight up shooter.

There are a lot of scripted sequences that are broken easily, the game can be continued but you will miss out on dialogue and hints. I would've beaten the game a lot faster if I wasn't so confused on what to do to proceed. One of the biggest faults of the game is not making it clear enough what to do or where to go next. The Marsh Refinery is one of the best examples. The refinery is insanely large, its easy to get lost and not obvious what they want you to accomplish.

I like the localized healing system even if it slows the combat down. Depending on where you get injured it can affect your aim with a weapon or make you limp and stagger. Considering how insanely unforgiving fall damage is you will probably break your legs a few times. The shooting is decent even if there isn't a lot of enemy variety. I wish enemy corpses wouldn't disappear, it breaks the immersion a bit.

My favourite mechanic has to be the sanity system. Its not overly complex, but it adds a lot of charm. Jack Walter franticly talking to himself when he witnesses something horrific is a nice touch. Very interesting that this came out before Amnesia: The Dark Descent because it very much reminded me of the same system.

I enjoy the cutscenes that are taken from other creatures perspective, it creates some great tension. The opening cutscene does a really good job of establishing the dark world the game takes place in. The horror elements did a lot to uplift the games atmosphere. The decision to have no HUD elements on the screen helps the immersion. I only wished they would have done what Condemned: Criminal Origins did which is let you check the remaining ammo instead of having to guess how much you have left.

Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth is an extremely hard game to recommend to most people in its current state on Steam, but if you can get past all of the road blocks and you are a big fan of the Cthulhu Mythos then you will probably get something positive out of the experience.

A Diamond in the rough 

10/10

I really wanted to like Call of Cthulhu, before I get into the problems, let's look at the good. The atmosphere got me from the beginning of the game, even now this game has some damn good eerie vibes. Like the dark clouds hanging over the town and the gloomy look of the town. The first act of the game is brilliant, it's slow burn build up done right, it goes from a adventure detective game from the start, to running intense shooter the next. Literally if the entire game was the first act, plus bits of the second act, I would say this is a really solid horror game. 

But sadly that's not the case, first of all the bugs is the worst thing about the game. Now I installed the patches, widescreen and 60fps to where the game doesn't crash. But even with all that, this game is really janky to a bad degree, one part was where I was waiting to ride the ore cart, I had to look up a guide, try to glitch onto the cart, only to find out that there is like one cart that is ridable after looking it up on an old forum. I almost quit playing several times, and I can bare some old mechanics, glitches and a lot more if the game has great strengths, But the game's biggest strength is the first act and that's about it. 

Now the breaking point was the ship section, seriously that section is just awful, the cannon controls awful, the going in and out to fetch ammo and first aid for the one crewmate awful, and the final nail in the coffin for me was escorting that same crewmate back to the infamy only for him or I to die because my character still hasn't learned to close doors 4 hours into the game.

Overall I give this game a 3/10, has an amazing beginning  but a sour third act which you need the patience of god to get through.

Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth is a long-awaited horror action adventure that blends stealth, exploration, and first-person combat into a deeply unsettling experience. Despite technical flaws and dated visuals, it stands out for its originality and ability to create genuine tension.

You play as Jack Walters, a private investigator with a troubled past who arrives in the eerie town of Innsmouth to investigate a missing persons case. What begins as a routine job quickly spirals into something far more sinister. The story gradually builds its sense of dread, drawing you deeper into a world inspired by H.P. Lovecraft’s mythos. Even without prior knowledge of Lovecraft, the narrative remains engaging and full of surprises.

The game excels at atmosphere. Everything is presented from a first-person perspective with no traditional HUD, relying instead on visual and audio cues. Injuries are shown through blurred vision, labored breathing, and impaired movement, while sanity effects distort your perception during particularly disturbing moments. These systems enhance immersion and make every encounter feel more intense.

Gameplay is a mix of stealth, puzzle-solving, and combat. For much of the game, you are unarmed, forcing you to rely on observation and evasion. These sections are often the most effective, especially during scripted escape sequences that create a strong sense of panic and urgency. Combat, when it appears, is less refined. Weapons feel powerful, but enemy behavior can be inconsistent, and firefights are not as satisfying as the buildup suggests.

Exploration and puzzles play a significant role, though the lack of a map or objective system can lead to confusion. This design choice adds to the tension but may also frustrate players who get stuck. Similarly, the limited save system increases the stakes but can feel restrictive.

Visually, the game shows its age. Character models and textures are rough, and animations can be stiff. However, strong art direction and detailed environments help compensate, creating memorable and atmospheric locations. The sound design is a highlight, with convincing voice work, eerie ambient effects, and well-timed music that reinforces the game’s tone.

In the end, Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth is an ambitious and memorable horror experience. Its technical shortcomings and rough edges are noticeable, but they do little to diminish its impact. For players willing to overlook its flaws, it offers a tense, immersive journey that captures the spirit of Lovecraft’s work and delivers plenty of unforgettable moments.

What's with all the bad reviews? I'm sure it's because it's a little buggy and difficult to play, but I never had any serious problems with bugs and I think the difficulty makes it that much more scary. And that's another thing about this game, it is absolutely terrifying and great at being it, and the added realism in the gameplay makes it all the more genuinely intense. All that, and you get a genuinely well made story that's faithful to the Cthulhu mythos to a tee. What more could you want?

So if you wanted a version of Amnesia where you can actually fight back, and I'm sure there's other comparisons to great games that I could make, buy it, it's cheap, a true underappreciated classic, and it'll keep you hooked for hours on end.

Il trailer di Brink è stato uno dei trailer che vidi di più quando uscì su uno dei dischi di winmagazine o giochi per il mio computer. Essendo un grande amante di mirror's edge(giocato alla gloriosa risoluzione 640*480 con dettagli al minimo ^^ ) l'idea di uno sparatutto con parkour era assolutamente esaltante! Ricordo ancora lo stupore, nel trailer, di vedere il muscolo del braccio del tank dei rivoluzionari tremare agli spari. Incredibile!

Dopo averlo giocato devo però ammettere che il gioco è a dir poco mediocre. Totalmente inadatto a essere interessante nel giocatore singolo, tra poche mappe e una IA assolutamente da dimenticare, un doppiaggio tremendo e una regia...migliorabile. In multiplayer sicuramente ci guadagna perchè TUTTE le classi sono davveo utili a loro modo. I medici curano e rianimano, i tecnici creano torrette(che fanno schifo! Non servono quasi a niente!) e riparano, i soldati rimpinzano di munizioni e fanno saltare in aria cose e le spie si inflitrano e hackerano.
Carino... ma dal trailer io mi aspettavo una grandissima libertà di movimento. Mappe davvero ampie in cui zompare, arrampicarsi, aggirare... più una sfida di parkour che uno spara spara. Mi aspettavo mappe MOLTO interagibili(visto quello che si vede nel trailer), ma niente. Le mappe non sono brutte...ma decisamente non sono neanche lontamente quello che avrei voluto vedere. Ripeto, non sono brutte...ma mi aspettavo molto più mirror's edge.
La storia non è un granchè... però apprezzo molto vedere quanto, crescendo, mi sia profondamente immedesimato nell'animo egualitario dei rivoluzionari stanchi di dover vedere un mondo allo sfascio con il 5% della popolazione che detiene il 90% delle ricchezze, controlla l'acqua potabile(che raziona solo ai poveri) e sembra ben felice che tra gli "ospiti" ci siano epidemie così da tenerli schiacciati e sotto controllo.

SIcuramente in multiplayer questo gioco poteva donare aspetti interessanti, ma per me che ho giocato in singolo e mi aspettavo qualcosa di molto più vicino al trailer...e che l'ho giocato con quel doppiaggio e che per tutto il tempo mi è sembrato di usare dei controllo non molto precisi... è stata davvero una brutta esperienza, piena di imprecazioni dall'inizio alla fine. Mi spiace essere contento di non riarprirlo mai più.

[h1]BRINK[/h1]

[b]Gêneros:[/b] Ação, Gratuitos para Jogar
[b]Avaliação na Steam:[/b] Mistas, com 8181 avaliações
[b]Preço:[/b] Gratuito

[b]Visão geral[/b]
BRINK é um shooter em primeira pessoa com foco em mobilidade, objetivos e combate em equipe, ambientado em um futuro distópico onde a humanidade sobrevive em um refúgio flutuante chamado Ark. A proposta do jogo mistura tiroteio tradicional com movimentação mais ágil, classes funcionais e mapas construídos para incentivar rotas alternativas e ações coordenadas. Na época do lançamento, a ambição era clara: oferecer algo diferente dos FPS militares mais convencionais, com personalidade visual própria e ênfase em partidas orientadas por objetivo.

Mesmo com a recepção dividida e uma reputação que acabou ficando pior do que a experiência realmente entrega, BRINK ainda mostra ideias interessantes. Ele não é um clássico injustiçado em todos os sentidos, mas também está longe de ser o desastre absoluto que parte da fama sugere. Hoje, funciona mais como uma curiosidade competente do gênero: um jogo com boas intenções, algumas qualidades reais e limitações que impedem seu potencial de brilhar por completo.

[b]Jogabilidade[/b]
O principal diferencial de BRINK está no sistema de movimentação, que permite correr, deslizar, saltar obstáculos e atravessar o cenário com mais fluidez do que em muitos FPS contemporâneos ao seu lançamento. Esse ritmo mais dinâmico ajuda a dar identidade própria ao combate, principalmente para quem gosta de se reposicionar rápido e explorar o mapa de forma agressiva ou inteligente. A sensação de mobilidade é um dos pontos que mais sustentam a experiência até hoje.

As classes cumprem papéis bem definidos dentro das partidas, com funções voltadas para ataque, suporte, reparo e objetivos específicos. Isso incentiva cooperação e torna o jogo mais interessante quando o time realmente joga com noção de função. Em contrapartida, quando a equipe não se organiza, a experiência pode ficar desbalanceada e frustrante, já que boa parte da diversão depende de jogadores fazendo o que o mapa e o objetivo pedem.

O sistema de progressão e personalização tem boas ideias, permitindo ajustar habilidades e montar um personagem mais alinhado ao estilo de jogo desejado. A variedade de armas e equipamentos não é revolucionária, mas é suficiente para criar abordagens distintas. O gunplay em si é funcional, embora não tenha o mesmo impacto ou precisão tátil dos grandes nomes do gênero. Ainda assim, há uma base sólida aqui, especialmente para quem valoriza objetivo e movimentação acima de realismo militar.

Vale mencionar que a experiência pode exigir alguns ajustes para rodar da melhor forma em sistemas atuais, especialmente no desempenho e em configurações mais específicas. Além disso, por ser um jogo fortemente voltado ao multiplayer, sua longevidade depende da atividade da comunidade. Ainda existe algum público interessado, mas não é o tipo de jogo em que se pode contar com filas sempre cheias ou variedade constante de partidas. No solo ou com bots, ele quebra um galho, mas claramente foi pensado para confrontos entre jogadores.

[b]Apresentação e atmosfera[/b]
Visualmente, BRINK aposta em um estilo estilizado que ajuda o jogo a manter certa personalidade mesmo com a idade. A direção de arte da Ark consegue transmitir bem a sensação de uma sociedade em colapso tentando sobreviver em um espaço limitado, com cenários industriais, urbanos e improvisados. Não é um jogo particularmente impressionante hoje em dia, mas a identidade visual ainda tem valor.

A ambientação funciona melhor como pano de fundo do que como narrativa marcante. O mundo tem premissa interessante, mas o jogo não explora esse universo com a profundidade que poderia. O áudio cumpre seu papel no combate e na leitura da ação, embora sem grande destaque. No geral, a atmosfera é competente e diferenciada, mas não chega a ser o elemento mais memorável do pacote.

[b]Pontos positivos[/b]
[list]
[*] Sistema de movimentação ágil que dá personalidade ao combate
[*] Partidas com foco em objetivos e trabalho em equipe
[*] Classes com funções úteis e bem integradas ao fluxo do jogo
[*] Direção de arte estilizada que envelheceu melhor do que o realismo da época
[*] Boa variedade de rotas e verticalidade nos mapas
[*] Tem ideias próprias e não parece apenas mais um FPS genérico
[/list]

[b]Pontos negativos[/b]
[list]
[*] Gunplay não é tão impactante ou refinado quanto o de concorrentes mais fortes
[*] A experiência depende bastante de comunidade ativa e equipes cooperativas
[*] Pode exigir ajustes extras para funcionar de forma ideal em PCs atuais
[/list]

[b]Para quem é indicado[/b]
[b]Recomendado para:[/b] fãs de FPS com foco em objetivo, jogadores que gostam de movimentação mais dinâmica e quem tem curiosidade de revisitar shooters subestimados da era Xbox 360/PS3/PC.
[b]Pode não agradar:[/b] quem busca matchmaking muito ativo, campanha forte, tiroteio mais pesado e polido ou uma experiência moderna sem necessidade de adaptação.

[b]Conclusão[/b]
BRINK é um jogo melhor do que sua reputação sugere, mas também carrega problemas reais que explicam por que nunca alcançou o status que prometia. Sua movimentação, proposta de equipe e estilo visual ainda têm mérito, especialmente para quem aprecia FPS com identidade própria. Por outro lado, a dependência do multiplayer e a falta de acabamento em áreas importantes limitam bastante seu apelo atual. No fim, é uma experiência interessante, com valor para nichos específicos, mas difícil de recomendar de forma ampla.

[b]Nota final: 6,5/10[/b]‍

Brink is one of the classic Class based shooters I grew up with that died before it got it's chance.
This is one of those games that Could've used more love over time with patches and tunings.

Long story short, you're either the Security or the Rebels of the last Known bastion of Humans after a great flood drowns most of the world. After many years conflict breaks out between the Guests who arrived to the Arc for shelter vs the Founders the wealthy originals who built the Arc and their Security forces. 

Where this game falls flat is the Maps, Perks and Lack of Players.

BRINK is a multiplayer focused first person shooter set in a futuristic floating city called the Ark. The city is falling apart, and I can play as either the Security forces or the Resistance while taking part in missions built around objectives rather than simply getting the most kills. The setting gives the game a distinctive identity, and I like that the story is told from two opposing sides rather than presenting one group as completely good or evil.

The biggest gameplay feature for me is the SMART movement system. It allows me to vault over obstacles, slide and move around the environment more smoothly than a traditional shooter. When the movement works properly, it makes getting around the maps feel much more fluid, and it encourages me to think about routes instead of always taking the obvious path.

The objective based combat is another strong point. Matches can involve escorting objectives, defending positions, hacking systems or completing other tasks, so I have to pay attention to what my team is actually trying to accomplish. I like this more than a pure deathmatch because a player can still contribute by completing objectives or supporting teammates.

The character customisation is also surprisingly detailed. I can change my character's appearance and choose different abilities, weapons and classes depending on the role I want to play. The class system gives me more options during matches, and I like being able to switch my approach depending on what the team needs.

The biggest problem is the age of the game. BRINK originally released in 2011, and the graphics, animations and overall presentation now feel quite dated. Some of the character movement can look awkward, and the environments do not have the same level of detail I would expect from a modern multiplayer shooter. That is understandable given its age, but it can make the game harder to appreciate today.

The multiplayer population is another major issue. BRINK depends heavily on having enough players for its objective based matches, and an older game naturally has a much smaller community than a modern shooter. Even when I enjoy the mechanics, the experience suffers if I cannot find enough people to create a proper match.

I also think the AI can be inconsistent. When I am playing with bots, they do not always understand objectives or behave as intelligently as I would like. That makes the single player and offline experience feel much weaker than the original multiplayer concept, especially because teamwork is such an important part of the game.

Overall, BRINK is an interesting old school shooter with some genuinely good ideas. I like the SMART movement, objective focused missions and detailed character customisation, and the futuristic Ark setting gives it plenty of personality. The dated presentation, inconsistent AI and small player base hold it back today, but there is still a fun and distinctive shooter underneath the age.

This game is excellent when you play with humans. In fact I might go as far to say that playing this upon its initial PC release in full servers was some of the most fun I've had in an online PvP game to date. 

If you have people to play with or you happen to be online when a few public servers show some signs of life in them, you'll likely have a lot of fun. Also for reasons I can't fathom, you can only get 60fps in online free play; so this is where the actual game resides.

However, if you plan to play this solo, be prepared for some genuine frustration during your initial levelling up stages. My advice would be to get a few levels in the campaign first, then attempt the challenges to unlock more gear options. 

Some weapons will feel genuinely awful to use, yet others will feel very satisfying. Health pools seem fair yet weapon damage seems to essentially be random, so it's best to try and play conservatively; utilising cover and even friendly bots to shield you, which is quite possibly their one useful trait.. 

The over-use of camera shake isn't particularly fun for me and you'll find the bots very much enjoy spamming grenades. But in a game about building control and managing/helping your team it's understandable as to why this was a design choice, since you have to destabilise a team's hold on objectives, so messing with their ability to aim and fire competently is an actual game mechanic.

The level design is excellent, with any objective area having multiple paths and sub-objectives to pursue so no one can get too comfortable. The parkour elements may seem a little clunkier than modern day games too, but this was one of the first that ever implemented it as part of the movement ecology, and the level designs capitalise on it very well.

Overall and despite its age, it's a game that places emphasis on team cohesion and working together. Perhaps it's not for most, but it's definitely more cerebral than many similar shooters. The solo experience isn't great, or perhaps to be fair, unremarkable. But it was never really intended to be a solo experience.

There's a whole story out there on how Bethesda overhyped this game and put Splash Damage (Wolf and Quake Enemy Territory) in a position where an original IP game that was intended for a PC audience had to cut an enormous amount of scope in order to encompass a console release, where it ultimately didn't land that well. Whereas on PC and in the absence of Bots, it was excellent.

Interesting that it's now free to play, yet I suppose it remains as a monument to Publishers making bad decisions and letting the developers take the fall for its commercial failings. An all too common story.

SHORT VERSION: 'Brink is over 15 years old, and is a dinosaur of a game in many ways. But dinosaurs are awesome, and so is Brink.'

-----------------------------------------

Brink is a faction-based team-based game (security forces vs rebels) where you play handcrafted missions. It could be ungenerously described as 'Counter Stirke 3000', but it has a basic storyline at least.

There are two campaigns (one per faction) which can be played against bots, solo or in a group (with bots filling any empty friendly slots). I imagine you could also face off against other human players but I'm not sure the game is popular enough for that to happen unless you organised it yourself.

I was gaming back when this first launched all those years ago. I remember hearing it was a weird game that didn't know what it wanted to be. That's nonsense. Brink is clearly an 'objective-based team shooter'.

 I saw a review here that described Brink as 'ahead of its time'. I think that's true.

Sure, only by a few years or so - but still. It didn't get the credit it deserved at the time.

Don't get me wrong. This isn't a masterpiece of gaming.

But it sure is some damned good *fun*. This game has become my 'I need to waste 30 minutes and I want to shoot stuff' game. And it's solid as hell, which is the main thing I look for in a game.

What do I mean by 'solid'?

Many things.

The game has never crashed on me. It might in future of course, but it's not part of the experience, like with certain other games. The balance seems pretty well done. Having a turret as an engineer isn't an instawin like in other games, it's more like a decoy that can shoot. The graphics have held up pretty well in my opnion, although some of the animations are a little janky.

The only real weakness is the sound of the guns, which sound incredibly plniky and/or tinny. All other sound design is fine.

There is another complaint folks might have: The game UI feels kind-of half-finished, like it's all indie placeholder stuff. I like it because it's easy to read at a glance, and I reckon you can't really go wrong with minimalism. The actual layout is fine, no issues there, everything is where it should be.

The game itself is basically a series of Counter-Stirke-esque missions: Free the prisoner, hack the safe, hold the area, all that great stuff. Every mission has multiple objectives, but if you play well enough you might finish the map by completing the first objective (the first mission is a good example of this).

You can replay the missions whenever/if you want. You need to beat a mission to play the next one, which seems fair enough to me.

There's a basic challenge mode, and also a few dedicated tutorials, as well as a simple primer to get you started. You have a set number of missions for free (8 per faction, I think), a handful more if you buy the reaasonably-priced DLC. 

Sidenote - this game has the perfect pricing for DLC in my opnion. Just thought I'd mention that. This is one of the few games in existence where I wish they'd make more DLC, but sadly that ain't happenig.

The atmosphere of desolation is as thick as molasses and just as delectable. Uplifting radio stations juxtapose it in a way that creates a wistful dissonance. Exploration is as free flowing as the interactivity. There are many choices to make, builds to try out, and unique places to go. It is easy to get lost in the experience and forget yourself. Much of the lore is experienced organically and poses intriguing questions. Despite being a chaotic open world it still manages to be well paced. There is something special about the loop of exploration, rare treasure hunting, character progression, questing and combat that pushes the player forward. Also you can mod the absolute bajeezus out of it. Modders basically made entire additional games to play.

However...dialogue really doesn't fit the setting and the leaves the characters feeling almost disconnected to it. Worldbuilding makes no sense. Combat is clunky, and eventually everything is a bullet sponge. So definitely don't go to Project Purity with Dad until after you've finished wandering around the main map, otherwise it's reavers, overlords, and albinos all the way down. Most of the expansions are a combat slog. Useful weapon variety is a bit low. It's so imbalanced you can max out everything and still get dumpstered unless you are ready to spam stimpaks. Oh well, can't win em' all.

Fallout 3 est un excellent jeu !
Malgré son âge (2008 tout de même), il reste parfaitement jouable sur des configurations PC assez modestes, même les plus anciennes. Il est particulièrement fluide, ne souffre quasiment d'aucun ralentissement et peut même accueillir de nombreux mods sans forcément mettre votre machine en détresse. 
Certes, graphiquement, le jeu a pris un petit coup de vieux, mais cela n'enlève rien à ses qualités. C'est justement ce qui fait son charme : contrairement à Fallout 4 ou Fallout 76, beaucoup plus exigeants en matière de configuration, Fallout 3 reste accessible à un très grand nombre.
Et puis franchement, pour seulement 20 € avec le jeu de base et l'ensemble de ses DLC, difficile de trouver à redire sur le rapport qualité-prix !
Cependant, il y a un gros point négatif qui me déçoit particulièrement : l'absence totale de succès Steam:
Ayant auparavant joué à Fallout 3 sur Xbox 360, j'avais pris l'habitude de retrouver ce petit plaisir de débloquer des succès au fil de l'aventure. C'est peut-être un détail pour certains, mais pour moi, cela fait partie intégrante de l'expérience de jeu. Avoir un objectif supplémentaire, découvrir qu'on vient de débloquer un succès après une quête ou une action particulière, c'est toujours gratifiant !
Malheureusement, sur cette version Steam, aucun succès n'est disponible. Je trouve cela vraiment dommage, car cette absence enlève une petite dimension au gameplay et rend parfois la progression plus monotone. C'est d'autant plus regrettable qu'une fonctionnalité aussi simple aurait parfaitement trouvé sa place dans cette version PC.

**En résumé : un excellent RPG, accessible, fluide et généreux en contenu, mais dont la version Steam aurait vraiment mérité un système de succès.**

Никогда не играл в первые две части игры. И познакомился впервые именно с третьей частью. Fallout и Stalker с детства были любимыми для меня играми хоть и не совсем мой сеттинг. Наверное постапокалиптическая Америка для будет все же ближе. Fallout 3 не любят фанаты старых частей, фанаты Нью-Вегаса что это Вегас но хуже и не фанаты более новых частей. Игра во многом забылась среди всей франшизы, но как по мне, это лучшая часть серии. Fallout 3 лучше всего попадает в атмосферу пустоши и пост ядерной войны. Под радио Новостей Галактики, стычками с рад-скорпионами и рейдерами вы размеренно блуждаете по остаткам когда-то великой цивилизации. 
Геймплейно это тот же Вегас, да может предметов поменьше, рецептов крафта маловато и квесты где-то слабее Вегаса. Но в ограниченности и первопроходца тройки и создается что-то такое уникальное, что завлекает меня проходить эту игру раз в несколько лет. 
Сюжет как и во всех частях. Кто-то кого-то ищет и скучновато, хотя глобальная цель и конфликт у этой части лучше чем у всех последующих. Учитывайте, что это игра от Беседки и сюжеты никогда не были сильной стороной их игр.
Главная проблема на сегодня это хромая работоспособность. У меня за примерно 80 часов игра вылетела раз 7 и один раз словил софтлок. Притом запускалась всегда хорошо, что можно сказать очень повезло. Термин "пердолинг" хорошо подходит к объяснению, что ждет большинство игроков желающих поиграть. К сожалению все не кончается смешной физикой движка. Ну я про сюжет рассказал, но у тройки сеттинг в целом странный. Анклав, что кажется был уничтожен в первых частях появился снова. События происходят в 2277 году, спустя двести лет после ядерки. Но мир выглядит словно бахнуло лет 30-50 назад. Самая важная миссия и потребность это базовая чистая вода. Города до сотни человек в лучшем случае, некоторые поселения как Арефу живут в целом три семьи и таких мест хватает как Города детей например. 
Короче изливаю в отзыве, что этот фолыч хорош, если он у вас работает, то стоит дать ему шанс и проникнуться прогулками по пустошам с лутингом локаций. Да игра неидеальна, да работает как говно, и да он слабее Вегаса и может быть даже слабее Четвёрки. Но это все тоже прекрасное приключение. И я супер кайфнул снова окунуться в эту вселенную. Просто попробуйте, проигнорируйте общий хейт и почетный возраст игры. 
Ах да, обязательно берите GOTY версию. Дополнения с Питтом и Поинт-Лукаутом просто шикарны, да и другие не так плохи как я их запомнил.

Fallout 3 was a massive departure from the original games but one that I think deserves recognition. taking the series away from California and giving us an entirely new setting in the ruins of Washington DC. For the first time, we got to experience the wasteland in full 3D. Being able to explore the world, come acrross abandoned buildings, discover hidden locations, and go into places that at 1st seemed insignificant made exploration one of my favourite aspects of the game. It genuinely feels like almost every corner of the map has something worth investigating. Whether it's an abandoned subway station, a forgotten settlement, or some obscure location hidden away from the main roads, there's always something to discover. The presentation of Washington DC is a highlight to. The destroyed monuments, collapsed buildings, and total urban devastation create a fantastic visual representation of what nuclear annihilation might leave behind or what places like the Boneyard might look like ifit were in 3D. The atmosphere is something I love & appreciate. The music, ambient sounds, and environmental storytelling.  the radio adds personality to the world. Having Three Dog report on events happening throughout the wasteland occasionally commenting on my own actions, makes the world feel more connected and alive. The characters are also quite memorable, and I enjoyed encountering the different personalities and communities throughout the Capital Wasteland.

However there are a few things I would have changed. 
1.My biggest disappointment was the decision to reuse the Enclave and essentially revisit a very similar conflict from FO2. After being in the previous game I would have preferred something entirely new rather than another confrontation with the remnants of the American government. There was so much potential for a different antagonist and a new ideological conflict.

2.Another issue I had was the radio. While I enjoy the music and Three Dog's commentary, I sometimes feel it undermines the atmosphere. There are moments where the game should feel quiet unsettling or genuinely somber... but instead I'm listening to upbeat music while exploring the ruins of a destroyed civilization. I would have preferred the music to be tied to functioning radios throughout the world, rather than constantly broadcasting from a device on my wrist. Music has its place, but I think FO3 could have benefited from allowing its environmental atmosphere and silence to speak for themselves.

3.The story also suffers from a overly simplistic good versus evil. One thing I appreciated about FO1 was the ability side with antagonist even if that ment the game ending much sooner and not being cannon. FO3 doesnt offer freedom. President Eden even acknowledges that you might be immune to the FEV because of your upbringing in Vault 101 and even mentions i could perhaps replace the colonel! which makes me wonder why joining the Enclave wasn't a genuine possibility. I would have loved to see the game allow players to pursue that path!

4.I also really missed the ending slides. Fallout 1/2 and eventually New Vegas all showed how your decisions affected the various settlements, characters and factions throughout the world. It gave your choices weight and made completing the game feel like the conclusion to a much larger journey. FO3s ending feels considerably less personal. I would have loved to see what happened to the places and people I encountered depending on the decisions I made.

5.Lastly, I found the climax and final confrontation disappointing. Liberty Prime is certainly impressive to look at but it ends up doing so much of the fighting that the final encounter lacks the personal intensity I expect. Colonel Autumn never really feels like the intimidating antagonist the story needed, and the final confrontation doesnt feel like the encounters with the Master inFO1 or the Enclave in FO2.

Despite these criticisms, I genuinely enjoyed FO3. It brought the Fallout universe into 3D, introduced an huge world to explore, and created an incredibly memorable interpretation of post apocalyptic America. I also think it's important to remember that this was bethessdas first attempt at bringing the series into an entirely new dimension now having to imagine what everything shoulld look like 3D, with a new development team and a very different approach to RPG design. Though i feel like they should learned alot after the release of FONV sadly that never happened and it declined as a series from FO4 onwards.

Fallout 3 may not have captured everything I loved about the original games, but it introduced a new way to experience the wasteland, and for that, I think it deserves credit.

Меня сильно оскорбило однажды заявление одного сотрудника Bethesda о Fallout New Vegas. Мол, все лавры достались этой игре, а ведь оригинальные разработчики дали богатый инструментарий для Obsidian.  Дали им основу, на которой они построили свой шедевр, а люди проигнорировали этот великий вклад. 

А чё вы дали-то? Убогий движок, где шаг влево, шаг вправо - вылет на рабочий стол. Убогую графику, которая не делает мир Пустоши хоть в какой-то мере интересным и захватывающим местом? Или убогую стрельбу, от которой нельзя получить удовольствие. Ну тут как говорится, спасибо, папаша. Всё, чё дала Беседка Obsidian'ам - это товарный знак. Всё! Ещё раз повторяюсь...

Поэтому я и поражаюсь этим нездоровым нарциссизмом Тодда Говарда и Ко. Тут же не вопрос в возрождении серии, типа, хорошо, спасибо, что возродили; тут же вопрос в объективной реальности. Я ни грамма не сомневаюсь во всех этих слухах про то, что Тоддя ненавидит Нью-Вегас. Но, братишка, тройка полный отстой. Это не вина Обсидиан, что вы налажали.  

Давайте на чистоту, я прекрасно понимаю, что в ВСЖ пространстве это первый Фоллач у людей, первое их знакомство с серией, и у меня тоже. И я тоже безумно кайфовал от тройки, когда был школьником, у которого не было чувство вкуса. Но давайте снимем пелену ностальгии. 

Сюжета, на самом деле, кот наплакал. Большую часть времени я просто потратил на отстрел врагов в разных ветках метро. Большая часть игры - это шутер, причём ужасный. Это отвратительная стрельба. Отвратительный импакт. Отвратительная милишка. И нет никакой продуманной РПГ системы: ты так или иначе прокачаешь все навыки, а полезные перки практически все будут собраны под финальный уровень, потому бездарные геймдизайнеры не смогли придумать перковую систему, где перки действительно полезны, а не просто прибавляют тебе очков навыков, которые ты все равно соберёшь с помощью журналов.

В Нью-Вегасе практически куда бы ты не зашёл, всегда есть либо интересный квест, либо НПС с интересной историей, либо лорные записки, в тройке большая часть локаций пустые, когда дело касается сюжета. Культовые американские места по типу Капитолия - это просто локация с кучей врагов. Нет никакого хотя бы крошечного квеста, который был дал мотивацию туда заглянуть. Просто наваленная куча врагов - и так 90 процентов локации. Это позор.

Да и сюжет не самый выдающийся, сделанные на отшибись. Непропачтенная концовка, где хотели навалить драмы, но при этом оставили спутинков, из-за которых вся драма превратилась в комедию, о многом говорит.

91 балл на Метакритике. 91 балл. За что? Не понятно. Долгое время я действительно не мог понять, почему, пока многочисленные скандалы с игровыми журналистами не всплыли наружу. Я, вот кстати, только недавно узнал, как Тоха Жирный облизывал третий фоллач, а сам даже не прошел ветку квестов с Три-Дог-Найтом. Теперь понятно, почему 91 балл. Чемонданчики в виде бесплатных поездок на презентации, ранние пресс-релизы и дорогие коллекционки это очень хорошо. Играть мы в это не будем, конечно же, но балл высокий поставим.

Мне ещё предстоит сыграть в ДЛС для тройки, тут я лишь рассказал впечатления от основной игры. Все, за что стоит благодарить тройку, это то, что благодаря ей вышел Нью-Вегас. За остальное благодарить не буду. А ну еще за рассказ про хардкорный гейминг и Спотыкушку. Не было бы этой игры, не было бы этой истории.

It's better than New Vegas.

Which seems counterintuitive given that NV was built on the guts of Fallout 3. I started playing Fallout 3 after I'd already beat New Vegas (and attempted but given up on a second playthrough because of how lifeless it is), and I was surprised to find that despite 3 being older, it actually fixed almost every problem I had with its sequel.

The map was one of the biggest improvements (or rather, it was one of the biggest downgrades in NV since that came later). For one thing, it actually feels like a post nuclear wasteland, rather than an old-west desert with the occasional robot or mutant. Funny how that's possible in a post nuclear roleplaying series. I particularly liked the ruined megastructures, which do a lot to add some scale to the environment, and the green tint that makes it feel as if even the air around you is hazardous. This is also one of the rare cases in which I think the low graphical quality almost works to the games benefit, where it looking a bit uglier still suits the 'hostile wasteland' environment. The best part of the map though is that you can stand pretty much anywhere and see half a dozen or more POIs nearby that look like they might be worth exploring. I was able to constantly detour on my way to each objective, which lead to me encountering many more characters and questlines; a stark contrast to NV where I felt like I was actively disincentivized from going anywhere except directly to my next objective marker.

Another major highlight is performance. I'm currently on my third playthrough, almost 30 hours in, and the only technical problems I've run into are a single crash to desktop and some more than playable frame rate drops in Mothership Zeta due to engine limitations. Again, a huge improvement over New Vegas's constant crashes every 15-20 minutes. It's meant that I can actually enjoy playing the game without needing to worry about losing heaps of progress.

I also preferred the story and dialogue. Voice performances have been mostly great, and I haven't noticed any that sounded outright bad. The set up to the plot makes more sense: you're born and raised in a vault, and have to venture out into unfamiliar territory to track down your Dad (someone who you've already had several gameplay interactions with prior to this point). You can help the other factions you run into, but they still pull their weight. Compare that to New Vegas, where you're shot in the head (something that probably would've instantly killed anybody else), buried alive (again, this would've killed anybody else), revived and restored to full health for free by a complete stranger who then gives you one of the most invaluable items in the wasteland for free and sends you on your merry way. From there, every major faction (most of whom are powerful enough to have influence over an entire region/part of the continent) treats you a like the most important thing in the universe, trusting you to do all the work for them and forgiving you of all your crimes against them (including slaughtering hundreds of their soldiers and dropping a literal nuclear bomb on them) just for a chance to talk to you.

Fallout 3 is of course not perfect by any means. Combat is still terrible, and is one of the games weakest elements. The only good inclusion (exclusion?) is the lack of iron sights, which at the very least didn't give me false confidence that my bullets would hit exactly where I was aiming. And as mentioned earlier, the game still doesn't look particularly good even if the look it has suits its setting. There are many older games that look and play a lot better, and have held up years later in ways that Fallout 3 simply can't.



However, I think the best thing about Fallout 3 isn't the game itself; it's that the fanbase seemingly consists of mostly regular people who just like playing a good game. I haven't had many interactions with other Fallout 3 players, but I have noticed a distinct lack of certain behaviours that would otherwise be a regular occurance amongst one other fanbase in particular

- No being told that you're "not a real Fallout fan" just because you like a game made by Bethesda
- No schizoid rants about how Todd Howard manipulated review scores to avoid payouts to Obsidian, or his supposed decade spanning grudge against the developers he's previously said he has great respect for
- No constant repeats of the same 'jokes' (IE: lines of contextually irrelevant game dialogue stated verbatim) that were never funny in the first place
- No derailments of discussions about other topics to forcefully make them about your favourite game
- No bold declarations that the game is the greatest thing to ever exist and anyone who disagrees is an illiterate, uncultured moron
- No delusional fantasies about what the game could've been like if it had 3x as much development time, which have slowly warped into a genuine belief that this is what the game is truly like

And most importantly, the fanbase as a whole doesn't feel like a complete circlejerk. Case in point, the top recent review for Fallout 3 is a negative one, saying that the game crashes on startup and it can't be fixed despite hours of effort, with a comment thrown it at the end criticising Bethesda for not maintaining a game they're selling. 160+ helpful votes. Fair complaints, given that it's an older game running on newer hardware. However, the top recent review for New Vegas is a positive one that says the exact same thing: the game crashes on startup and can't be fixed despite hours of effort, but it's still perfect in every way and this is a testament to the reviewers love for the game. 110+ helpful votes, no comment on Obsidians decision to continue selling a broken game that not only doesn't work today, but also didn't work when it released.

It truly gets to a point where you've gone beyond obsessing over a game, and are instead totally unwilling to accept the concept of other people not feeling the same way, or that the game might not actually be as flawless as you've deluded yourself into thinking. When every minor criticism or nitpick of a game is met with immediate, visceral backlash, it becomes clear that you've reached that point. Fallout 3's fanbase is a much more mellow one, content with quietly enjoying the game they like, and I can respect them in that regard. It's a game that I don't regret playing, and one that I can see myself coming back to.

本作最突出的价值在于选择与后果的落实程度。玩家在莫哈韦废土中面对的不是简单的善恶二分，而是新加州共和国、凯撒军团、豪斯先生及独立路线之间的意识形态取舍。每一个主要势力的任务线都包含道德灰色地带，最终结局以幻灯片形式逐项反馈玩家在各聚落与派系中的具体行为。这种将宏观政治格局与微观个体决策相勾连的设计，在2010年的RPG中属于前列水准，即便置于今日，其叙事密度仍值得肯定。但主线本身流程并不长，直通核心路线约在五小时左右，真正的体量在于支线与势力任务编织出的网状结构
属性与技能系统支持较为充分的角色分化。口才、修理、科学等非战斗技能在任务解决路径中具有实质价值，而非装饰性选项。比如修理技能尤为关键，50点解锁武器修理工具包制作，90点后可实现武器互修，直接影响中前期的资源管理节奏。Perk系统的选择密度较高，但原版每两级获取一个Perk的节奏偏慢，部分Build的成型期较长。硬核模式引入的弹药重量、饥渴睡眠需求，进一步强化了资源规划的严肃性，但也放大了引擎本身在物品管理上的不便
Gamebryo引擎的局限在本作中体现得尤为明显。即便在社区补丁的辅助下，崩溃与卡顿仍偶有发生，射击手感缺乏反馈力度，NPC寻路与AI逻辑在复杂地形中表现不稳定。画面水准停留在fo3同期水平，人物动画僵硬，场景加载频繁。这些问题并非吹毛求疵，在三十六小时的游玩过程中，技术瑕疵持续干扰沉浸感，属于必须纳入评价的扣分项
最后总而言之，FNV仍然是不可多得的优秀RPG！

This masterpiece of roleplaying choices and worldbuilding consequences is genuinely without parallel. The fact that it was ever created, let alone under the circumstances that limited development, is bewildering. Everything matters in Fallout: New Vegas. There's so much substance I almost wish it had more filler just to feel like I could wander around aimlessly.

Characters are thought provoking without even trying. Just the level of attention to detail that cements their role is enough to make one wonder about the world. Factions are layered, interconnected, have history and a clear trajectory into the future that you get to shape. Quests are unique and branching to the point that it is easy to remember nearly all of them off the top of your head after just one playthrough. The setting is deeply thought out, and fully committed to its lore.

Even the weakest of the four expansions (HH) is among the best of all time for games in general. Dead Money is super polarizing though. Kind of like how its atmosphere is so thick you can cut it with a knife...while it suffocates you and corrodes your skin. You will probably hate it before you love it. That's why it is mislabeled as the worst of the four. If you go in expecting a brutal survival experience that requires you to tryhard it then it may even be Fallout at its absolute peak. There are many tricks to make it easier, like certain perks, or having melee/unarmed skill. Or you could just cheat yourself out of a great experience with mods.

Themes are razor sharp, yet effortlessly conveyed and worked into the gameplay. Comedy is plentiful and never in conflict with the setting or its themes, and generally ends up reinforcing both. A western atmosphere primes the player for so much of what happens in game that getting over-invested in the setting is trivial. The radio stations help. They may not be as immediately grabby as Fallout 3, but if you give them a chance (BLACK MOUNTAIN RADIO FOREVER) it is honestly incredibly fitting and still has that same dissonant charm.

Builds are creative and varied, not solely focused on fighting, and it definitely helps to have so much interesting unique gear to try out. The world reacts to your choices throughout the game. It thoroughly rewards the player for being thorough. There are tonnes of branching paths that independently factor into a complex ending. Replay value is insane. Also this might just have the best array of mods for any game ever...I just wish it was as easy to mod as it used to be--cuz it keeps getting more complicated due to frustrating individuals...

What a game. I played almost exclusively on Steamdeck and played to completion through the vanilla un-modded game and all dlc’s. I did 119 quests and visited every location with a map marker on the map. I had a great time.

Story was solid from the beginning and I appreciated how it branched out and opened new possibilities as you progressed. There is a wealth of content here and I’m not even sure how much of it I missed based on my story choices. You don’t see a lot of current day games that so clearly give you competing options for resolution that really make you sit down and think about what path you want to take. And then new options open up depending on dialogue choices and your skillset too. One I guy I tried duking it out with in a firefight turned into an ally against a third party after I died and reloaded my save and tried a different dialogue option when talking to him instead. I would have never even known that was a possibility and how many of these instanced did I miss!? That low rumbly sound every time you uncovered a new quest and the name of it rolled across the screen…..so good. I also felt pretty satisfied with the ending of the story too and how my choices played out. I think Obsidian did a really nice job of some simple cutscenes and dialogue to wrap up story elements whenever you finished a large segment or dlc. 

Combat and movement were ok but probably the weakest part of this game. Looking back now it seems like even some basic mods might have smoothed this out a bit, but the game was still very playable vanilla. I relied almost exclusively on VATS for all combat and was quite satisfied with it overall. Shoot an enemies gun out of their hand and they drop it and go running for it. Cripple legs and they can barely walk. It might have been a partial result of perks I decided to take but I ended up level 50 with more than enough skill points to fully max out a couple different abilities and I think it almost detracted from the gameplay a bit. I think I had 6 or 7 skills maxed out at 100 and while it did open the door for a lot of play style flexibility, it was almost so many points that my decisions didn’t feel like they carried a whole lot of weight anymore. There was a huge variety of guns and weapons and armor though which was fun to sort through and try out the different options. 

Graphics and presentation were ok and I didn’t feel like they detracted from my experience playing it so many years after release. I do wish there were more graphics and game settings to adjust, and a quick save button would have been amazing, but I managed just fine without these things. I did have a fair number of game crashes and from reading up on this more after I finished playing it sounds like some crucial mods address this. 

New Vegas was a game I never played through on original release after I played through Fallout 3, but I’m very happy with my play through now and thoroughly enjoyed my time with it. Would highly recommend.

Hunted: The Demon’s Forge это классический экшн от третьего лица с легким налетом рпг элементов от малоизвестной американской студии inXile Entertainment, и данную игру я могу назвать максимально стандартной для седьмого поколения консолей, со всеми вытекающими отсюда плюсами и минусами.
Как я уже говорил ранее перед нами экш от третьего лица с элементами рпг, игрок волен выбирать между двумя персонажами - эльфийкой Э’ларой и человеком по имени Каддок, переключаться между ними можно в определенных точках на карте по своему выбору. Геймлей за них не сказать чтобы прям сильно отличался, единственное что Каддок делает ставку на ближний бой и будет чуть живучее, эльфийка же может использовать разные типы луков от скорострельного как автомат, до крайне медленных, но с хорошим дамагом. Для каждого персонажа можно качать активные спецспособности, есть две ветки - одна из них рассчитана на профильное оружие персонажа, то есть меч или лук, вторая универсальная и представляет из себя примитивную атакующую магию. Арсенал в игре не богат и все отличие в одном и том же классе оружия сводится с разным цифрам дамага, даже те же мечи и топоры не отличаются какими либо мувсетами или другими особенностями. Противников по игре не сказать что большое разнообразие, особенно это заметно в самом начале, во второй половине ситуация становится получше, тем более разработчики достаточно грамотно миксуют врагов на аренах. Дизайн локаций представляет из себя прямую кишку с очень редкими необязательными ответвлениями, пройдя которые можно получить какое нибудь редкое мощное оружие. Иногда встречаются головоломки, но какой либо сложности и интереса они как правило не вызывают. Так же на сколько мне известно в игре есть кооператив на двух человек, но лично я ничего не могу сказать по этому поводу так как не проверял.
Сюжет игры представляет из себя стандартное темное фентези, где мир подвергается нападению орд монстров, а два главных героя - наемника изначально просто хотят поживиться золотом, но в конце концов приходят к героическому избавлению мира от зла, не могу сказать что сюжет плох, скорее он крайне клиширован. Так же частички лора, если это можно так назвать, игрок может получать находя останки людей и призывая их призраков, дабы узнать щепотку полезной или не очень информации. Каддок и Э'лара пусть и не особо глубоко прописаны, но получились весьма неплохо, особенно радуют их постоянные подколы друг друга и комментарии тех или иных событий, от чего ощущаются они не как картонные болванчики. Остальные немногочисленные персонажи появляются в игре крайне редко и чем либо не запоминаются. В игре присутствуют несколько концовок и какая у Вас будет зависит лишь от того, принимал ли один или оба персонажа слэг - таинственную серебристую жидкость дающую огромную силу, но я не знаю кем надо быть чтобы с самого начала не понять подвоха с ее употреблением.
С технической стороны у игры все в порядке, каких либо багов или фризов я не встретил. Графика в игре на момент времени выхода достаточно посредственная, работа художников обильно сдобрена стандартным для того времени коричнево-серым светофильтром, хотя могу отметить что самыми слабыми локациями как по мне являются первые две главы, потом становится поинтереснее. Музыка просто нормальная, когда надо звучат эпичные треки, в моменты где надо немного нагнать жути звучит атмосферный эмбиент, все неплохо, но абсолютно не запоминается. Ну и как итог - если перетерпеть первые пару часов игры, то перед нами вполне нормальный, пусть и не хватающий звезд с неба продукт своей эпохи и играть в него или нет решать только Вам, как по мне учитывая его продолжительность не более 10 часов и невысокую цену на распродажах, то на 5-6 вечеров вполне себе просто нормальная игра.

Hunted: THE DEMON'S FORGE is a game i remember just seeing places. Rental store when I was young, and also seeing it later when I was a conscious human at a flea market and going "what even is this crap". Not until recently when I saw I could get it for extremely cheap online that I was like "yeah okay, lets pour more knowledge in my Alexandria Brain".

Hunted: THE DEMON'S FORGE is a game developed by InXile, who started by making that Bard's Tale game in 2004, then they made some flash games/mobile games until 2011 when this game was made. Then they made Wasteland 2, Tides of Numenera, and then get taken hostage by the bumbling entity known as Microsoft. In this first foray into a console game since 2004, they decided to make a co-op game where you actually "Work" together instead of just "play together" (the quotes they have on Wikipedia). What does this mean for the design of the game? Well Its what I wouldnt expect it to be, a cover shooter à la Gears of War, but with some hack and slash too.

Even with the surprise factor of that, this game is pretty boring. I enjoy the pulpiness of the main characters being scantily clad hot fantasy guy and girl, but besides that it is a pretty generic Tolkien-esque fantasy setting form what I saw. Combat isn't great, as it has both hack and slash and Arrow Cover shooting it just flops on both ends with no oomph. There are kind of "neat" (in the context of a cover shooter) puzzles to solve in the maps, but the maps themselves are pretty meh to explore.

My friend says this was the worst game he's ever played. But how can that be true? You play as Mr. Inbetween... oh, but I guess he had to play as the elf... nobody likes elves... everyone wants to be the man... the man... everyone... just ignore this games community page.

Hunted: The Demon's Forge is a jank RPG from 2011 that is halfway to being a good game. With voice acting from Laura Bailey, Lucy Lawless and Graham McTavish in the main roles we're treated to surprisingly competent work in that department for what is clearly a low budget bargain bin title. The important female characters are hilariously oversexualised, the gameplay is super basic, graphics are solid for the time period but dated now and there were a lot more puzzles and secrets than I expected, which I didn't enjoy so much. 

You play as either the ranger E'lara (voiced by Laura Bailey), seemingly the last living elf, or the human warrior Caddoc (voiced by Graham McTavish). Early on you encounter Seraphine (voiced by Lucy Lawless), a ghostly sorceress who offers to share her power with you as she guides you a great evil that you must defeat. Combat is your typical hack n slash as caddoc and the game turns into a third person shooter as E'lara. The movement and cover system feels very similar to gears of war, and you will need to use it if you play as E'lara becuase she is not very tanky. 

The character upgrade system is pure cheeks, and not the nice ones they spent way too much time making for E'lara and Seraphine, level design is often pretty bad, the loot system sucks (you have no real inventory and there isn't a merchant system in place), your consumables are ridiculously limited and it takes ages to earn more item slots, items can easily get stuck in the ground so you might not even get the tiny bit of loot you need to survive and rather than doing something interesting with the gold you can find in the campaign it is only used in the online mode that was tied to GameSpy, whose services were fully shut down in May 2014. 

Even on easy difficulty, this game gets too hard for how jank it is. You can easily get stunlocked, it controls kinda poorly, they just keep throwing enemies at you mindlessly, and there are some awful hold out sections that exist solely to tempt you into drinking a silver liquid called Sleg. It is worth noting that if either character drinks Sleg even once you are automatically locked into a bad ending. Your AI partner does not drink Sleg on their own, thankfully. I managed to get through it without trying the stuff, because I'd looked up what would happen after passing the first of these holdout sections without it and decided I would stubbornly get the good ending. 

I'll be here forever if I keep going, so I'll quickly finish up and recap what I've already said.

The good:
Voice acting for important characters is well done, and passable for side characters
Sometimes the dialogue is amusing, even if its usually in a so bad it's good way
E'lara and Caddoc are pretty likeable, I was fond of them and their friendship dynamic
The gameplay is fun enough to make up for the game's shortfalls, especially once it clicked and I figured out how to properly play as E'lara

The mid: 
The puzzles really aren't great
Graphically it looks a bit rough by modern standards, can't knock it too hard though as it would have been fine for the time
The story is okay, mostly
The game's length is pretty much perfect for what it is
Enemy/character design balances out to be okay, some are really cool but most are generic and boring

The bad:
Level design is usually terrible
Controls kinda suck
Jank game full of bugs
Chapters are too long (although with frequent checkpoints)
Loot system sucks, could use a merchant system
Character skill/ability development is terrible
Bossfights mostly suck, the one good bossfight was pretty much stolen from Gears of War
Weird difficulty curves, it feels like a rollercoaster at times
The online and some parts of the offline are nonfunctional due to GameSpy dependence

Overall I don't feel like it's worth more than a 4 or a 5 out of 10 for quality, but the fun rating was a solid 7/10 for me. The full price is fair, but if you can get it on sale I would recommend doing that instead. Originally I was going to keep this in the "keep installed" section of my library as I figured I would try the level selection and maybe hunt down all the collectibles, but as I thought about this game some more before reviewing I realised I don't really care about that and don't want to play the game again.
