To all the new players that came from Kai and Duke's stream, read this review. I've been playing this game on console since 2015 so ik what im talking about.

When you start, you can pick to be a hero or a villain, and that choice completely shapes your experience based on your mentor. If you choose the hero side, you get to roll with mentors like Batman, Superman, or Wonder Woman. If you go villain, you get Lex Luthor, Circe, or the Joker. Your mentor changes your starting city, your main gear sets, and the missions you get, which makes replay value crazy good.

This game is definitely dated, but it is still so good if you are a massive DC fan. The sheer amount of content they have packed into this game over the years is insane, and honestly, this might actually have the best customization in any video game ever made. The style system is incredibly deep and lets you look exactly how you want. Plus, once you equip something, you have that unlocked as a permanent style that you can change to even when you're not wearing that actual gear piece. You never have to sacrifice your stats just to keep a dope outfit.

Being able to freely explore iconic cities like Metropolis and Gotham is amazing. The lore runs so deep, and they pull so much straight out of the actual comic books, which is exactly what fans have always wanted from a superhero game.

They even have the Batman Who Laughs in the game now, and he is cool asf. Seeing newer, darker comic storylines like that get brought to life in an MMO is awesome.

The combat definitely lacks modern updates, and the same goes for the graphics. Though to be fair, the graphics actually aren't even bad for real, they just could look so much better now that time has passed and we have access to way stronger CPUs and GPUs.
Also, the microtransactions are kinda ridiculous if we are being honest, but thankfully you are not forced to buy them 
to enjoy the game.

On the bright side, the voice acting is fairly decent, at least for some of the main characters (I absolutely love how the Joker sounds in this game). Plus, all the different powers you can choose from are so cool. You get to play with unique abilities and not just the standard powers you see all the time in every other game. 

They have some insanely dope magic-based powers like Sorcery and Celestial where you can literally summon guardians, distort reality, or use dark and light magic to kill everything. They also have crazy elemental stuff like Fire and Ice, and wild power sets like Rage where you channel the Red Lantern light.

And even after all this which sounds pretty great dont it? 

You get to pick if u want super speed, acrobatics, or flight. Exploring the world with those movement types feels completely different for each one. Plus, even after you get past all the dope power sets, you still have an awesome weapon selection that feels great to use.

The community in this game is also really great. Since it's been around for so long, you have a lot of veterans who are genuinely down to help out newer players, run older content with you, and show you the ropes when you're trying to figure out your builds.

If you love the DC universe, you have to try it out.

[h1]DC Universe Online[/h1]

[b]Gêneros:[/b] Ação, Aventura, Multijogador Massivo, RPG
[b]Avaliação na Steam:[/b] Very Positive, com 22.078 avaliações
[b]Preço:[/b] Gratuito

[b]Visão geral[/b]
DC Universe Online oferece aos jogadores a oportunidade de criar seu próprio herói ou vilão dentro do icônico universo da DC. O jogo mistura elementos de ação e RPG, permitindo que você enfrente figuras lendárias como Batman, Superman e o Coringa. Como um título free‑to‑play, grande parte do conteúdo está disponível sem custo, mas há microtransações que podem acelerar o progresso. A proposta inicial é atraente, especialmente para fãs da franquia que buscam reviver momentos de infância. No entanto, o ritmo pode se tornar cansativo quando se avança nas missões de história e nos eventos temporários.

[b]Jogabilidade[/b]
A mecânica central gira em torno de combates em tempo real, combinando ataques corpo a corpo, habilidades especiais e uso de armas de fogo. O sistema de classes permite escolher entre poderes de energia, força bruta ou tecnologia, oferecendo certa personalização. A progressão é baseada em níveis, pontos de habilidade e equipamentos que podem ser obtidos tanto por gameplay quanto por compras na loja. Um ponto crítico é o chamado “catch‑up” que, em eventos antigos, pode exigir gasto real ou tempo excessivo para desbloquear itens, desequilibrando a experiência. Apesar disso, o modo cooperativo e as missões de arena mantêm uma boa dose de rejogabilidade, especialmente para quem gosta de jogar em grupo.

[b]Apresentação e atmosfera[/b]
Gráficos que já mostram sinais de idade, mas ainda conseguem captar a estética dos quadrinhos da DC, com cores vibrantes e personagens bem modelados. As cidades icônicas – Gotham, Metropolis e Themyscira – são bem detalhadas e ajudam na imersão. A trilha sonora combina temas heroicos com efeitos sonoros que reforçam a sensação de ação. O enredo, embora linear em partes, traz diálogos divertidos e momentos de referência que agradam fãs de longa data.

[b]Pontos positivos[/b]
[list]
[*] Mundo aberto baseado em um universo amado, cheio de personagens conhecidos.
[*] Sistema de combate dinâmico que mistura habilidades e armas.
[*] Conteúdo gratuito robusto, com muitas missões e eventos regulares.
[*] Opção de jogar como herói ou vilão, oferecendo duas linhas de história distintas.
[*] Experiência cooperativa sólida para grupos de até quatro jogadores.
[*] Atualizações frequentes que adicionam novos trajes, habilidades e áreas.
[/list]

[b]Pontos negativos[/b]
[list]
[*] Monetização que favorece quem investe dinheiro real, criando desequilíbrios.
[*] Repetitividade nas missões de história e em alguns eventos de longo prazo.
[*] Sistema de “catch‑up” que pode tornar o conteúdo antigo quase inacessível sem gastos.
[/list]

[b]Para quem é indicado[/b]
[b]Recomendado para:[/b] fãs da DC que desejam criar seu próprio super‑herói ou vilão, jogadores que apreciam MMOs gratuitos e quem gosta de conteúdo cooperativo.
[b]Pode não agradar:[/b] quem procura experiência narrativa profunda, gráficos modernos ou um modelo de negócios completamente livre de microtransações.

[b]Conclusão[/b]
DC Universe Online entrega uma experiência divertida e nostálgica para os amantes da DC, com combate satisfatório e um mundo rico em referências. Entretanto, a necessidade de investir dinheiro para acelerar o progresso e a sensação de repetição em fases avançadas podem afastar jogadores menos pacientes. No geral, o título ainda se destaca como um dos MMOs gratuitos mais completos do gênero.

[b]Nota final: 7,5/10[/b]‍

Hier hat alles angefangen. Noch bevor die Reihe mit immer größeren Raubzügen, verrückten Masken und jeder Menge Zusatzinhalten gewachsen ist, gab es dieses vergleichsweise kompakte Koop-Spiel. Und auch heute macht es noch erstaunlich viel richtig.

Das Grundprinzip ist schnell erklärt: Mit bis zu vier Spielern plant und überfallt man Banken, Geldtransporter und andere lohnende Ziele. Was zunächst wie ein einfacher Bankraub aussieht, entwickelt sich regelmäßig zu einem ausgewachsenen Feuergefecht mit immer neuen Polizeiwellen.

Besonders gefällt mir, dass Teamwork hier wirklich wichtig ist. Man muss Geiseln sichern, Türen aufbrechen, Bohrer bewachen, Munition verwalten und gefallene Mitspieler wieder auf die Beine bringen. Wer einfach allein losrennt und alles um sich herum ignoriert, wird schnell feststellen, dass das keine besonders gute Idee ist.

Die Gefechte fühlen sich angenehm direkt und intensiv an. Die Gegner setzen einen ordentlich unter Druck, und gerade auf höheren Schwierigkeitsgraden wird aus einem vermeintlich einfachen Überfall eine echte Herausforderung. Dazu kommen verschiedene Fähigkeiten und Ausrüstungsgegenstände, mit denen man seinen Spielstil anpassen kann.

Natürlich merkt man dem Spiel sein Alter inzwischen an. Die Grafik ist nicht mehr zeitgemäß, die Anzahl der Überfälle überschaubar und manche Abläufe wiederholen sich. Auch die Schwierigkeit kann gelegentlich ziemlich gnadenlos sein.

Trotzdem hat das Spiel einen ganz eigenen Charme. Es konzentriert sich auf das Wesentliche und liefert genau das, was einen guten Koop-Shooter ausmacht: spannende Situationen, knappe Rettungsaktionen und jede Menge Chaos mit Freunden.

Für mich ein gelungener Klassiker, der den Grundstein für eine ganze Reihe gelegt hat. Wer gerne gemeinsam spielt und taktische Action mag, sollte sich diesen Titel nicht entgehen lassen.

The original of the franchise, PD:TH introduces us to the core four of the Payday Gang in a less extravagant heisting experience than its sequel. Being upfront, this game is much more punishing than Payday 2 is, and is also generally a very different experience. If you've played Payday 2, prepare yourself for a very different game going into this. However, the difficulty is the fun kind, pushing you to think differently than you would in PD2 for your own survival's sake. The loadout system is also far less advanced, making every decision of your build count, both when playing solo and with others. 

The visuals have aged, sure, but in a way I'd describe as charming, an example of something I call "stylized realism" (even if most examples of it, including this one, are due to technical limitations) and something I really like. Combine this with great map design and you have yourself an absolute classic that would become the foundation for a franchise with a lot of charm, wit, and some pretty damn good heisting.

This game is excellent. It has something the other PAYDAY games don't, a very scrappy feeling with incredible chemistry between the four heisters. PAYDAY 3 tried to emulate this at launch but it was never really the same. The Heist also strikes a brilliant blend between hardcore shooter (smaller enemy counts, intelligent pushes, and precision always required to take them out) and more quality of life/arcadey elements (mainly the armour/health system). PAYDAY 3 missed the mark enormously on that front. It got them both switched up!

PAYDAY The Heist is definitely a little rough around the edges though. But it makes up for it with the sheer aura. It also runs on basically anything with a GPU nowadays. As opposed to PAYDAY 3's intense Unreal Engine graphics load. It fortunately isn't as limited by the Diesel engine as PAYDAY 2, because of its lower graphics. Honestly, I don't notice the lower texture resolution because of how gritty the art style feels.

I got this one for free back in 2013 or so and never touched it until now. Payday 2 is the one everybody loves, so I figured I’d go back and see where the cult classic started. There is no time like the present to play a 15 year old game.

I played on  normal, single player with bots,. I put in 2 hours and 36 minutes and got to the end of every mission. I didn’t technically beat them all, because I lost at the finish line more often than I’d like to admit, but close enough for me. The missions are cool and unique enough, and I get why people made this series a cult classic. The first one, where you walk in and rob a big bank, was a blast. The Diamond Heist was the highlight for me. I was also glad every level was open from the start, so I didn’t have to beat one to get to the next. The music is some good shit too. I already have a few tracks on Spotify.

Now the bad news. This game is damn hard when your teammates are bots who have no idea what is happening. In single player, if you go down, the mission is over. You can’t take over a bot to keep going, which is the dumbest thing I have ever seen. Over and over I made it to the escape prompt, went down far away from bots who move about two miles an hour, and watched the mission end. Those bots were alive and could have finished it if I could have just played as one of them. Shields are impossible to kill unless you flank them, and flanking is not really an option when 45 cops are trying to end your life.

The whole game is hurry up and wait, and too much of it is fetch quests and escort baloney. Quick, go here and put the saw up, now wait 300 seconds in a corner while bad guys try to kill you. Hope you like doing that 20 times in a row.

The shooting feels off to me. There is no hit marker, and I’m so used to one that aiming feels like painting a screen one pixel at a time. It’s so precise it started to hurt my hand, the same way painting a tiny detail makes me shake. Ammo is a problem too. There are enemies everywhere and you can carry almost nothing to shoot them with. Progression is way too slow on top of that. My first new weapon showed up at the very last mission, and it was a shotgun with 24 shots total. That is nothing for a game built around waves of enemies. Come on, guys. Give me a new toy after every mission so I can see what is out there. A grenade would have saved me so many times.

I understand why people love a glorified shooting gallery with a unique premise. I just hate boring, repetitive dump choices, and this is repetitive and hard even on normal. If you like wave shooters and playing the same thing over and over with friends, I see the appeal. By yourself, absolutely not. PC Gamer said it best when they compared playing solo with AI partners to technically drinking your own urine is a option as well. It feels like a developer’s first game, and the UI shows its age. I would love smarter bots, more customization after every mission, and a way to keep playing after I die. I’m sure they fixed this stuff in the sequel, but the first one is rough, man.

review:
PAYDAY: The Heist — Обзор

PAYDAY: The Heist — это игра, которая в 2011 году фактически создала поджанр «кооперативного Left 4 Dead про ограбления». Разработанная шведской студией Overkill Software (ныне часть Starbreeze), она предложила игрокам то, чего им так не хватало: возможность почувствовать себя героями фильма «На гребне волны» или «Схватка», планируя дерзкие налеты и отстреливаясь от спецназа SWAT.

Сюжет и концепция
В отличие от большинства шутеров, здесь нет глубокого сюжета с драмой. Вы — команда из четырех профессиональных грабителей в масках (Вулф, Даллас, Хокстон и Чейн). Ваша цель — совершать дерзкие преступления: грабить банки, угонять инкассаторские броневики, красть золото из Федерального резервного бюро или похищать кокаин из доков.
Сюжет подается через брифинги перед миссиями. Вы — плохие парни, и игра не пытается вызвать у вас сочувствие. Ваша задача — забрать деньги и уйти, оставляя за собой горы трупов спецназа.3 источника

Геймплей: Оргия свинца
Если вы играли в Left 4 Dead, вы сразу поймете, как это работает:

Волны врагов: Полиция (впоследствии спецназ FBI и GenSec) нападает волнами. Ваша задача — удерживать позиции, пока скачиваются данные или пилится дверь.
Командная работа: В одиночку выжить невозможно. Нужно лечить напарников, поднимать их, прикрывать огнем и координировать действия.
Динамические миссии: Каждое ограбление может пойти не по плану. В любой момент «тихий» стелс-подход может сорваться, и полиция пойдет на штурм. В зависимости от ваших действий, на карте появляются новые цели (например, нужно взять заложников, чтобы обменять их на товарища).2 источника
Классы и прокачка: По мере выполнения контрактов вы получаете опыт и открываете новые виды оружия (штурмовые винтовки, дробовики, снайперские винтовки) и навыки (увеличиваете здоровье, скорость перезарядки или эффективность навыков).

Атмосфера и стиль
PAYDAY: The Heist берет эстетику криминальных боевиков 90-х. Здесь нет места морали — только жестокость, тяжелая музыка и адреналин. Фраза «Coming in hot!» (Входим горячо!) стала культовой. Игра не стесняется своей жестокости: здесь можно брать заложников, связывать их и требовать выкуп.

Плюсы:

Уникальный сеттинг: Первый полноценный симулятор ограблений с видом от первого лица.
Кооператив: Игра раскрывается на 100% только в команде из четырех человек.
Атмосфера: Отличный саундтрек и ощущение «последнего дела».

Минусы:

Устаревшая графика: Даже на момент выхода игра выглядела скромно, а сегодня и подавно (особенно версия для PS3/PS4).
Повторяемость: Карт мало, и после десятка прохождений они начинают приедаться.
ИИ: Напарники-боты в сингле практически бесполезны.

Итог
PAYDAY: The Heist — это классика кооперативного гейминга. Это игра не про сюжет, а про процесс. Если у вас есть трое друзей, гарнитуры и желание ограбить банк, отбиваясь от спецназа, — это идеальный выбор. Это «Left 4 Dead для взрослых», где вместо зомби — полицейские, а вместо аптечек — мешки с деньгами.3 источника

Плюсы:
– Атмосферные и интенсивные ограбления с акцентом на кооператив
– Разнообразие сценариев (банки, склады, транспортные миссии)
– Высокая сложность, требующая координации и планирования
– Удачное сочетание шутера и тактического планирования

Минусы:
– Устаревшая графика и анимации даже для 2011 года
– Ограниченное количество карт и повторяемость геймплея
– Слабый ИИ союзников в одиночном режиме

[h1][i]“On second thought, let's not go to Camelot. It is a silly place.”[/i]
~King Arthur[/h1]

What's cool about King Arthur: The Role-Playing Wargame is that it's its makers' dream project. Let's get back to the late 2000s for a moment. The initial craze that started with Braveheart (yes, it was a movie-based game that started it all; deal with it) and was popularized in the legendary Shōgun: Total War was pretty much over. It wasn't like such games stopped appearing—exactly the opposite. What I'm trying to say is that people stopped wanting “more of the same”. They wanted the next big thing. And a young Hungarian team called NeocoreGames? They believed they knew exactly what that thing should be. Yes, the title says it all. They wanted to add an RPG element.

The publisher, on the other hand, was rather skeptical. I mean, we all know about how it can be with the young teams. Lots of them have a childish “And then, and then!..” way of thinking, which, with a lack of experience, can lead to a complete disaster and make a publisher lose money. Here's the thing, though: Neocore were not such people. They were young, sure, but they had their own in-house engine, they already worked on a prototype, and were totally ready to prove themselves. Still, Paradox didn't want an RPG; they wanted a strategy. And with no other way to break the ice, that's exactly what Neocore gave them in Crusaders: Thy Kingdom Come.

See, our guys are smart. While working on Crusaders, they pretty much worked on their dream project, King Arthur, at the same exact time. The Braveheart / Total War-like battles, units that can level up, heroes that can equip the artifacts... all of that did fit the “Total War clone” formula, [i]but[/i] at the same exact time? At the same exact time, it also served as the bricks for the future project. Which, like I said, was already in development at the same exact time. All Neocore really needed was a big “yes” from Paradox, and King Arthur was ready to rush to the finish line. And since Crusaders did manage to convince Paradox... yeah. Later the same year, King Arthur finally came out. The dream came true. Sometimes it happens.

Sure, sure, I romanticized things a bit, but honestly, why not? It's a pretty inspiring story. A story about how a dedicated team can achieve a lot simply by working hard and believing in their goal. To us players, on the other hand, the real question is – how's the game? I mean, the dudes had that grand vision and fought for it. Must be one heck of a game, huh? Well. About that.

Like I said, in its core (no pun intended), King Arthur feels (and looks) a lot like Crusaders: Thy Kingdom Come. Like, [i]a lot[/i]. Tactical battles, for example? Those are almost identical. Which isn't really a bad thing. Sure, Crusaders felt rather clunky, but it was hard not to praise things like weather affecting the units' performance. King Arthur has all that too. Except now there's a proper Risk-like “grand strategy” map, on which we can conquer provinces, collect taxes, do quests (both main and optional ones), etc. Sounds cool, right?

Well, in a way, it is. King Arthur isn't just Crusaders with more elements; it [i]is[/i] a role-playing game. First, let me praise the feature I enjoyed the most – text-based quests. Remember Space Rangers? I can't say the quests in King Arthur are nearly as deep and complicated, while sometimes they're rather frustrating (there's that one text-based quest that wants you to navigate a maze, for example, and I bloody hate it), but they're trying and I just... I love such stuff, OK? Even though such quests can be much better, it's still a really nice touch. There's also quite a lot of choices here. Like, [i]a lot[/i] of them.

Three endings aside (this game lets you choose between Christianity and two branches of the so-called Old Faith, another thing that I absolutely loved), you can be either a good ruler or a tyrant; you can choose which knights to add to your Round Table (you can have up to 12, while the game lets you choose from up to 30 heroes with the unique abilities for both tactical battles and provinces on the grand strategy map); you'll be able to give your knights wives for certain bonuses (cheesy, I know), etc. Sounds absolutely fantastic, right? It is. It sure is. Unfortunately, King Arthur also suffers from the same exact problem many other European games that dream big do. The thing is... this game can be frustrating as F.

There is a tutorial, of course, but... let's just say simply knowing how the things work is not enough to know how things [i]really[/i] work. Does that make sense to you? What I'm trying to say is that it's all about the school of hard knocks here. And it'll take quite a lot of time to learn how exactly the game responds to your actions. How to do certain tricks in battle, what's considered to be better choices on the grand strategy map... But wait, you may argue that what I'm describing is actually... you know. [i]Playing the freakin' game.[/i] Like, that's the way things are [i]supposed to be[/i]. Technically, that's correct. The problem is – it's not a fun thing to do here.

See, there are two kinds of flawed games that can still be enjoyable. First – there are games that make things absolutely clear for you and then make you suffer through rather rough execution. Like, when it's obvious to you that you need to use this specific kind of unit and make them achieve that certain task, you can deal with the tactical mission being a bit clunky and forcing you to reload for a couple of times until you'll finally manage. Now, there's the second kind. The one that has its goals vague, but is also ready to forgive mistakes. Like, “OK, you lost a hero or two, who cares, let's just continue and see what'll happen next!” The problem with King Arthur is that... it's neither. And both. At the same time.

Everything here is vague. The UI, while being heavily based on what we had in Crusaders (meaning that it's both simple [i]and[/i] confusing), simply fails to explain things to you. There aren't enough tooltips and stuff like that. Again and again, you'll need to take a guess and, of course, most of the time you'll be guessing poorly. And the game? The game will punish you for that. Did I mention that lots of things here are timed? Well, they are. Heck, your heroes can even be taken hostage, and if you won't pay the ransom in time? Poof! Dead. Ah, and no hero? No army. That's right; you can't even move your troops without a hero. That's just how this game works. It's rough, it's unpolished, and it hates you.

It's clunky too, of course. Neocore did fix some of Crusaders' problems (for example, tactical battles now come with much better speed settings to make them much more dynamic and save time), but all in all, this here is still a very clunky thing that can't compete with the big guys. Also... yeah, let's say a couple of words about this specific release. Surprisingly, multiplayer is still playable (thanks to it being based on LAN / Direct IP connection), but making this version to work on Windows 10 / 11 can be quite a challenge. It won't work on x64 systems without the so-called 4GB patch (the patch that allows the game to access more than 2GB of RAM), and if you will apply said patch, Steam will prevent you from launching the game because, well, you modified the game file. There's a way to fix that too by using third-party software called Steamless, but you've got the idea. This here is yet another one of those “Nah, we don't care!” releases that the publisher decided not to support. With everything I've said above in mind, it makes this game... let's just say that King Arthur is a history now. A tale. An inspiring one, sure, but... not the one you'll want to live through for real. You know what they say. It's fun to dream about living during the Middle Ages, but actually time-traveling there is not... really... a good idea. Because you know. The smell. And diseases.

King Arthur - The Role-playing Wargame: Прекрасный мир Артура, омраченный вылетами.

King Arthur - The Role-playing Wargame - это уникальное сочетание стратегии в реальном времени и ролевой игры, выпущенное в 2009 году. Игра предлагает захватывающую кампанию, основанную на легендах о короле Артуре, с элементами фэнтези и мифологии. Однако, как и в случае с The King's Crusade, частые вылеты могут значительно омрачить игровой процесс.

Что могло бы радовать (если бы не вылеты):

•  Уникальное сочетание жанров: King Arthur успешно объединяет элементы стратегии в реальном времени и ролевой игры, предлагая игрокам принимать тактические решения на поле боя и развивать своих персонажей за пределами битв.
•  Захватывающая кампания: Игра предлагает интересную кампанию, основанную на легендах о короле Артуре, с элементами фэнтези и мифологии.
•  Ролевая система: Игроки могут развивать своих героев, изучать новые навыки и получать доступ к мощным артефактам.
•  Тактические сражения: Битвы в King Arthur требуют тактического мышления и умелого управления юнитами.
•  Красивый мир: Игра предлагает красивый и атмосферный мир, вдохновленный кельтской мифологией.

Что омрачает игровой опыт (вылеты и прочие проблемы):

•  Частые вылеты: Это, к сожалению, самая большая проблема игры. Как и с The King's Crusade, частые вылеты без видимой причины могут сильно испортить игровой процесс.
•  Проблемы с оптимизацией: Игра может испытывать проблемы с производительностью, особенно на слабых компьютерах.
•  Несбалансированность: Некоторые юниты и навыки могут быть слишком сильными или слишком слабыми, что влияет на баланс игры.
•  Искусственный интеллект: Искусственный интеллект врагов не всегда ведет себя логично.
•  Кривая обучения: Игра может быть сложной для новичков в жанре, особенно из-за множества механик и систем.

Вердикт (с учетом проблем):

King Arthur - The Role-playing Wargame - это потенциально отличная игра с уникальным сочетанием жанров и интересной кампанией, но частые вылеты делают ее прохождение сложным и неприятным. Пока проблема с вылетами не будет решена, я не могу рекомендовать эту игру.

Рекомендации (если вы все же хотите попробовать):

•  Проверьте системные требования: Убедитесь, что ваш компьютер соответствует минимальным системным требованиям игры.
•  Обновите драйвера видеокарты: Обновите драйвера видеокарты до последней версии.
•  Запустите игру в режиме совместимости: Попробуйте запустить игру в режиме совместимости с более старой версией Windows.
•  Понизьте настройки графики: Понизьте настройки графики, чтобы улучшить производительность игры.
•  Часто сохраняйтесь: Сохраняйтесь как можно чаще, чтобы не потерять прогресс в случае вылета. Это критически важно для этой игры.
•  Поищите патчи от сообщества: Проверьте, есть ли неофициальные патчи от сообщества, которые исправляют проблемы с игрой. Это может помочь, но гарантии нет.
•  Установите неофициальный патч (если есть): Найдите и установите неофициальный патч, созданный сообществом для решения проблем с вылетами. Некоторые патчи помогают, но не все.

Оценка:

•  Без учета проблем: 8/10 - Отличная игра с уникальным сочетанием жанров и интересной кампанией.
•  С учетом вылетов: 5/10 - Интересная игра, испорченная техническими проблемами.

Shame to give this game a negative review, as its otherwise a solid 8/10. But frequent, basically unfixable, crashing on modern systems has left this older title basically unplayable. Supposedly the GOG version is more stable, but that has sadly never come over to Steam. Valve ought to make it a priority to either fix or remove from the store games that don't work. 

What this game is, though, is Warhammer: Total War-Bretonnia edition. You play as King Arthur in a Total War style campaign pitting you against your fellow Englishmen, Romans, and a whole host of monsters and baddies from English lore. Like in any classic Total War game you manage settlements and armies on the main strategy map, as well as event & decision chains which is where the 'roleplaying' aspect comes in. In battles, you control your force, wield powerful magics, try not to get blasted by the games very powerful archers, and fight your way to victory. The game nails the feel of a TW campaign, and the inclusion of both strong story elements, powerful monsters & characters, plus magic gave the game a very unique feel vs. Medieval or Napoleon, which were contemporaries of this game. One wonders if when WH1 was in development if CA took a hard look at this game, because I see a lot of that game's DNA in this. 

Beyond technical issues, though, the game always sort of lacked something. Battles were small, units are often below 50 entities. Archers are OP, so much so that there is an option in the menu to nerf them! And magics seemed to either be nukes, or do nothing, and so also never quite felt right. And of course, the whole game lacked the polish that WH1 and sequels have. It was good-but-not-great looking even at the time, and a lot has aged badly since then. But past that, this game was a winner back in the day and could be again today. IF you can get it running. I have had to give this a thumbs down simply because in my most recent play attempts I crashed repeatedly crossing the ford in the tutorial. Apparently a common problem area. The 4gb patch and the alternate launcher and EXE all have failed to resolve my troubles, so here we are. Another classic game on Steam, still up for sale, no longer working on modern systems.

Decided to review this, because despite some of it's flaws this IS still game is a masterpiece of European folklore. The thing that makes this game so worth it, is it isn't a clone of Total War. It's of more a take, that's similar to Total war but alternates so much so from the path Total War took. The management and benefit of territories there more intrinsic to the land itself and not by the buildings constructed. They can have lords appointed to different regions to make these areas more productive as well as making your Lords more loyal. There are so many widely different lords you can recruit too, they can be of the Old Faith (Pagan) or the new (Christianity) depending on your route. Some of which you have to go through fun little puzzle solving text adventures to recruit, totally being worth it. The funny thing looking back at it now, alot of the formula Creative Assembly is using now with Warhammer, this did much earlier and with greater affect. As with Total War: Warhammer things feel less distinct, but in this game everything is just oozing with history/story which immediately draws you in. Now could this game use a little bit of love? Answer is yes, it has bugs and from what I've heard has trouble playing on newer systems. But should it be overlooked absolutely not, this game is a diamond in the rough and should be treated as such.

2009年のゲームでシステム周りも2000年代の頃の古くっさい不便な洋ゲー感満載ですが慣れると味があって中身はとても面白いゲームです。
シミュレーションゲームが好きな人だけでなく、どちらかというとTRPGが好きな人のほうが楽しめるロールプレイングゲームになっています。

アーサー王というタイトル名のため誤解するかもしれませんが、このゲームに操作可能なキャラクターとしてのアーサー王は登場せず、ネームドユニットとして登場する円卓の騎士たちを操作してイングランドを舞台に領土拡張と外交及びTotal War風の戦闘をマネジメントするシミュレーション+ロールプレイングゲームになっています。また各ネームド騎士たちには魔法スキルが備わっていることがこのゲームの特徴です。ランスロット、トリスタン、ボールスといった有名な騎士はもちろんのことユーウェインやルーカンといったマイナー騎士まで登場して円卓に招き入れることが出来、オリジナルの円卓の騎士12人を結成することができます。

一応メインシナリオのクエストがあり、それに沿って進んでいくことになりますがクエストがゲームブック方式のアドベンチャーパートになっているため選択肢次第でストーリーがどんどん分岐していきます。最終的には3つくらいのエンディングに収束していくのですが途中のシナリオ分岐がどうなるかはプレイヤーの選択肢次第といったところでTRPGが好きな人は大体楽しめると思います。英語に関してはそんなに難しい言い回しもないのでスルスル読めると思いましたが、残念ながら日本語化や日本語modはないのである程度の語学力は必要かと思います。

戦闘フェイズについてはTotal Warに近い作風ですがネームドキャラクターが魔法スキルを使えることで差別化されています。バトルに関しての難易度はそんなに複雑ではなく、初期設定ではアーチャーがかなり強めに設定されているためアーチャーゲーになってます。オプション画面からアーチャーの弱体化ボタンというのがわざわざ設定されている辺り、これは意図的に強くして救済策にしてるのではないかと思われます。また一部のネームド騎士の持つ固有スキルが戦術面で超強力であるため、そいつを円卓に加えるかどうかでも難易度が下がったりします。

メインクエストと最低限必要な領土を占領しつつゲームを進めれば20～30時間程度で終わるボリュームですが、イングランド全域制圧やサブクエスト含めてランダムクエストも全部拾いながらプレイしていくと50時間を超えるボリュームになります。またDLCコンテンツのThe Saxonsを追加すると本編でアーサー王に制圧される側だったサクソン陣営に立ちイングランド南部から侵攻してくるアーサー王を迎撃する逆ポジションとしてのサンドボックスモードのゲームが遊べるようになります。こちらは完全にサンドボックスになっており、スタート時に勝利条件を10個ほど列挙されるのでそのうちの一つないし複数の条件にチェックを入れてゲームを開始することになります。例えば「全州制圧」や「ネームドキャラクターをどれか一つレベル20に上げる」「Gold/Foodを20万まで貯める」といったものがあり、複数にチェックを入れるとそれだけ条件成就の難易度が上がる仕様になっています。

非常にボリュームが多くて面白いゲームだと思いますが難点もたくさんあります。
まずシステム全体が古いため昨今のTotal Warやシミュレーションゲームを遊んだ後にプレイすると、あれが出来ないこれが出来ないというのが目につきます。戦闘中にユニットへコマンドを指示しても動き出しが遅かったり、思った通りに動かなかったり細かいストレスはあります。カメラワークも取り回しがあまり良くありません。
ゲーム内でもいくらかシステムに関する説明はありますが根本的に画面をパッと見ても知りたい情報には辿り着けません。始めた人は60Pあるオンラインマニュアルをとりあえず一読したほうがいいです。さらに言えばそのマニュアルにも書かれてない情報が画面上の小さなアイコンにカーソルを合わせることで表示される、なんてこともザラにあるので攻略したいなら最終的には海外wiki等を見てくださいということになります。
つまり大体いつものパラドゲーってやつです。

また一つのモニターで遊んでいる方には関係ありませんが、マルチモニターで並べて遊んでいる環境の方は画面外にカーソルが飛び抜けていくので注意が必要です。フルスクリーンモードのはずなのにウィンドウモードのような挙動をします。
重大な欠点として、steamにおいてインストールしてメニューからプレイボタンを押してゲームを起動すると戦闘が終わる度にゲームがクラッシュして強制終了します。毎回10分くらい掛けてた戦闘が終わる度にパーになるためそのまま遊ぶことはお勧めしません。steamのコミュニティにおいて、バグ修正プログラムが入ったランチャーとexeが配布されているのでそちらからダウンロードして上書きしてください。ゲームクラッシュに関する問題はそれで解決できます。

かなり尖ったゲームですが雰囲気は最高です。
アートワークの一枚絵はどれも素晴らしいし、クエスト・アドベンチャー部分のゲームブックはアーサー王物語の雰囲気を盛り上げるのに一役買っていてロールプレイングゲームとしてとても良いものでした。
かなり古いゲームのためほとんどの大規模セールで75%オフにされておりDLC全部合わせても1000円程度で揃います。
シミュレーションゲームとしては比較的簡単でシステム面の問題を除けば難易度的には取り付きやすいゲームになっています。
TRPGとか好きで物語を読むのが好きな人にもおすすめできます。

This is sadly one of the most astonishingly poorly balanced games I've ever played, and that's when it bothers to work. Even with every province under your control and fully researched tech tree, you can only support two standing armies, one if they're the top end troops, otherwise you begin to bleed food, and no food means no recruitment so you can't replenish those armies. Couple this with a game of whack-a-mole of False Prophets and Rebellions, both of which lead you to losing entire provinces that need to be re-conquered and it becomes a chore to play. You march your army across to one side of the map, put down the rebellions, then march them back to put down the ones that occurred while you were away, only for the ones you just re-conquered to be rebelling again by the time you get to the other side of the map. It gets in the way of the story.

Couple this with an AI that is not constrained by the same rules as the player, and frequently has four to five full armies, and a dozen partial armies of varying sizes and any and all fun you might have got out of the game evaporates - and this is on the lowest difficulty setting.

Then there's the "Runtime error" crashes after every other battle, requiring a restart of the game after each one, and this after having to edit the exe file to tone it down otherwise it's every battle. The sad thing is this game had all the ingredients for a fine wine, but instead came out tasting like battery acid. The crashes I can live with, the game starts very fast, but the balance issues suck the life out of the game and any enjoyment along with it.
Years ago, I had fun playing the campaign for a short while, but eventually the campaign became statstically impossible to win due to an endless horde of incoming spawning elite AI armies.

[h1] King Arthur - The Role-playing Wargame [/h1]
King Arthur - The Role-playing Wargame kesinlikle beklemediğim kadar zevk aldığım bir oyun oldu. Neocore, TotalWar ve Rpg türlerini, Kral Arthur mitoslarını temel alarak birleştirmeye çalışmış ve bu doğrultuda zamanında pek örneği olmayan birçok yeni mekanik denemiş.

Öncelikle oyun adından da belli olacağı gibi Kral Arthur döneminde geçiyor. Arthur efsaneleri hakkında biraz okuma yaparsanız Britanya'dan Romanın ayrıldığı, Sakson istilalarının gerçekleştiği dönemlerde geçtiğini görürsünüz efsanelerin. Bu dönemde Hristiyanlık ve Pagan inançları birlikte görülür ve iki inanca da ağır bir gizemcilikle sarmalanmıştır. Mucizeler, büyüler, tanrılar, kutsal ruhlar Britanya topraklarının her yerindedir.

Oyun geliştiricileri de bütün bu ögeleri gerçekten büyük bir başarıyla koymuş oyuna. Oyunda Old Faith/Christian RightfullvsTyrant mekaniği var. Oyun size farklı eventlar veriyor ve yaptığınız seçime göre bu çatışmada tarafınızı seçiyorsunuz yavaş yavaş. Ve buna göre de farklı üniteler ve yetenekler-büyüler açıyorsunuz. Oldfaith-rightfull bir rotadan gittiğinizde edindiğiniz üniteler ve yetenekler, Cristian-Tyrant bir rotadan gittiğiniz aldığınız ünitelerden çok farklı. Bu da oynanış süresini arttırması açısından güzel olmuş.

Oyun Total War oyunlarından kendisini ayırmak için rol yapma ögelerine fazlaca yer vermiş. Yukarıda bahsettiğim Event sistemi üzerinden Kral Arthur'un hikayesini anlamak için fazlaca çaba harcamışlar yapımcılar. Gerçekten de o dönemi ve efsaneleri detaylıca incelemiş oldukları gözlemlenebiliyor. Paradox oyunlarından tanıdığımız eventlarla kendimize farklı rotalar çizebiliyoruz. 

Oyunda artifact ve büyü sistemi var. Ordumuzun başına geçirdiğimiz Şövalyelerimizi farklı maceralara gönderiyoruz, bu sayede onlara level atlatıp statlarını dağıtıyoruz ve bunları yaparken değişik büyü yeteneklerini atayıp farklı bufflar ve özel büyüler veren artifactler bulup verebiliyoruz. 

Oyunda şövalyeler büyük yer tutuyor bu arada. Onları toplayıp yuvarlak masaya katmak da ayrı bir zevk veriyor. Yuvarlak masayı doldurmaya çalışırken farklı maceralarda farklı şövalyeleri kendimize katılmaya ikna ediyoruz. Söz gelimi A Şövalyesi gelip sizden B şövalyesine karşı yardım istiyor yada kaçırılan bir Leydi'yi kurtarmak için size başvuruyor, bu görevleri yaparak onları Yuvarlak masaya katıyorsunuz Bu mekanik Old Faith/Christian RightfullvsTyrant mekaniğiyle iç içe ayrıca, yani bir şövalyeyi aldığınızda o şövalyenin inancı ve değerleri de önemli oluyor sizin için. Söz gelimi eski inanca bağlı bir şövalyeyi yuvarlak masaya çağırınca diğer seçenek olan Hristiyan şövalye sizi düşmanı belleyip Hristiyanlardan topladığı bir orduyla başınıza bela olabiliyor.  Bu şövalyeleri farklı Leydilerle evlendirip topraklar vererek onların sadakatini yüksek tutmak oldukça önemli.

Oyunun savaşları TotalWar mekaniklerine benzer, ama onlar kadar akıcı dersem yalan olur. Alışırken biraz yadırgıyor insan, ama farklı üniteleri açmaya başlayıp büyülerinizi kazandıkça, şövalyeleri toplayıp güçlendirdikçe savaşların zevki çıkmaya başlıyor.

Asıl oyunun diplomasi mekanikleri yok dersek yalan olmaz. Ama The Druids ek paketiyle gelen yeni Campaing'le beraber farklı mekanikler eklemişler ve bu baya iyi olmuş. Oyuna aranızı iyi tutmanız gereken dört fraksiyon eklemişler;  Yağmacılar, Haydutlar, Hristiyan Rahipler, ve oyunda daha önce de olsa da sadece eventler yoluyla diplomatik ilişki kurabildiğimiz Sidhe, yani Old Faith'e inanan büyülü varlıklar. Bu fraksiyonları kullanarak rakiplerinize sabotaj düzenleyebiliyor, onların topraklarında isyanlar çıkartabiliyor, başlarına yağmacıları bela edebiliyor, şövalyelerine suikast düzenleyebiliyoruz. Ama dikkat etmemiz gerek bir şey var; Aynı şeyi bize de yapabiliyor rakiplerimiz! Yani durup dururken yağmacılar topraklarınızda biterse yada insanlarınız bir anda isyan çıkarırsa şaşırmayın...

Oyunun tek can sıkıcı noktası stabil olmaması. Oynarken çok sık save almanızı öneririm zira savaşa girdiğinizde yada savaştan çıktığınızda oyun hata verip kapanabiliyor. FPS açısından sorunlu olduğu yazılmış bazı yorumlarda ama o sorunlar şu an yok. Dediğim gibi, tek sıkıntılı yanı savaşlara girip çıkarken oyundan atması. Onun dışında bir hatayla karşılaşmadım ben. Gerçekten çıktığı dönemde çok kötü performans sorunları olması, oyunun hak ettiği değeri görmemesine neden olmuş. Birçok farklı mekaniği bir araya getiren bir oyuna yazık olmuş...

Oyun indirime girdiğinde farklı bir tat arayanlar kesinlike kütüphanelerin ekleyip bir şans versinler oyuna. Özellikle Kral Arthur mitosuna ilgisi olanlar kaçırmasın. Zira şu ana kadar Kral Arthur anlatılarını bu kadar başarılı aktaran başka bir oyun görmedim. Fiyatı zaten çok uygun, alın ve deneyin...

I think this is one of the first games I bought on Steam, but I didn't review it at the time.  Back then I had kind of long load times that made me dread everytime I had to enter a new battle.  But now I'm trying it again with my much upgraded computer (only the chassis, keyboard and mouse of the original remain) and it's a much smoother experience.  There's so much to like about this game.  While the tactical do eventually get repetitive (how can they not), they are also varied with a lot of different battlefields that offer different obstacles.  Unlike other RTS of this sort, the battlefields have points of interest you must control to gain access to spells and bolster your troops morale.  Morale wins or loses the battle in this game, not decimating the opponent (although that certainly helps).  And that is an idea I quite like because it really adds another layer of tactical depth.

But where the game really shines is in the campaign.  The base game comes with a story campaign that is very interesting with lots of flavor and text quests to go on.  Even in can be played through a number of times because you have a few different paths through it.  You can be good or evil, and you can be pagan or Christian.  I can't bring myself to play King Arthur as a bad guy, but it's interesting having to choose between the old gods or the new.  After you're done with that, the expansions offer two more campaigns that give you something of a Crusader Kings lite experience.  Now you're free to conquer the map or make friends however you'd like.  

It's hard to recommend this game highly enough.  Especially, since as popular as King Arthur is as a setting for games, they rarely seem to take it very seriously (the only exceptions I can think of being Infocom's Quest for Excalibur (which really adapts the Sword in the Stone) and Spirit of Excalibur (and presumably its sequel Vengeance of Excalibur, but I haven't played that.)) This is better than Spirit of Excalibur, though, because it is a working game, and that was something more like an experiment.

As a side note, some people are leaving this game bad reviews because they are having glitches.  I wish they would say in their reviews what their computer specs are because my game is running perfectly.  I'm using Windows 10 with an Nvidia GTX 1070.

[h1][i]“To Jerusalem, we pray
It's time to meet you there~ 🎶”[/i]
~Alphaville[/h1]

In June 2000, something cool happened – Creative Assembly released Shōgun: Total War. Why was it so important? Well, because Creative Assembly finally made it absolutely clear – one genre is just not enough anymore. Nowadays, games that combine different elements from various genres are rather common. Action games, for example, often include stealth parts, while real-time strategies incorporate a lot of the RPG elements. We take it for granted today, but even despite the fact that there were tons of the experiments before, the mainstream gaming was pretty strict. This here is, say, Sid Meier's Civilization with its grand strategy map, while this here is BUNGiE's Myth. Which is strictly tactics. Now, Shōgun? It combined both. The grand strategy screen allowed us to recruit units, manage the economy and taxes, deploy ninjas, trade, etc. And when the diplomacy failed (it a-a-always does), there was a time for tactical battles. People loved that, and up to this day, the Total War franchise is doing really well. What's funny, though, is that Creative Assembly wasn't the first to make such a game. Say wha-a-a...

No, seriously, it is funny, so bear with me for a moment. You know how nowadays people tend to say bad things about movie-based games? Like they always suck and stuff. I guess we all know which “angry” YouTuber to blame for that, but the thing is – some movie-based games were actually quite good. And in our case? One of such games was quite groundbreaking. I'm talking about Braveheart. The game based on Mel Gibson's 1995 epic. Well, originally it wasn't like that and a Scottish team from Glasgow just wanted to make a realistic game about their ancestors, but Eidos jumped on board and brought the expensive license with them, so... yeah. Braveheart. A year before the very first Total War, it did exactly that – combined two things that at this point feel like they were supposed to co-exist.

You may have noticed something in common at this point, right? Between Shōgun and Braveheart, I mean. Both were obsessed with history. Braveheart, as I already mentioned, was designed as some sort of tribute to Scotland (it actually used a satellite imagery of Scottish terrain for its campaign maps), while Total War was obsessed with Sengoku jidai Japan and even had Dr. Stephen Turnbull, a British military historian specializing in samurai and Japanese warfare, as a consultant. Now, it's finally time for us to stop talking about the sub-genre's origins and focus on this specific game, Crusaders: Thy Kingdom Come. Released eight years after the first Total War, it's the very first game from Neocoregames.

And you know what? On the paper, it's a pretty... obvious thing. Crusaders was made by a then-young Hungarian team from Budapest. It's a historical strategy that follows the First Crusade (1096–1099) and looks suspiciously like what we had in Braveheart / Shōgun. Naturally, it was a wannabe team imitating the big names, right? Wrong. Neocoregames were visionaries. They had that dream about an epic hybrid between a wargame... and an RPG. The problem was – the publisher didn't really want to share their vision, not yet. I mean, it's Paradox we're talking about, right? The guys are all about strategies. Naturally, they wanted a strategy. And when you're young and have no experience? There's no other way but to listen to the big daddy. Here's the thing, though. Neocoregames were smart.

While trying to pretend they were working on “yet another one of those” games, they kept working towards their dream. Slowly, sure, but as Lucretius said, "the fall of dropping water wears away the stone". Does Crusaders feel a lot like the Braveheart formula all over again? Yes. Look at the comments and lots of people call it “poor man's Total War”. “Poor man's” because at the point this game came out, Total War already had Medieval II with Empire well on the way. All while Crusaders was...

OK, I don't want to say that it looks bad. Exactly the opposite. If anything, I want to praise our guys here. They do deserve that. Not only did they fight for their dream, but they were on a very strict schedule (Paradox only gave them, like, a year to develop their game), yet not only did they manage, they even did it with their own in-house engine called Coretech. Now [i]that's[/i] what I call dedication. If you don't go too hard on them for not being able to compete with Creative Assembly, I'd say their game looks good. What I liked the most, for example, is how the weather effects work. Like, when there's, say, a fog or sandstorm that makes it hard for your units to see (with corresponding penalties being in play), it'll also be hard for you personally. Pretty cool stuff.

The most important thing for us, though, is that this game was pretty much King Arthur's prototype. That means that you'll have that certain hero you won't be able to afford to lose. And naturally, that hero can be leveled up. And so can be your units. Again, Paradox made it clear that they didn't want an RPG, so all the touches are pretty subtle, but still, leveling up is a thing, you'll be able to find and equip relics, and there's a non-linear approach (you'll be able to manually choose which side-quests to do, while very often it'll be either one [i]or[/i] another). Actually, that's what the “non-combat” part is all about. Like, there's no grand strategy map at all. You just manage your troops and their stuff, level up heroes, equip them, and choose optional quests for better relationships with certain factions (rep unlocks new units and relics). In other words, don't expect miracles. Crusaders is more like a proof of concept.

Now, I made it all sound good, right? Well, in a way, it is. But it comes from me and I'm more than used to clunky European stuff. And let me tell you, this here [i]is[/i] clunky. It's not like I can't see where all that comes from (again, the game took only one year to finish), but... let's just say that when it's about one of those NPCs you must protect who act like they're too tired of life and just want to end their suffering? The fact that the devs did their very best won't be much of a comfort. This game? It's just... it doesn't feel like it was meant to be enjoyed. I can't call it broken, and with enough patience, you'll be able to overcome even the highest difficulty and even enjoy the process. Like I said, though, it involves patience.

Crusaders is one of those games in which losing a fully leveled up unit is a life-changing tragedy. While the missions are just way too random. You never know what will happen next and who will spawn where or do what. That means you [i]will[/i] lose people. Ah, and there's that ambush mechanic. Neat on paper, torture in reality. You proceed as usual, then [i]boom![/i] Enemies are everywhere, the trees are speaking Arabic and you're dead. So yeah, despite all the praise I want to give here, I don't think I can recommend this game to anyone. Even at the release, it was more like a proof of concept. A way to sell King Arthur idea to Paradox. And nowadays, when we have juggernauts like Total War: Warhammer? There's just no reason to get back to this game. Not a single one.

Sure, it won't take long to beat this game (there is only one 15-mission-long campaign and no story), but you know how it is. The game just can't provide anything special to make it worth it. Aside from, maybe, a multiplayer, but since it's peer-to-peer only, relies on RakNet middleware, and comes with the same exact clunkiness the main game has... you know how it is. You'll need to find some fellow necromancers first (it's also fun to mention that the Steam version keeps trying to install Xfire every time you launch it. Every. Bloody. Time.) At the end of the day, Crusaders is an interesting project to talk about. But when it's about actually spending your time on it? Like I said, not worth it.

A simple vista, Crusaders: Thy Kingdom Come parece un clon más de los Total War. Sin embargo, sentado ante él descubres que no, aunque a nivel de jugabilidad y control las batallas sean similares, el desarrollo de las mismas es muy diferente. La razón principal de esto es que Crusaders carece del mapa del mundo dividido en provincias típico de los Total War, sino que su campaña prescinde en gran medida del control del jugador (y de la gestión) para centrarse en las batallas. Y, al ser una serie lineal de batallas, esto permite que los creadores le den una variedad de objetivos y de retos poco habituales, uniendo objetivos primarios, secundarios, eventos scripteados, oledas de enemigos que aparecen de la nada, etc. El resultado son batallas bastante más imprevisibles que las de los Total War, y con mayor variedad.

Sin embargo, como juego, aqueja de problemas importantes. La IA, tanto de unidades propias como enemigas, es bastante limitada y muy belicosa, y a menudo encontraremos que nuestras unidades cargan cuando tenían otras órdenes. La dificultad de las misiones también está mal calibrada, pasando de una sucesión de batallas muy fáciles, a algunas complicadillas, y luego de golpe el infierno de la batalla final en Jerusalén. Y el uso tan serio del scriptado a menudo hace que haya que jugarse las batallas un par de veces para ver por dónde van a salir los enemigos, en lugar de planificar todo desde el principio.

Por su parte, el sonido cumple sin grandes alardes. Y los gráficos achacan el paso del tiempo y resultan algo pobres, aunque cumplen. Un 5.

[h1][b] Reseña de Aquaria[/b][/h1]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
Aquaria es un indie 2D de exploración tipo metroidvania, pero con la brillante idea de que TODO ocurra bajo el agua. Controlas a una protagonista femenina en un mundo subacuático “precioso” y atmosférico, donde avanzar no es tanto correr y saltar… sino nadar, descubrir rutas ocultas y resolver el clásico “¿por dónde demonios sigo?” con estilo.

La primera impresión es clara: esto no quiere ser un paseo guiado. Aquaria te suelta en su océano de fantasía con una vibra inmersiva, una historia que se toma en serio a sí misma (a ratos filosófica), y una banda sonora tan buena que casi te perdona cuando te pierdes por quinta vez buscando la salida.

En resumen: un metroidvania indie de desplazamiento lateral, con aventura, acción y rompecabezas, que apuesta por la exploración y la ambientación por encima de la comodidad moderna. Controversialmente: me encanta que no te trate como bebé… pero también se pasa de listo.

[h2]Lo Profundo y lo Turbio[/h2]

Lo Bueno:
  Exploración metroidvania bien marcada: mapa mental, backtracking y desbloqueos que abren el mundo de forma satisfactoria.  
  Banda sonora “gran banda sonora” de verdad: de esas que cargan media experiencia y te meten en el mood.  
  Visuales 2D atmosféricos y “preciosos”: dirección artística que hace que perderse duela menos.  
  Protagonista femenina con presencia: no es un adorno, es el centro del viaje.  
  27 logros: para el que necesita validación digital por explorar hasta la última cueva húmeda.

Lo No Tan Bueno:
  Compatibilidad parcial con mando : o sea, “funciona… a veces… más o menos… tú verás”.  
  Mundo abierto subacuático + metroidvania = perderse es parte del contrato: si odias deambular, esto te va a sacar canas.  
  Rompecabezas que pueden cortar el ritmo: cuando quieres explorar y el juego te dice “piensa”, pero tú solo querías nadar bonito.  
  0 jugadores actuales: sí, estás explorando un océano… pero también un museo. Inmersivo, pero por abandono.

[h2]Conclusión (Muy Bueno)[/h2]
Aquaria es de esos indies que no piden permiso: te avienta a un mundo abierto subacuático, te obliga a explorar, y te premia con ambientación y música de primera. Si te gustan los metroidvania de verdad (con backtracking y “a ver si ahora sí encuentro el camino”), aquí hay sustancia.

Pero también hay que decirlo: su “compatibilidad parcial con mando” es el equivalente a un salvavidas con fugas, y el ritmo puede tropezar si los rompecabezas te agarran con poca paciencia. Aun así, cuando el juego hace clic, se siente especial.

Lo más irónico: hay 0 jugadores actuales, pero 723 recomendaciones totales. Traducción: no está “de moda”, pero sí dejó huella. Y eso, en Steam, vale más que mil tendencias pasajeras.

I got this game a long time ago as part of one of the OG Humble Bundles.  But it might've been the last of that bundle that I tried because it kind of looked like those old NES/SNES games they made for girls like The Little Mermaid, Barbie, etc.  At the time of release, that was kind of all they made when you combine non-violence, a female protagonist, and cutesy graphics.  Because of the stark contrast between games that were targeted toward boys and girls, it often felt that the games targeted toward girls were just boy games without the shooting and such.

But this game was one of the originals that proved that gaming could have all of those elements and still be as interesting gameplay wise as any other game.  There were predecessors like Ecco the Dolphin, The Oregon Trail, etc. that made non-violent gameplay interesting, but this one went all-in on feminine aspects that had historically meant the game wasn't interesting to a male audience as much.  But they made a great game, which was wonderful for gaming history.  If only more modern games learned from this one and not every female protagonist had to be a skin-swapped man or a girl boss, gaming would be a little more interesting.


The Positives:
-The visuals are beautiful.  They still hold up, as you can find similar games like Hollow Knight and its sequel that have that beautiful blend of Metroidvania gameplay with colorful, world-building visuals.  Unfortunately, mobile games kind of ripped off this near-exact visual style for some of their titles, cheapening this in retrospect, but please don't let modern bad games affect how great this was (apply this rule to any modern ensloppification of your beloved classic IPs).

-It took me an hour or two to get into it, but once I did, I liked the environment and the story.  I have a weakness of not being able to get into games right away if I don't get to do something, and that applied here where I was waiting for something to "happen"—but once I got some things to do and reasons to explore, I got into it.  It really comes into its own and rewards exploration and continuing the story with new creatures and new pieces of story.

-All of the alternatives to just moving around and shooting everything that most games do were great.  Explore, discover, enjoy the game...and it's not boring.  Definitely one of the predecessors to modern games that are all about exploration and storytelling and eliminated all combat-type gameplay elements.


The Negatives:
-Only a negative because it hits on my weakness, but I did find that it took a while to get into things.  Unfortunately, I can say that about a lot of games that aren't Sim City-style monitor-everything-24-7 kinds of games, but you need to give it some time and not let your social-media-caused-attention-deficit ruin you here.

-As I mentioned, you might notice that the visuals got ripped off by cheap mobile games, so don't let that ruin it for you.  I love the Langrisser series, and they did a remake that had "mobile-quality" graphics.  It really was hard not to feel like it was "cheapened" by that, as the original Genesis versions were unique and beautiful, and I would say the same thing here: appreciate the game, anyway, as this was great back in the day and caused the modern art style that is now cliché.

-I played it through and enjoyed it, but I didn't feel any great need to cover every inch of the game or anything like an old Zelda game or a Resident Evil game where I played it a bunch of times (though, to be fair, RE is replayable because you play once in total fear and a second time with infinite weapons to shoot everything that scared you).  I liked it a lot but am glad that I played through once and didn't try to play it into the ground.


Overall, this was the biggest surprise from that bundle back in the day.  I think it was in the same bundle as like Gish and such, and I thought I'd like that and not care for this...surprisingly, it was the other way around (Gish's controls made it annoying to play, and this was fluid and beautiful and I ended up liking it a lot).  Whether or not you play it, you'll see the influence it had on modern gaming with a lot of its bold decisions that, at the time, would've meant it had no chance.  But some bold decisions and a world-changing Humble Bundle model later, and it's a classic that will have its place in gaming history.  It might not be your thing, but it definitely left its mark on multiple genres in the years since its release.

This game is almost 20 years old now? I'm one of those people who wouldn't register a Steam account before a few more years after the time it came out. I wanted a quick play as I asked, "Has it aged graciously?" and the answer is "No, but also not enough for it to feel bad to play nowadays".

I wasn't a fan of the pivot animation back in the day and it doesn't look any better today, getting especially awkward in some cutscenes, and keeping its contrast with the beautiful art. One of those games that look relatively better in screenshots than in motion.
The underwater world is sprawling yet sparse, in line with the idea of being (mostly) alone in a vast ocean, but not translating just as greatly in terms of gameplay, feeling heavily padded out with some areas that have little more than nothing and a few enemies, with chances to save a game placed far between each other. The combat is quite basic, based around avoiding attacks and letting a lock-on of sorts take care of the enemies.
It's also hard wanting to replay it for the story, knowing how it goes off on tangents eventually, and then nowhere, even if it's not the first game that never resolved its cliffhanger and won't be the last.

Even if time hasn't been completely generous with it, it's still fascinating and atmospheric, something that is best enjoyed slowly, checkpoint after checkpoint. Reaching the surface of the water (the "Veil") for the first time is still an experience, even if later parts where Naija is forced out of the water are some of the most annoying (she can't walk, only leap around from point to point).

I wouldn't even call [b]Aquaria[/b] overrated in light of nowadays: its original release came at a time the market was much, much less saturated than it is today, and digital distribution on a mass level was still young. It was in fact one of the first games to really show what indie developers could do. It simply cannot recreate the impression it was capable of leaving when it was brand new, but it can still be liked today.

Is there a good guide: I used the ones on steam by PB and Marie Anette, I also used the wiki for recipes (aquaria.fandom.com/wiki/Recipes)
Notes:

* The game's code unlocks the achievement for the shrimp boss along with the rock crab boss for beating the later. This is a positive cause the shrimp boss is hard to reach, but still worth mentioning
* Please note that the unlock all of the "Fast travel" turtle achievement requires the 2 dead-end turtles behind the race track.
* once you have unlocked songs you need to know you can hotkey them with 0-9 on your keyboard!
* There is no "real" fast travel or stage select. You'll have to swim toggling the minimap for a long while to get anywhere in particular, even the fast travel turtles don't let you select where to go, instead they just cycle their points. 
* the cooking screen is really bad. There's no option to quick cook something you have a recipie for, and no option to make 5x of something for example. You'll have to painstakingly go to a different ingreidents screen drag every ingredient one by one and cook individually then start again for the second dish.  
* To add to the point above you can only hold a max of 8 of each ingredient and the good recipies hog the same ingredients. you'll reload areas to farm leaves for hours.
* The bosses and puzzles are cryptic. Without a guide it's almost impossible. Hitting a boss is sometimes indicated by them flashing red, sometimes not. this aspect could really use improving.
* Remember in Skyrim when you'd pause the game mid combat to eat 20 wheels of cheese? This game is just like that but now you have to cook the wheels of cheese right there before you eat it.. And no, unlike Skyrim you don't have spells to heal.. so get cooking.
* I can see why this metroidvania never really took off. While the premise is good and the gameplay is fun, it's clear the game design has some flaws that keep it just under "good". A re-mastered version with proper fast travel, and many quality of life cooking and shape-change improvements would be awesome.

All that being said the game is still:
Above 51%, Recommended.

It’s almost impossible to approach Aquaria without anchoring it to 2007. This was an "Indie Metroidvania" released before I was fully familiar with those terms, and before digital storefronts made small‑team projects feel commonplace.  I don't think I even had a Steam account in 2007! For its time, it’s remarkably accomplished: you can see clear echoes of Ecco the Dolphin and Super Metroid, and the ambition behind it is unmistakable. Bit Blot was working hard to prove that a handcrafted indie title could stand shoulder‑to‑shoulder with the classics. 

But expectations have shifted. Today, I look to indie games for brevity, focus, and experimentation rather than faithful retro recreation. In that sense, Aquaria doesn’t quite transcend its era. It’s an important milestone in the rise of indie gaming—just not one that fully resonates with my modern sensibilities. A meaningful artifact, but a dated experience. [b]3 out of 5[/b].  On a binary scale, I'm recommending, but I'm not sure it is worth your time in 2026 or beyond.

Aquaria is a little gem, especially considering the fact that it was released back in 2007 and developed by just two people. It surely deserves much praise for delivering a quite unique Metroidvania experience, focusing on the ability of the protagonist to use special songs to change form and unlock new powers. The hand-drawn graphics are impressively detailed, and the game map is quite large, with lots of secrets to find. However, it is worth noting that some aspects of the game didn't age too well: the controls feel especially clunky and because of that some sections are extremely frustrating to play through - the jump-climbing parts are just painful to pull off, and made me feel like I was playing Getting Over It. Exploration is generally rewarding but level design is not too great at times, with many dead ends and loops that frankly only seem to have been purposefully placed to make the player waste more time than needed, and some game mechanics (including some gimmick boss fights) are quite obtuse to figure out. The game would have also benefited a lot from at least a couple more fast travel spots, because the amount of backtracking needed to reach distant areas is seriously tiresome. 

If you can overlook the imperfections and embrace the flow - pun intended - of the game, Aquaria will reward you with an immersive - also intended - adventure enriched by an original and surprising storyline, rich visuals and a great, dream-like atmosphere. I'm glad I had the opportunity to catch up with it, albeit it feels very sad to know that a sequel was originally planned but it will never see the light of day due to the tragic fate suffered by one of its developers. A real, real pity.

Аквария... Забытая жемчужина, о которой с ностальгией вспоминает не такое уж и большое количество людей. Но не будем затягивать и приступим к погружению. Вполне возможно, длительному, часов на 10-20 (steam-версия это моё далеко не первое прохождение). Наша древняя черепаха отправляется в путь!

Сразу же нас встречает вступительная заставка, на первый взгляд никак не относящаяся к происходящему. Сюжет здесь будет подаваться мелкими кусочками и по большей части ближе к концу игры. Впрочем, можно строить свои теории, основываясь на элементах дизайна локаций и надписях на стенах. Да, их можно перевести, это не бессмыслица, а просто надписи на английском, только придуманным разработчиками шрифтом! Не стоит питать больших надежд на сюжетную составляющую, она не без недосказанностей. Но лично мне нравится, тем более есть над чем подумать и есть связь сюжетной линии с элементами геймплея и, вы не ослышались, саундтрека.

А что по геймплею? Аквария демонстрирует целый риф интересных фишек: волшебная песнь, перевоплощение в различные формы, готовка, свободное перемещение по подводному миру. Не всегда они идеально отполированы, но что есть, то есть. Кстати, сразу отмечу, что прокачки характеристик в игре нет, но она, как по мне, и не нужна: игровые механики и так дают прокачку. 

Начну сразу с плохого. Готовка для играющих вслепую слишком неочевидна, ибо не все рецепты можно найти в игре. а интуитивно тоже вряд ли дойдёшь, а для опытных слишком сломана: усиления атаки поднимают урон довольно значительно, а лечение не имеет кулдауна и поглощается на полной паузе. Впрочем, уничтожать боссов с ядовитым пирогом на +3 атаки или носиться по карте под ускоряющим супом это весело. И я даже не говорю про радужный суп, это надо видеть. Плавание ощущается довольно приятно... пока Найя в воде. Да, в игре есть выход на поверхность, и это полный хаос. Здесь вы будете либо ржать над происходящим, либо гореть от непонимания, как добраться до цели: по суше героиня перемещается только рывками, и это бывает крайне резко и дёргано. 

Не буду подробно описывать ужас мира вне воды и расскажу о хорошем. Формы и пение - сильнейшие из особенностей игры. Петь можно и просто для веселья (может, даже сочините какую-то музыкальную композицию), и для "заклинаний" (которых по сути только два), и для смены формы (хотя куда удобнее использовать горячие клавиши, в данном случае цифры), и для некоторых головоломок, и для использования некоторых необязательных механик (например, катание на морских коньках!). Формы, хоть и кажутся, за исключением первых двух, основной и "боевой", просто инструментами для преодоления преград, на самом деле имеют свои особенности, до которых не сразу дойдёте и которые могут вас выручить, не бойтесь экспериментировать с их применением. В последнем прохождении довелось почувствовать всю силу [spoiler]заряженной атаки природной формы[/spoiler]: эта штука превращает Найю в ракету, используется как живой щит или опора, и просто ломает некоторых боссов, либо сразу пробивая по слабому месту, либо игнорируя их кадры неуязвимости.

Говоря о боссах... Весьма интересные твари. Многие боссы представляют из себя головоломку: просто так не убиваются, и надо понять, как их побеждать, или хотя бы найти слабое место. Как только суть дела понятна, боссы обычно большой проблемы не составляют, сложность игры не такая уж и большая. Нельзя не отметить и внешний вид боссов: здесь есть и огромные морские животные, и пугающие древние боги. А ещё у некоторых из них есть несколько различных фаз! Финальный босс здесь особенно отличился, но вы всё сами увидите, если поиграете.

Теперь об игровом мире. Акварию можно считать метроидванией: порядок посещения локаций не всегда линейный, а для преодоления преград придётся открывать новые способности. Есть и немного нарушений прогрессии путём абьюза особенностей игровых механик, но не будем об этом. Игровой мир огромный и красочный, рисованная графика радует глаз, и у каждой локации есть свой колорит и свои особенности. Тут вы найдёте и руины храмов, и водорослевые леса, и тропические побережья, и мрачные глубины, и... плоть? Да, некоторые локации могут быть и пугающими. На игровой карте всегда отмечается местоположение Найи и исследованные воды, так что вряд ли вы потеряетесь, если конечно не уплыли слишком глубоко (в темноте карта не работает!). Но всё же большой мир не без проблем. Часто локации ощущаются слегка пустыми, плотность интересных для геймплея точек невысока, в основном красивые пейзажи и рядовые враги. Быстрое перемещение тоже слегка коряво: только 7 древних черепах-телепортов на разных концах карты ([spoiler]не считая двух секретных, соединённых только между собой и ведущих к одному из опциональных испытаний[/spoiler]), дальше плывите сами. 

Что же можно найти в этом обширном подводном мире? Кучу собираемых предметов, а именно 4 питомца и 32 сокровища! Но большинство из них - просто безделушки для перфекционистов. Питомцы не слишком полезны, хоть и вполне очаровательны, а большая часть сокровищ - просто лежащие дома у Найи декорации. Особого упоминания заслуживают костюмы (изменяют внешний вид обычной формы героини и иногда дают дополнительный пассивный бафф), а также два сокровища, дающие ресурсы для готовки.

В длительных и не всегда осмысленных плаваниях очень выручает музыка. Алек Холовка написал потрясающий душевный саундтрек, который приятно слушать и вне игры. Главный лейтмотив простой, но запоминающийся, и его можно найти во многих треках... Поиграете и узнаете, почему. 

Что я могу сказать ещё? Аквария - жертва своего времени. В 2007 году сцена инди-игр только зарождалась, и у разработчиков не было ни обилия средств (движок для Акварии они сами с нуля сделали), ни толпы заинтересованных игроков. Ко временам расцвета инди Аквария уже была забыта, и вряд ли её вспомнят. Иронично, что игра, где тебе приходится исследовать разрушенные забытые подводные цивилизации, стала таким же затерянным миром среди прочих игр.

А что в итоге? Безусловно, Аквария не идеальна. Но это очень атмосферное приключение с красивой музыкой, приемлемой рисовкой, слегка корявым, но потенциально интересным сюжетом, и парочкой необычных геймплейных фишек. Однозначно советую любителям подводного мира, метроидваний и старых забытых игр.

Под описание к данной игре, на мой взгляд, подходит выражение: от любви до ненависти один шаг. И игра Aquaria тот самый случай, когда негатив, от прохождения игры, порой тебя накрывает, буквально, с головой. Начинается это с момента, когда ты заплываешь в новую локацию, и поскольку кристаллы сохранения находятся на достаточном удалении друг от друга, тебя убивают и ты начинаешь свое исследование по новой. 
Я привык, что в хороших метройдваниях HP выпадает из всех поверженных врагов. Тут же разработчики пошли по другому пути. HP выпадает далеко не из всех врагов, чаще не выпадает вообще. По мимо этого в игре есть система крафта, когда ты, путем смешивания различных ингредиентов, получаешь продукт с необычными свойствами. С этим есть небольшие заморочки и плюс ко всему теряется темп игры, когда тебе во время ожесточенного боя приходится смешивать ингредиенты, чтобы элементарно подлечиться.
Это и управление в местах, где надо передвигаться по суше. Это отдельный вид боли и потраченных в пустую нервов.
За что же так полюбилась данная игра, дак это гениальная задумка разработчиков. Что как в метройдвании нам, в процессе игры, предстоит совершенствовать главного героя путем приобретения новых форм. И в основе каждой новой формы лежит сочетание звуков и цветов. Т.е. чтобы изменить свою форму надо исполнить определенную последовательность звуков, которые обозначены разными цветами и рисунками. И хорошо, что во время битвы с различными боссами, когда нам для победы требуется использовать несколько форм, они сменяются клавишами цифр на клавиатуре.
Так же музыкальное и визуальное оформление данной игры оставляет добрые положительные эмоции. Имеется и сюжетная история о потерянных воспоминаниях. В общем это те положительные моменты, которые остаются в памяти на долго.
Игру однозначно рекомендую, но порой очень непросто разобраться с отдельными загадками и с методами, как одержать победу над очередным боссом не читая гайдов.

I've tried several times to get into this game over the many years I've had it, but it always fails to click for me.

The movement feels sluggish, only worsened in areas slightly too big that have no clear design language for the flow so, its just aimless wandering hoping you get lucky and hit an area with the tools you have. The song system might be innovative (is it though plenty of pre-2005 games had skill wheels of one form or another) its far from intuitive, and even the auto aim I swear does nothing. Crafting doesn't support the game play either its just a kitchen sink feature tossed in.

The sea life is varied but that variety also lacks design language to say what hurts and what doesn't, some  "jelly fish" like creature swim by peacefully others hurt you for sometimes surprising amounts which with the floaty movement and clunky combat, doesn't feel good.

To sum it up, for a game about water, what it really lacks is flow, in design, in progression in movement, in combat, in everything. And even the often praised part, the art I have to say, while is no way bad, feels mismatched with the narrative being attempted. 

This should have spent a little longer in the oven, having the devs step back and look at all those parts they wanted and re-worked how to plate them up.

I can't see myself giving this another go, and I don't recommend you do, honestly Ecco the Dolphin felt better in design and ambience in the 90s and certainly now there are a whole host of better metrodvanias to try.

Overview:
Aquaria, developed by Derek Yu and Alec Holowka, is a unique indie game that combines elements of exploration, puzzle-solving, and storytelling in an underwater world. The game is often praised for its beautiful hand-drawn art style, atmospheric music, and engaging gameplay mechanics.

Gameplay:
Players control Naija, a mermaid-like creature, as she navigates the vast ocean, uncovering secrets and solving puzzles. The controls are fluid, allowing for seamless swimming through the vibrant underwater environments. The game features a non-linear structure, encouraging exploration and rewarding players with hidden treasures and lore.

Visuals and Sound:
The hand-drawn graphics are stunning, with each area of the ocean offering a distinct visual style. The game’s soundtrack, composed by Alec Holowka, complements the visuals perfectly, enhancing the immersive experience. The music dynamically changes based on the player’s actions and location, adding to the overall atmosphere.

Story:
Aquaria weaves a captivating narrative about self-discovery and connection with the ocean. As Naija uncovers her past and the mysteries of her world, players become emotionally invested in her journey. The storytelling is subtle, often conveyed through environmental cues and interactions rather than traditional dialogue.

Legacy:
The game has had a lasting impact on the indie game scene, inspiring many developers with its art and design. Sadly, Alec Holowka's passing in 2020 was a significant loss to the gaming community. His contributions to Aquaria and other projects continue to resonate, and his legacy is honored through the games he helped create.

Final Thoughts:
Aquaria is a beautifully crafted game that stands out for its artistic presentation and engaging gameplay. It’s a heartfelt journey that encourages exploration and discovery, making it a must-play for fans of indie titles. The tragic loss of Alec Holowka adds a poignant layer to the game's legacy, reminding us of the passion and creativity that fuel the gaming industry
